# hostap categorical FP/TP patterns

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `16-40_b32`, 107 findings, `src/crypto/milenage.c` + `src/eap_peer/eap_wsc.c` + `src/l2_packet/l2_packet_none.c` + `src/wps/wps_er_ssdp.c` + `wpa_supplicant/ctrl_iface.h` + `src/ap/ieee802_11.h`, all six entire files, 2026-08-08)

- **Reconfirms at very high density, no new sub-shapes:** INT14-C container/element-vs-pointer-arithmetic conflation (11 instances, `milenage.c` — loop index `i` misattributed as "bitwise" when only array elements `tmp2[i]`/`opc[i]` are XORed, plus `auts`/`autn` pointer-arithmetic-vs-element-bitwise conflation); INT10-C signed-modulo-on-a-loop-bounded-nonnegative-index (4 instances, `milenage.c`'s `(i+N)%16` with `i` always `0..15`); API00-C internal-only-API pedantry at very high density (`milenage.c` 8 instances + `l2_packet_none.c` 6 instances, every param a fixed-size caller buffer or struct-array field from a closed internal call set); EXP43-C same-buffer-disjoint-ranges misfire (`milenage.c:51`, `os_memcpy(tmp2+8,tmp2,8)` on a 16-byte array — `[0,8)`/`[8,16)` never overlap); ARR01-C `sizeof(*ptr)`/`sizeof(ptr->fixed_array_member)`-correct-idiom (3 instances, `eap_wsc.c`'s `cred`/`cred->ssid`/`cred->key`); EXP34-C same-condition short-circuit guard miss + callee-NULL-safe-internally (2 instances, `eap_wsc.c`'s `identity` — `wpa_hexdump_ascii`/`_wpa_hexdump_ascii` in `wpa_debug.c` explicitly checks `buf==NULL` before any deref); EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref (`eap_wsc.c:173`, `data` unassigned at the `sizeof` site); DCL30-C heap-vs-automatic-storage confusion (4 instances: `eap_wsc.c`'s `data`/`resp`/`r` all `os_zalloc`/`eap_msg_alloc`-backed, `l2_packet_none.c`'s `l2` via `os_zalloc`); DCL13-C eloop-callback dispatch-contract FP (3 instances: `l2_packet_receive`'s `eloop_ctx`/`sock_ctx`, `wps_er_ssdp_rx`'s `sock_ctx`) vs. `struct eap_method` vtable dispatch-contract FP (`eap_wsc_deinit`'s `sm`) vs. the `#ifdef FEATURE ... #else` no-op-stub genuine-if-low-value TP sub-shape, reconfirmed by name for `ctrl_iface.h` and extended to `ieee802_11.h` (18 instances total: `ctrl_iface.h`'s `wpa_s`/`priv`/`global`/`buf` stubs; `ieee802_11.h`'s `ieee802_11_get_mib`/`_sta`, `sae_clear_retransmit_timer`, `hostapd_eid_mbo`, `hostapd_mbo_ie_len` stubs — including one instance where the "unused" param is itself normally a written output buffer in the real branch, `eid` in `hostapd_eid_mbo`'s stub, which just does `return eid;`) vs. genuine plain-function-if-low-value TP on ordinary (non-callback, non-stub) exported functions (5 instances, `l2_packet_none.c`'s `l2_packet_get_own_addr`/`_send`/`_get_ip_addr`/`_notify_auth_start`/`_set_packet_filter` — default to TP for these rather than inventing a "multi-backend header contract" FP class, since no 3x-confirmed precedent for that shape exists yet); MEM31-C ownership-transfer-to-registration-API FP (`eap_wsc.c:592`, `eap_peer_method_register()` frees `eap` on every failure branch, `eap_methods.c:318-343`); MSC01-C no-final-else deliberate-guard-clause pedantry (2 instances: `eap_wsc.c`'s WAIT_START dispatch, `wps_er_ssdp.c`'s header-name if/else-if chain); MEM10-C ad-hoc-NULL-check pedantry (2 instances, `l2_packet_none.c`); API01-C buffer-before-pointer FP (`l2_packet_none.c:19`, `ifname[17]` bounded via `os_strlcpy`); PRE08-C legacy-8.3-filesystem no-value FP (`wps_er_ssdp.c:15`); ENV01-C wholesale zero-`getenv()` misfire (`wps_er_ssdp.c:26`); CON33-C/CON34-C no-pthread FP at volume (5 instances, `wps_er_ssdp.c`'s `inet_ntoa`/`strerror`, zero pthread usage in the file); EXP30-C pure-read-args unsequenced misfire (2 instances: `eap_wsc.c`'s `eap_wsc_state_txt()` calls, `wps_er_ssdp.c`'s `errno`/`strerror(errno)`); API02-C NUL-terminated-string-idiom + scalar-out-param misfires (4 instances: `ctrl_iface.h`'s `buf` response strings, `ieee802_11.h`'s `bandwidth`/`seg1_idx`/`elem_count` scalar out-params with companion sizes already present elsewhere); API05-C ptr+size_t idiom at very high density (11 instances across `ctrl_iface.h`/`ieee802_11.h`); DCL40-C 31-char collision, all genuinely exact (not near-misses) — `ctrl_iface.h`'s `wpa_supplicant_global_ctrl_iface_*` family (2 instances) and `ieee802_11.h`'s `hostapd_eid_eht_ml_tid_to_link_map`/`_len` — still graded FP per the established "not practically actionable on any toolchain hostap targets" convention even when exact; INT36-C `(void*)1`/`(void*)-1` non-NULL-sentinel TP(low) convention (2 instances, `ctrl_iface.h`).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, one file): ARR00-C "negative array subscript" on `pos[-1]` extends the established bounded-by-invariant idiom to a header-tokenizer loop with a provable *first-iteration* guard, not just a same-statement guard.** `wps_er_ssdp.c:62-63` (`if (pos[-1] == '\r') pos[-1] = '\0';` inside the SSDP header line-splitting loop): the very first loop iteration can't have `pos==buf` because the caller already matched a >=7-byte literal prefix (`"HTTP/1.1 200 OK"`/`"NOTIFY "`) with no `\n` in it before the loop starts; every subsequent iteration starts right after a `*prevpos++ = '\0'` write, so `pos-1` is always >= that write position, itself `>= buf`. FP.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: ARR00-C "loop uses uninitialized variable as bound" misfires when the loop-control variable is initialized in the for-statement's own init-clause.** `wps_er_ssdp.c:59` — `for (start = buf; start && *start; start = pos)`: `start` is assigned `buf` in the same statement, immediately before any use. Same root cause as the standing "uninitialized loop bound" FP class, new trigger shape (init-clause assignment, not a separate preceding statement).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP33-C "used uninitialized" misses a `recvfrom()`-style output-pointer parameter, extending the established ioctl/output-param blindness class to BSD sockets.** `wps_er_ssdp.c:39` — `addr` (a `struct sockaddr_in`) is passed as `recvfrom(sd, buf, ..., (struct sockaddr *) &addr, &addr_len)`'s output param and read only afterward (guarded by the preceding `if (nread <= 0) return;`), but the tool doesn't track the write-through-pointer.
- Confirms the `41plus_b159`-derived ERR07-C/ERR34-C "wire-data atoi()" TP sub-shape at a new severity tier: `wps_er_ssdp.c:86`'s `atoi(pos2)` on an SSDP `CACHE-CONTROL: max-age=` value is attacker-reachable over multicast UDP with zero validation, distinct from (and a stronger TP than) the usual local-admin-config-string atoi() default seen in `eap_wsc.c:213,260` (`dev_pw_id=`/`multi_ap=` from `phase1` config).
- No FNs found in any of the six files this batch: `milenage.c` is self-contained crypto arithmetic with no allocation/parsing; `eap_wsc.c`'s wire-parsing (`eap_wsc_process`) validates `message_length` against `end-pos` and a 50000 upper bound before use, and its config-string parsers (`new_ssid=`/`new_key=`/pkhash) all length-check before `hexstr2bin`; `l2_packet_none.c` is an inert documented stub (no real logic to miss a bug in); `wps_er_ssdp.c`'s partial-init failure path (`wps_er_ssdp_init` registering `multicast_sd` but not `ssdp_sd`) is safely cleaned up because the sole caller (`wps_er.c:1311`) unconditionally calls `wps_er_deinit()` -> `wps_er_ssdp_deinit()` on any failure, which closes both sockets by field value regardless of eloop-registration success.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `16-40_b26`, 115 findings, `src/crypto/sha512-internal.c` + `src/drivers/driver_openbsd.c` + `src/p2p/p2p_utils.c` + `src/rsn_supp/preauth.c` + `src/tls/bignum.c`, all entire files, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW, high-value FN-adjacent finding: `src/drivers/driver_openbsd.c` has a REAL missing closing brace, and sqc's MSC37-C+MSC07-C findings on it are genuine TP, not misfires.** `wpa_driver_openbsd_set_key`'s `if (key_len > IEEE80211_PMK_LEN || ... != KEY_FLAG_PMK) {` (`:83-84`) opens a brace that is never closed before the function's own closing `}` at `:97` — whole-file brace count is unbalanced by +1 (verified independently by walking every `{`/`}` in the file). Consequence: when the key is valid (the normal/expected case), the entire body — `memset`/`os_strlcpy`/`wpa_driver_openbsd_get_bssid`/`memcpy`/`ioctl`/`return 0` — sits inside the if-true branch, all *after* that branch's own unconditional `return -1;`, making it permanently dead code, so on the normal path the function falls off the end without returning (`MSC37-C:71`, TP high) and the dead code itself is flagged (`MSC07-C:87`, TP high). Net effect: this driver's set_key operation silently no-ops instead of installing the key, on every call that isn't already an error. Downstream of this same missing brace, several *other* findings in the same file are FP because sqc's scope/flow tracking gets confused by the malformed structure — not because they're independently wrong reads of well-formed code (see MEM31-C `:129` cross-function false double-free entry below). Any future batch touching an OpenBSD/rare-driver file should re-check brace balance first if the findings look locally inconsistent.
- **EXP05-C "cast away const" — 22/22 instances in `bignum.c` FP, exact 50/50 split between the two already-documented sub-classes, useful as a clean worked example for future EXP05-C batches.** `bignum.c` wraps LibTomMath (`mp_*`), whose functions are not const-correct. (a) Input operands genuinely declared `const struct bignum *` (`a`,`b`, and `c` when it's a modulus) are cast to `(mp_int *)` to satisfy the non-const `mp_*` signature but are only ever read by the underlying `mp_add`/`mp_sub`/`mp_mul`/`mp_mulmod`/`mp_exptmod`/`mp_cmp`/`mp_cmp_d`/`mp_unsigned_bin_size`/`mp_to_unsigned_bin` — no write-through, matches the long-established read-only-cast-away-const FP class. (b) Output/mutated operands (`c` in `bignum_add`/`bignum_sub`/`bignum_mul`, `d` in `bignum_mulmod`/`bignum_exptmod`, `n` in `bignum_set_unsigned_bin`) are declared plain non-const `struct bignum *` in the wrapper's *own* signature — there is no const to cast away at all, matching the established `41plus_b33`/"never-const-to-begin-with" category-error class (cf. `crypto_bignum_*` precedent at line ~6751). Always check the flagged variable's actual (non-)const declaration before grading an EXP05-C finding.
- **MSC13-C "value assigned never read" — 2 new instances of the loop-boundary-read-miss FP class, this time keyed on `break` rather than the end of the loop body.** `pmksa_candidate_add` (`preauth.c:399,434`): `cand = pos;`/`cand = NULL;` immediately precede a `break;` that exits the enclosing `dl_list_for_each`, and the very next statement after the loop is `if (cand) { ... }` — a real read. sqc's dead-store detector apparently doesn't look past a `break` to the code immediately following its enclosing loop. Distinguish from the genuine dead-store two lines earlier in the same file (`p = NULL;` at `preauth.c:333`, unconditionally overwritten on the *very next line* with zero intervening control flow — that one stays TP).
- **DCL39-C "struct passed to ioctl() may leak padding bytes" extended beyond the zeroed-struct-only reasoning: FP even when the struct is NOT explicitly zeroed first, because ioctl() to a local kernel network driver isn't a real cross-trust-boundary transfer in the first place.** `driver_openbsd.c:53`'s `struct ieee80211_bssid id` is only partially initialized (`i_name` via `os_strlcpy`) before `ioctl(SIOCG80211BSSID, &id)`, unlike the file's other 2 DCL39-C instances (`ifr`/`keyavail`, both `memset`-zeroed first) — graded FP at *medium* (not high) confidence since the padding genuinely isn't zeroed, but the underlying "this is a same-process kernel ioctl, not a serialization-to-an-external-party trust boundary" reasoning still applies. Batch-local — watch for recurrence before promoting to the main zeroed-struct entry.
- **Reconfirms at volume (not re-detailed above):** the crypto-round-macro PRE00-C/PRE01-C/PRE12-C real (low-severity) TP class extended to SHA-512's `Ch`/`Maj`/`Sigma0`/`Sigma1`/`Gamma0`/`Gamma1`/`ROR64c` (18 instances, `sha512-internal.c:92-101`) — exact 3rd hash-family reconfirmation of the SHA-256 `Ch`/`Maj`/`RND` precedent, including the same sub-split (bare-rvalue-operand params get PRE01-C, params only ever passed through a nested macro-call like `S(x,n)` don't); ARR01-C `sizeof(*ptr)`/`sizeof(ptr->member)`/`sizeof(array[0])`-correct-idiom (9 instances: `sha512-internal.c:188,227` on `md->buf`; `p2p_utils.c:117,206,532,588,658`; `driver_openbsd.c:64`); DCL13-C driver-ops-vtable dispatch-contract FP extended to `wpa_driver_openbsd_ops`'s `get_ssid`/`get_bssid`/`get_capa`/`set_key` (4 instances, `driver_openbsd.c:29,47,62,72`) and to `l2_packet_init`'s `rx_callback`/eloop's `eloop_timeout_handler` (2 instances, `preauth.c:62,130`) vs. plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP on read-only params with no dispatch binding (6 instances: `p2p_utils.c:320,384,617`, `preauth.c:523,550`, `sha512-internal.c:107`); API00-C internal-only-API FP at high density (13 instances across `p2p_utils.c`/`preauth.c`/`bignum.c`) plus one instance where the "unvalidated" param is in fact already null-safe via a ternary fallback (`p2p_get_pref_freq`'s `channels`, `p2p_utils.c:320`) and one where it's explicitly short-circuit-checked throughout the function body (`p2p_channel_select`'s `classes`, `p2p_utils.c:384`); API05-C `T *ptr, size_t len` idiom FP (5 instances) extended to opaque `void *ctx` callback-context params mistaken for the array half of the pair (`preauth.c:62,141`); MEM10-C ad-hoc-NULL-check pedantry (3 instances); PRE08-C 8.3-legacy-filesystem header FP (3 instances, `driver_openbsd.c:13,14`); MSC07-C goto-target-label-after-return blindness (2 instances, `preauth.c:266`, plus the genuine `driver_openbsd.c:117` — but see the missing-brace note above for why `driver_openbsd.c:87`'s superficially-similar MSC07-C is TP, not this FP class); EXP33-C both the `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref sub-shape (2 instances: `driver_openbsd.c:104`, `preauth.c:217`) and the interprocedural out-param-written-via-aliased-address sub-shape (3 instances: `nwid`/`id` filled through `ifr.ifr_data`/direct ioctl in `driver_openbsd.c:39,52`; `r` filled through `os_get_random(&r,...)` in `p2p_utils.c:379`); INT30-C char-pointer-arithmetic-misclassified-as-unsigned-int category error (`p2p_utils.c:349`); STR34-C char-to-char no-widening (`p2p_utils.c:368`); EXP40-C phantom cast-away-const where neither side is const (`preauth.c:526`, both `buf` and `pos` are plain non-const `char *`); ARR00-C pointer-parameter-treated-as-implicit-1-element-array (`preauth.c:487`'s `ssid+2`, exact `eap_sim_db.c` `imsi=username+1` precedent); MSC01-C no-final-else deliberate-fallback pedantry (`p2p_utils.c:621`, both branches already `return`); DCL00-C genuine (trivial) never-reassigned-pointer TP (`p2p_utils.c:391`); DCL30-C heap-vs-automatic-storage confusion (`driver_openbsd.c:115`, `os_zalloc`'d).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `6-15_b11`, 105 findings, `src/eap_common/eap_teap_common.c` + `src/eap_peer/eap_tnc.c` + `src/eap_server/eap_server_wsc.c` + `src/utils/browser-android.c` + `src/utils/ext_password.c` + `src/utils/pcsc_funcs.h` + `wpa_supplicant/wpas_kay.c`, all entire files, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances, one file, extends the existing "#ifdef-variable-size array, hardcoding a bound would be wrong" ARR02-C FP precedent to a distinct compile-time-fixed sub-shape): ARR02-C "implicit bounds" on a `static const` array whose size is fully and unambiguously fixed by its own braced initializer and is never consumed except via `ARRAY_SIZE()`.** `eap_teap_common.c`'s `sha1_cs[]`/`sha256_cs[]`/`sha384_cs[]` (`:228,249,274`, each a `static const u16 [...] = {...}` cipher-suite lookup table passed straight into `tls_cipher_suite_match(arr, ARRAY_SIZE(arr), cs)`). Unlike the ifdef-variable-size case, there's no cross-#ifdef ambiguity here, but the underlying rationale is the same: there is no separate hardcoded count anywhere to drift out of sync with the initializer, so specifying an explicit bound would be pure redundancy, not a safety or maintainability improvement. Watch for other `static const T arr[] = {...}` + `ARRAY_SIZE(arr)` lookup tables (crypto suite tables, OID tables, string tables) hitting this same shape.
- **Reconfirms in this batch (not re-detailed above):** the `struct eap_method` vtable DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP extended to `eap_tnc_deinit`/`_process`'s `sm` (`eap_tnc.c:59,201`) and `eap_wsc_check`/`_isDone`/`_isSuccess`/`_getTimeout`'s `sm`/`priv` (`eap_server_wsc.c:275,467,474,481`, 7 instances total) vs. the plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP sub-shape on functions that are themselves *not* vtable-bound (`eap_wsc_build_start`'s `sm`/`data`, `eap_server_wsc.c:167-168`; `ieee802_1x_alloc_kay_sm`'s `ssid`, `ieee802_1x_auth_get_msk`'s `wpa_s`, `wpas_kay.c:196,274`; `ext_password_get`'s `data`, `ext_password.c:75`); the eloop_timeout_handler DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP (`browser_timeout`'s `eloop_data`/`user_ctx`, `browser-android.c:22`); the MEM31-C ownership-transfer-to-`*_method_register()` FP class reconfirmed on both the peer side (`eap_peer_tnc_register`'s `eap`, `eap_tnc.c:414`) and the server side (`eap_server_wsc_register`'s `eap`, `eap_server_wsc.c:494`; matches the previously-documented `eap_md5.c`/`eap_server_psk.c` instances almost exactly) plus a 3rd, distinct MEM31-C FP shape — ownership transfer to the *caller via return* (`eap_tnc_process`'s `resp`, `eap_tnc.c:354`); EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref at very high density (13 instances: `eap_tnc.c:41`, `eap_server_wsc.c:99`, `eap_teap_common.c:631`, `ext_password.c:41`, `wpas_kay.c:216,320,321,322,387,391`); DCL30-C heap-vs-automatic-storage confusion at very high density (11 instances: `eap_tnc.c:55,84,144,362`, `eap_teap_common.c:69,644,660,676`, `eap_server_wsc.c:152,184,240`, `ext_password.c:63,99`); EXP34-C `%p`-format-NULL-is-safe FP (`eap_tnc.c:221`) plus the internal-only-API-guaranteed-non-NULL-struct-pointer FP sub-shape (`eap_tnc.c:177`'s `ret`); EXP30-C pure-accessor-sibling-arg FP, both the plain-function-call sub-shape (`eap_wsc_state_txt`, `eap_server_wsc.c:57`) and the `wpabuf_head`/`wpabuf_len`/`wpabuf_mhead` sibling-arg sub-shape (`eap_tnc.c:314,396`, `eap_teap_common.c:367,375`, `ext_password.c:93,107,109`); API00-C internal-only-API FP at very high density (11 instances: `eap_teap_common.c:33,121,327`, `ext_password.c:35`, `wpas_kay.c:196,303,377`x2), including a caller-already-dereferenced-so-provably-non-NULL sub-instance (`ieee802_1x_create_preshared_mka`'s `ssid`, `wpas_kay.c:377`, caller dereferences `ssid->mka_psk_set` immediately before the call); API05-C ptr+size_t/fixed-output-buffer idiom FP at very high density (8 instances: `eap_teap_common.c:74`, `pcsc_funcs.h:17,21,22,23,24`x3); API02-C "no size arg" misfire when the size *is* the last param and IS the semantically-paired one, verified against the .c implementation (`pcsc_funcs.h:17,21` — `scard_get_imsi`'s `size_t *len`, `scard_umts_auth`'s `size_t *res_len`, both confirmed as the actual in/out capacity by reading `pcsc_funcs.c`); PRE02-C single-token negative-literal FP reconfirmed at volume (`pcsc_funcs.h:33-37`, 5 instances, exact `6-15_b3` precedent) plus a new statement-macro (not expression-body) sub-shape (`#define scard_deinit(s) do { } while (0)`, `pcsc_funcs.h:32`); PRE08-C 8.3-legacy-filesystem FP (`wpas_kay.c:15`, `ieee802_1x_key.h` vs `ieee802_1x_kay.h`); CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()` no-pthread FP reconfirmed at volume (8 instances: `browser-android.c:90,109`, `ext_password.c:95,111`); MEM10-C ad-hoc-NULL-check stylistic pedantry (`ext_password.c:78,105`); MSC41-C hexdump-title FP (`wpas_kay.c:347`, `"Derived CAK"` is the log label, not the secret); MSC13-C genuine dead-NULL-init TP (`wpas_kay.c:199`'s `res = NULL`, unconditionally overwritten by `ieee802_1x_kay_init()` before any read — matches the already-confirmed genuine-dead-NULL-init class, contrast with the `dl_list_for_each`-blind-spot FP class); MSC07-C both the goto-target-after-return FP sub-shape (`eap_tnc.c:403`'s `fail:` label, reached via earlier `goto fail`) and a genuine (trivial) dead-code-after-`exit()` TP sub-shape (`browser-android.c:111`'s `return -1;` after `exit(0)` in a forked child's failed-execv path); ERR07-C/ERR34-C unchecked-`atoi()`-with-no-downstream-validation genuinely TP (`browser-android.c:44`, `atoi(url+5)`, contrast with the `6-15_b3` FP resolution where the value *was* range-checked); ENV03-C/ENV33-C `system()`/no-env-sanitization graded TP but low-severity/low-confidence when the invoked command is a hardcoded literal with no attacker-controlled input (`browser-android.c:121`, `system("/system/bin/input keyevent KEYCODE_HOME")` in an Android-only debug utility) — distinguish from the higher-severity TP this pair would deserve if any part of the command string were derived from untrusted input; ARR02-C `#ifdef`-variable-size-array-with-NULL-sentinel FP reconfirmed (`ext_password.c:19`'s `backends[]`, exact `drivers.c: wpa_drivers[]` precedent); ARR01-C `sizeof(ptr->struct_member)`-via-member-dereference misapplied as if it were array-parameter decay-to-pointer (`eap_teap_common.c:536`, `sizeof(*tlv->crypto_binding)` — a plain struct-size computation, unrelated to ARR01-C's actual concern); MSC01-C exhaustive-enum-switch-no-default pedantry (`eap_tnc.c:317`, all 6 `enum tncc_process_res` members covered) and deliberate-no-op-fallthrough-if/else-if pedantry (`browser-android.c:43`); EXP05-C cast-away-const to satisfy `execv()`'s `char *argv[]` signature — standard POSIX exec idiom, not a real defect (`browser-android.c:105`).
- **NEW FN (medium confidence): stale/dangling stack-address escape into an `eloop_register_timeout()` registration, currently latent only because the callback ignores its own parameters.** `browser-android.c:58`, inside `http_req(void *ctx, ...)`: `struct browser_data *data = ctx;` is a local *pointer variable*, and `eloop_register_timeout(0, 500000, browser_timeout, &data, NULL)` passes `&data` — the address of that local pointer variable, not the `browser_data` struct it points to. That stack address is invalid the instant `http_req` returns. It happens not to matter today because `browser_timeout(void *eloop_data, void *user_ctx)` never reads either parameter, but it's a real, exploitable-if-`browser_timeout`-ever-changes escape-of-local-address bug, distinct from and not caught by the DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable" detector (this is an *escape via callback registration*, not a return).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `16-40_b27`, 113 findings, `src/wps/wps_attr_build.c` + `wpa_supplicant/hs20_supplicant.c` + `wpa_supplicant/nan_supplicant.h` + `src/drivers/driver_nl80211_android.c` + `src/drivers/netlink.c`, all entire files, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: ARR30-C/STR31-C cross-function buffer conflation, worse than the previously-catalogued name-collision class — the flagged buffer's declared TYPE is wrong, not just its scope.** `wps_attr_build.c:176`'s ARR30-C ("Buffer 'addr' with size 1, allocated at line 428") wrongly cites `wps_build_oob_dev_pw`'s unrelated `const u8 *addr[1]` (declared ~250 lines later, in a different function) as the backing store for `wps_build_authenticator`'s own `const u8 *addr[2]` (declared at `:162`, correctly sized). The same line-428 declaration is independently misread by STR31-C (`:428` itself, "character array too small to hold any string data") as a character buffer — but `addr[1]` is an array of *pointers* (`const u8 *`), not char/string data at all. Two different rules, same root variable, both wrong for different reasons.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: INT14-C "variable used with both bitwise and arithmetic operations" fired on a `#define` macro CONSTANT, not a variable.** `hs20_supplicant.c:74`, `HS20_VERSION` (`#define HS20_VERSION 0x20`, `ieee802_11_defs.h:1664`) used as `(HS20_VERSION >> 4) + 1` — sqc's message literally says "Variable 'HS20_VERSION'...", but there is no such variable; it's a preprocessor token substituted before any type/variable resolution applies. New category-error sub-shape for the already-large INT14-C misattribution family (distinct from container-vs-member, deref-vs-pointer, ternary-condition — this one is macro-vs-variable).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MSC13-C "dead store" misfires on a `static` (file-scope-persistent) variable reset inside a function, because the rule's liveness analysis treats the assignment as dying at function return instead of recognizing it survives to the next call.** `driver_nl80211_android.c:36`, `drv_errors = 0;` inside `wpa_driver_send_hang_msg` — `drv_errors` is `static int drv_errors = 0;` at file scope (`:30`), read again on every subsequent call via the `if (drv_errors > ...)` check at `:35`. Contrast with the standing genuine-dead-store TP class (plain locals unconditionally overwritten before their one read within the *same* function, e.g. `android_pno_start`'s `int ret = 0` at `:81`, reassigned at `:132` before any read of the initial value — still a real, if trivial, TP).
- **Reconfirmed with a new twist: `struct wpa_driver_ops` vtable DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP now covers `#ifdef ANDROID_LIB_STUB`-gated stub bodies, not just real implementations.** `driver_nl80211_android.c`'s `wpa_driver_set_p2p_noa`/`_get_p2p_noa`/`_set_p2p_ps`/`_set_ap_wps_p2p_ie` stubs (`:156,162,168,174`) are assigned directly to `.set_noa`/`.get_noa`/`.set_ap_wps_ie` in `driver_nl80211.c:15561-15563`'s `wpa_driver_ops` struct literal — even though the stub body itself never touches the param (which would otherwise match the "`#ifdef FEATURE...#else` no-op-stub, TP" class from earlier batches), the vtable binding takes precedence and makes it FP, same as any other `wpa_driver_ops` member. Distinguishing test: check whether the specific function name appears as a `.field = function` initializer anywhere in `driver_nl80211.c`/`driver_wired.c`/etc, not just whether the function body is a trivial stub.
- Reconfirms in this batch (not re-detailed above): MEM31-C/MEM30-C false-positive-before-allocation and reassignment-clears-freed-state misses (`wps_attr_build.c:39,54,59,72` — `pubkey`/`dh_ctx` correctly freed/reassigned on every path, sqc's flags fire on returns that precede the actual allocation or on a check that follows an immediate reassignment); API00-C internal-only-API FP at very high density (16 instances across all 5 files); DCL13-C plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP split from the vtable/eloop/`#ifdef`-stub dispatch-contract FP families (10 instances: `wps_build_authenticator`/`_enrollee_nonce`/`_registrar_nonce`/`_auth_type_flags`/`_encr_type_flags`/`_conn_type_flags`/`_assoc_state`/`_key_wrap_auth`/`_encr_settings`'s `wps`, `is_hs20_network`/`hs20_get_pps_mo_id`'s `wpa_s`/`ssid`, `hs20_parse_rx_hs20_anqp_resp`'s `bss`, `netlink_receive_link`/`netlink_send_oper_ifla`'s `netlink`) vs. the `#ifdef CONFIG_NAN[_USD]...#else` static-inline no-op-stub TP sub-shape at very high density (21 instances, `nan_supplicant.h`, exact `ap_list.h`/`gas_query.h` precedent) vs. the `eloop_sock_handler` dispatch-contract FP (`netlink_receive`'s `sock_ctx:36`); EXP30-C pure-accessor/pure-macro-arg FP (`wpabuf_head`/`wpabuf_len:382`, `MAC2STR:310`, `NLMSG_DATA`/`NLMSG_ALIGN`/`NLMSG_PAYLOAD:30`, `linkmode_str`/`operstate_str:216`); DCL30-C heap-vs-local-storage confusion (4 instances: `wps_ie_encapsulate`'s `ie:491`, `hs20_build_anqp_req`'s `buf:217`, `netlink_init`'s `netlink:124`, all `wpabuf_alloc`/`os_zalloc`-backed); DCL31-C function-pointer-parameter-call misfire (`netlink_receive_link`'s `cb:30`); ARR39-C pure-integer-sum/byte-pointer-offset-isn't-double-scaling, both sub-shapes (`driver_nl80211_android.c:94`, plain `int bp` sum; `netlink.c:31`, `(u8*)ptr + N` byte-offset arithmetic); ENV01-C wholesale zero-`getenv()` misfire (2 instances, `driver_nl80211_android.c:47,82`); DCL39-C zeroed-struct-before-`ioctl()`/`send()` FP (3 instances: `:62,132,220`, all `os_memset`'d immediately before use); CON03-C/CON07-C no-thread FP on static counters (`drv_errors:30,32`, `nl_seq:171`); CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()` no-pthread FP at volume (5 instances, `netlink.c`); POS02-C `bind()`-without-privsep categorical FP (`netlink.c:111`); MEM10-C ad-hoc-NULL-check stylistic pedantry (3 instances: `hs20_supplicant.c:157,180`, `netlink.c:130`); EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref (`netlink_init`'s `netlink:96`); PRE08-C low-value-TP header-family convention (`ieee802_11_common.h`/`ieee802_11_defs.h`, `:14`); MSC01-C no-final-else guard-clause pedantry (`:51`); INT13-C/INT14-C genuinely-signed-int TP (low severity) split from the wrong-type-detection FP class (`release`, truly `int`, `:84`x2); API05-C ptr+size_t idiom FP (`buf`/`len:162`); API02-C misfire on an ordinary NUL-terminated `char *cmd` string param with no separate size needed (`nan_supplicant.h:19`). No FNs found on read-through of any of the 5 files (all short, mostly wrapper/dispatch/header code); all 5 marked clean for FN.

## Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed (from `16-40_b29`, 120 findings, `src/ap/preauth_auth.c` + `src/common/cli.c` + `src/common/wpa_common.h` + `src/crypto/aes-internal-enc.c` + `src/eap_peer/eap_methods.c` + `src/eap_server/eap_server_vendor_test.c`, all entire files, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW (2 instances, one file): MEM30-C "use-after-free: accessing member of freed pointer" misfires on `X->free(X)` — a struct member function pointer literally named `free`, called to deallocate the struct itself — treated as if reading the `free` member (or the call itself) had already deallocated `X` before the call completes.** `eap_peer_method_unload()`'s `if (m->free) m->free(m); else eap_peer_method_free(m);` (`eap_methods.c:259`) and the identical shape in `eap_peer_unregister_methods()` (`:369`) are both flagged, but in both cases `m->free(m)` **is** the deallocation call — nothing reads or writes `m` afterward in the same scope. Root cause looks like the free-tracker keying off the literal token `free` (member name or call target) rather than tracking real `os_free()`/`free()` calls. Watch for other structs with a member literally named `free`/`deinit`/`destroy` invoked as `obj->free(obj)`.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `16-40_b28`, 105 findings, `wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant_i.h` + `src/fst/fst.c` + `wpa_supplicant/op_classes.c` + `wpa_supplicant/win_if_list.c` + `src/ap/hostapd.h`, all entire files, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, 1 file): `foreach_X(var) { ... }` opaque dispatch-macro loop misparsed as a standalone function-like construct, producing a whole cluster of bogus findings on the *loop's own line*.** `fst.c:51` (`foreach_fst_group(g) {`) is flagged simultaneously as MSC37-C "non-void function has no return statement" AND EXP33-C "'g' used uninitialized" — sqc's parser is treating the macro-invocation-plus-brace as if it were a function definition rather than a for-loop-style macro. Same macro opacity also makes the loop induction variable look declared-but-unused (`g`, MSC13-C `:42`) and makes each `= NULL` initializer above the loop look like a dead store (`group`/`iface`, MSC13-C `:43,44`) even though both are read by an `if (!x)` check right after the loop. Watch for this shape (a local declared, then only ever touched inside a `foreach_*`/dispatch-style macro call) elsewhere.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (1 instance, extends the existing cross-function variable-name-collision family from ARR30-C to MEM31-C): a memory-leak/not-freed finding cites a variable name shared with an *allocation in a different function*, not the local in scope.** `fst.c:86` ("Memory leak: 'group' allocated with 'fst_group_create' is not freed") — the `group` in scope at that line (`fst_detach`) comes from `fst_iface_get_group()` (a lookup, not an allocation) and is never passed through `fst_group_create` at all; the allocator name match is purely coincidental with `fst_attach`'s unrelated local of the same name.
- **Reconfirms/extends `sizeof(*ptr)`-before-assignment misread as an uninitialized-pointer dereference (EXP33-C), now seen twice more in one batch:** `fst.c:141` (`h = os_zalloc(sizeof(*h))`) and `win_if_list.c:77` (`size_t blen = sizeof(*b) + 1024;`, before `b`'s first real assignment at `:84`). `sizeof` never evaluates its operand at runtime — this is purely a type-size computation, not a deref.
- **Reconfirms DCL30-C heap-vs-automatic-storage confusion, now 2 more instances beyond `comeback_token.c`:** `fst.c:153` returns `h` from `os_zalloc()`; `op_classes.c:648` returns `classes` from `os_zalloc()`. Both are heap pointers, not local automatic-storage objects — ARR00-C double-fires on the `op_classes.c` instance with the same underlying confusion ("local array... destroyed when function returns" — `classes` is not a local array at all).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances, 1 file): MSC01-C "if/else-if chain has no final else" / "switch has no default" fires on chains that are deliberately used as filters with an already-established default, not as exhaustive decision trees.** `op_classes.c:295` (bw-specific override chain — `res`/`res2` already default to `allow_channel()`'s result *before* the chain; unmatched bw values intentionally keep that default), `:344` (frequency-classification chain inside a loop — frequencies outside all listed bands are intentionally left uncounted, not an error), `:363` (switch used purely as a case filter that falls through past the switch body for every unlisted `op_class`, exactly the desired behavior). All three are "default already happened, or fallthrough is the design," not missing-handling bugs.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances, 1 file): FIO47-C "%s expects Pointer but argument is Integer" type-inference misfire on plain fixed-size `char` array locals declared via a multi-declarator line.** `win_if_list.c:118` (`char name[256], desc[256];` — both `name` and `desc` flagged as Integer for `%s`) and `:150` (`char err[PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE + 1];`, single-declarator, same misclassification). All three are unambiguous char arrays that decay correctly to `char *`; likely the same declarator-type-resolution gap already tracked internally (ast_utils declarator-name/type dup bug). Companion EXP33-C "may be used uninitialized" fires on the same `name`/`desc` at the same line despite an unconditional `name[len]='\0'`/`desc[len]='\0'` terminator write executing on every path (even `len==0`) just before use — also FP.
- **Reconfirms EXP30-C-on-side-effect-free-args FP, extended from macro args to plain accessor *function* calls:** `op_classes.c:620`, `os_memcpy(pos, wpabuf_head(buf), wpabuf_len(buf))` — `wpabuf_head`/`wpabuf_len` are pure getters with no side effects on `buf`, so "unsequenced" is harmless (no UB the rule is meant to catch).
- **Reconfirms MEM31-C ownership-transferred-to-a-container FP (not detailed as its own bullet before, but same shape as the `fst_group_create`/global-list case):** `fst.c:59`, group allocated then attached to the global groups list (`fst_group_attach_iface`) and freed later in bulk by `fst_global_deinit`; and `fst.c:74`, explicitly freed via `fst_group_delete(group)` two lines above the flagged return (guarded correctly by the `new_group` flag so pre-existing/shared groups are never double-freed).
- **NEW (1 instance): FIO23-C "main() returns without calling fclose(stdout)" is a FP by the C standard's own guarantee** — reaching the end of `main()` is equivalent to calling `exit()`, which flushes all open streams automatically (`win_if_list.c:58`).
- **NEW (1 instance): PRE32-C "printf called with preprocessor directives in arguments" misfires from proximity, not actual content** — `win_if_list.c:139`'s `printf(...)` call contains no `#if`/`#ifdef` inside its own argument list; the function merely sits inside a `#else ... #endif`-guarded region, which the rule appears to conflate with "directive inside the call."
- **NEW (1 instance): MEM05-C "variable-length array" misfires on a fixed-size array whose bound is a library-defined compile-time constant** — `win_if_list.c:147`, `char err[PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE + 1]` (`PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE` is pcap.h's `256`), not a runtime VLA.
- **NEW (1 instance): STR31-C "argv used without validating argc" fires even when argv/argc are never referenced in the function body at all** — `win_if_list.c:164`'s `main(argc, argv)` never touches either parameter; nothing is "used unsafely" because nothing is used.
- **Batch-local, ARR02-C on *local* (not parameter) arrays with an initializer consumed via `ARRAY_SIZE()`, treated as low-value FP, not yet 3x confirmed as a distinct sub-class from the existing param-array ARR02-C FP entry:** `op_classes.c:80,81,150,151,221,395` — six instances, all `const u8 foo[] = {...}` immediately paired with `ARRAY_SIZE(foo)`, so the implicit bound is unambiguous and safely derived; no real size-mismatch risk exists.
- **Reconfirms API00-C-mostly-FP-on-internal-only-APIs at high volume (10 instances across `fst.c`/`op_classes.c`)**, plus one refinement: `op_classes.c:525`'s `ssid` param isn't dereferenced directly in `wpas_supp_op_class_ie` at all — it's passed on to `wpas_op_class_supported()`, which already does its own `if (ssid && ...)` guard, so the caller-side flag is doubly unnecessary.
- **Reconfirms API01-C/API02-C/API05-C categorical FPs at very high volume in this batch** (7+2 API01-C, 2+2+1 API02-C misfiring on callback-fn-ptr/companion-size-already-present/NUL-terminated-string shapes, 2 API05-C ptr+size_t idiom) — no new sub-shapes, just reinforces existing entries.
- **DCL13-C default-TP holds for ordinary plain functions/static-inline accessors in this batch** (`op_classes.c` `mode`/`wpa_s`/`ssid` params in `allow_channel`/`get_center_*mhz`/`verify_*mhz`/`wpas_op_class_supported`; `hostapd.h`'s `ap_pmf_enabled`/`hostapd_is_{ht,vht,he,eht}_enabled`; `wpa_supplicant_i.h`'s `external_scan_running`/`network_is_persistent_group`) — all genuinely read-only, non-callback, real (if low-severity) const opportunities, consistent with the file's established default disposition.
- **NEW (1 instance): PRE00-C/PRE01-C/PRE12-C graded TP (not FP) on a small, genuinely-reusable two-member-access macro** — `hostapd.h:22,25` (`OCE_STA_CFON_ENABLED`/`OCE_AP_ENABLED`), where the parameter (`hapd`) really does appear twice in the body and is unparenthesized before `->`. Distinguish from the established eloop-callback/dispatch-table DCL13-C FP family — this is a different rule class (macro hygiene, not param constness) and the hazard is real (if currently low-risk since all call sites pass plain variables), so graded low-confidence TP rather than FP. Same disposition extended to `hostapd.h:208`'s `STA_HASH(sta)` → `(sta[5])` and `:890`'s `for_each_mld_link(partner, self)` → `&self->mld->links` (both unparenthesized-before-`[]`/`->` PRE01-C, medium confidence).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `6-15_b10`, 114 findings, 8 files: `src/eap_server/eap_server_identity.c`, `src/eap_server/eap_server_md5.c`, `src/eapol_auth/eapol_auth_dump.c`, `src/fst/fst_ctrl_iface.h`, `src/utils/browser-wpadebug.c`, `wpa_supplicant/wpa_passphrase.c`, `src/ap/airtime_policy.c`, `src/ap/ap_mlme.c`, all entire files, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances, one file): DCL31-C "called without prior
  declaration" misses declarations that ARE present via a standard C
  library header already `#include`d.** `wpa_passphrase.c` includes
  `<termios.h>` (line 10) which declares both `tcgetattr` and `tcsetattr`;
  sqc still flags all 3 call sites (`:39,49,60`) as if the functions were
  implicitly declared. sqc appears not to resolve declarations from at
  least some system/libc headers the way it does for project-internal
  headers. Watch for this on other POSIX/libc calls guarded only by a
  system `#include`.
- **EAP-method-table dispatch-contract FP extended to `struct eap_method`
  itself (not just eloop/vtable callbacks already documented above).**
  Every `sm`/`priv` DCL13-C hit across two full EAP server method files
  (`eap_server_identity.c`, `eap_server_md5.c`, 22 combined instances) is
  FP for the same reason as the eloop-callback entry: `init`/`initPickUp`/
  `reset`/`buildReq`/`check`/`process`/`isDone`/`isSuccess` are all
  fixed-signature fields of `struct eap_method` (`eap_i.h:24`), assigned
  by address (`eap->init = eap_identity_init;`), so their non-const
  `struct eap_sm *sm` / `void *priv` params cannot be changed
  independently of the shared typedef.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, same file): MEM31-C "not freed" on an
  object whose registration function's doc comment explicitly transfers
  ownership away from the caller regardless of return value.**
  `eap_server_{identity,md5}_register()` build `eap` via
  `eap_server_method_alloc()` then pass it to
  `eap_server_method_register()`, whose doc comment states "The caller
  must not free the allocated method data regardless of the return
  value" (`eap_server_methods.c:105-106`) — it frees `eap` itself on
  every rejection path and stores it on success. Extends the existing
  ownership-transfer-not-modeled theme to a documented,
  return-value-independent contract.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, same file): DCL30-C "returns pointer to
  local variable" — same heap-vs-automatic-storage confusion as the
  `comeback_token.c` entry, now on EAP-method `init`/`buildReq` return
  values.** `eap_identity_init`/`eap_md5_init` return `data` from
  `os_zalloc()`; `eap_identity_buildReq`/`eap_md5_buildReq` return `req`
  from `eap_msg_alloc()` (heap `wpabuf`). Neither is automatic storage.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, one file): FIO39-C misfires across two
  *different*, unrelated streams (`stderr` vs `stdin`) as if sequencing
  mattered — the rule only applies to reads/writes on the SAME stream
  without an intervening reposition.** `wpa_passphrase.c:54-55`:
  `fprintf(stderr, ...)` then `fgets(stdin, ...)`, and the reverse order
  a few lines later — no shared stream, no real hazard.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (1 instance, real if niche): EXP33-C
  "may be used uninitialized" correctly identifies a real gap masked by a
  correlated boolean guard that sqc doesn't model, but the surrounding
  code independently has a genuine uninitialized-read bug the audit
  flagged as an FN, not this finding — see FN notes.** `ctrl_echo` in
  `wpa_passphrase.c:60` is only read inside `if (!notty && ctrl_echo &&
  ...)`; `notty` and `ctrl_echo`'s initialization are correlated by
  construction (the only path that skips assigning `ctrl_echo` also sets
  `notty = true` via `goto`), so short-circuit `&&` on `!notty` always
  prevents the uninitialized read. FP for the exact variable/line cited,
  but see the FN entry for the real uninitialized-read bug one line up.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (1 instance): MSC04-C indirect-recursion misfire from
  name-similarity, not an actual call-graph edge.** `airtime_policy.c:96`
  claims `sta_set_airtime_weight -> hostapd_sta_set_airtime_weight ->
  sta_set_airtime_weight`, but `hostapd_sta_set_airtime_weight`
  (`ap_drv_ops.c:715`) only forwards to `hapd->driver->
  sta_set_airtime_weight()`, a driver function pointer — it never calls
  back into `sta_set_airtime_weight`. Looks like sqc's call-graph
  resolution confused the two similarly-named functions.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (1 instance): MSC13-C "dead assignment, never read"
  misses a read that only happens when the flagged assignment's
  short-circuit condition is FALSE.** `airtime_policy.c:100`,
  `sta_set_airtime_weight`: `int ret = 0;` then
  `if (weight != sta->airtime_weight && (ret = f(...))) return ret;`
  followed by `return ret;` at the end. When the `&&` LHS is false, `ret`
  keeps its initializer and IS read by the final `return ret;` — sqc
  doesn't see that the initializer survives the untaken-RHS branch.
- **Reconfirms at volume (not re-detailed): DCL13-C plain-internal-helper
  genuine-if-low-value TP (`airtime_policy.c` `iface`/`hapd`x2/`hapd`,
  `ap_mlme.c`'s `mlme_deletekeys_request`'s `sta`, 5 instances — none are
  vtable/callback-bound); DCL13-C `#ifdef FEATURE...#else` no-op-stub TP
  (`fst_ctrl_iface.h`'s `fst_ctrl_iface_mb_info` stub `buf`, 1 instance);
  DCL13-C aliased-mutation-through-a-local-pointer FP
  (`eapol_auth_dump.c:121`'s `buf`, written only via `pos`/`end` aliases,
  1 instance); API05-C ptr+size_t idiom (`fst_ctrl_iface.h`, 12
  instances); API02-C both category-error sub-shapes — flags the
  semantically-wrong last pointer param (`fst_read_next_int_param`'s
  `char **endp` out-param, not an array, 1 instance) and flags a pointer
  that already has its own paired size_t (`fst_read_next_text_param`'s
  `buf`+`buflen`, 1 instance); API00-C internal-only-API FP at volume
  (`eapol_auth_dump.c`, `ap_mlme.c`'s 5 MLME indication functions x
  hapd/sta/addr, `airtime_policy.c`'s `airtime_policy_new_sta`/
  `_update_deinit`, 15 instances — several (`ap_mlme.c`) even deref the
  "unvalidated" pointer unconditionally on the very next line, so no
  placement for a check would help); PRE08-C 8.3-legacy-filesystem FP
  (`eapol_auth_dump.c`'s `eapol_auth_sm.h`/`_sm_i.h`, `ap_mlme.c`'s
  `ieee802_11_defs.h`/`ieee802_11.h`, 2 instances); EXP30-C
  side-effect-free macro/pure-function-call FP (`eapol_auth_dump.c`'s
  `_SB()`+state-name lookup functions x6, `ap_mlme.c`'s `MAC2STR`+
  `mlme_auth_alg_str()` x1, 7 instances); ARR30-C NUL-terminated-string-
  traversal-isn't-unbounded FP (`wpa_passphrase.c:66`, 1 instance);
  CON33-C/CON34-C no-pthread FP (`browser-wpadebug.c`'s `strerror()`x2,
  4 instances); FIO23-C main()-return-flushes-stdout FP
  (`wpa_passphrase.c:28`, 1 instance); API00-C on `main()`'s `argv` FP
  (`wpa_passphrase.c:16`, 1 instance).
- **NEW, likely FP but graded case-by-case: STR34-C fires on a plain
  `*pos = '\0';` char-literal assignment — no promotion/comparison
  context at all, nothing to sign-extend.** `wpa_passphrase.c:68`.
- **NEW: PRE32-C misfires on an ordinary adjacent string-literal
  concatenation spanning multiple physical lines — no `#`-directive
  appears anywhere in the call.** `wpa_passphrase.c:25`,
  `printf("usage: ...\n" "\nIf passphrase is left out, ..." "stdin\n");`
  — sqc's parser appears confused by the multi-line literal, not an
  actual preprocessor directive inside a call.

### FN read-through note (`6-15_b10`)

- **`wpa_passphrase.c:58`, genuine EXP33-C-class bug sqc missed (not the
  same line/variable as the FP above).** When `tcgetattr()` fails with
  `errno == ENOTTY`, the code `goto read_pw` *without* having
  successfully populated `struct termios term` (declared uninitialized,
  never memset). After the `goto`, `term.c_lflag |= ECHO;` (line 58)
  unconditionally reads-then-writes the uninitialized `term.c_lflag`
  field. Low severity in practice — the corrupted `term` is only
  consumed by a `tcsetattr()` call gated on `!notty` (false on this
  path), so the read value is never acted on — but it is a real
  read-before-write of automatic storage. `upstream_present: "unknown"`
  (no separate upstream tracking checkout configured for this pinned
  clone).

### Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed (from `6-15_b10`)

  forwarded into a non-const `char *argv[]` slot for `execve()`

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b280`, 90 findings, `wpa_supplicant/config_winreg.c` + `src/eap_common/ikev2_common.c`, both entire files, 2026-08-08)

- **GENUINE FN, not previously documented: `wpa_config_read()`'s cfgp-ownership guard is missing in the Windows-registry backend.** The sibling `config_file.c:wpa_config_read()` always frees its local `config` with `if (config != cfgp) os_free(config)`/`wpa_config_free(config)` (`config_file.c:401,497`) so it never frees a caller-owned `struct wpa_config *cfgp` passed in by the caller. `config_winreg.c:wpa_config_read()` (`:449-501`) aliases `config = cfgp` when `cfgp` is non-NULL (`:461`) but then unconditionally calls `os_free(config)` on a `RegOpenKeyEx` failure (`:478`) and `wpa_config_free(config)` on a parse-error path (`:496`) with no `!= cfgp` check — freeing memory this backend doesn't own whenever an existing config struct is passed in. Closest CERT-C rule: MEM00-C (allocate/free at the same level of abstraction/ownership). sqc did not flag this (no MEM3x finding on these lines) — filed as an FN. Watch for the same missing-ownership-guard shape in any other backend implementing the `wpa_config_read(name, cfgp, ...)` contract.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances, one function): MEM30-C "use-after-free" conflates freeing a struct's member *fields* with freeing the struct pointer itself.** `ikev2_derive_sk_keys()` calls `ikev2_free_keys(keys)` (`:665`), which frees each of `keys->SK_d/SK_ai/SK_ar/SK_ei/SK_er/SK_pi/SK_pr` (separate heap sub-allocations) and NULLs them — it never frees `keys` itself, which remains a fully valid, caller-owned struct pointer. sqc's use-after-free checker nonetheless flags every subsequent `keys->SK_*_len = ...`/`keys->SK_integ_len` etc. access as "pointer arithmetic on freed pointer 'keys'"/"accessing member of freed pointer 'keys'" (`ikev2_common.c:671`x3,`672`x2). Same root shape as the standing goto/switch-arm CFG-conflation MEM30-C FP family, but here the conflation is field-free vs. container-free, not a control-flow-path merge. Watch for `free_all_fields(struct_ptr)`-style helpers (frees each member, never the struct itself) elsewhere in hostap followed immediately by struct-field writes.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, one function): MEM12-C "returns without releasing all resources" misfires when the cited resources were already freed earlier in the very same statement block, or are the function's intentional output.** `ikev2_derive_sk_keys()`'s two `return`s (`:744` after `ikev2_free_keys(keys)` at `:743`, and `:747` on success) both list `keybuf, keys->SK_d, ..., keys->SK_pr` as "leaked" — but `keybuf` was already `os_free()`'d at `:740` on both paths, and on the error path `ikev2_free_keys(keys)` on the immediately preceding line already frees every `keys->SK_*` field; on the success path those fields are the function's designed persistent output (derived session keys the caller is meant to keep and free later via `ikev2_free_keys`), not a leak at all. Distinct from the standing genuine-leak MEM12-C class — this is a lookahead-window-too-short / doesn't-understand-compute-and-store-functions miss.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): ARR36-C "pointers from different arrays" fires on two *different* wire-message sub-pointers (`encrypted`, `hdr`) that are provably offsets into the same underlying received-message buffer, extending the established param-name-vs-same-buffer ARR36-C FP family from same-function-derived pointers to two separate function parameters traced through the call graph.** `ikev2_decrypt_payload(..., const struct ikev2_hdr *hdr, const u8 *encrypted, ...)`'s `integ - (const u8 *) hdr` (`ikev2_common.c:495`) — verified via `src/eap_server/ikev2.c:456,498`: `hdr` and `pl->encrypted` (later passed as `encrypted`) both derive from the same `ikev2_parse_payloads()` call over one message buffer.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): ARR30-C's "explicit prior clamp not recognized" FP class, extended to a cross-function variable-name-collision sub-shape.** `config_winreg.c:345` ("Buffer 'data' with size 4096, allocated at line 68") is doubly wrong: the actual `data[1024]` local at that line (declared `:322`, in `wpa_config_read_network`) is guarded by an explicit clamp two lines above (`if (datalen>=1024) datalen=1023;`), and the *cited* allocation (`data[4096]` at `:68`) is an unrelated local in a completely different function (`wpa_config_read_blobs`) that merely shares the variable name `data`. The plain same-function clamp instances (`:341,418,684`, all `name[255]`) reconfirm the standard clamp-not-recognized class without the cross-function mislabeling wrinkle.
- **Reconfirms in this batch (not re-detailed above):** DCL31-C Win32 SDK unresolved-header class at high density (`Reg*` calls, ~14 instances, `config_winreg.c`); DCL37-C block-scope-local misclassified as file-scope (`_val:508`, `_name:531`, `_buf:604`); PRE00-C/PRE05-C/PRE12-C stringify-bare-field-name macro bundle on `config_winreg.c`'s own `STR(t)`/`INT(t)`/`INT_DEF(t,def)`/`INTe(t,m)`/`INT_DEFe(t,m,def)` family (9 instances, `:881-885`) — reconfirms the exact `41plus_b25`-derived precedent already on file at line 6670 for this file; EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref (`phdr:277,587`) and output-already-filled-before-read (`decrypted:522`, filled by the preceding successful `ikev2_encr_decrypt()` call); ARR36-C same-buffer-different-param-name (`pos`/`end:274,276,280`); INT14-C container/member conflation (`phdr`'s pointer arithmetic vs. the unrelated `phdr->flags` bitwise test at a different line, `:295`); EXP30-C pure-accessor-args (`wpabuf_head`/`wpabuf_mhead`/`wpabuf_len`, `:424,609`); DCL13-C plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP extended to crypto-key-struct getters (`keys` in `ikev2_derive_auth_data`/`ikev2_decrypt_payload`/`ikev2_build_encrypted`/`ikev2_keys_set`, 4 instances: `:388,446,547,631`, all pure reads of `keys->SK_*`); ## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b282`, 88 findings, `wpa_supplicant/mbo.c` + `wpa_supplicant/wmm_ac.c`, both entire files, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (now 3x+ across corpus, 4 instances this batch): INT14-C
  "bitwise op mixed with arithmetic" misattributes the bitwise operator to
  the wrong identifier in a member-access expression.** `(wpa_s->enable_oce
  & OCE_STA)` gets reported as both "'OCE_STA' used with bitwise and
  arithmetic" and "'wpa_s' used with bitwise and arithmetic" — but the `&`
  is actually on the *field* `wpa_s->enable_oce`, and neither `OCE_STA`
  (a plain constant, never used arithmetically anywhere in the function)
  nor `wpa_s` (a pointer, never a bitwise/arithmetic operand at all) is
  the real operand. `mbo.c:238,464`. Same failure mode already seen once
  in the corpus on `p2p.c`'s `capab >> flen*8` misattributed to `flen`
  (not yet promoted to a general pattern) — now confirmed recurring;
  treat any INT14-C hit on an identifier that is a struct/pointer name
  rather than the actual bit-flag field as FP by default, verify the
  named identifier is truly used both ways before trusting the finding.
- **NEW, batch-local: PRE00-C/PRE05-C/PRE12-C on a stringify-and-forward
  macro (`#define FOO(field, ...) helper(#field, obj->field, ...)`) are FP
  when every call site passes a bare struct-member identifier as `field`.**
  `wmm_ac.c:380`'s `PARAM_IN_RANGE(field, min, max)` expands to
  `param_in_range(#field, params->field, min, max)`. All three rules cite
  "evaluates parameter multiple times", but `#field` is compile-time
  stringification (no runtime evaluation at all) and `params->field` is
  evaluated exactly once — there is no double-evaluation hazard unless a
  caller passes an expression with side effects as `field`, which none do
  here (`tsid`, `user_priority`, etc. are always plain member names). Watch
  for this shape (macro combines `#param` with a direct use of `param`)
  elsewhere before crediting the multiple-evaluation framing.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b278`, 92 findings, `src/drivers/driver_wired_common.c` + `src/eap_peer/eap_pwd.c`, both entire files, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW, batch-local (1 instance, but a decisive category error worth flagging): MSC07-C misidentifies a switch `case` label immediately following an unconditional `break` as unreachable "code after unconditional break."** `case` labels are always reachable dispatch targets of the enclosing `switch`, independent of what precedes them in source order — `break;`-then-`case FOO:` is completely ordinary C, not a fallthrough or dead-code shape. `eap_pwd.c:424` (`case EAP_PWD_PREP_SSHA1:` ends with `break;` at :423, then `case EAP_PWD_PREP_SSHA256:` at :424 is flagged). Same root family as the established goto-target-label-blindness class, now confirmed on switch-case labels specifically rather than goto labels.
- **NEW, batch-local (2 instances, same shape): ARR36-C "pointer subtraction between pointers from different arrays" misattributes the operands to two variables that are neither the actual operands nor even both assigned yet at the flagged line.** `copy = os_zalloc(end - pos + 1)` / `os_memcpy(copy, pos, end - pos)` (`eap_pwd.c:148,151`) is reported as "between `phase1` and `copy`", but the real subtraction operands are `end` and `pos` — both derived from the same `phase1` string (`pos = os_strstr(phase1,...)`, `end = os_strchr(pos,' ')`) — and `copy` is the (still-unassigned-until-this-statement) *destination* of the allocation size computation, not an operand of the subtraction at all. A pure variable-attribution bug, not a judgment call.
- **Reconfirms/extends in this batch (not re-detailed above):** CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()` no-pthread FP at high density (10 instances, `driver_wired_common.c`, zero pthread usage in the file); FIO24-C double-close misfire across mutually-exclusive if-fails/else-succeeds branches (4 instances, exact `41plus_b159`-class precedent); API00-C internal-only-API FP extended to the wired-driver's own `struct wpa_driver_ops` getters (`wired_multicast_membership`'s `addr`, `driver_wired_get_ssid`/`_bssid`/`_capa`'s `ssid`/`bssid`/`capa`, `driver_wired_init_common`'s `ifname`, 5 instances); MSC37-C ifdef-branch-blind reach-end-without-returning, now on a `#ifdef __linux__ ... #else return -1; #endif` shape where literally every branch already returns (`wired_multicast_membership:140`); DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP extended to the `struct wpa_driver_ops` vtable itself (`get_ssid`/`get_bssid`/`get_capa`'s `priv`, verified via grep against `driver_wired.c`/`driver_macsec_{qca,linux}.c`'s `.get_ssid = driver_wired_get_ssid` etc., 3 instances) vs. a genuine plain-internal-helper TP on `driver_wired_deinit_common`'s `common` (never vtable-bound, never mutated, `:284`); ARR01-C `sizeof(*ptr)`/`sizeof(ptr->array_member)`-correct-idiom (`sizeof(*capa)`, `sizeof(common->ifname)`, 2 instances); DCL31-C third-party/system-header-unresolved class extended to POSIX `<net/if.h>`'s `if_nametoindex()` (2 instances, included at `driver_wired_common.c:18`); INT13-C "genuinely correct per rule text" TP-low class (not the wrong-type-detection FP class) on a truly-`int flags` local/param used repeatedly with `&`/`|` (8 instances, `driver_wired_common.c`) — same idiomatic-bitmask-selector precedent as `wpa_supplicant_set_suites`. On `eap_pwd.c`: EXP30-C pure-accessor-arg misfire extended to `eap_pwd_state_txt()` (`:86`) plus the assign-then-test-idiom sub-shape `(x = f()) == NULL` wrongly read as an unsequenced modify+access of the same object (`:113`); EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref (`:113`); EXP34-C same-function-guard-already-checks-non-null (`:118`); MEM12-C false leak on a field explicitly `bin_clear_free`'d one line before the enclosing `os_free()` (`:131`), on a return that transfers ownership to the caller (`:171`), and on a `goto fail` path whose target calls `eap_pwd_deinit()` which frees everything (`:174`) — interprocedural cleanup not tracked, 3 instances; MSC07-C goto-target-label-after-return blindness (`fail::172`); DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP extended per the AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS.md prior to `struct eap_method`'s `init`/`getKey`/`getSessionId`/`isKeyAvailable`/`get_emsk` (`sm`/`priv`, 9 instances) vs. plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP on `eap_pwd_perform_id_exchange`/`_commit_exchange`/`_confirm_exchange`'s `sm` (entirely unused in all three function bodies, 3 instances); API05-C ptr+size_t idiom (3 instances); DCL30-C heap-vs-automatic-storage confusion at volume (`data`/`key`x3/`id`, all `os_zalloc`/`os_memdup`/`os_malloc`, 6 instances); EXP05-C read-only cast-away-const overlay (`id`/`ptr`, the latter verified against `compute_keys()`'s `const u8 *confirm_server` parameter, 2 instances); MEM03-C "sensitive buffer not cleared" misapplied to a borrowed alias (`password`, aliasing `pwhashhash`/`salthashpwd` which ARE `forced_memzero`'d, or persistent `data->password`, `:363`); MSC17-C fallthrough misfire where the preceding case already has an explicit break one line above (`:461`); MSC13-C genuine (trivial) dead-store TP on a defensive `=0`/`=NULL` initializer never read before being overwritten (`order_len:699`, `resp:889`); MEM31-C ownership-transfer-via-return-value FP on an `eap_method.process()` return (`resp`, 4 instances) and ownership-transfer-to-registration-API FP (`eap`, passed to `eap_peer_method_register()`, `:1158`) plus a persistent-struct-field-lifecycle misunderstanding on `data->inbuf` (freed on 3 different dedicated paths the rule doesn't correlate against every intervening `return`, 3 instances, one of which — `:1017` — is freed literally 2 lines above the flagged return); ARR39-C pure-integer-sum-no-pointer misfire (`data->mtu - EAP_PWD_HDR_SIZE - sizeof(u16)`, a plain `size_t` computation with no pointer operand at all, `:1093`).

### FN read-through note (`41plus_b278`)

`driver_wired_common.c` clean (no FNs found). `eap_pwd.c`: one plausible but narrow session-scoped resource-growth issue — a peer-side EAP-pwd request with the fragmentation LENGTH bit set but MORE bit clear allocates `data->inbuf` (`:987`) without freeing it on that call (the dedicated free at `:1064` is gated on `in_frag_pos != 0`, which stays 0 in this shape); it persists until `eap_pwd_deinit()`, and a follow-up LENGTH-bit request while it's still set hits the `:981` "unexpected new fragment" guard and returns without freeing it either. Requires a malicious/buggy EAP server (peer method), not attacker-controlled in the usual sense; graded low-to-medium confidence FN, not re-flagged as a correction to sqc's (FP) `:987` MEM31-C finding.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b279`, 92 findings, `src/p2p/p2p_build.c` + `src/utils/os.h`, both entire files, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW, batch-local (1 instance): EXP37-C "variadic function declaration should use proper header" misfires on an ordinary custom variadic wrapper prototype.** `os_snprintf(char *str, size_t size, const char *format, ...)` (`os.h:494`) is flagged for lacking "proper header", but a variadic *declaration* (the trailing `...`) needs no header at all in C -- `<stdarg.h>` is only required inside the *definition* that consumes the args via `va_list`, which lives in the corresponding `.c` file, not this header. Watch for recurrence on other custom printf-style wrapper declarations (`wpa_printf`, `hostapd_logger`, etc.) before promoting to a confirmed category.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b277`, 94 findings, `wpa_supplicant/robust_av.c` (entire file) + `wpa_supplicant/wpa_gui-qt4/wpagui.h` (entire file, C++ Qt header), 2026-08-08)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): MEM30-C "double-free" misfires on `os_free(array)` for a heap array-of-structs whose element cleanup helper (`free_up_tclas_elem`) frees a *nested* per-element field (`elem->tclas_elems`/its own sub-buffers), not the array itself — sqc appears to conflate the helper's internal `os_free()` calls with a second free of the outer array pointer.** `wpas_scs_reconfigure`'s `os_free(desc_elems)` (`robust_av.c:723`) and `free_up_scs_desc`'s `os_free(desc_elems)` (`:837`) are each the *only* free of that specific pointer in their function; every call to `free_up_tclas_elem()` earlier in the same loop frees a different, per-element pointer (`desc_data->tclas_elems`, and beneath that `filter_value`/`filter_mask`), never `desc_elems` itself. Extends the existing array-vs-element double-free-misattribution family; watch for the same shape (`os_calloc`'d struct array + a `free_up_X`-style per-element helper called in a loop before the array's own final `os_free`) elsewhere.
- **NEW, batch-local (real, low-likelihood FN — not flagged by sqc): double-free / use-after-free on OOM in `populate_type10_classifier_data()` via shallow-copied `filter_value`/`filter_mask` pointers.** `robust_av.c:267-309`. The destination array (`dst`) starts as a byte-for-byte `os_memdup()` of the source array, so before any element is processed its `filter_value`/`filter_mask` fields are *raw aliases of the source's own allocations* (owned by `wpa_s->active_scs_ids`/`scs_robust_av_req`). The loop replaces each element's `filter_value`/`filter_mask` with fresh, independently-owned allocations one element at a time; if a later element's `os_memdup()` fails (`:293` or `:299`), the function returns `-1` immediately, leaving every *not-yet-processed* later element still holding the aliased source pointers. Both call sites (`wpas_scs_reconfigure:695`, `wpas_send_scs_req:772`) respond to that `-1` by calling `free_up_tclas_elem()` on the *entire* destination array, which will `os_free()` the aliased pointers on the unprocessed elements — freeing memory still owned and later re-freed by the original source list entry (double-free) or used after free. Narrow trigger (requires an `os_memdup()` OOM failure mid-loop with `num_tclas_elem > 1`), but a real defect on the error path. Closest CERT rule: MEM30-C/MEM31-C. `upstream_present: unknown` (no separate upstream tracking checkout available in this environment).
- **Reconfirms/extends in this batch (not re-detailed above):** DCL13-C split three ways — the eloop-timeout-handler dispatch-contract FP (`scs_request_timer`'s `timeout_ctx:537`, `wpas_wait_for_dscp_req_timer`'s `timeout_ctx:978`) vs. the "misses a mutation through an aliased local pointer" FP, now on a `struct dscp_policy_data *policy` param whose `type4_param = &policy->type4_param` alias is written through (`set_frame_classifier_type4_ipv4:1293`, `set_frame_classifier_type4_ipv6:1360`) vs. plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP on params never mutated at all (`wpas_populate_mscs_descriptor_ie`'s `robust_av:24`, `wpas_populate_type10_classifier`'s `type10_param:87`, `wpas_send_dscp_response`'s `resp_data:1782`) — contrast the aliased-mutation-miss FP with `populate_type10_classifier_data`'s `dst:268` (also FP, same aliased-mutation-miss shape via `t10_param = &dst->frame_classifier.type10_param`); MSC13-C dead-store split — genuine (if trivial) TP on scalar `=0`/`=NULL` locals unconditionally overwritten before their only read (`control_info:121`, `buf_len:469`, `_wpa_send_scs_req`'s `buf=NULL:577`, `wpas_send_scs_req`'s `desc_elem=NULL:732`, `wpas_send_dscp_response`'s `buf=NULL:1784`/`ret=-1:1786`, `wpas_send_dscp_query`'s `buf=NULL:1866`) plus a distinct genuine-TP sub-shape — the *last* `pos += res` in a `write_ipv4_info`/`write_ipv6_info`-style snprintf-accumulator chain, where the function returns based on `rem_len` alone and never reads `pos` again (`write_ipv4_info:1198`, `write_ipv6_info:1269`) — vs. the standing `dl_list_for_each`-loop-blindness FP (`scs_desc_found:1079`, read at the `if (!scs_desc_found)` check immediately after the loop the assignment sits in); ## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b268`, 110 findings, `src/tls/tlsv1_server.c` + `wpa_supplicant/bgscan_learn.c`, both entire files, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP extended to a 4th vtable family, `struct bgscan_ops` (`wpa_supplicant/bgscan.h:15-28`).** `bgscan_learn_notify_signal_change`'s `priv` param (`bgscan_learn.c:556`) matches the fixed `void (*notify_signal_change)(void *priv, int, int, int, int)` field signature shared by every `bgscan_*_ops` implementation (`bgscan_simple_ops`, `bgscan_learn_ops`) — not a free choice, same class as the standing eloop/eap_method/`wpa_auth_callbacks` dispatch-contract precedent. Watch `bgscan_simple.c` for the same shape on its `init`/`deinit`/`notify_scan` entries.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP34-C "passing null pointer which does not check for NULL" misapplied to `os_realloc_array(ptr, ...)` where `ptr` is a local initialized to `NULL` specifically so the first call behaves like `malloc()`.** `bgscan_learn_get_freqs`'s `freqs` (`:222`, `int *freqs = NULL` at `:215`) — `realloc(NULL, size)` is well-defined C (equivalent to `malloc(size)`), not a NULL-deref hazard; `os_realloc_array` is designed around this idiom. Watch for the same `X = NULL; ... os_realloc_array(X, ...)` growable-array shape elsewhere (`bgscan_learn_get_supp_freqs:356`, `bgscan_learn_get_probe_freq` share the identical idiom in this same file but weren't flagged this batch).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: ARR00-C "returning pointer to local array, dangling pointer" misapplied to a heap-backed scalar pointer variable (`int *`), not an actual local array — a rule-name variant of the standing DCL30-C heap-vs-local-storage confusion.** `bgscan_learn_get_freqs` returns `freqs` (`:224,231`), which is always either `NULL` or a pointer previously returned by `os_realloc_array()` (heap); ARR00-C's "local array...destroyed when function returns" framing doesn't apply to a heap pointer variable at all. Distinguish from the genuine ARR00-C class (real fixed-size local arrays).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): EXP33-C "used uninitialized"/"may be used uninitialized" both misapplied — one to a stack array used purely as a `memcpy()`/write-only destination (never read before the write), one to a block-scope pointer unconditionally assigned immediately after declaration before any read.** `bgscan_learn_notify_scan`'s `bssid[MAX_BSS*ETH_ALEN]` (`:507`, written via `os_memcpy(bssid+offset, ...)`, is a destination, not a read) and `bss` (`:517`, declared at `:517`, unconditionally assigned at `:522` via `bgscan_learn_get_bss()` before the first read at `:523` — no code path reads it earlier). Neither has a real uninitialized-use path.
- **NEW, batch-local (2 instances, one file, watch for 3x): FIO20-C "fgets() without truncation check" is a genuine (low-severity) TP on a local admin-config cache-file reader with no truncation/short-read detection anywhere in the loop.** `bgscan_learn_load`'s two `fgets(buf, sizeof(buf), f)` calls (`:117,125`) never check whether the read line was truncated (missing trailing `\n`); low real impact since a truncated line just fails its own literal-prefix/format match (`"wpa_supplicant-bgscan-learn\n"`, `"BSS "`, `"NEIGHBOR "`) rather than misparsing silently.
- **Reconfirms/extends in this batch (not re-detailed above):** DCL13-C plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP at the usual density (10 instances: `bssid_in_array`'s `array:52`, `in_array`'s `array:195`, `tlsv1_server_log`'s `conn:24`, `tlsv1_server_established`'s `conn:455`, `tlsv1_server_prf`'s `conn:473`, `tlsv1_server_get_cipher`'s `conn:528`, `tlsv1_server_resumed`'s wholly-unused `conn:633`, `tlsv1_server_get_keyblock_size`'s `conn:669`, `tlsv1_server_set_cipher_list`'s `ciphers:686`, `tlsv1_server_get_failed`/`_get_read_alerts`/`_get_write_alerts`'s `conn:738,744,750`, `bgscan_learn_get_supp_freqs`'s `wpa_s:353`, `bgscan_learn_bss_match`'s `data:469`, `bgscan_learn_notify_scan`'s `scan_res:487`) vs. the embedded-mutation-miss FP split (`tlsv1_server_derive_keys`'s `conn:56`, genuinely mutated via `conn->rl.*`/`conn->master_secret` writes; `tlsv1_server_decrypt`'s `out_data:262`, mutated via the aliased local `out_pos`) and the eloop-timeout-handler dispatch-contract FP (`bgscan_learn_timeout`'s `eloop_ctx:270`); API00-C internal-only-API FP at very high density (24 instances across both files — every `tlsv1_server_*`/`conn` getter/setter, `tlsv1_server_set_log_cb`'s `cb`);
