## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b272`, 103 findings, `src/eap_common/eap_eke_common.c` + `src/common/proc_coord.c`, both entire files, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances, one file): DCL13-C "embedded-mutation miss" extended to a session-struct-as-implicit-output-buffer shape.** `eap_eke_common.c` passes `sess->shared_secret`/`sess->ke`/`sess->ki`/`sess->ka` directly as the `res` output-buffer argument to `eap_eke_prf`/`eap_eke_prfplus` (`eap_eke_shared_secret:413`, `eap_eke_derive_ke_ki:466,468`, `eap_eke_derive_ka:509`) or `os_memset`s those same fields to 0 (`eap_eke_session_clean:724-727`) — in every case `sess` genuinely IS mutated, just through a member's address rather than `sess` itself, so DCL13-C's const-param suggestion on `sess` is FP (`:377,422,476,722`). By contrast, functions that only *read* `sess->prf`/`sess->encr`/`sess->mac`/`sess->ke`/`sess->ki`/`sess->ka`/`sess->shared_secret`/`sess->prf_len`/`sess->auth_len` and write their outputs to a separate caller-supplied param never touch `sess` at all and are genuine TPs (`eap_eke_derive_key:303`, `eap_eke_dhcomp:342`, `eap_eke_derive_msk:521`, `eap_eke_prot:583`, `eap_eke_decrypt_prot:637`, `eap_eke_auth:686`) — a clean 6-vs-6 split in one file. Same aliased-mutation-miss mechanism also fires on a plain (non-struct) pointer: `eap_eke_prot`'s `prot` param (`:585`) is written via a local alias `pos = prot;` throughout the function — FP for the identical reason.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): MEM05-C "VLA" misfire extends the established fixed-macro-array class to sum-of-macro-constants sizing.** `u8 buf[EAP_EKE_MAX_KE_LEN + EAP_EKE_MAX_KI_LEN]` (`:426`) and `u8 buf[EAP_MSK_LEN + EAP_EMSK_LEN]` (`:531`) are both compile-time-constant-sized (sum of two `#define`s), not variable-length at all — same wholesale misfire as the single-macro case, just with an addition in the size expression that doesn't change its compile-time-constant nature.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances across 2 functions): INT30-C unsigned wrap flagged on expressions already bounds-proven by an earlier guard in the *same* boolean expression or an immediately preceding modulo computation.** `eap_eke_prot`'s `pad = block_size - pad` (`:604`) is guarded by the enclosing `if (pad)` (pad was just computed as `data_len % block_size`, so it's in `[1, block_size-1]` when nonzero — no underflow). `eap_eke_decrypt_prot`'s `if (prot_len < 2*block_size + icv_len || (prot_len - icv_len) % block_size)` (`:656-657`) short-circuits before the subtraction whenever the size check would make it unsafe; every later reuse of `prot_len - block_size - icv_len` (`:661,668,673`) inherits that same proof. Same underlying mechanism as the already-confirmed `sha*-kdf.c` loop-invariant class, just via an `if`-guard/short-circuit instead of a loop invariant — extend that pattern's scope accordingly.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances, one file): EXP33-C "used uninitialized" misfires when a local buffer/struct is populated as an output parameter of a `recv`/`recvmsg`-family syscall, which sqc doesn't model as initialization.** `proc_coord.c`'s `tmp[20]` passed to `recv(sock, tmp, 0, MSG_PEEK|MSG_TRUNC)` (`:315`, len 0 — it's a pure output arg, nothing is read from it here); `struct sockaddr_un from` used only after `recvmsg()` populates it via `mh.msg_name` and the call's return value was checked (`:351`); `struct proc_coord_msg_header hdr` used only after `recvmsg()` populates it via `io[0]` and a `res < sizeof(hdr)` guard confirms full receipt (`:379`). All three are the same shape: kernel-populated-via-syscall-output-param, not a real read-before-write. Distinguish from a genuine, narrower issue found by FN read-through at the same `from`/`tmp` site — `sockaddr_un.sun_path`/local `tmp` buffers populated by a syscall are *bounded* by what the syscall wrote, but downstream code that doesn't respect that bound (see FN below) is a real bug the "used uninitialized" framing doesn't capture at all.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (1 instance, high-value FN): unchecked-length `os_memcpy` into a small fixed stack buffer from a peer-controlled `sockaddr_un.sun_path`, plus a missing NUL-terminator before `atoi()`.** `proc_coord.c:375` (`proc_coord_receive`): `os_memcpy(tmp, pos, end - pos)` into `char tmp[20]` — `end - pos` is the trailing filename component of the *sender's own bind address* (as received via `recvmsg`'s `msg_name`), bounded only by `UNIX_PATH_MAX` (~108 bytes), not by `sizeof(tmp)`. The only upstream check (`:361-362`) verifies the path is *prefixed* by `pc->dir`; it does not bound what follows the last `/`. A same-machine peer able to bind a Unix socket under that directory with a long name overflows this 20-byte stack buffer; even within bounds, `tmp` is never NUL-terminated before `atoi(tmp)` (`:376`), which is itself UB. None of this batch's own findings caught this (its own atoi() findings are graded TP for the unrelated "lacks error checking" reason, not for the missing bounds check feeding it).
- **Reconfirms (not re-detailed above, this batch):** API00-C internal-only-API FP at very high density (24 instances across `eap_eke_common.c`'s crypto-derivation functions + `proc_coord.c`'s `pc`/`dir`/`msg` params, the latter's `msg` also matching the documented-nullable-checked-downstream sub-shape); ENV01-C wholesale zero-`getenv()` misfire (9 instances, `eap_eke_common.c` only, zero `getenv()` calls in the file); DCL13-C eloop-timeout/eloop-sock-handler dispatch-contract FP (4 instances: `timeout_ctx:126,581`, `sock_ctx:300`) vs. genuine plain-helper low-value TP on non-callback params that are only ever compared, not mutated (`cb_ctx:148,727`, `peer:195`) and one fully-unused param (`pc:267`); DCL30-C heap-vs-automatic-storage confusion (5 instances: `peer:77,97`, `req:203`, `pc:668`, all `os_zalloc`/dl_list-element-backed); EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref (4 instances: `peer:89`, `pc:609`, `handler:715`, `req:789`); EXP34-C same-condition short-circuit guard miss (`first:173`) and while-loop-condition-already-guards (`de:553`); DCL39-C zeroed-struct-before-`sendmsg()` FP (`mh:249`, `os_memset`'d immediately before use); CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()`/`readdir()` no-pthread FP at very high density (16 instances, zero pthread usage in either file); POS02-C `bind()`-without-privilege-drop FP (`:641`, local AF_UNIX IPC socket); MSC07-C goto-target-label-after-return blindness (`fail::670`); MSC17-C fallthrough misfire where the preceding case already has an explicit `break` one line above (`:386`); EXP43-C same-pointer-input/output misfire on a plain (non-restrict) function with no aliasing hazard, pointer passed once as the primary object and once as an opaque callback `cb_ctx` (`:573`); INT10-C "signed modulo" factually wrong — operand (`ms`) is declared `unsigned int` (`:188`); ERR07-C/ERR34-C `atoi()` on peer-address/dirent-derived strings graded TP per the established literal-rule-text default (2 sites, 4 instances: `tmp:376`, `de->d_name:553`).

Populated from batch `1-5_b2` (95 findings across 24 files).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b266`, 111 findings, `wpa_supplicant/nan_supplicant.c` + `src/eap_peer/eap_teap.c`, both entire files, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (12 instances, one macro-shape reused twice): PRE00-C/PRE01-C/PRE05-C/PRE10-C/PRE12-C bundle misfires on `NAN_PARSE_INT(_str,_min,_max)`/`NAN_PARSE_BAND(_str)` — a config-field-name-substitution macro, not a value-expression macro.** `nan_supplicant.c:182,195` (`wpas_nan_set`): `_str` is used only as `#_str` (stringized for an error message) and `config->_str`/`config->_str.rssi_close` (an identifier substituted directly into a member-access chain) — never as a bare rvalue operand and never runtime-evaluated more than once in any side-effect sense (every call site passes a literal field name like `master_pref`). PRE00-C/PRE12-C ("evaluates multiple times") and PRE01-C ("not parenthesized") are FP for the same reason as the established `C2S`/`RSN_SUITE_ARG`/`__AKM` identifier-substitution family; PRE05-C is FP because `_str` is always a bare field name, never a macro needing pre-expansion before stringizing. PRE02-C is FP because the macro body is one complete, already-braced `if (...) { ...; return 0; }` statement — wrapping it in an outer set of parens is invalid C (same "if-statement macro" category error as `__AKM`/`for_each_link`). PRE10-C is also FP here, but for a *new* reason not yet in the registry: unlike the genuinely-multi-bare-statement macros that need `do-while(0)` to be safely nestable inside an `if` without braces, this macro's replacement is already a single self-contained braced `if` statement with no trailing `else` — wrapping an already-atomic statement in `do { } while(0)` adds nothing, there is no dangling-else or multi-statement hazard to guard against. Watch for this "config-field-name substitution macro, only ever `#x`/`->x`" shape recurring elsewhere in the config-parsing code (`ctrl_iface.c`, ap config setters) — likely a repeat of this exact bundle.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP43-C "called with same pointer for output/input" misfires on `tls_get_tls_unique(conn, buf, len)` where the two pointer arguments are unrelated objects (a TLS connection handle vs. a freshly `os_malloc`'d output buffer).** `eap_teap.c:667` — `data->ssl.conn` (opaque TLS library handle) and `data->session_id + 1` (this function's own output buffer) share no memory at all; the rule appears to fire on any 2-pointer-argument call to a `restrict`-eligible-looking function without actually checking whether the two pointers could alias. New callee (`tls_get_tls_unique`) for the established EXP43-C false-overlap family.
- **Reconfirms in this batch (not re-detailed above):** the eloop_timeout_handler DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP (`timeout_ctx`, `nan_supplicant.c:472`); the `struct eap_method` vtable DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP extended to `eap_teap_isKeyAvailable`/`getKey`/`getSessionId`/`get_emsk`'s `sm`/`priv` (8 instances: `:1542,1550,1568,1586`) vs. plain-internal-static-helper genuine-if-low-value TP on non-vtable helpers (`wpas_nan_ready`/`wpas_nan_update_conf`/`wpas_nan_de_rx_sdf`/`wpas_nan_usd_unpause_publish`/`wpas_nan_transmit`/`wpas_nan_usd_cancel_remain_on_channel_cb`/`wpas_nan_usd_all_freqs`'s `wpa_s`, `eap_teap_derive_key_auth`/`_add_identity_type`/`_process_eap_payload_tlv`/`_validate_crypto_binding`'s `sm`/`eap_payload_tlv`/`data`, and `eap_teap_process_start`'s entirely-unused `sm`, 12 instances total); ## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b263`, 113 findings, `wpa_supplicant/mesh_rsn.c` + `hostapd/main.c`, both entire files, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (8 instances, one function): sqc's use-after-free/type-checking engine gets badly confused by a triple-pointer out-param (`char ***if_names`), producing a cluster of MEM30-C/DCL30-C/STR34-C misfires that all share one root cause.** `hostapd_get_interface_names(char ***if_names, size_t *if_names_size, char *arg)` (`main.c:711-745`) reallocates `*if_names` via `os_realloc_array()` each loop iteration and frees it only in the `fail:` cleanup path — yet sqc flags essentially every read/write of `*if_names`/`(*if_names)[...]` throughout the *whole* function (both the normal-path realloc/assign/populate at `:723,727,729,730` and the cleanup-path first-ever frees at `:740,741`) as "use-after-free", as if a free earlier in the same call had already happened (it hadn't — MEM30-C fires before any free exists in the current call). The same confusion produces two STR34-C "char... assigned without cast to unsigned char" findings (`:727,742`) on `*if_names = nnames;` / `*if_names = NULL;` — both assign a `char **` value, not any flavor of `char`, a flat type misclassification. Also produces DCL30-C "returns/assigns pointer to local automatic-storage object" on `nnames` (`:727`), which is heap memory from `os_realloc_array()`, not automatic storage. Watch for this shape (any `T ***`/`T **` out-param reallocated+populated across loop iterations) recurring elsewhere — it's a plausible sqc engine bug worth a fix (ownership/free-state tracking loses precision through a double dereference), not just an isolated FP.
- **Reconfirms/extends in this batch (not re-detailed above):** DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP extended to two new fixed-signature families — the `wpa_auth_callbacks` vtable (`logger`/`get_psk`/`set_key`/`start_ampe`/`for_each_sta`'s `ctx`, `mesh_rsn.c:66,77,102,126,146`) and `hostapd_logger_cb_func`/eloop-signal-handler/`hostapd_for_each_interface`/`eloop_timeout_handler`/`wpa_msg_get_ifname_func` typedefs (`main.c:46,443,452,474,656,773,781`); DCL31-C function-pointer-parameter-call misfire (`cb(sta->wpa_sm, cb_ctx)` where `cb` is itself a callback parameter, not an undeclared function, `mesh_rsn.c:155`); ARR01-C `sizeof(ptr->fixed_array_member)` correct-idiom at very high density (13 instances, `sta->aek`/`sta->mgtk_rsc`/`sta->igtk_rsc`/`rsn->mgtk`/`rsn->igtk`/`sta->sae->pmk`) plus the `sizeof(*ptr)`-for-os_zalloc-sizing sub-shape (`sta->sae:387`); EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref (`mesh_rsn:257`, `ampe:564`); EXP34-C while-loop-condition-already-guards (`entry:281`); DCL30-C heap-vs-automatic-storage confusion (`mesh_rsn:296`, `iface:436`, `nnames:727` — the latter co-cited above); EXP05-C read-only-cast-away-const-overlay (`ie->conf->rsn_ie:291`, never mutated downstream) and cast-into-a-callee's-own-const-parameter (`(u8*)password` into `sae_prepare_commit`'s own `const u8*` param, `:365`); MEM03-C "sensitive buffer not cleared" misapplied to a borrowed alias of a persistent config field, not an owned local (`password` aliasing `ssid->sae_password`, `:343`); CON34-C/MSC30-C/MSC32-C `rand()`-quality/seeding FP-by-context extended to a 3rd shape — mesh auth-retry timeout jitter (`rand() %% MESH_AUTH_TIMEOUT`, `mesh_rsn.c:428`), alongside INT10-C's signed-modulo concern being moot since `rand()` never returns negative; MEM05-C fixed-macro-sized-array-not-a-VLA (`context[]` sized by `RSN_SELECTOR_LEN`/`ETH_ALEN`/`WPA_NONCE_LEN`, 2 instances); DCL22-C "should be volatile" misapplied to a plain pointer walked across ordinary (non-signal, non-async) function calls (`ptr:476`); ARR02-C's local-array-sized-only-by-its-own-initializer sub-shape, genuine-if-trivial TP (`aad[]`/`aad_len[]`, 4 instances: `:559,560,659,660`); MSC13-C genuine dead-store TP — `crypt = NULL`'s initial value is always overwritten by `os_zalloc()` before any `goto free` can read it (`mesh_rsn.c:657`); ARR39-C pure-integer-sum-no-pointer-operand misfire (`2 + len + AES_BLOCK_SIZE` passed to `wpabuf_put()`, `:633`); ARR36-C same-underlying-wire-buffer misidentified as cross-array (`ampe_buf - start`, both derived from the same parsed frame buffer, `:689`); API00-C internal-only-API FP at very high density (12 instances across both files) vs. one genuinely-unused-param DCL13-C TP (`mesh_rsn_get_pmkid`'s `rsn`, `:435`, never read or written at all); FIO23-C "main() returns without fclose(stdout)" misattributed to a `return;` inside `hostapd_logger_cb`, not `main()` at all (`:58`, distinct from the standard "main()-return-equals-exit()" FP — here the finding isn't even in the right function); EXP33-C false "uninitialized static" on `global`, a file-scope `static struct hapd_global global;` that's zero-initialized by C and explicitly `os_memset`'d again in `hostapd_global_init()` before any use (2 instances: `:216,531`); ARR00-C "uninitialized loop bound" misapplied to `debug`, an ordinary caller-supplied `int` parameter, on a loop that doesn't even index an array with it (`:422`); CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()` no-pthread FP (4 instances); PRE32-C/FIO30-C `#ifdef`-fragmented string-literal args inside `fprintf()` — CONFIRMED categorical FP, exact `usage()`-helper precedent (established for `wpa_supplicant/main.c`) now reconfirmed in `hostapd/main.c`'s own `usage()` (7 instances: `:600,601,613,614,622,640,644`) plus a variant with zero `#ifdef` at all, misattributed to the adjacent `show_version()` call (`:600,601`); ERR05-C "dictates error handling via exit()" misapplied to `main()`'s own top-level CLI `usage()` helper, not application-independent library code (`:652`); MSC17-C fallthrough misfire on `case` labels adjacent to `#ifdef`/`#endif` in a `getopt` switch, every flagged case has an explicit `break`/`goto`/terminating `exit()` (5 instances: `:900,908,919,933,945`); INT14-C container-vs-member conflation (`interfaces`/`i`, bitwise ops belong to unrelated struct members or don't exist at all, 2 instances: `:985,1029`); EXP34-C count-already-guards-the-pointer FP (`if_names:1025`, `bss_config:1044`, both only indexed when their paired size variable is nonzero) and `os_free(NULL)`-is-safe FP (`if_names:1139`); STR34-C plain-char-literal-assignment-no-widening (3 instances: `:687,1052`, plus the 2 type-misclassified `char**` instances co-cited above); FIO47-C `char[100]` array-decay misclassified as Integer (`buf:762`); MSC07-C goto-target-label-after-return blindness (`fail::738`); API00-C/STR31-C `main()`-argc/argv-guaranteed-valid FP bundle (`:815`).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b258`, 119 findings, `wpa_supplicant/main_winsvc.c` + `wpa_supplicant/ctrl_iface_named_pipe.c`, both entire files, Windows-only build, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances): MSC37-C "non-void function may/has no return statement" misfires on functions declared with Windows' `VOID` return-type typedef (an alias for `void` from `windef.h`, transitively included via `windows.h`).** sqc doesn't resolve the unresolved-external-header typedef, so it treats `static VOID WINAPI foo(...)` as returning a non-`void` type and demands a return value even though the function is genuinely `void` and has no `return <expr>;` anywhere. `ctrl_iface_named_pipe.c:254,345,688,764` (all `*_write_completed`/`*_read_completed` overlapped-I/O callbacks). Same root family as the already-documented "external Win32 header not parsed" DCL31-C class, now hitting a typedef's *resolved type* rather than a called function's existence.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): DCL36-C "conflicting linkage" fires on the bare token `WINAPI` itself, not a real declared identifier.** `WINAPI` is a calling-convention macro (`__stdcall`), textually repeated across many unrelated function declarations with different storage classes (`extern`-by-default prototypes vs. `static` definitions). sqc's parser appears to treat the macro token's position as if `WINAPI` were the identifier being (re)declared, comparing storage class across completely different functions. `ctrl_iface_named_pipe.c:89,96` (vs. the unrelated extern prototypes at `:23-24`).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances): DCL11-C/FIO47-C "format string expects N arguments but M provided" misfires when the format string is built via adjacent string-literal concatenation with a macro that expands to a conversion specifier (`#define TSTR "%s"` / `"%S"`).** sqc doesn't expand `TSTR` inside the literal-concatenation chain (`"Registering service: " TSTR "\n"`), so it evaluates the format string as containing zero `%`-conversions when there is actually exactly one, matching the one argument supplied. `main_winsvc.c:259,300` (`register_service`/`unregister_service`, both DCL11-C+FIO47-C pairs).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances, one file): DCL30-C "local variable 'X' assigned to global/static variable 'dst'" is factually wrong — `dst`/`next` are both plain function-local variables (or a formal parameter), never any global or static object anywhere in the file (verified by grep).** `ctrl_iface_named_pipe.c:127,521,572` (`ctrl_flush_broken_pipes`/`wpa_supplicant_ctrl_iface_send`/`global_open_pipe`, all local `dst`/`next` swap-and-advance idiom over a `while`/list loop). Likely confused by the sibling struct field name `priv->ctrl_dst`, which does share the `dst` substring.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances, one file): MEM30-C "use-after-free"/MSC07-C "unreachable code after return" cascade from goto-`fail:`-label CFG blindness, now specifically producing spurious use-after-free (not just the already-documented dead-code/label-blindness shape).** `ctrl_open_pipe()`/`global_open_pipe()` end with `return 0;` followed by a `fail:` label reached only via earlier `goto fail;` statements (on `CreateEvent`/`CreateNamedPipe` failure); sqc's CFG treats the `fail:` block's `ctrl_close_pipe(dst)` as executing *before* the normal-path code textually preceding the label (`dst->next = ...`, `:210,211,644,645`) and even flags the `fail:` block's own free call as "passing a freed pointer" (`:217,651`) — `dst` was never freed in this run at all on these lines. `ctrl_iface_named_pipe.c:210,211,216,217,644,645,650,651`.
- **DCL31-C Win32-SDK-API-unresolved class reconfirmed at very high density (both files, ~35 instances): every `Reg*`/`Service*`/`*NamedPipe*`/`Sleep`/`CreateEvent`/`Overlapped*` call declared only via `windows.h` transitively.** Matches and extends the established `l2_packet_ndis.c`/`preauth_test.c` Windows-SDK-header-unresolved precedent to the two dedicated Windows-service/named-pipe files.
- **PRE32-C phantom-directive class reconfirmed at very high density (main_winsvc.c, ~20 instances): every multi-line concatenated `printf()` string literal, zero actual `#if`/`#ifdef` tokens in any flagged call's argument list.**
- **EXP33-C `sizeof(*uninitialized_ptr)` non-evaluated-context class reconfirmed (4 instances: `ctrl_open_pipe:138`, `global_open_pipe:582`, `wpa_supplicant_ctrl_iface_init:441`, `wpa_supplicant_global_ctrl_iface_init:811`).**
- **EXP33-C output-param-not-a-read class extended to Win32 `RegQueryValueEx(..., (LPBYTE)&dest, &buflen)` out-params (5 instances: `main_winsvc.c:83,94,105,116,158`).**
- **EXP33-C "static variable used without explicit initialization" — CONFIRMED FP, extends the existing zero-init-guarantee class from file-scope pointers (`ctrl_conn`) to file-scope `HANDLE`/`SERVICE_STATUS_HANDLE` scalars.** `main_winsvc.c:245,351,355` (`svc_status_handle`, `kill_svc`) — static storage duration + no initializer is C-standard-guaranteed zero, not UB.
- **ARR30-C "index N out of bounds" misfire when an explicit prior clamp already caps the index — CONFIRMED, extends the established "explicit-prior-bounds-check-not-recognized" class.** `main_winsvc.c:219`: `if (namelen >= 255) namelen = 255 - 1;` two lines above `name[namelen] = '\0';` guarantees `namelen <= 254` into a 255-element array.
- **DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP extended to two new fixed Windows/internal callback typedefs beyond eloop/sqlite/ap_for_each_sta: the `LPSERVICE_MAIN_FUNCTION` signature registered via `SERVICE_TABLE_ENTRY`/`StartServiceCtrlDispatcher` (`service_start`'s `argv`, `main_winsvc.c:362`), and hostap's own cross-file `wpa_msg_cb_func` message-callback typedef (`wpa_supplicant_ctrl_iface_msg_cb`'s `ctx`, `ctrl_iface_named_pipe.c:425`) — both pinned, non-const-able signatures.**
- **DCL37-C reserved-identifier-forced-by-platform-header judgment call — extends the `_LINUX_TYPES_H` precedent to Windows.** `_WIN32_WINNT` (`ctrl_iface_named_pipe.c:36`) is underscore+uppercase (always reserved per C 7.1.3) but is the standard, unavoidable Windows-SDK idiom for setting the target API version; graded TP(low) per rule text, matching the kernel-header-guard precedent rather than the DCL40-C "not practically actionable" FP convention.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b256`, 61 findings, `src/utils/xml-utils.c`, entire file, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances, one file): MEM31-C "not freed"/"leak" misfires on an `xml_node_create()` result that is attached as a child of an existing tree node.** `xml_node_create(ctx, parent, ns, name)` is implemented via libxml2's `xmlNewChild((xmlNodePtr) parent, ...)` (`xml_libxml2.c:119-126`), which links the new node into `parent`'s child list — ownership belongs to the tree/document from that point on, and it is freed transitively whenever the tree's root is passed to `xml_node_free()`. sqc treats every `xml_node_create()` return value as an independent heap allocation the *current* function must free, missing that attachment-as-a-child *is* the release mechanism. `node_to_tnds`'s `tnds` (`:240`, child of `out`), `add_ddfname`'s `node`x2 (`:266,269`, chained parent/child), `mo_to_tnds`'s `node` (`:292`, child of `root`, eventually freed by the caller via `xml_node_free(ctx, root)` or on the `fail:` path at `:304`). Extends the established ownership-transfer-to-a-data-structure MEM31-C FP family (previously documented for list/queue insertion) to tree-append via a wrapped 3rd-party XML library call — check whether a "create" helper's first argument is a *parent* node before accepting a bare MEM31-C leak claim on its result.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances, one function): MEM31-C "double free" misfires by conflating separate, mutually-exclusive early-return branches that each free the same local variable exactly once.** `add_mo_node`'s `nodename`/`value` are freed once in the `uri == NULL` branch (`:355-356`), once (independently) in the `parent == NULL` branch (`:366-367`), and once more on the normal success-fallthrough path (`:377-378`) — three disjoint control-flow paths, never more than one `xml_node_get_text_free()` call per path, yet sqc reports every call past the first lexical occurrence as re-freeing an already-freed `ctx`. Note the finding's own message is doubly wrong — it names the freed variable as `'ctx'` (the unrelated `struct xml_node_ctx *` parameter) rather than `nodename`/`value`, the actual arguments. Extends the existing "double free across mutually-exclusive branches" family (previously seen on single-branch-pairs) to a 3-branch fan-out, and reconfirms the "message identifier doesn't match the flagged line" sub-defect independently noted for ARR36-C.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, one file): ARR30-C "unbounded while loop with pointer increment" misfires on a `while (*pos) { ...; pos++; }` scan that is provably bounded by an explicit NUL terminator planted just before the loop.** `node_from_file`'s DOCTYPE-brace-counting scan (`:144`, `buf[len] = '\0'` set at `:138`) and `get_val`'s whitespace-skip scan (`:200`, over `xml_node_get_text()`'s NUL-terminated string) — both terminate on `*pos == '\0'`, not unboundedly. Reconfirms the standing "NUL-terminated-string-traversal-isn't-unbounded" ARR30-C FP class with a file-read/DOCTYPE-strip variant.
- **NEW: get_val() (`:192-207`) is a genuine MEM31-C memory leak sqc MISSED.** `val = xml_node_get_text(ctx, node)` heap-allocates via libxml2's `xmlNodeGetContent()`; the whitespace-skip loop returns `val` early only if a non-whitespace byte is found, otherwise falls through to `return NULL;` (`:206`) with **no** `xml_node_get_text_free(ctx, val)` call on that path — every all-whitespace (or empty) XML text node leaks. Triggered by ordinary pretty-printed/indented MO or PPS XML (a whitespace-only text node between sibling elements is common). Filed as an FN.
- Reconfirms in this batch (not re-detailed above): DCL13-C plain-internal-static-helper genuine-if-low-value TP (`get_node_uri_iter`'s `root`, `:16`, unmodified but blocked from being made const only by the downstream traversal API's non-const signatures, judged per the standing default rather than a new exception); DCL30-C heap/library-tree-object-vs-local-storage confusion at very high density (10 instances: `:42,59,85,102,116,165,202,223,301,320`, every one a pointer walked from/created by the `xml_node_*` tree API, never actual stack storage); API00-C internal-only-API FP at volume (18 instances across `get_node_uri`/`get_node`/`get_child_node`/`node_from_file`/`node_to_file`/`mo_to_tnds`/`tnds_to_mo`, all verified against the sole external caller `hs20/client/osu_client.c`, which NULL-checks every tree pointer before passing it in) plus one instance where the flagged param is a *documented*-nullable pass-through (`mo_to_tnds`'s `ns_uri`, called with a literal `NULL` at its one real call site and only ever forwarded to `xml_node_create_root()`, never dereferenced, `:277`); STR34-C char-to-char literal-assignment FP (`*end++ = '\0'`/`*pos++ = '\0'`, 2 instances: `:24,72`); MSC01-C no-final-else deliberate-guard-clause pedantry (`:147`); MEM10-C ad-hoc-NULL-check stylistic pedantry (6 instances: `:215,331,348,354,411`); PRE32-C phantom-directive misfire on a plain multi-line-string-literal `printf()` with zero preprocessor tokens (2 instances, `:401`); MSC07-C goto-target-label-after-return (`fail:`, `:303`, reached from `:294`); ## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b264`, 112 findings, `src/ap/pmksa_cache_auth.c` + `src/crypto/crypto_nettle.c`, both entire files, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): FIO50-C "output follows input without a positioning call" fires on a plain non-FILE* local variable purely because it's named `tmp` — no `fopen`/`fread`/`fwrite`/stdio call exists anywhere in the function.** `crypto_nettle.c`'s `des_encrypt`: `u8 pkey[8], next, tmp;` (`:32`), `tmp = key[i];` (`:38`) flagged at `:40`. Pure name-collision misfire; there is no file stream in this function at all. Watch for this on any local/param named `tmp`/`fp`/`stream`/`f` in a non-I/O function.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (48 instances, one file): DCL31-C third-party-header-unresolved FP class (established for OpenSSL/libdbus/LibTomCrypt/curl/GTK/Windows-SDK/POSIX) extends to libnettle (`<nettle/des.h>`, `<nettle/aes.h>`, `<nettle/arcfour.h>`) and, transitively through `<nettle/bignum.h>`, to GNU GMP's `mpz_*` API.** Every `nettle_des_*`/`nettle_aes_*`/`nettle_arcfour_*` and `mpz_init(s)/mpz_import/mpz_cmp_d/mpz_powm/mpz_clear(s)/mpz_sizeinbase/mpz_export` call in `crypto_nettle.c` is declared only in these system/third-party headers, unresolved by sqc's parser. Same root cause, two more libraries.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (9 instances): EXP33-C "used uninitialized" misfires on a GMP `mpz_t` local passed to its own `mpz_init`/`mpz_inits` call — the call IS the initialization, not a use-before-init.** `mpz_t pub; ... mpz_init(pub);` (`:339,347`) and `mpz_t p, q, tmp; ... mpz_inits(p, q, tmp, NULL);` (`:353,357` x3) and `mpz_t bn_base, bn_exp, bn_modulus, bn_result; ... mpz_inits(...)` (`:380,384` x4) in `crypto_nettle.c` — sqc doesn't know `mpz_init*` are GMP's opaque-type initializers (system-header-declared, same root cause as the DCL31-C class above) and treats the argument as read rather than written. Extends the established "output-param sqc doesn't recognize" family to system-library init calls specifically.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM30-C "use-after-free: returning freed pointer" conflates two sibling arms of the same `switch` as if they were one control-flow path.** `crypto_cipher_init` (`crypto_nettle.c:411-433`): the `case CRYPTO_CIPHER_ALG_RC4:` arm sets up the cipher and falls through to `return ctx;` (`:432`) without ever freeing `ctx`; only the unrelated `default:` arm (`:428-429`) does `os_free(ctx); return NULL;`. sqc's use-after-free checker appears to have merged the free from the `default:` arm onto the unconnected success-path `return ctx` in the same function. Worth a sqc CFG fix — this is a switch-arm-conflation bug, not the already-documented goto/loop-CFG-blindness families.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): MEM33-C "direct assignment of flexible array structure instances... use memcpy()" misfires on a plain fixed-size-array struct member, not an actual flexible array member (`type name[]`/`name[0]` trailing declarator).** `struct vlan_description` (`src/ap/vlan.h:14-18`) has `int tagged[MAX_NUM_TAGGED_VLAN]` — a normal fixed-size array field, not a FAM — so whole-struct assignment `*entry->vlan_desc = *vlan_desc;` (`pmksa_cache_auth.c:174,434`) is perfectly safe, ordinary C. Check the struct definition for an actual trailing `[]`/`[0]` member before accepting a MEM33-C verdict.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL13-C "not modified, should be const" on a `char *buf, size_t len` output-buffer param misses the const-breaking mutation when the function writes through an aliased local pointer initialized from `buf` (`pos = buf;` then `pos += os_snprintf(...)`), not through `buf` itself.** `pmksa_cache_auth_list_mesh`'s `buf` (`pmksa_cache_auth.c:711`) — adding `const` would make `pos = buf;` a compile error since `pos` is later written through. Same root cause as the previously-confirmed `eap_sim_db.c` aliased-mutation-miss sub-shape, now on an output buffer rather than a parse cursor.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances): ERR02-C "sprintf return value not checked" misfires on `wpa_snprintf_hex()`, which is not `sprintf`/`snprintf` at all and never returns a negative/error value to check** (`pmksa_cache_auth.c:680,737,745`) — exact same root cause as the previously-confirmed `eap_sim_db.c` `wpa_snprintf_hex()` FP, now reconfirmed 3x more in a different file (3rd+ occurrence, promoting from batch-local).
- Reconfirms in this batch (not re-detailed above): DCL13-C eloop-timeout-handler dispatch-contract FP (`pmksa_cache_expire`'s `timeout_ctx:112`); DCL13-C plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP (6 instances: `pmksa` in 3 read-only accessors `:492,528,664,710`, `entry`/`attr` in `das_attr_match:583,584`); API00-C internal-only-API FP at very high density (36 instances across both files: cache/context/pointer params and unchecked-arithmetic `len`/`prime_len` params, all traced to fixed-size internal callers); API05-C `T*ptr,size_t len` idiom FP (4 instances: `:664,665,711` x2, the `665`/scalar-`int *index` sub-shape extending the established "misfires on a scalar out-param with no array/bound semantics" family); MEM10-C ad-hoc-NULL-check pedantry (4 instances: `:149,377,455`); EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref at very high density (13 instances across both files, on `entry`/`pmksa`/`ctx` immediately before/at their `os_zalloc`/`os_malloc` assignment); DCL30-C heap-vs-automatic-storage confusion (12 instances across both files: `entry`/`pmksa`/`ctx` returned, all `os_zalloc`/`os_malloc`-backed, including cache-list-traversal returns that aren't even freshly allocated in the returning function — `pmksa_cache_auth_get`/`pmksa_cache_get_okc`'s `entry:503,509,540,555`); ARR01-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-correct-idiom (3 instances: `:48,468`); INT14-C misfire on a loop counter also used as a shift amount (`i` in `tmp >> i` plus `i++`, `crypto_nettle.c:39` — routine parity-bit-computation idiom, not a real mixed-role hazard, batch-local for now).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b245`, 65 findings, `src/eap_server/tncs.c`, entire file, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances, one file): ARR36-C "pointer comparison between pointers from different arrays" fires purely on distinct *parameter names* even when both parameters demonstrably alias into the very same caller-owned buffer.** `tncs_parse_imv(int id, char *start, char *end, int *error)` derives `pos`/`pos2` from `start` and compares them against `end` (`:988,990,1001`) — but `start`/`end` are themselves just `pos+4`/`line_end` from `tncs_read_config`'s single `config` buffer (`os_readfile()`), so every comparison is within one array. A 4th instance (`:1036`) even mislabels *which* variables it's comparing (`'pos' and 'config'` in the message vs. the actual `line_end < end` on that line) while still resolving to the same root cause. Extends the existing param-vs-param ARR36-C false-array-boundary class (previously only noted for genuinely-separate objects) to the common C idiom of a callee re-deriving/renaming pointers from a caller's single backing array.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable" misfires on a returned *value* that is not itself a pointer into automatic storage at all** — `tncs_get_sym()`'s `fptr = dlsym(handle, func); return fptr;` (`:329`). `fptr` is a scalar local holding a `dlsym()`-resolved code address; returning it is definitionally safe (it's a value copy, and the address itself is process-lifetime valid). Distinct from — but adjacent to — the established DCL30-C heap/persistent-storage-vs-automatic-storage confusion family; this sub-case doesn't even involve heap/list storage, just a plain returned-by-value pointer scalar.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM30-C "stack pointer escape... local array/VLA assigned to global" misfires on a heap pointer (`os_zalloc()`) being linked into a global list.** `tncs_init()`'s `tncs_global_data->connections = tncs;` (`:1075`) — `tncs` is heap-allocated, never a stack array or VLA. Same root confusion as the standing DCL30-C heap-vs-automatic-storage class, now observed on MEM30-C's stack-escape checker instead.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM31-C false "double free" across two sibling loops sharing one function-scope variable name, where the second loop explicitly resets the pointer to NULL before reuse.** `tncs_process_if_tnccs()` declares `unsigned char *decoded` once at function scope; loop 1 (IMC-IMV-Message) frees it each iteration and reassigns via `tncs_get_base64()` at the top of the next; loop 2 (TNCC-TNCS-Message) explicitly sets `decoded = NULL;` (`:907`) before conditionally reassigning and freeing it (`:934`) — there is only ever one `os_free()` per assignment. Extends the established MEM31-C free-then-NULL-reset-then-goto-fail FP family to the reused-variable-name-across-sibling-loops shape.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP (previously only documented for eloop timeout/socket callbacks and sqlite3 callbacks) extends to TNC IF-IMV interface functions bound via a `TNC_TNCS_BindFunction`-style name-resolution table** — `TNC_TNCS_GetAttribute`'s `pOutValueLength` (`:267`) is a fixed-signature IF-IMV spec function looked up by name and returned as a function pointer to external IMV shared-library code; its signature cannot be changed independent of the spec, regardless of whether this stub body happens to use every parameter.

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): EXP36-C alignment-1-to-4 cast graded FP when the destination struct is `STRUCT_PACKED`, refining the existing "check the cast's destination type's actual alignment" disposition (`41plus_b?` NDIS/`u8*` precedents) to compiler-packed structs specifically.** `(struct eap_hdr *) in_data` (`:731,857`) — `struct eap_hdr` (`eap_defs.h:18-23`) is declared `STRUCT_PACKED` (`u8 code; u8 identifier; be16 length;`), which forces byte alignment on every member; there is no real alignment requirement on the destination type at all, unlike an ordinary (non-packed) multi-field struct.   "minimal scope" misfire on file-scope `const` tables that ARE declared

  `hdr->identifier`/`hdr->class`).
- **NEW: FLP02-C "floating-point equality" misfires on a plain integer
  bitmask comparison with zero floating-point types involved anywhere in
  the expression — a new, cruder failure mode than the previously-confirmed
  epsilon-pedantry FLP02-C FPs (which at least involve real floats).**
  `asn1_get_next:188`, `(hdr->identifier & 0x1f) == 0x1f)` — `hdr->identifier`
  is `u8`. FP.
- **NEW: INT13-C "bitwise op on signed operand" misattributes a variable
  that only appears in a ternary *condition* next to a bitwise operator, not
  as an actual operand of it.** `asn1_put_oid:563`,
  `bytes[idx] = (idx ? 0x80 : 0x00) | (val & 0x7f);` — `idx` is the ternary
  condition; the `|` operates on the ternary's *result* and
  `(val & 0x7f)`, never on `idx` itself. FP.
- **NEW: EXP33-C "used uninitialized" misfires across an interprocedural
  out-param initialization chain sqc doesn't track — a struct local is
  filled by a callee-of-a-callee's `os_memset`, not directly in the
  caller.** `asn1_get_alg_id`'s `hdr` (`:492`) is declared uninitialized,
  then `asn1_get_sequence(pos, end-pos, &hdr, next)` (which itself calls
  `asn1_get_next(buf,len,hdr)`, whose first statement is
  `os_memset(hdr, 0, sizeof(*hdr))`) fully populates it before the
  short-circuit `||` reaches `hdr.payload`/`hdr.length` on success. FP.
- **NEW: DCL30-C "assigns pointer to local storage" misfires on a pointer
  that is an offset into the caller-owned *input* buffer, not any kind of
  local/automatic storage — a third DCL30-C sub-shape beyond
  heap-vs-local-storage and passthrough-parameter.** `asn1_get_alg_id`'s
  `*params = pos;` (`:496`) — `pos` traces back to the function's own `buf`
  parameter (the original externally-supplied DER bytes), which outlives
  the function call; nothing stack-allocated is involved. FP.
- Reconfirms/extends in this batch (not re-detailed above): ARR01-C
  `sizeof(*ptr)`/`sizeof(ptr->member)`-not-a-decayed-array idiom (4
  instances: `:176,212,296` plus the header-table pairing already covered);
  API00-C internal-only-API FP at volume (`hdr:171` len-overflow,
  `buf/len:290`, `buf:391`, `buf/params_len/len:480`x3 — one of which,
  `params_len`, is additionally guarded by `if (params && params_len)` so
  doubly FP —, `val:604`); API05-C ptr+size_t idiom (`:351,433`); EXP40-C
  neither-side-const phantom cast (`:353`); MEM31-C ownership-transfer-to-
  callee FP (`buf:627`, freed inside `asn1_encaps` via
  `wpabuf_clear_free`); DCL30-C heap-vs-local-pointer-variable confusion
  (`res:649`, holds a `wpabuf_alloc` heap object); EXP33-C array-fully-
  written-on-every-path FP (`bytes:559`, both the loop-fill and the
  idx==0 fallback branch write index 0 before any read); DCL13-C genuine
  low-value plain-helper TP (`hdr:106`, read-only through pointer);
  INT14-C genuine (if low-severity) TP where the SAME variable really is
  used with bitwise (`<<`,`|`) in one place and arithmetic (`/`,`-`,`*`) in
  another, not a misattribution (`val:308`, OID first-component split).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b244`, 65 findings, `src/ap/acs.c`, entire file, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances, one file): ARR02-C "implicit array bounds" extends the existing sizeof/ARRAY_SIZE-consumed-array FP family to sentinel-terminated arrays and designated-initializer-sized arrays with no `sizeof()` involved at all.** `bw_40[]`/`bw_80[]`/`bw_160[]`/`bw_320_1[]`/`bw_320_2[]` (`:260,277,287,293,297`) are each terminated by a `{ -1, -1, -1 }` sentinel and traversed with `while (bw_desc[bw][i].first != -1)` — no consumer anywhere assumes a hardcoded literal size, so the mismatch risk ARR02-C targets can't materialize. `bw_desc[]` (`:301`) is a `static const struct bw_item *bw_desc[]` sized purely by its designated initializers (`[ACS_BW40] = bw_40, ...`) keyed to the `enum bw_type` count — same no-mismatch-possible reasoning. Also extends to a local (not just file-scope) array: `bw320_str[]` (`:795`), a 3-literal `const char *` array indexed only by `conf_bw320_offset`, which an immediately-preceding `switch` constrains to exactly `{0,1,2}`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): MSC13-C "dead store" misfires on `dl_list_for_each`-loop init values whose only read happens on the zero-iterations path, extending the goto/loop CFG-blindness family to loop-count uncertainty.** `acs_survey_list_is_sufficient`'s `ret = -1` (`:503`) IS read at the post-loop `if (ret == -1)` check when the survey list is empty (loop body never executes) — sqc's flow analysis apparently assumes the loop body always runs at least once, missing this path. The following `ret = 1` (`:508`, set right before `break`) is likewise read later at the `if (!ret)`/`return ret` — also flagged dead, same root cause. Contrast with the genuine dead-store class (`int_factor:408`, `adj_chan:745,835`, `chan2:836` in the same file) where the initializer truly is unconditionally overwritten before any read on every path — always trace whether a loop can execute zero times before accepting a dead-store verdict on its pre-loop initializer.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances): DCL30-C "returns/assigns pointer to local automatic-storage object" extends the established local-variable-vs-local-storage confusion to pointers into a persistent heap-backed array element (`&mode->channels[i]`), not just single heap allocations.** `acs_find_chan_mode`/`acs_find_chan` (`:658,697`) return a local pointer *variable* `chan` that holds the address of an element inside `mode->channels` — a `struct hostapd_channel_data *channels` array member of the long-lived `hostapd_hw_modes` struct (part of `iface->hw_features[]`), never a stack array. Extends further to output-param writes (`*ideal_chan = chan`/`*rand_chan = chan`, `:1057,1071`) and to `acs_find_ideal_chan`'s own `ideal_chan`/`rand_chan` locals returned at `:1150,1153` — all ultimately trace back to the same persistent-array-element address, never anything stack-allocated.
- **Reconfirms in this batch (not re-detailed above):** the eloop-timeout-handler DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP (`acs_scan_retry`'s `user_data`, `:1508`); DCL13-C plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP at high density (`mode`/`survey`/`iface`/`chan` params across static helpers that only read through a pointer-typed struct member — e.g. `mode->channels`, `iface->conf` — so const-qualifying the outer param would still compile; ~15 instances) vs. a genuine miss where the rule doesn't see a through-pointer write (`acs_request_scan_add_freqs`'s `freq`, `*freq++ = chan->freq`, `:1396`); API00-C internal-only-API FP (`acs_cleanup`'s `iface`, `:349`, all callers in `acs.c`/`hostapd.c` pass always-valid pointers); EXP34-C internal-invariant-non-null on `chan` (3 instances: `:561,576,587`, always `&mode->channels[i]` or a pre-null-checked local) and a guarded-by-earlier-check instance (`freq:1456`, set from `os_calloc()` immediately after its own NULL check); INT14-C container-vs-member misattribution (`survey:376`, bitwise on `survey->filled`, arithmetic on other members); EXP40-C phantom cast-away-const where neither side is const (`:745`); the MSC01-C no-final-else deliberate-prior-value-preserved/already-defaulted family (3 instances: `:813,1031,1174`); MSC07-C goto-label-blindness (`fail::1388`); EXP43-C misfiring on all-integer `wpa_printf` calls with zero pointer arguments to overlap (2 instances: `:1465,1469`); CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()` no-pthread FP (`:1489`); EXP33-C "may be used uninitialized" missing an unconditional pre-read assignment (`bias:851`, set `NULL` at `:1023` before its only read at `:1038`).
- **NEW, batch-local (not yet 3x confirmed elsewhere): unchecked `pow()` calls with a constant positive base (10, 2) split by sub-finding.** FLP32-C/ERR01-C (domain/range-error-unchecked) graded genuine low-confidence/low-severity TP — domain error is impossible (base always positive) but a range/overflow error is theoretically reachable if a driver-reported `s8 nf`/`min_nf` noise-floor value is near its type extremes (`acs_survey_interference_factor`, `:393,395,396`, 7 instances total). FLP03-C ("division without error checking") on the same lines is FP — every flagged division's denominator is a hardcoded nonzero literal (`5.0L`/`10.0L`), not a runtime value. FLP07-C ("assigned without explicit cast") is FP both times — `:393` is a `double`→`long double` *widening* conversion via usual arithmetic conversions (never loses precision, not the narrowing risk the rule targets) and `:427` has no conversion at all (`acs_survey_interference_factor` already returns `long double`, assigned to a `long double` variable). INT33-C ("division by X without checking zero") at `:394` is FP — guarded in the same expression, `(total ? (busy / total) : 0)`.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b235`, 71 findings, `src/common/wpa_ctrl.c`, entire file, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW: `wpa_ctrl_close()` NULL-handling is genuinely inconsistent across the
  file's platform backends — real TP, not the usual internal-only-API FP.**
  The `CONFIG_CTRL_IFACE_UNIX` variant (`:247-255`) explicitly checks
  `if (ctrl == NULL) return;` before touching `ctrl->s`, matching the common
  `free()`-tolerates-NULL idiom callers reasonably expect from a `_close()`.
  The `CONFIG_CTRL_IFACE_UDP` (`:468-475`) and `CONFIG_CTRL_IFACE_NAMED_PIPE`
  (`:724-728`) variants unconditionally dereference `ctrl->s`/`ctrl->pipe`
  with no NULL guard at all. API00-C+EXP34-C pairs at `:468/470` and
  `:724/726` are TP (medium confidence — real if a caller uses the
  defensive-NULL-close idiom and happens to build against the UDP/NAMED_PIPE
  backend). Every OTHER ctrl-NULL-check finding in this file
  (`wpa_ctrl_get_remote_ifname:458`, `wpa_ctrl_attach:609`,
  `wpa_ctrl_get_fd:648`) stays FP under the established internal/
  documented-precondition class, since none of those have a diverging
  sibling implementation that DOES check — only `_close()` does.
- **NEW: ARR00-C "returns pointer to local array... destroyed when function
  returns" misfires on a `static` array — rule missed the `static` storage
  class specifier entirely, an ARR00-C-specific instance of the
  established DCL30-C heap/static-vs-automatic-storage confusion family.**
  `wpa_ctrl_get_remote_ifname` (`:461-464`) declares
  `static char ps[WPA_CTRL_MAX_PS_NAME] = {};` and returns `ps` — storage
  persists across calls precisely because of `static`; there is no
  dangling-pointer risk (the real, unflagged risk here is non-reentrancy/
  clobbering on repeated calls, not a stale stack frame). FP.
- **NEW: MEM10-C "direct NULL check" misfires on an optional-parameter
  sentinel branch, not a defensive pre-use guard.** `wpa_ctrl_open`
  (NAMED_PIPE variant, `:676,682`) does
  `if (ctrl_path == NULL) ret = _snwprintf(..., NAMED_PIPE_PREFIX); else ret = _snwprintf(..., ctrl_path);`
  — `ctrl_path == NULL` is a valid, expected input meaning "use the default
  pipe name," ordinary two-way control flow, not an ad-hoc validate-before-
  dereference check. Distinct from the previously-confirmed
  ad-hoc-NULL-check-stylistic-pedantry MEM10-C class (`:104,249`, which ARE
  genuine defensive guards, just stylistically flagged) — this sub-shape
  isn't a guard at all. FP.
- **NEW: ARR30-C "unsafe array access with variable index" misfires when the
  index is capped by an interprocedural output-parameter contract, not just
  a same-function recv-length cap (extends the `eap_sim_db.c`
  recv-length-cap FP to a cross-function variant).** `wpa_ctrl_open`
  (CONFIG_CTRL_IFACE_UDP, `:445,450`) does `buf[len] = '\0'` where `len` was
  passed by address into `wpa_ctrl_request(..., buf, &len, ...)`, whose
  contract only ever writes back a value `<= *reply_len` on input (bounded
  by the `recv(ctrl->s, reply, *reply_len, 0)` call inside it). sqc doesn't
  track the callee's write-back contract on an output param across the
  call boundary. FP.
- **NEW: MSC13-C "dead store" misfires when the flagged assignment IS read
  later in the same function — looks like a control-flow/data-flow miss
  distinct from the macro-conditional-branch MSC13 FPs seen before.**
  `wpa_ctrl_request`'s `_cmd = cmd_buf;` (`:500`, inside the
  `CONFIG_CTRL_IFACE_UDP` cookie-prefix branch) is consumed a few lines
  later by `send(ctrl->s, _cmd, _cmd_len, 0)` (`:517`) — there is no path
  where it's overwritten or the function returns before that read. FP.
- **NEW: EXP30-C on an errno-consuming logging call among other libc calls
  that *could* set errno — a real (if narrow-trigger) EXP30-C shape, distinct
  from the confirmed pure-accessor-args FP family.** `wpa_ctrl_open`
  (CONFIG_CTRL_IFACE_UDP connect-failure path, `:426,432`) does
  `wpa_printf(MSG_ERROR, "connect(%s:%d) failed: %s", inet_ntop/inet_ntoa(...), ntohs(...), strerror(errno))`
  in one statement. Argument evaluation order/sequencing is unspecified in
  C, and `inet_ntop`/`inet_ntoa` can set `errno` on failure — if that
  happens to be evaluated before `strerror(errno)` reads it, the logged
  error text is wrong. Graded TP at LOW confidence: only manifests if
  `inet_ntop`/`inet_ntoa` itself fails, which is unlikely given a
  correctly-sized destination buffer and an already-populated address —
  but unlike the `MAC2STR`/`WPA_GET_BE16`/`wpabuf_head`/`wpabuf_len`
  pure-read FP family, there IS a real potential write/read conflict on
  `errno` here.
- **Reconfirms (not re-detailed above, this batch):** CON33-C/CON34-C/
  CON07-C/CON03-C no-pthread FP at volume (`counter:94,98`,
  `readdir():286`, `gethostbyname():399`, `strerror():430,435`,
  `inet_ntoa():433`, `ps:461` — 10 instances, no thread-spawning code
  anywhere in this file); POS02-C `bind()`-without-privilege-drop
  categorical FP (`:151,347`); FIO24-C double-close-across-mutually-
  exclusive-error-branches (7 instances: `:163,178,199,217,224,375,405,437`
  — every one is a distinct, disjoint early-return path from the same
  `close()` call two branches up, never actually reached twice);
  EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref (`ctrl:107,316,670`); DCL30-C heap-vs-
  local-storage confusion (`ctrl:183,204,243,454,720`, all `os_zalloc`/
  `os_malloc`-backed); ENV01-C/MEM05-C wholesale fixed-buffer misfire with
  zero `getenv()` anywhere nearby (`pathname:272`, PATH_MAX buffer for
  directory-listing, no env var involved at all); API00-C internal-only/
  documented-precondition FP (`cli_path:94` — actually IS checked via
  `cli_path &&` before deref, plus `ctrl:458,609,648,481`'s `cmd_len`
  overflow-pedantry); API05-C ptr+size_t idiom (7 instances:
  `cmd/cmd_len:481`, `reply/reply_len:482,623,731,732,749`); DCL13-C split
  between genuine low-value TP on plain getters/helpers with no dispatch-
  table binding (7 instances: `ctrl:458,481,623,635,648,731,749,759,769` —
  none of these are eloop/vtable callbacks, just ordinary accessor
  functions that never mutate `ctrl`) vs. n/a here (no eloop/vtable
  callbacks present in this file to test the FP side); DCL37-C block-scope-
  local misclassified as file-scope (`_cmd:489`, `_cmd_len:491`); STR34-C
  char-to-char massively reconfirmed (`*pos++ = ' ':504`, plain-char literal
  into plain-char, no widening); ERR07-C/ERR34-C `atoi()` on a colon-split
  port string with no range check, graded TP per this audit's literal-
  rule-text default (`port_id:386`); EXP34-C's usual guard-already-present
  FP (`result:287`, checked in the same `while` condition) alongside the
  genuine `wpa_ctrl_close` NULL-handling TP noted above; MEM12-C misfires
  when `socket()` itself is what failed — nothing was ever opened, so
  there's nothing to leak (`:328`).

Contrast the same file's genuinely non-vtable static helpers (`eap_sim_ext_sim_req`/`eap_sim_response_challenge`/`_reauth`/`_notification`/`eap_sim_process_notification_reauth`/`_notification`/`_reauthentication`), where `data`/`attr`/`sm` params really are read-only plain-helper TPs (low value) — 10 instances (`:205,672,692,734,974,975,1037,1074`), and `eap_sim_ext_sim_result`'s `sm` (`:225`), genuinely unused, also a plain-helper TP not a dispatch FP.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, one function): DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable" misfires on a function PARAMETER passed through unchanged, not a fresh local at all.** `eap_sim_init_for_reauth(struct eap_sm *sm, void *priv)` does `return priv;` (`:1324`) — `priv` is the original heap `struct eap_sim_data *` passed in by the caller, never freshly declared in this function. Extends the established heap-vs-local-storage-confusion family to a passthrough-parameter sub-shape (previously only seen for freshly-allocated locals).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, one function): MEM30-C "double-free"/MEM31-C "double free" misfire on a `goto`-target cleanup label reached only via mutually exclusive paths from an early `os_strncmp` mismatch return and a normal-completion return — a 3-way disjoint-exit-path shape.** `eap_sim_ext_sim_result`'s `resp`: freed once at the format-mismatch early return (`:239`), once at normal completion (`:269`), and once at the `invalid:` goto target (`:274`) reached from 3 `goto invalid` sites inside the per-challenge loop (`:249,258,264`) — each path executes exactly one free. Same root-cause family as the already-confirmed mutually-exclusive-branch-confusion MEM30-C class (`proximity_ranging.c`, `41plus_b186`), now on a 3-way disjoint set of returns rather than a simple if/else.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (9 instances, one function): MEM30-C/DCL30-C misfire when a read of `data`'s members in the very if-CONDITION that guards a free is misread as happening after that free, plus every use in the mutually-exclusive fallthrough branch is flagged too.** `eap_sim_init`'s `data`: the guard condition itself (`data->min_num_chal < 2 || > 3`, `:131`x2) is evaluated *before* `os_free(data)` inside its own then-branch (`:139`); the normal-path uses after the `if` block closes (`:142,144,152,168`) and the final `return data` (`:170`, both DCL30-C-heap-storage and MEM30-C-use-after-free flavors) are only reachable when that free-and-return branch was NOT taken. 10 findings total, all FP.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): DCL13-C "not modified" factually wrong when the mutation is an `os_memset`/`hexstr2bin` write into a struct-member fixed-size array via the pointer, not a direct `ptr->field = value` assignment.** `eap_sim_clear_keys`'s `data` (`:174`, `os_memset(data->mk/k_aut/k_encr/kc/sres/msk/emsk, ...)`) and `eap_sim_ext_sim_result`'s `data` (`:225`, `hexstr2bin(pos, data->kc[i]/data->sres[i], ...)`) are both genuinely mutated through the pointer; sqc's DCL13-C mutation-detector doesn't recognize array-target output-function calls as writes.
- Reconfirms at volume (not re-detailed above): the `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-dereference EXP33-C class (`data:93`, `os_zalloc(sizeof(*data))`); EXP30-C pure-accessor misfire (`wpabuf_head`/`wpabuf_len`, 3 instances: `:81`(different shape, `eap_sim_state_txt` pure-switch),`533,553`); MSC07-C goto-target-label-after-return blindness (`invalid::272`); MSC37-C ifdef-branch-blind reach-end-without-returning (`eap_sim_gsm_auth:279`, all of PCSC_FUNCS/CONFIG_SIM_SIMULATOR/CONFIG_SIM_HARDCODED/#else already return); MSC09-C raw-`\x`-byte-pattern-constant-not-text (6 instances, hardcoded CONFIG_SIM_HARDCODED test Kc/SRES values, `:369,371,375,377,381,383`); API05-C ptr+size/NUL-terminated-string idiom (5 instances: `attr:516`, `priv`+`len` across all 5 getter vtable members `:1328,1354,1372,1404`x1 each); DCL30-C heap-vs-local-pointer-variable confusion at very high density (10 instances: `enc:556`,`resp:668`,`res:1280`,`key:1368`,`id:1400`,`key:1418`, plus the passthrough-parameter sub-shape at `:1324`, plus the free-branch-confusion sub-shape at `:170`); MSC01-C no-final-else deliberate-no-op-default pedantry (4 instances: `:585,645,1065,1273`, all leaving an already-correct default/prior value unchanged); STR00-C wrong-type-claim on a struct pointer mistaken for `char` when the bitwise op is really on a member field (`attr:1055`, `attr->notification & 0x4000`); ERR02-C split — genuine TP on plain unchecked `os_snprintf()` consumption (`:213,215`) vs. FP on `wpa_snprintf_hex()` which never returns an error value (`:216`); MSC13-C genuine (trivial) dead-store TP — `identity = NULL` initializer unconditionally overwritten before any read (`:434`); MEM31-C ownership-transfer-to-registration-API FP (`eap_peer_sim_register`'s `eap`, passed to `eap_peer_method_register(eap)` which takes ownership, `:1443`).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b231`, 74 findings, `src/crypto/tls_none.c`, entire file, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED extension of the DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP class beyond
  eloop/eap_method callback typedefs: a stub backend implementing a
  fixed multi-backend interface header.** `src/crypto/tls_none.c` is the
  "no TLS" stub implementation of the `tls_*()` API declared in
  `src/crypto/tls.h`, which is also implemented (with the exact same
  signatures) by `tls_openssl.c`, `tls_wolfssl.c`, `tls_gnutls.c`, and
  `tls_internal.c`. Every parameter in every function in this file is
  unmodified only because this particular backend is a no-op — the
  signature itself is pinned by the shared header contract (other
  backends genuinely mutate `tls_ctx`/`conn`/output params). Const-ing
  a param in `tls_none.c` alone without touching `tls.h` and every
  sibling backend would break the interface. 63 DCL13-C instances, 1
  file — the single largest DCL13-C FP concentration seen so far in
  this audit; watch for the same shape in `tls_internal.c` itself and
  any other file implementing a public backend/plugin interface header.
- **API05-C reconfirms both existing sub-shapes at volume in one file:**
  opaque `void *tls_ctx`/`ssl_ctx` handle misread as needing array
  syntax (8 instances: `:81,96,104,158,165,179` col matching the
  `tls_ctx`/`ssl_ctx` param) vs. genuine ptr+size_t companion-param
  idiom (`context`/`context_len`:97, `buf`/`buflen`:159,166,
  `buf`/`buf_len`:206). All FP, no new wrinkle.
- **API00-C internal-only-API FP reconfirmed:** `tls_get_library_version`'s
  `buf` (`:206`) — grepped all 6 definitions/call-sites across the tree;
  the only two callers (`wpa_supplicant/ctrl_iface.c:1045`,
  `hostapd/ctrl_iface.c:1347`) always pass a fixed non-NULL local stack
  buffer.
- **INT36-C "(void*)1" sentinel — same shape as the `eap_user_db.c:89,124`
  precedent, now a 3rd instance (`tls_init`, `:16`): `return (void *) 1;`
  as a non-NULL "init succeeded" handle for a backend with no real
  context object, never dereferenced. Graded TP (low confidence) per
  that precedent — literal violation shape, practically benign.
- **DCL40-C 31-char collision, genuinely exact this time (not a near-miss):**
  `tls_connection_set_success_data` is exactly 31 characters and
  `tls_connection_set_success_data_resumed` (`:219`) shares those 31
  characters identically (suffix-only extension) — a textbook exact
  match of the rule's literal trigger condition, not a "shares 32+
  chars" near-miss judgment call. Still graded FP per the established
  "not practically actionable on modern GCC/Clang/MSVC" convention
  (`dpp.h:577`/`wpas_dbus_getter_p2p_peer_modelname` precedent), medium
  confidence — worth flagging if a batch with an actually-legacy/8.3
  toolchain target ever surfaces, but hostap targets none.
- No FNs found — entire file is trivial no-op stub bodies (empty braces
  or a single `return NULL/0/-1`), no allocation, no fd/socket, no
  parsing of any kind. `wpabuf_free(data)` in
  `tls_connection_set_success_data` is the file's only resource op and
  is correct (ownership transferred in, freed once, no leak).
