## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b186`, 103 findings, `src/common/proximity_ranging.c`, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, high-value FN: ARR30-C out-of-bounds write, no rule flagged it.** `pr_process_channels()` (`:941`) loops `while (end-pos>2 && ch->op_classes <= op_class_count)` writing `cl = &ch->op_class[ch->op_classes]` with **no check of `ch->op_classes` against `PR_MAX_OP_CLASSES` (15, `proximity_ranging.h:28`)** — only against `op_class_count`, a raw wire byte (0-255) taken directly from an attacker-reachable Proximity Ranging Channel List (via `pr_process_edca_capabilities`/`pr_process_ntb_capabilities`/`pr_process_op_mode`, reachable from unauthenticated USD frames and the PASN Auth1/2/3 wrapper path). A crafted list with `op_class_count>15` plus enough trailing bytes drives a real out-of-bounds write (`os_memcpy(cl->channel, pos, cl->channels)`, up to 60 attacker-controlled bytes per overrun entry) past the 15-element array. Confirmed as an omission, not by-design: the sibling `pr_channels_intersect()`/`pr_op_class_intersect()` correctly bound-checks both `op_classes` and `channels` against the same two `PR_MAX_*` constants. Worth grepping other wire-parsing loops in this file/PR code for the same "counted by an attacker byte, capped only against the sub-count not the destination array size" shape.
- **NEW, reinforced at volume (12 instances): INT34-C "shift amount not validated" misfires when the shift amount is a `#define`d bit-position constant (e.g. `EDCA_MAX_TX_ANTENNA=4`, `NTB_FORMAT_AND_BW=0`) used to pack a bitfield — always non-negative, always in-width, provable at compile time.** Distinguish from a genuine TP shape in the same file: `capab >> flen * 8` (`:1635`) where `flen` is bounded only by a self-referential `while (capab >> flen*8) flen++;` loop (not checked against the 32-bit width of `capab`) — currently unexercised given the small bit-range of `capab` in practice, but not statically safe like the macro-constant shifts.
- **NEW, reinforced (2 instances): INT14-C "used with both bitwise and arithmetic" base-identifier misattribution extends to bitwise-op-on-dereference vs. arithmetic-op-on-the-pointer-itself.** `if (*pos & PR_ISTA_SUPPORT) ...; pos++;` (`:1028,1068`) — the bitwise op is on `*pos` (the byte value), the arithmetic is on `pos` (the pointer walk); these are different operands, not one variable doing double duty. Same root cause as the already-documented `capab >> flen*8` misattributed-to-`flen` case, now also present in this file at `:1635`.
- **NEW, reinforced (6 instances): MEM30-C double-free/UAF misfire extends the established mutually-exclusive-branch-confusion family to a "free is inside an early-return branch, later free/use sites are in a disjoint branch" shape spanning a whole function.** `pr_prepare_pasn_pr_elem`'s `buf`: an invalid-`forced_pr_freq` branch frees `buf` and returns immediately (`:1587`); the normal-path uses/final free (`:1599,1603,1606,1607`) are only reached when that branch was *not* taken. sqc treats all of these as one flow and flags 5 double-free/UAF findings; none is real.
- **NEW, reinforced at volume (9 instances): MEM31-C "leak due to goto" misfire when the goto target frees the resource — extends the established cleanup-label class.** All 6 `goto end;` sites in `pr_process_pasn_ranging_wrapper` (`:2081,2112,2120,2144,2160,2183`) route to an `end:` label that unconditionally frees `buf` (`:2213`) via `buf2 = pr_encaps_elem(buf, ...); wpabuf_free(buf);`.
- **NEW, reinforced at volume (6 instances): EXP33-C "uninitialized"/"used uninitialized" write-only-output-param class extends to locally-defined (not just libnl/WPS) output functions that `os_memset` the destination before filling it.** `pr_channels_intersect()` (`:1360,1512,2288`), `pr_get_edca_capabilities()`/`pr_get_ntb_capabilities()` (`:2189,2191`), and `wpa_pasn_auth_rx()` → `wpa_pasn_parse_parameter_ie()` (`:2422`) all zero the destination struct as their first statement.
- **NEW, batch-local, not yet independently 3x-confirmed: EXP33-C "may be used uninitialized" misfire when a `status`/valid-flag out-param's write and the later struct-out-param's write are correlated by the same conditional, so the only path that skips the write also skips the read.** `res_op_mode` (`:2197`) is only left unwritten when `trans_seq` matches neither of the caller's two possible values, but that same branch also leaves `status` at its FAIL initializer, which the immediately-following `if (status != SUCCESS && status != UPDATE) goto end;` gate catches before any read of `res_op_mode`.
- **NEW, reinforced (3 instances): EXP08-C "pointer arithmetic on struct pointer with byte offset, cast to char* first" misfires on plain integer subtraction that merely *uses* `offsetof()` to compute a length, not on any actual pointer arithmetic.** `len - offsetof(struct ieee80211_mgmt, u.auth.variable)` (`:2076,2238,2351`) — both operands are integers (`size_t`/`len`), no pointer is added to or cast at all.
- **NEW, batch-local (1 instance, graded TP not FP — distinguish from the pervasive no-final-else pedantry): MSC01-C missing-else on a protocol-type dispatch can be a real security-relevant gap when nothing downstream re-validates the unmatched case.** `pr_pasn_handle_auth_3`'s `if (NTB...) {...} else if (EDCA...) {...}` (`:2292`, no final else) lets an Auth3 frame whose `op_mode.protocol_type` matches neither bit skip *all* role/channel-intersection validation and fall through to set `dev->final_op_channel`/`final_op_class` directly from unvalidated peer-supplied `op_mode` fields. Contrast the FP disposition at `:1400,1820,1869,2154,2175` in the same file, where the unmatched case is independently caught by a downstream exhaustive check (e.g. `pr_pasn_get_best_op_mode`'s own final `else { return FAIL; }`) or is local/caller-selected rather than wire data — always check whether an equivalent re-validation exists before defaulting to the pedantry verdict.
- **NEW, batch-local: MEM31-C "double free" (not the goto-cleanup shape above) factually-wrong claim from an apparent cross-function parameter-name collision.** `pr_deinit(struct pr_data *pr)`'s `os_free(pr)` (`:156`) is flagged as freeing an already-freed `pr` — but there is no earlier free of `pr` anywhere in the function; the likely cause is that `pr_device_free(struct pr_data *pr, struct pr_device *dev)`, called earlier in the same function's cleanup loop, has its own same-named `pr` parameter (which it never frees either, only `dev`). Watch for this shape (double-free tracker conflating a caller's and callee's identically-named but distinct parameters) elsewhere.
- Reconfirms in this batch (not re-detailed above): ARR01-C `sizeof(*ptr)`/`sizeof(ptr->member)` correct-idiom at very high density (10 instances: `:90,95,176,197,277,461,541`); PRE08-C 8.3-legacy-filesystem FP (`:12`); DCL30-C heap-vs-stack-storage confusion (6 instances: `dev:44` a dl_list heap element, `pr:109`, `buf2:739`, `buf:1652`, all `os_zalloc`/`wpabuf_alloc`-backed); EXP34-C internal-invariant-non-null FP (`dev:27`, both call sites pre-checked truthy); EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref (`pr:90`); API00-C internal-only-API FP (5 instances: `pr:125,704`, `peer_addr:1098`, `data:1984`); API05-C ptr+size_t idiom (`pmk/pmk_len:187`); ENV01-C/MEM05-C wholesale fixed-macro-array misfire, zero `getenv()` (3 instances: `:356,357,415`); DCL37-C block-scope-misclassified-as-file-scope (5 instances: `_len` x4 + one more, `:588,627,657,684,1199`); ARR00-C pointer-parameter-treated-as-array[0] (2 instances: `data+1:782,795`); DCL13-C split into plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP (9 instances: `pr`/`common_channel`/`dev` across static helpers never bound to a callback typedef, `:25,125,1267,1303,1446,1622,1804`x2) vs. a real embedded-mutation miss (`pr:161` in `pr_deinit`, genuinely mutated via `dl_list_del` writing back through `pr->devices`'s own head pointers); MSC13-C genuine dead-store TPs at volume (12 instances, all plain locals unconditionally overwritten in every reachable branch before their one read: `ie:240,len:242,ranging_type:1307,1450,own_channels:1309,1452,own_ista_support:1312,1455,own_rsta_support:1312,1455,status:1453,ret:1909,1987`); EXP36-C alignment-1-to-4 cast graded genuine low-severity TP per established disposition, real struct target (`ieee80211_mgmt`), source alignment unproven in-function (`:1991`); EXP30-C pure-accessor-args FP (`wpabuf_head_u8`/`wpabuf_len`, 4 instances: `:1790,1961,2376,2419`); MSC07-C goto-target-label-after-return blindness (`fail::2500`).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b170`, 126 findings, `wpa_supplicant/sme.c`, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (8 instances, one file): MSC04-C "indirect recursion" fires on event-dispatch call chains that route through `wpa_supplicant_event()` and are refuted by direct code reading.** All 8 chains in this file (`sme_event_auth:2063`, `sme_deauth:2864`, `sme_event_assoc_reject:2969`, `sme_event_auth_timed_out:3062`, `sme_event_assoc_timed_out:3071`, `sme_check_sa_query_timeout:3453`, `sme_sa_query_timer:3521`, `sme_start_sa_query:3564`, `sme_event_unprot_disconnect:3581`) form a cycle of the shape `sme_X -> ... -> wpa_supplicant_event -> sme_X`. Verified one concretely: `sme_start_sa_query` (`:3564-3567`) calls `sme_sa_query_timer(wpa_s, NULL)` directly, but `sme_sa_query_timer` only recurses into the failure chain when `wpa_s->sme.sa_query_count > 0` (`:3527`) — on the direct call `sa_query_count` is always 0, so the deeper chain cannot fire in the same stack frame; it only executes later via a genuinely separate `eloop_register_timeout` callback invocation. The static call graph correctly finds the edges but is blind to (a) `eloop_register_timeout`-deferred calls being separate invocations, not tail calls, and (b) state guards (`wpa_state` checks, `sa_query_count` checks) that gate whether a given hop's failure path is taken. Treat this whole family as FP unless a specific hop can be shown to fire unconditionally on every call.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances, one file): EXP33-C "used uninitialized"/"dereference of uninitialized pointer" on two distinct FP shapes already partially documented elsewhere, both recurring heavily here.** (1) *Output-param struct, not yet populated at declaration but always populated-or-early-returned before use*: `struct ieee802_11_elems elems;` declared with no initializer, immediately passed to `ieee802_11_parse_elems(..., &elems, ...)`, which either returns `ParseFailed` (early return) or fully populates it — every one of `wpas_sme_ml_auth:506`, `sme_external_ml_auth:1653`, `sme_try_assoc_comeback:2938`, `sme_sa_query_rx:3753` is this shape. (2) *`for_each_link(links, i)` macro-expanded loop variable flagged as uninitialized at a use inside/after the loop*: the macro (`src/utils/common.h:626-628`) expands to `for ((i)=0; (i)<MAX_NUM_MLD_LINKS; (i)++) if (...)`, so `i` is always initialized by the loop header itself — `wpas_ml_connect_pref:426`, `wpas_sme_set_mlo_links:556`. sqc's uninitialized-read tracker apparently doesn't see through this macro's init-clause. Also a third shape, `wpabuf_put()`-returned struct pointer written immediately after (`bc_ie:3186`, `ic_report:3193` in `sme_send_2040_bss_coex`) — a write-destination, not a read of uninitialized memory (already documented as a general EXP33-C shape, reinforced here).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances, one file): DCL13-C fires correctly (TP, low severity) on plain internal `static`/non-callback helper functions in this file, cross-confirming the brief's prior distinction between real callback-contract signatures and ordinary helpers.** `wpas_ml_connect_pref(wpa_s,bss,ssid)` (`:409-410`), `wpas_sme_ml_auth(wpa_s,data,...)` (`:488-489`), `sme_handle_external_auth_start(...,data)` (`:1454`), `sme_sae_is_group_enabled(wpa_s,...)` (`:1587`), `sme_external_ml_auth(wpa_s,...)` (`:1640`), `sme_try_assoc_comeback(wpa_s,data)` (`:2918`) — none of these match an `eloop`/vtable/dispatch-table function-pointer type; all params are genuinely read-only. Conversely, every `void f(void *eloop_ctx, void *timeout_ctx)` in this file (`sme_assoc_comeback_timer:2892`, `sme_auth_timer:3099`, `sme_assoc_timer:3109`, `sme_obss_scan_timeout:3351`, `sme_sa_query_timer:3521`) is the established eloop-callback-contract FP. A third bucket also appeared: public `sme_event_*` handlers (`sme_event_auth_timed_out:3063`, `sme_event_assoc_timed_out:3072`, `sme_event_disassoc:3081`) called directly by name (not through a function-pointer table) with a completely **unused** `data`/`info` param — still a valid low-severity TP since nothing prevents adding `const`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances, one file): INT30-C `sizeof(x) - x_len` on `wpa_s->sme.assoc_req_ie`/`assoc_req_ie_len` is FP throughout this file because the invariant `assoc_req_ie_len <= sizeof(assoc_req_ie)` is maintained by construction** — every increment to `assoc_req_ie_len` anywhere in `sme.c` is preceded by an explicit `if (... <= sizeof(wpa_s->sme.assoc_req_ie))`-style bounds check (e.g. `:936`, `:953-956`, `:1003`). Lines `895,914,955,1000,1024,2542`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, one file): MEM05-C VLA misfires when the array size expression is a `#define` macro constant (not a VLA at all — compile-time constant expression) vs. a genuine (if trivially-bounded) VLA when the size comes from a local `const` variable.** `u8 nonces[2 * NONCE_LEN]` (`:2309`, `NONCE_LEN` is `#define NONCE_LEN 16`) and `u8 req[2+WLAN_SA_QUERY_TR_ID_LEN+OCV_OCI_EXTENDED_LEN]` (`:3475`)/`resp[...]` (`:3640`, both macro-constant-sized) are FP — not VLAs under the C standard at all. Contrast `struct wpabuf *hlp[max_hlp]` (`:2331`) where `const unsigned int max_hlp = 20;` is *not* an integer constant expression in C, so this genuinely is a VLA syntactically even though its runtime value is always the fixed literal 20 — a real but low-severity/low-risk TP.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b166`, 135 findings, `src/ap/sta_info.c`, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (8 instances, one file): MEM30-C "free"-named-helper misattribution extends to a *substring* match on an unrelated word — `ap_sta_get_free_vlan_id()`'s name contains "free" (meaning an available/unused VLAN id, not deallocation) and never calls `os_free`/frees anything at all.** `ap_sta_set_vlan_helper`/`ap_sta_bind_vlan_helper` call `ap_sta_get_free_vlan_id(hapd)` (`:1332`) or `ap_sta_get_free_vlan_id(vlan_bss)` (`:1361`); every later use/pass of `hapd`/`vlan_bss` in the same function is then flagged as UAF (`sta_info.c:1334(x2),1339,1377,1379,1391,1397,1409`). Distinct from the established "callee only frees sub-fields, not the whole struct" misattribution shape (`41plus_b107`) — here the callee doesn't free *anything*, the trigger is a bare substring hit on an adjective ("free" as in "available"), not even a real free-adjacent helper. Watch for this shape (`*_get_free_*`, `*_find_free_*`, `*_is_free`) elsewhere.
- **Reinforces the "free"-named-helper misattribution class with two more callees in the same file (12+7=19 instances): `ieee802_1x_free_station()` (only frees `sta->pending_eapol_rx`/the eapol state machine, never `sta`) called at `sta_info.c:748` (inside `ap_handle_timer`'s `STA_DISASSOC` case) and `:1037` (`ap_sta_disconnect_common`) taints every later `sta` use/pass in the same case/function as UAF, including the function's own *real* free (`ap_free_sta(hapd, sta)` at `:774`) as a phantom "double-free."** Also reconfirms the class via `__ap_free_sta()` (driver-remove only, never frees `sta`) at `:298`, causing the real `os_free(sta)` at `:538` to be flagged MEM31-C double-free.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances, one file): EXP33-C "may be used uninitialized" misfires on a local pointer declared with no initializer that is unconditionally assigned (via a direct call result, or a `for`-loop's own init clause) before its only read — a flow-insensitivity gap distinct from the already-documented alias-write-tracking miss.** `p2p_dev_addr` (`ap_get_sta_p2p:104`, assigned two lines later at `:109` before use), `sta2` (`ap_sta_remove_in_other_bss:987`, assigned at `:994`), `tmp_sta` (`ap_sta_ml_disconnect:1176`, assigned by its own enclosing `for (tmp_sta = ...; ...)` init clause at `:1183`; `ap_sta_set_vlan:1429` and `ap_sta_bind_vlan:1558`, both assigned via `ap_get_sta()` immediately after declaration). No path exists where any of these five are read before assignment.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: INT14-C "variable used with both bitwise and arithmetic operations" misattributes operations on a struct's *member fields* to the *container pointer variable* itself.** `sta`/`hapd` are flagged (`:285,611,919`) because `sta->flags`/`sta->aid`/`hapd->basic_rates` are used with `&`/`%`/`/`/`-` elsewhere in the same function — the pointer variables themselves are never used in any bitwise or arithmetic expression (C doesn't allow ANDing a struct pointer against a flag mask). Same root-cause family as the established STR34-C/EXP39-C cross-scope name-conflation class, now on INT14-C and container-vs-member.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP20-C "functions may return values > 1, use != 0" is wrong advice for a documented 3-way `{-1, 0, 1}` return contract.** `eloop_replenish_timeout()` (`src/utils/eloop.c:935-964`) returns exactly `-1` (timer not found), `0` (found, no change needed), or `1` (found and replenished); `ap_sta_replenish_timeout`'s `== 1` check (`sta_info.c:813`) is the *only* correct way to detect the replenished case — `!= 0` would incorrectly also match the "not found" (`-1`) case.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP43-C "called with overlapping memory regions" misfires on `os_realloc_array(ptr, nmemb, size)` — a single-pointer-argument API with no second pointer parameter to overlap with.** `sta_info.c:1640` (`nbuf = os_realloc_array(sta->sa_query_trans_id, ...)`); the rule's restrict-aliasing concern requires two pointer arguments, and this call only has one.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: STR34-C "signed/plain char converted ... without cast to unsigned char" wrong-type-claim extends to a local declared `const char *` (a pointer), not any flavor of `char` at all.** `prefix` in `ap_sta_set_authorized_event` (`sta_info.c:1808-1809`, `const char *prefix = " dpp_pkhash="; ... os_strlen(prefix)`) — same wrong-type-claim family as the established `pos`-is-`size_t`/`-u8*` misclassifications, now on a pointer rather than another scalar type.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: ARR30-C "variable index" misfires on an index that is actually a compile-time-constant string length.** `dpp_pkhash_buf[plen]` (`sta_info.c:1813`) — `plen = os_strlen(" dpp_pkhash=")` is always `12` (a fixed string literal), and the buffer is 100 bytes; the write is provably in-bounds despite `plen` being a runtime variable syntactically.
- **Reconfirms in this batch (not re-detailed above):** API00-C wholesale internal-only-API FP (38 instances — every `hapd`/`sta`/`addr`/`buf`/`timeout` param in this file is caller-guaranteed valid/bounded, including the one integer-overflow variant on `ap_sta_delayed_1x_auth_fail_disconnect`'s `timeout`, whose sole call site passes a hardcoded literal `0`/`10`); EXP34-C internal-invariant-never-null (15 instances, `hapd`/`sta`/`psta`); DCL13-C plain-helper-read-only-param genuine-if-low-value TP (13 instances) vs. the `ap_for_each_sta`/`int (*cb)(hapd,sta,ctx)` dispatch-contract FP on `ap_sta_wps_cancel`'s `ctx` (1 instance, registered at `wps_hostapd.c:1614`); MSC01-C no-final-else/no-default guard-clause-or-exhaustive-enum pedantry (7 instances, including a `switch (sta->timeout_next)` whose 4 cases cover all 5 enum values via combined `case STA_DEAUTH: case STA_REMOVE:` labels); DCL30-C heap-vs-local-pointer-variable confusion (5 instances, all `sta_info`/`sta` pointers into `hapd->sta_list`/`sta_hash` or fresh `os_zalloc`); INT10-C wrong-signedness-claim on provably-non-negative unsigned operands (2 instances: `sta->aid` is `u16` guarded `> 0` before `-1`; `os_random()` returns `unsigned long`); MSC37-C preproc/nested-control-flow-blindness "reach end without returning" on functions that return on every path (2 instances); FLP03-C integer-division misclassified as floating point (`passed.sec`/`.usec` are `os_time_t`, 1 instance); EXP30-C `MAC2STR` pure-accessor misfire (1 instance); MEM10-C ad-hoc-NULL-check stylistic pedantry (1 instance, `if (sta == NULL) return;`); API05-C ptr+size_t idiom (`buf`+`buflen`, 1 instance); PRE08-C low-value-TP header-family convention reconfirmed (6 instances: `ieee802_11_defs.h`/`ieee802_1x.h`/`ieee802_11.h`/`ieee802_11_auth.h` all genuinely share `ieee802_` as their first 8 chars). One new genuine TP: DCL37-C reserved-identifier violation on `__ap_free_sta` (leading double-underscore, `:209`).
- **FN read-through: none found.** Full read of `sta_info.c` (2140 lines) found no missed error-path leaks, unchecked-alloc derefs, or unvalidated wire-data parsing — this file is pure internal STA-table bookkeeping (no RADIUS/EAP wire decoding), and all `os_malloc`/`os_zalloc`/`os_realloc_array` call sites already have NULL checks with clean early-return paths.

- **Extends the `foreach_fst_group`/K&R-nested-function-definition macro-loop misparse (previously confirmed only for `foreach_fst_group`/`foreach_fst_group_iface` in `41plus_b143`, `src/fst/fst_ctrl_iface.c`) to a second, file-local wrapper macro (`foreach_fst_session(s)`, defined in this very file as `dl_list_for_each((s), &global_sessions_list, ...)`) — confirming the mechanism is general to any `IDENT(args) { block }` loop-macro shape, not specific to one macro name, plus TWO new collateral rule hits.** Every `struct fst_session *s;` declaration whose only use is inside a `foreach_fst_session(s) { ... }` block gets a spurious MSC13-C "declared but never used" at the declaration line, while the macro-call-plus-brace line itself is parsed as a K&R-style function definition, producing false MSC37-C "non-void function has/may reach end without returning" and EXP33-C "'s' used uninitialized" on the macro-invocation line, **plus now also a false EXP34-C "potential null pointer dereference" on the very next line's member access** (not previously documented for this bug) **and, once, collateral damage to an unrelated, correctly-used sibling variable in the same function** (`in_use` in `fst_find_free_session_id`, `:143` — its real read at `:152` is lost because the loop-plus-trailing-code gets swallowed into the fake nested scope). Seen in `fst_find_free_session_id` (`:140,143,145,146`), `fst_find_session_in_progress` (`:233,235,236`), `fst_session_get_by_id` (`:1166,1168,1169`), `fst_session_enum` (`:1179,1181,1182`), `fst_session_global_on_iface_detached` (`:1282,1284,1286`), `fst_session_global_get_first_by_group` (`:1295,1297,1298`) — 6 functions, ~24 findings. - **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances, one file): EXP33-C/EXP34-C don't track initialization of a `struct fst_group *` local performed via a `T **` out-param callee (`get_group_fill_session(struct fst_group **g, struct fst_session *s)`, which fills `*g` through a `foreach_fst_group(*g)` loop) — a sibling of the already-documented "callee writes through a pointer, sqc doesn't track it" family (previously seen for direct struct-field out-params, `tlsv1_client_read.c:477`), now for a genuine `T**` out-parameter.** Every one of `fst_test_req_send_fst_request`/`_response`/`_ack_request`/`_ack_response` calls `if (get_group_fill_session(&g, &s)) return -EINVAL;` then dereferences `g->dialog_token` (or passes `g` onward) on success; sqc flags `g` as uninitialized/possibly-null at every one of those later uses. `fst_session.c:1367,1435,1437,1492,1520`. CON03-C/CON07-C no-thread FP extended to a static `u32` counter's compound increment (`global_session_id`, 2 instances: `:73,84`); DCL00-C genuine low-value TP (`g` init'd-then-only-read, `:1231`); ARR02-C array-sized-by-designated-initializers genuine-if-trivial TP (`fst_action_names[]`, `:42`).

### FN read-through note (`41plus_b173`)

- **Latent type-confusion bug (CONFIG_FST_TEST-only, low severity): `get_group_fill_session()`'s `old_iface` derivation can yield a bogus non-NULL pointer when a group has exactly one interface.** `s->data.old_iface = dl_list_entry(s->data.new_iface->group_lentry.next, struct fst_iface, group_lentry);` (`fst_session.c:1322-1323`) assumes `new_iface->group_lentry.next` points to a second, distinct `struct fst_iface` node; if the group has only one interface, `dl_list` wraps around and `.next` points back to the group's own list-head sentinel field (not a real `fst_iface`), so `dl_list_entry()` computes a pointer into unrelated group-struct memory and mistypes it as a valid `fst_iface *`. The immediately following `if (!s->data.old_iface) return -EINVAL;` guard does NOT catch this, since the bogus pointer is non-NULL. Reachable only via the `CONFIG_FST_TEST` ctrl_iface test commands (`fst_test_req_send_fst_request`/`_response`/`_ack_request`/`_ack_response`), and only when a configured FST group has a single interface — narrow, test-only, but a real out-of-bounds/wrong-type access, closest to EXP39-C/ARR00-C in spirit. `upstream_present: "unknown"` (no separate upstream tracking checkout available for this pinned clone).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b125`, 150 findings, `src/ap/wps_hostapd.c#part1of2`, lines 1-1955)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances, one file): MSC13-C parser bug — mis-tokenizes the C
  keywords `if`/`return` as declared variables when a `#ifndef`/`#endif` pair
  interleaves an `if`/`else if`/`else` chain.** `hostapd_wps_config_ap`'s
  auth-type and encr-type selection chains alternate `else if (...)` clauses
  with `#ifndef CONFIG_NO_TKIP ... #endif` blocks; sqc reports "Variable 'if'
  is initialized but never read" (`:1940,1943,1952,1955`) and "Variable
  'return' is declared but never used" (`:1946`) — `if`/`return` are keywords,
  never variable identifiers anywhere in this file. Clear parser/tokenizer
  bug at the preprocessor-branch boundary, not a heuristic miss; same root
  cause family as the existing DCL40-C `#ifdef`/`#else` preprocessor-blind
  comparison bug, but manifesting as phantom keyword-as-variable declarations
  instead.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances): DCL11-C/FIO47-C "format string argument
  count mismatch" macro-blindness extends to fprintf calls mixing `MACSTR`
  (expands to 6 `%02x` specifiers) with `MAC2STR()` (expands to 6 args).**
  `hostapd_wps_new_psk_cb:152` (1 MACSTR + MAC2STR pair) and
  `hostapd_wps_pin_needed_cb:201` (1 MACSTR + MAC2STR pair) both report a
  mismatch that only exists if MACSTR/MAC2STR are treated as a single
  specifier/single arg; expanding them, specifier count and arg count match
  exactly (7==7, 14==14) in both cases. Same root cause as the already-
  documented macro-expansion-blindness theme (EXP33/DCL31/etc.), now
  confirmed on the format-string-arity checkers.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances): PRE32-C "function called with preprocessor
  directives in arguments" misfires with zero actual directive tokens
  present — triggered purely by a `MACSTR`/object-macro-constant appearing in
  the call's arguments.** `hostapd_wps_pin_needed_cb:201` (`MACSTR` string-
  literal-concatenation macro) and `hapd_wps_cred_cb:616`
  (`MGMT_FRAME_PROTECTION_OPTIONAL`, a plain enum-like constant) — neither
  call contains an `#ifdef`/`#endif`/`#if` anywhere in the argument list.
  Looks like the rule conflates "argument contains an all-caps macro
  identifier" with "argument contains a preprocessor directive."
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, worth watching for a 3rd): FIO47-C "format
  specifier %s expects Pointer but argument is Integer" misclassifies a
  `char buf[N]` local array passed by name (which decays to `char *`) as an
  Integer type.** `hapd_wps_cred_cb:687,689` (`fprintf(nconf, "%s", buf)`,
  `buf` declared `char buf[1024]`) — the array-to-pointer decay isn't
  recognized by the type checker feeding FIO47-C.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: two more `hostapd_*` dispatch-contract typedefs join the
  existing DCL13-C eloop-callback/EAP-method-table FP class.**
  (a) `hostapd_wps_for_each()`'s own callback shape
  `int (*func)(struct hostapd_data *h, void *ctx)` (used by
  `wps_stop_registrar`, `wps_pwd_auth_fail`, `wps_ap_pin_success`,
  `wps_add_pin`, `wps_button_pushed`, `wps_cancel`, `wps_ap_pin_disable`,
  `wps_ap_pin_set`, `wps_update_ie` — 9+ functions, `wps_hostapd.c` throughout).
  (b) `hostapd.h`'s `for_each_interface` callback
  `int (*cb)(struct hostapd_iface *iface, void *ctx)` (used by `wps_for_each`,
  `get_uuid_cb`, `count_interface_cb`). Both are struct-stored function-pointer
  fields with a fixed signature, not stylistic choices — DCL13-C's const
  suggestion on their `hapd`/`iface`/`ctx` params is FP for the same reason as
  the eloop/EAP-method precedent. Distinguish from the same file's *directly
  called* (non-table) static/exported helpers with a similar-looking
  `struct hostapd_data *hapd` first param (e.g. `hapd_new_ap_event`,
  `get_own_uuid`, `interface_count`, `hostapd_wps_set_vendor_ext`,
  `hostapd_wps_ap_pin_get`) — those remain genuine (if low-value) DCL13-C TPs
  per the established plain-helper-read-only-param exception.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM30-C/MEM31-C-adjacent free-tracking misses a
  reassignment of a *struct field* (not just a local variable) between the
  free and the next read, extending the existing "MEM30 reassign clears
  freed-state" fix scope from locals to struct members.**

  return" FP class at very high density (7 instances, one function) — new

  `hapd_wps_cred_cb`'s early returns at `:537,545,554,699,712` all cite
  `tmp_fname` as leaked on paths where it was demonstrably `os_free()`'d

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP30-C "unsequenced side effects" misfires when a
  genuinely pure accessor pair (`wpabuf_head`/`wpabuf_len`, or
  `wpabuf_head_u8`/`wpabuf_len`) is passed as sibling arguments to a logging/
  event call — extends the standing `MAC2STR`/`wpabuf_head`/`wpabuf_len`

  `hapd_new_ap_event(hapd, wpabuf_head_u8(attr), wpabuf_len(attr))`

- **CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()` non-thread-safety — confirmed FP for this
  codebase: hostapd/wpa_supplicant's core is single-threaded (eloop-based),
  no pthread usage found anywhere in the tree.** `wps_hostapd.c:697`.
  Extends the existing "no-thread" FP theme (previously CON03-C/ARR02-C) to
  CON33-C/CON34-C.
- **FIO24-C "double close" false positive across mutually-exclusive
  early-return branches — new instance of the established
  free/close-tracking-doesn't-separate-branches class.** `hapd_wps_cred_cb`'s
  `fclose(oconf)` at the `nconf==NULL` early-return (`:553`) and the
  `fclose(oconf)` on the unrelated success-continuation path (`:693`) are on

- **FIO39-C "input/output without intervening fseek" misfires across two
  *independent* `FILE *` streams, not the same stream reused for both
  reading and writing.** `hapd_wps_cred_cb`'s `fgets(buf, ..., oconf)` reads
  from `oconf` while the surrounding `fprintf(nconf, ...)` calls write to a
  completely different stream, `nconf` (`:668,687`). FIO39-C's underlying
  concern (mixing stdio input/output calls on the same stream without a

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b111`, 150 findings, `src/pae/ieee802_1x_kay.c#part1of2`, lines 19-3352)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances, one file): MSC13-C "dead assignment" misses a read that occurs inside a later iteration of, or immediately after, the same `dl_list_for_each`/`dl_list_for_each_safe` loop the assignment sits in.** `key_server = peer;` (elect_key_server, line 2309) is read both on later loop iterations (`compare_priorities(peer, key_server)`) and after the loop exits; `has_peer = false;`'s *initial* value (decide_macsec_use, line 2410) survives to the post-loop `if (has_peer)` read whenever no peer satisfies the loop's inner conditions; `all_receiving = true;`'s assignment inside the loop body (line 1504) is read at `if (all_receiving)` immediately after loop exit; `found = true;` (line 1546, nested loop) is read at `if (found)` right after the loop; `lpn = ...;` (get_lpn, line 1271) is read two lines later at `if (lpn == 0) lpn = 1;` after the loop's `break`. In every case a real, nearby read exists; sqc's dead-assignment detector doesn't see across the loop-body/post-loop boundary for `dl_list_for_each*`-style loops. Distinguish from the already-confirmed genuine dead-`NULL`-init TP shape (e.g. `sa_key = NULL;` unconditionally overwritten by `dl_list_first()` before any read) — that one really is dead; these five are not.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (8 instances, one function): MEM30-C/MEM31-C free-state bleeds across two sequential, independent `dl_list_for_each_safe` loops in the same function that reuse the same loop-variable name.** `ieee802_1x_participant_timer` has two separate `dl_list_for_each_safe(peer, pre_peer, ...)` loops (one over `live_peers` that ends with `os_free(peer);`, then later a second, unrelated one over `potential_peers` that also does `dl_list_del(&peer->list); os_free(peer);`). sqc flags every access/free of `peer` in the *second* loop as UAF/double-free of the *first* loop's already-freed `peer`, even though `dl_list_for_each_safe`'s own initializer clause reassigns `peer` to a fresh, live list node at the start of each loop. No real bug: each loop only ever frees its own, not-yet-freed nodes. `ieee802_1x_kay.c:2667,2669,2671,2672(x2),2673(x2)`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances, one file): ARR00-C "returning pointer to local array, dangling pointer" and MEM05-C "VLA" both misapplied to a function-`static` local array, not an automatic one.** `mi_txt()`, `sci_txt()`, and `algo_agility_txt()` each declare `static char txt[...]` (fixed compile-time size) and `return txt;` — the array has *static* storage duration (persists for the program's lifetime), so returning a pointer to it is completely safe, and it is not a VLA at all (the bound is a compile-time constant expression). Rule missed the `static` storage-class specifier on the declaration. `ieee802_1x_kay.c:109,112` (mi_txt), `:118,122` (sci_txt), `:128,131` (algo_agility_txt).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP33-C "used uninitialized"/"dereference of uninitialized pointer" misfires when the flagged variable is itself the *destination* argument of an `os_memcpy()` call (or an equivalent write), not a read.** `os_memcpy(tmp.addr, sci->addr, ETH_ALEN);` (`mka_sci_u64`, line 430) and `os_memcpy(ki.mi, body->lsrv_mi, sizeof(ki.mi));` (`ieee802_1x_mka_decode_sak_use_body`, line 1466) both flag the local struct being written to as "used uninitialized" — but the memcpy call is initializing it, not reading its prior value, and every field is fully set (via this call plus one more direct field assignment) before the struct is ever read. Distinct from the already-confirmed `sizeof(*ptr)`-is-not-a-dereference class; this is a plain write-vs-read confusion with no `sizeof` involved.
- **Reinforces the `ieee802_1x_secy_ops.c` (`16-40_b16`) API00-C file-internal-consistency TP class in a *second* file of the same KaY subsystem.** `ieee802_1x_kay.c`'s own "Interface between CP and KAY" section (`ieee802_1x_kay_set_latest_sa_attr`/`_set_old_sa_attr`/`_create_sas`/`_delete_sas`/`_enable_tx_sas`/`_enable_rx_sas`/`_enable_new_info`, lines 2811-3094) uniformly skip `if (!kay)`, while sibling public entry points elsewhere in the *same file* (`ieee802_1x_kay_deinit:3624` `if (!kay) return;`, `ieee802_1x_kay_create_mka:3678` `if (!kay || !ckn || !cak) {...}`) establish the check. Graded genuine (medium-confidence, low-severity) TP by the same file-wide-convention-outlier argument as the `secy_ops.c` precedent, not the usual internal-only-API FP default.
- **Reconfirms in this batch (not re-detailed above):** PRE08-C `ieee802_1x_*` header-family low-value-TP convention (10 instances, `:19-22`); CON03-C/ARR02-C no-thread + initializer-sized-array FP combo on file-scope lookup tables (`mka_algo_agility:39`, `cipher_suite_tbl:42`, `mka_alg_tbl:61`, `mka_body_handler:2029`); DCL13-C plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP at high density (`participant`/`ki1`/`ki2` params, ~20 instances, several structurally unused entirely e.g. `:405,719,1858,1965,1989,2012`) vs. the eloop-timeout-handler dispatch-contract FP (`eloop_ctx`/`timeout_ctx:2558`); EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref (8 instances: `psa`/`psc`/`peer`/`ether_hdr`/`eapol_hdr`); EXP05-C cast-away-const-read-only-overlay (10 instances, all `hdr`/`eth_hdr` wire-parsing pointers only ever read after the cast); ARR01-C `sizeof(ptr->fixed_array_member)`/`sizeof(*ptr)`-correct-idiom (8 instances: `participant->mi`, `body->kn`); ARR39-C byte-pointer-single-scaling and plain-integer-subtraction misfires (5 instances); INT13-C wrong-type-claim on an actually-`unsigned int` param (`:88,89`) vs. genuine (low-severity) TP on a truly-signed `int sak_len >> 3` (`:1798`); INT30-C wrap-on-tiny-cipher-table-bounded-values FP (`:2179`); ERR33-C genuine (low-severity) TP on unchecked `time(NULL)` (2 instances: `:2259,2563` — no realistic failure mode but a literal rule-text violation); EXP34-C internal-invariant-non-null on a caller-guarded static helper param (`other:2273`); DCL30-C heap-vs-stack confusion on both `dl_list`-owned participants/peers and directly-`os_zalloc`'d `psa`/`psc`/`txsa`/`rxsa` (16 instances); DCL37-C block-scope-local misclassified as file-scope (`_cs:410`); ## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b107`, 150 findings, `src/ap/hostapd.c#part1of2`, lines 17-4034)

- **"free"-named-helper misattribution (MEM30-C/MEM31-C) reconfirmed at very high density (19 instances, one file) — extends the 2-instance precedent to 6 new callee names.** `hostapd_free_stas()`, `hostapd_free_link_stas()`, `hostapd_bss_deinit_no_free()`, `hostapd_bss_link_deinit()`, `hostapd_free_hapd_data()`, and `hostapd_cleanup()` (which itself just calls `hostapd_free_hapd_data()`) all free only internal fields/sub-lists of the `hapd`/`bss` struct passed to them — never `os_free()` the struct pointer itself. sqc's name-based "contains 'free'"/"named cleanup function" heuristic treats every one of these calls as freeing the whole object, then flags every subsequent access/pass/second-`os_free()` of that same pointer as UAF or double-free, even though the *actual* single `os_free(hapd)` several lines later is the only real free. Verified against each callee's body in `src/ap/hostapd.c` and `src/ap/sta_info.c`. `hostapd.c:432,856,858,1944-1946,2692-2693,2710-2712,3006-3009,3015,3710-3711,3927,4021`.
- **MEM31-C goto-fail-cleanup blindness extends to `conf`/`new_iface`-alias leak claims.** `hostapd_add_iface()`'s `fail:` block (`:4000-4034`) does free `conf` and does clean up `hapd_iface` (aliased as `new_iface`) via the `hapd_iface->bss[]` loop + `hostapd_cleanup_iface()`; sqc's per-goto-target leak check doesn't connect the `goto fail`s at `:3962,3982,3988,3993` to that cleanup, and separately claims `conf`/`new_iface` "not freed before return" at the *success* return (`:3998`) where the whole point is that ownership is intentionally transferred/retained, not leaked. 11 instances.
- **DCL30-C linked-list-node-pointer variant of the established heap-vs-stack confusion class.** `hostapd_das_find_sta()` returns `selected`, a `struct sta_info *` that points to a node owned by `hapd->sta_list` (heap/list memory), not the local pointer variable's own automatic storage (`:1187`).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b105`, 150 findings, `wpa_supplicant/interworking.c#part1of2`, lines 49-1919)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (20 instances, one function): MEM12-C emits an
  identical flow-insensitive "Leaked: X, Y, Z" list at every `return`
  statement in a function, regardless of whether that specific return

  every single one is flagged with the exact same
  "Leaked: ssid->eap.eap_methods, anon, anon, id" list. Checked each
  cited name individually: `anon`/`id` are demonstrably `os_free()`'d
  immediately before every one of their own function's return
  statements (not leaked on any real path); `ssid->eap.eap_methods` is
  a genuine ownership-transfer case — `os_malloc()`'d into a
  longer-lived `struct wpa_ssid *ssid` field that the *caller's* `fail:`
  path frees wholesale via `wpa_config_remove_network()` ->
  `wpa_config_free_ssid()` -> `eap_peer_config_free()` (extends the
  existing param-owned-struct-field MEM31/MEM12 ownership-transfer FP
  class to this file). Watch for the "same leak list repeated verbatim
  at every return in the function" shape as a quick tell that the
  finding is flow-insensitive and needs the per-variable ownership
  check, not a per-line control-flow trace.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable" confuses
  a pointer *variable* computed via arithmetic from a parameter with
  local *storage*.** `e_end`/`f_end` (`nai_realm_parse_eap:459`,
  `nai_realm_parse_realm:520`) are `pos + offset` where `pos` is itself
  a parameter pointing into the caller's heap/wpabuf-backed ANQP
  buffer — not automatic storage at all. Same root cause as the
  existing `comeback_token.c` DCL30-C entry, now confirmed on
  arithmetic-derived pointers, not just aliased ones, and also recurs

- **Reinforces the ARR36-C pos/end-paired-buffer FP class at very high
  volume** (9 instances, `nai_realm_parse_eap`/`_realm` and
  `cred_conn_capab_missing`) — same shape as prior batches, no new

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP34-C on a `cred`/`bss` parameter that is never
  externally nullable — extends the "internal invariant never null"

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP33-C "static variable used without explicit

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b91`, 150 findings, `src/common/wpa_common.c#part1of2`, lines 19-2646)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP33-C "used uninitialized"/"may be used uninitialized" misfires on a local buffer populated through an aliased pointer (`pos = buf; *pos++ = ...; os_memcpy(pos, ...); pos += ...;`) before being passed as `(buf, pos - buf)` to a PRF/hash call — extends the write-through-alias-not-tracked class from read (MSC13-C "unused" alias miss, `41plus_b30`) to write-tracking.** sqc's def-use tracking doesn't connect writes through `pos` back to `buf` itself, so it reports `buf` as never written even though every byte up to `pos-buf` was populated immediately before use. 4 instances (`wpa_derive_pmk_r0:2397`, `wpa_derive_pmk_r1:2548`, `wpa_pmk_r1_to_ptk:2646`), plus the sibling shape where the *output* of the PRF/hash call itself (`r0_key_data`, `hash`) is read right after a `res < 0` early-return guard that only lets execution continue when the call actually wrote it (`:2425,2454,2512`).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP33-C "may be used uninitialized" on a `const char *title` (or similarly-typed) local that is assigned inside the *same* `if`/`#ifdef` branch as the `res =`-setting call that determines whether the value is ever read — a correlated-conditional-assignment blind spot.** `wpa_derive_pmk_r1_name`'s `title` (`wpa_common.c:2513`) is set in each of the SHA512/384/256 branches alongside `res = shaNNN_vector(...)`; the shared `if (res < 0) return res;` guard means `title` is read only on the same path that assigned it. sqc doesn't correlate the two assignments as gated by the same condition.
- **Reinforces the ARR30-C cross-function `addr[N]`/decl-site conflation class (`41plus_b76`) at higher volume in a single file — 15 instances.** `wpa_common.c`'s `fils_rmsk_to_pmk` (`addr[2]`, decl 713), `fils_key_auth_sk` (`addr[6]`, decl 925), `wpa_derive_pmk_r0` (`addr[2]`, decl 2342), and `wpa_derive_pmk_r1_name` (`addr[4]`, decl 2467) each declare their own same-named `addr[N]` scatter-gather array; every flagged access is in-bounds for its *own* function's array, but sqc cites an unrelated `const u8 *addr[1];` from a completely different function (`fils_domain_name_hash`, line 3534) as the "allocation site" for all of them. Lines `739,945,947,949,952,954,979,980,981,983,985,2434,2482,2484,2486`.
- **Reinforces the ARR36-C/ARR00-C same-underlying-buffer alias-derivation FP class (`16-40_b15`) with a new derivation shape: a pointer parameter renamed on entry (`pos = opt;`) where the caller passed a pointer already advanced into the *same* array as the other buffer param (`ie`/`ies`).** `wpa_ft_parse_ftie(ie, ie_len, parse, opt)` is always called with `opt` = a `pos` that started life as `ie` and was advanced within it by the caller (`wpa_common.c:1152,1154,1159`); `parse->ric` assigned from that same running `pos` inside `wpa_ft_parse_ies` shows the identical struct-field variant (`:1351,1356,1507`).
- **Reinforces the MSC17-C `#ifdef`-intervening-next-case fallthrough-misfire class with a new sub-shape: the flagged case's own `break;` sits *inside* the `#ifdef`, not just the next case's label.** `case RSN_HASH_SHA512: #ifdef CONFIG_SHA512 ... break; #endif` followed immediately by `case RSN_HASH_SHA384:` — every case in the file's SHA-selection switches has an unconditional `break`/`return`, just conditionally compiled; the enum value driving the switch is only ever produced when the matching `#ifdef` is itself enabled, so the "fallthrough" is unreachable in practice, not a real gap. `wpa_common.c:1687,1696`, plus the same `#ifdef`-gated-`return`-per-`case` shape without conditional breaks at `:180,198,220,1193`.
- **STR00-C "plain char variable ... signedness issues" reconfirmed as a wrong-type-claim (extends the `config.c` `ret`/`res` int-misidentified-as-char class, `41plus_b43`/`b44`, to a pointer variable).** `pos` in `wpa_ft_parse_ftie` (`wpa_common.c:1217,1232,1247`) is declared `const u8 *pos` (i.e., already unsigned), never `char` — the rule's premise is factually false, not just stylistically debatable.
- **API00-C internal-only-API FP class reconfirmed at very high density for FT/FILS/PASN key-derivation helpers (≈45 instances this batch alone).** `wpa_pmk_to_ptk`, `fils_rmsk_to_pmk`, `fils_pmkid_erp`, `fils_pmk_to_ptk`, `fils_key_auth_sk`, `wpa_ft_mic`, `wpa_ft_parse_ies`, `pasn_pmk_to_ptk`, `pasn_mic`, `pasn_auth_frame_hash`, `wpa_derive_pmk_r0/r1/r1_name`, `wpa_pmk_r1_to_ptk` are all `src/common/`-internal crypto derivation functions invoked only with pointers/lengths already validated or produced by the caller's own key-exchange state machine — never directly exposed to unchecked wire input. Includes the "integer parameter not validated for overflow" API00-C sub-variant on `dhss_len`/`ies_len`/`data_len`/`frame_len`/`kdk_len`, all of which are internally bounded by ECDH-output or 802.11-frame-size limits, not raw attacker-controlled lengths.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b74`, 150 findings, `wpa_supplicant/dbus/dbus_new_handlers_p2p.c` part1of3, lines 18-1706)

- **NEW: EXP34-C null-deref FP class extends from dict-entry-key extraction to plain D-Bus method string arguments.** `config_method` in `wpas_dbus_handler_p2p_prov_disc_req` (lines 927-937) is extracted via `dbus_message_iter_get_basic()` for a STRING-typed method argument; libdbus's method dispatch validates the incoming message's argument signature against the method's declared signature before ever invoking the handler, so a type-mismatched/missing arg never reaches the handler as NULL. Same root cause as the confirmed `is_signature_correct()`-guarded dict-key class (`41plus_b27`), generalized to ordinary positional method args.
- **DCL13-C forwarding-to-non-const-callee FP class (`bgscan.h:64` precedent) confirmed for plain (non-vtable) D-Bus helper wrappers.** `wpas_dbus_error_no_p2p_mgmt_iface(DBusMessage *message)` forwards `message` verbatim into `dbus_message_new_error(DBusMessage *reply_to, ...)`, whose libdbus prototype (`dbus-message.h:115`) takes a non-const `DBusMessage *` — const-qualifying the wrapper's param would fail to compile. Distinguish from the `wpa_dbus_p2p_check_enabled`/`wpas_get_p2p_role` case just below: those two plain helpers only *read* their pointer params (no forwarding to a non-const-requiring callee), so DCL13-C is a genuine low-severity TP for them.
- **Reconfirms the `plain helper, read-only param` DCL13-C TP exception (`41plus_b30` contrast note) for two more functions.** `wpa_dbus_p2p_check_enabled`'s `wpa_s` (line 515) and `wpas_get_p2p_role`'s `wpa_s` (line 1372) are ordinary static helpers, not registered in any `WPADBusMethodHandler`/`WPADBusPropertyAccessor` vtable, and only read `wpa_s->...` fields — real (if low-severity) DCL13-C findings.
- **MEM30-C/MEM31-C free-then-reassign FP class reconfirmed for a dict-loop shape without an explicit intermediate re-free.** `wpas_dbus_handler_p2p_removeclient`'s `peer_object_path`/`interface_addr` (lines 590-591): each is `os_free()`'d then immediately `os_strdup()`'d inside the `while (wpa_dbus_dict_has_dict_entry(...))` loop (lines 566-567, 571-572) if the corresponding dict key repeats, and the single free at the shared `out:` label frees only the final live allocation — not a double free of the same memory.
- **MSC07-C goto-label-blindness FP class reconfirmed at very high density (8 instances, one file) and additionally extends to MSC37-C "reach end without returning" on the exact same functions** — sqc's CFG doesn't connect a `goto error/err/out/inv_args;` jump to its target label, so it both (a) thinks straight-line code after an unconditional `return` immediately preceding a label is dead/unreachable (MSC07-C) and (b) independently thinks the function might fall off the end without returning (MSC37-C), even though every one of the 7 flagged functions (`wpas_dbus_handler_p2p_extendedlisten`/`_presence_request`/`_group_add`/`_remove_client`/`_connect`/`_invite`) was manually traced and returns on every path via the goto-reached label.
- **MSC13-C dead-initial-assignment genuine-TP class reconfirmed 4x for scalar `= 0`/`= NULL` locals that are either unconditionally overwritten before their only read, or never read on the branch where they're skipped.** `group_id = 0` (lines 361, 802, two different handlers) is unused in the `else`-branch and unconditionally reassigned via `strtoul()` before use in the `if`-branch; `err_msg`/`iface = NULL` (lines 636-637) are unconditionally overwritten by every `case` of a `switch` (including `default`) before their only read; `peer_info = NULL` (line 1289) is reassigned before the `while` loop's first read. Distinguish from the alias-blindness `path_buf`/`dbus_groupobj_path` MSC13-C FP shape (line 1424) where the "unused" variable is genuinely read/written via its alias.
- **ERR30-C genuine TP found alongside the usual ERR32-C misfire, breaking from the wholesale-FP default.** Two `strtoul(net_id_str, NULL, 10)` call sites (lines 464, 862) have **no** `errno = 0;` reset beforehand and check only `errno == EINVAL` (no `ERANGE` guard) — unlike the confirmed `errno=0`-preceded FP shape (`dbus_new_handlers.c:2484`), these genuinely lack the reset, so ERR30-C is correctly a real (low-severity) finding here even though the co-located ERR32-C "signal handler" finding on the same lines is still the standard FP (ordinary D-Bus handler, not a `signal()`-registered function).
- **DCL40-C 31-char judgment call reconfirmed for a `wpas_dbus_getter_*` accessor pair.** `wpas_dbus_getter_p2p_peer_modelname`/`_modelnumber` (line 1595) genuinely share 32+ significant characters; graded FP per the established "technically true, not practically actionable on modern GCC/Clang/MSVC" convention (`dpp.h:577` precedent), not a real risk for this codebase's actual toolchains.
- **PRE08-C convention reconfirmed not-FP-by-default for the `dbus_new*` header family** (lines 18-20): `dbus_new.h`/`dbus_new_helpers.h`/`dbus_new_handlers.h`/`dbus_new_handlers_p2p.h` all literally share `dbus_new` as their first 8 characters — graded low-value TP per the `41plus_b27` resolution of the earlier `16-40_b8`-vs-`dbus_common.c` ambiguity.

## Confirmed patterns

- **EAP method table / eloop callback const-param (DCL13-C, CONFIRMED FP)**:
  `eloop_register_timeout`/`eloop_cancel_timeout` callbacks match the fixed
  `eloop_timeout_handler` typedef `void (*)(void *eloop_ctx, void *user_ctx)`
  (src/utils/eloop.h:57). DCL13-C const-param suggestions on these
  (`tkip_countermeasures.c:24`, `bss_load.c:42`) are FP — signature is pinned
  by the dispatch contract, matches curl/mosquitto precedent.
- **`#ifdef FEATURE ... #else` static-inline no-op stub (DCL13-C, mostly TP)**:
  many headers declare a real function under `#ifdef CONFIG_X` and a
  no-op `static inline` stub with the same name under `#else` (`ap_list.h`,
  `gas_query.h`, `mesh_mpm.h`, `airtime_policy.h`, `ndisc_snoop.h`,
  `ctrl_iface.h`). In the stub branch the pointer param is genuinely
  100% unused, so const IS a real, harmless (if trivial) opportunity —
  unlike the eloop-callback pattern, these aren't constrained by a
  function-pointer typedef. Treated these as TP (low severity/value).
- **API01-C "buffer before pointer, could corrupt pointer" — CONFIRMED
  categorical FP.** Fires purely on struct layout (char buf[N] appearing
  textually before a pointer field) without checking whether the buffer is
  ever written unboundedly. Every instance checked (`proximity_ranging.h`
  country[3]/global_password[100], `driver_wext.h` ifname/phyname,
  `ieee802_1x_kay.h` if_name) is written via `os_memcpy(...,3)` or
  `os_strlcpy(..., sizeof(field))` — always bounded to the field's own
  size. No real overflow path found in any of 5 instances audited.
- **API05-C "pointer parameter should use conformant array syntax" —
  CONFIRMED categorical FP.** Fires on the extremely common C idiom
  `T *ptr, size_t len` (pointer immediately followed by its own size,
  or preceded by a companion buf/buflen pair). This is idiomatic, safe C,
  not a real conformant-array-syntax gap. Seen 15+ times across
  `driver_wext.h`, `eap_tls_common.h`, `ieee802_1x_kay.h`,
  `pmksa_cache_auth.h`/`pmksa_cache.h` (rsn_supp), `tlsv1_server.h`,
  `sha{256,384,512}-kdf.c`, `ip_addr.c`.
- **API02-C "pointer parameter without size argument" — CONFIRMED
  categorical FP when misapplied.** Fires even when a `size_t *`/`size_t`
  companion for the pointer already exists elsewhere in the signature
  (rule looks at the *last* pointer param, not the semantically-paired
  one). Confirmed nonsense instances: `eap_gpsk_common.h` (sk_len/pk_len
  already present), `pkcs1.h` (outlen/plain_len already present),
  `pasn_common.h` (pmk_len already present; also misfires on a
  function-pointer *callback* param, not an array at all),
  `aes_siv.h`/`aes_wrap.h` (num_elem+addr[]+len vector API, len already
  paired), `hw_features_common.h`/`wpa_auth_i.h` (misfires on plain
  scalar `int *` out-params and on callback `int (*cb)(...)` params —
  neither is an array).
- **ARR02-C "array declaration has implicit bounds" on function
  *parameters* — CONFIRMED FP.** `T *addr[]` / `const u8 *addr[]` as a
  function parameter is always just a pointer-to-pointer; there is no
  bound to specify (size is conveyed by a separate `num_elem`/count
  param). Seen in `aes_siv.h`, `aes_wrap.h`. Also fired once on a
  file-scope array (`drivers.c: wpa_drivers[]`) whose size legitimately
  varies per `#ifdef CONFIG_DRIVER_*` combination — hardcoding a bound
  there would be actively wrong.
- **C++ Qt header misparsed as C — CONFIRMED FP generator.**
  `wpa_gui-qt4/*.h` files are C++ (QObject-derived classes). sqc parses
  class declarations/constructors/destructors as if they were C
  functions, producing nonsense: MSC37-C "non-void function reaches end"
  on a `class Foo {` line, MSC13-C "dead assignment" on a constructor
  member-init statement, WIN04-C "function pointer without encryption"
  on a constructor declaration, EXP34-C "calling null function pointer"
  on a destructor declaration. All FP — CERT-C doesn't apply to C++ at
  all and the parse itself is wrong.
  **Extended (`41plus_b277`, `wpagui.h`, all 47 findings in the file
  FP): (a) NEW — DCL20-C "empty parameter list () should be (void)"
  fires 36x on ordinary C++ method declarations; in C++ `()` already
  means zero parameters (unlike C89), so the rule's premise doesn't
  hold for C++ at all. (b) NEW — EXP37-C "old-style function
  declaration without parameter types" on `bool serviceRunning();`, a
  valid empty-arg C++ declaration, not K&R style. (c) API02-C/API05-C
  fire on the `Q_OBJECT` macro invocation and on virtual-method
  *declarations with no body* (`ctrlRequest`, `processMsg`,
  `wpaStateTranslate`) — same ptr+size_t-idiom and no-array-syntax FP
  families as elsewhere, compounded by parsing a macro/prototype as a
  definable function. (d) MSC13-C "declared but never used" fires on
  class *member* declarations (`WpaGui *w;`, `int argc;`, `char
  **argv;`) inside a `class` body, which sqc's C parser mistakes for
  unused local variables — member declarations are never "unused" in
  the local-variable sense.**
- **EXP43-C misfire on NULL,NULL test-harness calls — FP.** In
  `wpas_module_tests.c`, calls like `wpa_bssid_ignore_get(NULL, NULL)`
  are deliberate API-robustness test calls (different pointer *types*,
  not restrict-qualified, and both NULL — no real aliasing). Flagged as
  "same pointer for input/output" purely because both literals are NULL.
- **INT33-C div-by-zero after an earlier-function guard — FP.**
  `bss_load.c`'s `update_channel_utilization` divides by
  `hapd->conf->bss_load_update_period`, but that value is already
  validated non-zero by `get_bss_load_update_timeout()` (called earlier
  in the same function; returns -1 / early-return on zero). Rule doesn't
  see cross-call guards.
- **INT30-C wrap-around flagged on a proven-safe bounded loop — FP.**
  `sha{256,384,512}-kdf.c`'s `clen = outlen - pos` / `pos += clen` loop
  maintains `pos <= outlen` as a loop invariant (clen is always
  `min(outlen-pos, MAC_LEN)`, loop exits exactly when `pos == outlen`),
  so neither the subtraction nor the addition can wrap. Identical
  pattern repeated verbatim across all three files.
- **DCL30-C "returns pointer to local automatic-storage object" —
  confused local *variable* with local *storage*.** `comeback_token.c`
  returns `buf`, a local pointer *variable*, but `buf` itself points to
  heap memory from `wpabuf_alloc()` — not stack/automatic storage. FP.
- **API00-C "does not validate pointer parameter" — mostly FP on
  internal-only APIs.** `tkip_countermeasures.c`, `comeback_token.c`,
  `sha*-kdf.c` all flagged for not NULL-checking params that are always
  struct-field addresses / fixed local arrays from a small, fully
  internal set of call sites — never externally-nullable. Consistent
  with the FN-focus-vs-per-project-disable prior: not a real bug class
  here, just missing-defensive-check pedantry.
- **EXP30-C on side-effect-free macro-expanded logging args — FP.**
  `comeback_token.c:48` flags `hostapd_logger(..., MAC2STR(addr),
  WPA_GET_BE16(token), token_idx)` as unsequenced side effects; both
  `MAC2STR` and `WPA_GET_BE16` are pure reads (array indexing / byte
  extraction), no actual side effects to unsequence.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b159`, 143 findings, `src/eap_server/eap_sim_db.c`, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances, one file): ARR00-C "pointer arithmetic goes past the end of array" misfires on a plain `const char *` pointer PARAMETER, which the rule appears to treat as an implicit 1-element array (`param[0]`) rather than a pointer with no declared bound at all.** `username + 1` (skipping a documented 1-byte type-prefix character, e.g. `EAP_SIM_PERMANENT_PREFIX`) is flagged as going "1 elements past the end of array 'username[0]'" — but `username` is `const char *username`, never declared as any kind of array, and the preceding `username[1] == '\0'` check in the same `if` condition already proves at least 2 bytes are present before the arithmetic. `eap_sim_db.c:942,1411,1504` (`eap_sim_db_get_gsm_triplets`, `eap_sim_db_get_aka_auth`, `eap_sim_db_resynchronize`, all identical `imsi = username + 1;` shape). Watch for the same shape (prefix-stripping `ptr + N` on a plain pointer param) elsewhere.
- **NEW: EXP34-C "%s-format NULL argument" is a genuine (if low-severity/rare-path) TP class, distinct from the long-confirmed "%p-format NULL argument is safe" FP family — passing NULL to a `%s` conversion is real UB (most libcs, unlike glibc's `(null)` extension, will crash), so this sub-shape doesn't get the same free pass.** Two sub-shapes, 7 instances total: (a) `wpa_printf(MSG_ERROR, "...: %s", err)` where `err` is `sqlite3_exec()`'s `pzErrmsg` out-param, initialized `NULL` and only guaranteed set by sqlite on error *except* when sqlite itself hits OOM allocating the error string — narrow/rare trigger, graded low confidence (`eap_sim_db.c:106,132,198,298`); (b) `wpa_printf(MSG_DEBUG, "...: %s", username)` inside `if (username == NULL || ...)  { wpa_printf(...); return ...; }` — the short-circuit `||` means the branch is entered (and the debug log fired) precisely when `username` can be NULL, so the function's own defensive check immediately mis-uses the value it just caught; not a same-function-guard miss like the confirmed EXP34-C FP families, but a genuine own-logic defect (current internal callers happen not to pass NULL, but the code as written has no guard against it) — graded medium confidence (`eap_sim_db.c:939,1408,1501`, `eap_sim_db_get_gsm_triplets`/`eap_sim_db_get_aka_auth`/`eap_sim_db_resynchronize`).
- **API00-C "does not validate pointer parameter" — mostly reconfirms the internal-only-API FP class (13/14 instances: `config`/`get_complete_cb`/`data`/`pseudonym`/`permanent`/`reauth_id`/`k_encr`/`k_aut`/`k_re`, all either compile-time-fixed function pointers, always-array-backed struct fields from real callers, or caller-guarded), but ONE instance is a genuine TP that happens to land on the exact right line for the wrong generic reason.** `eap_sim_db_add_reauth`'s `mk` param (`:1213`) — the function's own doc comment explicitly documents `@mk: ... or %NULL`, and while today's only two call sites (`eap_server_sim.c:737,805`) always pass `data->mk` (a fixed array member, never NULL), the non-`CONFIG_SQLITE` branch does an unconditional `os_memcpy(r->mk, mk, EAP_SIM_MK_LEN)` with **no** NULL guard — unlike the `#ifdef CONFIG_SQLITE` branch's `db_add_reauth(..., mk, ...)` which correctly treats `mk` as optional (`mk ? ", mk" : ""`). A real (if currently unreachable) contract violation, not caller-invariant FP. Distinguish from `eap_sim_db_add_reauth_prime`'s `k_encr`/`k_aut`/`k_re` (`:1254`) which are NOT documented nullable and stay FP.
- **Reconfirms/extends in this batch (not re-detailed above):** PRE08-C 8.3-legacy-filesystem FP (`eap_sim_common.h`/`eap_sim_db.h` share `eap_sim_`, 1 instance); API01-C buffer-before-pointer FP (`eap_sim_db_pending.imsi[20]` before `cb_session_ctx`, bounded via `os_strlcpy`, 1 instance); DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP extended to a 2nd kind of fixed callback signature beyond eloop timeouts — the `sqlite3_exec()` callback `int(*)(void*,int,char**,char**)` (`get_pseudonym_cb`/`get_reauth_cb`'s `ctx`/`argv`/`col`, 5 instances) and an `eloop_sock_handler` read-socket callback (`eap_sim_db_receive`'s `sock_ctx`, 1 instance), plus the established "misses a mutation through an aliased local pointer" sub-shape (`buf` in `eap_sim_db_sim_resp_auth`/`eap_sim_db_aka_resp_auth`, aliased to `start`/`pos`/`end` and mutated only through those, 2 instances) vs. genuine low-value TP on plain internal helpers (`data`/`reauth` params never forwarded/aliased, 5 instances); ARR01-C `sizeof(ptr->fixed_array_or_struct_member)`-correct-idiom (3 instances: `db_tmp_identity[100]`, `db_tmp_reauth` struct, `db_tmp_pseudonym_str[100]`); ARR30-C both the NUL-terminated-string-traversal-isn't-unbounded FP (`valid_db_string`'s `while (*pos) pos++`, 1 instance) and the recv-length-cap FP (`buf[res]='\0'` after `recv(sock,buf,sizeof(buf)-1,0)`, 1 instance); INT30-C wholesale category error, all 32 instances — pointer arithmetic (`pos++`, `pos + sizeof(cmd)`, `pos += os_snprintf(...)`, `end - pos`) on `char *`/`const char *` pointer variables misclassified as "unsigned integer" increment/addition/subtraction; ERR02-C split: genuine (low-severity) TP on plain `os_snprintf()` calls consumed via `pos += os_snprintf(pos, end-pos, ...)` with zero `os_snprintf_error()` checks anywhere in the function (`db_add_reauth`, 9 instances) vs. FP on `wpa_snprintf_hex()` (never returns a negative/error value at all, nothing to check, 6 instances); ERR07-C/ERR34-C `atoi(argv[i])` on a SQLite column value with no range check (`get_reauth_cb`'s `counter`, graded TP per this audit's literal-rule-text default, 1 each); MSC01-C no-final-else deliberate-unknown-column-skip in a SQL callback dispatch chain (`get_reauth_cb`, 1 instance); STR34-C char-to-char massively reconfirmed (`*pos = '\0'`/`*end = '\0'`/`*pos++ = prefix`, all plain-`char`-to-plain-`char`, 12 instances); MSC07-C goto-target-label-after-return (`parse_fail:`x3, `fail:`, 4 instances); EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`/`sizeof(ptr->member)`-not-a-deref (4 instances, including `sizeof(entry->imsi)` where `entry` is a still-uninitialized local pointer used only as a type source); DCL30-C heap-vs-local-storage confusion (`db`/`data`/`id`/`r`x2, all `os_zalloc`/`os_malloc`/list-node heap pointers, 5 instances); API05-C ptr+size_t idiom extended to fixed-protocol-constant-sized output buffers with no runtime bound param at all (`msg`+`len`, `_rand`/`autn`/`ik`/`ck`/`res`, 3 instances); CON33-C/CON34-C/CON07-C/CON03-C no-pthread FP reconfirmed at volume (`strerror()`x5 each, static `counter` compound-op + missing-volatile, 12 instances total); POS02-C `bind()`-without-privilege-drop categorical FP reconfirmed (1 instance); FIO24-C double-close misfire across 3 mutually-exclusive socket-setup failure branches (`local_sock==NULL`/`bind()`-fails/`connect()`-fails, 2 instances); DCL37-C block-scope-local misclassified as file-scope (`int _errno = 0;` inside `eap_sim_db_send`, 1 instance); STR00-C wrong-type-claim (`pos` is `size_t`, not `char`, 2 instances); MSC41-C hexdump-title FP (`"...external source"` is the log label, not the secret buffer, 1 instance);
