## Confirmed patterns (from batch `6-15_b3`, 120 findings across 16 files)

- **PRE02-C on single-token negative-number-literal macros — CONFIRMED
  FP.** `#define FOO -75` / `#define BAR -1` etc. flagged for missing
  parens. A unary-minus-plus-literal is already an atomic primary
  expression — there is no adjacent-token precedence hazard the
  parenthesization would guard against (unlike a multi-term body like
  `x+y`). Seen 8x in one batch (`config.h:46`, `config_ssid.h` x7 at
  lines 31/41/42/43/44/45/47).
- **EXP34-C misfire treating a `%p`-format NULL argument as a
  dereference — CONFIRMED FP.** Passing a possibly-NULL pointer to a
  logging/printf-style call purely to print its value (`%p`) is safe
  and standard-defined; it is not a dereference. Seen in
  `eap_md5.c:49` (`wpa_printf(..., "%p", pos, ...)` inside the very
  `pos==NULL` check).
- **FIO23-C "main() returns without fclose(stdout)" — CONFIRMED FP.**
  Returning from `main()` is equivalent to calling `exit()`, which the
  C standard guarantees flushes all open streams including stdout.
  Explicit `fclose(stdout)` is never required for normal termination.
  Seen in `nfc_pw_token.c:24` and `nt_password_hash.c:26`.
- **EXP39-C cross-function local-variable conflation — CONFIRMED FP,
  looks like a real sqc bug.** Two *different* functions each declare
  their own local `union wpa_event_data event` (each freshly
  `os_memset` to zero), and each writes only its own relevant member
  (e.g. `drv_event_disassoc`'s `event.disassoc_info`,
  `drv_event_eapol_rx`'s `event.eapol_rx`). sqc reports "accessing
  member X after writing member Y" as if these were the same object,
  when the "earlier write" it cites happened in an unrelated function's
  distinct local variable of the same type/name (`driver.h:7333,7342`,
  citing a write that only exists in `drv_event_assoc`). Worth a sqc
  fix: scope union-write tracking to a single variable/declaration, not
  by type+name across function boundaries.
- **DCL13-C forwarding-to-non-const-vtable-call — extension of the
  EAP-method/eloop dispatch-contract FP, not just the callback
  definitions themselves.** A plain wrapper function that forwards a
  pointer param verbatim into a non-const function-pointer/vtable field
  call (e.g. `bgscan_notify_scan`'s `scan_res` forwarded to
  `ops->notify_scan()` whose struct field type is non-const) cannot be
  made const without breaking the call. `bgscan.h:64`.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b1`, 119 findings across 3 files)

- **EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)` misidentified as a dereference of an
  uninitialized pointer — CONFIRMED FP, very common idiom.** `sizeof`
  never evaluates its operand for a non-VLA type, so `sizeof(*psk)` /
  `sizeof(*resp)` / `sizeof(*data)` used purely to size an allocation or
  a length guard (`os_zalloc(sizeof(*data))`, `left < sizeof(*resp)`) is
  never a real dereference, even when the pointer is still uninitialized
  at that point. Seen 5x in one file (`eap_server_psk.c:37,71,100,230,343`);
  this idiom is extremely common throughout hostap (`X = alloc(sizeof(*X))`)
  so expect it everywhere.
- **DCL31-C misfires on calling a function-pointer *variable*, treating
  it like an implicitly-declared bare function — CONFIRMED FP.** A local
  `int (*gkdf)(...)` assigned to one of several candidate functions and
  then invoked as `gkdf(...)` is a function-pointer call, not a call to
  an undeclared function; DCL31-C doesn't distinguish the two. Seen 3x
  in `eap_gpsk_common.c:157,164,389`.
- **DCL30-C misfires on a macro-constant identifier written through an
  out-param pointer, treating the macro name as a local variable whose
  address escapes — CONFIRMED FP.** `#define EAP_GPSK_SK_LEN_AES 16` then
  `*sk_len = EAP_GPSK_SK_LEN_AES;` (a plain integer literal written
  through a valid caller-supplied output pointer) gets flagged as
  "local variable assigned through pointer parameter - address will be
  invalid when function returns" — there is no address-of anything here,
  just an int value copy. Seen 3x in `eap_gpsk_common.c:213,214,248`.
- **MSC17-C fallthrough misfire when `#ifdef`/`#endif` intervenes between
  switch case blocks — CONFIRMED FP, extends the existing DCL40-C
  preprocessor-branch-blindness theme to a new rule.** A case block that
  has a real, unconditional `break;`/`return` right in its own body still
  gets flagged as "falls through" when the *next* case label sits behind
  `#ifdef EAP_GPSK_SHA256 ... #endif`. Seen 5x in one file, always the
  same shape (`case EAP_GPSK_CIPHER_AES: ...; break; #ifdef ... case
  EAP_GPSK_CIPHER_SHA256: ...`) — `eap_gpsk_common.c:123,318,355,488,533`.
- **Free/access tracking doesn't separate mutually-exclusive
  if/goto/return branches — CONFIRMED FP generator, 3 distinct rules hit
  by the same root cause in one file.** (a) MEM31-C "leak due to goto"
  when the goto target label *does* free the object
  (`eap_server_psk.c:122`, target `fail:` calls `wpabuf_free(req)`).
  (b) MEM31-C "double free" claiming a later `os_free(buf)` re-frees a
  buffer already freed earlier, when the earlier free's branch always
  `goto`s away and never reaches the later line (`eap_server_psk.c:124`).
  (c) ARR00-C "use after free" claiming a switch reads a freed pointer,
  when the free in question is in a sibling error-branch that `return`s
  immediately and never reaches the switch (`eap_server_psk.c:389`).
  All three: sqc treats mutually-exclusive control-flow branches as if
  both execute in sequence.

## Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed

- PRE02-C flagged on macro replacement lists that expand to a single
  atomic primary expression (array subscript `Te0[...]` or a function
  call `rotr(...)`) — no real precedence hazard exists since postfix/
  primary expressions already bind tighter than anything adjacent;
  extends the existing "single-token negative-literal" PRE02-C FP
  entry above to array-subscript/call-shaped bodies. 24 instances in
  one file (`src/crypto/aes_i.h` TE0-TE44/TD0-TD44 macros), but only
  one file seen so far — watch for other table-driven crypto macros.
- DCL22-C "declare as volatile" misfires on an ordinary local pointer
  with no setjmp/longjmp or signal-handler context anywhere in the
  function — the rule's volatile requirement doesn't apply outside
  those contexts. 2 instances so far in different files
  (`eap_gpsk_common.c:348` var `pos`, `eap_server_psk.c:218` var `pos`).
- EXP43-C flagged "overlapping memory regions" on a call to a function
  whose parameters are not `restrict`-qualified at all
  (`aes_128_eax_encrypt`, `aes_wrap.h:40-43` — plain `const u8 *`/`u8 *`,
  no `restrict`) — EXP43-C's UB only exists for restrict-qualified
  aliasing; 1 instance (`eap_server_psk.c:140`).
- MSC07-C "unreachable code after return" flagged on a `fail:` goto
  target label sitting right after a `return`, not recognizing the
  label is reached via an earlier `goto fail;`, not by falling through
  the return. 1 instance (`eap_server_psk.c:149`).
- ARR36-C "pointer comparison between pointers from different arrays"
  misapplied to a plain scalar ternary condition (`left > hashlen`,
  both `size_t`, no pointers involved at all). 1 instance
  (`eap_gpsk_common.c:97`).
- MEM05-C "VLA with runtime-sized allocation" flagged on a fixed-size
  array whose size is the sum of several `#define`d integer constants
  (`u8 kdf_out[EAP_MSK_LEN + EAP_EMSK_LEN + EAP_GPSK_SK_LEN_AES + ...]`)
  — not a VLA at all, just a macro-expansion/constant-folding gap. 2
  instances (`eap_gpsk_common.c:196,232`).
- MEM31-C false leak on ownership-transfer to a `*_method_register()`-
  style consumer, same shape as the already-noted
  `eap_peer_method_register()` FP but now confirmed on the *server*-side
  analog too (`eap_server_method_register()`, `eap_server_psk.c:510`) —
  2nd independent instance of this ownership-transfer class, worth
  promoting to Confirmed once a 3rd shows up.

- DCL37-C on deliberate kernel-header-guard-shadowing macros
  (`_LINUX_TYPES_H` etc. in `linux_wext.h`) — technically a real reserved-
  identifier violation, but intentionally shadows real Linux kernel
  headers to avoid conflicts; only one instance group seen so far.
- DCL40-C misparsing `STRUCT_PACKED` macro-suffixed anonymous structs
  as if they were the same redeclared object across different struct
  tags (`eap_psk_common.h`) — looks like a parser bug, only one file
  instance seen so far, worth confirming on other `STRUCT_PACKED` users.
- DCL40-C "incompatible declarations" flagged across two declarations
  of the same function name that live in mutually-exclusive
  `#ifdef`/`#else` branches (never both visible/compiled together) —
  e.g. `x_snoop.h:43`, real decl takes `u8 *buf`, stub decl (under
  `#else`) takes `void *buf`. Only one instance seen so far; plausibly
  the same root cause as the `STRUCT_PACKED` DCL40 bug above
  (preprocessor-branch-blind comparison), worth merging if confirmed.
- MEM10-C "use a dedicated pointer-validation function instead of an
  ad-hoc NULL check" fires on essentially any plain `if (ptr == NULL)`
  guard — stylistic, not indicative of a real gap since the check IS
  present. 2 instances this batch (`nfc_pw_token.c:23`,
  `config_none.c:25`); expect this to keep recurring.
- MEM31-C false leak when ownership of an alloc is transferred to a
  register/consumer function that frees-or-keeps it on every path (here
  `eap_peer_method_register()`, whose doc comment states "caller must
  not free... regardless of return value") — a different shape from
  the previously-documented param-owned-struct-field MEM31 FP class.
  Only 1 instance so far (`eap_md5.c:106`), worth watching for more
  register()-style ownership-transfer APIs across EAP methods.
- STR31-C misapplied to a GNU flexible-array-member of a non-char
  struct type (`struct mac_address mac_acl[0];` in `driver.h:2713`) —
  rule fired despite there being no string/char data involved at all.
  Only 1 instance so far.
- ARR30-C "unbounded while loop with pointer increment" flagged on a
  provably-bounded NUL-terminated-string scan, where an explicit
  `buf[sizeof(buf)-1] = '\0'` a few lines earlier guarantees
  termination (`nt_password_hash.c:30`). Same "rule doesn't see an
  earlier same-function guard" shape as the existing INT33-C/INT30-C
  entries above, just a new rule instance; only 1 instance so far.
- STR34-C "assigned without cast to unsigned char" misfired on a plain
  `*pos = '\0';` char *assignment* (not a widening char-to-int
  conversion, which is what the rule is actually about) —
  `nt_password_hash.c:32`. Only 1 instance so far.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b10`, 105 findings across 3 files)

- **Classic `dl_list_*` doubly-linked-list header macros (`src/utils/list.h`)
  — CONFIRMED categorical FP for PRE00-C/PRE01-C/PRE02-C/PRE10-C/PRE12-C/
  MSC21-C/DCL13-C (35 findings, one file).** This is the standard
  15-year-old kernel-list-style macro set (`dl_list_for_each[_safe/_reverse]`,
  `dl_list_entry`, `dl_list_first/last`, `DL_LIST_HEAD_INIT`,
  `DEFINE_DL_LIST`), always invoked with plain identifiers throughout
  hostap. Breakdown: (a) macro parameters used only as *lvalue
  assignment targets* (`item`, `n` in the `for_each*` loop headers)
  cannot receive a compound expression, so "evaluates multiple times"
  findings on them are moot — the genuinely-2x-evaluated parameter is
  `list`, which the tool sometimes misattributes to `item` instead;
  (b) `type`/`member`/`name` parameters are compile-time type-names,
  field-designators, or declarator identifiers, never runtime-evaluated
  expressions — PRE01/PRE12 "parenthesize"/"multiple evaluation"
  findings on these are category errors (parenthesizing a type inside
  a cast, or a field name after `->`, is invalid or meaningless); (c)
  PRE02-C's suggested fix (wrap an entire `for (...)` loop header in
  parens) produces invalid C — these are statement/loop-header macros,
  never used as sub-expressions; (d) PRE10-C's do-while(0) wrapping
  applies to statement-*block* macros, not for-loop-header macros
  designed to take a following loop body; (e) MSC21-C's `!=`-vs-relational
  concern is inapplicable to pointer-based circular-list traversal
  (`item != list`), which is the only correct termination test; (f)
  DCL13-C on `dl_list_add_tail`'s `list` param is the already-confirmed
  forwarding-to-non-const-vtable-call pattern (forwards `list->prev`
  into `dl_list_add`, a mutator).
- **MEM31-C false double-free across mutually-exclusive early-return
  branches — CONFIRMED FP, looks like a CFG bug.** `wnm_ap.c`'s
  `ieee802_11_send_wnmsleep_resp` has several `if (...) { os_free(wnmtfs_ie); return -1; }`
  branches plus a `fail:` label that also frees it; sqc flags every
  `os_free(wnmtfs_ie)` after the first as "already freed", but each is
  on its own immediately-returning branch — none of them can execute
  after another has run. 4 instances, one function (`wnm_ap.c:118,136,141,268`).
- **EXP05-C "cast away const" on a read-only struct/pointer overlay of
  a `const` wire-parsing traversal pointer — CONFIRMED FP when no
  write follows.** Casting `const u8 *pos` to a non-const struct
  pointer purely to read fields (never assigning through it) is safe;
  verified for `wnm_ap.c:313,710` (struct field reads only) and
  `wnm_ap.c:316,317` (buffer forwarded into a driver "set"/"del" op
  confirmed read-only via `driver.h`'s own doc comment: "fill in" only
  applies to "get" ops).
- **EXP33-C "dereference of uninitialized pointer" on `sizeof(*ptr)`
  right where `ptr` is being assigned — CONFIRMED FP.** `sizeof` never
  evaluates its operand (except VLAs); `mgmt = os_zalloc(sizeof(*mgmt) + ...)`
  is not a dereference. Seen twice (`wnm_ap.c:151,393`).
- **EXP33-C "passing pointer to uninitialized variable which reads the
  value" on a write-only output-param function — CONFIRMED FP.**
  `p2p_channels_union`/`p2p_channels_intersect` (`src/p2p/p2p_utils.c`)
  both overwrite their output `struct p2p_channels *res` unconditionally
  before ever reading it (memcpy/memset first) — safe with an
  uninitialized stack struct as the argument. 4 instances
  (`p2p_invitation.c:293,324,611,691`).
- **ENV01-C "fixed-size buffer may be used with environment variable"
  firing with no `getenv`/environment code anywhere nearby — looks like
  a real rule-logic bug, not a heuristic misfire.** Fired on plain PASN
  key buffers `u8 pmk[PMK_LEN_MAX]` / `u8 _pmk[PMK_LEN_MAX]` in
  `p2p_invitation.c:681,799` — the file has no environment-variable
  handling at all. Worth escalating to sqc if seen again outside hostap.
- **DCL37-C "file-scope identifier should not start with underscore"
  misapplied to block-scope local variables — CONFIRMED FP.** Per C
  7.1.3, the single-underscore+lowercase reserved-identifier
  restriction applies only at file scope; `_pmkid`/`_pmk` in
  `p2p_invitation.c:798,799` are ordinary automatic locals inside a
  function, not file-scope declarations (the rule's own message text
  calls them "file-scope" incorrectly).

## Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed (added in `16-40_b10`)

- ARR36-C "pointer subtraction between pointers from different arrays"
  firing on two members/fields of the *same* allocated struct or byte
  buffer (e.g. `pos - &mgmt->u.action.category` where both derive from
  one `os_zalloc`'d `mgmt`, or `pos - buf` where `mgmt` overlays `buf`)
  — a standard frame-length-computation idiom in packet construction
  code; 4 instances, one file (`wnm_ap.c:421,870,944,1094`).
- PRE00-C/PRE05-C/PRE11-C/PRE12-C all misfiring together on a single
  X-macro case-label generator (`#define W2S(wtype) case PREFIX_ ## wtype: return #wtype;`,
  `wnm_ap.c:673`): the parameter is only ever token-pasted/stringized
  at compile time, never evaluated as a runtime expression, so
  "evaluates multiple times" is a category error; `##` is the
  intentional/correct mechanism here, not a hazard; the trailing
  semicolon is required since it's a full case-arm generator. Only one
  macro site so far, worth watching for other X-macro case generators.
- INT32-C signed-overflow arithmetic on `end - pos` bounded by an IEEE
  802.11 management frame's realistic max size (~2KB) — same
  "rule doesn't see realistic protocol-level bounds" shape as the
  INT33-C/INT30-C/ARR30-C entries above, new rule instance
  (`wnm_ap.c:470`).
- INT34-C shift-amount validation flagged despite an earlier
  same-function guard (`color > 63` / `color == 0` both return before
  the shift) — same "rule doesn't see an earlier guard" family,
  new rule instance (`wnm_ap.c:784`).
- INT13-C "bitwise op on signed int operand" fired on a parameter that
  is actually declared `unsigned int` — the rule's type detection was
  simply wrong (`wnm_ap.c:1087`). Only 1 instance so far.
- DCL13-C missed a `param->field++` mutation when judging a pointer
  parameter unmodified (`peer->dialog_token++;` in
  `p2p_invitation.c:129`, param falsely deemed const-eligible). Only 1
  instance so far, worth watching — distinct from the eloop/vtable
  DCL13 FP family, this is a real tool miss in the "is it modified"
  scan.
- INT14-C "variable used with both bitwise and arithmetic operations"
  fired on a struct instance name (`msg`) where two *different member
  fields* are used with bitwise vs. arithmetic ops elsewhere in the
  function — the rule appears to match on the base identifier only,
  not distinguishing member accesses (`p2p_invitation.c:282`). Only 1
  instance so far.
- ARR01-C "sizeof applied to pointer/array parameter which decayed"
  fired on `sizeof(dev->inv_ssid)` where `inv_ssid` is a genuine
  fixed-size array *field* of the struct `dev` points to — member
  arrays retain full array type through `->` access; nothing decayed
  (`p2p_invitation.c:717`). Only 1 instance so far.
- MSC13-C "dead assignment" correctly caught 3 genuine (harmless)
  cases of initializing a variable to NULL/default that is always
  reassigned on every path before use, or (in one case) assigned then
  immediately orphaned by a `goto` that skips the only read site
  (`p2p_invitation.c:233,516,655`) — low-severity but real TPs, worth
  noting as MSC13-C's dead-NULL-init detection working correctly here
  (contrast with the tsf_len FP at `wnm_ap.c:697`, which the rule got
  wrong because tsf_len actually is read later).

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b4`, 116 findings across 3 files)

- **WPS attr-parse output-param — EXP33-C "uninitialized" misfire,
  CONFIRMED (8 instances in one file).** `wps_parse_msg(msg, &attr)`
  (`wps_attr_parse.c:606`) does `os_memset(attr, 0, sizeof(*attr))` as
  its unconditional first statement, then fills recognized fields.
  Every caller pattern `struct wps_parse_attr attr; ... wps_parse_msg(msg,
  &attr) < 0 ... else use attr.field` is flagged as using `attr`
  uninitialized, including one instance claiming wps_parse_msg "reads"
  attr's incoming value (it's write-only). sqc doesn't see the callee-side
  unconditional memset through the pointer param. Seen 8x in `wps.c`
  (lines 111, 248, 301, 327, 366, 395, 408, 557); likely recurs anywhere
  `wps_parse_msg`/similarly-memset-first parse functions are called.
- **ARR36-C "pointers from different arrays" on a paired buf/end
  bounds-parameter idiom — CONFIRMED (16 instances in one function).**
  `wps_attr_text(struct wpabuf *data, char *buf, char *end)` uses
  `pos` seeded from `buf` and repeatedly computes `end - pos`. `buf`
  and `end` are the classic two-pointer bounds-pair convention (both
  delimit the *same* caller-provided array), but sqc treats separately
  *named* parameters as provably-different arrays. 16x in `wps.c:559-642`.
  Extends the API02-C/API05-C "paired size param" FP class to pointer
  subtraction specifically.
- **ENV01-C / MEM05-C wholesale misfire on ordinary fixed-size local
  arrays sized by compile-time macros — CONFIRMED, no getenv/VLA
  anywhere in the file.** `sae_pk_gen.c` declares `u8 hash[SAE_MAX_HASH_LEN]`,
  `char hash_hex[2*SAE_MAX_HASH_LEN+1]`, `u8 pw_base_bin[SAE_MAX_HASH_LEN]`,
  `char m_hex[2*SAE_PK_M_LEN+1]` — all sized by `#define` constants
  (`sae.h`: `SAE_MAX_HASH_LEN 64`, `SAE_PK_M_LEN 16`). The file never
  calls `getenv()` and none of these are VLAs. 4 combined ENV01-C/MEM05-C
  misfires (lines 28, 29x2, 30, 35) in one file — looks like a severe,
  broadly-applicable engine bug, not a name-heuristic issue.
- **PRE32-C misfires on ordinary fprintf calls with ZERO preprocessor
  directives — CONFIRMED (5 instances in one file).** Every flagged
  `fprintf(stderr, "...", args)` call in `sae_pk_gen.c` (lines 43, 50,
  61, 116, 131) is a plain string literal with normal arguments — no
  `#define`/`#ifdef`/etc. token appears anywhere in the call. Looks like
  a systemic false-trigger on `fprintf`, worth an engine-level look.
- **FIO50-C flagged on a plain non-I/O arithmetic statement —
  CONFIRMED rule bug.** `sae_pk_gen.c:162`: `*dst = (val20 << 4) & 0xf0;`
  — `val20` is a local `u32`, not a `FILE*`; there is no stream I/O
  anywhere near this line. Fired twice (duplicate) on the same line.
- **INT14-C "used with both bitwise and arithmetic operations" —
  CONFIRMED stylistic-pedantry mismatch with real CERT INT14-C intent
  (apply bitwise ops only to unsigned operands), not a real defect.**
  Fires on ordinary idioms: a parity test (`len & 0x01`) followed by
  unrelated arithmetic on the same variable (`wpabuf.c:330`), a struct
  pointer whose *different fields* are used bitwise vs arithmetically
  (`wpabuf.c:69`), array-element bitwise use misattributed to the whole
  array variable (`sae_pk_gen.c:115`), and a loop counter with a
  parity check (`sae_pk_gen.c:154`). 4 instances this batch alone.
- **EXP30-C "unsequenced side effects" on pure accessor-function
  arguments — extends the existing macro-arg entry to plain function
  calls.** `wpabuf_head()/wpabuf_len()/wpabuf_mhead()` (getters with no
  side effects) passed as sibling arguments flagged as unsequenced.
  Seen in `wpabuf.c:177,215`, `wps.c:77`, `sae_pk_gen.c:106` (4 more
  instances beyond the original macro-arg case) — generalize the FP
  bucket from "macro-expanded args" to "any side-effect-free accessor
  call args".
- **MEM31-C false leak/double-free when ownership is transferred via
  free-then-reassign-in-loop or a callee that unconditionally frees its
  input — 2 sub-patterns.** (a) `sae_pk_gen.c:191`: `pw` is freed then
  reassigned every loop iteration (line 178/179) before the final free
  at cleanup — not a double-free, each `os_free(pw)` targets a
  *different* allocation. (b) `wps.c:505`: `ie` passed to
  `wps_ie_encapsulate()` (`wps_attr_build.c:464`) which unconditionally
  frees its `data` param on every path — extends the
  `eap_peer_method_register`-style ownership-transfer MEM31 FP class
  documented in `6-15_b3` (now 2 confirmed instances of that shape).
- **ARR39-C "double scaling" misfire on byte-pointer (`u8*`/`unsigned
  char*`) + sizeof offset arithmetic — CONFIRMED FP, not double
  scaling.** `(const u8 *) buf - sizeof(struct wpabuf_trace)` and
  `nbuf + sizeof(struct wpabuf_trace) + sizeof(struct wpabuf)` in
  `wpabuf.c:25,86` are normal single-scaled byte-pointer arithmetic
  (element size 1), not double-scaled index arithmetic.
- **EXP34-C null-deref flagged on a pointer computed via arithmetic
  from an already-checked base pointer.** `wpabuf_get_trace(buf)`
  (`wpabuf.c:22-26`) returns `(struct wpabuf_trace*)((u8*)buf -
  sizeof(...))`; every caller has already null-checked/dereferenced
  `buf` earlier in the same function, so the derived `trace` pointer
  can never be NULL. 3 instances (`wpabuf.c:34,61,193`).
- **STR34-C plain char-to-char assignment (no widening) — extends the
  confirmed `nt_password_hash.c:32` FP.** `sae_pk_gen.c:140` (x2) and
  `:143`: `*pos++ = *src;` / `*pos = '\0';` — both sides are `char`,
  no widening conversion is happening at all.

## Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed (from `16-40_b4`)

- MEM33-C misapplied to a plain `char*` dereference assignment
  (`*pos++ = *src;`, `sae_pk_gen.c:140`) — the rule is about assigning
  whole flexible-array-member struct instances; no struct is involved
  here at all. Only 1 instance so far.
- EXP33-C flags `sizeof(*ptr)` as a runtime dereference of a possibly-
  uninitialized `ptr` (`wpabuf.c:351`, `wa = os_zalloc(sizeof(*wa))`);
  `sizeof`'s operand is not evaluated at runtime per the C standard.
  Very common idiom (`os_zalloc(sizeof(*x))`) across this codebase —
  watch for recurrence.
- ARR00-C flagged an "uninitialized" loop-bound variable that is
  initialized in the very same `for (idx = 0; ...)` init-clause
  (`wpabuf.c:362`) — looks like a parser/CFG bug around for-loop init.
- ARR01-C misattributes a `sizeof(*param->field)` expression to the
  outer pointer parameter's array-decay, when sizeof is actually
  applied to a distinct dereferenced struct field (`wps.c:184`).
- DCL13-C false-positive extended to a free-ownership-transfer
  traversal parameter: `wps_free_pending_msgs(struct
  upnp_pending_message *msgs)` frees the memory `msgs` points to (via
  `p = msgs` then `os_free(prev)`); const-qualifying `msgs` would need
  an extra cast and misleadingly implies the function doesn't consume
  the pointed-to memory (`wps.c:535`).
- ERR33-C flagged `vsnprintf`'s return value as "not checked" when it
  literally is checked two lines later in the same function
  (`wpabuf.c:309`) — rule's lookahead window may be too short.
- DCL11-C variadic-format type-mismatch false positives: claimed a
  fully-double-typed expression (via explicit casts) was "long"
  (`sae_pk_gen.c:117`), and claimed a null-checked, non-nullable
  pointer argument "is NULL" (`sae_pk_gen.c:175`) — looks like stale/
  incorrect type inference for variadic call arguments.
- CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()` thread-safety flagged in a standalone,
  single-threaded CLI `main()` with no pthread usage anywhere in the
  file (`sae_pk_gen.c:62`) — rule doesn't gate on whether the binary is
  actually multi-threaded.
- INT00-C flagged `%llu` paired with an `unsigned long long` argument
  as a "type-size assumption" (`sae_pk_gen.c:131`) — `%llu` is the
  fully portable, correct C99 specifier for that exact type; no
  assumption is being made.
- EXP07-C "do not assume constant values" fired on shift operations of
  explicitly fixed-width `u32` values well within a defined 32-bit
  domain (`sae_pk_gen.c:151,160`) — deliberate protocol bit-packing on
  a width-explicit type, not an implementation-defined-representation
  assumption.
- FLP03-C misclassified plain integer division (`attr.authorized_macs_len
  / ETH_ALEN`, both integer operands) as floating-point division
  (`wps.c:339`) — no floats involved at all.
- MSC01-C "if/else-if chain has no final else" fired on independent
  boolean conditions where exhaustiveness isn't semantically required
  (`wps.c:173`) — stylistic pedantry, not a missing-case defect.
- ERR07-C/ERR34-C `atoi()` findings judged FP when the parsed value is
  immediately range-checked against a narrow fixed set (`sec != 3 &&
  sec != 5`, `sae_pk_gen.c:48`) — any malformed/overflowed conversion
  fails the check and safely errors out; a judgment call (literal rule
  text is still "violated") worth re-confirming in other batches.
- FLP34-C "float conversion without range checking" fired on integer-
  to-double conversions provably within double's exact-integer range
  given the program's validated input bounds (`sae_pk_gen.c:117`) —
  context-dependent, not a hard rule-engine bug like the others above.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b6`, 114 findings across 3 files)

- **CON32-C / POS49-C "bit-field accessed without mutex protection" —
  CONFIRMED categorical FP for wpa_supplicant core.** `grep -rn
  "pthread_create\|pthread_mutex"` across `wpa_supplicant/*.c` and
  `src/utils/eloop.c` returns nothing — wpa_supplicant's core event
  loop is single-threaded (eloop-based callbacks only), so there is no
  real concurrent access to any of its bit-fields. Seen 16x in one file
  (`gas_query.c`, struct `gas_query_pending`'s `sent`,
  `offchannel_tx_started`, `retry`, `wait_comeback`,
  `radio_work_removal_scheduled`, `maintain_addr`, `wildcard_bssid`
  bit-fields). Before crediting a CON32-C/POS49-C hit anywhere in
  wpa_supplicant core (not driver-thread or external-thread code),
  confirm there's an actual pthread/thread boundary in play.
- **PRE32-C / FIO30-C on `#ifdef`-fragmented string-literal args inside
  `printf()` — CONFIRMED categorical FP.** wpa_supplicant's `usage()`/
  `license()` helpers build one big literal via string-literal
  concatenation with `#ifdef`/`#else`/`#endif` blocks interleaved
  between fragments, e.g. `main.c:25-129`. The preprocessor resolves
  all directives and concatenates the surviving literals *before* the
  compiler ever parses the function call — there is no macro-argument-
  prescan hazard because `printf` is an ordinary library function, not
  implemented as a macro on any target this code supports. FIO30-C
  additionally mislabels the resulting compile-time-constant literal as
  "user input used as format string," which is simply false — the
  variables (`wpa_supplicant_version`, etc.) are passed correctly as
  `%s` arguments, not as the format string itself. Seen 20+ times in
  one file (`main.c`).
- **MSC17-C fallthrough misfires on `case` blocks adjacent to
  `#ifdef`/`#endif` — CONFIRMED FP, preprocessor-blind pattern
  extension.** Every one of 7 flagged `case` labels in `main.c`'s
  `getopt` switch (`'d'`,`'e'`,`'L'`,`'q'`,`'t'`,`'W'`,`'y'`, lines
  235-346) in fact terminates properly with an explicit `break;` or
  `goto out;`/`goto fail;` before the next `case` — verified by direct
  read of each. The common thread is that each of these `case` bodies
  is immediately followed in the source by a `#ifdef`/`#endif`-guarded
  case (or ends inside one), and the rule's fallthrough scanner appears
  to lose track of the preceding terminator across the intervening
  preprocessor line. Same root family as the existing `DCL40-C`/
  `STRUCT_PACKED` "preprocessor-branch-blind" entries above.
- **ARR00-C "loop uses uninitialized variable as bound" — CONFIRMED FP
  on the standard for-loop init-clause idiom.** `unsigned int ch;`
  declared with no initializer, then used exactly as `for (ch =
  o->min_chan; ch <= o->max_chan; ch += o->inc)` a few lines later —
  the variable *is* initialized, just in the for-statement's own init
  clause rather than at the declaration point. Rule doesn't look past
  the declaration to the loop header. Seen 2x (`pr_supplicant.c:151,
  211`, both `wpas_pr_setup_*_channels`).
- **MSC07-C "unreachable code after unconditional return" — CONFIRMED
  FP on goto-target labels.** `pr_supplicant.c:567`: a `return;`
  immediately followed by a `fail:` label is not unreachable — it's
  the target of an earlier `goto fail;` in the same function. Rule
  doesn't recognize label statements as valid jump targets that make
  the "following" code reachable.
- **EXP33-C "dereference of uninitialized pointer" misfires on
  `sizeof(*ptr)` inside `X = os_zalloc(sizeof(*X)); if (X == NULL)` —
  CONFIRMED FP, extends the general sizeof-is-compile-time-only class.**
  `sizeof(*gas)`/`sizeof(*query)` are evaluated on the pointer's
  *type* at compile time; nothing is actually dereferenced at runtime
  before `X` is assigned the zalloc result. Seen 2x in one file
  (`gas_query.c:106, 897`) — `os_zalloc(sizeof(*x))` is the standard
  allocation idiom throughout hostap, so expect this to recur.
- **FIO24-C double-close misfire across mutually-exclusive branches —
  extends the branch-blind FP family.** `main.c:162`:
  `wpa_supplicant_fd_workaround(int start)` closes `fd[i]` once inside
  `if (start) {...}` (only on the fd>2 early-exit case) and again
  inside the `else {...}` arm, guarded by `if (fd[i] >= 0)`. The two
  `close()` calls are in disjoint branches of the same static function,
  invoked on separate calls (`start=1` then later `start=0`), and the
  second is properly null/sentinel-guarded — no real double close.
- **DCL13-C on plain (non-callback) internal helper functions —
  clarification, NOT automatically FP.** The confirmed DCL13-C FP
  patterns above are specifically about params bound to a fixed
  callback/vtable-dispatch signature (eloop handlers, EAP method
  tables, `pr_config` function-pointer fields like `set_keys`). For
  ordinary internal functions where the flagged pointer param
  (frequently `wpa_s`) is only ever read and never forwarded to a
  non-const-requiring call, the finding is a genuine (if low-severity)
  TP — don't blanket-FP purely because the param is named `wpa_s`.
  Confirmed 10 real TPs this way in `pr_supplicant.c`
  (`wpas_pr_setup_edca_channels`, `wpas_pr_setup_ntb_channels`,
  `wpas_pr_usd_elems`, `wpas_pr_process_usd_elems`, `wpas_pr_flush`,
  `wpas_pr_update_dev_addr`, `wpas_pr_clear_dev_iks`,
  `wpas_pr_set_dev_ik`, `wpas_pr_pasn_auth_tx_status`,
  `wpas_pr_pasn_auth_rx`), vs. the dispatch-bound FPs at
  `pr_supplicant.c:291` (`set_keys` vtable field) and `:522` (eloop
  timeout callback). Separately, DCL13-C can also be a straightforward
  FP when its "not modified" premise is simply wrong — `gas_query.c:803`
  flags `query` as unmodified while the function writes
  `query->sa` via `os_memcpy` three times.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b7`, 111 findings across 3 files)

- **STR34-C "assigned without cast to unsigned char" misfired on
  char-array-lookup-to-char assignment — NOW CONFIRMED (13 total
  instances, promoted from the `nt_password_hash.c:32` batch-local
  entry above).** `base64.c`'s `*pos++ = table[...]` assigns a `char`
  (from `const char base64_table[65]`) to `*pos` (also `char *`) — both
  sides are `char`, no widening conversion occurs, so there is nothing
  for an unsigned-char cast to guard against. Seen 12x in one function
  (`base64.c:51,52,53,54,58,64,66,68,70,72,75,80,82`).
- **ARR01-C "sizeof applied to pointer/array parameter which has
  decayed to a pointer" misapplied to a file-scope/global array —
  CONFIRMED (8 instances in one file).** `global_oui` in `eth_p_oui.c`
  is `static const u8 global_oui[] = {...}` at file scope, not a
  function parameter; `sizeof(global_oui)` used directly on the true
  array object never decays and correctly yields the full array size.
  Rule text falsely calls it a "pointer/array parameter" — a real bug
  in how the rule classifies non-parameter array identifiers. Seen at
  `eth_p_oui.c:57,68,70,71,170,182,183,184`.
- **EXP33-C "dereference of uninitialized pointer" misfired on
  `sizeof(*ptr)` where `ptr` is a plain (non-VLA) pointer type —
  CONFIRMED (3 instances in one file).** `sizeof` never evaluates its
  operand for non-VLA types, so `sizeof(*ethhdr)`/`sizeof(*receiver)`
  on a not-yet-assigned pointer is not a dereference at all — purely a
  compile-time type-size computation. Seen at `eth_p_oui.c:57` (`if
  (len < sizeof(*ethhdr) + ...)`), `eth_p_oui.c:96` (`os_zalloc(sizeof(
  *receiver))`), `eth_p_oui.c:170` (`sizeof(*ethhdr) + ...` before
  `ethhdr` is assigned).
- **ARR39-C "double scaling" misfired when the pointer's pointee size
  is 1 byte, or on a non-pointer loop bound — CONFIRMED (3
  instances).** (a) `buf += sizeof(*ethhdr)` / `buf += sizeof(
  global_oui)` where `buf` is `const u8 *` (pointee size 1): pointer
  arithmetic on a 1-byte-element pointer has scale factor 1, so adding
  a byte count is exactly correct, not "double scaling"
  (`eth_p_oui.c:64,70`). (b) `for (i = 0; i < sizeof(base64_table) - 1;
  i++)` in `base64.c:98` isn't pointer arithmetic at all — `i` is a
  plain loop counter compared against a constant array-size bound. Rule
  doesn't check that the target pointer type actually has a >1-byte
  pointee, or that the expression is pointer arithmetic in the first
  place.
- **MEM31-C false leak on a "BIO helper" ownership-transfer pattern —
  extends the register()-style FP class to a second shape (5
  instances).** `tls_openssl_ocsp.c`'s `generalizedtime_str`/
  `octet_string_str`/`integer_str`/`algor_str`/`extensions_str` each
  allocate a `BIO *out` and pass it to `mem_bio_to_str(out)`, which
  frees `out` unconditionally on every path (success and the `res < 0`
  failure branch alike). Flagging `out` "not freed" in the caller
  ignores that ownership was transferred into a helper that always
  frees it. Lines 250, 291, 304, 317, 333.
- **MEM31-C "double free" misfired on the classic reassign-then-free
  local-variable-reuse idiom — CONFIRMED, major finding (11
  instances).** `tls_openssl_ocsp.c`'s `check_ocsp_resp` (and
  `issuer_match`) reuse a single `char *txt` across many independent
  `txt = foo_str(...); if (txt) { ...; os_free(txt); }` blocks in
  sequence. Each `os_free(txt)` frees a *freshly reassigned* value from
  the immediately preceding line — never the same allocation twice.
  sqc's free-tracking isn't clearing the "freed" flag on reassignment
  in this specific shape (note: `MEM30 reassign + fresh-binding fix`
  from task 232 apparently doesn't cover this exact idiom — worth a
  sqc regression look). Lines 441 (`issuer_match`), and 683, 690, 713,
  720, 727, 734, 752, 760, 768, 798 (`check_ocsp_resp`).

## Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed (from `16-40_b7`)

- DCL31-C misfires on OpenSSL `DEFINE_STACK_OF(...)`/`STACK_OF(...)`
  macro invocations at file/decl scope, parsed as if they were
  untyped/implicit-type declarations (no C preprocessor expansion).
  `tls_openssl_ocsp.c:219` (`DEFINE_STACK_OF(SingleResponse)`),
  `tls_openssl_ocsp.c:498` (`STACK_OF(X509) *untrusted = ...`). Only 2
  instances so far but plausibly generalizes anywhere OpenSSL-style
  stack macros appear.
- MSC13-C "dead assignment" misfired across a `dl_list_for_each` macro
  loop — the assignment is read right after the loop via `if
  (!found)`, but sqc's CFG doesn't see the post-loop read.
  `eth_p_oui.c:93` (`int found = 0;`) and `:110` (`found = 1;` inside
  the loop), both read at line 114.
- MSC07-C "unreachable code after unconditional return" misfired,
  ignoring that the following code is a `goto`-target error-handling
  label reachable from earlier failure branches. `eth_p_oui.c:135`
  (`err:` label after `return receiver;`, reached via `goto err;`
  earlier in the function).
- EXP34-C flagged `os_free(NULL)`/similar as an unchecked-NULL free;
  `free()` (and hostapd's thin `os_free` wrapper) is standard-guaranteed
  safe on NULL — no dereference occurs. `eth_p_oui.c:136`.
- ARR00-C conflated two distinct pointer variables: `mem_bio_to_str`
  frees the *BIO* `out`, and sqc reports the unrelated `txt` buffer
  (never freed on that path) as "accessed after being freed" /
  "returns dangling pointer to destroyed local array" — `txt` is
  actually heap-allocated and never freed before the return.
  `tls_openssl_ocsp.c:241,242`.
- MEM30-C free-state bled across mutually-exclusive `switch`/`case`
  branches: `responderid_str`'s `default:` case frees `out` and
  returns; sqc reports the *other*, non-overlapping case-0/case-1 path
  reaching `return mem_bio_to_str(out);` as a use-after-free of the
  never-freed-on-that-path `out`. `tls_openssl_ocsp.c:283`.
- MEM31-C/MEM30-C conflated an OpenSSL `_cleanup()` call with an actual
  `_free()`, flagging the real subsequent free as a double-free.
  `X509_STORE_CTX_cleanup(ctx)` at line 646 is not a free; the first
  and only `X509_STORE_CTX_free(ctx)` is at line 837. Similarly for the
  `certs`/individual-`X509_free` findings at line 834 — traced all 4
  code paths building `certs`, no double free exists in any of them.
  `tls_openssl_ocsp.c:834,837`.
- ENV01-C "fixed-size buffer may be used with environment variable"
  misfired on a plain crypto digest buffer (`unsigned char
  md[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE];`) with no `getenv`/`putenv` anywhere in the
  function — looks like the rule fires on any fixed-size buffer
  declaration rather than actually checking for env-var data flow.
  `tls_openssl_ocsp.c:395`. High-confidence bug, only 1 instance so
  far.
- ARR30-C "unsafe array access with variable index" misfired on a
  compile-time-constant char-literal index: `dtable['='] = 0;` — `'='`
  is a constant (61), not a variable, and well within `dtable[256]`
  bounds. `base64.c:100`.
- ARR00-C "loop uses uninitialized variable as bound" misfired on a
  function *parameter* (`len`) that is always initialized by the
  caller — confused parameter-with-a-value for an uninitialized local.
  `base64.c:103`.
- MEM12-C "returns without releasing all resources" fired on paths
  where nothing is actually leaked: once where `out` is NULL (alloc
  failed) so there is nothing to free, once immediately after `out` was
  already explicitly freed on the same path, and once on the normal
  successful return where `out` is being returned to the caller
  (ownership transfer, not a leak). `base64.c:115,146,154`.
- FIO50-C "output operation on file stream follows input without
  positioning call" misfired on a local `unsigned char block[4]` array
  — not a `FILE`/stream object at all, just a stack buffer of decoded

  `base64.c:135,136` (2 unique sites, each reported twice).

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b24`, 120 findings across 5 files)

- **DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP family extends to libdbus's own
  callback-registration APIs, not just eloop/EAP method tables —
  CONFIRMED, 5 instances.** `wpa_supplicant/dbus/dbus_common.c` passes
  fixed-signature callbacks into `dbus_connection_set_watch_functions()`
  (`add_watch`/`remove_watch`/`watch_toggled`, matching
  `DBusAddWatchFunction`/`DBusWatchToggledFunction`),
  `dbus_connection_set_timeout_functions()` (`add_timeout`/
  `remove_timeout`/`timeout_toggled`), `dbus_connection_add_filter()`
  (`disconnect_filter`, matching `DBusHandleMessageFunction`), and
  `eloop_register_signal()` (`process_wakeup_main`, matching the eloop
  signal-handler typedef). Every one of these pointer params (`data`,
  `eloop_ctx`, `timeout_ctx`, `signal_ctx`) can't be const-qualified
  without breaking the vtable/typedef contract — same root cause as the
  confirmed eloop-timeout/EAP-method-table entry, just proving it's not
  eloop-specific. Lines 51, 130, 158, 199, 263.
- **DCL31-C misfires wholesale on external-library API calls whose
  declarations live in an unresolved system header — CONFIRMED, new
  root cause, 10 instances in one file.** `dbus_common.c` calls
  `dbus_connection_get_dispatch_status`, `dbus_connection_dispatch`,
  `dbus_connection_ref`, `dbus_watch_get_enabled`,
  `dbus_timeout_handle`, `dbus_timeout_get_enabled` — all real,
  properly-declared libdbus functions from `<dbus/dbus.h>` (included at
  line 12). sqc's parser evidently doesn't resolve declarations coming
  from this external system header, so it treats every call as if the
  function were implicitly/undeclared. Lines 35, 37, 61, 105, 151, 161,
  169, 192, 206, 211, 212. Watch for this on any file that leans on a
  third-party C library header (libdbus, OpenSSL, libnl, etc.) rather
  than hostap's own headers.
- **Macro-blind CFG: EXP33-C "uninitialized" + MSC13-C "dead
  assignment" both misfire on values only read/written inside a
  function-like macro invocation — CONFIRMED, extends the existing
  macro-blindness theme (previously seen on `dl_list_for_each`) to a
  non-loop statement macro, 8 instances in one file.**
  `aes-internal-dec.c`'s `rijndaelDecrypt` assigns `s0..s3` (lines
  87-90) then reads them inside the very first `ROUND(1,t,s)` macro
  expansion (line 92's `ROUND` macro, invoked at line 100 or 125) —
  sqc doesn't see the read, so it calls each of the four assignments
  "dead" (MSC13-C, lines 87-90). Symmetrically, `t0..t3` are written by
  that same `ROUND()` expansion before being read at line 140, but sqc
  doesn't see the write either, so it calls all four "used
  uninitialized" (EXP33-C, line 140 x4). Both directions of the same
  root cause: sqc's data-flow tracking doesn't step into a
  function-like macro's expanded body to see reads/writes of the
  caller's local variables.
- **PRE00-C/PRE01-C/PRE02-C/PRE05-C/PRE12-C bundle misfires on
  identifier-only macro parameters used purely for `##`
  token-pasting/`#` stringizing (never runtime-evaluated) — CONFIRMED,
  promotes the `16-40_b10` W2S X-macro batch-local note to confirmed
  with a second, larger instance (18 findings across 7 macros in one
  file).** `src/utils/state_machine.h`'s `SM_ENTRY`/`SM_ENTRY_M`/
  `SM_ENTRY_MA` macros use `machine`/`state`/`_state`/`data` only inside
  `sm->machine ## _state`, `machine ## _ ## state`, and `#machine`/
  `#state` — never as a bare runtime expression. PRE00-C/PRE12-C
  ("evaluates parameter multiple times") and PRE01-C ("not
  parenthesized") are category errors here exactly like the dl_list
  type/member/name-parameter FPs: you cannot usefully parenthesize an
  identifier that's about to be token-pasted or stringized, and pasting/
  stringizing isn't "evaluation." PRE05-C ("## prevents parameter
  expansion") is also FP by the same logic — call sites always pass
  bare state/machine-name tokens (`TKIP`, `S0`, ...), never macros that
  would need pre-expansion. By contrast, PRE10-C (missing do-while(0))
  and PRE11-C (definition ends with `;`) are genuine TPs for these same
  macros — they really are multi-statement (`if {...} assignment;`)
  and really do end with a semicolon, an actual (if minor) hazard when
  used bare in an unbraced `if`. Lines 32, 46, 65, 83, 101, 114, 126,
  136.

## Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed (from `16-40_b24`)

- MSC37-C "non-void function may reach end without returning a value"
  misfired on `wpas_dbus_init()` (`dbus_common.c:341`), which has an
  explicit `return NULL;`/`return priv;` on every path — the function's
  `if` condition spans multiple physical lines with a
  `#ifdef CONFIG_CTRL_IFACE_DBUS_NEW ... #endif` block embedded *inside*
  the condition's `||`-chain (lines 350-354). Same "preprocessor-branch-
  blind" root cause as the confirmed DCL40-C/MSC17-C entries above, but
  first time seen against MSC37-C specifically and against an `#ifdef`
  inside an `if` *condition* rather than between `case` blocks. Only 1
  instance so far.
- `add_watch()` (`dbus_common.c:99-127`) has a genuine, sqc-missed
  resource leak: it calls `eloop_register_sock()` up to 3 times
  (EXCEPTION, then conditionally READ, then conditionally WRITE) and
  returns `FALSE` immediately if any later registration fails, without
  unregistering the earlier ones already registered on the same `fd`.
  E.g. if the EXCEPTION registration succeeds but READ fails, the
  EXCEPTION eloop registration for `fd` is never cleaned up. Closest
  CERT mapping: MEM12-C ("returns without releasing all resources"),
  though the resource is an eloop socket registration, not memory.
  `upstream_present: unknown` (no separate upstream tracking checkout
  available in this environment).
- PRE08-C "same first 8 characters" on `dbus_common.h` vs
  `dbus_common_i.h` (`dbus_common.c:16`) is a literally-true finding
  (both share `dbus_com`) rather than a misapplication — CERT PRE08-C is
  largely obsolete for modern toolchains (no compiler still truncates
  identifiers/filenames to 8 significant characters), so treated as a
  low-value but technically-correct TP, not FP. Worth watching whether
  other batches treat PRE08-C hits as FP by default — this one doesn't
  fit the "misfire" bucket, it's just a low-priority stylistic rule
  doing its literal job.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b8`, 108 findings across 3 files)

- **EXP33-C "dereference of uninitialized pointer" on `sizeof(*ptr)` —
  CONFIRMED FP (3x this batch).** `sizeof` is a compile-time type query;
  it never evaluates its operand at runtime, so `sizeof(*cap)` before
  `cap` is assigned is not a real uninitialized-use. Also fires on a
  `os_memcpy(&struct_var.field, ...)` write mischaracterized as a read
  of `struct_var`. Seen `ieee802_11_vht.c:54` (cap), `:98` (oper),
  `:172` (ap_vht_cap via memcpy-dest).
- **ARR39-C "scaled integer arithmetic with pointer" on pure integer
  sums with no pointer operand — CONFIRMED FP (3x this batch).** Fires
  on `len < 5 + 2 + sizeof(struct X)` (a bounds-check constant) and on
  `*pos++ = (5 + 2 + sizeof(A) + 2 + sizeof(B))` (an IE length-byte
  computation) where no pointer arithmetic exists in the flagged
  expression at all — rule triggers on the mere presence of `sizeof` in
  an additive expression. `ieee802_11_vht.c:254`, `:296` (x2).
- **API05-C "array parameter uses size variable declared after the
  array" on a #define macro constant — CONFIRMED FP (4x this batch).**
  When the "size variable" is actually a preprocessor macro
  (`MD4_DIGEST_LENGTH`, `MD4_BLOCK_LENGTH`) `#define`d earlier in the
  same file, it is not "declared after" anything — rule conflates macro
  token position with variable declaration order. `md4-internal.c:26,
  70, 168, 198`.
- **ARR01-C "sizeof applied to pointer/array parameter which has
  decayed to a pointer" on `sizeof(*ptr)` — CONFIRMED FP, same
  confusion family as the API05 sibling.** `sizeof(*ptr)` correctly
  dereferences to get the pointee's size — the exact idiom the rule
  should want, not the `sizeof(ptr)` mistake it's meant to catch.
  `ieee802_11_vht.c:332` (neg_vht_cap), `md4-internal.c:176` (ctx).
- **DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable" on a parameter (or a
  local that aliases a parameter) — extends the existing
  comeback_token.c precedent, now 5x more in one file.** In
  `ieee802_11_vht.c`, `eid` (a parameter) and `pos` (`u8 *pos = eid;`,
  a local alias of the parameter) are returned from
  `hostapd_eid_vht_capabilities`/`_operation`/`_vendor_vht` — none of
  this is local *storage*, it's the caller's buffer. Lines 49, 78, 95,
  149, 293, 306.
- **INT14-C "variable used with both bitwise and arithmetic ops"
  misattributes a preprocessor macro constant or a struct-access
  pointer as "the variable" — CONFIRMED FP (5x this batch,
  `md4-internal.c:116` x2, `:120`, `:157` x2).** `MD4_BLOCK_LENGTH - 1`
  used as a power-of-2 bitmask is a standard idiom and MD4_BLOCK_LENGTH
  isn't a real variable; `ctx` is flagged for `ctx->count`'s bitwise use
  even though `ctx` itself is only ever a member-access base, never a
  bitwise/arithmetic operand itself.
- **DCL13-C on `wpa_sm`-style read-only forwarding wrapper headers —
  CONFIRMED TP, explicitly distinct from the EAP/eloop dispatch-contract
  FP class.** `src/rsn_supp/wpa_i.h`'s ~30 `static inline` wrappers
  (`wpa_sm_set_state`, `wpa_sm_store_ptk`, etc.) only ever read `sm` to
  reach `sm->ctx->...` and forward `sm->ctx->ctx` (not `sm` itself) into
  the callback — `sm` is never itself passed to a fixed-signature
  callback/vtable slot, so unlike the eloop/EAP-method callback FP
  class, const-qualifying `sm` here is a genuine, harmless opportunity.
  Before assuming DCL13-C-on-a-dispatch-style-struct is FP, check
  whether the flagged param is itself forwarded into the vtable call
  (FP) vs. only used to reach a nested field that's forwarded (TP).

## Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed (from `16-40_b8`)

- FIO50-C "output operation on file stream X follows input" fired on a
  plain `u32` local variable named `hapd_nsts` — no FILE* exists in the
  function at all; rule appears to misfire on the name/shape rather
  than an actual stream object. `ieee802_11_vht.c:67` (x2, same line).
- MSC07-C "unreachable code after unconditional return" fired on a
  `goto`-target label (`no_capab:`) that is reached by three earlier
  `goto` statements in the same function — rule doesn't track
  label-based reachability across a preceding `return`.
  `ieee802_11_vht.c:280`.
- ARR30-C "macro may generate array access that cannot be statically
  analyzed" fired on `PUT_64BIT_LE`/`PUT_32BIT_LE`-style bit-packing
  macros that write fixed offsets (7..0) into an exactly-sized local
  buffer declared immediately above — statically bounded, not actually
  unanalyzable. `md4-internal.c:154`.
- DCL13-C "not modified, should be const" fired on an output-buffer
  parameter (`digest`) that IS modified, but only via a
  `PUT_32BIT_LE(digest + i*4, ...)` macro call — rule is macro-blind to
  writes performed through bit-packing macros (different shape from the
  documented "safe free"/output-param macro engine cases).
  `md4-internal.c:168`.
- PRE00-C/PRE01-C/PRE12-C on the MD4 `F1`/`F2`/`F3`/`MD4STEP` macros —
  judged TP here (real unparenthesized/multi-eval params in the macro
  body) even though every current call site passes only simple
  identifiers with no side effects or precedence hazard. Treated
  consistently with the existing `PUT_64BIT_LE`/`PUT_32BIT_LE` TP
  verdict: macro hygiene is evaluated on the macro definition itself,
  not gated on today's call sites. Worth reconciling with the "rule
  doesn't see cross-call/loop guards" FP precedents if a future batch
  disagrees on this call — the distinction is "definition-side hygiene
  defect" (TP) vs. "misreads a specific already-safe call" (FP).
  `md4-internal.c:184-189`.
- INT13-C "bitwise operator used on signed operand" fired on a loop
  index `i` used only as a shift-count (`x >> (i * 2)`), never as the
  shifted operand itself, and bounded non-negative by the loop —
  extends the existing "rule doesn't see loop invariants" family (INT30
  wrap-around, ARR30 bounded-scan) to INT13/INT14.
  `ieee802_11_vht.c:181, 184`.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b2`, 119 findings across 3 files:
l2_packet_freebsd.c, l2_packet_ndis.c, wpa_auth_kay.c)

- **EXP33-C misfires on `sizeof(*uninitialized_ptr)` — CONFIRMED FP (8
  instances this batch, reinforces the `16-40_b1`/`b8` entries above).**
  `sizeof`'s operand is never evaluated at runtime, so `X = os_zalloc(
  sizeof(*X))` (the single most common hostap allocation idiom) or a
  bounds check like `hdr.caplen < sizeof(*ethhdr)` never actually
  dereferences the pointer, regardless of its init state. Seen in
  `l2_packet_freebsd.c:91`, `l2_packet_ndis.c:116`, `wpa_auth_kay.c:297,
  402,403,404,464,468` (every `X = os_zalloc(sizeof(*X))` call in the
  file).
- **ARR01-C misapplied to `sizeof(ptr->member)` where member is a real
  fixed-size field, not a decayed array — CONFIRMED FP (4 instances).**
  `l2->rx_buf`, `l2->rx_overlapped`, `l2->rx_avail` are all concrete
  struct fields recovered correctly through the pointer dereference —
  sizeof gives the true field size. Worst case even fired on a
  non-array `HANDLE` field (`l2->rx_avail`). `l2_packet_ndis.c:166,252,
  255,515`.
- **PRE32-C fprintf/printf "preprocessor directive in arguments" —
  CONFIRMED FP generator (5 instances, one file).** Fires on ordinary
  multi-line string-literal fprintf calls with plain identifier args
  (`__func__`, a variable, `strerror(errno)`) or macro-constant text
  embedded *inside* a string literal (e.g. `"...(DLT_EN10MB)..."`) —
  no actual `#`-directive appears anywhere in the call.
  `l2_packet_freebsd.c:129,160(x2),255(x2)`.
- **MEM12-C false leak after the resource was already freed earlier in
  the same function — CONFIRMED FP (4 instances).** `eth_get()`'s
  non-Solaris branch in `l2_packet_freebsd.c` frees `buf` on every
  path (either never allocated, or an explicit `os_free(buf)` precedes
  the return); MEM12-C still reports "Leaked: buf" at each subsequent
  `return`. Lines 210 (buf is NULL, malloc failed), 213/231/234 (buf
  freed on the immediately preceding line/block). Notably, a genuine
  `MEM30-C` UAF-arithmetic bug (`buf + len` used after `os_free(buf)`)
  coexists one line away (229) in the same function — don't let the
  false-leak noise cause the real UAF to be dismissed too.
- **PRE08-C 8.3-legacy-filesystem header-name-collision — CONFIRMED FP
  for hostap (3 instances, one file).** Fires whenever two headers
  share their first 8 characters case-insensitively (`ieee802_1x_key.h`
  / `ieee802_1x_kay.h` / `ieee802_1x.h` all begin `ieee802_`).
  Technically a literal rule match, but the underlying DOS/8.3-filename
  concern is not applicable/actionable for a modern POSIX/embedded C
  project — no competent hostap maintainer would rename headers for
  this. Treat as FP for this codebase.
- **EXP43-C multiple-NULL/0-literal-argument WinAPI calls — extension
  of the existing NULL,NULL test-harness FP pattern to real production
  code.** `CreateEvent(NULL, TRUE, FALSE, NULL)` and `CreateThread(NULL,
  0, fn, l2, 0, NULL)` get flagged as "same pointer used for input and
  output" purely because multiple literal `NULL`/`0` args are present —
  no actual aliasing. `l2_packet_ndis.c:396,406,413,434`.
- **MSC13-C "dead assignment" misfires on a defensive null-out of a
  static/global pointer after `os_free()` — CONFIRMED FP, new shape.**
  `l2_ndisuio_global = NULL;` right after `os_free(l2_ndisuio_global);`
  is flagged as never-read, but the variable is a `static` GLOBAL whose
  NULL value is read by a *future, separate* invocation of
  `l2_packet_init()` — essential double-free/reuse prevention, not dead
  code. Rule's intra-function-liveness view misses cross-call
  significance of file-scope statics/globals. `l2_packet_ndis.c:508`.

- EXP34-C null-deref flagged on a global (`l2_ndisuio_global`) whose

  `l2_packet_ndis.c:250,279`.
- MSC41-C "hard-coded sensitive information" misfired on a debug-log

- FIO24-C "double close" misfired across two mutually-exclusive
  branches: one `CloseHandle()` sits inside an early-`return` branch

- DCL31-C "called without prior declaration" misfired on a standard
  WinAPI function (`DeviceIoControl`) that's genuinely declared in

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b5`, 114 findings across 3 files:
ap_drv_ops.h, ieee802_11_ht.c, ikev2.c)

- **EXP33-C `sizeof(*uninitialized_ptr)` non-evaluated-context misfire —
  massively reinforced (11 more instances, now 25+ total across batches).**
  hostap's `X = wpabuf_put(msg, sizeof(*X));`/`os_zalloc(sizeof(*X))`/
  bounds-check idioms trip this every single time. `ieee802_11_ht.c:34,53,
  137,273`; `ikev2.c:129,217,803,892,914,919,924,980,1009,1033,1059`. This
  is now the single highest-volume FP class across the whole audit — a
  sqc fix (treat `sizeof(*expr)` as non-dereferencing unless the pointee
  is a VLA-having type) would eliminate it categorically.
- **ARR36-C "pointer subtraction between different arrays" on `pos`/`end`
  threaded through parser helper functions — CONFIRMED (4 instances,
  `ikev2.c:129,136,217,224`).** `ikev2_parse_transform(data, prop, pos,
  end)`/`ikev2_parse_proposal(...)` compute `end - pos` where both derive
  from the same wire buffer, just passed down as params through 2-3
  helper-call hops; rule can't trace shared provenance interprocedurally
  and defensively assumes different arrays. Expect this in any hostap
  parser using the common `helper(pos, end)` idiom (EAP/RADIUS/IKEv2/WPS
  TLV walkers all use this shape).
- **INT14-C conflates a struct-pointer variable with its dereferenced
  member field — reinforced (4 more instances: `ieee802_11_ht.c:267,273,
  461`, `ikev2.c:839`).** Flags `iface`/`bc_ie`/`hdr` (the pointer) as
  "used with both bitwise and arithmetic" when only a member access
  (`iface->conf->ht_capab & ...`) is bitwise and the pointer itself is
  only ever member-accessed or (once) idiomatically incremented (`hdr +
  1`) — never both on the same object.
- **DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable" on a plain function
  PARAMETER (not just a local alias) — reinforced, 4 more instances
  (`ieee802_11_ht.c:31,78,134,148`).** `hostapd_eid_ht_capabilities`/
  `_operation` return `eid` (the parameter itself) or `pos` (`u8 *pos =
  eid;`, a local alias of it) — neither is this function's automatic
  storage, it's the caller's buffer. Also reconfirmed the original
  wpabuf_alloc-heap form 2x more (`ikev2.c:1120,1181`, `msg`).
- **DCL13-C real/harmless TP (not FP) on ~29 static-inline
  `hostapd_drv_*` wrapper functions in ap_drv_ops.h.** Each checks
  `hapd->driver`/`hapd->drv_priv` and forwards only *field values* (never
  `hapd` itself) into the vtable call, and never writes to `hapd` — since
  `hapd` is never itself passed to a fixed-signature callback/vtable slot
  (unlike the eloop-callback/EAP-method-table FP class), const-qualifying
  it is a genuine (if trivially low-value) opportunity. Key test to apply
  before calling a DCL13-C-on-dispatch-adjacent-struct finding FP: is the
  *pointer parameter itself* forwarded into the vtable call (FP), or only
  used to reach/forward a field (TP)? Same distinction already noted for
  `wpa_i.h` in batch `16-40_b8`.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b3`, 117 findings across 3 files)

- **ARR37-C "compound assignment on non-array pointer" misfires on plain
  `size_t` byte-counters — CONFIRMED FP, 7 instances in one file
  (`src/tls/tlsv1_client_read.c` lines 113, 384, 857, 1051, 1147, 1211,
  1359).** In every instance the flagged variable (`left`) is declared
  `size_t left;` — an integer byte-remaining counter, not a pointer of any
  kind. `left -= 4;` is plain integer subtraction; the rule's premise
  ("non-array pointer") is categorically inapplicable since there is no
  pointer type in the expression at all.
- **MSC01-C "no default/final else" fires on deliberate guard-clause
  fallthrough — CONFIRMED FP class, 6 instances across 3 files
  (`eap_server_gpsk.c:552`, `eap_server_pax.c:505`,
  `tlsv1_client_read.c:318,564,947,954`).** Two shapes recur: (a) a
  `switch` on a wire-format opcode that intentionally silently ignores
  unrecognized values (protocol robustness by design, not a bug); (b) an
  `if/else-if` chain of independent guard/failure checks where omitting
  the final `else` means "no failure detected, continue normally" (often
  into a struct already zero-initialized via `os_memset`). Neither shape
  leaves anything in an unhandled/undefined state; the rule doesn't
  distinguish a deliberate guard-clause idiom from a genuine
  missing-case bug.
- **MEM30-C conflates "helper frees some sub-fields of `*ptr`" with "`*ptr`
  itself is freed" — CONFIRMED FP, likely a real sqc bug, 4 instances
  (`tlsv1_client_read.c:688` x2, `692`, `693`).**
  `tlsv1_client_free_dh(conn)` only does `os_free(conn->dh_p/dh_g/dh_ys)`
  then NULLs those three fields (verified in `tlsv1_client.c:32`); `conn`
  itself is never freed and is dereferenced extensively afterward. sqc
  appears to treat the call as freeing `conn` wholesale, then flags every
  subsequent member access/function-arg use of `conn` as use-after-free —
  including cases where the "passed pointer" claim is doubly wrong (e.g.
  `count_bits(pos, conn->dh_p_len)` doesn't even pass `conn`, only a
  scalar field value derived from it).
- **DCL13-C misapplied to prototype-only forward declarations that don't
  see the real definition — CONFIRMED FP, 3 instances
  (`tlsv1_client_read.c:23,25,27`, all `in_len`).** A `size_t *in_len`
  param is flagged "not modified" at the file-top forward-declaration
  line, but each function's real definition later in the same file writes
  through it (e.g. `*in_len = end - in_data;`). The rule doesn't
  cross-reference the definition when analyzing the standalone prototype.
  Contrast with `tlsv1_client_read.c:1454`'s `tls_process_application_data`,
  where the *same*-shaped `in_len` really is never written in that one
  function — DCL13-C is a genuine TP there, so check the definition, not
  just the parameter name/type, before dismissing.
- **API02-C misfires when the "missing" size argument is actually a
  `size_t *` in/out parameter — extends the existing API02-C FP class.**
  `tls_process_server_key_exchange(conn, ct, in_data, in_len)` etc.
  (`tlsv1_client_read.c:22,24,26`) already have `size_t *in_len`
  immediately after `in_data`, conveying both input capacity and output
  consumed-length. The rule wants an additional plain `size_t`, not
  recognizing the pointer-to-size_t as sufficient.

## Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed (from `16-40_b3`)

- ENV01-C "fixed-size buffer may be used with environment variable"
  misfired on a plain local buffer declaration (`u8 mic[EAP_GPSK_MAX_MIC_LEN];`)
  with no `getenv`/environment-variable usage anywhere nearby.
  2 instances, same file (`eap_server_gpsk.c:247,479`).
- STR31-C "character array too small" misapplied to non-character
  single-element arrays used for a vectorized hash API
  (`const u8 *addr[1]; size_t len[1];` feeding `sha256_vector()`) —
  neither is a char array at all. 2 instances
  (`tlsv1_client_read.c:300,301`); plausibly the same root cause as the
  already-documented flexible-array-member-of-non-char-type STR31-C
  entry, worth merging if a 3rd shape shows up.
- EXP05-C "cast away const" on `(struct eap_pax_hdr *) pos` where `pos`
  is `const u8 *` — genuinely casts away const by the letter of the rule,
  though the resulting pointer is only ever read from afterward in each
  of the 3 instances seen (`eap_server_pax.c:214,322,503`). Graded TP
  (low-severity) rather than FP since the cast is real; flag for
  reconciliation if a future batch treats this same read-only
  buffer-to-struct-view idiom as FP/idiomatic instead.
- EXP34-C didn't see that a callee (`x509_certificate_chain_validate`)
  safely no-ops on a NULL "chain" argument via a `for (cert = chain;
  cert; ...)` loop-condition guard plus a `chain_trusted` fallback that
  correctly rejects an empty chain — no explicit `if (ptr == NULL)` guard
  exists in the callee, but the control flow is still safe. Verified by
  reading the callee in `x509v3.c:2138-2259`. 1 instance
  (`tlsv1_client_read.c:566`); extends the general EXP34-C
  insufficient-dataflow theme to "safe via loop-condition" rather than
  "safe via explicit guard."
- MEM30-C "accessing freed pointer" misfired on `&ptr->field` (address-of
  a struct field immediately after the field's *old* value was freed),
  passed to an out-param function to receive a fresh value — this is the
  standard free-then-reassign idiom, not a read of freed memory.
  1 instance (`tlsv1_client_read.c:477`, `&conn->server_rsa_key` passed
  to `tls_parse_cert` right after `crypto_public_key_free(conn->server_rsa_key)`).
- EXP39-C flagged a real, deliberate common-initial-sequence union
  reliance: `ev.peer_cert.subject = subject;` right after
  `ev.cert_fail.depth = depth;` on the same `union tls_event_data ev` —
  `cert_fail` and `peer_cert` share identical leading `{int depth; const
  char *subject;}` layout (verified in `crypto/tls.h:64-73`), which is
  legal under the C standard's common-initial-sequence rule but is
  exactly the kind of layout reliance EXP39-C is meant to catch. Graded
  TP (unlike the previously-documented cross-function EXP39-C FP class,
  which was a genuine sqc bug — this one is a real, single-function,
  intentional reliance). 1 instance (`tlsv1_client_read.c:341`).

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b14`, 93 findings across 3 files:
src/crypto/aes-ccm.c, src/crypto/aes-gcm.c, src/eap_server/eap_server_ikev2.c)

- **MSC41-C "hard-coded sensitive information" on a `wpa_hexdump_key`

  1-instance `16-40_b2` batch-local note (`wpa_auth_kay.c:431`,
  `"Derived CAK"`).** 7 more instances this batch: `aes-ccm.c:43,122,
  128,132(none? see below),137,143` (`"CCM B_0"`, `"CCM T"`, `"CCM U"`
  x3) and `aes-gcm.c:186,247` (`"Hash subkey H for GHASH"`,
  `"S = GHASH_H(...)"`). Every instance is the descriptive title
  argument to a `wpa_hexdump*`/`wpa_hexdump_key` call, not the actual
  secret data (which is a separate runtime binary-buffer argument in
  every case) — the rule appears to trigger on any string literal
  containing security-sounding words (key/CAK/hash/secret/etc.) passed
  to a `*_key` logging function, regardless of which argument position
  holds the real secret.
- **API05-C on a `void *` opaque crypto-context handle — CONFIRMED
  extension of the existing opaque-handle API05-C FP class (now seen
  outside EAP/wpa_sm_ctx callback contexts).** `void *aes` (an AES
  cipher context returned by `aes_encrypt_init`) flagged repeatedly as
  "should use conformant array syntax" purely because it's the first
  pointer parameter — there is no array or size pairing possible for an
  opaque handle. 6 instances (`aes-ccm.c:28,64,92,117,132`,
  `aes-gcm.c:143,215`).
- **DCL13-C "not modified" factually wrong on a pointer that IS written
  through — CONFIRMED, looks like a real tool bug distinct from the
  dispatch-contract FP family.** `xor_aes_block`/`xor_block`'s `dst`
  parameter (`*d++ ^= *s++;`) and `inc32`'s `block` parameter
  (`WPA_PUT_BE32(block + ..., val)`) are both genuinely mutated through
  the pointer, yet DCL13-C claims they're unmodified and suggests
  `const`. 3 instances (`aes-ccm.c:17`, `aes-gcm.c:16,25`).
- **MEM33-C "direct assignment of flexible array structure instances"
  fired on plain `u32` XOR-assignment through a cast pointer — CONFIRMED
  rule-engine bug, no struct or flexible-array member is present at
  all.** `*d++ ^= *s++;` (both `u32 *`, from a `(u32 *) src`/`dst` cast)
  in `xor_aes_block`/`xor_block`. 9 instances (`aes-ccm.c:21,22,23,24,
  112`, `aes-gcm.c:29,30,31,32`).

- **DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable with automatic storage"
