## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b12`, 99 findings across 3 files:
src/common/ieee802_11_common.h, src/crypto/sha256-internal.c, src/drivers/linux_ioctl.c)

- **DCL39-C "struct ifr leaks padding bytes to ioctl()" — CONFIRMED FP (7
  instances, one file).** Every `struct ifreq ifr;` in
  `linux_ioctl.c` (lines 30,47,70,87,113,162,196) is explicitly
  zeroed via `os_memset(&ifr, 0, sizeof(ifr));` immediately before use
  in the same function, and `struct ifreq` passed to `ioctl()` is the
  universal, standard POSIX/Linux networking idiom — no vendor-specific
  or unusual struct, no actual leaked garbage since it's zeroed first.
- **CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()` thread-safety — CONFIRMED categorical FP
  for all of hostap's driver-wrapper code, not just standalone CLI
  tools (18 instances, one file, extends the `sae_pk_gen.c:62`
  batch-local entry to promoted/confirmed).** hostap's driver layer
  (like wpa_supplicant core, per the `16-40_b6` CON32/POS49 finding) is
  single-threaded/eloop-driven with no `pthread_create`/mutex usage;
  `strerror(errno)` inside an error-log `wpa_printf()` call
  (`linux_ioctl.c:33,51,73,89,115,129,142,167,198`) is safe. Before
  crediting CON33/34-C anywhere in hostap core/driver code, confirm an
  actual pthread boundary exists.
- **API00-C "does not validate pointer parameter" on internally-linked
  (non-static) but closed-call-site driver-wrapper functions —
  extends the existing internal-API FP class to functions with
  external linkage.** `linux_get_ifhwaddr`/`linux_set_ifhwaddr`/
  `linux_master_get` (`linux_ioctl.c:81,104,226`) aren't `static`, but
  every real call site (`driver_wext.c`, `driver_nl80211.c`) passes a
  fixed non-null buffer/name — same FP reasoning as the previously
  `static`-only-confirmed cases, now shown to apply regardless of
  linkage as long as the call-site set is closed/internal.
- **MSC13-C dead-assignment misfire on restoring a global (`errno`) for
  the *caller* to observe after return — extends the existing
  static/global cross-call-significance MSC13-C FP class from a
  file-scope pointer (`l2_ndisuio_global`) to the standard-library
  `errno` global.** `linux_ioctl.c:130`'s `errno = saved_errno;` right
  before `return -1;` looks locally dead but exists so `errno` reflects
  the original ioctl failure if the caller inspects it afterward —
  rule's intra-function-liveness view misses this.
- **DCL31-C "called without prior declaration" misfired despite the
  correct POSIX header being included — extends the existing
  external-header-not-resolved DCL31-C FP class from Win32 APIs to
  standard POSIX functions.** `if_nametoindex()` (`linux_ioctl.c:155,
  189`) is declared by `<net/if.h>`, which the file does include
  (line 11); sqc's declaration-resolution just doesn't see it — a
  parser/header-processing gap, not a real missing declaration.
- **POS30-C "readlink() without space for terminator" misfired despite
  an explicit guarded manual-NUL-termination step — CONFIRMED FP (2
  instances).** `linux_ioctl.c:213,234` both do
  `res = readlink(path, buf, sizeof(buf)); if (res < 0 || (size_t) res
  >= sizeof(buf)) return -1; buf[res] = '\0';` — the `>= sizeof(buf)`
  rejection guarantees `res <= sizeof(buf)-1`, so the manual terminator
  write is always in-bounds. Rule doesn't look past the `readlink()`
  call for a guarded manual terminator.
- **`for_each_element`-family loop-header macros (`ieee802_11_common.h`)
  — CONFIRMED extension of the `16-40_b10` `dl_list_for_each` FP class
  to a second for-loop-header macro family (18 instances, one file).**
  `for_each_element`/`for_each_element_id`/`_extid`/`for_each_subelement`/
  `_id`/`_extid` are all for-loop-header (or loop-header+if) macros built
  by nested composition. PRE00-C/PRE12-C "evaluates multiple times" and
  PRE01-C "not parenthesized" fire on `_elem`/`element`, which is only
  ever used as an lvalue loop-assignment target or through `->`/`*`
  (member-access/dereference, already precedence-safe); PRE02-C "wrap
  entire replacement in parens" and PRE10-C "wrap in do-while(0)" both
  produce invalid C for a macro whose body is a bare `for (...)` header
  (or `for(...) if(...)`) meant to take a following loop body, not a
  self-contained expression or statement block.
- **ARR01-C `sizeof(ptr->buf)` on a genuine fixed-size struct-member
  array reached through a pointer parameter — reinforces the existing
  `l2_packet_ndis.c`/`neighbor_db.c` ARR01-C FP class (2 more
  instances).** `sha256-internal.c:150,189`: `md` is `struct
  sha256_state *`; `md->buf` is `u8 buf[SHA256_BLOCK_SIZE]` (verified
  in `sha256_i.h`), a real fixed-size array field, not a decayed
  parameter array.
- **Crypto round macros (RORc/Ch/Maj/Sigma0/Sigma1/Gamma0/Gamma1/RND in
  `sha256-internal.c`) — CONFIRMED TP, reinforces the MD4
  F1/F2/F3/MD4STEP precedent (`16-40_b8`) with a second hash
  implementation (20 instances).** Each macro genuinely uses its bare
  parameter(s) in bitwise/shift contexts with real precedence/
  multi-evaluation hazards (e.g. `Ch(x,y,z) = (z ^ (x & (y ^ z)))`);
  graded on the macro *definition* independent of today's safe call
  sites, per established precedent. Caveat within this same family:
  parameters used ONLY as a compound-assignment lvalue (`d` in
  `d += t0;`) or ONLY as an array subscript (`i` in `K[i]`/`W[i]`) are
  FP for PRE01-C specifically — no precedence hazard in either context
  — while a parameter used bare as an rvalue operand (`h` in `t0 = h +
  Sigma1(e)+...`) is a real TP. Also: PRE02-C "wrap in parens" is FP
  when the macro body is multiple `;`-separated statements (RND) since
  that's invalid C, but PRE10-C/PRE11-C (do-while(0) wrapping / trailing
  semicolon) ARE real TPs for the same multi-statement macro.
- **MSC13-C "dead assignment" macro-blind to variables used only inside
  a later macro invocation — new mechanism, 1 instance.** `sha256-internal.c:83`'s
  `t0`/`t1` locals are declared, then written and read exclusively
  inside every `RND(...)` macro call later in the function body; sqc's
  liveness analysis doesn't see uses that only occur through macro
  expansion. Same root idea as the confirmed `dl_list_for_each`
  MSC13-C entry (`16-40_b7`), now against a compute macro rather than a
  loop macro.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b19`, 107 findings across 4 files:
src/eap_server/eap_server_tls_common.c, src/eap_server/eap_server_tnc.c,
src/fst/fst_group.c, wpa_supplicant/wifi_display.c)

- **STR00-C "Plain 'char' variable used as array index" misfires on a
  genuinely `int`/`unsigned int` variable — CONFIRMED, rule's own type
  claim is factually wrong (12 instances, one file).**
  `wpa_supplicant/wifi_display.c`'s `subelem` is declared `int subelem;`
  (`wifi_display_subelem_set`/`_get`) or `unsigned int subelem;`
  (`wifi_display_subelem_set_from_ies`) in every flagged instance — never
  `char` — and every use is already range-checked (`subelem < 0 ||
  subelem >= MAX_WFD_SUBELEMS`, or `subelem < MAX_WFD_SUBELEMS` guarding
  the same line) before being used as an index. Double-wrong: the type
  claim is false AND the bounds are already validated.
  `wifi_display.c:290,291,328,333,334,335,342,343,344,374,378,380`.
- **DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable with automatic storage
  duration" misapplied to a `foreach`/`dl_list`-iteration variable that
  points into a long-lived list-linked object — new sub-shape of the
  confirmed DCL30-C heap-vs-stack FP class, CONFIRMED (6 instances, one
  file).** `fst_group.c`'s `foreach_fst_group_iface(g, f)` (and similar
  macros) bind `f`/`other_iface` to whichever `struct fst_iface *` is
  currently linked into the group's `dl_list` — the loop variable is a
  local pointer, but its *pointee* is a heap object owned by the list,
  not this function's automatic storage. Distinct from the
  os_malloc/os_zalloc/wpabuf_alloc heap-return sub-shape already
  documented (comeback_token.c et al.) since there's no allocation call
  at all here, just an iteration binding. `fst_group.c:246,315,370,419,429`.
- **MEM31-C "conditional leak, only freed in one branch" on a
  free-or-return-buffer pattern where the un-freed branch returns the
  buffer to the caller — extends the MEM12-C
  ownership-transfer-on-return FP to MEM31-C.** `fst_group_create_mb_ie`
  frees+NULLs `buf` only when `nof_ifaces_added==0`; the other branch
  doesn't free it because it's about to `return buf;` to the caller
  (both branches reach the same `return buf;`) — not a leak.
  `fst_group.c:169`.
- **MEM30-C false UAF from comparing a freed pointer's *value* (not
  dereferencing it) — new sub-shape, plus a reassignment-blind
  instance.** `eap_server_tls_phase1`'s `WPA_ASSERT(data->tls_out ==
  NULL)` right after `wpabuf_free(data->tls_out)` only reads the pointer
  value for a NULL comparison, never dereferences it — not a real UAF
  even though the field isn't actually nulled first (`eap_server_tls_common.c:342`).
  Three more instances in the same function are a plain reassignment-
  blind tracking bug: `data->tls_out` is unconditionally reassigned by
  `tls_connection_server_handshake()` a few lines later, then read/resized/
  appended-to multiple times afterward with no intervening free — sqc's
  free-state tracking doesn't clear on the struct-field reassignment
  (`eap_server_tls_common.c:348,412,419`). Reinforces the general
  "MEM30-C doesn't see reassignment" theme (task 232 covers local-var
  reassignment; this shows the gap also applies to struct fields).
- **Reinforces the confirmed EAP-method/eloop dispatch-contract DCL13-C
  FP class with a 4th interface: EAP *server-method* `init`/`reset`/
  `check`/`process`/`isDone`/`isSuccess` callbacks wired via
  `eap_server_method_register()`.** `eap_server_tnc.c`'s `eap_tnc_init`,
  `eap_tnc_reset`, `eap_tnc_check`, `eap_tnc_process`, `eap_tnc_isDone`,
  `eap_tnc_isSuccess` all get `sm`/`priv` DCL13-C FPs pinned by the
  `struct eap_method` function-pointer field types (10 instances,
  `eap_server_tnc.c:73,94,323,323,446,540,540,547,547` + the already
  known `eap_server_method_register()` MEM31-C ownership-transfer FP
  once more at `eap_server_tnc.c:558`).
- **Reinforces the EXP30-C pure-accessor-args FP class heavily (8
  instances across 2 files) and the confirmed sizeof(*ptr) EXP33-C class
  (3 instances) and API00-C internal-API-no-NULL-check class (9
  instances) — no new wrinkles, all textbook matches of prior entries.**

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b9`, 106 findings across 3 files:
preauth_test.c, neighbor_db.c, rrm.c)

- **"free"-named helper that only frees an internal field/list, misread
  as freeing the whole object it was passed — NEW pattern, CONFIRMED
  mechanism (2 instances, verified against each callee's source).**
  `pmksa_candidate_free(sm)` (`src/rsn_supp/preauth.c`) frees only
  `sm->pmksa_candidates`'s list nodes, not `sm`; sqc still flags the next
  call `wpa_sm_deinit(wpa_s->wpa)` as a MEM30-C use-after-free of
  `wpa_s->wpa` (`preauth_test.c:195`). `hostapd_free_neighbor_db(hapd)`
  (`src/ap/neighbor_db.c`) frees only `hapd->nr_db`'s list entries, not
  `hapd`; sqc flags the very next line as "passing freed pointer 'hapd'"
  (`rrm.c:613`). Consistent with a name-based "contains 'free'" heuristic
  that doesn't check whether the callee frees its argument or an
  internal collection reachable from it — worth a sqc fix.
- **wpa_sm_ctx callback struct — CONFIRMED extension of the
  eloop/EAP-method-table DCL13-C/API05-C dispatch-contract FP class.**
  `preauth_test.c`'s `wpa_init_conf` wires ~13 static functions into a
  `struct wpa_sm_ctx` (`set_state`, `get_state`, `deauthenticate`,
  `set_key`, `get_network_ctx`, `get_bssid`, `ether_send`,
  `get_beacon_ie`, `alloc_eapol`, `cancel_auth_timeout`, `add_pmkid`,
  `remove_pmkid`, `set_config_blob`, `get_config_blob`,
  `mlme_setprotection`, `reconnect`). Every one of these gets DCL13-C
  and/or API05-C FPs on its `void *wpa_s`/`void *ctx`/`void
  *network_ctx` params — pinned by the struct's function-pointer field
  types, same shape as `wpa_i.h` (`16-40_b8`) and `ap_drv_ops.h`
  (`16-40_b5`), except here the *parameter itself* (not just a field) is
  forwarded, so unlike those two TP-graded cases this one is genuinely
  FP. 13+ instances in one file.
- **API05-C on an opaque `void *` handle, or a `T **` out-param with no
  size — CONFIRMED extension of the ptr+len-pair API05-C FP class.**
  Beyond the ptr-immediately-followed-by-its-len idiom, API05-C also
  fires on plain opaque context handles (`void *wpa_s`/`void *ctx`,
  never treated as arrays, just cast back to a concrete pointer inside
  the callee) and on out-params like `void **data_pos` (a single
  pointer-to-pointer, not an array at all). 6+ opaque-handle instances
  in `preauth_test.c`'s wpa_sm_ctx callbacks; 2 `T**` instances at
  `preauth_test.c:53,80`.
- **EXP34-C null-deref flagged inside `while ((x = f(...)))` whose own
  condition already null-guards `x` — NEW pattern (2 instances, one
  file).** `while ((ie = get_ie(pos, end-pos, EID))) { if (ie[1] < 3)
  ... }` — `ie` cannot be NULL inside the loop body; the
  assignment-as-condition already excludes that case before the body
  runs. `rrm.c:107,310`.
- **FLP03-C "floating-point division without error checking" on integer
  division — NEW pattern, 1 instance, related to the existing
  FLP06/INT33 float-vs-integer-typing confusion family.**
  `rrm.c:177`'s `diff.usec / 100000` operates on `os_time_t` fields
  (plain integers per `src/utils/os.h`) — no floating-point operation
  exists at that line.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b16`, 117 findings across 4 files)

- **DCL13-C on `struct ieee802_1x_kay *kay` params in `src/pae/ieee802_1x_secy_ops.c`
  — CONFIRMED TP, large-scale example of the "plain internal helper, real
  opportunity" clarification.** 24 wrapper functions read `kay->ctx` (and
  sometimes `kay->vf`/`kay->co` by value) but never write through `kay`
  itself and never forward `kay` (only `kay->ctx`/`ops->ctx`, a distinct
  pointer) into a non-const call — const-qualifying `kay` is genuinely
  safe and low-severity-correct. Not the eloop/EAP-method vtable-bound FP
  class (that's about the outer function's own signature matching a fixed
  callback typedef, not about a struct field being forwarded).
- **API00-C real TP by file-internal-consistency argument.** In the same
  file, `secy_cp_control_validate_frames`/`secy_cp_control_confidentiality_offset`
  dereference `kay->vf`/`kay->co` with **no** `if (!kay)` guard, while
  every other one of the file's ~25 sibling functions explicitly checks
  `if (!kay) { ...; return -1; }` first. The "internal-only API, no real
  NULL risk" API00-C FP default doesn't apply when the file itself
  establishes a NULL-check convention and these two functions are the
  outliers — a competent reviewer would flag the inconsistency.
- **ARR01-C "sizeof applied to pointer/array parameter which decayed"
  misapplied to a plain (never-array) pointer parameter — extends the
  confirmed ARR01-C misclassification family.** `eap_pax.c:141,257`:
  `left = req_plen - sizeof(*req);` where `req` is declared
  `const struct eap_pax_hdr *req` (always a pointer, never an array) —
  `sizeof(*req)` correctly yields the struct size via dereference; there
  is no decay bug because there was never an array to decay from. Adds a
  second ARR01-C sub-shape (previous entries were about *non-parameter*
  arrays/fields wrongly called "decayed"; this one is a pointer parameter
  wrongly assumed to have been an array).
- **INT14-C conflates a struct-field bitwise use with pointer-arithmetic
  on the base pointer identifier itself — new sub-shape of the confirmed
  member-conflation family.** `eap_pax.c:134,250,345`: `req->flags &
  EAP_PAX_FLAGS_CE` (bitwise, on a *field*) plus `(req + 1)` /
  `sizeof(*req) + ...` (pointer arithmetic / sizeof-as-arithmetic, on
  `req` itself) get merged into one "req used with both bitwise and
  arithmetic operations" finding — two entirely different operations on
  two different things (a field vs. the pointer) sharing only the base
  identifier name.
- **PRE08-C "header filenames share first 8 characters" — CONFIRMED
  not-applicable / no-real-value.** `ieee802_1x_secy_ops.c:15,16` flags
  `ieee802_1x_kay.h`/`ieee802_1x_kay_i.h`/`ieee802_1x_secy_ops.h` for
  sharing the `ieee802_` prefix. Technically true per rule text (legacy
  8.3-short-filename collision risk), but hostap never targets such
  filesystems and essentially every header in `src/pae/` shares this
  prefix by design — a competent reviewer would not act on this. Treat
  as FP ("not applicable") whenever it fires in this codebase.
- **MEM31-C false leak, 2nd/3rd distinct EAP peer methods** (`eap_pax.c:545`,
  `eap_psk.c:480`) — same `eap_peer_method_register(eap)`
  ownership-transfer FP already confirmed for `eap_md5.c:106`; now 3
  independent instances, fully confirmed as a general EAP-method

- **DCL30-C "returns pointer to local automatic-storage object" on

  `preauth_test.c:57,235` `sizeof(*hdr)`/`sizeof(*ctx)`) with no new
  wrinkle; not re-detailed here.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b15`, 93 findings across 3 files)

- **ARR36-C/ARR00-C "pointers from different arrays" misfired when the
  second pointer is `hdr.payload` derived by nested ASN.1 parsing from
  the *same* underlying buffer — extends the existing "same allocated
  struct/byte buffer" ARR36-C FP class to ASN.1 DER-parsing code.**
  `tls_process_ocsp_single_response`/`tls_process_basic_ocsp_response`
  (`src/tls/tlsv1_client_ocsp.c`) repeatedly call `asn1_get_next(pos,
  end - pos, &hdr)` where `pos`/`end` are always offsets into the
  original `resp` buffer; `hdr.payload` is just `pos` advanced further
  into that same buffer. sqc's alias tracker loses this derivation
  chain through the `struct asn1_hdr` field assignment and reports
  `param:resp` vs `hdr.payload` as distinct arrays. 15 instances in one
  file (`tlsv1_client_ocsp.c:157,161,186,208,241(x2),254,269,270,
  294,296(x2),322,324`) — likely recurs in any ASN.1/TLV-nested-parsing
  file using a `pos`/`end`/`hdr.payload` idiom.
- **STR31-C misapplied to non-char local arrays (`T *addr[1]`,
  `size_t len[1]`) used for the `sha1_vector`/`sha256_vector`-style
  scatter-gather hashing API — CONFIRMED, extends the existing
  "STR31-C misapplied to non-char array" entry.** These are
  single-element pointer/size arrays, never string/char buffers.
  `tlsv1_client_ocsp.c:55,56,70,71` (2 functions, `ocsp_responder_id_match`
  and `ocsp_hash_data`).
- **DCL13-C on plain (non-callback) internal helper functions where the
  param truly is read-only — reinforces the `16-40_b6` clarification
  that this is a genuine (if low-severity) TP, not automatically FP.**
  Confirmed real in `radius_das.c` (`das` in `radius_das_disconnect`/
  `radius_das_coa`, lines 34, 197 — only ever read, never forwarded to
  a non-const call) and `tlsv1_client_ocsp.c` (`oid`, `conn`, `cert`,
  `issuer` in `is_oid_basic_ocsp_resp`/`tls_process_ocsp_single_response`,
  lines 34, 110, 111, 112).
- **CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()`/`inet_ntoa()` thread-safety flagged in
  hostapd's single-threaded eloop core — reinforces the existing
  CON32-C/POS49-C "no pthread in wpa_supplicant core" FP class, now
  extended to CON33/34-C specifically.** `radius_das.c` has no
  pthread usage; 8 instances (`radius_das.c:417,421,512,529,537`).
- **POS02-C "privileged operation without subsequent privilege
  dropping" — CONFIRMED categorical FP for the whole hostapd/wpa_supplicant
  codebase.** Grep for `setuid|setgid|seteuid` across the tree finds
  only an `#ifdef ANDROID`-gated `capset()` privilege-drop in
  `src/utils/os_unix.c:355-367`; standard (non-Android) builds run as
  root for the daemon's entire lifetime by design (continuous
  CAP_NET_ADMIN/nl80211 access needed), with no privilege-separation
  model. Flagging every `bind()`/socket-setup call site
  (`radius_das.c:536`) is a systemic false trigger, not a real
  actionable gap at that line.
- **DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable with automatic storage
  duration" on a heap-allocated (`os_zalloc`/`radius_msg_new`) local
  pointer — reinforces the existing `comeback_token.c`-style DCL30-C FP
  class, now 4 more instances.** `radius_das.c:193,387` (`reply` from
  `radius_msg_new`), `radius_das.c:592` (`das` from `os_zalloc`).
- **MSC01-C "if/else-if chain has no final else" — reinforces the
  existing stylistic-pedantry FP class, 2 more instances.**
  `radius_das.c:465` (optional Event-Timestamp check, no else needed)
  and `tlsv1_client_ocsp.c:632` (unhandled enum values correctly fall
  through to `return res` with no side effect needed).

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b13`, 98 findings across 3 files)

- **Reinforces `16-40_b3`'s confirmed ARR37-C "compound assignment on
  non-array pointer" misfire on a plain `size_t left` byte-counter** —
  recurs 4x in a *different* TLS file this time
  (`tlsv1_server_read.c:161,427,928,1172`, all `left -= 4;`), including
  2 instances where INT30-C also double-fires on the same line despite
  an earlier same-function `if (left < 4)` guard 10-20 lines prior

  the existing INT33-C/INT30-C/ARR30-C entries.

  (`l2_packet_winpcap.c:230,231,232,293`), identical shape to the
  `l2_packet_ndis.c` instances already documented.
- **Reinforces the confirmed MSC01-C "no final else" guard-clause FP
  class** — a new shape: a `while` loop parsing a TLV/extension list
  where an `if/else-if` chain dispatches on known extension types and
  simply skips (via `pos += ext_len` after the chain) any type it
  doesn't recognize — deliberate protocol robustness, not a missing
  case. `tlsv1_server_read.c:372`.
- **Reinforces the confirmed DCL13-C driver-vtable-dispatch FP class
  (`ap_drv_ops.h`/`wpa_i.h`/`preauth_test.c`'s `wpa_sm_ctx`) with a new
  concrete instance: `struct wpa_driver_ops`.** Every callback wired
  into `wpa_driver_roboswitch_ops` (`get_ssid`, `get_bssid`, `get_capa`,
  `get_ifname`) gets a DCL13-C FP on its `void *priv` param, several of
  which don't even use `priv` at all in the stub body — still FP,
  pinned by the `wpa_driver_ops` function-pointer field types, not a
  real const opportunity. `driver_roboswitch.c:183,190,198,233`.
- **NEW: DCL13-C false-positive extended to the `l2_packet` rx_callback
  contract itself (not just eloop/EAP-method tables).** A driver's RX
  handler passed as the `rx_callback` argument to `l2_packet_init()`
  must match the fixed `void (*)(void *ctx, const u8 *src_addr, const
  u8 *buf, size_t len)` typedef; DCL13-C flags its unmodified `void
  *priv` param anyway. `driver_roboswitch.c:172`
  (`wpa_driver_roboswitch_receive`).
- **NEW: DCL15-C/DCL19-C "should be static / minimize scope" firing on
  a driver's `struct wpa_driver_ops` table that has genuine, verified

  wpa_driver_ops wpa_driver_roboswitch_ops;` plus a live reference
  (`&wpa_driver_roboswitch_ops` in `drivers.c`'s driver table) — the
  external linkage is required, not an oversight. `driver_roboswitch.c:477`.
  Likely generalizes to every other `wpa_driver_*_ops` table in

- **NEW: EXP34-C null-deref flagged on a pointer that is the result of

  mii_ioctl_data *) &rq->ifr_ifru` — an `&`-expression is never a null
  pointer, yet both call sites of the returned `mii` are flagged as a

- **NEW: CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()` non-thread-safety flagged in a
  driver backend with zero pthread usage — extends the existing
  CON32-C/POS49-C "wpa_supplicant core is single-threaded" entry to a

  FN pattern for future batches: an ioctl-driver `_init()` that opens a

  `wpa_driver_roboswitch_init()` opens `drv->fd = socket(...)` near the

  idiom is common across this directory).

## Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed (from `16-40_b13`)

- WIN04-C "function pointer stored without encryption" misfired twice
  on a plain integer/version-constant assignment through a struct field
  (`conn->rl.tls_version = TLS_VERSION_1_2;` and `= conn->client_version;`)
  — no function pointer exists anywhere near these lines at all.
  `tlsv1_server_read.c:197,200`. Looks like a severe rule-engine bug
  (not a naming heuristic), only one file/function seen so far.
- MSC13-C "dead assignment" misfired twice inside the same short
  if/else-if/else chain assigning `conn->rl.tls_version`, each claiming
  the value is never read when in fact all branches converge on a read
  2-5 lines later (`tlsv1_server_log(conn, "Using TLS v%s", ...
  conn->rl.tls_version)`) — rule doesn't see the post-chain convergence
  read. One finding even cites `'if'` as the assigned-to variable name,
  suggesting a parser confusion distinct from the ordinary dead-assignment
  logic. `tlsv1_server_read.c:200,203`.
- DCL31-C "called without prior declaration" misfired on two functions
  that are, in fact, already fully defined earlier in the very same
  file, well before the flagged call site (`tls_process_certificate_verify`
  defined at line 884, called at line 1299; `tls_process_client_finished`
  defined at line 1095, called at line 1307) — a real tool bug distinct
  from the already-documented "external Win32 header not parsed"
  DCL31-C FP shape (`16-40_b2`). `tlsv1_server_read.c:1299,1307`.
- MEM30-C "use-after-free" misfired on `&conn->client_rsa_key` (address
  of a just-freed struct field) passed as an *output* parameter to
  reinitialize it (`crypto_public_key_free(conn->client_rsa_key);
  tls_parse_cert(pos, cert_len, &conn->client_rsa_key)`) — the freed
  value is never read, only overwritten via the out-param; a new shape

  family. `tlsv1_server_read.c:518`. 1 instance so far.
- INT32-C "signed integer addition may overflow" misapplied to array-
  to-pointer-decay arithmetic (`_read + 1` where `_read` is `u16
  _read[2]`) — this is pointer arithmetic advancing by one element
  within a 2-element array, not integer addition at all.
  `driver_roboswitch.c:426`. 1 instance so far.
- API05-C "size variable declared after the array parameter" misfired
  on a `#define`d compile-time constant used as an array-size

- DCL13-C "rq is not modified" on `if_mii(struct ifreq *rq)`, which

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b11`, 103 findings across 3 files)

- **Empty-stub `.c` file (`os_none.c`-style OS shim) — DCL13-C on unused
  params is a genuine (if trivial) TP, API05-C on the ptr+size_t
  companion idiom is FP.** `src/utils/os_none.c` is a documented
  "starting point when adding a new OS target" — every function body is
  a no-op or `return -1/0/NULL`. Every pointer parameter is therefore
  provably 100% unused, same reasoning as the existing `#ifdef`-stub
  DCL13-C TP entry, just applied to a whole file of always-stub bodies
  rather than one `#else` branch (16 TPs this batch). Every API05-C
  finding in the same file is the already-confirmed ptr+size_t-len/size/n
  companion-param idiom (`os_get_random`, `os_memdup`, `os_realloc`,
  `os_memcpy`/`os_memmove` dest+src+n, `os_memset`, `os_memcmp`/
  `os_strncasecmp`/`os_strncmp` two-arrays-one-length, `os_strlcpy`,
  `os_memcmp_const`, `os_snprintf`) — 19 more confirmed API05-C FPs.
- **DCL13-C on EAP-peer-method internal (non-vtable) helper functions —
  clarifies the b6 "not automatically FP" rule with a concrete negative
  case.** `eap_sake.c`'s `eap_sake_process_identity`/`_challenge`/
  `_confirm` take an `sm` param purely for signature symmetry with
  their sibling dispatch function, but never reference `sm` in the
  body at all, and are only ever called internally by
  `eap_sake_process` (never assigned to any `struct eap_method` field)
  — genuine low-severity TP (3 instances: `eap_sake.c:140,183,285`).
  Contrast with the *actual* vtable-registered functions in the same
  file (`eap_sake_deinit`→`eap->deinit`, `eap_sake_isKeyAvailable`→
  `eap->isKeyAvailable`, `eap_sake_getKey`→`eap->getKey`,
  `eap_sake_get_session_id`→`eap->getSessionId`, `eap_sake_get_emsk`→
  `eap->get_emsk`), where DCL13-C on `sm`/`priv` remains the confirmed
  EAP-method-table FP (6 instances). The distinguishing test: is this
  exact function name assigned into an `eap->field` (or other
  callback/vtable field), not merely "does it look like an EAP method
  function."
- **MEM31-C false leak on a struct-field allocation whose lifetime is
  tied to the enclosing heap object, freed later by a dedicated
  destructor — new sub-pattern of the ownership-transfer MEM31-C FP
  family.** `p2p_sd.c`'s `p2p_sd_request()` allocates `q = os_zalloc(...)`,
  sets `q->tlvs = wpabuf_dup(tlvs)`, links `q` into `p2p->sd_queries`,
  and returns `q` as an opaque request handle. `q->tlvs` is correctly
  freed later via `p2p_free_sd_query()`/`p2p_free_sd_queries()`
  (`wpabuf_free(q->tlvs)`) whenever the query completes or is canceled
  — not a leak, just a lifetime that outlives the allocating function.
  2 instances (`p2p_sd.c:893,917`). Distinct from the `eap_peer_method_register()`-style
  "callee frees on every path" shape — here the *caller-returned handle
  itself* owns the field until an explicit destructor call much later.
- **MEM30-C reassign-then-check misfire — 3rd confirmed instance of the
  reassign-doesn't-clear-freed-state gap, now on a struct field rather
  than a local.** `p2p_sd_response()` frees `p2p->sd_resp` (if
  non-NULL) at line 447, unconditionally reassigns it to a fresh
  `wpabuf_dup()` result at line 449, then checks `p2p->sd_resp == NULL`
  at line 450 — sqc reports this NULL-check as a use-after-free access
  of the freed pointer, not recognizing the intervening reassignment.
  Same root cause as the `tls_openssl_ocsp.c` reassign-then-free class
  documented in `16-40_b7`, but this time on a struct field
  (`p2p->sd_resp`) instead of a local variable, and the manifesting
  rule is MEM30-C (use-after-free) rather than MEM31-C (double-free).
  `p2p_sd.c:450`.
- **INT14-C conflates a pointer's own arithmetic with bitwise ops on
  its dereferenced value — new shape of the base-identifier-conflation
  FP.** `p2p_sd.c:736`: `pos` (a `const u8 *`) is only ever advanced via
  ordinary pointer arithmetic (`pos++`, `pos += 2`), while `*pos & 0x7f`
  / `(*pos & 0x80) >> 7` (both reads of the *pointee byte*, assigned to
  `frag_id`/`more_frags`) are the only bitwise uses — the rule doesn't
  distinguish the pointer identifier from its dereference. Same
  underlying "matches on base identifier only" bug as the existing
  `p2p_sd.c:57`/`p2p_invitation.c:282` entries, now confirmed a 3rd way.
- API00-C's internal-only-API FP class held up broadly in this batch:
  every `p2p_sd.c` API00-C finding (10 instances: `p2p_pending_sd_req`,
  `p2p_free_sd_queries`, `p2p_rx_gas_initial_req`(x2 params),
  `p2p_sd_response`, `p2p_rx_gas_initial_resp`, `p2p_rx_gas_comeback_req`,
  `p2p_rx_gas_comeback_resp`, `p2p_sd_request`, `p2p_sd_request_wfd`,
  `p2p_sd_service_update`) is an internal p2p-module function always
  invoked by `p2p.c`/`p2p_i.h` machinery with an already-valid `p2p`
  handle or non-NULL `sa`/`data` pointer sourced from validated RX
  frame processing — none externally exposed to a possibly-NULL caller.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `16-40_b17`, 118 findings across 4 files:
tlsv1_common.c, wps_dev_attr.c, taxonomy.c, dh_groups.c)

- **MEM30-C "reassign-then-check" now confirmed on a struct FIELD target
  (not just a bare local variable) — NEW shape, 5 instances one file.**
  `wps_dev_attr.c`'s `wps_process_manufacturer`/`_model_name`/
  `_model_number`/`_serial_number`/`_dev_name` all do
  `os_free(dev->manufacturer); dev->manufacturer = dup_binstr(str,
  str_len); if (dev->manufacturer == NULL) return -1;` — sqc flags the
  `if` check as accessing a freed pointer, missing that the field was
  reassigned to a fresh allocation one line earlier. The `MEM30
  reassign + fresh-binding fix` (task 232) evidently covers bare local
  variables/fresh declarations but not this `os_free(ptr->field);
  ptr->field = fresh_alloc();` struct-field shape — worth a regression
  look. Lines 272, 291, 310, 329, 348.
- **ARR02-C "implicit array bounds" on a file-scope initializer array
  whose size is always retrieved via `sizeof()`/`ARRAY_SIZE()` —
  CONFIRMED FP, 12 instances across 2 files.** The size-mismatch risk
  ARR02-C exists to prevent never materializes when every consumer uses
  `sizeof(the_array)` or an `ARRAY_SIZE()`-derived macro instead of a
  separately hardcoded literal. Seen on `tls_cipher_suites[]`/
  `tls_ciphers[]` (`tlsv1_common.c:26,76`, paired with
  `NUM_TLS_CIPHER_SUITES`/`NUM_TLS_CIPHER_DATA` `ARRAY_SIZE()` macros)
  and on all of `dh_group{22,23,24}_{generator,prime,order}[]` plus
  `dh_groups[]` itself (`dh_groups.c:947-1156`, each field's size comes
  from `sizeof(dh_group##id##_x)` inside the `DH_GROUP()` macro).
  `dh_groups[]` additionally reconfirms the existing "size legitimately
  varies by `#ifdef`" carve-out (`ALL_DH_GROUPS`), same as the
  `wpa_drivers[]` precedent.
- **STR31-C "character array too small to hold string data" misapplied
  to a 1-byte raw binary value array — CONFIRMED FP, extends the
  non-char/non-string STR31-C misapplication family, 8 instances one
  file.** `dh_groups.c`'s `dh_group{1,2,5,14,15,16,17,18}_generator[1] =
  { 0x02 }` is a single raw DH generator byte, not string data at all —
  the "too small for a NUL terminator" framing is a category error since
  no string was ever intended. Lines 23, 57, 101, 161, 235, 341, 479,
  681.
- **PRE00-C/PRE01-C/PRE12-C misfire on a token-paste-only (`##`) macro
  parameter — 2nd confirmed instance of the X-macro-generator FP class
  (first was `wnm_ap.c:673`, batch `16-40_b9`), now promotable.**
  `dh_groups.c`'s `#define DH_GROUP(id,safe) { id, dh_group##id##_generator,
  sizeof(dh_group##id##_generator), ... safe }` — `id` is only ever
  used via `##` token-pasting to build identifiers (never evaluated as
  a runtime expression), so "evaluates multiple times"/"needs
  parenthesizing" are category errors; `safe` is a bare trailing
  struct-field literal, not a computed expression. `dh_groups.c:1150`.
- **MEM30-C "accessing member of freed pointer" on a caller-owned
  struct pointer whose free-helper only finishes/NULLs internal
  sub-object handles — extends the existing "helper frees a sub-field,
  not the whole object" conflation family (was previously seen on heap
  pointers via `os_free`; now confirmed on non-heap crypto-handle
  fields via `crypto_hash_finish`), 13 instances one function.**
  `tls_verify_hash_init` calls `tls_verify_hash_free(verify)` (which
  only calls `crypto_hash_finish()` on each hash-context field and NULLs
  it — `verify` itself, a caller-owned stack/embedded struct, is never
  freed) then immediately re-checks `verify->md5_client` etc. for NULL;
  sqc treats the whole `verify` object as freed. `tlsv1_common.c:207-
  222`.
- **MSC09-C "non-ASCII byte in string/character literal" misapplied to
  a deliberate binary byte-sequence literal used for `os_memcmp`, not
  human-readable text — NEW pattern, 3 instances one function.**
  `tls_verify_signature`'s DER `DigestInfo` OID-prefix comparisons
  (`os_memcmp(buf, "\x30\x31\x30\x0d\x06\x09\x60\x86\x48\x01..." , 19)`)
  use string literals purely as raw byte-pattern constants; MSC09-C's
  locale/portability concern is inapplicable to byte-for-byte protocol
  constant matching. `tlsv1_common.c:476,483,490`.
- **MEM31-C false double-free on a `wpabuf **out` param reassigned via
  `wpabuf_clear_free(*p); *p = wpabuf_alloc(...);` before later
  error-path frees — extends the reassign-then-free FP class to a
  double-indirection out-param, 2 instances one function (also
  mutually exclusive from each other).** `dh_init`'s `*priv` is freed
  and reassigned once near the top; the two later
  `wpabuf_clear_free(*priv)` calls (on the `pv==NULL` failure branch and
  the `crypto_dh_init` failure branch, which cannot both execute) each
  free the *new* allocation, never re-freeing the original.
  `dh_groups.c:1209,1217`.
- **DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable with automatic storage
  duration" confused a local pointer VARIABLE with local storage on a
  heap-backed `struct wpabuf *` — reinforces the `comeback_token.c`/
  `ieee802_11_ht.c`/`ieee802_11_vht.c` precedent, 2 more instances.**
  `dh_init`'s `pv` and `dh_derive_shared`'s `shared` are both assigned
  from `wpabuf_alloc()` (heap) before being returned; only the pointer
  *variable* is local automatic storage, not the memory it references.
  `dh_groups.c:1226,1265`.
- **EXP30-C "unsequenced side effects" on pure `wpabuf_head`/

  existing accessor-args FP class, 4 more instances across 2 files.**
  `wps_dev_attr.c:208,233` (`wpabuf_head_u8`/`wpabuf_len` in hexdump
  calls), `dh_groups.c:1213,1251` (`wpabuf_mhead`/`wpabuf_head`/
  `wpabuf_len` in `crypto_dh_init`/`crypto_dh_derive_secret` calls).
- **DCL13-C real (if low-severity) TP class reinforced, now including a
  case where the flagged param is entirely unused.** `wps_dev_attr.c`'s
  ~14 `wps_build_*`/`wps_process_device_attrs` functions only read
  `dev`/`attr` fields (never forwarded to a vtable/callback and never

- **API00-C/API05-C internal-only-API and ptr+len-pair FP classes

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `16-40_b20`, 106 findings across 4 files:
nan_usd_ap.c, pasn_common.c, wps_supplicant.h, accounting.c)

- **EXP33-C output-param-uninitialized misfire now confirmed through an
  INDIRECT function-pointer/vtable call, not just a direct callee —
  extends the `ieee802_11_parse_elems`/`wps_parse_msg` unconditional-
  memset-first FP family one hop further.** `accounting.c`'s
  `accounting_sta_update_stats`/`accounting_sta_report` declare `struct
  hostap_sta_driver_data data;` uninitialized and pass `&data` through
  `hostapd_drv_read_sta_data()` (an inline wrapper) into
  `hapd->driver->read_sta_data(...)`, a driver vtable call. The actual
  registered implementation for the nl80211 backend,
  `driver_nl80211_read_sta_data()` (`driver_nl80211.c:11540`), does
  `os_memset(data, 0, sizeof(*data))` before delegating to
  `i802_read_sta_data()`, whose async netlink callback
  (`get_sta_handler`) then only conditionally overwrites individual
  fields (e.g. `data->bytes_64bit` stays 0 unless both 64-bit netlink
  attrs are present). sqc can't see through the vtable indirection to
  the callee's memset, so it flags `data.bytes_64bit`/`data.rx_packets`
  reads as uninitialized-use. FP (`accounting.c:212,296`), but flag:
  this pattern is only as safe as every registered `read_sta_data`
  backend actually memsetting up front — worth spot-checking other
  drivers (`driver_bsd.c` etc.) if this ever needs re-litigating.
- **DCL40-C "incompatible declarations" across mutually-exclusive
  `#ifdef`/`#else` branches — 2nd confirmed instance, promoting the
  `16-40_b10` `x_snoop.h` entry out of batch-local.**
  `wps_supplicant.h:109`: the `#ifdef CONFIG_WPS` prototype
  `enum wps_request_type wpas_wps_get_req_type(struct wpa_ssid *ssid);`
  (line 31) and the `#else` stub `static inline u8
  wpas_wps_get_req_type(...)` (line 109) are never both compiled
  together, but sqc compares them as if they were two declarations of
  one visible function and flags the return-type mismatch (`enum
  wps_request_type` vs `u8`). Same preprocessor-branch-blind root cause
  as the `STRUCT_PACKED`/`x_snoop.h` entries.
- **DCL13-C dispatch-bound-callback FP family reconfirmed on a new
  vtable shape: NAN USD callback table (`struct nan_callbacks` in
  `nan_de.h`).** All `void *ctx` params of `hostapd_nan_de_tx`/
  `_discovery_result`/`_replied`/`_publish_terminated`/
  `_subscribe_terminated`/`_receive` in `nan_usd_ap.c` are fixed by
  `nan_callbacks` struct-field function-pointer typedefs (`cb.tx = ...`
  etc. at `nan_usd_ap.c:155-161`) — same shape as the eloop-handler/EAP-
  method-table family, just a new dispatch table. 6 instances
  (`nan_usd_ap.c:39,47,71,108,119,130`).
- **API05-C misapplied to a `void *` opaque callback-context parameter
  with no size/array pairing at all — new sub-shape of the API05-C
  ptr+len-idiom FP family.** `accounting_receive`'s `void *data`
  (`accounting.c:414`) is the fixed `RadiusRxResult` callback-context
  slot registered via `radius_client_register(hapd->radius, RADIUS_ACCT,
  accounting_receive, hapd)` — not an array, no companion size
  parameter anywhere in the signature; API05-C's array-syntax
  suggestion is a category error here, and the paired DCL13-C
  "not modified" finding on the same param is the now-familiar
  dispatch-bound-callback FP applied to a 3rd callback family (RADIUS
  client RX, alongside eloop and NAN USD above).
- **API00-C integer-overflow-flavored variant ("does not validate
  integer parameter for overflow before arithmetic") on protocol-
  bounded arithmetic — extends the existing "rule doesn't see
  realistic protocol-level bounds" INT30/INT32/INT33/ARR30 family to
  this API00-C wording.** `pasn_add_encrypted_data`'s `data_len`
  (`pasn_common.c:268`, feeding `os_zalloc(data_len + pad_len)` at line
  284 and the `padded_data[data_len] = 0xdd` write at line 289) has
  exactly one caller (`p2p.c:6912`, `p2p_pasn_add_encrypted_data`),
  always sized from a locally-built P2P2 IE (`wpabuf_mhead_u8`/
  `wpabuf_len`), realistically bounded to a few hundred bytes by 802.11
  element-size limits — nowhere near `size_t` overflow range. FP for
  both the API00-C overflow finding and the paired ARR30-C
  `padded_data[data_len]` finding at line 289 (same root cause, same
  caller).

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b21`, 102 findings across 4 files:
src/ap/wpa_auth.h, src/common/wpa_ctrl.h, src/ap/mbo_ap.c, src/common/gas_server.c)

- **MSC41-C "hard-coded sensitive information" misfiring on ctrl_iface/
  wpa_msg event-*name* macros — CONFIRMED FP, new sub-shape distinct
  from the existing `wpa_hexdump_key` label-string entry (21 instances,
  one file).** `src/common/wpa_ctrl.h` defines wire-protocol event tags
  like `#define WPA_EVENT_PASSWORD_CHANGED "CTRL-EVENT-PASSWORD-CHANGED "`,
  `#define DPP_EVENT_C_SIGN_KEY "DPP-C-SIGN-KEY "`, `#define
  WPS_EVENT_PIN_NEEDED "WPS-PIN-NEEDED "`. These are ctrl_iface
  event-name string constants (monitor-socket message prefixes), not
  actual secret material — the rule appears to pattern-match on
  security-sounding substrings (PASSWORD/KEY/PIN/AUTH) in the macro
  name/string alone. Seen 21x in `wpa_ctrl.h` (lines 34, 38, 109, 161,
  164, 199, 200, 204, 212, 216, 217, 218, 257, 258, 283, 285, 361, 366,
  367, 368, 473).
- **MEM30-C conflates "helper frees a sub-list/field hanging off `*ptr`"
  with "`*ptr` itself is freed" — 2nd confirmed instance of the
  `tlsv1_client_read.c:688`-style class, different shape (linked-list
  field vs. OpenSSL sub-object).** `mbo_ap_sta_free(sta)`
  (`mbo_ap.c:19-30`) only frees the nodes of `sta->non_pref_chan`'s
  linked list and NULLs that one field; `sta` itself is never freed and
  remains valid. sqc flags every subsequent `mbo_ap_parse_non_pref_chan(sta,
  ...)`/`mbo_ap_wnm_notif_req_cell_capa(sta, ...)` call after
  `mbo_ap_sta_free(sta)` as passing a freed pointer. 3 instances
  (`mbo_ap.c:109,194,197`).
- **`dl_list_for_each` search-and-capture idiom (`tmp` loop var copied
  into an outer `T *result = NULL;` local, used after the loop) —
  CONFIRMED FP for both MSC13-C and DCL30-C, 2 instances/2 functions.**
  `gas_server_set_resp`/`gas_server_set_comeback_delay`
  (`gas_server.c:483-532`) both declare `struct gas_server_response *tmp,
  *response = NULL;`, assign `response = tmp;` inside a
  `dl_list_for_each` loop, then read `response` in the very next
  statement after the loop (`if (!response || ...)`). (a) MSC13-C "dead
  assignment" is wrong because `response` is read immediately after the
  loop — extends the existing `eth_p_oui.c:93`-style dl_list_for_each
  post-loop-read blind spot to a second file/shape. (b) DCL30-C "local
  variable assigned to global/static variable" is *additionally* wrong
  on its own terms: both `tmp` and `response` are ordinary automatic
  locals in the same function — there is no global/static object
  anywhere in either function. Lines `gas_server.c:491,518` (both
  findings at each line).

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b22`, 100 findings across 4 files:
src/crypto/crypto.h, src/drivers/driver_nl80211_monitor.c, src/drivers/rfkill.c,
src/eap_peer/eap_proxy_dummy.c)

- **`num_elem` + `addr[]` + `len` hash-vector API — API02-C/ARR02-C
  reconfirmed (12 instances, one header).** `crypto.h`'s
  `md4/md5/sha1/sha256/sha384/sha512_vector(size_t num_elem, const u8
  *addr[], const size_t *len, u8 *mac)` is the exact `aes_siv.h`/
  `aes_wrap.h` vector-API shape already confirmed FP for both rules —
  `len` is already the per-element size array, and `addr[]`'s bound is
  conveyed by `num_elem`, not a fixed array dimension. Lines 34, 44, 55,
  81, 92, 103 (×2 rules each).
- **pkcs1/outlen-style "size_t *len already present" — API02-C
  reconfirmed (7 instances, one header).** `crypto_hash_finish`,
  `crypto_*_pkcs1(_v15)`, `crypto_dh_derive_secret`, `crypto_mod_exp`,
  `crypto_csr_get_attribute` (`crypto.h:215,351,368,385,418,424,468,
  1279`) all already carry a `size_t *len`/`*outlen`/`*plain_len`/
  `*result_len` out-parameter; API02-C's "add a size_t parameter" fix
  ignores it. Same FP class as `pkcs1.h` from the original audit batch.
- **API05-C "conformant array syntax" on a bare `const char *passwd`
  string argument — new sub-shape, not just the ptr+len pair.**
  `crypto_private_key_import`'s `passwd` (`crypto.h:319`) is a
  NUL-terminated C string (or NULL), not a length-prefixed buffer at
  all — there is no size argument to declare because none is needed.
- **DCL37-C on `__must_check` — judged TP, not FP, unlike the
  `_LINUX_TYPES_H` shadowing case.** `crypto.h:437` defines
  `__must_check` itself (`common.h:495`, `__attribute__((warn_unused_result))`)
  — a real double-underscore reserved identifier per C 7.1.3, and
  (unlike `_LINUX_TYPES_H`, which shadows an external kernel header this
  code must interoperate with) there's no comparable external-contract
  reason for hostap to own this exact name. Low severity but a genuine,
  literal violation.
- **EXP33-C "uninitialized"/"dereference of uninitialized pointer" on a
  stack struct passed by address to `read()` — CONFIRMED FP, new
  root-cause sub-shape of the sizeof(*ptr) family.** `rfkill.c:74,154`:
  `struct rfkill_event event; len = read(fd, &event, sizeof(event));
  ... if (len == RFKILL_EVENT_SIZE_V1) { ...event.op... }` — `read()` is
  a well-known write-through syscall; once the length check confirms a
  full read, every field of `event` is populated. sqc doesn't recognize
  `read()`/`recv()`-style syscalls as initializing their output-buffer
  argument (parallel to the already-known WPS `os_memset`-first
  output-param gap, but via a syscall instead of a local helper).
- **MSC13-C "dead assignment" misses a read that occurs only as a
  function-call argument — CONFIRMED FP, 3 instances in one function
  family.** `rfkill.c:164` (`rfk_phy`, read via `os_strcmp(phy,
  rfk_phy)` on the very next-but-one line before `free(rfk_phy)`),
  `:188`/`:198` (`phy`, read via the same `os_strcmp` call earlier and/or
  consumed as the argument to `free(phy)` on that branch) — sqc's
  liveness view doesn't count "used only inside a function-call
  argument position" as a read, so it calls the value dead right before
  the free that actually needs it.
- **MEM30-C/MEM31-C double-free — reconfirmed, mutually-exclusive
  `goto fail`/`goto fail2` branches.** `rfkill.c:198`: `phy` is freed
  either at line 188 (success path, after `!found` check fails to skip)
  or at line 198 (`fail:`, reached only via `goto fail`/`goto fail2`
  from earlier failure branches) — never both on the same execution.
  Same root cause as the `wnm_ap.c`/`eap_server_psk.c` instances in
  earlier batches.
- **DCL30-C "returns pointer to local automatic-storage object" —
  reconfirmed, heap pointer conflated with local storage.**
  `rfkill.c:191`: `rfkill_init` returns `rfkill`, a local pointer
  *variable* whose value is `os_zalloc()`-allocated heap memory, not a
  stack object. Same shape as the `comeback_token.c` precedent.
- **Whole-file build-alternative dummy stub — DCL13-C extension of the
  `#ifdef/#else` no-op-stub pattern to an entire `_dummy.c` file,
  judged TP (low severity).** `eap_proxy_dummy.c` is a build-swap stub
  (only implementation of `eap_proxy.h` present in this tree; the real
  Qualcomm QMI implementation lives outside the open-source tree) where
  every function body is trivial (`return NULL/0/-1;` or empty) — every
  parameter is 100% unused, so const-qualifying them is a real, harmless,
  low-value opportunity, not FP-by-vtable-contract (there's no
  function-pointer struct here, just plain extern declarations). All 21
  DCL13-C findings in this file: TP (low).
- **CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()` — reconfirmed for driver code
  (`driver_nl80211_monitor.c`, `rfkill.c`), no pthread found.**
- **POS02-C "bind without privilege drop" — reconfirmed
  (`driver_nl80211_monitor.c:125`).**
- **PRE08-C 8.3-filename collision — reconfirmed FP
  (`driver_nl80211_monitor.c:19`, `ieee802_11_defs.h`/`_common.h`).**

## Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed (from `16-40_b22`)

- FIO47-C misparsed which call argument binds to a `%s` format
  specifier, blaming the *size* argument (`IFNAMSIZ`, the 2nd
  `snprintf` parameter) instead of the actual vararg
  (`drv->first_bss->ifname + 4`) for a claimed pointer/integer type
  mismatch — the real vararg is a valid `char *`.
  `driver_nl80211_monitor.c:83`.

  buffer is unconditionally NUL-terminated (`buf[IFNAMSIZ-1] = '\0';`)
  a few lines later regardless of which branch ran — the explicit
  terminator already neutralizes the only real risk truncation would
  pose. `driver_nl80211_monitor.c:83`.
- DCL39-C "struct passed to trust-boundary function may leak padding
  bytes" misapplied to a `struct msghdr` argument to `sendmsg()` — the
  `msghdr` itself is a local kernel-API descriptor consumed in-process
  by the syscall, never serialized/transmitted to the peer (only the
  `iovec` payload is sent); padding-leak concerns don't apply to a
  control structure that never crosses the wire. `driver_nl80211_monitor.c:188`.
- POS01-C "open() without O_NOFOLLOW/lstat" fired on a hardcoded,
  root-owned device path (`open("/dev/rfkill", O_RDONLY)`) — `/dev` is
  not attacker-writable on any normal system, so there's no realistic
  symlink-race actor here. `rfkill.c:126`.

  `struct iovec.iov_base` for an outbound `sendmsg()` — POSIX's
  `iovec.iov_base` is unconditionally non-const even for pure-output
  use; the underlying buffer is only ever read, never written through
  this cast. `driver_nl80211_monitor.c:165`.

  decayed-array pointer passed to a mutating function call — looks

  are each subsequently passed as `(u8 *) name` into

  writes the parsed attribute into the buffer. sqc's "never modified"
  scan doesn't follow the array-to-pointer decay into the call to see

  struct members and whole-struct sizeof via a pointer parameter.**

  real member array), `eap_user_db.c:170` (`sizeof(hapd->tmp_eap_user)`
  — not even an array, a struct member). 5 instances this batch alone,
  now a large, well-established rule-logic gap: the rule doesn't
  distinguish "sizeof of the pointer's own decayed type" from "sizeof
  of a member/dereferenced object reached through the pointer."

- **Free/access-tracking mutually-exclusive-branch FP reconfirmed for

- **EXP33-C "reading uninitialized data" misfire on an output
  parameter written by an ordinary (non-macro) function call —

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `16-40_b18`, 113 findings across 4 files)

- **INT30-C mislabels pointer-arithmetic on a `u8 *`/`const u8 *` variable
  as "unsigned integer" wrap-around — CONFIRMED, new sub-shape (9
  instances in one file, distinct from the existing bounded-loop
  INT30-C entry).** `eap_sake_common.c`'s `eap_sake_compute_mic` has a
  local `u8 *pos` used purely for pointer bump/advance
  (`pos += peerid_len`, `*pos++ = 0`, `pos + (mic_pos - eap)`); INT30-C
  fires with "Unsigned integer compound addition/increment ... may
  wrap" even though the flagged variable is a pointer, not an unsigned
  integer type at all — and separately, every increment is bounded by
  the `tmplen` the destination buffer was `os_malloc`'d with. Two
  independent FP reasons stacked on the same findings
  (`eap_sake_common.c:193,355,357,360,362,370,372,375,377,385`). Watch
  for this whenever INT30-C fires on a `pos`/`p` style pointer variable
  rather than a genuine size_t/unsigned-int counter — check the
  declared type before crediting the finding.
- **API00-C flags a boolean 0/1 flag parameter for "integer overflow
  validation before arithmetic" despite the parameter never being used
  in any arithmetic expression — CONFIRMED rule bug, 1 clear instance.**
  `eap_sake_compute_mic`'s `int peer` is only ever tested via
  `if (peer)`; API00-C's overflow-validation sub-check still fires on
  it as though it participated in size/length arithmetic.
  `eap_sake_common.c:335`.
- **EXP40-C fires despite the "const" pointer in its own message not
  actually being const-qualified — CONFIRMED rule bug.** `wmm.c:104`:
  `u8 *pos = eid;` where `eid` is declared as plain `u8 *eid` (not
  const) in `hostapd_eid_wmm`'s own signature; EXP40-C's "pointer to
  const assigned to non-const pointer without cast" message describes
  a scenario that doesn't exist in this code at all.
- **INT14-C misattributes a bitwise+arithmetic conflict to the callee
  function/macro identifier itself (`le_to_host16`) instead of the
  variable actually receiving its result — CONFIRMED new sub-shape of
  the existing member-conflation family.** `wmm.c:251`: `val =
  le_to_host16(...)` then `val >> 13` (bitwise) and `10000 * (val &
  0x1fff)` — all real operations are on `val`; `le_to_host16` is a
  macro name, never a variable, yet it's the identifier named in the
  finding.
- **STR00-C flags a struct for using "signed char" when no such field
  exists anywhere in the struct at all — CONFIRMED rule bug (fabricated
  finding), 1 instance.** `dpp.h:357`: `struct dpp_config_obj`'s `ssid`
  field is `u8 ssid[SSID_MAX_LEN]` (unsigned uint8_t); grepped the
  whole struct body, no `signed char` field is present anywhere.
- **API01-C misapplied to a nested/anonymous struct-typed field standing
  in for "the buffer," compared against an unrelated field of the
  *enclosing* struct many lines later — extends the confirmed API01-C
  categorical-FP class to cross-struct-nesting-level comparisons.**
  `dpp.h:357`: flags `struct dpp_config_obj { ... }` (a whole nested
  struct, containing its own char arrays followed by its own pointer
  fields) as "before" `dpp_authentication`'s outer-level
  `conf_key_pkg` pointer field — not a real single-buffer-then-pointer

- **DCL40-C 31-significant-character external-identifier collision on a

  `_..._override_len` share their first 31 characters. Technically
  matches the rule's literal (historical C89 linker) concern, but every
  realistic toolchain hostap targets (GCC/Clang/MSVC) supports far more

- **API05-C on a plain NUL-terminated C-string parameter (`const char
  *name`/`*identifier`/`*channel_list`/`*own_connector`, no paired
  length param) — extends the confirmed ptr+len-pair API05-C FP class
  to the equally-idiomatic "it's a C string, length is the NUL" case.**
  6+ instances in `dpp.h` alone (channel_list x3, identifier x2,
  own_connector x1).
- **API05-C/API02-C on a fixed-size well-known-length buffer (`const u8
  *own_mac`, ETH_ALEN/6 bytes by hostap-wide convention) or a
  self-terminating sentinel array (`int *opclasses`, consumed via
  `int_array_len()`) — extends the paired-len FP class to two more
  "size is implied, not missing" sub-shapes.** `dpp.h:614` (opclasses),
  `dpp.h:683` (own_mac).

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b4`, 150 findings, 1 file:
wpa_supplicant/ctrl_iface.c, lines 3412-5293)

- **DCL30-C/ARR36-C/INT32-C triple-misfire on the `pos`/`end`/`start`
  wire-formatting helper idiom — CONFIRMED, massive volume (60+
  instances in one file, largest single-batch reinforcement so far).**
  hostap's many `print_*`/`anqp_add_hex`-style helpers
  (`anqp_add_hex`, `print_fils_indication`, `print_rnr`, `print_ml`,
  `ctrl_iface_get_capability_*`) all follow `T *fn(char *pos, char *end,
  ...) { char *start = pos; ...; ret = os_snprintf(pos, end-pos, ...);
  if (os_snprintf_error(...)) return start; pos += ret; ...; return
  pos; }`. Three rules misfire on this single idiom: (a) DCL30-C
  "returns pointer to local automatic storage" on `return start;`/
  `return pos;` — both are aliases of the *parameter* `pos` (caller's
  buffer), never real local automatic storage; (b) ARR36-C "pointers
  from different arrays" on every `end - pos` — both derive from the
  same caller-supplied buffer, just threaded through differently-named
  params, exactly the `ikev2.c`-family FP already confirmed in
  `16-40_b5`; (c) INT32-C "signed addition may overflow" on every `pos
  += ret` — `ret` is always bounded to `[0, end-pos)` by the preceding
  `os_snprintf_error(end - pos, ret)` check, so the addition cannot
  realistically overflow. `ctrl_iface.c:5047-5293` (DCL30-C x5,
  ARR36-C ~40x, INT32-C ~15x).
- **DCL13-C on plain read-only struct-pointer parameters (`wpa_s`,
  `struct wpa_driver_capa *capa`, `char *end`) in internal ctrl_iface
  helpers — TP, reinforces the `16-40_b6` clarification (not
  automatically FP just because it's `wpa_s`/a common struct name).**
  13 genuine instances this batch: `wpa_s` in
  `wpa_supplicant_ctrl_iface_{get_network,dup_network,list_creds,
  save_config}` and `ctrl_iface_get_capability_{channels,freq}`; `capa`
  in all 7 `ctrl_iface_get_capability_*` helpers; `end` in
  `anqp_add_hex`/`print_fils_indication`/`print_rnr`/`print_ml`. None
  of these pointers are forwarded to a vtable/callback slot or written
  through directly.
- **DCL13-C on an output-buffer `buf` aliased via `pos = buf;` then
  written through `pos` — reinforces the single prior
  `neighbor_db.c:38` instance from `16-40_b17`, now promoted to
  CONFIRMED with 3 more (`ctrl_iface.c:3888,4229,4686,4736`, all the
  `ctrl_iface_get_capability_*`/`list_creds` snprintf-into-buf
  helpers).**
- **STR34-C "char without cast to unsigned char" — reinforces the
  confirmed plain-char-to-char-assignment FP class, 10 more instances
  this batch (`*name++ = '\0'`, `*value++ = '\0'`, `*id++ = '\0'`,
  `*next_param++ = '\0'` shapes throughout `ctrl_iface.c`'s
  cmd-tokenizing helpers).**

  pair threaded through `os_snprintf(pos, end - pos, ...)` buffer-

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b2`, 150 findings, `ctrl_iface.c` part2of11)

- **ERR07-C/ERR34-C `atoi()` boolean-coerced by `!!`/`!`/ternary —
  CONFIRMED FP sub-class, 8 instances one file.** When the raw `atoi()`
  result is immediately flattened to 0/1 via `!!atoi(value)`,
  `!atoi(value)`, or `atoi(value) ? a : b`, the function's error return
  (0 for non-numeric input) is indistinguishable from — and no more
  harmful than — a legitimate "0"/false input; the missing error
  detection has zero behavioral consequence. Distinct from the
  already-documented "range-checked-atoi" FP shape (checks a numeric
  range) and the "mostly TP" default (raw value stored/forwarded
  unchecked). `ctrl_iface.c:869,871,874,912,974,987,991,993`.
- **ARR00-C "negative array subscript" on `value[-1] = '='`/`value[-1]
  = ' '` — CONFIRMED FP, new pattern, restoring-the-delimiter idiom.**
  Throughout `wpa_supplicant_ctrl_iface_set`, `value` is produced via
  `value = os_strchr(cmd, ' '); *value++ = '\0';` (space in the
  original `cmd` buffer overwritten with NUL). When a branch wants to
  re-run `wpa_config_process_global()` over the *whole* original
  `"cmd value"` string, it does `value[-1] = '=';` to put a delimiter
  back before forwarding. `value[-1]` is the very byte that was just
  written by `*value++ = '\0'` a few lines earlier — valid memory
  inside the same `cmd` buffer, not a real negative/out-of-bounds
  access. The rule's negative-literal-subscript check doesn't
  recognize this restore-the-separator idiom. `ctrl_iface.c:926,996`
  (peers of the already-noted `dot11RSNAConfig*` instances at
  `:539,549,558` from an earlier batch — worth confirming those got
  the same disposition).
- **EXP20-C/ERR34-C/FIO47-C/INT05-C/MSC24-C all misfire together on
  `sscanf(str, "key=%i", &out) == 1` chained-`||` option parsers —
  CONFIRMED FP cluster, 5 rules × 6 sites in one function.** `wmm_ac_ctrl_addts`
  parses space-separated `key=value` tokens via
  `sscanf(token, "tsid=%i", &params.tsid) == 1 || sscanf(...) == 1 || ...`.
  (a) EXP34-C/ERR34-C: the `== 1` **is** the error check — sscanf's
  documented contract is "return = count of successfully assigned
  items," so testing `== 1` for a single `%i` specifier is the
  textually-correct success test, not a defect. (b) EXP20-C
  "testing for equality with 1, functions may return >1" is inapplicable
  here since exactly one conversion is requested — there's no
  ambiguous ">1 still truthy" case to worry about. (c) FIO47-C "format
  specifier expects Integer but argument is Pointer" is simply wrong:
  `scanf`-family `%i` *requires* a pointer argument
  (`&params.tsid`) by definition; flagging the correct calling
  convention as a type mismatch is a rule bug. (d) INT05-C errno/ERANGE
  checking after `sscanf` is unreliable/implementation-defined across
  libc's, not a clean actionable gap. (e) MSC24-C's suggested
  `sscanf_s` is an optional C11 Annex K function absent from
  glibc/Linux — not an available, portable substitute.
  `ctrl_iface.c:1334,1335,1336,1338,1340,1342` (all col 7).
- **EXP40-C "pointer to const assigned to non-const pointer without
  cast" on `u8 *_bssid = bssid` — extends the confirmed `wmm.c:104`
  rule-bug entry (fabricated const-qualifier), 3rd+ instance.**
  `wps_pbc`/`wps_pin`/`wps_nfc` all declare
  `u8 bssid[ETH_ALEN], *_bssid = bssid;` — `bssid` is a plain
  non-const local array; there is no `const`-qualified object anywhere
  in this statement for EXP40-C's premise to apply to.
  `ctrl_iface.c:1409,1462,1574`.
- **DCL37-C "file-scope identifier should not start with underscore"
  on `_bssid`/`_p2p_dev_addr` — same block-scope-misapplied family as
  the earlier `p2p_invitation.c:798,799` entry, 4 more instances.**
  Both are ordinary block-scope locals inside `wps_pbc`,
  `ctrl_iface.c:1409,1414,1462,1574`.
- **EXP33-C "may be used uninitialized" on a variable set via an
  earlier `goto`-target-reaching branch — new instance of the existing
  goto/CFG-blind-spot family.** `wpa_supplicant_ctrl_iface_wps_pin`'s
  `ret` is populated by `wps_generate_pin((unsigned int *)&ret)` then
  `goto done;`; the only path reaching the flagged `os_snprintf(...,
  ret)` at the `done:` label is that same goto, so `ret` is always
  initialized in practice. `ctrl_iface.c:1517`.
- **MSC41-C "hard-coded sensitive information" flags a debug-log
  label/tag string, not the actual secret argument — CONFIRMED rule
  bug, 1 instance.** `wpa_hexdump_ascii_key(MSG_DEBUG, "WPS_CHECK_PIN",
  (u8 *) cmd, os_strlen(cmd))` — `"WPS_CHECK_PIN"` is just the dump's
  descriptive tag; the real PIN data is `cmd`, and it's already routed
  through the dedicated `*_key` (sensitive-data) hexdump variant.
  `ctrl_iface.c:1532`.
- **MSC01-C "if/else-if with no final else" flagged 4x on chains whose
  implicit fallthrough is the correct default — extends the existing
  stylistic-pedantry MSC01-C entry.** E.g. `wps_pbc`'s
  `if (cmd=="any") ... else if (p2p_dev_addr=...) ... else if
  (multi_ap=...) ... else if (hwaddr_aton(cmd,bssid)) {...; return -1;}`
  — the "no matching branch" case is exactly "a valid BSSID was parsed
  into the already-declared `bssid` array," which is the intended
  default, not a missing case. `ctrl_iface.c:1002,1435,1476,1578`.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b6`, 150 findings, `wpa_supplicant/ctrl_iface.c` P2P service-discovery/group-add functions, lines ~6790-7850)

- **FIO47-C self-referential type-mismatch bug on sscanf() — NEW,
  CONFIRMED categorical engine bug, 10/10 instances.** Every flagged
  `sscanf(str, "%x"/"%d"/"%llx", &var)` call produces a message like
  "format specifier '%x' expects Integer but argument 1 ('\"%x\"') is
  Pointer" — the rule is quoting the format-string *literal itself*
  (always Pointer-typed as a string) as if it were the corresponding
  vararg, instead of checking the actual `&var` argument. This is
  guaranteed to "mismatch" on every single sscanf numeric conversion
  regardless of correctness. Seen at `ctrl_iface.c:6846,7009,7022,7031,
  7159,7394,7395,7396,7397,7403`.
- **ERR34-C "sscanf lacks error detection" fires despite an inline
  `!= 1`/`== 1` return-value check at the call site — NEW, CONFIRMED,
  10/10 instances.** Every flagged call is already wrapped in
  `if (sscanf(...) != 1) return -1;` or chained via `sscanf(...) == 1 ||`
  in a validating `if`. Same lines as the FIO47-C entry above.
- **MSC24-C "sscanf is deprecated/obsolescent" — NEW, CONFIRMED FP,
  10/10 instances.** `sscanf()` is not among the C standard's actually
  obsolescent functions (`gets`, `asctime`, `rewind`); the suggested
  replacement `sscanf_s()` is an optional, rarely-implemented C11 Annex K
  function (not available in glibc). Same lines as above.
- **EXP20-C "==1 test, function may return >1" misapplied to
  single-specifier sscanf() calls — NEW, CONFIRMED, 5 instances.** When
  the format string has exactly one `%`-conversion, `sscanf()` can only
  return -1/0/1 — `== 1` is the only meaningful success test, not a
  >1-vs-!=0 hazard. `ctrl_iface.c:7394,7395,7396,7397,7403`
  (`p2p_ctrl_group_add`'s `str_token` parse loop).
- **EXP33-C "uninitialized" extended to a variable read immediately
  after a checked `sscanf() != 1 → return -1` guard — extends the
  existing output-param EXP33 FP family to scanf-style writes.** 5
  instances: `ctrl_iface.c:6848,7009,7022,7034,7162`.
- **INT05-C sscanf-without-ERANGE-check judged TP this batch (unlike
  the sibling ERR34/FIO47/MSC24 findings on the same calls) — real,
  low-severity violation.** sscanf's numeric conversions don't reliably
  signal overflow via errno the way strtol does; CERT INT05-C's literal
  text is violated even though severity is low for trusted local
  ctrl_iface input. Same 10 sscanf call sites as above — worth flagging
  that a single sscanf() call site can legitimately split TP/FP across
  its 5 co-located rule hits.
- **MEM31-C "not freed"/"leak before return" when the free already
  happened earlier in the same function, before the flagged
  return — new shape of the mutually-exclusive-branch free-tracking
  bug family (this time same-branch, sequential, not exclusive
  if/else).** `p2p_ctrl_serv_disc_req`'s `tlvs` is `wpabuf_free()`'d
  unconditionally at line 6830 (end of the `else` block); sqc still
  flags the alloc site (6821) as "not freed" and a later, unrelated
  `return res;` (6837, outside the block, after `tlvs` is already
  freed and never touched again) as "leak before return".
  `ctrl_iface.c:6821,6837`.
- **MSC17-C misfires on stacked/grouped `case` labels with no code
  between them — NEW, CONFIRMED.** `case A: case B: case C: case D:
  break;` (grouped labels sharing one body, the standard C idiom for
  "any of these values") flagged as unintentional fallthrough.
  `ctrl_iface.c:6992` (`p2p_ctrl_service_add_asp`'s auto-accept switch).
- **EXP34-C null-deref flagged on a pointer field only read after a
  short-circuit `||` guard on the *same source line/condition* — new
  variant of the guard-blindness family (previous instances were
  cross-line/cross-function; this is the same boolean expression).**
  `if (pos == NULL || pos[1] == '\0' || ...)` — `pos[1]` can only
  evaluate once `pos == NULL` has already failed. `ctrl_iface.c:6792`.
- **EXP40-C misfires on the const-safe direction (adding, not
  removing, qualification) — NEW.** `const u8 *t; t =
  &info->wps_sec_dev_type_list[...];` assigns a non-const array
  element's address into a const-qualified pointer — a standard-legal
  implicit conversion, not the const-removal EXP40-C is meant to catch.
  `ctrl_iface.c:7605`.
- **ERR02-C name-substring misfire on a custom `wpa_snprintf_hex()`
  helper (not libc snprintf) — NEW.** Its return value is used directly
  (`pos += wpa_snprintf_hex(...)`); it has its own bounded-write
  contract, not the truncation-signaling one `os_snprintf_error()`
  checks for real `os_snprintf()`. `ctrl_iface.c:7633`.
- **DCL13-C "not modified" real miss extended to pointer-alias writes —
  reconfirms the `p2p_invitation.c:129` tool-bug family.** `buf`'s
  pointee is written repeatedly via `pos = buf; os_snprintf(pos, ...)`
  — the const-param param itself is never reassigned, but the memory it
  points to plainly is. `ctrl_iface.c:7530`.
- **ERR07-C/ERR34-C atoi() FP set extended with 3 new validated
  shapes** (all confirming the existing `sec != 3 && sec != 5`-style
  precedent): (a) enumerated switch/default rejection
  (`ctrl_iface.c:6990`, `auto_accept`), (b) exact-string pre-validation
  via `os_strcmp(cmd,"0")`/`"1"` before the atoi() call
  (`ctrl_iface.c:6906`), (c) indirect validation via a downstream
  helper's own error return (`ctrl_iface.c:7239` id looked up via
  `wpa_config_get_network`+`disabled!=2`; `:7277,7281` freq2/chwidth fed
  into `chwidth_freq2_to_ch_width()` whose result is `< 0`-checked).

  fields, ~17 instances) remain genuine TP, consistent with the
  existing `ctrl_iface.c` ERR07/ERR34 "mostly TP" disposition.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b8`, 150 findings, 1 file:
wpa_supplicant/ctrl_iface.c, lines ~9428-10636)

- **MEM31-C "double free" on the reassign-then-free idiom reconfirmed

  if (!x) goto fail;` inside a `str_token` parse loop, then a single
  unconditional `wpabuf_free(x)` per variable at the shared `fail:`
  cleanup label. Each variable is freed at most once per distinct
  allocation — same root cause as the `tls_openssl_ocsp.c` precedent,
  now confirmed on a parse-loop/output-union shape instead of repeated
  `foo_str()` helper calls. `ctrl_iface.c:10053-10060`.
- **EXP39-C/MEM30-C union-conflation extended to same-function
  mutually-exclusive if/else-if branches (not just cross-function) —
  new sub-shape, 1 site (2 rules).** `wpas_ctrl_iface_driver_event`'s
  giant `if (os_strcmp(cmd, ...) == 0) { ... } else if (...) { ... }`
  dispatcher shares one `union wpa_event_data event` across all
  branches; the `AVOID_FREQUENCIES` branch only ever touches
  `event.freq_range`, but sqc credits a `channel_list_changed` write
  and/or a free from a different (mutually-exclusive, same-function)
  branch as if it always precedes this one. `ctrl_iface.c:10093`.
- **ARR37-C "arithmetic on non-array pointer" misapplied to a pointer
  derived from indexing into a buffer parameter (`p = &buf[N]`) — new,
  2 instances, watch for a 3rd.** `pos = &buf[sizeof(*eth)+sizeof(ip)]`
  (`ctrl_iface.c:10240`) and `eth = (struct ether_header *) &buf[2]`
  then `ip = (struct ip *)(eth + 1)` (`ctrl_iface.c:10335`) are both
  legitimately array-backed (via the `const u8 *buf`/`u8 buf[N]`
  parameter/local), but the rule doesn't trace that provenance through
  an intervening array-subscript/cast, so subsequent `pointer++`/
  `pointer+1` gets flagged as "non-array".
- **INT30-C genuine TP: integer underflow from an unvalidated protocol
  length feeding a loop bound, contrasted directly against the file's
  many "earlier-guard" FP instances.** `wpas_data_test_rx`
  (`ctrl_iface.c:10234`) never checks `ntohs(ip.ip_len) >= sizeof(ip)`
  before `ntohs(ip.ip_len) - sizeof(ip)` sizes a for-loop bound — unlike

  `i >= sizeof(*ip)` before ever reaching the equivalent subtraction.

- **STR34-C misapplied to a `char *` pointer parameter passed to
  `atoi()`, not a scalar char — new, 1 instance.** `enabled =

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b1`, 150 findings, 1 file:
wpa_supplicant/ctrl_iface.c, lines 78-813, 2026-07-29)

- **ARR00-C "negative array subscript" on `ptr[-1]` where `ptr` was
  deliberately advanced past a delimiter via `*ptr++ = '\0'` —
  CONFIRMED FP, 3 instances in one function shape.** `SET`'s
  `dot11RSNAConfigPMKLifetime`/`PMKReauthThreshold`/`SATimeout`
  handlers do `value = os_strchr(cmd, ' '); *value++ = '\0';` (so
  `value` now points one past the original space) then later
  `value[-1] = '=';` to restore the delimiter in-place so `cmd` can be
  re-parsed as `key=value`. `value[-1]` is a valid, in-bounds byte of
  the original `cmd` buffer — the rule treats any `ptr[-1]` as if
  `ptr` still indexed from the array's element 0, not accounting for
  a pointer that has been legitimately walked forward first.
  `ctrl_iface.c:539,549,558`.
- **MEM30-C "accessing member of freed pointer" on the *containing*
  struct pointer itself, after only a local field-source variable was
  (falsely) flagged freed — CONFIRMED FP, looks like a real sqc bug,
  new extension of the branch-blind free-tracking family, 5 instances
  in one function.** `set_disallow_aps` frees local `bssid`/`ssid`
  only on sibling error branches that `return -1` immediately (never
  reachable together with the normal path), which is the
  already-documented branch-blind conflation on its own (flagged
  `MEM30-C`/`ARR00-C` on `bssid`/`ssid` directly, lines 180-207). But
  once the (falsely-flagged-freed) `bssid` is stored via
  `wpa_s->disallow_aps_bssid = bssid;`, every *subsequent* access of
  `wpa_s` itself — a struct that is never freed anywhere in this
  function — gets flagged "accessing member of freed pointer 'wpa_s'"
  too. The freed-taint appears to propagate from an assigned field
  value onto the whole containing object pointer, not just the field.
  `ctrl_iface.c:217,220,224(x2),225`.
- **INT30-C "unsigned integer multiplication may wrap" on
  `2 * sizeof(fixed_size_buffer)` where the buffer is a small
  compile-time-constant array — CONFIRMED FP, new sub-shape, 3
  instances.** `dpp_pkex_ephemeral_key_override`/
  `dpp_protocol_key_override` are fixed `u8 buf[600]` globals
  (`src/common/dpp_pkex.c:24`, `dpp_auth.c:23`) and
  `dpp_nonce_override` is `DPP_MAX_NONCE_LEN`-sized; `2 * sizeof(...)`
  is a few hundred to ~1200, astronomically far from `SIZE_MAX` — no
  realistic wrap path exists. Same "rule doesn't recognize a small
  compile-time bound" family as the existing INT33-C/INT30-C/ARR30-C
  entries, now for a `2 * sizeof(fixed-array)` shape specifically.
  `ctrl_iface.c:709,719,729`.
- **FIO47-C "type mismatch" misattributes the format-string literal
  itself as "argument 1" — CONFIRMED rule bug, matches earlier
  DCL11-C-family format-arg confusion but for a different rule.**
  `sscanf(pos, "%d %d %d %d %d", &a, &b, &c, &d, &e)` flagged as
  "argument 1 ('\"%d %d %d %d %d\"') is Pointer" — argument 1 named in
  the finding is literally the format string, not a data argument;
  the actual data arguments are all correctly-typed `int *`.
  `ctrl_iface.c:471`.
- **ERR34-C "sscanf lacks error detection" fires despite the call's
  return value being checked against the expected field count
  (`!= 5`) — CONFIRMED FP, this IS the correct/idiomatic sscanf
  validation.** `ctrl_iface.c:471`; extends the general
  "rule flags a function call whose result actually is checked"
  family (cf. the `wpabuf.c:309` ERR33-C entry) to sscanf/ERR34-C.
- **ERR07-C/ERR34-C atoi() judged FP when the result is only ever
  consumed via `if(x)`/`!!x` boolean use — CONFIRMED extension of the
  existing "immediately range-validated" atoi FP class, ~14 instances
  in one file.** Distinct from the range-checked-but-0-is-valid class
  below: here the field is genuinely binary/boolean
  (`tdls_disabled`, `radio_disabled`, uapsd `be/bk/vi/vo`,
  `wifi_display enabled`, `no_keep_alive`,
  `ext_mgmt_frame_handling`, `ext_eapol_frame_io`,
  `p2p_go_csa_on_inv`, `ignore_auth_resp`, `ignore_assoc_disallow`,
  `disable_sa_query`, `ignore_sae_h2e_only`), so a malformed/
  non-numeric string collapsing to `atoi()==0` is behaviorally
  identical to a legitimate explicit "0"/off input — no information
  is lost and no unintended state is reachable. `ctrl_iface.c:612,
  624,636,641,646,651,669,680,741,743,757,759,761,763,765`.
- **Correction/nuance to the "immediately range-validated atoi() is
  FP" precedent (`sae_pk_gen.c:48` etc.): only holds when 0 falls
  OUTSIDE the valid range.** `relative_rssi`/`adjust_rssi` are
