  is itself a valid, in-range value for both — so a malformed
  non-numeric string silently parses as an accepted "0", indistinguishable
  from deliberate input. Graded these 2 instances TP, not FP;
  re-confirm the "0-is-in-range" distinction in future batches before
  auto-applying the range-check FP precedent. `ctrl_iface.c:380,400`.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b7`, 150 findings, one file/part —
`ctrl_iface.c#part7of11`, lines ~7830-9430)

- **DCL13-C output-buffer-write-via-alias FP — RECONFIRMED, 4 more
  instances in this file alone (now well past 3x, treat as
  categorical).** Same shape as `ctrl_iface.c:7530` above: `pos = buf;
  os_snprintf(pos, ...)` writes through `buf`'s pointee while `buf`
  itself is never reassigned, so DCL13-C's "not modified" check misses
  the real mutation and wrongly suggests const. `ctrl_iface.c:8603,
  8734, 9220` (`buf` params) plus one eloop-adjacent case sharing the
  same shape.
- **ERR07-C/ERR34-C atoi() FP set extended with 2 more validated
  shapes, plus a new "boolified" sub-class — extends the
  `sec != 3 && sec != 5` / range-check precedent.** (a) `!!atoi(x)`
  boolean-coercion: valid "0" and a parse failure (also 0) both map to
  `false`, so there is no real ambiguity to guard against
  (`ctrl_iface.c:7863` per_sta_psk, `:7869` nfc_tag, `:7869`
  wpas_p2p_nfc_tag_enabled, `:7873` disable_ip_addr_req — 3 sites, 6
  findings). (b) truthiness-only use where atoi's 0-on-error and a
  legitimate literal "0" are handled identically by the caller
  (`id[num_id] = atoi(pos); if (id[num_id]) num_id++;` at
  `ctrl_iface.c:8212`; `nested_attr_flag = atoi(pos+7) ? A : B;` at
  `ctrl_iface.c:8929`). (c) reconfirms the existing immediate-range-check
  shape 3 more times (`ctrl_iface.c:8194,8203,8384`, all
  `num <= 0 || num > N` guards right after the call).
- **STR34-C misapplied to a `char *` pointer variable/parameter passed
  to `atoi()`, not a scalar `char` undergoing widening conversion —
  CONFIRMED (4 instances in one file, promote from batch-local).**
  The rule's message text ("'pos'/'cmd' (signed/plain char) converted
  to larger integer type without cast") is simply the wrong category:
  `pos`/`cmd` are declared `char *` and are never dereferenced or
  widened at the cited site — only passed as a pointer argument
  (`atoi(pos + N)`, `atoi(cmd)`). No unsigned-char cast could apply
  here at all. Seen at `ctrl_iface.c:8194,8203,8384,9351`.
- **CON07-C "compound operation on shared static variable" fired on an
  ordinary function *parameter* — engine misclassification, NEW (1
  instance, high confidence).** `wpas_ctrl_iface_wnm_bss_query(struct
  wpa_supplicant *wpa_s, char *cmd)` — `cmd` is a plain parameter, not
  `static`, and the function is not called concurrently from multiple
  threads (wpa_supplicant core is single-threaded/eloop-driven, per the
  existing CON32-C/POS49-C confirmed pattern above). `ctrl_iface.c:8560`.
- **MSC24-C suggesting `sscanf_s()` in place of `sscanf()` — NEW,
  non-actionable on this codebase's target platforms.** `sscanf_s` is a
  C11 Annex K bounds-checking function that glibc (and virtually every
  Linux libc) does not implement; hostap builds primarily for
  Linux/BSD/embedded targets where this replacement does not exist.
  `ctrl_iface.c:8027`.
- **FIO47-C "format specifier expects Integer but argument is Pointer"
  misfired on `sscanf()`'s output arguments — NEW, rule applies
  printf-style value-type checking to scanf-style pointer arguments.**
  `sscanf(cmd, "%d %d %d %d", &freq, &period, &interval, &count)`:
  `&freq` etc. are `int *`, which is exactly correct for `%d` with
  `sscanf` (unlike `printf`, where `%d` wants a plain `int` by value).
  `ctrl_iface.c:8027`.
- **ARR30-C buffer-size cross-function identifier conflation — NEW,
  extends the confirmed EXP39-C cross-function local-variable
  conflation pattern to a different rule.** Flagged `dst` in
  `hs20_get_nai_home_realm_list` (where `dst` is the full,

  `ctrl_iface.c:8442`.
- **EXP34-C null-deref flagged on `strtoul()`'s `endptr` output
  parameter — NEW, standard-guaranteed non-NULL.** `strtoul(cmd, &pos,
  16)` always writes a valid pointer into `*endptr` (into the input
  string, at minimum equal to the start if no conversion occurred);
  `pos` can never be NULL here. `ctrl_iface.c:8900`.
- **ARR36-C "pointers from different arrays" on a `temp`/`pos` pair
  both derived from the same buffer via `os_strchr(pos, ' ')` —

- **EXP33-C "used uninitialized" on the `dl_list_for_each_safe` macro's

- **INT34-C shift-amount-validation misfire on a shift bounded by an

- **ERR33-C/ERR00-C/ERR01-C/ERR30-C on `strtoul()` results that ARE

  `wpa_supplicant_vendor_cmd`'s `vendor_id = strtoul(cmd, &pos, 16)` /

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b10`, 150 findings, 1 file: wpa_supplicant/ctrl_iface.c#part10of11)

- **sscanf single-`%i`-specifier-checked-`==1` bundle — NEW CONFIRMED FP
  class, 5 rules × 9 call sites = 45 findings in one file.** Every
  `sscanf(token, "field=%i", &var) == 1` call (NAN publish/subscribe
  id/handle parsing, lines 12875, 12903, 12939, 13104, 13130, 13160,
  13163, 13218, 13221) trips the same 5-rule bundle, all FP: (a)
  **ERR34-C** "lacks error detection" is wrong — the `== 1` return check
  *is* the error detection. (b) **EXP20-C** "may return values > 1" is
  impossible — exactly one conversion specifier and one output arg means
  the return can only be 0, 1, or EOF. (c) **FIO47-C** "type mismatch...
  argument 1 is Pointer" misparses which argument binds to the format —
  it reports the literal format-string argument itself as the
  type-mismatched value, not the real `&int` arg (extends the existing
  FIO47-C argument-binding-misparse entry). (d) **INT05-C** "no errno
  check for ERANGE" is inapplicable — `sscanf`'s `%i` doesn't reliably
  set errno for overflow the way `strtol` does, so the rule's own
  suggested fix wouldn't work here. (e) **MSC24-C** "prefer sscanf_s()"
  fires on every scanf-family call regardless of context; Annex K is
  optional/unused in this codebase. Watch for this exact 5-rule bundle
  wherever hostap uses the `sscanf(str, "key=%i", &out) == 1` idiom.
- **MEM31-C "double free" on a self-nulling ("idempotent") free
  wrapper — NEW CONFIRMED FP shape.** `free_up_scs_desc()`
  (`robust_av.c:816`) unconditionally sets `data->scs_desc_elems = NULL;
  data->num_scs_desc = 0;` as its *first* statements, before checking
  whether there's anything to free — calling it twice (once as a
  pre-clear at `ctrl_iface.c:12079`, once at the `free_scs_desc:`
  cleanup label, `:12359`) is safe by construction. Distinct from the
  existing `os_free(NULL)`-is-safe EXP34-C entry: here the *whole
  helper function*, not just libc `free()`, is deliberately
  double-call-safe. Watch for other `free_up_*`/`*_cleanup` helpers that
  null their own struct fields unconditionally up front.
- **DCL13-C "not modified" factually wrong on a `buf`/`pos` output-reply
  idiom — extends the existing aes-ccm.c `dst` alias-mutation entry to
  the pervasive ctrl_iface reply-buffer pattern.** `pos = buf; ... ret =
  os_snprintf(pos, end - pos, ...); pos += ret;` genuinely writes
  through `buf` every loop iteration via the `pos` alias, but DCL13-C
  claims `buf` itself is unmodified. `ctrl_iface.c:12461,12617`
  (`wpas_ctrl_iface_mlo_signal_poll`/`_mlo_status`). Likely recurs
  anywhere a ctrl_iface handler uses the `pos = buf; end = buf + buflen`
  reply-building idiom.
- **DCL31-C "called without prior declaration" across a very large
  same-file distance — NEW sub-shape of the existing DCL31-C
  external-header-blindness family, but for an ordinary in-file
  `static` function.** `wpa_supplicant_ctrl_iface_status`
  (defined `ctrl_iface.c:2276`) and `wpa_supplicant_ctrl_iface_set`
  (defined `:497`) are both called correctly ~11,000 lines later
  (`:13321`, `:13344`) in the same 14,000+-line file — genuinely
  declared/defined earlier, just very far away. Suggests sqc's
  declaration-visibility lookup has a distance/window limit rather than
  being truly whole-file. 2 instances so far, worth watching in other
  giant files.
- **STR30-C "passing string literal which may modify it" on a callee
  whose parameter is `const char *` — CONFIRMED rule-logic bug, not
  just a heuristic miss.** `wpas_ctrl_iface_send_twt_setup(wpa_s, "")`
  (`ctrl_iface.c:14061`) calls a function declared `const char *cmd`
  (`:10593`) that only reads via `os_strstr`/`atoi`/`sscanf` — cannot
  modify the argument at all; the `const` qualifier alone disproves the
  finding. 1 instance so far, but the const-qualifier check should be a
  cheap, high-value fix.
- **ERR07-C/ERR34-C atoi() reduced to a strict boolean via `== 0` or
  `!!` — extends the existing "immediately range-checked" atoi FP class
  to boolean-collapse, not just narrow-set/range checks.** `wpa_s->
  auto_reconnect_disabled = atoi(buf + 16) == 0;` (`:13895`) and
  `params.srf_include = !!atoi(token + 12);` (`:13055`): any malformed/
  overflowed input collapses to atoi's own 0-on-failure return, which
  *is* the intended "false" semantics — there is no unsafe value atoi
  can produce here. 2 instances so far.
- **INT30-C/INT32-C mislabels `char *` pointer-bump arithmetic as
  integer-overflow-prone — extends the confirmed
  `eap_sake_common.c` pointer-mistyped-INT30 entry to INT32-C.**
  `pos2` is `char *`; `pos2 + 19`/`+27`/`+15`/`+11`/`+14`/`+12`
  (`ctrl_iface.c:12299,12305,12311,12317,12324,12330,12336`) are plain
  pointer-advance-past-prefix arithmetic, not signed integer addition.
  7 instances, one function (SCS QoS characteristics parsing).

- **Cross-function local-variable-name conflation now confirmed on
  ARR30-C too, not just EXP39-C/union tracking — NEW CONFIRMED (3
  instances).** ARR30-C cites "Buffer 'X' with size 6 (allocated at
  line N)" where the size/allocation site belongs to a completely
  unrelated function's same-named local, while the *actual* access at
  the flagged line is already bounds-checked a few lines above
  (`num_peers==WPAS_MAX_PASN_PEERS` guard for `peer`, `alen>=
  INET6_ADDRSTRLEN` guard for `addr`). `ctrl_iface.c:11674` (`peer`,
  cites an unrelated size-6 alloc at line 8007) and `:11792,11821`
  (`addr`, cites the unrelated `_addr[ETH_ALEN]` from
  `wpas_ctrl_iface_mac_rand_scan` at line 10992, while the real `addr`
  in scope is `char addr[INET6_ADDRSTRLEN]`). Same root cause as the
  already-confirmed EXP39-C cross-function union conflation — extend
  the "don't trust a cited allocation-site line number without
  checking it's actually in the same function" rule to ARR30-C.
- **EXP33-C "may be uninitialized"/"dereference of uninitialized
  pointer" on a local whose only prior reference is an *assignment*,
  never a read — NEW CONFIRMED FP class (4 instances, one function).**
  `pos2`, `temp[20]`, `n`, and `next_tclas_elem` in
  `wpas_ctrl_iface_configure_scs` are all declared without an
  initializer but are unconditionally assigned (`pos2 = os_strstr(...)`,
  `os_snprintf(temp, ...)`, `n = os_realloc(...)`, `next_tclas_elem =
  os_strstr(...)`) before the very first place their value is ever
  read or checked — there is no code path that reads the declaration's
  indeterminate value. Distinct from the existing "sizeof(*ptr)" and
  "for-loop init-clause" EXP33/ARR00 FP families: this is a plain
  definite-assignment-analysis gap on ordinary straight-line
  declare-then-assign code. `ctrl_iface.c:12084,12094,12168,12169`.
- **atoi() guarded by its own inline `> 0` condition in the enclosing
  `if` before being reused for the assignment — extends the
  "immediately range-checked" atoi FP family to the
  `if (pos && atoi(p) > 0) { x = atoi(p); }` idiom specifically.**
  `set_type4_frame_classifier`'s src_port/dst_port/dscp parsing calls
  `atoi()` twice (once in the guard, once in the branch body) with the
  guard's `> 0` check rejecting atoi's own 0-on-failure return before
  either atoi call's result is used. 9 findings, 3 fields
  (`ctrl_iface.c:11840,11842,11844` src_port; `:11849,11851,11853`
  dst_port; `:11858,11860,11862` dscp).
- **CON07-C "compound operation on shared static variable... without
  synchronization" fired on an ordinary function *parameter* — NEW
  CONFIRMED rule bug, not a heuristic miss.** `cmd` in
  `wpas_ctrl_iface_send_neighbor_rep`/`wpas_ctrl_iface_pasn_driver` is a
  plain `char *cmd` parameter, not a `static`/global variable at all —
  there is no shared state and no synchronization question applies.
  2 instances (`ctrl_iface.c:10937,11631`).
- **STR34-C "char converted to larger integer type without cast"
  misfired on a plain pointer-argument atoi() call, not a char
  conversion at all — extends the existing STR34-C
  plain-char-assignment FP family to a case with no char conversion
  present whatsoever.** `int frame = atoi(cmd);` where `cmd` is
  `char *cmd` — the message names `cmd` as the widened char, but no
  such conversion exists on this line; likely a stale/misattributed
  finding location. 1 instance (`ctrl_iface.c:10761`).
- **ERR02-C "sprintf return value not checked" fired on
  `wpa_snprintf_hex()`, which is not `sprintf` and always returns the
  actual (internally bounded/clamped) byte count written, never a
  negative/error value — nothing to check.** 2 instances
  (`ctrl_iface.c:11129,11137`, PMKSA cache entry formatting).
- **MSC01-C "switch has no default" stylistic-pedantry FP extends from
  if/else-if chains (already confirmed) to switch statements with a
  deliberately narrow, exhaustively-intentional case set.**
  `wpas_ctrl_neighbor_rep_cb`'s `switch (pos[2])` only cares about 2
  subelement types and correctly/intentionally no-ops on any other
  value by falling out of the switch — not a missing-case defect.
  `ctrl_iface.c:10900`.

## Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed (from `41plus_b9`)

- EXP34-C null-deref flagged on `wpa_s` after `wpa_s =
  wpas_vendor_elem(wpa_s, frame)` reassigns it to `wpa_s->p2pdev` in
  the P2P-frame cases — but `p2pdev` is unconditionally set (to itself
  or its parent) during interface initialization, before any
  ctrl_iface command can run, so it's never actually NULL in practice.
  3 instances, one file (`ctrl_iface.c:10734,10767,10796`).
- MSC24-C "prefer sscanf_s()" fired on ordinary `sscanf()` calls;
  `sscanf` is not actually on CERT's obsolescent-function list and
  `sscanf_s` (C11 Annex K) isn't used/available anywhere in this
  portable codebase — likely a systemic over-broad match on the
  scanf-family name. 2 instances (`ctrl_iface.c:10636,11229`), matches
  a similar note in the `41plus_b10` sscanf-bundle entry above.
- FIO47-C sscanf argument-type-mismatch conflates the format-string
  literal with "argument 1", rather than checking the real `int*`
  arguments against their `%d` specifiers, which do match correctly.
  1 instance (`ctrl_iface.c:11229`), same shape as the `41plus_b10`
  FIO47-C argument-binding-misparse entry.
- MEM03-C "sensitive buffer not cleared" fired on a `const char
  *password` that is just a pointer alias into the caller-owned `cmd`
  token string, not a distinct local buffer this function allocates —
  clearing the pointer variable itself wouldn't zero anything.
  1 instance (`ctrl_iface.c:11582`).

## Confirmed/reinforced patterns (from batch `41plus_b5`, 150 findings, `wpa_supplicant/ctrl_iface.c` part5of11, lines ~5280-6800)

Mostly reinforces already-confirmed classes from sibling `41plus_*`
ctrl_iface.c batches (paired buf/end ARR36-C, os_snprintf_error-guarded
INT32-C `pos+=ret`, API05-C buf/buflen + bare-cmd-string idiom, STR34-C/
ERR02-C/EXP40-C/DCL30-C/MSC07-C/DCL37-C-block-scope/MEM05-C-const-array/
MSC01-C-no-final-else/MSC37-C-preprocessor-blind/dl_list-style
for_each-macro-init/FIO47-C-sscanf-self-mismatch/MSC24-C-sscanf-not-
obsolescent/EXP45-C-already-parenthesized families). Two sub-shapes not
yet explicitly logged:
- **EXP34-C/EXP33-C short-circuit-`||`-blindness extended to non-pointer
  reads within the very same multi-clause condition — 2 instances.**
  `if (ssid == NULL || ssid->disabled != 2 || ssid->mode != ...)`
  (`ctrl_iface.c:6505`) and `if (sscanf(pos, "%x", &id) != 1 || id >
  0xff)` (`ctrl_iface.c:6788`): the second/third clause can only
  evaluate once the guarding first clause has already failed
  (respectively "ssid non-NULL" and "sscanf wrote id"), yet the rule
  flags the later clause as an unguarded null-deref/uninitialized-read.
  Same root cause as the existing cross-line/cross-function guard-
  blind family, now confirmed for a single boolean `||` expression.
- **INT32-C misclassifies `char *pos2 + <small int literal>` pointer
  arithmetic as signed-integer addition subject to overflow — 2
  instances, one function.** `persistent_id = atoi(pos2 + 12)` /
  `chwidth = atoi(pos2 + 18)` (`p2p_ctrl_connect`, `ctrl_iface.c:6502,
  6547`) — `pos2` is `char *`; adding a small compile-time constant
  offset to a checked non-NULL string pointer has no realistic
  overflow path and isn't "signed integer arithmetic" at all. Same
  category-error family as the existing `INT32-C`/`id++`
  pointer-vs-int confusion entries above, extends the shape from
  increment (`id++`) to pointer-plus-constant addition.

## Confirmed/reinforced patterns (from batch `41plus_b11`, 51 findings, `wpa_supplicant/ctrl_iface.c` part11of11, lines ~14380-15100)

Mostly reinforces already-confirmed classes (STR34-C plain char-to-char
assignment, API05-C bare-string/paired-size-param idioms, DCL30-C
local-pointer-to-heap-storage confusion, MSC07-C goto-label
"unreachable" misfire, MEM05-C fixed-size-macro-array, MSC01-C
no-final-else pedantry, EXP30-C side-effect-free-accessor args, ARR02-C
ifdef-varying implicit-bounds array, API00-C internal-only-API
pedantry, DCL13-C "plain internal helper, not automatically FP"
clarification — 8 genuine low-severity TPs this batch where a `global`
param truly is never mutated/forwarded mutably). One new sub-shape:

- **DCL13-C false "not modified" on an output-buffer param whose
  pointee IS written, but only through a locally-aliased pointer
  variable — NEW, 3 instances in one file.** `wpa_supplicant_global_
  iface_list`/`_interfaces`/`wpas_global_ctrl_iface_status` all do
  `pos = buf; ...; os_snprintf(pos, end - pos, ...)` — the write target
  is `pos`, never literally `buf`, but `pos` is initialized from `buf`
  and the write lands in the same memory `buf` points to. DCL13-C's
  "was this param's pointee ever written" scan apparently only looks
  for writes through the parameter identifier itself, missing writes
  through a same-scope alias seeded from it. `ctrl_iface.c:14564,
  14607, 14882`. Distinct from the existing callback/vtable and
  free-ownership-transfer DCL13-C FP families — this one is a real
  tool miss (false "make it const" on a genuine output buffer), not a
  contract-driven non-fixability.
- EXP33-C "may be used uninitialized" misapplied to a fixed-size
  pointer *array* (`struct wpa_supplicant *wpa_s[2]`) where every
  element is assigned inside the very loop that later reads it
  (`for (i = 0; i < ARRAY_SIZE(wpa_s); i++) { wpa_s[i] = ...; }`) before
  any use — extends the existing "ARR00-C doesn't see for-loop-init/
  in-loop initialization" family to array-typed locals and to EXP33-C.
  Only 1 instance so far (`ctrl_iface.c:14824`).
- ARR00-C "negative array subscript" misfired on `value[-1] = ' ';`
  where `value` had just been advanced by exactly 1 (`*value++='\0'`)
  from that same valid in-bounds location two lines earlier — safe
  pointer-arithmetic restore, not a literal out-of-bounds access. Only
  1 instance so far (`ctrl_iface.c:14808`).
- ERR07-C/ERR34-C `atoi()` judged FP (judgment call, per existing
  narrow-range-check precedent) when the result is only ever coerced
  via `!!` into a boolean enable/disable flag — any malformed input
  safely yields 0 (disable), no exploitable path. 1 instance
  (`ctrl_iface.c:14802`, `wifi_display_enable(global, !!atoi(value))`).

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b14`, ~140 findings, `src/drivers/driver_nl80211.c` part3of8, lines ~4700-7800)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP30-C "modified and accessed without sequence
  point" misfires on `if (!(x = f(...)) || cond_using_x || ...)` —
  the `||` operator's sequence point after each operand makes this
  well-defined C, not unsequenced.** C11 6.5.14p4 guarantees a
  sequence point after evaluation of the left `||` operand before the
  right operand is evaluated, so `msg = nl80211_bss_msg(...)` is fully
  sequenced before any later clause reads `msg`. This is the
  extremely common hostap idiom `if (!(msg = alloc_msg(...)) ||
  nla_put(msg, ...) || ...) goto fail;`. 33 instances this batch alone
  (`driver_nl80211.c:4878`x6, `4942`x2, `5362`x3, `5572`x6, `6445`x4,
  `6856`, `6904`x2, `7582`x2, plus paired `EXP45-C` "assignment in if
  condition" findings on the same `msg = ...`/`params = ...` sites —
  the latter is the already-confirmed parenthesized-assignment
  mitigation idiom (`41plus_b5`'s `EXP45-C-already-parenthesized`
  entry), now extended from `&&`-chains to `||`-chains and from a bare
  `(x = f())` to the `!(x = f())` negated form). Worth an sqc
  engine-level fix: `||`/`&&` operands should be treated as separate
  sequence points for EXP30-C's unsequenced-access analysis.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP34-C null-deref flagged on `nl80211_get_link()`'s
  return value, which the function's own implementation guarantees is
  never NULL.** `nl80211_get_link(struct i802_bss *bss, s8 link_id)`
  (`driver_nl80211.c:4664`) always returns either `&bss->links[link_id]`
  or, on any invalid/out-of-range `link_id`, falls back to
  `bss->flink` — there is no path that returns NULL. 2 instances
  (`driver_nl80211.c:4826`, `:5552`), both dereferencing the `link`
  local immediately after `nl80211_get_link()`.
- **NEW: EXP34-C null-deref/guard-blindness extended to a single
  `&&`-chain condition (sibling of the confirmed `||`-chain guard-
  blindness family).** `if (addr && iftype != NL80211_IFTYPE_MONITOR &&
  linux_set_ifhwaddr(drv->global->ioctl_sock, ifname, addr))` —
  `addr` is null-guarded by the first `&&` operand in the very same
  condition before being passed to `linux_set_ifhwaddr`, yet flagged as
  passed-without-a-NULL-check. `driver_nl80211.c:6633`. Only 1 instance
  so far in this batch but directly extends the confirmed `||`-chain
  short-circuit-blindness entry (`41plus_b5`) to `&&`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL13-C on `struct wpa_driver_ops` vtable member
  functions — direct extension of the EAP-method-table/eloop-callback
  dispatch-contract FP family to driver op tables.** Functions assigned
  into `wpa_driver_nl80211_ops` (verified via `grep '\.set_acl ='` etc.
  at `driver_nl80211.c:15485-15506`) have their signatures pinned by
  the `struct wpa_driver_ops` contract, not by this file's own choice —
  `wpa_driver_nl80211_set_acl`'s `priv`/`params` (`:4900,4901`),
  `wpa_driver_nl80211_sta_add`'s `params` (`:6042`). Distinguish from
  the sibling internal-helper functions in the same file (not
  themselves vtable members, e.g. `nl80211_put_beacon_rate`,
  `nl80211_fils_discovery`, `nl80211_unsol_bcast_probe_resp`,
  `nl80211_mbssid`, `nl80211_put_freq_params`, `rtnl_neigh_*_fdb_entry`,
  `wpa_driver_nl80211_ap`, `nl80211_put_fils_connect_params`,
  `nl80211_ht_vht_overrides`), where DCL13-C is judged TP (low
  severity) per the already-documented `16-40_b6` "plain internal
  helper, not automatically FP" clarification — 11 such TPs this batch
  (`:5020,5206,5237,5239,5268,5401,6351,6393,6922,6979,7133,7134`).
- **DCL13-C "not modified" premise simply wrong — reconfirmed
  (2nd instance of the `gas_query.c:803` class).**
  `connect_ext_feature_set(u8 *features, ...)` writes through
  `*idx_byte |= BIT(idx % 8)` where `idx_byte = &features[idx / 8]` —
  a genuine write to the pointee via an aliased pointer, so `features`
  cannot be made const; the rule's "unmodified" premise is factually
  false here, not just contract-driven. `driver_nl80211.c:7557`.
- **DCL31-C "called without prior declaration" on `if_nametoindex()` —
  extends the existing "external-library API call in an unresolved
  system header" FP class (previously seen for libdbus) to a standard
  POSIX function from `<net/if.h>`.** 3 instances
  (`driver_nl80211.c:6613,6654,6673`).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: INT32-C "signed integer negation '-ret' may
  overflow (-INT_MIN)" on the `strerror(-ret)` errno-negation idiom —
  CONFIRMED FP, 8 instances one file.** `ret` in every flagged instance
  comes from `send_and_recv_cmd()`/`send_and_recv()`/kernel netlink
  calls, which return small negative errno-range values (roughly
  -1..-200); none can realistically equal `INT_MIN`. Same "rule doesn't
  see realistic bounds" family as the existing INT30/INT33/ARR30
  entries, new instance shape (`strerror(-ret)` after an errno-style
  return). `driver_nl80211.c:4958,5011,5173,5984,6342,6462,6606,6913`.
  Given how pervasive `strerror(-ret)` is in Linux driver code, expect
  this shape to recur heavily in any file following this idiom.
- **CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()` thread-safety — reconfirmed for
  `driver_nl80211.c`** (no pthread usage in this file; wpa_supplicant's
  eloop remains single-threaded). 15+ instances, same lines as the
  INT32-C entry above plus `5390,5894,5914,6778,6815,6962,7113,7736`.
- **MSC01-C "no final else" — reconfirmed guard-clause/default-value
  FP family, 7 instances one file.** Every instance is either (a) a
  deliberate no-op remaining case (nothing needs to be added/changed
  when none of the listed conditions hold), or (b) a variable already
  holds a sane default from its declaration/an earlier assignment that
  the unhandled case correctly leaves alone (e.g. `cmd` pre-initialized
  to `NL80211_CMD_NEW_BEACON` before the `if (beacon_set) ... else if
  (...)` chain). `driver_nl80211.c:5547,5558,5659,5920,6192,6252,7340`.
- **MSC07-C "unreachable code after unconditional return" —
  reconfirmed goto-target-label FP family, 4 instances.** Each is a
  `return;`/`return ret;` immediately followed by an `err:`/`fail:`
  label that is a real jump target reached via an earlier `goto`.
  `driver_nl80211.c:5942,5942(dup),6887,6916` (functions
  `qca_set_allowed_ap_freqs`, `wpa_driver_nl80211_set_ap`,
  `wpa_driver_nl80211_sta_set_flags`,
  `driver_nl80211_sta_set_airtime_weight`).
- **MEM31-C "double free" on the mutually-exclusive
  free-then-goto-retry branch — extends the confirmed
  branch-blind free-tracking family.** `nl80211_join_ibss`'s
  `-EALREADY`/retry path does `nlmsg_free(msg); goto retry;` (jumping
  back up to re-fetch/rebuild `msg`, never falling through to the
  function's `fail:` label), while the later `fail: nlmsg_free(msg);`
  is reached only on entirely disjoint paths where `msg` was never
  freed. `driver_nl80211.c:7128`.
- **ARR01-C `sizeof(*params->field)`/`sizeof(params->array_field)` on
  a struct pointer parameter's own member — reconfirmed, 8 instances.**
  `sizeof(*params->ht_capabilities)`,`vht_capabilities`,
  `he_6ghz_capab` (dereference-then-sizeof, correct idiom, not decayed)
  and `sizeof(params->he_spr_bss_color_bitmap)`/
  `he_spr_partial_bssid_bitmap` (genuine `u8 field[8]` array members
  accessed via `->`, which retain full array type) —
  `driver_nl80211.c:5828,5831,6098,6100,6108,6110,6126,6128`. Also
  `sizeof(drv->ssid)` where `drv->ssid` is a real fixed-size array
  field, not a decayed parameter — `:7304`.
- **EXP30-C "unsequenced side effects" on pure accessor-function
  arguments — reconfirmed, extends to `wpabuf_len()`/`wpabuf_head()`
  pairs used as a `nla_put()` length/data argument pair (5 instances)
  and to `MAC2STR()`/`fc2str()` macro-expanded logging args (6
  instances).** `driver_nl80211.c:4741,5727,5735,5743,5790,5794,6375,
  6420,6460`.
- **MSC41-C "hard-coded sensitive information" on a `wpa_hexdump_key`
  title string — reconfirmed.** `wpa_hexdump_key(MSG_DEBUG, "  * PSK",
  params->psk, 32)` — the flagged text is the debug-log label, not the
  secret (which is the separate `params->psk` runtime argument).
  `driver_nl80211.c:7485`.
- **MEM03-C "sensitive buffer not cleared" on a borrowed pointer alias
  — reconfirmed.** `const char *password` is assigned
  `params->sae_password` or `params->passphrase` (both caller-owned),
  never copied into a local buffer this function owns — nothing to
  clear here without corrupting caller state. `driver_nl80211.c:7680`.
- **ENV01-C/MEM05-C wholesale misfire on fixed macro-sized local
  arrays with no `getenv`/VLA anywhere nearby — reconfirmed.**
  `u8 rates[NL80211_MAX_SUPP_RATES]` (`:4857`, ENV01-C) and
  `u8 features[(NUM_QCA_CONNECT_EXT_FEATURES + 7) / 8]` (`:7574`,
  MEM05-C) are both fixed-size, macro-dimensioned arrays.
- **API00-C "does not validate pointer parameter" on an internal-only
  API — reconfirmed.** `nl80211_create_iface()` is called only from
  within this driver's own internal call graph; 4 params flagged
  (`drv,addr,handler,arg`). `driver_nl80211.c:6642`.
- **API05-C "conformant array syntax" on the ptr+len-pair idiom —
  reconfirmed, 2 instances.** `nl80211_tx_control_port(..., const u8
  *buf, size_t len, ...)` (`:6743`) and
  `wpa_driver_nl80211_hapd_send_eapol(..., const u8 *data, size_t
  data_len, ...)` (`:6822`).
- **INT14-C "bitwise and arithmetic ops on the same variable" —
  reconfirmed 2 sub-shapes.** `val &= val - 1;` in `num_bits_set()`
  (`:7179`) is the standard Kernighan lowest-set-bit-clear idiom
  (bitwise-AND with an arithmetic-decrement of the *same* value is the
  whole point of the trick, not sloppy mixing); `drv` flagged at
  `:7334` for `drv->capa.enc & ...` is the established
  struct-pointer-conflated-with-its-member's-bitwise-use shape (`drv`
  itself is never used bitwise or arithmetically, only as a
  member-access base).
- **NEW: EXP33-C "used uninitialized" misfire on the `for_each_link()`
  macro's loop variable — extends the existing macro-blind
  for-loop-init family (previously seen for `dl_list_for_each` et al.)
  to a new hostap-specific macro.** `for_each_link(__links, __i)`
  expands to `for ((__i) = 0; (__i) < MAX_NUM_MLD_LINKS; (__i)++) if
  ((__links) & BIT(__i))` (`src/utils/common.h:626`) — `link_id` in
  `nl80211_connect_common` is declared without an initializer but is
  unconditionally set to 0 by the macro's own `for`-init clause before

  recurrence.
- MSC13-C "dead assignment" correctly caught 1 more genuine
  (low-severity) case: `int ret = -1;` in
  `wpa_driver_nl80211_associate` is always overwritten before any read
  on every path that reaches the function's shared `fail:`/return
  site. `driver_nl80211.c:7791`.
- INT10-C "modulo operator used with potentially signed operands"
  flagged on `idx % 8` where `idx` is an `enum
  qca_wlan_connect_ext_features` parameter — in practice always a
  small non-negative named enum constant (bitmap index), so the
  negative-remainder concern the rule is about has no real call-site

  (enum's underlying signedness is implementation-defined) rather than

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b17`, 150 findings, src/drivers/driver_nl80211.c#part6of8 lines ~11440-13270)

- **EXP30-C "modified and accessed without sequence point" on the
  ubiquitous `if (!(msg = alloc_fn(...)) || put1(msg,...) || put2(msg,...))`
  netlink-message-build idiom — NEW MAJOR CONFIRMED PATTERN (60+
  instances, one file).** `msg` is assigned in the first `||` operand
  and read in every subsequent operand; C's `||` is a sequence point
  after each operand, so this is fully, standard-legally sequenced —
  not unsequenced at all. Same shape recurs with `params`/`data`/
  `wowlan_triggers` (anything assigned via `nla_nest_start()` as a
  later `||` operand and read by a following one). Seen at line after
  line throughout `driver_nl80211.c` (e.g. 11582, 11609, 11995, 12199,
  12327, 12358, 12423, 12470, 12501, 12536, 12590, 13231 — the last
  alone has 12 instances). Before crediting EXP30-C on any assign-then-
  read pair, check whether both sit in the same short-circuit `||`/`&&`
  chain — if so it's FP by definition.
- **DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP extended from EAP/eloop tables to
  `struct wpa_driver_ops` — CONFIRMED (7 instances, one file).** Any
  `driver_nl80211.c` function directly assigned into a
  `const struct wpa_driver_ops wpa_driver_nl80211_ops = { .field = fn,
  ... }` initializer has its first `void *priv` (and any other) param
  signature pinned by the vtable's fixed prototype, same as the
  eloop-callback/EAP-method-table precedent. Confirmed via grep cross-
  reference of the assignment list at `driver_nl80211.c:15472+`:
  `wpa_driver_nl80211_get_macaddr`/`.get_mac_addr` (`:11628`),
  `wpa_driver_nl80211_status`/`.status` (`:11665`, both `priv` and
  `buf` — `buf` doubly FP since its pointee is also genuinely written
  via `pos = buf; os_snprintf(pos, ...)`, the `p2p_invitation.c:129`/
  `ctrl_iface.c:7530` alias-write class), `nl80211_set_mac_addr`/
  `.set_mac_addr` (`:12614`), `wpa_driver_br_add_ip_neigh`/
  `.br_add_ip_neigh` (`:12896`), `wpa_driver_br_delete_ip_neigh`/
  `.br_delete_ip_neigh` (`:12961`), `wpa_driver_br_port_set_attr`/
  `.br_port_set_attr` (`:13065`), `wpa_driver_br_set_net_param`/
  `.br_set_net_param` (`:13097`). Contrast: `nl80211_put_mesh_config`
  (`:12685`) and `nl80211_qca_do_acs` (`:13219`) are plain internal
  helpers (never themselves a vtable field, only called by the real
  `.init_mesh`/`.do_acs` entry points) with genuinely never-modified
  params — real (low-severity) TPs, matching the existing "plain
  internal helper, not automatically FP" clarification.
- **MEM31-C false leak on hostap's nl80211 send wrapper —
  `send_and_recv_cmd()`/`send_and_recv_resp()` always free `msg` —
  CONFIRMED, new ownership-transfer sub-shape specific to this
  driver.** Both are thin `static inline` wrappers around
  `send_and_recv()` → `send_and_recv_glb()`, whose `out:` label
  unconditionally runs `nl80211_nlmsg_clear(msg); nlmsg_free(msg);` on
  every reachable path (verified by reading `send_and_recv_glb`,
  `driver_nl80211.c:620-729`). Any caller that does
  `ret = send_and_recv_cmd(drv, msg); ... return ret;` with no further
  reference to `msg` is not leaking — ownership was transferred on the
  call. 1 direct instance this batch (`:12339`,
  `nl80211_vendor_cmd`), but the underlying idiom is used 20+ times in
  this file alone; watch for recurrence anywhere `send_and_recv_cmd`/
  `send_and_recv_resp` is the last touch of `msg`.
- **CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()` — reconfirmed specifically for
  `driver_nl80211.c` (7+ instances).** `grep -c
  "pthread_create\|pthread_mutex" driver_nl80211.c` = 0.
- **EXP05-C cast-away-const on netlink copy-in calls — reconfirmed,
  new call sites.** `(void *) data`/`(void *) ipaddr`/`(void *) addr`
  passed into `nlmsg_append()`/`nla_put()`, which only copy the bytes
  into the outgoing message and never write through the pointer.
  4 instances (`:12304,12941,12942,13005`).
- **FIO24-C double-close misfire — reconfirmed, new instance.**
  `linux_write_system_file()`'s two `close(fd)` calls are on mutually
  exclusive paths (write-failure branch closes and `return`s; the
  success path falls through to the other) — same branch-blind shape
  as the `main.c:162` precedent. `:13044`.
- **MEM05-C fixed `struct nlattr *tb[NL80211_ATTR_MAX + 1]` misfired as
  VLA — reconfirmed, 2 more instances (`:12238,12374`).**
- **EXP33-C write-only out-param class extended to a raw array-element
  address and to an `nla_parse()` output array — CONFIRMED, 3
  instances.** `ieee80211_freq_to_chan(freq, &ch_list[num_channels])`
  writes through its `u8 *channel` out-param, never reads it — passing
  `&ch_list[...]` is not a read of `ch_list`'s (uninitialized,
  `os_malloc`'d) contents (`:13185`). Same reasoning for `nla_parse(tb,
  ...)` filling the `tb[]` output array (`:12247,12378`) — extends the
  established "write-only output-param function" EXP33-C FP class from
  single-pointer out-params to array out-params/elements.

  a plain local pointer reassignment (`bss = priv;` where `bss` is
  `struct i802_bss *bss = priv;`, a function-local variable, not
  global/static at all) — category error, rule seems to conflate any

  `:11483`), worth watching for recurrence.
- EXP33-C "used uninitialized" misfired on the `for_each_link(links, i)`

- MSC13-C dead-assignment flagged `ret`'s initializer (`-ENOBUFS`) as
  never read, missing that the `fail:`/`error:` goto-target labels
  `return ret;` on the early-failure paths — new instance of the

  specifically rather than MEM31-C/ARR00-C/MSC07-C. 1 instance

- INT32-C "signed integer negation '-ret' may overflow (-INT_MIN)"
  fired repeatedly on `strerror(-ret)` where `ret` is always the small
  netlink/errno-magnitude return of `send_and_recv_cmd()` — extends the
  "rule doesn't see realistic value-range bounds" family from
  arithmetic/shift to negation specifically. 7 instances
  (`:11592,11621,12039,12142,12182,12209,12884`).
- MSC07-C "unreachable code after return" on `fail:`/`error:` labels
  reached via earlier `goto` — reconfirms the established goto-target

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b18`, 150 findings, `src/drivers/driver_nl80211.c` part7of8, lines ~13270-15415)

- **INT32-C "'-ret' negation may overflow (-INT_MIN)" on `strerror(-ret)`
  after `send_and_recv_cmd`/`send_and_recv_resp` — PROMOTED TO CONFIRMED
  (10 more instances this batch alone, was batch-local in `41plus_b17`).**
  `send_and_recv_cmd`/`_resp` bottom out in `send_and_recv_glb`
  (`driver_nl80211.h:306`), which returns small negative libnl/errno-range
  values (`-NLE_*`/`-E*`), never anywhere near `INT_MIN` — same
  "rule doesn't see realistic value-range bounds" family as the
  INT33-C/INT30-C/ARR30-C entries, now fully confirmed for the negation
  shape specifically. `driver_nl80211.c:13270,13328,13715,13908,13961,
  14150,14813,14856,14984,15033`.
- **`for_each_link(links, i)` loop-header-macro EXP33-C "uninitialized"
  misfire — PROMOTED TO CONFIRMED (extends the `41plus_b17` batch-local
  entry).** `src/utils/common.h:626`: `#define for_each_link(__links,
  __i) for ((__i) = 0; (__i) < MAX_NUM_MLD_LINKS; (__i)++) if
  ((__links) & BIT(__i))` initializes the loop variable in its own
  header, same shape as the confirmed `dl_list_for_each`/`for_each_element`
  for-loop-macro-init family. `driver_nl80211.c:15193`.
- **NEW: EXP30-C "`msg` modified and accessed without sequence point"
  misfired on the ubiquitous nl80211 message-building idiom — CONFIRMED,
  very high volume (30+ instances, one file).** The standard shape is
  `if (!(msg = nl80211_bss_msg(bss, 0, CMD)) || nla_put_u32(msg, ...) ||
  nla_put_u32(msg, ...) || ...) { nlmsg_free(msg); return -ENOBUFS; }`:
  `msg` is assigned exactly once (in the first `||` operand) and every
  subsequent operand only *reads* it; each `||` is itself a full sequence
  point per C11 6.5.14p4 (short-circuit evaluation), so there is no
  unsequenced modify+access of `msg` anywhere in the chain — sqc's
  sequence-point analysis doesn't recognize `||` operands as
  sequence-point-separated for this purpose. `driver_nl80211.c:13310,
  13507,13561,13611,13663,13694,13864,13938,15022` (5x/2x/etc. duplicate
  findings per site).
- **EXP45-C "assignment in if condition" on the same `!(msg = ...) ||
  ...` idiom — CONFIRMED, extends the existing "already-parenthesized
  mitigation" FP class (`ctrl_iface.c:2475`) to the `!(...)`-wrapped
  form.** `!(msg = nl80211_bss_msg(...))` double-wraps the assignment in
  both `!` and its own parens, which is the standard idiom signaling
  "deliberate assignment, not mistyped `==`" — same root cause, new
  wrapping shape. 14 instances across the same call sites as the EXP30-C
  entry above plus nested `nla_nest_start`/`nla_put_u32` result
  assignments (`data =`, `params =`).
- **NEW: EXP33-C "`tb`/`tb_vendor`/`tb_msg`/`nl_pcl` used
  uninitialized" after `nla_parse()`/`nla_parse_nested()` — CONFIRMED,
  extends the `wps_parse_msg`/`ieee802_11_parse_elems`
  unconditional-fill-through-pointer-param FP family to libnl's
  attribute-parsing API.** `nla_parse(tb, MAX, data, len, NULL)` always
  writes through `tb[]` (a write-only out-param filled by index from the
  netlink message), but sqc doesn't see the callee-side fill and treats
  the local array as read-before-init. 7 instances
  (`driver_nl80211.c:13375,13382,13408,13798,13802,13814,15045`).
- **NEW: MEM05-C "VLA with runtime-sized allocation" on
  `struct nlattr *tb[SOME_ATTR_MAX + 1]` / `static struct nla_policy
  policy[MAX+1]` / `char buf[ETH_ALEN * 3]` — CONFIRMED, extends the
  fixed-macro-sized-array FP class (`sae_pk_gen.c` precedent) to the
  extremely common netlink attribute-table declaration idiom.** Every
  `*_MAX` here is a compile-time enum/`#define` constant, so none of
  these are VLAs at all. 9 instances
  (`driver_nl80211.c:13365,13370,13371,13779,13780,13781,13782,14557,
  15041`).
- **NEW: DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP family extended to
  `struct wpa_driver_ops` vtable implementations — CONFIRMED (9
  instances).** Verified against `driver.h`: `send_pasn_resp`,
  `set_secure_ranging_ctx`, `nan_publish`, `nan_subscribe`,
  `get_ext_capab`, `get_mld_capab`, `send_external_auth_status`,
  `setup_link_reconfig` are all declared as non-const-pointer-param
  function-pointer fields; the `driver_nl80211.c` functions assigned to
  them (`nl80211_send_pasn_resp`, etc.) can't have their `priv`/`params`
  const-qualified without breaking the vtable-field type match — same
  root cause as the eloop/EAP-method-table family, just a new dispatch
  table. `driver_nl80211.c:13975,14071,14203,14355,14462,14699,14732,
  14822,15158`. Also extends to libnl's `nl_recvmsg_msg_cb_t`
  (`int(*)(struct nl_msg*,void*)`) callback signature:
  `wpa_driver_get_wiphy_name_handler`'s `arg` param (`:15039`),
  registered via `send_and_recv_resp`.
- **Clarification: plain (non-dispatch-bound) internal helpers with a
  genuinely-unmodified `struct nlattr *` array param are real (if
  low-severity) DCL13-C TPs, not automatic FPs** — `get_pcl_attr_values`
  (`:13339`) and `nl80211_parse_btm_candidate_info` (`:13749`) are static
  helpers, never registered as callbacks, and `nla_get_u32`/`nla_data`
  accept `const struct nlattr *` — nothing blocks constifying them.
- **NEW: CON03-C "shared variable lacks synchronization" on a `static
  struct nla_policy policy[...]` fully-initialized read-only lookup
  table inside a single eloop-driven netlink callback — extends the
  confirmed CON32-C/POS49-C "no pthread boundary in wpa_supplicant/hostap
  driver layer" FP class to CON03-C.** `driver_nl80211.c:13782`.
- **NEW: FIO05-C/POS01-C on `open(name, O_RDWR)` where `name` is built
  from a fixed `/proc/sys/net/ipv{4,6}/conf/%s/...` prefix (`%s` =
  `bss->ifname`, a local/kernel-known interface name) — extends the
  confirmed POS01-C hardcoded-root-owned-path FP class (`/dev/rfkill`
  precedent) from a fully-hardcoded path to a locally-parameterized
  procfs sysctl path; `/proc/sys/net` entries aren't attacker-writable.**
  `driver_nl80211.c:14594` (`nl80211_write_to_file`).
- **NEW: EXP43-C "same pointer for output and input parameters" on
  `send_and_recv_resp(drv, msg, handler, drv)` — extends the existing
  "callee params aren't restrict-qualified" EXP43-C FP class to the
  deliberate idiom of passing the same context object as both a
  function argument and opaque callback userdata.**
  `driver_nl80211.c:15074`.
- **NEW: MSC09-C "non-ASCII byte in string/character literal" misfired
  on a 6-byte binary protocol constant (`(u8 *) "\x04\x09\x50\x6f\x9a\
  \x1a"`, a DPP/Wi-Fi-Alliance OUI+subtype value) cast to `u8 *` — not
  human-readable text at all, so the ASCII-locale-portability concern
  doesn't apply.** `driver_nl80211.c:14929`.
- **MSC37-C preprocessor-branch-blind "reach end without return"
  reconfirmed on a 3rd shape: a `#if defined(A)&&defined(B)` *testing*
  block that conditionally returns, falling through into an unconditional
  `#ifdef X return ...; #else return NULL; #endif` that always returns
  regardless of which branch compiles.**
  `driver_nl80211.c:14535` (`nl80211_get_bss_transition_status`).
- **DCL30-C "returns/assigns pointer to local automatic-storage object"
  reconfirmed twice, both extending the local-*variable*-vs-local-*storage*
  confusion to new allocation/list idioms.** (a) `info` returned from
  `qca_get_bss_transition_status` is a local pointer *variable* pointing
  to `os_zalloc()` heap memory (`:13911`). (b) `drv2` assigned through
  `*match_drv` in `wpa_driver_nl80211_name_match` is a `dl_list_for_each`
  loop pointer into the global `drv->global->interfaces` list of
  heap-allocated nodes, not a stack object (`:15092`).
- **EXP20-C correctly caught a genuine (low-severity) TP:**
  `nl80211_get_4addr(bss) == 1` compares a `data.use_4addr` field set
  directly from `nla_get_u8(tb[NL80211_ATTR_4ADDR])` with no masking to
  strict 0/1 — fragile against a non-conformant driver reporting a
  non-1 truthy byte; `!= 0` would be more robust. `driver_nl80211.c:14893`.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b15`, 150 findings, `src/drivers/driver_nl80211.c` part4of8, lines ~7830-9670)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP33-C "used uninitialized" misfires on
  `nla_parse()`/`nla_parse_nested()` output attribute tables (8
  instances, 6 functions).** `struct nlattr *tb[NL80211_ATTR_MAX + 1]`
  (or `stats`/`rate`/`tid_stats`/`txq_stats`) is the *output* parameter
  of `nla_parse(tb, MAX, ...)`/`nla_parse_nested(...)` — per the libnl
  contract this zero-fills every slot before parsing, exactly the same
  "callee-side unconditional memset through the pointer param" shape as
  the already-confirmed `wps_parse_msg` EXP33-C FP class, just for a
  different (very common, netlink-idiomatic) output-param function.
  `get_key_handler:8204`, `get_sta_tid_stats:8356,8359`,
  `get_sta_handler:8419,8432,8517`, `nl80211_wdev_handler:9351`,
  `cookie_handler:9617`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP30-C "modified and accessed without sequence
  point" misfires on the pervasive `if (!(msg = alloc_msg(...)) ||
  nla_put(msg, ...) || nla_put(msg, ...)) goto fail;` idiom (20+
  instances, one shape, throughout the file).** `msg` is assigned in the
  left operand of an `if (... || ... || ...)` chain and read in later
  operands; `||` (like `&&`) is a sequence-point operator in C — its
  left operand is fully evaluated and sequenced before the right operand
  is even reached. There is no real unsequenced access here, just the
  single most common message-building idiom in this driver file. Seen
  2x at `driver_nl80211.c:8167`, and again at `8265,8293,8419,8659,
  8675,8763`, 4x at `8767`, `8780,9351,9617`, and 8x at `9642`. The
  sibling `EXP45-C` "assignment in if condition" on the same lines is a
  separate, already-confirmed FP (parenthesized-mitigation class) —
  don't conflate the two rule IDs even though they fire on the same
  source line.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP extended from
  EAP/eloop/`pr_config` callback tables to `struct wpa_driver_ops`
  itself (6 instances).** Functions assigned to a `driver_nl80211_ops`
  field (`.get_capa = wpa_driver_nl80211_get_capa`, `.get_seqnum =
  i802_get_seqnum`, `.sta_clear_stats = i802_sta_clear_stats`,
  `.hapd_init = i802_init`, `.if_add = wpa_driver_nl80211_if_add`) have
  their signature pinned by the corresponding `struct wpa_driver_ops`
  function-pointer field in `driver.h`, which declares `void *priv`
  (and, for `if_add`, `char *force_ifname`) without `const` — the same
  "can't const a param bound by a fixed dispatch-table signature" root
  cause as the eloop/EAP-method family, just for the driver-ops vtable
  that this entire file implements. `8110` (`priv`), `8221` (`priv`),
  `8805` (`priv`), `9149` (`params`), `9366` (`priv`), `9369`
  (`force_ifname`). Contrast with plain internal helpers never put in a
  vtable (`dump_ifidx:8878`, `nl80211_has_ifidx:8972`,
  `nl80211_vif_addr:9315`) — those 3 are genuine (low-severity) TPs per
  the existing DCL13-C internal-helper clarification, since their
  pointer params are only read and never forwarded to a non-const call.
- **NEW: INT32-C "signed negation may overflow (-INT_MIN)" flagged on
  `-ret`/`-res` where the operand is always a small `send_and_recv_cmd`/
  `send_and_recv_resp`-family return value (a negated errno, bounded
  roughly -1..-4095) — never realistically `INT_MIN` (7 instances).**
  Extends the existing "rule doesn't see realistic protocol/domain
  bounds" INT30/32/33/ARR30 family to negation overflow specifically.
  `7914,8178,8245,8275,8303,8335,8783`.
- **API00-C internal-only-API FP class extended to EXP34-C
  null-deref specifically (4 instances, one static helper).**
  `dump_ifidx`'s `drv` parameter is only ever reached via
  `add_ifidx(drv,...)`/`del_ifidx(drv,...)`, both always called with a
  live `struct wpa_driver_nl80211_data *` derived from `bss->drv` at a
  small, closed set of call sites — never actually NULL. Same
  "internal-only, closed call-site set" reasoning as the confirmed
  API00-C class, just manifesting as an EXP34-C finding instead.
  `8886,8917,8958,8977`.
- **MEM05-C fixed-macro-array misfire reconfirmed with a new sizing
  source: kernel netlink enum constants (12 instances, one file).**
  `struct nlattr *tb[NL80211_ATTR_MAX + 1]` and siblings
  (`NL80211_TID_STATS_MAX`, `NL80211_TXQ_STATS_MAX`,
  `NL80211_STA_INFO_MAX`, `NL80211_RATE_INFO_MAX`) are all
  `enum { ... = N }` compile-time constants from the vendored
  `nl80211_copy.h`, not VLAs. `8201,8347,8348,8349,8376,8379,8380,
  8405,8406,8992,9348,9614`. The 3 co-located `CON03-C` findings
  (`8349,8380,8406`) on the paired `static struct nla_policy
  X_policy[...] = {...}` tables are FP for a second, independent
  reason too: these are read-only, write-once (designated-initializer)
  lookup tables, and the file is single-threaded/eloop-driven per the
  existing CON32-C/POS49-C precedent.

## Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed (from `41plus_b15`)

- ARR01-C "sizeof applied to pointer/array parameter which decayed"
  misapplied to `sizeof(*capa)` where `capa` is an ordinary
  struct-pointer parameter (`struct wpa_driver_capa *capa`) being
  dereferenced for its pointee size in `os_memcpy(capa, &drv->capa,
  sizeof(*capa))` — not an array/pointer-decay situation at all, a
  different shape from the already-confirmed "sizeof on a genuine array
  field/global" ARR01-C FP entries. `driver_nl80211.c:8118`.
- EXP33-C misfire extended from memset-first output params to a
  `recvfrom()` syscall output param: `struct sockaddr_ll lladdr;` is
  filled by `recvfrom(sock, buf, ..., (struct sockaddr *)&lladdr,
  &fromlen)` before the guarded read at the next line (`if (len < 0)
  return;` already passed) — sqc doesn't recognize a POSIX syscall as
  an output-param function. `handle_eapol:9079`.
- STR34-C "converted to larger integer type without cast to unsigned
  char" misapplied to a bare pointer argument: `if_nametoindex(ifname)`
  — `ifname` is a `const char *` being passed as a function argument,
  not any char-widening scalar conversion. `9535`.
- **Genuine FN, error-path resource leak (MEM31-C shape) — new
  instance.** `wpa_driver_nl80211_if_add`'s `new_bss = os_zalloc(...)`
  (`:9458`) is correctly freed + interface-removed on the two sibling
  error branches just below (`i802_check_bridge` failure at `:9481`,
  `linux_set_iface_flags` failure at `:9491`, both do `if (added)
  nl80211_remove_iface(...); os_free(new_bss);`), but the intervening
  `if (nl80211_set_mode(new_bss, nlmode)) return -1;` (`:9477-9478`)
  does neither — `new_bss` leaks and, if `added`, the just-created
  kernel interface is never removed. sqc did not flag this. A related,
  not-yet-confirmed follow-on: once `new_bss` is linked into
  `drv->first_bss->next` (`:9502`), the later `if
  (nl80211_setup_ap(new_bss)) return -1;` (`:9508-9509`) also returns
  without any cleanup, leaving a partially-initialized `new_bss` linked
  into the driver's own BSS list while reporting failure to the caller.

  `sinfo[NL80211_SURVEY_INFO_MAX+1]`/`tb2[...]` — extends the confirmed
  compile-time-constant-size MEM05-C FP class to nl80211's enum-sized
  netlink attribute-table idiom specifically (9 instances, one file).**
  `NL80211_ATTR_MAX`/`NL80211_SURVEY_INFO_MAX` are `enum` constants,
  not runtime values. `:10243,10304,10306,10307,10362,10375,10853,
  10855,10860`.
- **NEW: CON03-C "shared variable lacks synchronization" on a
  function-local `static struct nla_policy survey_policy[...]` —
  extends the single-threaded-driver-layer FP class (previously
  CON32-C/POS49-C/CON33-C/CON34-C) to CON03-C.** Write-once at
  declaration, read-only thereafter, no pthread anywhere in the file.
  `:10860`.
- **NEW: EXP39-C bogus/unrelated-member citation — looks like a
  location or symbol-table mismatch bug, worse than the established
  cross-function union-conflation shape.** Finding claims
  `wpa_driver_nl80211_get_survey`'s `union wpa_event_data data` write to
  `.survey_results` happens "after writing to `wiphy_idx`" — but
  `wiphy_idx` is not a member of `union wpa_event_data` at all; it's an
  unrelated field of `struct wiphy_idx_data` (`:886`) used by a
  completely different function elsewhere in the file. `:10928`.
- **Batch-local, not yet re-seen:** MSC13-C correctly caught a genuine
  (if trivial) dead-init TP — `survey_handler`'s `u32 surveyed_freq =
  0;` initializer is never read on any path (every early `return`
  precedes the real assignment from `nla_get_u32()`) — verified true,
  contrast with this file's many *false* MSC13/goto-blindness FPs.
  `:10857`. Also: MSC13-C flagged `ret = -ENOBUFS`'s initializer as
  dead in `nl80211_tdls_enable_channel_switch`, missing that an early
  `||`-chain short-circuit (before reaching `(ret =
  nl80211_put_freq_params(...))`) falls into the same `if`-body's
  `return ret;`, reading the original value — same goto/early-exit
  blindness family as the confirmed `MSC13-C`/`fail:`-label entries,
  now via an unresolved `||` operand rather than a `goto`. `:11305`.
  Also: ERR33-C/ERR00-C/ERR01-C/ERR30-C on `strtol()` in
  `nl80211_set_param`'s selector list parser judged FP (not the usual
  TP per the `ctrl_iface.c:8899` strtoul precedent) because the
  immediately-following `sel > 127 || sel < 0` range check catches
  ERANGE overflow as a side effect (overflow always returns
  LONG_MAX/LONG_MIN, always outside 0-127) — distinguish from the
  strtoul TP precedent, which had no such catching range check. `:10537`.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b12`, 150 findings, 1 file — `src/drivers/driver_nl80211.c` part1of8, lines 1-1949)

- **`nla_parse(tb, MAX, ...)` / `nla_parse_nested(tb, ...)` output-array
  idiom — EXP33-C "uninitialized" CONFIRMED, extends the WPS
  attr-parse output-param pattern to the libnl parsing idiom
  specifically.** `struct nlattr *tb[X_MAX + 1];` declared then passed
  bare (not `&tb`) to `nla_parse`/`nla_parse_nested`, which
  unconditionally fills it before any read. 13 instances across 8
  different handler functions in one file (`ack_handler_cookie:335`,
  `error_handler:387`, `family_handler:761,768`,
  `netdev_info_handler:899`, `process_beacon_event:1031`,
  `get_mlo_info:1211,1221`, `nl80211_get_assoc_freq_handler:1730,1733`).
  Expect this in every nl80211/netlink-parsing file.
- **libnl/eloop/wpa_driver_ops callback-signature DCL13-C FP family —
  CONFIRMED, extends the existing eloop/EAP-method dispatch-contract
  pattern to three new fixed-signature families.** (a) libnl callback
  typedefs (`nl_recvmsg_msg_cb_t int(*)(struct nl_msg*,void*)` for
  `NL_CB_VALID/FINISH/ACK/SEQ_CHECK` — `ack_handler:299`,
  `ack_handler_cookie:313`, `finish_handler:343`, `no_seq_check:447`x2)
  and `nl_recvmsg_err_cb_t` (`error_handler`'s `nla` param:357\); (b)
  `struct netlink_config`'s `newlink_cb`/`dellink_cb` fixed signature
  (`void(*)(void*,struct ifinfomsg*,u8*,size_t)` — `ifi` param at
  `wpa_driver_nl80211_event_rtm_newlink:1456`,
  `_dellink:1625`); (c) `struct wpa_driver_ops`'s universal `void *priv`
  first parameter (`nl80211_get_ifindex:1168`,
  `wpa_driver_nl80211_get_bssid:1177`, `_get_ssid:1188`). All are
  fixed-signature dispatch contracts pinned by a struct field/typedef
  elsewhere, not real const opportunities.
- **MEM31-C false leak: `struct nl_msg *msg` passed to
  `send_and_recv`/`send_and_recv_glb` — CONFIRMED, new ownership-transfer
  shape.** `send_and_recv_glb` unconditionally calls `nlmsg_free(msg)`
  at its `out:` label (line 729) on every path, including success. Any
  caller that builds `msg` and hands it to `send_and_recv`/
  `send_and_recv_glb` without an explicit local free is flagged as
  leaking, when the callee always frees it. 2 instances
  (`nl_get_multicast_id:791`, `nl80211_register_beacons:987`) — extends
  the BIO-helper/`register()`-style ownership-transfer MEM31-C FP class
  documented earlier; expect this throughout `driver_nl80211.c`
  wherever `send_and_recv*` is called.
- **MEM31-C false leak/"not freed before return" ignoring a free
  2 lines earlier in the same block — CONFIRMED, CFG-lookback bug.**
  `nl80211_get_wiphy_data_ap`'s `w->nl_cb` (from `nl_cb_alloc`) is
  `nl_cb_put()`-freed immediately before two different early `return
  NULL;` statements, yet both returns are separately flagged as leaking
  it. 2 instances, one function (`:1100`, `:1107`, both citing the free
  at `:1098`/`:1105` two lines prior). Also flagged the *successful*
  `return w;` as leaking `w->nl_cb` even though ownership transfers to
  the long-lived `nl80211_wiphys` list and is freed later by
  `nl80211_put_wiphy_data_ap` (`:1130`) — a third, ownership-transfer
  sub-shape of the same false-leak family.
- **ARR39-C "double scaling" on byte-pointer (`u8*`/`unsigned char*`)
  arithmetic and on pure size_t computations — CONFIRMED, 2 sub-shapes,
  extends the existing single-scale-byte-pointer pattern.** (a)
  `(u8*)nlmsg_data(...) + sizeof(nlmsghdr) + sizeof(int)` /
  `(unsigned char*)orig_nlh + offset`: byte pointers have scale factor
  1, so adding byte counts is correct (`ack_handler_cookie:325`x2,
  `error_handler:408`). (b) `ack_len = sizeof(x) + sizeof(y) +
  sizeof(z)`: pure `size_t`/`int` arithmetic with **no pointer
  involved at all** — not even byte-pointer arithmetic, just sizing a
  scalar (`ack_handler_cookie:322`, `error_handler:366`) — a new,
  more extreme sub-shape than any prior ARR39-C FP (rule fires on
  sizeof-sum expressions even absent any pointer).
- **INT14-C misattributes a function-call target/function name as "a
  variable used with both bitwise and arithmetic operations" —
  CONFIRMED new rule-logic bug, distinct from the existing
  member-field-conflation INT14-C entries.** `nlmsg_hdr` (a function,
  called as `nlmsg_hdr(msg)`) is flagged as a "variable" with bitwise
  usage; no bitwise operation exists on it or on the sibling `msg`
  anywhere in the cited expression (`ack_handler_cookie:325`,
  `error_handler:366`). Pure rule misidentification, not a semantic
  judgment call.
- **CON03-C on a `static` local `struct nla_policy` lookup table —
  CONFIRMED FP, extends the confirmed CON32-C/POS49-C
  no-pthread-anywhere-in-core finding to a new rule.** `static struct
  nla_policy X_policy[N+1] = {...}` inside a handler function is
  initialized once and never mutated after; combined with the already
  -verified fact that wpa_supplicant/hostapd's core has zero
  `pthread_create`/`pthread_mutex` usage anywhere, "lacks
  synchronization" is moot. 2 instances (`get_mlo_info`'s
  `link_policy:1204`, `nl80211_get_assoc_freq_handler`'s
  `bss_policy:1719`).
- **ERR02-C misidentifies `os_snprintf()` as `sprintf()` — CONFIRMED,
  high-confidence rule bug, 7 instances one file.** hostap's own bounded
  wrapper `os_snprintf()` is not `sprintf()` at all, and — unlike the
  rule's "return value not checked" claim — the return value **is**
  actively consumed via `pos += os_snprintf(pos, end - pos, ...)` for
  pointer advancement, the standard hostap incremental-buffer-fill
  idiom. Seen in both `wpa_driver_nl80211_event_rtm_newlink` (`:1487,
  1490,1493,1497`) and `_dellink` (`:1654,1657,1661`).
- **INT32-C negation overflow (`-ret`) flagged on an errno-style
  return value that can never realistically be `INT_MIN` — CONFIRMED,
  extends the "rule doesn't see a realistic/bounded value range"
  family (previously seen for INT30/INT33/ARR30-C) to INT32-C.** `ret`
  comes from `send_and_recv_resp`'s libnl/errno-style negative return
  (bounded to the small standard errno range, never anywhere near
  `INT_MIN`) in `nl80211_get_assoc_ssid/_freq/_bssid` (`:1838,1885,
  1932`).
- **EXP45-C on the parenthesized `if (!(x = alloc()))` alloc-failure
  idiom — judged FP (not yet promoted to Confirmed, only 1 file
  seen).** `if (!(msg = nl80211_cmd_msg(...)))` already applies the
  disambiguating extra parens that make the assignment's intent
  unambiguous (not a typo'd `==`); this exact idiom for allocation
  failure checks is pervasive throughout hostap. 4 instances
  (`:927,944,960,974`). Watch for recurrence before fully confirming,
  since EXP45-C's literal rule text does still technically prohibit
  any assignment in a selection-statement condition.
- **`||`/`&&` not recognized as C sequence points — CONFIRMED sqc bug,
  worth an engine-level fix.** `if (!(msg = f()) || g(..., msg, ...))`
  triggers both MSC13-C ("msg's assignment never read" — false, it's
  read in the very next `||` operand) and EXP30-C ("msg modified and
  accessed without sequence point" — false, `||`'s short-circuit
  evaluation IS a sequence point in C). One instance (`:974`), but a
  fundamental CFG/dataflow gap likely to recur anywhere
  `if (!(x = f()) || use(x))`-shaped code appears.
- **DCL30-C "returns pointer to local automatic storage" on a loop
  variable walking a heap-allocated linked list — extends the existing
  local-var-vs-storage confusion to list-traversal idioms specifically.**
  `for (bss = drv->first_bss; bss; bss = bss->next) if (...) return
  bss;` returns a node from a heap-allocated `i802_bss` list, not a
  stack object. 4 instances across 2 functions
  (`get_bss_ifindex:262`, `nl80211_find_bss:1417,1420`, plus
  `nl80211_get_wiphy_data_ap:1130` for the analogous `w` case and
  `nl80211_cmd_msg`/`msg:841` for a heap-`nlmsg_alloc()` case) — this
  DCL30-C shape (any heap-backed pointer returned from a local variable)
  is now confirmed broadly, not just the single-object
  `os_zalloc`/`wpabuf_alloc` case documented earlier.

### Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed (from `41plus_b12`)

- PRE08-C (8.3-filename ambiguity) fired on 3 legitimate, unrelated
  header pairs (`qca-vendor.h`/`qca-vendor-attr.h`,
  `ieee802_11_defs.h`/`ieee802_11_common.h`, `radiotap.h`/
  `radiotap_iter.h`) — technically true (first 8 chars match
  case-insensitively) but not actionable on any modern filesystem;
  judged FP on relevance grounds rather than a rule-logic bug.
- INT09-C "enum has duplicate value" fired twice with objectively
  false claims — `NLMSGERR_ATTR_UNUSED` (`:53`) is the only 0 in its
  enum (no duplicate exists), and `NLMSGERR_ATTR_MAX` (`:59`) evaluates
  to 3 via `__NLMSGERR_ATTR_MAX - 1`, not 0. Only 1 file so far but a
  clear, high-confidence rule-logic bug worth flagging upstream.
- ARR01-C "sizeof applied to decayed pointer parameter" misapplied to
  `sizeof(*ptr)` (correctly dereferencing to size the pointee, e.g.
  `os_memcpy(mlo_info, ..., sizeof(*mlo_info))`, `:1262`) in addition
  to the previously-documented `ptr->field`-via-arrow shape
  (`drv->sta_mlo_info:280`, `err->msg:401`) — same rule family, third
  distinct triggering shape.
- DCL13-C's "clarification, not automatically FP" carve-out (plain
  internal non-callback helpers with a genuinely unmodified pointer
  param) confirmed again on 8 more functions in this file
  (`get_bss_ifindex:255`, `nl80211_put_control_port:734`,
  `nl80211_cmd:809`, `nl80211_set_iface_id:819`,
  `nl80211_bss_msg:879`, `nl80211_register_beacons:982`,
  `wpa_driver_nl80211_event_newlink/_dellink`'s `global:1282,1314`,
  `wpa_driver_nl80211_own_ifname`'s `buf:1347`) — reinforces that
  DCL13-C on a plain helper (not bound to a vtable/callback typedef)
  is a real, if low-severity, TP.
- MSC13-C correctly caught genuine dead `= NULL` initializers that are
  reassigned before any read, in `wpa_driver_nl80211_event_rtm_newlink`
  (`bss:1461`, `drv:1548`) and `_dellink` (`bss:1630`) — same
  correct-catch class as the `p2p_invitation.c` precedent, contrasted
  against this same batch's *false* MSC13-C hits on the
  `dl_list_for_each`-scoped `found` variable (`:1120,1148`).

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b20`, 150 findings in one file: `hostapd/config_file.c`)

- **ARR30-C misattributed to the outer `while (fgets(buf, sizeof(buf), f))`
  loop header, paired with a bogus EXP05-C "cast away const: 'f'" at the
  same line — CONFIRMED, 4 instances, looks like a real sqc line-tracking
  bug.** Every `hostapd_config_read_*` line-oriented file parser in this
  file has the shape `while (fgets(buf, sizeof(buf), f)) { ...; pos = buf;
  while (*pos != '\0') {...pos++;} }`. sqc reports ARR30-C "Loop increments
  'pos'" *at the fgets-while's own line*, not at the real pos-scan loop a
  few lines below — and simultaneously reports an EXP05-C "cast away const
  qualification: 'f'" at that same misattributed line, even though no cast
  of `f` (a plain non-const `FILE *`) exists anywhere in the function. Seen
  at `config_file.c:44` (`hostapd_config_read_vlan_file`), `:136`
  (`hostapd_config_read_maclist`), `:278` (`hostapd_config_read_eap_user`),
  `:1041` (`hostapd_config_read_rxkh_file`) — same exact duo every time.
  The *real* pos-scan loop a few lines later is separately (and correctly,
  if still FP-per-bounded-scan) flagged on its own line.
- **ARR30-C "unbounded while loop with pointer increment" on the
  fgets-populated pos-scan loop itself — CONFIRMED, extends the existing
  bounded-NUL-scan FP class, 6 instances in one file.** `pos = buf; while
  (*pos != '\0') {...; pos++;}` where `buf` was populated by `fgets(buf,
  sizeof(buf), f)` (guaranteed NUL-terminated within bounds) is provably
  bounded, same as the `nt_password_hash.c:30` precedent. Seen at
  `config_file.c:50,144,284,1047` (fgets-buffer scans) and also at
  `:646,824` in a *different* bounded shape: `while (pos) { pos =
  os_strchr(pos, ' '); if (pos) *pos++ = X; }`, which is bounded by
  `os_strchr`'s own NUL-terminated-string semantics (terminates when no
  more matches), not a raw unbounded pointer walk either.
- **STR34-C "assigned without cast to unsigned char" on a literal-constant
  char assignment (`*pos = '\0'`, `*pos++ = ','`, etc.) — RECONFIRMED at
  massive scale, 30+ instances in one file.** Continues the
  already-confirmed `nt_password_hash.c:32`/`base64.c` pattern: assigning a
  char literal (`'\0'`, `','`) through a `char *` is never a widening
  conversion. Essentially every `os_strlcpy`/manual-line-parsing loop in
  this file trips it (`:52,81,95,146,201,228,246,286,374,381,620,655,748?,
  827,861,947,957,994,1004,1049,1064,1269,1291,1338,1391,1458,1461` and
  more) — treat as the single highest-volume FP class in hostapd config
  parsers generally.
- **Cross-function identifier-name conflation: sqc applies one function's
  variable *type* to a different function's same-named variable —
  CONFIRMED, a distinct and more serious tool bug than ordinary
  misfires, 6 instances.** This file reuses the identifiers `pos` (as
  both `char *pos` in most line-parsers AND `char **pos` in
  `hostapd_config_eap_user_salted`) and `val` (as both `char *val` in
  several parse-helpers AND `int val` — a bitmask accumulator — in
  `hostapd_config_parse_key_mgmt`). sqc's STR34-C/EXP40-C checks appear to
  resolve the *wrong* function-scope's type for these names: (a)
  `char *pos2 = *pos;` in the `char **pos`-typed function flagged as
  `*pos2 = *pos` (an assignment, not a declarator init) with an EXP40-C
  const-cast-away complaint that doesn't apply to either variable
  (`:201`); (b) `*pos += 2 * len;` (legitimate pointer-arithmetic
  increment of a `char **pos`-dereferenced value) flagged as a "char
  dereference assigned without cast" (`:228`); (c) `*pos = pos2;` (a
  pointer-to-pointer assignment) flagged the same way (`:246`); (d)
  `size_t len = os_strlen(val);` in TWO different functions
  (`hostapd_config_read_wep:768`, `parse_roaming_consortium:1291`,
  where `val`/`pos` are both plain `char *` args to `os_strlen`) flagged
  as "'val'/'pos' (signed/plain char) converted to larger integer type" —
  there is no char-to-int conversion in a `size_t = os_strlen(ptr)` call
  at all; (e) DCL13-C on `val` at `hostapd_config_parse_key_mgmt:836`
  ("pointer parameter 'val' is not modified") when the real `val` in that
  function is `int val = 0`, not a pointer at all. Worth an sqc
  engine-level look: these checks seem to key off bare identifier text
  rather than the resolved declaration for the enclosing function.
- **MEM30-C false "use-after-free"/"writing to freed memory" on
  `os_realloc_array`'s own input/output pointer — CONFIRMED, 5 instances
  across 2 call sites, looks like a real sqc tracking bug.** The standard
  hostap growable-array idiom is `T *tmp = os_realloc_array(*outparam,
  newcount, size); if (!tmp) return -1; *outparam = tmp; /* use tmp */`.
  sqc flags the *input* pointer passed to `os_realloc_array` (e.g.
  `*server`, `*array`) as already "freed" — even on its very first use at
  the realloc call site itself — and continues to treat it as freed even
  after the very next statement reassigns it (`*server = nserv;`,
  `*array = ls;`), which is the idiom's whole point (restoring validity
  via the out-parameter). Seen in `hostapd_config_read_radius_addr`
  (`:593` MEM30-C on `server` at the realloc call + EXP33-C on
  `sizeof(*nserv)`; `:597` DCL30-C + MEM30-C on the `*server = nserv`
  reassignment) and `parse_lang_string` (`:1347` MEM30-C on the realloc
  call with `*array`; `:1352` DCL30-C + MEM30-C on `*array = ls`; `:1353`
  MEM30-C x2 on `&(*array)[*count]`, still treating `*array` as freed
  after it was already reassigned to the fresh block two lines earlier).
- **INT32-C "signed integer addition may overflow" misapplied to pointer
  arithmetic on a fixed local char array (`buf + N`) — CONFIRMED, 4
  instances in one file.** `pos = buf + 1` / `hostapd_parse_radius_attr(buf
  + 19)` where `buf` is a fixed local array (`char buf[128]` /
  `buf[512]`) and the offset is a small compile-time constant already
  proven in-bounds by an earlier check (e.g. an `os_strncmp(buf,
  "radius_accept_attr=", 19)` match) is safe, provably-bounded pointer
  arithmetic, not "signed integer addition" at all — `buf` isn't an int.
  Seen at `:62,297,300,334`.
- **INT10-C/INT33-C misparsing text *inside a string literal* as a real
  modulo/division operator on a variable — CONFIRMED, a severe-looking
  parser bug, 3 instances.** `wpa_printf(MSG_ERROR, "Line %d: invalid
  key_mgmt '%s'", ...)` (`:725`) and `wpa_printf(MSG_ERROR, "Line %d: no
  key_mgmt values " "configured.", line);` (`:738`, INT10-C) trip a
  "modulo operator used with potentially signed operands" finding with no
  `%` arithmetic operator anywhere in the statement — only `%d`/`%s`
  *printf format specifiers* inside the string literal. Separately at the
  same `:738`, INT33-C reports "Division or modulo by 'configured' without
  checking for zero" — but `configured` is not a variable at all, it's the
  tail fragment of the split string literal `"...values " "configured."`
  (adjacent string-literal concatenation). sqc appears to tokenize/scan
  string-literal contents as if they were code identifiers/operators in
  this constant-folding path.
- **DCL13-C "not modified, should be const" wrong because the parameter's
  *pointee* is mutated via an aliased local pointer initialized from it —
  new sub-class of the already-confirmed "not-modified premise is simply
  wrong" DCL13-C family (`gas_query.c:803` precedent), 3 instances.**
  `add_r0kh(bss, char *value)` / `add_r1kh` / `hostapd_parse_he_srg_bitmap
  (bitmap, char *val)` never reassign `value`/`val` itself, but do
  `pos = value; ...; *next++ = '\0';` (or `pos = val; ...; *end = '\0';`)
  — writing through an alias derived from the parameter, which does
  modify the string content `value`/`val` points to. Const-qualifying the
  parameter would be actively wrong (or require an ugly cast) since the
  function genuinely mutates the pointee. Seen at `:934, 980, 1259`.
- **ENV01-C wholesale misfire on an ordinary fixed-size local array with
  zero getenv/env-var code in the function — reconfirmed, extends the
  `sae_pk_gen.c`/`p2p_invitation.c` precedent.** `u8 oi[MAX_ROAMING_
  CONSORTIUM_LEN];` in `parse_roaming_consortium` (`:1292`) — no
  environment-variable code anywhere near it.
- **fclose() return value ignored — largely not actionable on a read-only
  `FILE *`, CONFIRMED as a low-value ERR00-C bucket distinct from the
  write-stream case, 9 instances.** Every `hostapd_config_read_*` parser
  opens its config file `"r"` and never checks `fclose()`'s return; there
  is no data-loss risk for a read-only stream (unlike an unflushed write),
  so a competent reviewer would not typically act on this. Seen at
  `:69,86,101,114,162,180,185,568,1084` (plus paired ERR33-C at a few of
  these lines making the identical complaint under a second rule ID).
- **FIO24-C "double close" (and MEM30/31-style double-free) flagged across
  branches that are mutually exclusive because each one `return`s
  immediately after its own close/free — reconfirmed, extends the
  `wnm_ap.c`/`config.h` mutually-exclusive-branch family to file-handle
  closes and to `hostapd_config_parse_key_mgmt`'s `os_free(buf)`, 7
  instances.** `fclose(f); return -1;` appearing in several independent
  early-return error branches of the same function, plus one final
  unconditional close on the success path, is not a real double-close —
  at most one of them ever executes per call. Seen at `:86,101,114` (vlan
  file), `:180,185` (eap_user), plus `os_free(buf)` in
  `hostapd_config_parse_key_mgmt` (`:736` MEM30-C + MEM31-C, error-branch
  free at `:727` vs. success-path free at `:736` — never both).
- **FIO05-C "file opened without fstat ownership verification" on a
  hostapd-admin-supplied local config path — CONFIRMED FP for hostapd's
  own config-file family, extends the general "internal-only API, not
  adversarial input" theme.** VLAN/MAC-ACL/EAP-user/RxKH config files are
  paths named in `hostapd.conf` by the local administrator, not
  attacker-influenced network input; fstat/uid ownership checking is not
  a realistic concern for this trust boundary. Seen at
  `:38,130,271,1035`.
- **EXP33-C "dereference of uninitialized pointer" on `sizeof(*ptr)` —
  reconfirmed at very high volume (8+ instances) and extended to
  `sizeof(ptr->member)` for the first time.** Standard
  `X = os_zalloc(sizeof(*X))` idiom (`:97,891,939,985,593`) plus a new
  variant, `sizeof(ls->lang)` where `ls` is an as-yet-unassigned `struct
  hostapd_lang_string *` (`parse_lang_string:1341`) — `sizeof` of a
  struct member's *type* likewise never evaluates the base pointer.
- **ERR07-C/ERR34-C atoi() judged TP vs FP depends entirely on whether an
  immediate downstream check exists — both sub-classes reconfirmed
  side-by-side in one file.** FP when immediately range-checked

- **Real bug found (FN): off-by-one 1-byte OOB write in
