## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b13`, 150 findings, 1 file: src/drivers/driver_nl80211.c, lines ~1940-4700)

- **`nlmsg_alloc()`/`nl80211_*_msg()` + `send_and_recv_cmd`/`send_and_recv_resp` ownership-transfer — CONFIRMED new MEM31-C FP class, very high-volume.** `send_and_recv_glb()` (driver_nl80211.c:620-729) unconditionally calls `nl80211_nlmsg_clear(msg); nlmsg_free(msg);` at its single `out:` label on every path (success, every internal error, and the `nl_cb_clone` failure before send). Any driver-op helper that builds `msg` and hands it to `send_and_recv_cmd()`/`send_and_recv_resp()` (the two `send_and_recv()` wrapper's inlines in driver_nl80211.h) has msg freed by the callee even though the local var is never explicitly freed/NULLed after the call. 4+ instances this batch (lines 2092, 2135, and the same shape recurs at every `send_and_recv_cmd(drv, msg)`/`send_and_recv_resp(...)` call site in the file — expect dozens more across the other `driver_nl80211.c` batches).
- **libnl `nla_parse()`/`nla_parse_nested()` output array — CONFIRMED EXP33-C "uninitialized" FP, extends the WPS/p2p output-param class to libnl specifically.** `struct nlattr *tb[MAX+1];` declared with no initializer, then passed as the fill-target to `nla_parse(tb, ...)`/`nla_parse_nested(sinfo, ...)`; libnl's `nla_parse` zeroes the array before populating it (standard, documented libnl behavior), so the "uninitialized" premise is wrong. 5 instances this batch (lines 1949, 1957, 2117, 3262 — all `driver_nl80211.c`'s per-attribute nl80211 event/reply parsers use this exact idiom hundreds of times in the file).
- **`genlmsg_attrdata(gnlh, 0)`/`genlmsg_attrlen(gnlh, 0)` as `nla_parse()` arguments — CONFIRMED EXP30-C "unsequenced side effects" FP, extends the pure-accessor-args class to libnl-genl macros.** Both are simple header-offset/length accessor macros with zero side effects; passing both as sibling arguments to `nla_parse()` is safe regardless of evaluation order. 4+ instances (lines 1949, 2002, 2117, 3262).
- **`struct nlattr *tb[NL80211_ATTR_MAX + 1]` / `ARRAY_SIZE(struct-field-array)+1` — CONFIRMED MEM05-C/ARR32-C fixed-size-array misfire, extends the existing enum/macro-constant class to libnl attribute-table idiom.** `NL80211_ATTR_MAX` is a compile-time enum constant; `NL80211_ATTR_MAX + 1`-sized `nlattr*` arrays are the standard libnl attribute-table declaration, never a VLA. 4 instances (lines 1998, 2114, 3255, and 4402's `ARRAY_SIZE(drv->extra_bss_membership_selectors) + 1` variant, which also drew a companion ARR32-C "unsafe size" FP since the size is a compile-time constant of a fixed struct field).
- **`if (!(x = builder_fn(...)) || step2(x) || step3(x) || ...)` netlink-message-build chain — CONFIRMED NEW: EXP30-C "modified and accessed without sequence point" + EXP45-C "assignment in if condition" both misfire on this idiom.** This is THE standard hostap nl80211 message-construction pattern (`nl80211_cmd_msg`/`nl80211_bss_msg`/`nl80211_drv_msg` assigned in the first `||` operand, then `nla_put_*(msg, ...)` calls as later operands). C's `||` is a sequence point between operands with guaranteed left-to-right short-circuit evaluation, so `msg` is assigned exactly once and only ever *read* in later operands — not unsequenced at all. EXP45-C's concern (accidental `=` for `==`) doesn't apply either: this is the deliberate, idiomatic combined alloc+null-check+build pattern used essentially everywhere nl80211 messages are constructed. Seen 5 distinct call sites this batch alone (lines 2670, 3286, 3806, 4220, plus 3290), each firing 3-4 EXP30-C + 1 EXP45-C = ~20 findings from one shape. Expect this to be the single largest FP volume driver across the rest of `driver_nl80211.c`'s batches — any `if (!(msg = nl80211_*_msg(...)) || nla_put*(msg, ...) || ...)` chain in this file is FP for both rules.
- **`__AKM(a, b)`-style X-macro AKM-suite-table generator — CONFIRMED, extends the existing dl_list/W2S X-macro family to a new shape, plus a genuine EXP43-C engine bug.** `wpa_key_mgmt_to_suites`'s `#define __AKM(a, b) if (...) suites[num_suites++] = (RSN_AUTH_KEY_MGMT_ ## b)` macro, invoked ~20x as `__AKM(IEEE8021X, UNSPEC_802_1X)` etc.: (a) PRE00-C "evaluates multiple times" is a category error — `a`/`b` are only token-pasted, never runtime-evaluated; (b) PRE02-C's parenthesize-the-whole-macro fix is invalid C (it's a full `if` statement); (c) PRE05-C's "use two-level indirection" concern doesn't apply — `a`/`b` are plain enum-suffix identifiers, not macros needing pre-expansion; (d) **NEW, more severe: EXP43-C "called with same pointer for output/input" fires 13x on `__AKM(...)` invocations, even though `__AKM` is a macro (not a function) and its arguments are bare enum-suffix identifiers (`IEEE8021X`, `PSK`, ...), not pointers at all** — the finding is a category error, not just a false positive on real pointer arguments. (e) sqc's macro-expansion blindness ALSO caused DCL13-C to falsely claim `suites`/DCL00-C to falsely claim `num_suites` are unmodified/never-modified, when both are written inside every `__AKM(...)` call (`suites[num_suites++] = ...`) — a real "doesn't see the macro body's writes" miss, same shape as the earlier-confirmed macro-hidden-mutation DCL13-C class. (f) DCL37-C on `__AKM` itself, by contrast, is a genuine TP — a real double-underscore reserved identifier per C 7.1.3 with no external-header-shadowing justification (same reasoning as the `__must_check` precedent, not the `_LINUX_TYPES_H` exception).
- **`for_each_link(links, i)` macro (`src/utils/common.h:626`, `for ((i)=0; (i)<MAX_NUM_MLD_LINKS; (i)++) if ((links)&BIT(i))`) — CONFIRMED NEW: EXP33-C "used uninitialized" misfire on the loop variable, extends the macro-hidden-for-loop-init family (previously seen as ARR00-C on plain for-loops) to a macro-wrapped for-loop.** `u8 link_id;` declared with no initializer, then used only via `for_each_link(bss->valid_links, link_id) {...}`; the macro's expansion fully initializes it. `driver_nl80211.c:4685`.
- **nl80211 netlink response-handler callback (`int (*)(struct nl_msg *, void *)`, the `valid_handler` parameter type used by `send_and_recv`/`send_and_recv_resp`/`send_and_recv_cmd`) — CONFIRMED NEW DCL13-C dispatch-contract sub-family, alongside eloop/EAP-method/vtable-forwarding.** Handler functions like `qca_vendor_test_cmd_handler(struct nl_msg *msg, void *arg)` match this fixed callback typedef; `arg`'s type can't be tightened without breaking every other handler assigned through the same function pointer slot. `driver_nl80211.c:3252`.
- **`nl80211_nlmsg_clear(msg)` already NULL-checks internally (`if (msg) {...}`, driver_nl80211.c:453-465) — reinforces the confirmed `os_free(NULL)`-is-safe EXP34-C FP class to a project-local wrapper, not just libc `free`.** EXP34-C flagged `nl80211_nlmsg_clear(msg)` inside `if (!(msg = ...) || ...) { ...; }` as "does not check for NULL" when the callee demonstrably does. `driver_nl80211.c:3850`.
- **Reinforces the mutually-exclusive-branch double-free/leak FP family with a 3rd shape: a shared cleanup pair (`nl80211_nlmsg_clear`+`nlmsg_free`+"set to NULL") reused across a builder function's several independent success/fail sub-steps.** `wpa_driver_nl80211_set_key`'s `key_msg` is allocated once, freed-and-NULLed after each of 2 independent successful-build stages (~lines 4021-4023, 4088-4090), with numerous `goto fail`/`goto fail2` branches in between; traced every goto site — each either frees a still-live first-or-second allocation exactly once, or hits `nlmsg_free(NULL)` (a safe no-op) if the goto occurs after the preceding NULL-out. MEM31-C's "double free" claim at the shared `fail2:` cleanup (`driver_nl80211.c:4118`) is FP. Same "msg=NULL after send_and_recv_cmd, then fail: nlmsg_free(msg) is a safe no-op" shape recurs standalone at `driver_nl80211.c:4612`.
- **CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()` — reconfirmed exhaustively for `driver_nl80211.c` (16+ instances, no `pthread_create`/mutex anywhere in the file), same no-pthread FP class as `linux_ioctl.c`/`driver_nl80211_monitor.c`.**
- **INT32-C "signed negation of -ret may overflow" on `strerror(-ret)` where `ret = send_and_recv_cmd(...)`/`send_and_recv_resp(...)` — NEW sub-shape of the "rule doesn't see realistic protocol/domain bounds" INT32-C family.** `ret`'s only possible values are small negative errno-range netlink ack/error codes (bounded by `send_and_recv_glb`'s own error paths: `-EBADF`, `-EAGAIN`, kernel ack errors, etc.); it is never realistically `INT_MIN`. 9 instances, always the identical `ret = send_and_recv_cmd/resp(...); ...; strerror(-ret);` shape (lines 3164, 3184, 3300, 3350, 3819, 3858, 4042, 4110, 4546).

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b22`, 150 findings, `hostapd/config_file.c` part3of7, lines ~2440-3210, `hostapd_config_fill`'s TLS/EAP-server/RADIUS/WPA/FT/ctrl_iface option block)

The other 57 lines (e.g. `check_crl`, `fragment_size`, every `eap_teap_*`/`eap_sim_*` field, every `radius_*_port`/`*_interval`, `wpa`, `wpa_group_rekey`, all the FT `rkh_*`/`r*_key_lifetime` timers) assign the raw `atoi()` result straight into a struct field with zero downstream validation — genuine TP.
- **DCL31-C "called without prior declaration" reconfirmed for the same-file-distance blind spot, 5 instances, one function.** `hostapd_config_parse_cipher` is defined at `config_file.c:747` and called correctly ~2200 lines later at `:2985,2995,3006,3019,3031` — extends the `41plus_b6` `wpa_supplicant_ctrl_iface_status`/`_set` precedent (declaration-visibility window has a distance limit, not truly whole-file) to a second giant hostap file.
- **MSC01-C "if/else-if chain has no final else" — extends the chain-mislocation sub-class (`41plus_b13`'s driver_nl80211.c:4592 precedent) to `hostapd_config_fill` itself.** `:2487` is a nested else-if deep inside the single ~2700-line dispatch chain that starts at `config_file.c:2237`; the chain's real final `else` (logging "unknown configuration item") is at `:4978`, thousands of lines later — not missing, just far away.
- **EXP43-C "same pointer for output/input" on `os_memmove(term, term + 1, ...)` — extends the confirmed no-restrict EXP43-C FP class to an intra-buffer shift-left (not just aliased-arg calls).** `os_memmove` (a plain `memmove` wrapper, no `restrict`) at `config_file.c:2581` shifting a string left by one byte to strip an escaped `\0` marker is exactly the overlapping-but-legal-for-memmove case the rule can't distinguish from real UB.
- **INT32-C misclassifies `char *` pointer-plus-1 as a scalar integer addition — extends the existing pointer-mistyped-INT32-C family (`eap_sake_common.c`, `sae_pk_gen.c` precedents) to a new call site.** `term + 1` at `config_file.c:2581` (`term` is `char *`, the post-`\0`-terminator scan pointer) is pointer arithmetic on a fixed offset, not integer addition that can overflow.
- **INT30-C unsigned-subtraction-wrap misfire on an `os_strstr`-bounded offset — new sub-shape of the existing "rule doesn't see an earlier same-function/library-postcondition guard" INT30-C family.** `bss->eap_req_id_text_len - (term - bss->eap_req_id_text) - 1` (`:2582`) can't underflow: `term` was found via `os_strstr(eap_req_id_text, "\\0")`, so `term`'s offset is always `<= eap_req_id_text_len - 2`, guaranteeing the subtraction result is `>= 0`.
- **ERR33-C/ERR00-C "strtoul() return value not checked" — FP when a downstream `*endp`+range check exists, reconfirmed as a distinct (weaker-validation) sub-case from the ctrl_iface.c:8899 "TP" precedent.** `wpa_group_update_count`/`wpa_pairwise_update_count` (`:2900,2911`) both immediately check `*endp || val < 1 || val > (u32) -1` right after the call — the rule's literal "not checked" claim is simply false here, unlike the ctrl_iface.c precedent which had no check at all.
- **ERR30-C "errno not reset before strtoul" — judged TP (low) even alongside the above ERR33-C/ERR00-C FPs, since the range check doesn't fully substitute for ERANGE detection on platforms where `unsigned long` is 32-bit.** Same two sites (`:2900,2911`).
- **ERR33-C/ERR00-C/ERR30-C on `strtol()` reconfirmed as TP (low) per the exact ctrl_iface.c:8899 "partial validation, no ERANGE guard" shape.** `bss->ctrl_interface_gid = strtol(group, &endp, 10)` (`:3145`) only checks `*group == '\0' || *endp != '\0'` (empty-string/trailing-char), never guards overflow — weaker validation than the `wpa_group_update_count` case above, so all three rules stay TP here.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b23`, 150 findings, 1 file: hostapd/config_file.c#part4of7, lines ~3208-3630)

- **Reinforces + sharpens the "0-inside-valid-range" nuance (originally from `41plus_b1`'s relative_rssi/adjust_rssi note) with a dense, mostly-unchecked config-directive block — 9 range-checked-atoi FP instances (18 findings) vs. ~55 unchecked-TP instances in one function (`hostapd_config_fill`).** Config directives assigned straight to a struct field with zero downstream validation (`op_class`, `edmg_channel`, `ieee80211n`, all `he_*`/`vht_*`/`ieee80211a[cx]` feature-enable fields, etc.) stay TP — this is the file's dominant shape, not the exception. The FP sub-class only applies when the range check's rejection boundary excludes 0 (`beacon_int` `<10||>65535`, `acs_num_scans` `<=0||>100`, `dtim_period` `<1||>255`, `fragm_threshold`'s `-1`-or-`256..2346` else-chain, legacy `beacon_rate` `<10||>10000`, `assoc_sa_query_max/retry_timeout`'s `==0` reject) — 6 distinct range shapes, all confirming the existing precedent, not new. Conversely `min_tx_power` `[0,255]`, `rts_threshold` `[-1,65535]`, `bss_load_update_period` `[0,100]`, `send_probe_response` `{0,1}`, and all three `beacon_rate ht:/vht:/he:` MCS ranges (`[0,31]`/`[0,9]`/`[0,11]`) include 0 as a legitimate value, so malformed non-numeric input silently aliases to a valid setting — genuine TP per the nuance rule, not FP.
- **Bitmasked `atoi(pos) & 0xNN` / `set_he_cap(atoi(pos), mask)` shift-and-mask assignment — NEW sub-shape, judged TP (not a safety net).** `he_bss_color = atoi(pos) & 0x3f`, `he_mu_edca_ac_be_timer = atoi(pos) & 0xff`, and the ~13 `he_mu_edca_*` fields built via `set_he_cap(atoi(pos), MASK)` (`mask & (val << offset)`) all mechanically truncate the parsed value into a bit-field, but truncation is not error detection: malformed non-numeric input still maps to a valid in-range 0, indistinguishable from a legitimate "0" setting for the multi-bit AIFSN/ECWMIN/ECWMAX/timer fields. Distinct from the confirmed boolean-coercion FP class (`!!atoi`, bare `if(atoi(...))`) — masking to a multi-bit field is not the same as collapsing to a true boolean.
- **`ocv` config field: NOT a boolean despite `if (bss->ocv && ...)` truthy-looking use nearby — 3-valued field (0=off/1=optional/2=mandatory, confirmed via `wpa_auth_ie.c:1128` `if (wpa_auth->conf.ocv == 2)`).** Unlike the confirmed boolean-coerced atoi FP class, judged TP: `ocv=atoi(pos)` is unchecked and a malformed value silently becomes 0 (off), which is a real, distinguishable-from-1/2 state change, not a "harmless" boolean collapse. `config_file.c:3527`.
- MSC01-C "no final else" reconfirmed once more on the guard-clause fallthrough shape: `fragm_threshold`'s `if (== -1) {/*allow*/} else if (out of range) {error}` needs no final else because valid in-range values require no action. `config_file.c:3325`.

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: API00-C "does not validate pointer parameter" on `iter`/`error`/`property_desc` in the same accessor family — extends the internal-only-API FP class.** These are supplied exclusively by the internal D-Bus property dispatcher (`dbus_new.c`); never externally nullable. 33 instances.
- **STR30-C "passing string literal which may modify it" on `dbus_set_error`/`dbus_set_error_const` — CONFIRMED rule-logic bug (new callee, same root cause as the `ctrl_iface.c:14061` const-param entry).** Both libdbus functions declare their `message` param as `const char *` (`dbus-errors.h`); the const qualifier alone disproves the finding for every one of the 31 instances in this batch.
- **DCL31-C "called without prior declaration" on `dbus_set_error`/`dbus_message_iter_close_container`/`dbus_message_iter_next` — reconfirms the `dbus_common.c` unresolved-external-header (`<dbus/dbus.h>`) DCL31-C FP class in a 2nd file, 24 instances.**
- **EXP40-C "pointer to const assigned to non-const pointer" on `char *str = country;`** — `country` is a plain non-const `char[3]` local; fabricated-const rule bug, extends the `wmm.c:104` entry.
- **EXP34-C null-deref family, all 4 instances this batch confirmed FP via the "callee guarantees non-null" class:** (a) `country`/`new_value` set by `wpas_dbus_simple_property_setter` → `dbus_message_iter_get_basic()` on a type-validated `DBUS_TYPE_STRING` D-Bus arg, which cannot yield NULL on success (2 sites: `:4057` array-access on `country`, `:4625`/`:4634` `os_strlen`/array-access on `new_value`); (b) `end` from `strtol(new_value, &end, 0)` — extends the confirmed strtoul-endptr-never-NULL class (`:4651`).
- **NEW: MSC13-C "declared but never used" on `path_buf` when a second pointer variable is declared as its alias in the same statement (`char path_buf[N], *bss_obj_path = path_buf;`) and only the alias is subsequently written/read — name-alias-blindness, not a real unused variable (2 instances, `:4187`, `:4215`).**
- **ENV01-C wholesale misfire (3 instances) reconfirmed** on ordinary fixed local buffers (`path_buf`, `eap_mode_buf`) with zero `getenv()` calls anywhere in the function.
- **MSC37-C preprocessor-branch-blind "reach end without return" reconfirmed 2x** on `#ifndef X ... return ...; #else ... return ...; #endif` bodies (`wpas_dbus_getter_pkcs11_engine_path`/`_module_path`).
- **STR34-C literal-char-assignment reconfirmed** (`*p = '\0';`, `:4603`).
- **NEW: INT30-C unsigned-decrement wrap misfire on the `while (i) os_free(paths[--i]);` cleanup idiom — extends the proven-safe-bounded-loop INT30-C FP class to a new shape.** The `while(i)` guard makes wraparound structurally impossible (decrement only fires when `i>0`). 3 instances, one per bss/network/sta path-array getter (`:4396,4460,4750`).
- **MSC01-C "no final else" reconfirmed 2x** on deliberate default-value (`wpa_sm_param` pre-set to `-1`, checked via `!= -1` later) and intentional-no-op (`ret>0` → fall through to success) guard shapes.
- **NEW: MSC13-C dead-initial-assignment judged TP (not FP) when the initializer genuinely can't be read before being overwritten on every path to first use.** `char **paths = NULL;` (`:4703`) is always overwritten by `os_calloc()` before the only `goto out`/cleanup site can observe it, and `unsigned int rand_type = 0;` (`:4773`) is always reassigned inside its loop before any read — both are real dead-init MSC13-C findings, distinguishing this from the alias-blindness `path_buf` FP shape above.
- **ERR33-C/ERR01-C/ERR30-C on `strtol()` reconfirmed TP (low severity), extending the `ctrl_iface.c:8899` strtoul-partially-validated class to strtol.** `wpas_dbus_setter_iface_global`'s `val = strtol(new_value, &end, 0)` validates trailing garbage via `if (*end)` but never checks `errno`/`ERANGE` for silent overflow (`:4650`, 3 rules).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b30`, 150 findings, `wpa_supplicant/dbus/dbus_new_handlers.c` part4of5, lines ~4850-6210: BSS/STA/network property getters+setters)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (12 instances): DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP family extends to the D-Bus `WPADBusPropertyAccessor` typedef itself.** Every `wpas_dbus_getter_*`/`wpas_dbus_setter_*` property accessor matches `DECLARE_ACCESSOR` (`dbus_new_helpers.h:25-27`: `dbus_bool_t f(const struct wpa_dbus_property_desc *property_desc, DBusMessageIter *iter, DBusError *error, void *user_data)`); `user_data`'s type is pinned by that single shared typedef across every getter/setter, so it can never be tightened to `const` per-function without breaking the vtable-style dispatch — same root cause as eloop/EAP-method/driver-ops, just a new fixed-signature family. Contrast: a *plain* internal helper only called directly (not itself registered as an accessor) — `get_bss_helper`'s `args` (`:5190`), `wpas_dbus_get_bss_security_prop`'s `ie_data` (`:5447`), `wpas_dbus_signal_preq`'s `wpa_s` (`:6155`) — stays a genuine low-severity TP, consistent with the existing "plain helper, read-only param" clarification.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (25 instances): DCL15-C "should be static" FP extends to D-Bus property accessors declared `extern` via `DECLARE_ACCESSOR(...)` in `dbus_new_handlers.h` and registered by address in `dbus_new.c`'s property-desc tables** — same root cause as the `wpa_driver_*_ops`/DCL15-C entry, just a new extern-linkage-needed family.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (47 instances): API00-C "does not validate pointer parameter" FP extends to D-Bus getter/setter/handler params (`iter`, `error`, `property_desc`, `message`).** These are only ever invoked by the D-Bus property/method dispatch framework itself, which always supplies non-null values by contract — consistent with the existing "internal-only API, never externally nullable" API00-C FP class.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (10 instances): DCL31-C "called without prior declaration" FP extends to `dbus_message_iter_close_container`/`dbus_set_error`**, both declared in `<dbus/dbus.h>`/`<dbus/dbus-errors.h>`, transitively included via `dbus_new_helpers.h:13`'s `#include <dbus/dbus.h>` — same libdbus-third-party-header root cause as the `dbus_common.c` entry.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (14 instances): STR30-C "passing string literal which may modify it" is a rule-logic bug against `dbus_set_error`/`dbus_set_error_const`, whose `name`/`message` params are both declared `const char *`** (`dbus-errors.h:69-76`) — cannot be modified by definition, same class as the `ctrl_iface.c:14061` const-qualified-callee entry, now with a concrete pair of always-FP callees to check first in any dbus file.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (7 instances): MSC37-C "reach end without return" preprocessor-branch-blind misfire, now on a `#ifdef CONFIG_AP ... return X; #else return FALSE; #endif }` shape** (both branches end in `return`) — same root cause, new shape, joining the `dbus_common.c:341`/`ctrl_iface.c` instances.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (15 instances, 1 function): EXP30-C "unsequenced side effects" on `wpabuf_head()`/`wpabuf_len()` sibling-argument pairs inside `wpas_dbus_getter_bss_anqp`'s big `if (anqp->X && !wpa_dbus_dict_append_byte_array(&iter_dict, "X", wpabuf_head(anqp->X), wpabuf_len(anqp->X)))` chain** — both are pure read accessors, reconfirms/bulk-extends the existing side-effect-free-accessor EXP30-C FP class.
- **NEW: DCL30-C "returns pointer to local automatic-storage object" confuses a local pointer *variable* with the persistent `dl_list`-owned struct it points to.** `get_bss_helper`'s `res = wpa_bss_get_id(...)` returns an element live inside `wpa_s->bss`'s list, not stack storage (`:5203`) — same confusion class as the `comeback_token.c`/heap-vs-stack entries, now for a linked-list element.
- **NEW: ARR00-C "use after free" on `ie_rates` in `wpas_dbus_getter_bss_rates` is another mutually-exclusive-branch misfire** — `os_free(ie_rates)` only runs inside the `if (!real_rates) { ...; return FALSE; }` branch, which never reaches the later loop that reads `ie_rates[i]` (`:5433`); same root cause as the `eap_server_psk.c` free/access-tracking-across-branches family.
- **NEW: INT13-C "bitwise op on signed operand" misattributes the operand to the struct *pointer* itself (reported type "int") when the real operand is a `u16` struct field (`res->caps & IEEE80211_CAP_*`)** — extends the existing "INT13-C type detection simply wrong" class (previously a plain `unsigned int` parameter misjudged; here compounded with reporting the wrong variable name too). 3 instances (`:5280,5308,5324`).
- **NEW: EXP05-C cast-away-const in a qsort comparator (`cmp_u8s_desc(const void *a, const void *b) { return *(u8*)b - *(u8*)a; }`) is read-only (dereference only, no write through the cast pointer)** — extends the existing read-only-cast-away-const EXP05-C FP class to the standard qsort-comparator idiom. 2 instances (`:5391`).
- **NEW: EXP33-C "may be used uninitialized" misapplied to a counted partial-fill `const char *` array (`key_mgmt[19]`/`pairwise[5]` filled via `arr[n++] = "literal"`, then passed with count `n` to `wpa_dbus_dict_append_string_array(..., arr, n)`, whose own loop only iterates `i < n`)** — extends the existing counted-partial-fill-array family (previously seen for a fixed-size pointer array) to `const char *` string-literal arrays and to a callee-enforced count bound rather than a same-function loop bound. 2 instances (`:5521,5575`).
- **NEW: ARR30-C "unbounded while loop with pointer increment" misapplied to a NULL-terminated `char *` pair-array scan (`iterator = props; while (*iterator) {...; iterator += 2;}`, `props` from `wpa_config_get_all()`)** — extends the existing NUL/sentinel-terminated-scan ARR30-C FP family from char-buffer scans to NULL-terminated pointer-array scans. 1 instance (`:6049`).
- **NEW: MSC13-C "declared but never used" misses a variable used only as another pointer's initializer (aliasing), not referenced again by its own name.** `u8 mask_buf[ETH_ALEN]; u8 *mask = mask_buf;` — `mask_buf` is genuinely used (as `mask`'s initializer, and `&mask` is later passed to `dbus_message_iter_append_fixed_array`), but sqc's unused-variable check doesn't follow the alias. 1 instance (`:4863`), worth a regression watch alongside the pointer-alias/ownership-tracking gaps noted elsewhere.
- **MSC01-C "no final else" reconfirmed** on a default-value guard shape (`type = ""` pre-set, `if/else if` only overrides it) (`:5711`).
- **MSC07-C "unreachable code after unconditional return" reconfirmed 3x** on the `return TRUE; nomem: dbus_set_error_const(...); return FALSE;` idiom, reached via earlier `goto nomem;` sites — same goto-label-blindness root cause (`:5600,5725,5935`).
- **MSC13-C dead-assignment reconfirmed genuine TP (low severity):** `dbus_bool_t success = FALSE;` in `wpas_dbus_getter_bss_rates` is unconditionally overwritten before any read on every path that reaches it (`:5413`).
- **NEW FN, not sqc-flagged:** `wpas_dbus_getter_sta_address`/`_sta_aid`/`_sta_caps` (`:4961,4991,5021`) dereference `args->wpa_s->ap_iface->bss[0]` with **no** NULL check on `ap_iface`, while their 4 sibling getters (`sta_rx_packets`/`tx_packets`/`tx_bytes`/`rx_bytes`, `:5053,5092,5131,5170`) all guard `if (!args->wpa_s->ap_iface) return FALSE;` first — an inconsistent/missing guard, plausible NULL deref (closest rule EXP34-C).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b28`, 150 findings, `wpa_supplicant/dbus/dbus_new_handlers.c` part2of5, lines ~1987-3951)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: API00-C "does not validate pointer parameter" on `wpas_dbus_handler_*`/`wpas_dbus_getter_*`/`wpas_dbus_setter_*` — extends the internal-only-API/dispatch-bound-callback FP family to D-Bus method/property dispatch specifically.** Every `wpas_dbus_handler_*` is registered as a `WPADBusMethodHandler` (`DBusMessage *(*)(DBusMessage *message, void *user_data)`, `dbus_new_helpers.h:17`) and every `wpas_dbus_getter_*`/`_setter_*` as a `WPADBusPropertyAccessor` (`:22`); both are invoked exclusively by libdbus-driven dispatch machinery in `dbus_new.c`/`dbus_new_helpers.c` that always supplies a live `message`/`iter`/`error`/`user_data` — never attacker-triggerable NULL. ~60 instances this batch (`message`, `wpa_s`, `global`, `iter`, `error` params across dozens of handlers/accessors).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP family extends to `WPADBusMethodHandler`'s own signature.** `message`/`wpa_s`/`global` params of `wpas_dbus_handler_*` functions are pinned by the fixed typedef (cast to `WPADBusMethodHandler` at each `dbus_new.c` registration site, e.g. `(WPADBusMethodHandler) wpas_dbus_handler_expect_disconnect`) — cannot be const-qualified without breaking the vtable, same root cause as eloop/EAP-table/libdbus-callback/`WPADBusPropertyAccessor` precedents. ~20 instances.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable with automatic storage" extends the heap-vs-stack-pointer-variable FP class to `DBusMessage *` handler return values.** `reply`/`error_reply` locals in `wpas_dbus_handler_*` always point to heap-allocated, refcounted `DBusMessage` objects (`dbus_message_new_error`/`dbus_message_new_method_return`, or an out-param from a helper like `get_peer_hwaddr_helper`) — never actual stack/automatic storage. 8 instances (lines 2708, 2863, 2897, 2932, 2941, 2961, 3117).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: ERR32-C "errno should not be used in signal handlers" misfires wholesale on ordinary D-Bus method-handler functions that are not POSIX signal handlers at all.** `wpas_dbus_handler_remove_network`/`_select_network`/`_network_reply` each do `errno = 0; id = strtoul(...); if (errno != 0) ...` — a correct, CERT-recommended errno-based strtoul validation — and ERR32-C fires on every `errno` read/write in the function regardless of whether it is registered as a `signal()`/`sigaction()` handler. 6 instances, one file (lines 2349, 2351, 2425, 2427, 2483, 2485). Rule appears to trigger on any errno use inside a function whose name/registration it hasn't actually checked against `signal()`/`sigaction()`.
- **ERR33-C/ERR00-C/ERR30-C strtoul false triggers — CONFIRMED, textbook errno-checked strtoul.** `net_id`/`id = strtoul(net_id, NULL, 10)` at `dbus_new_handlers.c:2484` is preceded by `errno = 0;` on the immediately prior line and followed by `if (errno != 0)` — ERR33-C/ERR00-C ("not checked") and ERR30-C ("errno not reset first") are all factually wrong for this exact call.
- **MSC37-C "non-void function may reach end without returning" — reconfirmed 2x, same `#ifdef X ... #else ... #endif` preprocessor-branch-blindness as `dbus_common.c:341` (`16-40_b24`).** `wpas_dbus_handler_network_reply` (`#ifdef IEEE8021X_EAPOL`) and `wpas_dbus_handler_roam` (`#ifdef CONFIG_NO_SCAN_PROCESSING`) both have an explicit `return` in every preprocessor branch; sqc only sees one branch. Lines 2455, 2522.
- **ARR02-C "implicit array bounds" reconfirmed 7x, all `ARRAY_SIZE()`-consumed local arrays** (`wpas_dbus_getter_capabilities`'s `scans[]`/multiple `args[]` locals, each immediately passed through `ARRAY_SIZE(args)`/`ARRAY_SIZE(scans)`) — same confirmed "size-mismatch risk never materializes" class as `16-40_b22`. Lines 3238, 3250, 3252, 3293, 3368, 3462, 3490.
- **STR30-C "passing string literal to function which may modify it" — CONFIRMED FP, both callees take `const char *` and never modify.** `wpa_dbus_mark_property_changed(..., const char *property)` (`dbus_new_helpers.h:141`) and libdbus's own `dbus_set_error_const(DBusError*, const char *name, const char *message)` (real API, by definition takes and stores a literal without copying/modifying). 5 instances.
- **FLP03-C "floating-point division without error checking" on integer division — reconfirmed 2x, same shape as `rrm.c:177` (`16-40_b19`).** `wpa_s->roam_time.usec / 1000` / `session_length.usec / 1000` operate on plain integer `os_reltime` fields; no floating point exists. Lines 3812, 3878.
- **ARR30-C/STR34-C reconfirmed on `wpas_dbus_getter_state`'s lowercasing loop** (`while (*tmp) { *tmp = tolower(*tmp); tmp++; }` over an `os_strdup()`'d NUL-terminated string) — same "provably-bounded NUL scan" (ARR30-C) and "plain char-to-char assignment, no widening" (STR34-C) FP shapes as `nt_password_hash.c`/`base64.c`. One new wrinkle: **STR37-C on the same `tolower(*tmp)` call judged a genuine (if low-severity) TP** — the cast really is absent, even though the actual runtime strings (`wpa_supplicant_state_txt()`'s fixed ASCII state names) can never contain a negative `char` in practice.
- **EXP34-C "passing null pointer to os_strlen" — FP, rule missed an `&&` short-circuit guard in the very same condition** (`arg != NULL && os_strlen(arg) == 0`). `dbus_new_handlers.c:2773`.
- **MSC13-C "declared but never used" on `path_buf` — same alias-blindness shape independently confirmed in `41plus_b29`'s note above** (`char path_buf[N], *path = path_buf;`, only `path` subsequently read/written) — first instance seen here at `:2171`, generalizes across the file.

### New FN this batch: invalid free on non-heap D-Bus string pointer

`wpas_dbus_handler_set_pkcs11_engine_and_module_path` (`dbus_new_handlers.c:3170-3217`): `dbus_message_iter_get_basic(&iter, &value)` returns a pointer into the **incoming DBusMessage's own internal string buffer** (never allocated by the caller); `pkcs11_engine_path = value;` (`:3187`) aliases it directly. If the *second* argument (module_path) is then missing/wrong-typed, the error path at `:3192` calls `os_free(pkcs11_engine_path)` — freeing memory that was never heap-allocated. Undefined behavior (MEM34-C: "only free memory allocated dynamically"), reachable by any D-Bus caller supplying a valid engine path followed by an invalid module path argument. sqc did not flag this call at all despite flagging unrelated `os_free`-adjacent findings elsewhere in the same file.

  NULL-check idiom, extends the mutually-exclusive-early-return family.**
  `wpas_dbus_get_scan_channels`'s `freqs` (lines 1578, 1592): `nfreqs =
  os_realloc_array(freqs, ...); if (nfreqs == NULL) os_free(freqs);
  freqs = nfreqs; if (freqs == NULL) return -1;` — the freed-and-null'd
  path always `return`s before the flagged "accessed after free" line
  is reached; sqc doesn't correlate the intervening `if (freqs == NULL)`
  guard with the earlier conditional free.
- **MEM30-C cross-function struct-field conflation, extends the
  EXP39-C/ARR30-C "cited allocation site is in an unrelated function"
  family to a same-file, same-execution false UAF with no cited
  cross-function site at all.** `wpas_dbus_handler_scan`'s cleanup loop
  `os_free((u8*)params.ssids[i].ssid)` / `os_free((u8*)
  params.extra_ies)` (lines 1778-1779) are the ONLY frees of these
  fields anywhere in the function — no genuine prior free exists on any
  reachable path (verified `wpas_dbus_get_scan_ssids`/`_get_scan_ies`
  never call free). Root cause unclear (possibly a `struct
  wpa_driver_scan_params` field-name match against an unrelated
  function elsewhere in the driver layer), but definitively FP here.
- **ERR32-C "errno should not be used in signal handlers" reconfirmed
  wholesale-misfire on ordinary (non-signal-handler) functions using the
  textbook `errno = 0; id = strtoul(...); if (errno != 0)` idiom** —
  matches the `41plus_b13` `wpas_dbus_handler_remove_network`-family
  entry exactly. `wpas_dbus_handler_remove_cred` (lines 1904, 1906).
- **PRE08-C "same first 8 characters" reconfirmed literally-true/
  low-value-TP convention, not FP-by-default.** `dbus_new_helpers.h` /
  `dbus_new_handlers.c` / `dbus_new.h` (lines 32, 32, 33) all genuinely
  share `dbus_new` as their first 8 characters.
- **MSC13-C dead-NULL-init on `DBusMessage *reply = NULL;` reconfirmed
  genuine-but-harmless TP** (every `wpas_dbus_handler_*` unconditionally
  overwrites `reply` before any return/goto-out reads it). Lines 771,
  992, 1817.
- **MSC07-C "unreachable code after unconditional return" reconfirmed FP
  on `error:`/`err:`/`oom:` goto-target labels reached from earlier
  `goto` statements in the same function.** Lines 348, 918, 1867.
- **ARR02-C "implicit array bounds" reconfirmed FP on file-scope
  self-sized initializer arrays, including one whose element count
  genuinely varies by `#ifdef` (hardcoding would be actively wrong).**
  `debug_strings[]` (line 43) and `dont_quote[]` (line 141, contains
  `#ifdef CONFIG_MESH`/`CONFIG_P2P`/`CONFIG_INTERWORKING`-gated entries).
- **MSC13-C "declared but never used" FP on a fixed buffer only accessed
  through an aliasing pointer.** `char path_buf[N], *path = path_buf;`
  (`wpas_dbus_handler_add_cred:1820`) — `path_buf` itself is never
  referenced again by name, but its storage is written/read throughout
  via `path`. Same aliasing-blindness root cause as the confirmed
  DCL13-C `pos = buf` family, now hitting MSC13-C.
- **ENV01-C reconfirmed wholesale misfire on an ordinary fixed-size
  local buffer with no `getenv()` anywhere in the function.**
  `path_buf[WPAS_DBUS_OBJECT_PATH_MAX]` (line 1820).
- **NEW FN class (not flagged by sqc): duplicate-dict-key parameter
  overwrite leaks.** `wpas_dbus_handler_scan`'s per-key helpers
  (`wpas_dbus_get_scan_ssids`/`_get_scan_ies`/`_get_scan_channels`)
  each start from a fresh local (`ssids_num = 0`/`ies = NULL`/`freqs =
  NULL`) and unconditionally overwrite `params->{ssids,extra_ies,
  freqs}` at the end. The `a{sv}` D-Bus dict has no dedup guarantee —
  a client that sends the "SSIDs"/"IEs"/"Channels" key twice in one
  `Scan()` call causes the first call's allocation(s) to be silently
  overwritten and leaked (never reaches the `out:` cleanup that only
  frees the final value). Closest CERT mapping: MEM31-C
  ("ensure resources are freed exactly once" — here: not at all for
  the shadowed first allocation). `dbus_new_handlers.c:1425-1426`
  (ssids), `:1491` (extra_ies), `:1594` (freqs). `upstream_present:
  unknown` (no separate upstream tracking checkout in this
  environment).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b35`, 91 findings, `src/crypto/crypto_openssl.c#part4of4`, lines ~4606-5698: RSA-OAEP + CONFIG_DPP3 HPKE code)

- **MEM31-C "leak due to goto" / "not freed" wholesale misfire, extreme
  volume in HPKE code -- reconfirms the existing goto-target-frees-it FP
  class at very high density (17 instances, one file section).** Every
  `hpke_*` helper (`hpke_encap`, `hpke_decap`, `hpke_aead_seal`,
  `hpke_aead_open`, `hpke_base_seal`, `hpke_base_open`) follows the
  standard OpenSSL `goto fail;`/`goto out;` idiom with a single trailing
  label that unconditionally frees every local resource
  (`EVP_PKEY_CTX_free`, `EVP_CIPHER_CTX_free`, `wpabuf_free`); sqc
  doesn't see the label's frees. Lines 5180, 5227, 5233, 5241, 5250,
  5259, 5347, 5392, 5398, 5406, 5416, 5555, 5640 (+ MEM30/31-C "double
  free" false positives on the same idiom at 4920x2, 5063, 5257, 5422
  where two `goto`s to the same label are mutually exclusive branches).
- **NEW sub-shape of the reassign/ownership-transfer MEM30-C family:
  "use-after-free: returning freed pointer" on a `res = buf; buf =
  NULL;` handoff followed by a shared cleanup label that frees `buf`
  (now NULL, so a safe no-op) and returns `res`.** sqc conflates `res`
  and `buf` as the same freed object even though the explicit
  `buf = NULL` before the label means the label's free never touches
  the memory `res` now owns. 2 instances, symmetric functions
  (`hpke_base_seal:5591`, `hpke_base_open:5658`). Only 2 so far -- watch
  for a 3rd before promoting out of batch-local.
- **STR34-C fires on a `size_t x = os_strlen(ptr)` assignment with zero
  char-widening involved -- new, more severe misfire than the previously
  documented char-to-char/pointer-arithmetic STR34-C sub-shapes.** The
  flagged "conversion" is a `const char *` argument to `os_strlen()`,
  not a char value being assigned into a wider integer type at all.
  1 instance (`crypto_openssl.c:4954`, `label_len = os_strlen(label)`).
- **DCL13-C correctly caught 3 genuine (low-severity) TPs on plain
  internal HPKE helper structs (`struct hpke_context *ctx`), read-only
  in each function and not bound to any callback/vtable contract** --
  distinct from the eloop/EAP-method-table DCL13-C FP family.
  `hpke_suite_id:4836`, `hpke_aead_seal:5211`, `hpke_aead_open:5370`.
- **MSC13-C correctly caught 2 more genuine (harmless) dead-NULL-init
  TPs** -- `EVP_PKEY_CTX *pctx = NULL;`/`struct crypto_ec_key *pk_e =
  NULL;` in `hpke_decap`, both unconditionally overwritten on the very
  next statement with no intervening read. `crypto_openssl.c:5317,5321`.
- **API00-C "does not validate pointer parameter" FP, extended to a
  genuinely cross-file (non-static) API** -- `hpke_base_seal`/
  `hpke_base_open`'s `info`/`aad` params are intentionally NULL-able
  (empty HPKE `info` field is protocol-legal; real caller
  `dpp_supplicant.c:3891` passes `info=NULL, info_len=0` by design) and
  every downstream use is length-gated or 0-length-safe; `pt` has no
  such caller ever passing NULL. `crypto_openssl.c:5663,5676`.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b36`, 150 findings, hostapd/ctrl_iface.c#part1of4)

- **DCL13-C "buf" output-buffer written through a local alias pointer —
  NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances, one file).** The common hostapd ctrl_iface
  reply-formatting idiom `pos = buf; end = buf + buflen; ...
  os_snprintf(pos, end - pos, ...); pos += ret;` never reassigns or
  writes through the `buf` parameter variable itself, but `pos` is a
  raw alias of the same memory, so every `os_snprintf(pos, ...)` call
  *does* write through `buf`'s pointee — the entire point of these
  functions is to fill the caller-supplied buffer. DCL13-C's "not
  modified" tracking apparently only follows direct writes to the named
  parameter, not writes through a same-address local alias, so it
  misses that `buf` can never be `const`. 4 instances:
  `hostapd_ctrl_iface_wps_get_status:549`,
  `hostapd_ctrl_iface_get_key_mgmt:794`,
  `hostapd_ctrl_iface_get_config:957`, `hostapd_ctrl_iface_get_rxkhs:1457`.
- **DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP class extended to `ap_for_each_sta()`
  per-STA iterator callbacks — CONFIRMED, same root cause as the
  eloop-timeout/EAP-method-table family.** A callback matching
  `ap_for_each_sta`'s fixed `(struct hostapd_data *hapd, struct
  sta_info *sta, void *ctx)` signature can't drop the unused `ctx` (or
  otherwise reshape the signature) without breaking the generic
  iterator contract. `hostapd_ctrl_iface_kick_mismatch_psk_sta_iter:1399`
  (registered at `:1447`).
- **DCL13-C "hapd" read-only-in-body reply-formatter functions —
  genuine, if low-severity, TPs (distinct from the forwarding-to-
  non-const-consumer FP class).** When a ctrl_iface handler only reads
  `hapd->conf->X`/`hapd->wps_stats.X` (never forwards `hapd` itself to
  a mutating callee, never assigns through it) the parameter really
  could be `const`. 4 instances: `hostapd_ctrl_iface_wps_get_status:548`,
  `hostapd_ctrl_iface_get_key_mgmt:793`, `hostapd_ctrl_iface_get_rxkhs:1456`,
  `hostapd_ctrl_iface_reload_rxkhs:1507` (the last only dereferences
  `hapd->conf` to pass the *conf* pointer onward — the pointee getting
  mutated doesn't require `hapd` itself to be non-const).
- **EXP34-C "os_free() does not check for NULL" — CONFIRMED categorical
  FP.** hostap's `os_free()` (`src/utils/os_unix.c:766`, also
  `os_none.c`/`os_internal.c`) explicitly does `if (ptr == NULL)
  return;` before freeing — exactly the standard `free(NULL)` no-op
  contract. The rule's premise is factually wrong for every `os_free`
  call site. 1 instance so far (`ctrl_iface.c:1657`), watch for more
  since `os_free` is used pervasively.
- **ERR02-C misidentifies `wpa_snprintf_hex()`/`wpa_snprintf_hex_uppercase()`
  as `sprintf()` — extends the confirmed `os_snprintf`-misidentification
  ERR02-C FP class to hostap's other bounded custom formatters.** Both
  functions (`src/utils/common.c:293-360`) always return a non-negative
  byte count (self-truncating, bounded by `buf_size`), never signal
  error via a negative return the way `sprintf` can overflow
  undetectably. 2 instances (`ctrl_iface.c:1480,1495`).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b38`, 150 findings, `hostapd/ctrl_iface.c` part3of4, lines ~3576-5274: NAN USD publish/subscribe, MIB dump, MLD ctrl_iface receive/init/deinit, hostapd_ctrl_iface_init UDP+UNIX socket setup)

- Heavy reconfirmation of established families: **sscanf(...,"key=%i",&v)==1
  bundle** (EXP20/ERR34/FIO47/INT05/MSC24, 5 sites), **atoi() ERR07/ERR34**
  split cleanly along the existing unchecked-vs-range-checked line (9 TP
  unchecked NAN/DPP command args vs 2 FP immediately-range-checked:
  `link_id`/`port`), **API05-C** ptr+size idiom (7 sites), **DCL13-C**
  eloop_sock_handler/proc_coord-callback `ctx`/`sock_ctx` FP (4 sites) vs
  genuine TP on plain non-callback params (`mld`, `hapd`, `buf` — 4 sites),
  **CON33-C/CON34-C** `strerror()` (26 sites, no pthread), **POS02-C**
  bind/chmod without privdrop (6 sites), **DCL30-C** returns-heap-not-stack
  (2 sites), **EXP40-C** fabricated-const (2 sites).
- **NEW: ARR30-C cross-function `buf`-name misattribution.** Two sibling
  socket-receive functions (`hostapd_ctrl_iface_receive`,
  `hostapd_mld_ctrl_iface_receive`) each declare their own `char buf[4096]`
  and write `buf[res] = '\0'` where `res` is bounded by that same
  `recvfrom(sock, buf, sizeof(buf)-1, ...)` call — safe. sqc's ARR30-C
  message cites a buffer size of 256 "allocated at line 5697", which is
  actually a *different*, unrelated function's `char buffer[256], *buf =
  buffer;` (`hostapd_global_ctrl_iface_receive`) — a same-file,
  same-variable-name conflation across function scopes, same root-cause
  family as the earlier-documented `EXP39-C` cross-function union
  conflation, now manifesting as a wrong-buffer-size citation in ARR30-C.
  `ctrl_iface.c:4610,4786`.
- **NEW: EXP33-C `sizeof(struct_var.field)` extends the confirmed
  `sizeof(*ptr)`-non-evaluated FP class to plain struct-member access.**
  `sizeof(addr.sun_path)` (where `addr` is an uninitialized-at-that-point
  `struct sockaddr_un`) flagged as "addr used uninitialized" — `sizeof` on
  a non-VLA member access never evaluates its operand, identical reasoning
  to the `sizeof(*ptr)` idiom already established, just one level of
  indirection different (member access instead of dereference).
  `ctrl_iface.c:4876,5203`.
- **Reinforces the `for_each_link`-style loop-macro EXP33-C/MSC13-C
  blindness for two more macros**: `for_each_mld_link(link_itr, ...)`
  (EXP33-C "link_itr uninitialized" + EXP34-C "null deref" at the same
  site, plus a paired MSC13-C "found never read" miss on the very next
  `if (!found) goto out;`) and `dl_list_for_each_safe(dst, prev, ...)`
  (EXP33-C "prev uninitialized" — the macro manages `prev` internally).
  `ctrl_iface.c:4715,4716,4717,4991`.
- **Reinforces the mutually-exclusive-branch MEM31-C "double free" FP
  family with a clean 3rd/4th/5th instance**: `os_free(fname)` on the
  success path (after `chmod()` succeeds) is followed immediately by a
  `return`/fallthrough that never reaches the later `fail:` label's own
  NULL-guarded `os_free(fname)` — sqc doesn't see that the two frees are
  on disjoint execution paths. `ctrl_iface.c:4936/4951` (MLD variant) and
  `:5274` (non-MLD variant).
- **NEW: MSC37-C ifdef-blind, reconfirmed for a case where *both* arms of
  the top-level `#ifdef`/`#else` return properly** — `hostapd_ctrl_iface_init`
  wraps its entire body in `#ifdef CONFIG_CTRL_IFACE_UDP ... return
  0;/return -1; #else ... return 0;/return -1; #endif`; naive text-order
  reading (ignoring the `#else`) makes it look like control can fall off
  the end. `ctrl_iface.c:5044`.
- **NEW: EXP34-C on `getaddrinfo()`'s output pointer guarded by the
  return-code check, not a direct NULL check.** `n = getaddrinfo(...); if
  (n) goto fail;` is the POSIX-correct way to validate `res` (on success,
  `*res` is guaranteed non-NULL) — rule doesn't recognize a nonzero-return-
  code check as equivalent to a NULL guard on the output param. `ctrl_iface.c:5096`.
- **NEW: INT32-C on a small-buffer reply-accounting idiom
  (`reply_size - reply_len` / `reply_len += res`).** `reply_size` is a
  small compile-time-bounded reply buffer (4096), so neither the
  subtraction nor the compound addition can realistically approach
  `INT_MIN`/`INT_MAX` — extends the "rule doesn't see realistic
  protocol/domain bounds" INT32-C family to buffer-size bookkeeping.
  `ctrl_iface.c:3984,3988,3992,3996,4002,4006`. Also reinforces the
  pointer-mistyped-INT32-C family once more (`buf + 7` where `buf` is
  `char[4096]`, `:4648`).
