## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b33`, 150 findings, `src/crypto/crypto_openssl.c` lines ~1362-3027, part 2 of 4)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP05-C "cast away const" fires on casts from a
  pointer that was never const-qualified to begin with — a straight
  rule bug, not a judgment call.** The opaque wrapper types in this
  file (`struct crypto_bignum *`, `struct crypto_ec_point *`) are
  frequently declared as plain (non-const) output/in-out parameters
  (e.g. `crypto_bignum_add(..., struct crypto_bignum *c)`,
  `crypto_bignum_rand(struct crypto_bignum *r, ...)`,
  `crypto_ec_point_add(..., struct crypto_ec_point *c)`). Casting such
  an already-non-const `r`/`c`/`y` to `(BIGNUM *) r` /
  `(EC_POINT *) c` cannot "cast away const" because there was no
  const to begin with — the rule appears to flag *any* cast from the
  opaque wrapper type to the underlying OpenSSL type regardless of the
  parameter's actual qualification. 9 confirmed-bogus instances one
  file/batch (`crypto_openssl.c:2086,2094,2109,2157,2171,2193,2259,
  2270,2626,2934` — `r`/`c`/`y` all declared non-const). Contrast: 2
  genuine TPs survive scrutiny in the same batch where the source
  really is `const struct crypto_bignum *a` and the cast-away pointer
  is then passed to `BN_set_flags(..., BN_FLG_CONSTTIME)`, which
  really does mutate the pointee's flags field through the cast
  (`crypto_openssl.c:2155,2191`, `crypto_bignum_inverse`/
  `crypto_bignum_div`) — so the rule can be right when the source
  param is genuinely `const` and something writes through it; the bug
  is specifically misfiring on non-const sources.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: ARR01-C "sizeof applied to pointer/array parameter
  which decayed" misfires on `sizeof(*ptr)` (dereference-then-sizeof)
  applied to a plain pointer *parameter*, conflating the correct
  pointee-sizing idiom with the decayed-array-sizeof bug ARR01-C is
  meant to catch.** `bin_clear_free(ctx, sizeof(*ctx))` where `ctx` is
  a `struct crypto_hash *` parameter — `sizeof(*ctx)` correctly yields
  `sizeof(struct crypto_hash)` via dereference; nothing "decayed" since
  there was never an array. The rule's own suggested fix ("Do not use
  `sizeof(*ctx)`") shows it is specifically confusing the dereference
  form with the bug shape. 5 instances, one file
  (`crypto_openssl.c:1528,1535,1541,1565,1573`, all in
  `crypto_hash_finish`/`crypto_hash_update`). Distinct from the
  already-documented `eap_pax.c:141,257` ARR01-C sub-shape (`16-40_b16`)
  in that this one is specifically the `bin_clear_free`/`free`-sizing
  idiom rather than a struct-size computation for later use.
- **Reinforces EXP20-C "==1, may return >1" OpenSSL-contract FP class
  with 4 more confirmed-exact-contract functions.** `BN_rand_range`,
  `BN_rshift`, `EC_POINT_get_affine_coordinates`,
  `EC_POINT_is_on_curve` all return exactly 1 (success) or 0 (failure)
  per OpenSSL's own documented API convention — none can return values
  `>1`. `crypto_openssl.c:2086,2270,2546,2685`.
- **Reinforces the API00-C/EXP34-C "internal-invariant opaque handle,
  no per-file NULL-check convention" FP class at large scale.** Every
  `crypto_ec`/`crypto_ecdh` accessor in this file (`crypto_ec_prime_len`,
  `_prime_len_bits`, `_order_len`, `_get_prime/order/a/b`,
  `_point_to_bin/add/mul/invert/is_at_infinity/is_on_curve/cmp`,
  `crypto_ecdh_get_pubkey`, etc.) dereferences its `struct crypto_ec *e`
  / `struct crypto_ecdh *ecdh` parameter with no NULL check; only the
  two boundary functions (`crypto_ec_deinit`, `crypto_ec_point_init`)
  ever guard, which is the opposite of an established per-file
  convention (contrast with the `ieee802_1x_kay.c` outlier-TP case from
  `16-40_b16`, where ~25 sibling functions *did* establish a
  convention) — confirms the FP default applies here. ~20 API00-C +
  8 EXP34-C instances, `crypto_openssl.c:2485-2871` range.
- **Reinforces the "MEM31-C leak due to goto when the goto target
  label DOES free the object" FP class, including a 2-hop
  fail→done cascade.** Several functions here `goto fail` where
  `fail:` itself just does `goto done;`, and `done:` is the one that
  actually frees the resource — the rule doesn't see through the
  2-hop indirection. `crypto_ecdh_init`'s `params` (`:2790,2801,2807`,
  freed at `done:` via `EVP_PKEY_free(params)`), `crypto_ecdh_get_pubkey`'s
  `x`/`buf` (`:2925`, freed via `fail: wpabuf_free(buf); ...; goto done;`
  then `done: BN_clear_free(x); ...`), `crypto_ecdh_set_peerkey`'s `pub`
  (`:3025`, freed at `done: ... EC_POINT_free(pub);`).
- **NEW: MEM03-C real FN — sensitive private-key debug-print buffer
  freed without clearing (1 instance, not caught by sqc).**
  `crypto_ec_key_debug_print()` (`crypto_openssl.c:4239-4263`) renders
  an EC private key via `EVP_PKEY_print_private()` into a heap `txt`
  buffer, logs it, then `os_free(txt)` with no `forced_memzero`/`memset`
  first — every other sensitive buffer in this file (`dhss`, `eae_prk`,
  `secret`, `key_schedule_context`, `shared_secret`) is properly
  cleared before free/return, making this the one outlier. Debug-path
  only, so low real-world severity, but a genuine gap sqc's MEM03-C
  scan missed.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b32`, 150 findings, `src/crypto/crypto_openssl.c#part1of4`, lines 59-1362)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP20-C "==1 test, function may return >1" misapplied
  to OpenSSL EVP_* API calls — 20 instances, one file.** `EVP_EncryptInit_ex`,
  `EVP_DecryptInit_ex`, `EVP_CIPHER_CTX_set_padding`, `EVP_EncryptUpdate`,
  `EVP_DecryptUpdate`, `EVP_EncryptFinal_ex`, `EVP_DecryptFinal_ex` are all
  documented by OpenSSL to return *exactly* 1 on success or 0 (occasionally
  a negative code) on failure — never anything >1. `== 1` is the
  textually-correct, officially-recommended success test, not a hazard.
  Extends the existing sscanf-single-specifier "==1 is fine when only one
  outcome is possible" EXP20-C FP class to the OpenSSL EVP API's
  documented 1/0 contract. `crypto_openssl.c:410,411,412,413,677,678,679,
  681,721,722,723,725,763,764,765,767,790,791,792,794`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MSC13-C "dead assignment" on file-scope `static`
  variables whose value is read by a *different function* on a
  *later call* — 4 instances, one file.** `openssl_disable_fips`'s
  `done = true`, `openssl_load_legacy_provider`/`_unload_legacy_provider`'s
  `openssl_legacy_provider = ...`/`= NULL`, and the matching
  `openssl_default_provider` pair are all read via the guard check
  (`if (x) return;` / `if (x) {...}`) on a subsequent, separate
  invocation of a sibling function — sqc's dead-assignment dataflow is
  intra-function only and doesn't track cross-function/cross-invocation
  reads of static/global state. `crypto_openssl.c:197,223,233,263`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM31-C "double free" bleeding across mutually-exclusive
  `#if`/`#elif`/`#else` alternative function bodies — 2+ instances,
  extends the existing preprocessor-branch-blind family (previously only
  seen for MSC37-C/DCL40-C) to MEM31-C.** `dh5_init()` has 3 OpenSSL-version
  variants, each starting with its own independent `wpabuf_free(*publ)`
  call; sqc treats the 2nd/3rd variant's own first free as a repeat of the
  1st variant's free, even though only one variant is ever compiled/executed.
  `crypto_openssl.c:1092,1147` (paired with the un-flagged 1st occurrence at
  `:1038`).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM30-C/MEM31-C container-vs-sub-field free
  conflation — reinforces the existing entry (`:1158,1948,2124` in this
  doc), now with a `struct`-with-2-sibling-pointer-fields shape, 15+
  instances one function.** `crypto_cipher_init()`'s cleanup paths free
  `ctx->enc`/`ctx->dec` (sub-object fields) then `os_free(ctx)` (the
  container itself) — 3 genuinely distinct allocations, but sqc reports
  "ctx already freed"/"UAF" as soon as any field is freed, including
  flagging the *condition chain that runs before any free* as if the
  free already happened. `crypto_openssl.c:975-981,986-993,997`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM31-C false leak/double-free on the
  alloc-then-transfer-ownership-then-NULL-out idiom — extends the existing
  ownership-transfer MEM31 FP class (`sae_pk_gen.c` free-then-reassign;
  `eap_md5.c` register()-consumes) to a new shape: local `BIGNUM
  *g/p/q/pub_key/priv_key` handed to `DH_set0_pqg()`/`DH_set0_key()`
  (which take ownership) and then explicitly set to `NULL` right after,
  so the shared `err:` cleanup label's `BN_free()`/`BN_clear_free()` calls
  are no-ops on the success path and the sole real free on the failure
  path.** 6 instances, one file: `crypto_openssl.c:1154,1182` (`g`),
  `:1270,1288` (`g`), `:1293,1294` (`pub_key`/`priv_key`).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: multi-line `||`-chained `if` condition findings
  misattributed to the condition's *first physical line* — extends the
  existing "||/&& not recognized as sequence points" engine bug (`:3981`)
  with a location/attribution symptom, 3 instances one file.** EXP30-C
  "variable modified/accessed without sequence point" cites variables
  (`priv_len`, `pubkey`, `params`, `dctx`) that don't even appear on the
  cited line — they're assigned several `||`-chained lines further down,
  properly sequenced by `||` short-circuit evaluation.
  `crypto_openssl.c:1106,1240,1312`.
- **EXP34-C "passing null pointer to X which does not check for NULL"
  extended to `wpabuf_clear_free()` — CONFIRMED, extends the existing
  `os_free(NULL)`-is-safe FP class.** `wpabuf_clear_free()`
  (`src/utils/wpabuf.c:212`) explicitly does `if (buf) { ...; wpabuf_free(buf);
  }` — NULL-safe by construction. `crypto_openssl.c:1126,1189`.
- **EXP34-C false NULL-deref where the pointer's non-NULL-ness is
  guaranteed by an `||`-short-circuited alloc check earlier in the same
  condition — new shape of the short-circuit-blindness family.**
  `!(res = wpabuf_alloc(len)) || EVP_PKEY_derive(dctx, wpabuf_mhead(res), ...)`:
  `wpabuf_mhead(res)` only evaluates once the alloc-check operand already
  proved `res` non-NULL. `crypto_openssl.c:1321`.
- Compat-shim functions that intentionally reproduce a fixed external
  OpenSSL API signature (`EVP_PKEY_get0_EC_KEY`-style polyfills for older
  OpenSSL) are a DCL13-C FP shape distinct from eloop/EAP dispatch tables
  but same root cause — signature is pinned by the real external API, not
  a genuine const opportunity. `crypto_openssl.c:97`. Only 1 instance so
  far, batch-local.
- A compat shim casting away const purely to call a legacy non-const
  *pure-getter* (`ASN1_STRING_data()`) is a real but arguably-idiomatic
  EXP05-C hit — no mutation actually occurs through the cast pointer, but
  the literal cast-away-const is present and CERT's text doesn't carve out
  a "getter" exception. Judged TP here (low severity); only 1 instance,
  batch-local, worth reconciling if a future batch disagrees.
  `crypto_openssl.c:126`.
- MSC42-C "weak cryptographic function" (DES/RC4/3DES) judged TP even
  though the calls exist solely for legacy WEP/TKIP/EAP wire-protocol
  interop, not implementer preference — a competent reviewer can't simply
  swap the algorithm without breaking protocol compatibility, but the
  weak-crypto usage is real and worth surfacing/gating regardless.
  5 instances: `crypto_openssl.c:410,440,932,958,961`.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b37`, 150 findings, `hostapd/ctrl_iface.c#part2of4`, lines ~1690-3580)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: INT07-C "variable of type char used in numeric
  operation" misattributes 'char' to a variable actually declared `int`
  — rule bug, 6/6 instances in one file.** `hostapd_ctrl_iface_log_level`,
  `hostapd_ctrl_driver_flags`/`flags2`, `hostapd_ctrl_iface_driver_cmd`
  (ANDROID), and `hostapd_ctrl_iface_link_remove` all declare `int ret;`
  (sometimes `int ret, i;`) and are flagged as if `ret` were `char` —
  no `char`-typed variable is even present at the flagged lines. Only 2
  genuinely `char`-typed instances exist anywhere nearby
  (`hostapd_ctrl_iface_notify_cw_htaction`/`_notify_cw_vhtaction` return
  `char`, forwarding an `int`-returning driver call's 0/-1 result as a
  boolean-ish flag) and even those aren't "numeric operations" in any
  meaningful sense — just tested truthy and returned. `ctrl_iface.c:2984,
  3378,3406,3463,3562,3564`. Watch for recurrence anywhere sqc flags
  INT07-C on a `ret`/counter variable — check the actual declaration
  before trusting the message.
- **ARR37-C "pointer arithmetic on non-array pointer" on `pos =
  &buf[sizeof(*eth)+sizeof(ip)]` then `pos++`/`pos != end` — direct
  cross-codebase reconfirmation of the `41plus_b8` wpa_supplicant
  precedent (`ctrl_iface.c:10240`), same exact shape now in hostapd's
  port of the same test-data-RX code.** `ctrl_iface.c:1884,1986`.
- **INT30-C genuine TP reconfirmed cross-codebase: `hostapd_data_test_rx`
  is hostapd's port of the wpa_supplicant `wpas_data_test_rx` function
  already flagged as a real underflow TP in `41plus_b8`.** Never
  validates `ntohs(ip.ip_len) >= sizeof(ip)` before `ntohs(ip.ip_len) -
  sizeof(ip)` sizes a for-loop bound — same bug, same missing guard, in
  the hostapd copy. `ctrl_iface.c:1878`. Sibling
  `hostapd_ctrl_iface_data_test_tx` (`:1998`) IS guarded (validates
  `i >= sizeof(*ip)` first) — same guarded/unguarded pair distinction as
  the wpa_supplicant precedent.
- **ERR33-C/ERR00-C/ERR01-C strtol()/strtoul() FP when a TIGHT downstream
  magnitude range check exists (not just an endptr/trailing-char check)
  — clarifies/extends the `41plus_b23` "downstream *endp+range check"
  distinction with a tighter-bound sub-case.** `val = strtol(pos, &pos2,
  0); if (val < 0 || val > 0xff)` (`:1969`) and `color = strtol(pos,
  &end, 10); if (pos == end || color < 0 || color > 63)` (`:2567`) both
  bound the result to a narrow range that no realistic overflow could
  land inside — FP for ERR33-C/ERR00-C/ERR01-C. ERR30-C ("errno not
  reset first") still graded TP (low) per the existing precedent's own
  logic even though the tight bound arguably makes it moot too — flagged
  for reconciliation if a future batch wants to tighten that call.
  Contrast with `:2412` (`type = strtol(cmd, &pos, 16); if (*pos != ' ')`)
  and `:2875,2879` (`strtoul` with only a following-blank-char check) —
  both have only an endptr/trailing-char check with NO magnitude bound
  at all, matching the original weaker-validation TP shape.
- **DCL13-C correctly misses a mutation performed via a direct (non-
  aliased) struct-field write — NEW sub-shape, distinct from the
  documented "aliased local pointer" miss.** `hostapd_ctrl_iface_data_test_config`'s
  `hapd` parameter is flagged as a const candidate, but the function
  directly writes `hapd->l2_test = NULL;` and `hapd->l2_test =
  l2_packet_init(...);` through `hapd` itself (no alias/second local
  involved) — this genuinely cannot be `const`. `ctrl_iface.c:1938`.
  Contrast with the reconfirmed aliased-`buf`-via-`pos`-alias FP shape
  at `:3018,3053` (buf only ever written through a `pos = buf` local).
- **MSC41-C "hard-coded sensitive information" flags a plain control-flag
  string, not secret material — new sub-shape of the confirmed
  security-substring-pattern-match family.** `wpa_auth_resend_m1(...,
  os_strstr(cmd, "change-anonce") != NULL, ...)` — `"change-anonce"` is
  a ctrl_iface command-flag substring (matches CERT's ANonce protocol
  term), not a password/key/token. `ctrl_iface.c:2280`.
- **EXP33-C "used uninitialized"/"reading uninitialized data" on
  `dst`/`src`/`buf` where the first two are function parameters already
  filled by an earlier `hwaddr_aton2()` output-param call, and the third
  is only having its *address* taken (`&buf[2]`), never its contents
  read — extends the established EXP33-C output-param-write-blindness
  family to a 3-site cluster in one function.** `ctrl_iface.c:1982,1983,
  1984` (`hostapd_ctrl_iface_data_test_tx`).
- **EXP33-C "used uninitialized" on a fixed local array whose elements
  are written element-by-element through an output-param call inside a
  loop (`hwaddr_aton(token, responders + n_responders * ETH_ALEN)`),
  flagged on the very call that performs the write — same
  output-param-write-blindness family, new "self-referential" sub-shape.**
  `ctrl_iface.c:3135` (`hostapd_ctrl_iface_req_range`).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b40`, 150 findings, 1 file:
wpa_supplicant/config.c#part1of4, lines 1-1992: the `struct parse_data`
generic network-config parser/writer table)

- **NEW: config-parser dispatch-table DCL13-C — extends the eloop/EAP-method
  callback-contract FP class to `wpa_supplicant/config.c`'s `ssid_fields[]`
  table (`struct parse_data.parser`/`.writer` fixed-signature function
  pointers).** ~21 instances, all on the `ssid` param. Two distinct reasons,
  both FP: (a) parser-side functions (`wpa_config_parse_str/int_impl/psk/
  proto/key_mgmt/...`) actually DO write through `ssid` via computed pointer
  offsets (`dst = (T*)((u8*)ssid + data->paramN); *dst = val;`) — sqc's
  "not modified" claim is simply wrong, since it doesn't track writes
  through offset-computed derived pointers as aliasing the parameter; (b)
  writer-side functions (`wpa_config_write_str/int/bssid/psk/...`) never
  modify `ssid` but are pinned by the `char *(*writer)(const struct
  parse_data*, struct wpa_ssid*)` callback-table signature, same as the
  already-documented eloop/EAP-method class. Test to disambiguate from a
  real DCL13-C opportunity in this same file: is the function itself
  wired into `ssid_fields[]` as a `.parser`/`.writer` entry (FP either way)
  vs. a private helper never registered in the table, e.g.
  `wpa_config_write_addr_list`'s unused `name` param (TP, confirmed) or
  `wpa_config_print_int_array`'s `array` param, whose pointee is
  never written even though the local pointer is incremented (TP, confirmed).
- **NEW: ARR00-C "negative subscript" on `end[-1]` where `end = buf + N`
  (a computed end-of-buffer pointer from a fixed-size `os_zalloc(N)`) —
  CONFIRMED FP, third variant of the existing `ptr[-1]`-after-delimiter-
  advance pattern family.** Unlike the `ctrl_iface.c` variants (delimiter-
  restore after `*ptr++`), here `end[-1]` is used to truncate the buffer's
  last byte on an `os_snprintf` overflow (`end[-1] = '\0'; return buf;`) —
  always a valid, in-bounds byte since `end` points one past the
  allocation's last valid index. 24+ instances in one function
  (`wpa_config_write_key_mgmt`), reconfirmed in 5 sibling writer functions
  (`write_freqs`, `write_eap`, `write_auth_alg`, etc.) — expect this
  `end = buf + N` / `end[-1]` idiom throughout every `wpa_config_write_*`
  function in this file.
- **NEW: DCL30-C/ARR00-C "returns pointer to local variable/array" on
  every `wpa_config_write_*` function's `buf`/`value`/`freqs` — CONFIRMED
  FP, ~20 instances, reinforces the existing heap-not-stack confusion
  class to an entire file's writer-function family.** Every instance is
  `os_malloc`/`os_zalloc`/`os_calloc`/`os_realloc_array`-allocated heap
  memory returned to the caller, not automatic storage.
- **NEW: DCL30-C "local variable assigned through pointer parameter" —
  extends the existing macro-constant-out-param FP to a plain
  pointer/int *value* copied into a `(T*)((u8*)ssid+offset)` computed
  out-param slot** (`*dst = tmp;`, `*dst = val;` where `tmp`/`val` hold a
  heap-pointer or plain int *value*, never an address-of). 4 instances
  (`config.c:130,132,233,330`). Same root confusion as the earlier
  macro-constant case, just a different target shape (struct-field slot
  instead of a plain out-param).
- **NEW: STR34-C misattribution/line-drift — fires on lines with no char
  assignment or conversion at all.** `config.c:130` flags `*dst` (type
  `char **` deref → `char *`, a pointer, not a char) and `config.c:1216`
  flags `value` (a `const char *` parameter) at a line that is actually
  `int val = wpa_parse_cipher(value);` — no char-to-int conversion
  exists there. Distinct from (but adjacent to) the already-confirmed
  "plain char assignment, no widening" STR34-C FP class, which also
  recurs heavily in this file (`*end = '\0';`/`*pos++ = ' ';`, 5+ instances).
- **NEW: string-literal misparse (INT10-C/INT33-C) reconfirmed in a 2nd
  file, extended to INT14-C too.** Same bug as the `hostapd/config_file.c`
  precedent (batch `41plus_b25`-adjacent): `wpa_printf(..., "invalid
  key_mgmt '%s'", ...)` trips INT10-C/INT14-C on `%s`, and `"key_mgmt:
  0x%x"` trips INT33-C/INT10-C "division/modulo by 'x'" on the `%x` format
  specifier. 6 instances (`config.c:893,906,912`, each 2 rules).
- **NEW: INT14-C struct-pointer/field conflation reconfirmed for `ssid`
  itself (not just other struct pointers).** `ssid->key_mgmt`/`ssid->eap.
  flags` are used with `&`/`|=` (bitwise) in various branches, but `ssid`
  itself is never itself a bitwise/arithmetic operand, only ever
  member-accessed. 3 instances (`config.c:910,1950,1985`).
- **NEW: MEM30-C false UAF/free-arithmetic with literally no preceding
  `os_free()` call anywhere in the function — looks like cross-function
  name conflation, same root cause as the documented EXP39-C bug.**
  `wpa_config_write_key_mgmt` (`config.c:931,935`) is flagged for
  "pointer arithmetic on freed `end`" and "returning freed `buf`", but
  `buf`/`end` are freshly `os_zalloc`'d in this exact function with zero
  `os_free()` calls anywhere in it — the free calls that exist are in
  *sibling* writer functions (`write_proto`, `write_auth_alg`, etc.) that
  happen to reuse the same local variable names `buf`/`end`. Same cluster
  also produced a nonsense STR31-C ("character array too small" on a
  plain pointer-assignment line), a nonsense MSC13-C (dead-assignment to
  a variable literally named `if`, i.e. an `else if (...)` line), and a
  nonsense MEM05-C (VLA on a line with no array at all) — all pointing at
  line numbers with no matching construct, suggesting a batch of findings
  got attributed to the wrong lines/functions in this densely repetitive
  100+-line `if (flag & MASK) {...}` writer function.
- **NEW: ARR00-C "accessed after freed" cross-function conflation for
  `freqs`.** `wpa_config_parse_int_array` (`config.c:1492,1493`) is
  flagged for accessing `freqs` after it was freed, but no `os_free
  (freqs)` occurs anywhere in that function — the frees are in *caller*
  functions (`wpa_config_parse_scan_freq`/`_freq_list`) that declare their
  own distinct local `int *freqs`. Same conflation root cause as the
  MEM30-C entry above.
- **MSC37-C "may reach end without returning" reconfirmed wrong on
  functions with full #ifdef/#else return coverage** — 3 instances
  (`config.c:796,1211,1233`), consistent with the existing preprocessor-
  branch-blindness family.
- **MSC01-C "no final else" reconfirmed wrong when the terminal `else`
  exists but is separated from the `if`/`else if` chain start by many
  `#ifdef CONFIG_*` blocks** (`config.c:826`, else exists at `:892`).
- **INT13-C "bitwise op on signed operand" on a local `int val` that is
  provably non-negative from an earlier same-function `if (val == -1)
  return -1;` guard — extends the existing "rule doesn't see an earlier
  guard" family (INT30/INT33/ARR30) to INT13-C.** 3 instances
  (`config.c:1261,1299,1332`, all `wpa_config_parse_cipher`'s callers).
- **ERR07-C/ERR34-C `atoi()` graded FP when 0 is used purely as a
  list-termination sentinel and 0 is never a semantically valid parsed
  value (frequency list parsing)** — extends the existing "range-checked
  atoi" FP shape to a "sentinel-value" shape. `config.c:1492`
  (`wpa_config_parse_int_array`).
- **ERR33-C/ERR00-C/ERR01-C/ERR30-C on `strtol()` reconfirmed TP (low),
  same "*end-checked but no errno/ERANGE guard" shape as the ctrl_iface.c
  precedent.** `config.c:209` (`wpa_config_parse_int_impl`).
- **NEW: EXP34-C "potential null pointer dereference" on `strtol()`'s
  `&end` output parameter — CONFIRMED FP.** `strtol()` always writes
  through a non-NULL `endptr` argument per the C standard; the pointer it
  populates can never be NULL after the call. `config.c:210`.
- **MEM30-C UAF reconfirmed FP where the "freed" pointer is reassigned to
  a fresh allocation before the flagged read — same shape as the
  `mem30-reassign-and-fresh-binding` fix class, apparently not fully
  covering `str_clear_free()`.** `ssid->passphrase` is freed then
  immediately reassigned via `dup_binstr()` before the NULL-check reads
  it. `config.c:609`.


## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b34`, 150 findings, `src/crypto/crypto_openssl.c` part3of4, lines ~3033-4610: EC key/CSR/PKCS7/RSA-read OpenSSL wrapper functions)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (~35 instances): "MEM31-C leak due to goto" is FP whenever
  the goto target (a `fail:`/`out:` label, possibly chained `fail: ...; goto
  out;`) genuinely frees the object** — this file's dominant idiom is
  `alloc; if (!x || ...) goto fail; ...; out: free(a); free(b); return
  result; fail: free(c); ...; goto out;`. Every `EC_POINT_new`/`EC_KEY_new`/
  `EVP_PKEY_new`/`EVP_PKEY_CTX_new`/`BN_CTX_new` "leak due to goto" finding
  checked in `crypto_ecdh_decrypt`, `crypto_ec_key_set_priv`,
  `crypto_ec_key_set_pub(_point)`, `crypto_ec_key_gen`, and
  `crypto_ec_key_get_subject_public_key`'s BoringSSL branch was FP —
  the label chain frees it. Reconfirms/bulk-extends `16-40_b1`'s original
  "MEM31-C leak due to goto when target frees" entry.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (~10 instances): "MEM31-C leak/not freed before return"
  on the function's own return-value pointer is FP — returning a pointer
  transfers ownership to the caller, it is not a leak.** E.g.
  `crypto_ec_key_parse_priv`/`_set_priv`/`_set_pub`/`_set_pub_point`/`_gen`
  all `return (struct crypto_ec_key *) pkey;` and get flagged as "pkey not
  freed before return". Also covers the `EVP_PKEY_assign_EC_KEY(pkey,
  eckey)` sub-case: once `eckey`'s ownership is merged into `pkey` via
  `_assign_`, freeing/returning `pkey` alone covers `eckey` too — a 2nd
  "not freed" finding on `eckey` at the same return is also FP.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances): "wrapper function frees it, tool doesn't
  see through the wrapper" MEM31-C FP, now for `crypto_ec_key_deinit()`**
  (a 1-line `EVP_PKEY_free((EVP_PKEY *) key)` wrapper) — same root cause as
  the earlier BIO-helper/`nl80211_nlmsg_clear` wrapper entries, extended to
  this project's own key-deinit wrapper. `crypto_ec_key_parse_priv:3157`,
  `crypto_ec_key_parse_pub` fail: path.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (~15 instances): mutually-exclusive `#if
  OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER >= 0x30000000L ... #else ... #endif` (sometimes
  3-way with a nested `#ifdef OPENSSL_IS_BORINGSSL`) branch conflation —
  a NEW preprocessor-blindness shape beyond the existing MSC17/MSC37/DCL40
  family: sqc conflates same-named locals (`pkey`, `der`, `priv_bin`,
  `pub_bin`, `priv`) declared independently in mutually-exclusive
  branches, producing bogus "double free"/"leaked"/"use-after-free"
  findings that reference a free or allocation that only exists in the
  *other*, never-simultaneously-executed branch.** E.g. `priv_bin`/
  `pub_bin` (only declared in the `>=3.0` branch) "leaked" inside the
  `#else` branch that has no such variables at all
  (`crypto_ec_key_set_priv:3250,3287`); `priv`'s `BN_clear_free` in one
  branch flagged as a "double free" of the other branch's independent
  `BN_clear_free(priv)` (`:3285`); `der`'s `OPENSSL_free` in the
  non-BoringSSL branch flagged as a double-free of the BoringSSL branch's
  unrelated `der` (`crypto_ec_key_get_subject_public_key:3748`); `pkey`
  in the `>=3.0` branch (borrowed param, never freed there) flagged as
  "use-after-free"/"leak" by conflating it with the `>=3.0` branch's
  unrelated `EVP_PKEY_free(copy)` (`crypto_ec_key_get_ecprivate_key:3804`,
  and 6 more "leak not freed before return" instances across
  `crypto_ec_key_get_subject_public_key`'s 3 branches and
  `crypto_ec_key_get_ecprivate_key`'s 2 branches).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances): "reassign-then-free" aliasing extended
  to `EVP_PKEY_dup()`.** `copy = EVP_PKEY_dup(pkey); ...; pkey = copy;`
  then `EVP_PKEY_free(copy)` before/at return — sqc tracks the dup'd
  allocation under the post-reassignment name `pkey` but the free under
  the pre-reassignment name `copy` (same underlying pointer), so it
  doesn't see the free. Same root cause as the `tls_openssl_ocsp.c`
  reassign-then-free class (`16-40_b7`), new call (`EVP_PKEY_dup` vs
  simple pointer reassignment). `crypto_ec_key_get_subject_public_key:
  3663,3672`, `crypto_ec_key_get_ecprivate_key:3790,3796`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances): EXP34-C "passing null pointer to
  wpabuf_alloc_copy" FP when the call is already guarded by the
  preceding `i2d_*()`/`OSSL_ENCODER_to_data()` success/length check.**
  OpenSSL's "allocate into a double pointer" convention
  (`i2d_X(x, &der)` / `OSSL_ENCODER_to_data(ctx, &pdata, &len)`) only
  returns a positive length / success code when the output pointer was
  actually allocated; `der_len <= 0` / `!= 1` checks immediately above
  each `wpabuf_alloc_copy(der, der_len)` call already exclude the NULL
  case. `crypto_ec_key_get_subject_public_key:3720,3747`,
  `crypto_ec_key_get_ecprivate_key:3793,3821`, `crypto_csr_sign:4536`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances): MSC07-C "unreachable code after
  unconditional return" misfiring on a `fail:`/similar label that IS a
  live goto target — extends the existing goto/label-blindness family
  (previously seen on MEM31-C/ARR00-C/MSC13-C) to MSC07-C.** A `return
  X; fail: ...` shape where earlier lines in the same function `goto
  fail;` is not dead code just because it textually follows a return.
  `crypto_ec_key_parse_pub:3318`, `crypto_ec_key_sign_r_s:4109`,
  `crypto_csr_verify:4380`, `crypto_rsa_key_read_public:4588`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances): DCL31-C "called without prior
  declaration" FP on genuine OpenSSL library functions declared in a
  system header included at the top of the file.** `PEM_read_PUBKEY`/
  `PEM_read_X509`/`PEM_read_PrivateKey` (`<openssl/pem.h>`) and
  `X509_free`/`EVP_PKEY_base_id` (`<openssl/x509.h>`/`<openssl/evp.h>`,
  both included) — sqc doesn't resolve declarations pulled in from
  system/library headers, only from project-local ones.
  `crypto_rsa_key_read_public:4552,4557,4577,4581`,
  `crypto_rsa_key_read:4603`.
- **Reinforces the existing DCL30-C heap-vs-stack-pointer-variable FP
  class (6 instances):** `sig_der`/`buf` returned from `crypto_ec_key_
  sign`/`_sign_r_s`/`crypto_csr_sign` are `wpabuf_alloc()`-backed heap
  pointers; `pkey` returned from `crypto_rsa_key_read_public` is a
  heap `EVP_PKEY *` from `PEM_read_PUBKEY`/`X509_get_pubkey`. Local
  *variable*, not local *storage*.
- **Reinforces the "MSC13-C dead-NULL-init genuinely correct" class (6
  instances) vs. a "NULL-as-safe-cleanup-guard, so NOT actually dead"
  counter-shape in the *same* function** — worth flagging as its own
  sub-pattern: in `crypto_ec_key_set_priv`'s `>=3.0` branch, `ctx`/
  `ec_group`/`pub_bin`'s NULL inits ARE read (as safe no-op guards for
  `EVP_PKEY_CTX_free`/`EC_GROUP_free`/`os_free`) on the `priv_bin`-alloc-
  failure early-`goto fail` path, so MSC13-C is FP for those 3 — while
  `priv_bin` itself (unconditionally overwritten by `os_malloc()` right
  after declaration, no intervening branch) is a genuine dead init (TP).
  Distinguishing test: is there ANY goto/early-return path that reaches
  a cleanup label *before* the variable is first reassigned? If yes and
  the cleanup free is NULL-safe, the "dead" init is actually a live
  safe-cleanup guard (FP); if the very next statement unconditionally
  overwrites it with no such path, it's genuinely dead (TP).
- **EXP20-C "testing for equality with 1" — FP when the OpenSSL function
  is documented to return exactly 1 on success (0/negative on error),
  i.e. 1 is provably the *only* success value, not just the common
  one.** `EC_GROUP_get_curve(...) == 1` — no other positive return value
  is ever "success" per the OpenSSL API contract, so this isn't the
  fragile magic-number check EXP20-C warns about. `crypto_openssl.c:4042`.
- **MSC17-C `#ifdef`-intervening-case-label FP reconfirmed** (`crypto_ec_
  key_group`'s `switch(nid)`, `case NID_secp521r1: return 21;` immediately
  followed by a case label behind `#ifdef NID_brainpoolP256r1`) — exact
  match to the `16-40_b1` entry, now on a different file. `:4203`.
- **`if (!(x = alloc()) || use(x) || ...)` chain reconfirmed a 3rd file**
  (EXP30-C "unsequenced" + EXP45-C "assignment in if", both FP — `||`
  is a sequence point, and the assignment is already parenthesized per
  CERT's own compliant example) — same shape as the `driver_nl80211.c`
  nlmsg-build-chain entry (`41plus_b13`), now in
  `crypto_ec_key_get_pubkey_point:3839,3844`.
- **NEW, genuine FN (MEM31-C-shape leak):** `crypto_csr_verify()`
  (`crypto_openssl.c:4372`) leaks the `EVP_PKEY *pkey` obtained from
  `X509_REQ_get_pubkey()` on every call — neither the success return nor
  the `fail:` path calls `EVP_PKEY_free(pkey)`. CSR data is
  attacker-relayed protocol input (DPP enrollment), so this is an
  externally-triggerable leak sqc's MSC13-C dead-init check flagged the
  *initializer* of but not the real leak.

## Confirmed/reinforced patterns (from batch `41plus_b43`, 52 findings, `wpa_supplicant/config.c#part4of4`, lines ~5620-6159: global_fields macro table + wpa_config_dump_values/get_value/process_global + wpa_dev_ik identity accessors)

- **STR00-C "Plain 'char' variable 'ret' assigned value -1" reconfirmed wrong-type-claim, 7 instances two functions.** `ret` is declared `int ret = 0;` in both `wpa_config_process_global` (line 5952) and `wpa_config_set_identity` (line 6041) — never `char` anywhere in either function. Same rule-bug class as the `wifi_display.c subelem`/`dpp.h ssid` entries (`16-40_b19`/`41plus_b27`).
- **PRE01-C on `INT_RANGE(f, min, max)`/`STR_RANGE` judged TP, not FP — new refinement of the "graded on the macro definition" precedent.** Unlike `f` (used only via `#f`/`OFFSET(f)` token-composition, a confirmed FP shape), `min`/`max` are used bare as rvalue operands inside `(void *) min`/`(void *) max` casts — a real (if currently unexercised, since every call site passes integer literals) precedence hazard, matching the established "crypto round macro, bare rvalue operand = real TP" distinction from the SHA256 `RND`/`Sigma` entries (`16-40_b8` family) rather than the token-paste-only FP class.
- **DCL37-C on `_INT`/`_STR` judged TP, not FP — refines the existing DCL37-C scope split.** These are macro *names* (`_INT`, `_STR`), always file-scope, beginning with underscore+uppercase — "always reserved" per C 7.1.3 regardless of scope, unlike the confirmed underscore+lowercase-block-scope-local FP class (`p2p_invitation.c _pmkid`/`_pmk`, `ctrl_iface.c _bssid`).
- **API00-C internal-only-API FP class reconfirmed 7x** on `wpa_config_dump_values`/`wpa_config_get_value`/`wpa_config_set_identity`/`wpa_config_add_identity`/`wpa_config_remove_identity` — every caller passes `wpa_s->conf` or an internally-parsed buffer, never externally-nullable.
- **API00-C non-arithmetic-int-param overflow-flag FP reconfirmed** on `wpa_config_remove_identity`'s `id` (only ever compared with `==`, never arithmetic) and `wpa_config_dump_values`'s `buflen` (only decremented) — same category error as the `eap_sake_common.c:335 peer` precedent.
- **ERR07-C/ERR34-C atoi() judged TP** — `identity->dik_cipher = atoi(value);` assigned straight into a struct field with zero downstream validation, consistent with the established unchecked-vs-range-checked atoi() split.
- **MSC01-C "no final else" judged FP** on `wpa_config_set_identity`'s trailing `else if (line)` — deliberate guard clause (only logs/errors when called from config-file context; silent no-op otherwise is intentional), consistent with the established guard-clause FP default.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b42`, 150 findings, `wpa_supplicant/config.c` part3of4)

- **NEW, batch-local (4 instances): STR00-C "Plain 'char' variable assigned value -1" misidentifies a locally-declared `int res;` as a `char` variable.** `wpa_config_get_str`/`get_bgscan`/`get_freq_list`/`get_ipv4` all declare `int res;` then do `res = -1;` after an `os_snprintf_error()` check — the rule's premise (that `res` is `char`-typed) is simply false; looks like the same declaration-lookup gap as other type-misidentification rule bugs in this file. `config.c:5503,5528,5567,5591`.
- **DCL13-C "config not modified" correctly misses mutation via an offset-computed aliased pointer or a struct-field passed as an output buffer — reconfirms/extends the existing "aliased local pointer"/"direct struct-field write" DCL13-C miss classes, now 11 instances in one file.** The `wpa_global_config_parse_*`/`wpa_config_process_*` setter family computes `dst = (T*)((u8*)config + offset)` then does `*dst = val` (or passes `config->field` directly to a fill-in helper like `wps_dev_type_str2bin`/`hexstr2bin`/`hwaddr_aton2`), which is a real write through `config` even though `config` itself is never reassigned. FP for DCL13-C at all such setter sites (`:4890,4946,4986,5057,5120,5186,5202,5209,5354,5371,5601`); by contrast the paired *getter* family (`wpa_config_get_int/bool/str/bgscan/freq_list/ipv4`, `:5464,5476,5488,5509,5534,5574`) and pure list-traversal accessors (`wpa_config_get_cred/get_blob`, debug-dump, `:4259,4589,4665,4839`) are genuine (low-severity) TPs — and one function (`wpa_config_process_load_dynamic_eap`, `:5163`) doesn't touch `config` at all.
- **MEM12-C "returns without releasing all resources" ownership-transfer-on-return FP reconfirmed at its largest scale yet (30 instances in one file).** `wpa_config_get_cred_no_key`'s `req_conn_capab`/`domain`/`home_ois`/`required_home_ois`/`roaming_consortiums` branches all `buf = os_malloc(...)`, fill it via `os_snprintf`/`wpa_snprintf_hex` in a loop, and `return buf;` on both early-truncation and normal-completion paths — `buf` is the function's return value, not a leak. `config.c:4397-4585` (30 sites).
- **ERR02-C name-substring misfire on `wpa_snprintf_hex()` reconfirmed (3 more instances, extends the `ctrl_iface.c:7633` precedent).** `config.c:4464,4489,4514`.
- **EXP43-C "overlapping memory regions" misfires on `os_realloc_array(void *ptr, size_t nmemb, size_t size)` — NEW sub-shape of the existing non-restrict-param EXP43-C FP class.** The function has exactly one pointer parameter; there is no second pointer to overlap with at all — a category error, not just a missing-`restrict` one. 3 instances, `config.c:4022,4129,4151`.
- **INT32-C "signed integer addition may overflow" on `pos + 4000`/`end - pos` extends the existing `buf + N` pointer-arithmetic FP class to a heap (`os_malloc(4000)`) buffer instead of a fixed local array.** `config.c:4310,4399,4534,4563`.
- **ERR33-C/ERR00-C/ERR01-C strtol() FP-vs-TP split reconfirmed via the TIGHT-downstream-range-check distinction, now for `wpa_global_config_parse_bool` (`val<0||val>1` catches any overflow) vs `wpa_global_config_parse_int`'s check_range=false call path (no magnitude bound at all, only the endptr/trailing-char check)** — FP for the former (`:4955`), TP (low) for the latter (`:4898`); ERR30-C ("errno not reset") stays TP (low) in both, per the established precedent that the range check doesn't substitute for an ERANGE guard.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b44`, 150 findings, `src/crypto/tls_openssl.c#part1of4`, lines 1-2177: compat wrappers, Windows CryptoAPI RSA_METHOD glue, tls_init/tls_deinit, tls_connection_init/deinit, altSubjectName/domain-suffix matching)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL13-C extended to hostap's own public multi-backend `tls.h` interface functions — 9 instances, one file.** `tls_get_errors`, `tls_connection_deinit`, `tls_connection_established`, `tls_connection_peer_serial_num`, `tls_connection_shutdown` all take `void *tls_ctx`/`ssl_ctx` and/or `struct tls_connection *conn` per the fixed signatures declared in `src/crypto/tls.h` (shared verbatim across every TLS backend: openssl, gnutls, mbedtls, wolfssl, ...). Recommending `const`-qualification here would require touching the shared header and every backend implementation in lockstep — same root cause as the eloop/EAP-method-table/RSA_METHOD DCL13-C FP class, now extended from callback vtables to a cross-backend public API surface. `tls_openssl.c:1561,1939,1964(x2),1970,1971,1995(x2)`. Contrast with genuinely-unused-param TPs on *static/internal* functions in the same file (`tls_cryptoapi_ca_cert:810`, `check_server_key_exchange:1696` — real, if low-value, opportunities since these aren't part of any pinned external contract) and the `#ifdef FEATURE...#else` no-op-stub class (`tls_cryptoapi_cert:879`, already-documented TP).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: signature-pinned-type reasoning extended from DCL13-C (pointer constness) to INT13-C/INT14-C (integer signedness/shift suggestions) — 2 instances.** `ssl_info_cb`'s `ret` parameter is fixed by the `SSL_CTX_set_info_callback` external callback contract (`void (*)(const SSL *, int, int)`); "change to unsigned int" would break the pinned prototype. `tls_openssl.c:912` (both INT13-C and INT14-C on the same `(ret >> 8)`). Contrast with `w`, a fresh non-parameter local in the same function, correctly graded TP since retyping a plain local is harmless (`:894,896`).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: STR30-C "modify string literal" misfires on plain array-of-pointers element reassignment — 10 instances, one file.** `pre_cmd[1] = pkcs11_so_path;` / `post_cmd[0] = NULL;` (and siblings) merely repoint a `const char *pre_cmd[]` slot at a different string; nothing writes through any string literal's character storage. `tls_openssl.c:1046,1047,1049,1051,1078,1079` (2 findings each).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM30-C false UAF from within-function statement-ordering confusion (not the cross-branch/cross-function conflation already documented) — batch-local, 2 instances so far.** `cryptoapi_finish()`: `cryptoapi_free_data((...)rsa->meth->app_data)` (line 656) is flagged as "accessing freed pointer" even though the actual free of `rsa->meth` doesn't happen until the *next* line (657); line 657 itself (`os_free((void*)rsa->meth)`, i.e. the free statement) is flagged as "accessing freed pointer 'rsa->meth'" too — the tool appears to treat a free as retroactively applying to the line(s) immediately preceding it. Watch for recurrence; worth confirming as a 3rd instance elsewhere before promoting out of batch-local.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM31-C doesn't know that library free functions transitively free embedded/attached sub-objects — 2 shapes, ~15 instances.** (a) `RSA_free(rsa)` frees `rsa->n`/`rsa->e` (assigned via `BN_dup`) as part of freeing the RSA struct — flagged as leaked/leak-before-return regardless (`:786,787,795x2,806x2`). (b) `SSL_set_bio(conn->ssl, conn->ssl_in, conn->ssl_out)` transfers BIO ownership into the SSL object, so `SSL_free(conn->ssl)` (called later via `tls_connection_deinit`, or directly on nearby error paths) transitively frees `conn->ssl_in`/`conn->ssl_out` too — flagged as leaked at `tls_connection_init`'s multiple return points regardless of an explicit adjacent `BIO_free`/`SSL_free` already covering them (`:1882,1914,1920,1923,1930x2,1935x3`). Extends the existing RSA_free/BN_dup-class reasoning to a 2nd OpenSSL ownership-transfer API (`SSL_set_bio`).
- **Reconfirms the goto-label MSC07-C class, the sizeof(*ptr) EXP33-C class (4 instances: `:721,722,1235,1877`), the os_free(NULL)-safe EXP34-C class, the dl_list_for_each-heap-pointer DCL30-C class (`get_session_data:1097`), the DCL31-C system-header class (`SSL_SESSION_set_ex_data:1121`, `SSLv23_method:1237`), the OpenSSL exact-1/0-contract EXP20-C class (`SSL_clear()==1:2005`), the pos/end begin-end-pointer-pair EXP43-C class (`:1785,1787`), the pure-accessor-args EXP30-C class (`:906,1765,1988`), the NULL-literal-args EXP43-C class (`SSL_SESSION_get_ex_new_index(0,NULL,NULL,NULL,NULL):1299`), the no-pthread CON03-C/CON32-C/POS49-C/CON33-C/CON34-C class (getenv extended at `:1818,1909`; strerror at `:1826,1840`; bitfields at `:1774,1943`; statics at `:209,210,226,366,1180`), and the guard-clause MSC01-C no-final-else class (`:683,927`).**
- **NEW, batch-local: EXP30-C "modified and accessed without sequence point" misfires on a self-referential for-loop reassignment `i = f(..., i)` — distinct from the documented `||`/`&&`-sequence-point-blindness family (no boolean chain here).** `for (i = -1; (i = X509_NAME_get_index_by_NID(name, nid, i)) > -1;)` — the read of `i` as an argument necessarily completes before the call returns, which necessarily precedes the assignment's side effect; properly sequenced, safe idiom. `tls_openssl.c:2177`. Only 1 instance so far.
- **NEW, batch-local: API00-C factually wrong — claims a pointer parameter is unvalidated when the function body literally validates it inline.** `tls_connection_established`'s body is `return conn ? SSL_is_init_finished(conn->ssl) : 0;` — a ternary NULL-guard on `conn` — yet API00-C fires "does not validate pointer parameter 'conn'". Not a judgment-call FP, a factual error. `tls_openssl.c:1964`. Only 1 instance so far.
- **NEW, batch-local: STR34-C misattributes a `char`-widening-conversion finding to a plain pointer parameter, at a line containing no char conversion at all — 3 instances, extends the `config.c` (`41plus_b40`) STR34-C misattribution/line-drift entry to a 2nd file.** `keystore_get(key, strlen(key), &value)` flags `key` (a `const char *`) at both its uses on the same line (`:141`, 2 findings); `os_strlen(encoded_key_alias)` flags the pointer parameter itself (`:185`).
- **NEW, batch-local: MSC13-C "declared but never used" is factually wrong when the variable IS used, just only as a while-condition drain-loop test-and-assign, with an intentionally empty body.** `unsigned long err; while ((err = ERR_get_error())) { /* ignore */ }` — `err` is assigned and tested every iteration; the comment even explains the empty body is deliberate. `tls_openssl.c:306`. Only 1 instance so far.
- FIO02-C/POS01-C on `tls_keylog_cb`'s `open(getenv("SSLKEYLOGFILE"), ...)` graded TP (low): a real canonicalization/symlink gap by rule text, though the env var is attacker-controlled only in the sense of "whoever controls this process's environment," and the whole feature is `CONFIG_TESTING_OPTIONS`-gated (debug/testing builds only, matches curl's well-known `SSLKEYLOGFILE` debug convention) — low real-world severity but not dismissed as purely stylistic. `tls_openssl.c:1822`.

(b) `tls_cryptoapi_cert`'s `rsa->n = BN_dup(...); rsa->e = BN_dup(...);` (`:786,787`) don't NULL-check either `BN_dup` return — real but low real-world relevance (CONFIG_NATIVE_WINDOWS-only path).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b45`, 150 findings, `src/crypto/tls_openssl.c#part2of4`, lines 2179-4114: DN/altSubjectName/domain-suffix matching, tls_verify_cb, CA-cert/CA-store loading, Suite B config, client-cert/PKCS12 loading, engine/provider cert loading)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (~24 instances, largest single-batch cluster): MEM31-C "store not freed"/"leak before return" doesn't know `SSL_CTX_set_cert_store(ssl_ctx, store)` transfers ownership of a freshly-`X509_STORE_new()`'d store into `ssl_ctx`.** `tls_connection_ca_cert`, `tls_connection_engine_ca_cert` both do `store = X509_STORE_new(); ...; SSL_CTX_set_cert_store(ssl_ctx, store);` immediately, then sqc flags every subsequent `return` in the function as leaking `store` — but `store` is now owned by `ssl_ctx` and freed when `ssl_ctx`/`SSL_CTX_free()` happens. Extends the existing `SSL_set_bio`/`RSA_free` transitive-ownership-transfer MEM31-C FP family (`41plus_b44`) to a 2nd OpenSSL ownership-transfer setter. `tls_openssl.c:3008,3024,3033,3039,3044,3049,3053,3069,3076,3094,3104,3113,3121,3131,3160,3169,3185,3194,3202,4084,4104,4114`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP34-C "passing null pointer" fires on a pointer that is guarded non-NULL by the exact same `&&`/`while` condition at the call site — 6 instances.** `if (ca_cert && os_strncmp(ca_cert, ...))` (`:3027,3126,3135`) and `while ((cert = PEM_read_bio_X509(...)))  { ... tls_add_ca_cert(ssl_ctx, cert) ...}` (`:3091`) both make the flagged pointer provably non-NULL inside the branch/loop body the rule fired in.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM31-C/MEM30-C "double free" mutually-exclusive-branch FP family gets 2 new sub-shapes, same root cause as the established family.** (a) `tls_parse_pkcs12`'s cert-chain loops: `X509_free(cert); break;` inside the failure branch exits the loop before the loop-bottom's own `X509_free(cert)` can run — not a double free (`:3881,3884,3927`). (b) `tls_connection_engine_ca_cert`'s `if (!X509_STORE_add_cert(...)) { ... if (already-in-hash) {/* fall through, no free */} else { X509_free(cert); return -1; } } X509_free(cert);` — the two `X509_free(cert)` calls are on mutually exclusive paths (one returns before reaching the other) (`:4107`).
- **NEW pattern (batch-local, 1 instance so far): MEM31-C misidentifies a `X509_free` *function-pointer callback argument* passed to `sk_X509_pop_free(certs, X509_free)` as itself a variable being double-freed** (`"Double free detected: 'X509_free' was already freed"`, `:3932`), alongside a legitimate-looking but still-FP claim that `certs` itself double-frees (the stack's elements were already individually popped+freed by `sk_X509_pop()` in the preceding `while` loop, so `sk_X509_pop_free()` only frees the now-empty container — not a double free). Worth watching for recurrence before promoting out of batch-local.
- **NEW pattern (batch-local, 4 instances): MEM31-C "memory leak: 'bio' not freed" fires at return statements in a *different* function than the one that allocated `bio`, with no `bio` variable in scope at the flagged line at all** — `tls_global_client_cert`'s 4 `return` statements (`:3755,3764,3772,3782`, none of which declare or touch `bio`) get tagged with a leak message that only makes sense for `tls_connection_client_cert`'s local `bio` (declared/freed entirely within lines 3690-3713, always freed on every path). Looks like a preprocessor-nested-`#if defined(...)/#else/#endif` block confusing the leak-tracking CFG into carrying state across into the next function; extends the "preprocessor-branch-blind" family to cross-function state bleed rather than just same-function branch blindness.

Contrast: the paired `fclose(f)` 5 lines later (`:3958`) genuinely never checks its return value — graded TP (low) for both ERR00-C/ERR33-C, unlike the fopen findings at the same line number cluster.
- **Reconfirms established classes at scale in this file: API05-C companion-pointer+size idiom (`:2326,2998,2999,3611,3661,3977`), OpenSSL exact-1/0-contract EXP20-C (`:2349,2382,2975,3680,3730,3751,3760,3767`), DCL31-C system-header class (`i2d_X509:2459,2468`; `X509_get_notBefore/notAfter:2705,2711`; `d2i_X509:3063`; `X509_free:3068,3075,3092,3096`; `PEM_read_bio_X509:3082`), DCL31-C `STACK_OF(X509)` macro-type class (`:2790`), DCL30-C local-pointer-vs-heap-storage confusion (`get_x509_cert` returning a `wpabuf_alloc()`'d buffer, `:2469`), STR31-C misapplied-to-non-char-array (`const u8 *addr[1]`/`size_t len[1]`/`int nid[1]`/`uint16_t sigalgs[1]`, `:2558,2559,2758,2759,3461,3539,3540`), EXP39-C cross-function `union tls_event_data`/`ev` conflation (no `alert` member write in either flagged function, `:2487,2554`), EXP30-C pure-accessor-args class (`ASN1_STRING_get0_data/length:2573`; `X509_LOOKUP_file():2945`), no-pthread CON03-C/CON07-C/CON32-C/POS49-C class (`:3017,3022,3023,3046,3199,3611,3615,3622,3626,3631,4112`), MSC01-C no-final-else guard-clause class (`:2520,2694,2711,2767,2854,2915,3395,3455,3651,3685,3904`), MSC37-C preprocessor-branch-blind reach-end class (`:2397,3786,3946,3976,4034,4065`), MEM10-C stylistic ad-hoc-NULL-check class (`:3618,3718,3792,3806`), EXP05-C read-only cast-away-const class (`(u8*)client_cert_blob` into `SSL_use_certificate_ASN1`, read-only, `:3680`), and DCL13-C static/internal-function real-if-low-value opportunities (`openssl_tls_fail_event:2473`, `openssl_tls_cert_event:2529`, `tls_load_ca_der:2939`, `tls_connection_client_cert:3660`, `tls_global_client_cert:3786`, `tls_engine_get_cert:4000`, `tls_connection_engine_ca_cert:4065`).**
