## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b49`, 150 findings, `wpa_supplicant/wpa_cli.c#part2of4`, lines ~1600-4345: command-handler bodies, completion callbacks, wpa_ctrl_command_sta/bss helpers, and the file's edit.h-callback glue)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP33-C "static variable used without explicit initialization" on a file-scope `static struct wpa_ctrl *ctrl_conn;` — categorical FP.** C guarantees zero/NULL-initialization for objects with static storage duration that have no explicit initializer (C99 6.7.8p10); reading `ctrl_conn` before its first `wpa_ctrl_open()` assignment is not an uninitialized-memory read at all, just a well-defined NULL check. 3 instances, one file (`wpa_cli.c:1955,2483,3194`). Worth checking for recurrence on any other bare `static T *x;` file-scope pointer across the codebase.
- **DCL30-C "assigned to global/static variable" factually wrong — flags a plain local function PARAMETER as global/static.** `wpa_ctrl_command_sta(..., const char *cmd, ...)`'s `cmd = buf;` reassigns the function's own parameter (never a global/static), and the reassigned pointer never escapes the function (used only in the same-function `wpa_ctrl_request(...)` call right after) — no dangling-pointer risk exists. `wpa_cli.c:1963`. Distinct from, but same rule-engine-misclassification family as, the existing heap-vs-stack DCL30-C FPs.
- **FIO47-C "type mismatch ... argument is Integer" on a `%s`/printf pointer argument that IS a `char*`/`const char*` — NEW sub-shape of the existing FIO47-C argument-binding-misparse family (previously documented for sscanf only).** `printf("...%s...", cmd)` / `printf("...%s...", addr)` where `cmd`/`addr` are unambiguously pointer-typed params — the engine's Integer-vs-Pointer classification is simply wrong here, not a binding-index issue. 8 instances (`wpa_cli.c:1969,1972,2015,2489,2492,2506,3200,3203`).
- **FIO47-C/DCL11-C/INT00-C 3-rule bundle misfires on `%c` paired with a genuinely-`char` loop variable assigned from `struct_field->char_ptr[n]`.** `print_cmd_help`'s `char c; for (n=0; (c = cmd->usage[n]); n++) printf("%c", c);` — `c` is plain `char`, correctly matching `%c` after default promotion; engine appears to conflate the *indexed element type* with the *indexing pointer field's own type* (`cmd->usage` is `const char *`), misreporting `c` as Pointer/char*. `wpa_cli.c:4231` (3 findings, one line).
- **ARR30-C "unsafe variable-index access" on `buf[len]='\0'` where `len` is an in/out `size_t` bounded by the `wpa_ctrl_request()` API's own size contract — NEW shape of the existing "rule doesn't see a cross-call/API guard" family.** `len` starts at `sizeof(buf)-1` and is only ever shrunk (never grown) by `wpa_ctrl_request`, which writes at most the caller-supplied `len` bytes into `buf` — `len` can never exceed `sizeof(buf)-1`. 3 instances (`wpa_cli.c:1976,2496,3207`).
- **ARR00-C "use after free" flagged across mutually-exclusive early-return branches — reconfirms the existing class, largest instance yet (7 findings on consecutive lines).** `wpa_cli_complete_p2p_find`: `os_free(res); return NULL;` fires only inside the `if (res[0] == NULL)` branch; every subsequent `res[1..4] = ...` access is on the normal, non-freed continuation path. `wpa_cli.c:2199,2200,2202,2203,2205,2206,2209`.
- **INT32-C "signed integer addition may overflow" on `char *pos + <small literal>` — reconfirms/extends the existing pointer-arithmetic-misclassified family to a 6-site burst in one function.** `id/bssid/freq/level/flags/ssid = pos + N` in `wpa_ctrl_command_bss` — ordinary bounded pointer arithmetic on a 512-byte stack buffer, not signed-int addition. `wpa_cli.c:3214,3216,3218,3220,3222,3224`.
- **ERR07-C/ERR34-C atoi() judged TP (not FP) — extends the "0-is-a-valid-value" distinction.** `id = atoi(pos + 3)` (parsing a BSS `id=` field) has no downstream validation beyond `id != -1`; a malformed/non-numeric value silently collapses to `atoi()==0`, indistinguishable from a legitimately-reported id of 0. `wpa_cli.c:3214`.
- Reconfirms in this batch: DCL13-C on `argv`/dispatch-table-handler params (44 instances, `wpa_cli_commands[]`'s fixed `int(*)(struct wpa_ctrl*,int,char*argv[])` signature) and on `ctx` params matching `edit.h`'s pinned `completion_cb`/`filter_cb` typedefs (`:4250,4331`); STR34-C on pointer params/locals (`str`/`cmd`/`fields`/`iftypes`) and on plain char-to-char `*pos = '\0'`/`*pos++ = '\0'` assignments (18 instances); PRE32-C on plain concatenated-string-literal printf calls with zero preprocessor tokens (28 instances); ARR02-C implicit-bounds on `ARRAY_SIZE()`-consumed local arrays (`cred_fields`/`fields`/`iftypes`/`wpa_cli_commands`, 5 instances); API05-C pointer+size-param idiom (`addr`/`addr_len`, 4 instances); MEM12-C ownership-transfer-on-return for completion-callback `res` arrays (6 instances, incl. a 4306 case combined with a heap-vs-stack DCL30-C FP on the same `res`); MSC01-C no-final-else guard-clause pedantry (3 instances); EXP45-C already-parenthesized `for (...; (c = expr); ...)` idiom (2 instances); ARR30-C/STR31-C unbounded-loop misfire on a NUL-terminated-scan already bounded by an earlier `buf[len]='\0'` (`:3212`); DCL11-C false-NULL claim despite an explicit same-function non-NULL guard 2 lines earlier (`:1857,1860`); MSC13-C dead-NULL-init-then-reassign graded TP (`:2188`, matches the established "genuine harmless dead assignment" precedent).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b48`, 150 findings, `wpa_supplicant/wpa_cli.c#part1of4`, lines 1-1600: globals, connection open/close, generic command dispatch helpers, WPS/network command handlers)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM12-C "returns without releasing all resources" misapplied to module-static connection-pointer globals (`ctrl_conn`, `mon_conn`) — new variant of the ownership-transfer FP class, 8 instances one function.** `wpa_cli_open_connection`'s early-return branches (lines 141,147,155,162,167,174) never actually leak: `ctrl_conn`/`mon_conn` are file-scope statics, not per-call local resources, and at each flagged return either nothing was allocated yet, the just-freed `cfile` was already released, or `ctrl_conn` is provably NULL (open failed). The mon_conn-attach-failure path (`:195`) already calls `wpa_cli_close_connection()`, which frees both. The success path (`:199`) intentionally leaves both set for later use/cleanup by `wpa_cli_close_connection()` — ownership lives at module scope, not the function's local frame. Same root confusion as the confirmed return-value ownership-transfer MEM12 class, just via a static global instead of a return value.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP33-C "static variable used without explicit initialization" — static/file-scope pointers are implicitly zero-initialized per C 6.7.9p10; checking them against NULL is safe by the language guarantee, not an uninitialized-use.** `ctrl_conn`/`mon_conn` at `wpa_cli.c:205,214,234`. A 4th instance at `:392` is a separate misattribution: sqc mistook a call to the forward-declared static *function* `wpa_list_cmd_list()` for a read of a same-named static *variable* — no such variable exists.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MSC13-C "dead assignment" reconfirms the static/global cross-call-significance FP class (`linux_ioctl.c:130` precedent) for plain int flags, not just errno.** `wpa_cli_attached = 0/1` and `ctrl_conn`/`mon_conn = NULL` (`:210,213,217`) are module statics read by *other* functions invoked later (`wpa_cli_close_connection`, `_wpa_ctrl_command`, etc.) — never dead, just outside the assigning function's own body.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP class extends to (a) hostap's own CLI command table `struct wpa_cli_cmd` (`wpa_cli.c:3438-3444`, `handler` field typed `int (*)(struct wpa_ctrl *ctrl, int argc, char *argv[])`, non-const) and (b) `wpa_ctrl_request`'s `msg_cb` callback parameter (`void (*)(char *msg, size_t len)`).** Every `wpa_cli_cmd_*`/`wpa_cli_complete_*` handler registered in `wpa_cli_commands[]` cannot have its `ctrl`/`argv` params const-qualified without breaking the vtable match (~35 instances this batch: lines 222,286,292,308,314,326,332,339,378,400,407,416,422,549,556,563,649,655,662,668,708,759,788,836,908,968,1047,1080,1114,1147,1179,1212,1245,1278,1365,1594,1600). Same root cause as the eloop/EAP-method/driver-ops dispatch families documented earlier, just a 3rd/4th kind of fixed-signature table.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: STR34-C "converted to larger integer type without cast to unsigned char" misattributed to pointer/array identifiers passed as ordinary function-call arguments — no scalar char widening conversion exists at the cited line at all, 9 instances.** Two shapes: (a) `int arg = get_cmd_arg_num(str, pos);` — `str` is a `const char *` parameter merely forwarded into a helper call (`:387,455,577,1519,1543,1570`); (b) `int i, num_fields = ARRAY_SIZE(fields);` where `fields`/`network_fields` is `const char *arr[]` (array of pointers, not chars) (`:529,631`); (c) `wpa_cli_cmd(ctrl, "REMOVE_NETWORK", 1, argc, argv)` — `argv` is `char *argv[]` forwarded as-is (`:1377`). Rule appears to fire on any char-pointer-ish identifier appearing in a call-argument position, independent of whether an actual scalar char-to-int conversion occurs.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: ARR02-C "array declaration has implicit bounds" on locally-declared arrays whose size is exactly the initializer's brace-list count, consumed only via `ARRAY_SIZE()` — extends the existing file-scope (`wpa_drivers[]`) ARR02-C FP entry to local completion-helper arrays.** `const char *fields[] = {...}` (`wpa_cli.c:456,578`) and `static const char *network_fields[] = {...}` (`:1441`); all three are always read through `ARRAY_SIZE(fields)`, never hardcoded — there is no real bound to "specify" that isn't already implied and correctly used.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: ENV01-C/MEM05-C wholesale misfire reconfirmed on fixed-size local buffers sized by macro/literal arithmetic (`char ssid_hex[2*SSID_MAX_LEN+1]`, `char key_hex[2*64+1]`) with zero getenv/VLA anywhere in the function — 3rd+ confirmed instance of the `sae_pk_gen.c`-class engine bug.** `wpa_cli_cmd_wps_reg:845,846`, `wpa_cli_cmd_wps_er_config:974,975`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP33-C "variable may be/is used uninitialized" misfires on `end = buf + sizeof(buf)` / `pos = buf` — array-to-pointer decay for boundary/address computation is not a read of the buffer's contents, and the buffer is subsequently written via `os_snprintf(pos, ...)` before any real use — 8 instances, one shape repeated across near-identical command handlers.** `wpa_cli_cmd_identity/_password/_new_password/_pin/_otp/_sim/_psk_passphrase/_passphrase`, `wpa_cli.c:1058,1091,1125,1158,1190,1223,1255,1289`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: FIO47-C "format specifier expects Pointer/Integer but argument is X" argument-type misidentification extends from sscanf (previously documented) to plain printf.** `printf("Invalid %s command...", cmd, min_args, ...)` in `wpa_cli_cmd` flags `cmd` — declared `const char *cmd`, a genuine pointer matching its `%s` — as "Integer". `wpa_cli.c:248,251,275`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: ARR30-C "unsafe array access with variable index" on `buf[len]='\0'` where `len` is the *out* parameter of `wpa_ctrl_request(ctrl, cmd, cmdlen, buf, &len, cb)`, bounded by the *in* value of `len` (`sizeof(buf)-1`) per the function's recv-style size-in/size-out contract.** Same "rule doesn't see a well-known control function's own bounding contract" family as the confirmed INT33/INT30/ARR30 protocol-bound entries, now for the ctrl_iface request/reply idiom itself (used pervasively across all `wpa_cli_cmd_*`/`ctrl_iface.c` functions). `wpa_cli.c:255`. The paired `EXP33-C` at `:256` ("buf may be used uninitialized") is the output-param-write-blindness class (same shape as `wps_parse_msg`/`nla_parse`): `buf` is written by `wpa_ctrl_request` through the pointer parameter just before this read.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL30-C "local variable assigned to global/static variable — creates dangling pointer" is factually wrong on a local-parameter-to-local-buffer reassignment.** `cmd = buf;` in `_wpa_ctrl_command` reassigns the *local parameter* `cmd` (not a global/static) to point at the *local* `buf`; both live in the same stack frame and `cmd` is only read later in the same function call before returning — no dangling pointer, no global/static involved at all. `wpa_cli.c:242`.
- **MSC01-C "if/else-if chain has no final else" reconfirmed on the guard-clause fallthrough shape** (`ret==-2`/`ret<0` branches both `return`; the fallthrough "success" case needs no explicit else). `wpa_cli.c:250`.
- **Reconfirms the no-pthread CON03-C/CON02-C class** for wpa_cli.c's module globals (`wpa_cli_quit`, `wpa_cli_attached`, `wpa_cli_connected`, `wpa_cli_last_id`, `ctrl_ifname`, `reconnect`, `ping_interval`, `interactive`, `ifname_prefix`) — confirmed no pthread usage in the file; `wpa_cli_quit` is only ever set from eloop's *deferred* signal dispatch (`eloop_handle_signal` only increments counters in real async-signal context; the actual `wpa_cli_terminate`/quit-setting callback runs later from the normal eloop main-loop, not inside a signal handler), so there is no real cross-context race either. `wpa_cli.c:42-58`.
- **API05-C "pointer parameter should use conformant array syntax" reconfirmed** on the `wpa_ctrl_request` `msg_cb(char *msg, size_t len)` callback pair — idiomatic pointer+length convention. `wpa_cli.c:222`.

No new FN findings in the reviewed portion (lines 1-~1600 of this ~4600-line file, i.e. this batch's part1of4 scope only — not the full file).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b50`, 150 findings, `wpa_supplicant/wpa_cli.c#part3of4`, lines ~4270-5270: command dispatch (`wpa_request`), action-file event processing (`wpa_cli_action_process`/`wpa_cli_exec`), interactive-editor callbacks, connection management, `main()`)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (12 instances): ARR37-C "subscript on non-array pointer" misfires on `argv[N]` where the parameter is declared `char *argv[]`** — a genuine array parameter (just decayed in the ABI), not a "non-array pointer". `wpa_request(struct wpa_ctrl *ctrl, int argc, char *argv[])`, lines 4366,4367,4368,4379(x2),4382,4393,4396,4397,4405,4408. Worth checking any other `int argc, char *argv[]`-shaped handler in hostap.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (37 instances): EXP34-C "passing null pointer" on `action_file`/`global` — interprocedural caller-guard blindness, a new sub-shape of the established "rule doesn't see an earlier guard" family (previously same-function-only).** `wpa_cli_action_process()`'s ~35 `wpa_cli_exec(action_file, ...)` calls (lines 4504-4576) are only reachable via `wpa_cli_action()`, itself only invoked from `main()` behind `if (action_file)` (lines ~5265,5305) — action_file is provably non-NULL by the caller, not just by a check inside the flagged function. Same shape for `global` at `wpa_cli_open_global_ctrl()` (`:4603` DCL11-C+EXP34-C), gated by `global &&` at both its call sites (`:4631,5257`).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (9 instances): EXP33-C "static variable used without explicit initialization" fires on `ctrl_conn`/`mon_conn`, ignoring C's static-storage-duration zero-initialization guarantee.** Both are `static struct wpa_ctrl *ctrl_conn;`/`mon_conn;` (no initializer, `:40,41`) — per C 6.7.9p10 these are implicitly initialized to NULL; every flagged read is a `if (ctrl_conn)`/`if (ctrl_conn == NULL)`-style boolean/NULL test, which is well-defined. Lines 4725,4741,4783,4804,4814,4834,5011,5267.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances): EXP33-C "static variable used without explicit initialization" fires on a bare *function call*, mistaking the callee name for an uninitialized static variable.** `wpa_list_cmd_list()` (`:4347`) and `wpa_cli_get_default_ifname()` (`:5015,5263`) are both functions (declared `:74,75`); factual error, not a heuristic judgment call.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (7 instances): PRE32-C "function called with preprocessor directives in arguments" is a phantom finding — no `#if`/`#else`/`#endif` exists anywhere in or near the flagged call, and in several instances the rule literally quotes the plain string-literal argument itself as "the directive".** Extends the existing `l2_packet_freebsd.c` "no actual #-directive appears anywhere in the call" PRE32-C class from spurious-trigger-only to this quote-the-literal-as-directive sub-shape. `wpa_cli.c:4601,4727(x2),4770(x2),4791(x2),5019(x2)`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances): MSC13-C "dead assignment" misfires on an assignment to a file-scope `static` variable, not accounting for the fact that statics persist across function invocations and are read at the top of the SAME function on its next call.** `wpa_cli_connected`/`wpa_cli_last_id` (`:4502,4503,4508`, consumed by the `wpa_cli_connected <= 0 || new_id != wpa_cli_last_id` check at the top of the very next invocation) and `warning_displayed` (`:5022`, consumed by `if (!warning_displayed)` on `try_connection`'s next timer-driven call) are genuinely read later, just not within the current call — distinct root cause from the previously-documented "correctly-caught genuine dead-NULL-init" MSC13-C class (which was about locals never read on any path, this batch's `ret=0` at `:4364` is a normal instance of that correct-TP class).
- **MEM05-C/ARR32-C VLA-on-macro-constant-size family extends to `char *argv[max_args]`** — `max_args` is `#define max_args 10` (`src/common/cli.h:44`), a compile-time constant, not a runtime size at all. `wpa_cli.c:4810` (both rules).
- **STR30-C const-param rule-logic-bug class extends to `os_setenv`/`os_unsetenv`** (`src/utils/os_unix.c:402,408`, both take `const char *name`) — cannot modify a passed string literal by signature. 6 instances (`:4472,4473,4474,4486,4495,4499`).
- **ARR30-C sentinel-scan FP family extends to a `while (cmd->cmd)` walk over a static NULL-terminated `struct wpa_cli_cmd` table** (`wpa_cli_commands[]`, terminated by a `{NULL,...}` sentinel row) — a bounded compile-time table scan, not an unbounded pointer walk. `:4378,4395`.
- **ARR30-C recv/request-length-cap FP family extends to `wpa_ctrl_recv`/`wpa_ctrl_request`'s in/out `size_t *len`**, initialized to `sizeof(buf)-1`/`sizeof(buf)` before the call — the callee never writes past the caller-supplied cap, so `buf[len]='\0'` afterward is always in-bounds. 6 instances (`:4749,4874,4908,4940,4972,5181`).
- **API00-C/STR31-C "argc/argv not validated" — CONFIRMED categorical FP when applied to `main()` itself.** `main(int argc, char *argv[])`'s parameters are guaranteed valid by the C standard (5.1.2.2.1: `argv[0..argc-1]` non-null, `argv[argc]==NULL`) — they are supplied by the OS/runtime, not attacker-controlled or user-computed; "add a NULL/overflow check" is defensive pedantry against a language-level invariant, not a real gap. `wpa_cli.c:5195` (3 findings: 2x API00-C + STR31-C).
- **EXP34-C "callee guarantees non-null via its own while-condition" — new shape of the established callee-guarantees-non-null family.** `while ((dent = readdir(dir))) { ...dent->d_type... }` — the loop condition itself is the NULL-guard for every `dent->` access in the body. `:5152`.
- **ENV34-C judged FP when the `getenv()` result is consumed immediately in the same scope with zero intervening env-mutating calls** (`home = getenv("HOME"); ...; if (home) { ...os_strlen(home)...os_snprintf(...,home,...); }`, `:4840`) — no actual invalidation window exists despite the missing `strdup`; a narrower carve-out than a blanket "always copy getenv results" rule.
- **ENV30-C "passing getenv result to a function which may modify it" misfires on `os_strlen()`**, a pure read-only length function that cannot modify its argument by any stretch. `:4844`.
- **ERR33-C "getenv return not checked" is factually wrong when the very next line is `if (home) {`.** `:4840`.
- **MEM12-C ownership-persists-elsewhere FP family extends to file-scope `static` connection handles** (`ctrl_conn`/`mon_conn`) that are intentionally kept alive for the process's lifetime and closed later by `wpa_cli_close_connection()` — not leaked at the allocating function's own return. `:4604,4624`.

### New FN this batch (not previously flagged)

- `main()`'s two early `return -1;` paths (`:5289` non-global ctrl_ifname connect failure, `:5300` wpa_ctrl_attach failure) both skip the function's normal tail cleanup (`os_free(ctrl_ifname); eloop_destroy(); wpa_cli_cleanup();`) — low real-world impact (process exits immediately after) but the same goto-chain-cleanup gap class MEM12-C targets elsewhere in this file. Closest rule: MEM12-C. `upstream_present: unknown` (no separate upstream tracking checkout available in this environment).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b46`, 150 findings, `src/crypto/tls_openssl.c#part3of4`, lines ~4030-5530: engine/provider private-key loading, DH/DSA param setup, TLS handshake/encrypt/decrypt wrappers, tls.h getter family, OCSP callbacks, TPM2 PEM-tag file scan)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL13-C tls.h-pinned-public-API FP class (from `41plus_b44`) extends to 20+ more `tls_connection_*`/`tls_get_*` functions in this file** (`tls_connection_get_random`, `_export_key`, `_get_eap_fast_key`, `_handshake`, `_server_handshake`, `_encrypt`, `_decrypt`, `_resumed`, `_set_cipher_list`, `_enable_workaround`, `_client_hello_ext`, `_get_failed`, `_get_read_alerts`, `_get_write_alerts`, `tls_get_version`, `tls_get_cipher`) — all non-static, all declared verbatim in `tls.h` with `void *tls_ctx`/`ssl_ctx` and/or `struct tls_connection *conn` (confirmed via grep against `tls.h`), including cases where the header's own declaration is already non-const (`u8 *ciphers`). **Contrast, reconfirmed:** static/internal helpers in the same file with the identical unused-param shape (`tls_connection_engine_private_key:4121`, `tls_use_private_key_file:4148` `data`, `tls_connection_private_key:4195` `conn`, `tls_global_dh:4395` `data`, `openssl_get_appl_data:4866` `conn`) are graded TP (low) since they aren't part of any pinned cross-backend contract — always check `grep <fn_name> tls.h` before crediting/dismissing DCL13-C in this file.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL13-C callback-contract FP class extends from eloop/EAP-table/D-Bus vtables to OpenSSL's own fixed callback prototypes.** `ocsp_resp_cb`/`ocsp_status_cb`'s `void *arg` matches `SSL_CTX_set_tlsext_status_cb`'s pinned `int (*)(SSL *, void *)` signature; const-qualifying would break the registration cast. `tls_openssl.c:5282,5461`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM30-C/MEM31-C "double free"/"use-after-free" misfires on a variable that is freed, then reassigned via a fresh allocation before the 2nd "free" — extends the `mem30-reassign-and-fresh-binding` class, 3 instances one file.** `bio = BIO_new_file(...); ...; BIO_free(bio); ...; bio = BIO_new_file(...); ...; BIO_free(bio);` (`tls_connection_private_key:4173`, `tls_global_dh:4496,4507`) — each `BIO_free` targets a *different* live allocation, not a repeat free of the same one.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM31-C/MEM30-C "double free"/"UAF" misfires on `if (cond) { ...; free(x); break; } free(x);`-shaped mutually-exclusive if/break branches — 2 instances, extends the branch-blind family to a break-guarded if.** `tls_connection_private_key`'s `pkey`/`bio` frees at `:4263-4264` (success branch, breaks) vs. `:4267,4269` (fallthrough only reached when the success branch did NOT run) never both execute. Also seen as return-after-free in `tls_connection_decrypt`'s SSL_read-error branch (`wpabuf_free(buf); return NULL;` at `:5058`) vs. the normal-path `wpabuf_put(buf,res)`/`return buf` at `:5062,5066,5070` — the freeing branch always returns immediately, so the "later" line is provably unreached from it.
- **NEW: MEM30-C false UAF/double-free from within-function statement-ordering confusion, 2nd+3rd confirmed instance of the `cryptoapi_finish` pattern (`41plus_b44` batch-local note).** `tls_global_dh:4467,4471` — `pkey` has exactly one free (`EVP_PKEY_free(pkey)` at `:4471`, inside the `SSL_CTX_set0_tmp_dh_pkey` failure branch); sqc flags the *earlier* line `:4467` (the call itself, before any free) as "passing freed pointer" and `:4471` (the free statement itself) as "freed multiple times" — the tool appears to treat a free as retroactively applying to the line(s) immediately preceding/at it. Promotable: now 3 total instances across 2 files (this + `41plus_b44`'s `cryptoapi_finish`).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP20-C "implicit boolean test may be unclear" extends the OpenSSL-documented-1/0-contract FP class (previously only the `==1` message shape) to the implicit-test message shape.** `SSL_check_private_key`/`SSL_CTX_check_private_key`/`OCSP_check_validity` are all documented to return exactly 1 (success)/0 (failure); `if (!f())` is the textually-correct, unambiguous idiom given that contract, not a real clarity gap. `tls_openssl.c:4128,4316,4346,5434`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM31-C false double-free when a pointer is set to NULL on a failure branch (`sk_X509_free(certs); certs = NULL;`) before an unconditional cleanup call (`sk_X509_pop_free(certs, X509_free)`) that safely no-ops on NULL — extends the reassign-to-NULL-then-safe-free FP family to `sk_X509_pop_free`.** `tls_openssl.c:5371`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM12-C "leaked" report factually wrong immediately after the exact free of the named variable, and/or naming variables that were never successfully allocated (alloc-failed branch) or don't exist in the reached preprocessor branch — extends the `l2_packet_freebsd.c`/base64.c "already freed earlier" MEM12-C FP class with 2 new sub-shapes.** (a) alloc-failed: `tls_connection_get_eap_fast_key:4701` frees `tmp_out` inline and returns -1 because `rnd`'s own allocation failed (`rnd` never existed to leak). (b) preprocessor-branch-blind: `:4732`'s `return -1;` is under `#else /* !OPENSSL_NEED_EAP_FAST_PRF */`, where `tmp_out`/`rnd` are never even declared. (c) already-freed-earlier (classic shape): `:4728` (both freed via `bin_clear_free`/`os_free` moments earlier) and `match_lines_in_file:5527` (`buf` freed inline, `f` never opened since `fopen` failed).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: ARR01-C "sizeof applied to pointer/array parameter which decayed" — both established sub-shapes recur.** `sizeof(*keys)` (`tls_connection_get_random:4557`, correct pointee-dereference idiom) and `sizeof(conn->client_random)`/`sizeof(conn->server_random)` (`:4560,4563`, real fixed-size struct-member arrays, not decayed).
- **NEW: CON43-C "double-fetch vulnerability" extends the single-threaded-eloop FP family (previously CON32-C/POS49-C/CON33-C/CON34-C) to a `switch` on a dereferenced local scan pointer.** `tls_connection_set_cipher_list`'s `switch (*c)` scans a caller-owned, non-shared array in a codebase with zero pthread usage — no concurrent modifier exists. `:5098`.
- **NEW: ARR30-C "unbounded while loop with pointer increment" extends the sentinel-terminated-scan FP family to a `TLS_CIPHER_NONE`-terminated cipher-ID array**, per `tls.h`'s own doc comment ("Zero (TLS_CIPHER_NONE) terminated list"). `:5095`.
- **NEW: STR34-C "converted without cast to unsigned char, may cause sign extension" misidentifies a whole pointer argument (`os_strlen(*p)`, `*p` being `const char *`) as a scalar-char widening — extends the `ctrl_iface.c:2794,2827` "analyzer matches on identifier/short-type-spelling without checking pointer-ness" STR34-C bug to a dereferenced double-pointer.** `max_str_len:5502` (2 findings, same site).
- **NEW: DCL37-C "file-scope identifier should not start with underscore" reconfirmed on a block-scope local (`_out`)** — same `p2p_invitation.c`/`ctrl_iface.c` block-scope-misapplied family. `:4667`.
- **MSC37-C preprocessor-branch-blind reconfirmed 4x, new file** (`tls_use_private_key_file:4148`, `tls_global_dh:4395`, `openssl_get_keyblock_size:4570`, `tls_connection_get_eap_fast_key:4657`), all `#ifndef/#else` or nested `#if` shapes where every branch returns.
- **MSC13-C `||`-chain-blindness reconfirmed** (`res` assigned-and-compared inline in each `||` operand of `(res = BIO_reset(...)) < 0 || (res = BIO_reset(...)) < 0`, `tls_connection_encrypt:4988,4989`) alongside the already-common genuine-dead-init shape (`ctx`/`skip`/`tmp_out`/`_out` pre-set then unconditionally overwritten before any read, `:4407,4665,4666,4667`, and a defensive `tmpkey = NULL` after ownership transfer at `:4464` — all graded TP-low per the established "real, low-severity" disposition, not FP).
- **EXP05-C read-only cast-away-const reconfirmed 8x** on password/key-blob/extension-data buffers cast to satisfy external non-const OpenSSL API params (`PEM_read_bio_PrivateKey`'s userdata, `SSL_use_PrivateKey_ASN1`'s `u8*`, `BIO_new_mem_buf`, `SSL_set_session_ticket_ext`'s `void*`) — no write ever occurs through any of the casts.
- **EXP20-C "==1, may return >1" OpenSSL-1/0-contract FP class reconfirmed 5x** (`SSL_use_PrivateKey_ASN1` x3, `SSL_use_RSAPrivateKey_ASN1`, `SSL_use_PrivateKey`).
- **API05-C conformant-array-syntax FP class reconfirmed at high volume** (10+ instances) on the standard `T *ptr, size_t len` idiom throughout the tls.h getter family.
- **EXP30-C pure-accessor-args / ||-`&&`-sequence-point FP classes reconfirmed at high volume** (7x `bld`/`params`/`ctx` in one `||` chain, plus `wpabuf_head`/`wpabuf_len`/`wpabuf_mhead`/`wpabuf_size` sibling-arg pairs across `openssl_handshake`/`openssl_get_appl_data`/`tls_connection_encrypt`/`_decrypt`, 8+ more instances) and EXP45-C already-parenthesized-assignment FP class (3x, same `bld`/`params`/`ctx` chain).
- **DCL30-C local-variable-vs-local-storage FP class reconfirmed 6x** on heap-backed `struct wpabuf *`/`EVP_PKEY *` returns (`openssl_dsa_to_dh:4389`, `openssl_handshake:4861`, `openssl_get_appl_data:4896`, `openssl_connection_handshake:4954`, `tls_connection_encrypt:5013`, `tls_connection_decrypt:5070`).
- **DCL31-C third-party-OpenSSL-header FP class reconfirmed 2x** (`PEM_read_bio_PrivateKey:4255`, `SSL_session_reused:5076`) — extends the `dbus.h`/`libnl` "watch for this on any file that leans on OpenSSL" note with concrete OpenSSL instances.
- **MEM10-C stylistic "use a validation function" FP class reconfirmed 6x**; **API00-C internal-API-no-NULL-check FP class reconfirmed 6x** on `tls_connection_handshake`/`_server_handshake`/`_enable_workaround`/`_get_eap_fast_key`'s params; **POS49-C single-threaded-eloop FP class reconfirmed 2x** (`client_hello_generated:4799`, `server:4972`); **MSC41-C hexdump-title FP class reconfirmed** (`:4894`); **FIO05-C admin-config-path FP class reconfirmed** for a private-key/PEM path (`match_lines_in_file`/`is_tpm2_key`, `:5524`); **ERR00-C "fopen not checked" factually wrong** (checked the very next line, `:5524`).
- **NEW, batch-local: WIN03-C "fopen without 'N' flag" graded TP (low), not dismissed** — literally true per rule text (mode string is `"r"`, no `N`) though Windows-build-conditional and low real-world severity; consistent with the "don't propose fixing/disabling WIN* rules without a Windows oracle" guidance, this is about adjudication verdict only. `:5524`.
- **NEW FN, not sqc-flagged:** `tls_connection_engine_ca_cert`'s ANDROID/engine-provider path leaks the `X509_STORE_new()`-allocated `store` if `X509_STORE_add_cert()` fails with anything other than `X509_R_CERT_ALREADY_IN_HASH_TABLE` — `store` is never handed to `ssl_ctx` before this early return. Closest rule: MEM12-C. `tls_openssl.c:4084`. `upstream_present: unknown`.

Closest rule: EXP34-C/API00-C. `tls_openssl.c:5017`. `upstream_present: unknown`.

## Confirmed/reinforced patterns (from batch `41plus_b53`, 150 findings, `src/ap/wpa_auth.c#part2of4`, lines ~2530-5600: WPA_PTK state machine, FILS assoc encrypt/decrypt, MLO/ML KDE builders, SAE PW ID KDE)

- **Reinforces in this batch:** MSC17-C `#ifdef`-intervening-case fallthrough (`:2537`); ARR01-C `sizeof(ptr->member)` on real fixed-size struct fields (8 instances: `:2571,4402,4404,4414,4416,4435,4437`); MEM05-C "VLA" misfire on fixed compile-time-constant-sized local arrays (`u8 msk[2*PMK_LEN]:2770`, `u8 addr[3*4]:5261`); ENV01-C misfire on plain fixed crypto-key buffers with zero `getenv()` in the file (5 instances: `:3132,3135,3173,3824,3825`); EXP30-C pure-accessor-args (`wpa_auth_get_aa/get_spa`, `wpabuf_head/len`, `wpa_cipher_to_alg/key_len`, `MAC2STR`) misread as unsequenced side effects (14 instances); the DCL30-C/ARR36-C/ARR00-C "pos/end/start" wire-buffer-builder-idiom triple-misfire family, now also producing "pos from NULL" mislabels when a later `pos = NULL` in an unreached error branch is conflated with an earlier, still-valid use (`:4927,4935`); INT30-C/ARR39-C "already validated upstream" (comment-documented `wpa_receive()` precondition) on `last_rx_eapol_key_len` arithmetic (`:3965,5370`); INT30-C/INT32-C "small compile-time bound" family extended to KDE-length accumulators built from protocol/config constants (`kde_len +=`/`buf_len +=`, ~20 instances) and to `u8`-field additions (`wpa_ie[1]+2`, `ie[1]+2`, `assoc_resp_ftie[1]+2`); MSC01-C no-final-else stylistic pedantry, now also inside a state-machine `SM_STEP` switch where the missing else correctly means "no transition" (5 instances); MSC37-C `#ifdef`-branch-blind reach-end-without-return (`ocv_oci_add:4318`); API05-C paired-pointer+size-param idiom (`replace_ie:4349`); API00-C mostly-FP on internal-only APIs (~16 instances); STR31-C misapplied to non-char arrays (`const u8 *aad[1]`/`size_t aad_len[1]`, `:3228,3229`); ARR02-C misfire on a local array whose size is exactly its initializer count (`u32 ids[]:4999`); INT14-C struct-field bitwise/arithmetic conflation (`gsm->GN`, `ml_key_info`, 4 instances); DCL13-C TP-vs-FP split holds (14 genuine read-only-param TPs this batch, all internal helpers not vtable/callback slots).
- **NEW: EXP33-C "static variable used without explicit initialization" mistakes a call to a same-named static *function* for a read of a static *variable* — extends the `wpa_cli.c:392`/`wpa_list_cmd_list()` misattribution (`41plus_b44`) to a 2nd file.** `fils_prepare_plainbuf`/`ieee80211w_kde_add` are static functions; no variable of either name exists. 3 instances (`:3503,3602,3706`).

### Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed (from `41plus_b53`)

- DCL30-C "returns pointer to local automatic-storage object" misapplied to a `size_t` **scalar** return value (`fils_encrypt_assoc`'s `current_len`, `:3534`) — a new sub-shape distinct from the established heap-vs-stack-pointer-variable family; here there is no pointer at all, just a plain integer.
- EXP05-C "cast away const" on `(struct ieee80211_mgmt *) buf` where `buf` is declared plain non-const `u8 *buf` — no const qualifier exists anywhere to cast away (`:3478`). Distinct from the already-confirmed "non-const wrapper-type source" `crypto_openssl.c` shape; here it's a completely ordinary non-const local parameter.
- MSC37-C "non-void function has no return statement" on `SM_STEP(WPA_PTK)`, which macro-expands (`src/utils/state_machine.h:126-127`) to `static void sm_WPA_PTK_Step(...)` — the function genuinely returns void; sqc doesn't see the return type because it's hidden inside the `SM_STEP` macro definition, not written literally at the call site. Distinct from the existing ifdef-branch-blind MSC37-C family (root cause is macro-hidden signature, not preprocessor branching). `:5488`.
- EXP34-C "potential null pointer dereference" on `gsm` after `gsm = wpa_select_vlan_wpa_group(gsm, vlan_id)` — the callee provably falls back to returning its own (non-NULL) input `gsm` whenever no matching VLAN group is found, so it can never return NULL here; an interprocedural miss. `:4397`.

## Confirmed/reinforced patterns (from batch `41plus_b52`, 150 findings, `src/ap/wpa_auth.c#part1of4`, lines 1-2524: init/deinit, GTK/GMK derivation, `wpa_receive`, `__wpa_send_eapol`, `wpa_auth_sm_event`)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (9 instances, one function): MEM30-C double-free/use-after-free cluster on `hdr`/`buf` is entirely the mutually-exclusive-branch free-tracking bug, now for MEM30-C specifically (previously seen for MEM31-C/ARR00-C).** `__wpa_send_eapol` has four `os_free(hdr)`-then-`return` early exits (buf-alloc failure, aes_wrap failure, unsupported-KEK-length else, PTK-not-valid, MIC-compute failure) plus one final `os_free(hdr)` at the true end of the function. Every one of these is on its own immediately-returning branch; none can execute after another in the same call. sqc reports the final free (and the `wpa_eapol_key_mic`/`wpa_hexdump`/`wpa_auth_send_eapol` calls that precede it) as "double-free"/"use-after-free" against the early-return frees. `wpa_auth.c:2276,2284,2288(x2),2291,2307(x2),2308(x2)`.
- **Reinforces the `gas_server.c`/`41plus_b17` DCL30-C "local variable assigned to global/static variable" category error (now 4th+ confirmation): a local pointer is reassigned to another local of the same declared name pattern, and DCL30-C conflates the local with a same-named global/field.** `wpa_rekey_all_groups`/`wpa_update_all_gtks` both declare `struct wpa_group *group, *next;` as ordinary locals and do `group = next;` at the end of a free/iterate loop — neither is global/static (the *field* `wpa_auth->group` is global-ish, but the local variable named `group` is not it). `wpa_auth.c:544,562`.
- **DCL30-C "returns pointer to local automatic-storage object" misapplied to heap-allocated (`os_zalloc`) pointers — reinforces the confirmed heap-vs-stack class, 2 more instances.** `wpa_group_init` returns `group = os_zalloc(...)` (`:757`); `wpa_auth_sta_init` returns `sm = os_zalloc(...)` (`:1044`).
- **ARR01-C "sizeof applied to pointer/array parameter which decayed" — reinforces the dereference/member-access misclassification class, 9 instances in one file.** All are `sizeof(*ptr)` (`:1000,1182`) or `sizeof(ptr->fixed_array_field)` (`sm->key_replay/prev_key_replay/PTK/PMK/xxkey/pmk_r1`, `:1103,1989,1992,2413,2456,2459,2461`) — every one yields the true size via dereference/member-access, no decay involved.
- **EXP20-C "==1, function may return >1" judged FP when the callee is defined in the same file and provably restricted to {0,1} — extends the OpenSSL-contract EXP20-C FP class to an internal function.** `wpa_sm_step()` (defined `:6397-6435` in this same file) only ever `return 0;` or `return 1;` on every path — verified by reading the full definition. `wpa_auth.c:1113,2479`.
- **NEW: MEM05-C/ENV01-C wholesale misfire reinforced (const-macro-sized fixed arrays, zero getenv() in file) — 2 MEM05-C (`:682,2024`, `u8 buf[ETH_ALEN+8+sizeof(unsigned long)]` / `u8 data[ETH_ALEN+WPA_NONCE_LEN+8+WPA_GTK_MAX_LEN]`) and 4 ENV01-C (`:1422,1423,2024,2388`) instances; whole-file `grep -c getenv` = 0.**
- **NEW: STR31-C "character array too small" misapplied to non-char arrays — category error, 2 instances.** `const u8 *aad[1]; size_t aad_len[1];` (`:2202,2203`) are an array-of-pointers and an array-of-size_t, not character arrays at all.
- **NEW: MSC07-C "unreachable code after break" is a switch-case-label-blindness variant of the established goto-blindness family.** The line immediately after `break;` is a new `case WPA_REAUTH:` label (`:2465`) — obviously reachable when the switch expression equals that value; sqc doesn't recognize a case label as a valid entry point distinct from straight-line fallthrough. Paired with the already-confirmed `fail:`-label-reached-via-earlier-`goto`-blindness shape at `:894`.
- **NEW: EXP05-C "cast away const" fires on casts of a plain (never-const) `u8 *data`/`void *data` parameter — reinforces the `41plus_b33` "cast from a pointer that was never const-qualified to begin with" rule-bug class, 4 instances across 2 rules.** `wpa_receive(..., u8 *data, ...)` (`:1685` EXP05-C+EXP36-C) and `wpa_verify_key_mic(..., u8 *data, ...)` (`:2394` EXP05-C+EXP36-C) both declare `data` non-const. EXP36-C (alignment 1→4 cast) on the same two lines graded TP (low severity) instead — the underlying buffer's alignment isn't proven by anything in-function, distinct from the const question.
- **NEW, batch-local: EXP34-C null-deref flagged on a custom lookup helper that only returns NULL if its own input argument was NULL — interprocedural non-null-by-construction, not a same-function guard.** `wpa_select_vlan_wpa_group(gsm, vlan_id)` falls back to returning `gsm` itself when no VLAN match is found (`:8100-8105`), so it can only return NULL if `partner_auth->group` was already NULL going in — not reachable for a properly-initialized authenticator. `wpa_auth.c:130`. Watch for recurrence before promoting out of batch-local.
- **API00-C "does not validate pointer/integer parameter" reconfirmed at high volume (17 instances) on internal-only entry points** (`wpa_auth_store_ptksa`, `wpa_auth_logger`/`vlogger`, `wpa_init_keys`, `wpa_deinit`, `wpa_auth_sta_init`, `wpa_store_eppke_pmk_ptk_sm`, `__wpa_send_eapol` x4, `wpa_remove_ptk`) — all always called with already-validated pointers from within hostap's own state machine.
- **DCL15-C/DCL19-C "should be static" reconfirmed FP on a function with genuine cross-file linkage via its own header declaration** — `wpa_auth_vlogger` is declared in `wpa_auth_i.h` and called from `wpa_auth_ie.c`, a different translation unit. `:448`.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b54`, 150 findings, `src/ap/wpa_auth.c#part3of4`, lines ~5590-8130: WPA_PTK/WPA_PTK_GROUP state-machine bodies, group GTK/IGTK/BIGTK rekey helpers, MIB dump, PMKSA cache accessors, FILS/FT/testing-options accessors)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances, one file): EXP33-C misidentifies a call to the static function `ieee80211w_kde_add()` (defined `wpa_auth.c:4237`, forward-declared `:78`) as a read of an uninitialized *static variable* of the same name — a pure category error, not a heuristic judgment call.** The call shape `pos = ieee80211w_kde_add(sm, pos);` recurs at `:5702,5215,3602` and is misfired on at `:7655,7753,8005` in this batch. Worth checking any other rule/file where a function name happens to match this pattern.
- **DCL13-C "plain internal helper, read-only param is a genuine low-severity TP" clarification reconfirmed at very high volume in one file (~35 instances).** Every `wpa_auth_get_*`/`wpa_auth_sta_*`/`wpa_auth_pmksa_*` accessor that only reads its `sm`/`wpa_auth` parameter (never forwards it to a vtable/eloop/for_each-style callback, never writes through it) is a real (if low-value) TP — don't blanket-FP on `wpa_auth.c`'s own public API surface just because it's the same file that also hosts the eloop/for_each-callback FP family. Contrast sharply with `wpa_group_update_sta`/`wpa_group_disconnect_cb`/`wpa_auth_fils_iter` (`:5960,6274,7376`), which stay FP because they're registered as callbacks via `wpa_auth_for_each_sta`/`wpa_auth_for_each_auth`.
- **DCL13-C real miss (finding factually wrong) — os_memcpy writes through a struct field, contradicting "not modified".** `wpa_auth_pmksa_set_to_sm`'s `wpa_auth` parameter is flagged as unmodified, but the function does `os_memcpy(wpa_auth->dot11RSNAPMKIDUsed, pmksa->pmkid, PMKID_LEN)` — a direct write through the param. `wpa_auth.c:7038`. Same root cause as the established `gas_query.c:803` precedent, now via `os_memcpy` into a fixed-size array field rather than a pointer field.
- **API00-C "internal-only API, never externally-nullable" FP class reconfirmed at very high volume (~45 instances) across nearly every `wpa_auth_pmksa_*`/`wpa_auth_*_fils_*`/`wpa_auth_write_fte`/`wpa_auth_resend_*` function.** All have 0-3 call sites, every one internal to hostapd's own AP-side handshake/PMKSA-cache code, always passing live non-NULL pointers (station's own MAC, freshly-built local structs, or already-checked `hapd->wpa_auth`). Includes several functions that dereference an unchecked param that IS handling wire-adjacent data (`wpa_auth_radius_das_disconnect_pmksa`'s `attr`, `wpa_auth_pmksa_get_fils_cache_id`'s `sta_addr`/`pmkid`) — the pointers themselves are never attacker-nullable even though the *data* they reference ultimately derives from the network; that's a distinct, separate concern from a NULL-pointer-parameter check.
- **API00-C "factually wrong" class (body already validates the flagged param inline) — 2 more instances, extends the `tls_connection_established` precedent.** `wpa_auth_pairwise_set`'s body is `return sm && sm->pairwise_set;` (`:6647`); `wpa_auth_sta_get_pmksa`'s body is `return sm ? sm->pmksa : NULL;` (`:6718`) — both are inline null-guards on the exact param API00-C claims is unvalidated.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MSC01-C guard-clause-default class extends from if/else-if chains to a fully-covered `enum` switch with no `default` label.** `wpa_auth_set_ocv_override_freq`'s switch on `enum wpa_auth_ocv_override_frame` covers all 4 declared enum values with no other way to reach the switch; `default` is genuinely unneeded. `wpa_auth.c:7824`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable with automatic storage" misfires on a local pointer *variable* that actually holds a heap allocation from a callee — 3rd+ instance of the established `comeback_token.c` confusion class, now specifically via `os_zalloc`-backed cache-entry constructors.** `wpa_auth_pmksa_create_entry` returns `entry` from `pmksa_cache_auth_create_entry()` → `os_zalloc()` (`:6968`); `wpa_auth_add_group` returns `group` from `wpa_group_init()` → `os_zalloc()` (`:7138`). Also a *stronger* variant: `wpa_group_setkeys`'s dead code at `:7747` flags `kde_buf`/`pos` (assigned `kde = pos = kde_buf;` where `kde_buf = os_malloc(...)`) as "local variable assigned to *global/static* variable 'pos'" — `pos` is not global/static at all, just another local in the same function; two independent factual errors in one finding.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MSC37-C "no return on all paths" misfires when the only reachable code path is inside one arm of an `#ifdef`/`#else` that always returns — extends the confirmed `dbus_common.c`/state-machine-macro ifdef-blindness family to a 3rd shape.** `wpa_auth_get_pmksa_cache` has `return NULL;` then, depending on `CONFIG_IEEE80211BE`, either `return is_ml ? ... : ...;` or `return wpa_auth->pmksa;` — exactly one of the two mutually-exclusive branches is compiled and it always returns, but sqc doesn't resolve the `#ifdef` so treats the declaration/preprocessor-branch boundary as a possible fall-through. `wpa_auth.c:6993`. Also reconfirms the `SM_STEP` variant (see below).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MSC37-C fires on a `SM_STEP(machine)` macro-declared function, misjudging its return type because sqc doesn't expand the declaration macro.** `SM_STEP` (`src/utils/state_machine.h:126`) expands to `static void sm_##machine##_Step(...)`; the finding claims the (void) function "has no return statement." `wpa_auth.c:5844`. New shape of the existing "macro-expansion blindness" theme (previously seen on statement/loop macros, now on a function *declaration* macro that hides the return type itself).
- **INT14-C identifier-only-match FP reconfirmed 3x in one file, same shape as `p2p_invitation.c:282`.** `gsm` (a `struct wpa_group *`) is flagged merely because different member-field expressions off it use `&`/arithmetic in different statements (`gsm->GN & 0x03` vs `gsm->GN - 1`/`gsm->GTK_len` arithmetic) — `:6069,7739,8000`. Also `conf` at `:6512` (bitwise `conf->wpa & WPA_PROTO_RSN` vs arithmetic `wpa_cipher_key_len(conf->wpa_group) * 8` — different fields).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: PRE00-C/PRE02-C/PRE12-C bundle misfires on a single-parameter macro that expands to *multiple comma-separated printf varargs*, not a single expression.** `RSN_SUITE_ARG(s)` (`wpa_auth.c:6488`) expands to `((s)>>24)&0xff, ((s)>>16)&0xff, ((s)>>8)&0xff, (s)&0xff` — 4 separate `%02x` arguments. `s` is always a side-effect-free field/variable read at every call site, so "evaluates multiple times" (PRE00/PRE12) is moot; PRE02-C's suggested fix (wrap the whole body in one set of parens) is actively wrong here since it would collapse 4 comma-expression varargs into a single argument, breaking every `RSN_SUITE` format-string call site. New wrinkle on the existing dl_list-style "PRE02-C fix produces invalid C" category, now via variadic-argument-producing macros rather than statement macros.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP33-C "may be used uninitialized" misses a same-function coupled-invariant between two variables set together in one branch.** `wpa_group_update_sta`'s local `g` is unconditionally assigned immediately after declaration inside the loop, before its one read (`:5968`, benign tool miss on ordering, not a coupling issue). Separately, `wpa_auth_resend_m3`'s `gtkidx` (`:7650`) is only read inside `if (gtk)`, and `gtk`/`gtkidx` are always assigned together in the same `WPA_VERSION_WPA2` branch a few lines earlier — the read is safe by a same-function invariant sqc doesn't track across the two variables.
- **NEW, batch-local: EXP34-C real (medium-confidence) TP — `wpa_select_vlan_wpa_group` can return NULL (falls back to its own possibly-NULL `gsm` input param when no VLAN match and the list itself started NULL), and `wpa_group_update_sta`'s MLD partner-group loop dereferences the result (`partner_group->GKeyDoneStations++`) with no check.** `wpa_auth.c:6028`. Medium confidence since `partner_auth->group` should always be initialized for a live authenticator in practice, but the function contract genuinely allows NULL.
- **NEW, batch-local: INT13-C misattributes a bitwise-on-signed-operand finding to a variable that is only ever a ternary *condition*, not an operand of the `|`.** `wpa_auth_resend_m3`'s `(secure ? WPA_KEY_INFO_SECURE : 0) | ...` — the `|` combines the ternary's *result* (an already-appropriately-typed flag constant) with other flags; `secure` itself never participates in the `|`. `wpa_auth.c:7709`. Category error, not a judgment call. Only 1 instance so far.
- **NEW, batch-local: INT30-C/ARR39-C wrap-around/double-scaling findings on a length subtraction already guarded by an earlier, *different*-function check — extends the existing INT30/INT33/ARR30 cross-call-guard family to ARR39-C.** `key_data_length > sm->last_rx_eapol_key_len - sizeof(*hdr) - sizeof(*key) - mic_len - 2` (`:5766`, and identically shaped at `:3965,5370` elsewhere in the file) can't underflow because `last_rx_eapol_key_len` (== `data_len`) was already validated `>= sizeof(*hdr) + sizeof(*key) + mic_len + 2` in `wpa_receive()` (`:1680`) before ever being stored. ARR39-C's "double scaling" framing is additionally a category error here: this is a plain scalar-length subtraction, not pointer arithmetic at all.
- **NEW, batch-local: INT10-C flags a signed local as "may be negative" when it's a straight copy of a `const u32`/positive compile-time constant.** `int timeout_ms = eapol_key_timeout_subseq;` where `eapol_key_timeout_subseq` is `static const u32 ... = 1000;` (`wpa_auth.c:84,7299`) — `timeout_ms % 1000` can never see a negative operand despite the `int` type. Only 1 instance so far.
- **NEW, batch-local: ENV01-C fires with zero getenv/environment-variable code anywhere in the function — extends the `p2p_invitation.c:681,799` rule-logic-bug entry to a 3rd file.** `wpa_auth_sm_known_sta_identification`'s `u8 exp_mic[WPA_EAPOL_KEY_MIC_MAX_LEN];` (`:7934`) has no environment-variable handling in scope at all.
- **REAL FN found: `wpa_auth_eid_key_delivery` (`wpa_auth.c:7977`) accepts a `max_len` parameter but never references it in the body, writing a Key Delivery IE (header + fragmented KDE payload) with no bound check at all; upstream's own comment flags the gap ("TODO: Make sure there is sufficient length for the element", `:7989`). Caller `wpa_auth_write_assoc_resp_eppke` computes and passes the real remaining buffer length as `max_len`, but it's silently dropped by the callee. Closest CERT mapping: ARR30-C (out-of-bounds array write). `upstream_present: unknown`.**

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b60`, `wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.c#part2of3`, lines ~3985-7180: `wpas_populate_assoc_ies`/`wpas_start_assoc_cb` WPA-IE builder, network enable/disable/select, driver-init, HT/VHT/HE/EHT override setters, FST vtable callbacks)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (30+ instances, highly generalizable): INT30-C/INT32-C/EXP30-C/EXP40-C wholesale misfire on a size-checked IE/buffer-append sequence.** `wpas_populate_assoc_ies` builds `wpa_ie` by repeatedly doing either (a) `if (wpa_ie_len + X <= max_wpa_ie_len) { memcpy(...); wpa_ie_len += X; }` or (b) calling a callee that itself writes only into the remaining `max_wpa_ie_len - wpa_ie_len` capacity and returns the actual bytes written, which is then added. sqc flags almost every `+=`/`-`/addition in this idiom as INT30-C wrap/underflow, even the *guard condition itself* (e.g. `:4011,4022,4074,4249,4290`) — the check that proves safety is not a separate overflow site. Also flags pointer-arithmetic-on-a-byte-value as INT32-C signed overflow (`2 + pos[1]`/`2 + ie[1]`, `:4014,4621` — `pos[1]`/`ie[1]` are `u8`, max 255, can't overflow `int`) and pointer addition (`mdie + 2`, `:4185`) as "signed integer addition." EXP30-C fires on the `memcpy`/`os_memcpy` calls themselves purely because `wpabuf_head()`/`wpabuf_len()` appear as sibling arguments — both are pure accessors (extends the existing pure-accessor-args EXP30-C class). EXP40-C fires on `*start = pos` (`:4291`) despite neither `pos` nor `start` being const-qualified (both plain `u8 *`) — a plain pointer copy, not const removal at all (extends the existing EXP40-C fabricated-const class). Same shape recurs identically for HS20, FST, MBO, FILS, OWE, DPP-PFS, IEEE80211R/MDIE, TESTING_OPTIONS RSNXE-override, MSCS, Multi-AP, and RSN-override IE blocks — one function, ~35 combined findings, all FP.
- **DCL13-C FST-vtable dispatch-table class — extends the existing eloop/EAP-method-table callback-contract FP family to `struct fst_wpa_obj`.** `wpas_fst_get_bssid_cb`/`_get_channel_info_cb`/`_get_hw_modes`/`_send_action_cb`/`_get_mb_ie_cb`/`_update_mb_ie_cb`/`_get_peer_first`/`_get_peer_next`'s `ctx`/`get_ctx` params all match the fixed `void *ctx` signature assigned into `struct fst_wpa_obj` function-pointer fields at `fst_wpa_supplicant_fill_iface_obj` (`:7066-7079`); FP the same way `eloop_timeout_handler` callbacks are. `wpa_supplicant.c:6960,6969,6987,7021,7045,7059`.
- **DCL13-C real miss — finding factually wrong, param IS modified.** `wpa_supplicant_update_mac_addr`'s `wpa_s` is flagged as unmodified/const-eligible, but the function writes `wpa_s->l2 = l2_packet_init(...)` and `os_memcpy(wpa_s->own_addr, ...)` directly through it. `wpa_supplicant.c:6232`. Same shape as the established `wpa_auth_pmksa_set_to_sm`/`gas_query.c` "os_memcpy through param" DCL13-C miss class.
- **ARR01-C "sizeof applied to pointer/array parameter which decayed" — 2 sub-variants, both FP, extend the existing `sizeof(*param->field)`-misattribution class.** (a) `sizeof(wpa_s->bridge_ifname)`/`sizeof(wpa_s->imsi)` (`:6327,6342,6904`) target a *fixed-size array struct member*, not the decayed `wpa_s` pointer itself — `sizeof` on a dereferenced member retains the member's real array type regardless of how the outer pointer decays. (b) `sizeof(*iface_obj)` (`:7069`) is the textbook-correct `os_memset(ptr, 0, sizeof(*ptr))` idiom for a genuine (never-array) pointer parameter — dereferencing to get the pointee's size is exactly right, not a decay bug at all.
- **ARR30-C cross-function fixed-size-buffer misattribution — reconfirms/extends the existing `buf`-name class to a `freqs`-name instance.** `wpas_get_bands(wpa_s, const int *freqs)` iterates its 0-terminated `freqs` parameter (`for (i = 0; freqs[i]; i++)`, standard sentinel-terminated array, no fixed bound at all) but sqc attributes an unrelated fixed-size-15 allocation from a *different* call site (`:9590`) to this generic pointer parameter. `wpa_supplicant.c:7118,7119`.
- **MSC01-C guard-clause-default class reconfirmed at very high volume (9 instances) in this file alone** — every flagged if/else-if chain either leaves a variable at an already-set default (`addr=NULL:5118`, `timeout=60:5009`, `band=0:7138`) or is a deliberate "do nothing for the unlisted case" branch (`:4307,4877,4897,5397,6212`).
- **EXP34-C short-circuit-guard-on-same-line misfire — 1 new instance, extends the general short-circuit-blindness class.** `wpa_supplicant_enable_one_network`'s `if (!ssid || !ssid->disabled || ...)` (`:5174`) flags `ssid->disabled` as a null-deref of `ssid`, but the `!ssid ||` immediately before it on the same line guarantees `ssid` is non-NULL by the time `ssid->disabled` evaluates.
- **EXP34-C "%p-format NULL argument" misfire reconfirmed — `end` at `wpa_supplicant.c:6531` is passed to `wpa_msg(..., "%p", end)` purely for debug logging; not only is a NULL `%p` argument harmless, `end` is never actually NULL there (unconditionally set by the preceding `strtol(tmp, &end, 16)`, which always writes `*endptr` even on a failed conversion).**
- **MEM05-C "recursive function" — finding factually wrong, function has no recursion at all.** `wpas_set_pkcs11_engine_and_module_path` (`:5663`) is flagged as recursive/excessive-stack-risk; it contains no self-call or call cycle anywhere in its body.
- **DCL31-C "called without prior declaration" — finding factually wrong, static function is defined earlier in the same file with no `#ifdef` gating.** `wpas_populate_assoc_ies` is `static`-defined at `:3772` and called (correctly, after its definition) at `:4343,4365,4508,4598`; the `:4598` call site is flagged anyway — a plain engine miss, not a real declaration-order issue.
- **MSC04-C indirect-recursion on event-driven state-machine cycles — judged TP (medium confidence), NOT blanket-FP like the single-level-guarded `l2_packet_ndis.c` precedent.** `wpa_supplicant_deauthenticate`'s 8-hop cycle through `wpa_supplicant_event`→`sme_start_sa_query`→`sme_sa_query_timer`→`sme_check_sa_query_timeout`→back to `wpa_supplicant_deauthenticate` (`:5095`) and `wpa_supplicant_select_network`'s 16-hop P2P-group-formation cycle (`:5472`) both differ from the earlier-confirmed FP shape: `sme_sa_query_timer` is called *directly* (synchronously) at `sme.c:3566`, not only via `eloop_register_timeout`, so the cycle is genuinely reachable within one call stack, not capped by async dispatch. Treat this shape (direct synchronous call re-entering the cycle) as TP; keep the async-only/depth-capped shape as FP.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b64`, 117 findings, `src/ap/ieee802_11.c#part3of3`, lines ~6860-9270: mgmt-frame dispatch/callbacks, TPE/wide-bandwidth/RNR/MBSSID IE builders)

- **DCL13-C misses that a `u8 *eid`-style IE-builder parameter IS modified via `*eid++ = X` / `os_snprintf(buf+len, ...)` writes — NEW, CONFIRMED, 5 instances.** hostap's dominant `u8 *hostapd_eid_X(hapd, u8 *eid)` idiom writes through `eid` (`*eid++ = ...`) throughout the file; DCL13-C still suggests const on it as if only direct-assignment (`eid = ...`) counts as "modified", missing writes-through-the-pointer entirely. Also caught the same miss on an `os_snprintf(buf+len, buflen-len, ...)` write target. `ieee802_11.c:7669`(buf), `7809`(eid), `7995`(eid), `8063`(eid), `8706`(eid). Contrast with genuinely-TP DCL13-C on `hapd`/`sta`/`skip_profiles`/`end`/`link` params in the same functions, which really are read-only or unused — the miss is specific to write-through-pointer, not DCL13-C as a whole in this file.
- **DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable" fires on returning an IE-builder's own `eid`/`eid_start` parameter (or a local alias initialized from it) — NEW, CONFIRMED, 9 instances.** `eid` in every `hostapd_eid_*` builder is a *parameter* (caller-owned output buffer position), and `eid_start`/`eid_len_pos`-style locals are just copies of that parameter's value advanced by pointer arithmetic — never an address-of an automatic-storage object. Returning any of them is exactly the documented API contract (return the advanced write position), not a dangling-pointer bug. Extends the existing "confused local *variable* with local *storage*" DCL30-C entry (comeback_token.c) to the parameter case specifically. `ieee802_11.c:8599,8698,8721,8728,8777,8780,8869,8880,8882`.
- **ARR37-C "arithmetic/subscript/increment on non-array pointer" on the same IE-builder `eid`/`known_bss` pointers — reconfirms and extends the existing "array-backed via parameter/cast" ARR37-C FP class, 14 instances in one function family.** `*eid++ = X` / `eid += ETH_ALEN` throughout `hostapd_eid_rnr_bss` is pointer arithmetic into a caller-supplied output buffer (backed by an array at the call site), not a "single object" pointer; `known_bss[i/8]` is the standard `buf+buflen`-companion subscript idiom. `ieee802_11.c:8639,8640,8641,8642,8646,8648,8650,8666,8667,8680,8683,8692,8891` (+`8939`,`9082` for plain `size_t i++` loop counters mistaken for pointers, same rule/different sub-shape).
- **PRE32-C "#ifdef used inside invocation of MACRO" misattributes an unrelated `#ifdef`/`#endif` elsewhere in the same function to a macro call that has nothing to do with it — NEW, CONFIRMED, 5 instances.** `WLAN_FC_GET_STYPE(fc)` is called exactly once, cleanly, at `ieee802_11.c:6994`; the 5 flagged lines (`7014,7018,7023,7049,7053`) are `#ifdef CONFIG_NAN_USD`/`CONFIG_P2P`/etc. blocks used to conditionally `&&`-chain unrelated boolean sub-expressions inside two large `if (...)` statements — a completely standard, legal preprocessor idiom, uninvolved with the macro call at all.
- **EXP34-C null-deref flagged on the result of `hostapd_mbssid_get_tx_bss()`, which structurally never returns NULL — NEW, CONFIRMED, 4 instances.** The helper (`hostapd.c:96`) is `return hapd->iconf->mbssid ? hapd->iface->bss[0] : hapd`, i.e. always one of two non-NULL hapd pointers; rule can't see into the callee. `ieee802_11.c:9020,9085,9113(chained ->conf deref),9210`.
- **API00-C "does not validate pointer parameter" flagged on parameters the SAME function explicitly guards later — new sub-shape of the existing "mostly FP" API00-C entry, now factually contradicted rather than just internal-API pedantry, 7 instances.** `hostapd_eid_mbssid_len`'s `elem_count` is null-checked at `:9026` and `rnr_len` at `:9043` before any deref; `hostapd_eid_mbssid`'s `rnr_eid`/`rnr_count`/`rnr_offset` are all folded into the `add_rnr = ... && rnr_eid && rnr_count && rnr_offset && rnr_len` guard at `:9221-9223` before use. `ieee802_11.c:9013`(elem_count,rnr_len),`9199`(rnr_eid,rnr_count,rnr_offset); remaining `known_bss`/`hapd_probed`/`end` findings in the same two functions are the ordinary internal-API/unused-param FP shape.
- **ARR30-C "unsafe array access, buffer X with size N allocated at line M" cites a completely unrelated same-named local variable from a distant, different function — NEW, looks like a real sqc name-based (not binding-based) buffer-size lookup bug, 1 instance (watch for recurrence).** Flags `ssid->wep.key[i]`/`ssid->wep.len[i]` (both sized `NUM_WEP_KEYS`==4, matching the loop's `i<4` bound) in `hostapd_set_wds_encryption` (`:7188`) citing "buffer 'len' with size 2 allocated at line 4118" — that line is an unrelated `size_t len[2];` local inside a different function (`ap_sta_wpa_get_pmk`-area OWE code) that merely happens to share the identifier `len`.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b59`, 150 findings, `wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.c#part1of3`, lines 143-3962: WEP/WPA-None key setup, eloop timeout callbacks, PSK/PT derivation, cipher/AKM suite selection, extended-capabilities builder, IBSS/mesh HT/VHT/HE/EHT channel-width setup, FILS HLP/WFA-capability IE builders)

- **ARR30-C "buffer X with size N allocated at line M" cites an unrelated same-named local from a distant, different function — REINFORCED, now 3rd+ instance of the `hostapd_set_wds_encryption`-class name-based (not binding-based) buffer-size lookup bug, extends it to a cross-function-parameter case too.** `wpa_s_setup_sae_pt`'s `ids->buf[idx]` (a `struct wpabuf_array` member, dynamically sized, `idx` provably `< ids->num` from the guard one line above) is cited as "Buffer 'buf' with size 30 allocated at line 9713" — an unrelated local in a different function entirely. Same shape hits `wpa_is_non_eht_scs_traffic_desc_supported`'s `const u8 *wfa_capa` (a vendor-IE pointer of arbitrary parsed length) 3x, conflated with an unrelated `u8 wfa_capa[1]` local declared in a *different* function (`wpas_populate_wfa_capa:3712`) purely by sharing the identifier `wfa_capa`. `wpa_supplicant.c:2741,3698(x2),3699`.
- **MSC04-C "indirect recursion" — reinforces the existing genuinely-guarded-cycle FP class with a new guard shape: a call-site argument, not a runtime flag, caps recursion depth.** `wpa_supplicant_start_autoscan` -> `autoscan_init` -> `request_scan` -> `wpa_supplicant_req_sched_scan` -> `wpa_supplicant_set_state` -> `wpa_supplicant_start_autoscan` is a real static call-graph cycle, but every call to `wpa_supplicant_start_autoscan` passes `autoscan_init(wpa_s, 0)` with `req_scan=0`, and `autoscan_init` returns immediately without calling `request_scan()` when `req_scan` is false — the recursive leg never actually executes. 2 instances, same file (`wpa_supplicant.c:1016,1139`).
- **INT13-C "bitwise op on signed int operand" — genuinely correct per rule text, NOT a categorical FP here.** Unlike the earlier-confirmed "wrong-type" INT13-C FP class (rule fired on a param actually declared `unsigned int`), `wpa_supplicant_set_suites`'s `sel`/`wpas_set_mgmt_group_cipher`'s `sel` are both truly plain `int` used repeatedly with `&`; graded TP (low severity/idiomatic bitmask-selector code, but a literal rule match, not a tool misfire). 25 instances, one file.
- **ARR00-C/ARR30-C array-subscript-by-unvalidated-parameter — bounded-by-construction FP, new shape.** `ieee80211_mode` (used to index `mode->he_capab[]`/`mode->eht_capab[]`) is always `wpas_mode_to_ieee80211_mode(ssid->mode)`, a `switch` with an explicit `default` guaranteed to return a value inside `IEEE80211_MODE_NUM`; never an attacker-controlled or otherwise-unbounded index. 10 instances, one file (`wpa_supplicant.c:3154,3173,3420,3443,3517,3518`).
- **MEM30-C/MEM31-C "use-after-free"/"double free" that is simply factually wrong — no prior free exists at all.** `wpa_supplicant_cleanup`'s `wpa_sm_deinit(wpa_s->wpa)` (`:691`) is flagged as accessing an already-freed `wpa_s->wpa`, but nothing earlier in the function frees it — line 691 *is* the deinit/free call, immediately NULLed after. Separately, `free_bss_tmp_disallowed(wpa_s)` (`:824`) is flagged "double free: wpa_s was already freed" though `wpa_s` itself is never freed anywhere in this function and the callee is invoked exactly once.

## Confirmed/reinforced patterns (from batch `41plus_b62`, 150 findings, `src/ap/ieee802_11.c#part1of3`, lines 1-3078: SAE/FILS/PASN authentication handling)

- **MEM30-C "reassign-then-check" misfire — extends the `mem30-reassign-and-fresh-binding` fix class to `wpabuf_clear_free()`, which the existing fix apparently doesn't cover.** `sta->fils_dh_ss` is freed via `wpabuf_clear_free()` then immediately reassigned via `crypto_ecdh_set_peerkey()` on the very next line; later reads see the fresh pointer, not the freed one. 2 instances (`:2246,2251`); matches the already-documented `config.c:609` `str_clear_free()` gap — the underlying fix apparently tracks a specific set of free-wrapper names, not free-then-reassign-in-general.
- **STR30-C on `sae_set_state(sta, state, "literal")` — reconfirms the const-qualified-callee-param rule-logic bug at high volume (14 instances, one function family).** `sae_set_state`'s third parameter is declared `const char *reason`; passing a string literal into a genuinely const param can never trigger the "literal may be modified" concern the rule exists to catch.
- **ARR30-C "buffer X with size N allocated at line M" cites an unrelated same-named local from a different function — reconfirms the cross-function name-conflation class with a new variable name (`groups`, `pos`).** `sae_pick_next_group`/`sae_is_group_enabled`'s `groups` (either `conf->sae_groups` or the local 3-element `default_groups[]`) is cited as "size 2 allocated at line 872" — that line is `auth_build_sae_commit`'s unrelated local `int groups[2]`. Separately, `check_sae_rejected_groups`'s `pos` (walking a dynamically-sized wpabuf, loop-bounded correctly) is cited as "size 2 allocated at line 4118" — that line is `const u8 *addr[2];` in an unrelated OWE-key-derivation function. 6 instances (`:1512,1513,1589,1590,1626,2205`).
- **ARR01-C "sizeof applied to pointer/array parameter which decayed" fired on `sizeof(*ptr->field)` where the flagged parameter was never an array at all — new sub-shape, extends the confirmed member-array-doesn't-decay class.** `sizeof(*sta->sae)` dereferences a struct pointer *field* (`sae`); the rule's own message blames parameter `sta` for "decaying", but `sta` is a plain pointer parameter that was never an array — the premise doesn't apply regardless of the sizeof target. `:1693`. (Companion instance `:1881`, `sizeof(hapd->comeback_pending_idx)`, is the already-confirmed fixed-size-array-field-doesn't-decay shape.)
- **INT33-C div-by-zero guard can live in the *caller*, not just an earlier line of the same function — reconfirms with a same-function-guard variant too.** `sae_password_mark_success`'s `% pw->num_success_mac` is guarded by both callers checking `hapd->conf->sae_track_password != 0` beforehand (cross-function guard, `:584`); `sae_password_track_fail`'s `% pw->num_fail_mac` is guarded by an identical check at the *top of the same function*, just ~20 lines earlier (`:632`) — an even more clear-cut in-function miss.
- **MSC13-C "dead assignment" is factually wrong when the "dead" value is read on the un-erred/success fallthrough path.** `handle_auth_fils`'s `resp = WLAN_STATUS_SUCCESS` initializer is claimed never-read, but the function's only exit funnel is the `fail:` label, which every success path also falls into unconditionally, reading `resp` via `cb(hapd, sta, resp, data, pub)` — the label name suggests error-only, but it's a shared cleanup/dispatch point. `:2172`.

## Confirmed/reinforced patterns (from batch `41plus_b61`, 142 findings, `wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.c#part3of3`, lines ~7150-10228: radio work queue, interface init/add/remove/deinit, global init/deinit, ctrl_iface response handling, connection-failure/auth-failure bookkeeping, MAC-addr randomization, vendor elements, shared-radio-frequency helpers)

- **dl_list_for_each(_safe)/for_each_link macro lvalue-init EXP33-C misfire — REINFORCED at 5 instances across 4 distinct variable names in one file, extends the `16-40_b10` dl_list entry.** `tmp`/`prev`/`i`/`j` are all flagged "used uninitialized" purely because their real initialization happens inside the macro's own hidden for-loop init clause (`dl_list_for_each_safe(work, tmp, ...)`, `for_each_link(links, i)`), not at the point sqc treats as "the declaration". `wpa_supplicant.c:7392,7435,9621,9893,10071`.
- **DCL30-C "returns pointer to local automatic-storage variable" confusing a local pointer *variable* that walks a heap-allocated dl_list with an actual stack object — REINFORCED at volume (10 instances, one file), extends the `comeback_token.c` entry.** Every flagged variable (`tmp`, `work`, `iface`, `wpa_s`, `eapol_method`, `global`, `bss`, `scan_res`) is a pointer assigned from `os_zalloc`/`os_malloc`/a dl_list traversal/another heap-owning source — never actual `struct foo x;` automatic storage. `wpa_supplicant.c:7253,7313,7601,8246,8370,8456,8473,8714,9813,10060`.
- **DCL13-C dispatch-contract callback FP class — extends beyond eloop timeout handlers to two more fixed-signature callback types.** `offchannel_send_action()`'s `tx_cb` parameter type (`offchannel.h`) fixes its first arg as non-const `struct wpa_supplicant *wpa_s`; `wpa_msg_register_ifname_cb()`'s `wpa_msg_get_ifname_func` typedef does the same for its `ctx` param. Neither callback implementation can add `const` without breaking the registration. `wpa_supplicant.c:7665` (`wpas_gas_server_tx_status`), `:8480` (`wpa_supplicant_msg_ifname_cb`).
- **MEM12-C "returns without releasing all resources" false leak when cleanup happens via a *later call to a paired deinit function*, not a direct free in the same function — reconfirms the `base64.c` class with a new shape (deferred cleanup-via-helper across ~10 failure branches).** Every failure branch in `wpa_supplicant_init()` calls `wpa_supplicant_deinit(global)` before returning, and that function does free both `global->params.match_ifaces` and `global->drv_priv` (verified by reading its body) — sqc's leak check doesn't see through the deinit call. A third instance flags the *successful* `return global;` path, which is plain ownership transfer, not a leak. `wpa_supplicant.c:8700,8707,8714`.
- **MEM31-C "double free" false positive from conflating separate recursive-call invocations on distinct objects — NEW shape, not previously documented.** `wpa_supplicant_deinit_iface()` recursively calls itself (via `wpa_supplicant_remove_iface()`) once per *child* interface, but each recursive invocation operates on a different `wpa_s` pointer (verified: the loop guard `iface->parent != wpa_s` guarantees `prev != wpa_s`). sqc's free-tracking appears to attribute the single `os_free(wpa_s)` at the end of each frame to the same logical object across the recursive call chain, flagging it as already-freed. `wpa_supplicant.c:8215`.
- **MSC04-C real, runtime-bounded recursion cycles through interface-removal and connection-failure event chains — new shapes, extends the `41plus_b59` autoscan-guard-argument class.** `wpa_supplicant_deinit_iface -> wpa_supplicant_remove_iface -> wpa_supplicant_deinit_iface` is a genuine cycle bounded by the finite child-interface tree (never the same `wpa_s` twice); `wpa_supplicant_add_iface -> wpas_p2p_add_p2pdev_interface -> wpa_supplicant_add_iface` is bounded by there being exactly one P2P Device interface; `wpas_connection_failed -> wpa_supplicant_fast_associate -> ... -> wpas_connection_failed` is bounded by the finite BSS ignore-list. All graded low-severity TP (real structural cycle, literally true per rule text) rather than FP, per the existing "real-but-low-value" precedent (MSC01-C/PRE08-C). `wpa_supplicant.c:8125,8302,8911`.
- **EXP34-C "does not check for NULL before passing" factually wrong when the callee's very next statement is the guard — 3 paired instances (addr+mask), reinforces the "callee does check, rule doesn't see it" class.** `wpas_mac_addr_rand_scan_set()` (`scan.c:4106`) opens with `if (addr) { ...; os_memcpy(tmp+ETH_ALEN, mask, ETH_ALEN); }` — both `addr` and `mask` are only ever dereferenced inside that guard, and passing both NULL together (the "clear randomization" case) is an intentional, safe call shape. `wpa_supplicant.c:9932,9938,9947` (addr+mask each).
