## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b57`, 150 findings, `wpa_supplicant/p2p_supplicant.c#part2of3`, lines ~4438-8761: channel-bandwidth verification, P2P config-object callback table, join/GO-negotiation state machine, group init/teardown)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP33-C mistakes a function-call identifier for a "static variable used without explicit initialization" — a distinct tool bug from the sizeof(*ptr) class.** Four instances all name the *callee* `wpas_p2p_get_group_iface` as the uninitialized static, at plain call sites like `group = wpas_p2p_get_group_iface(wpa_s, 0, 0);` (`:6771,8205,8229,8479`) — there is no static variable with that name anywhere; the identifier being flagged is the function being called.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MSC13-C "dead assignment" blind to a read on the next loop-iteration's condition or a post-loop `if (var)` check — the assignment is inside a loop body and the read happens on the back-edge or after loop exit, not "before the function returns."** `ssid = NULL; continue;` inside a `dl_list_for_each` loop is read by `if (ssid)` right after the loop exits (`:7185`); `other_iface_found = 1;` inside a loop is read by the very next iteration's `if (!other_iface_found || ...)` condition (`:8335`). A third instance in the same function, `force_freq = ifs->ap_iface->freq;`, is read a few lines after the loop as a call argument (`:7189`) — not loop-scoped but the same "rule stops scanning too early" root cause.
- **Extends the confirmed ARR01-C member-array-doesn't-decay class with 9 more instances, all `sizeof(wpa_s->some_fixed_array_field)`** (`pending_interface_name:4948`, `pending_join_password:6808,7141,7232,8422`, `p2p_pin:7123,7127,7129,7130,7135`) — same struct-pointer-not-array-param shape as prior batches, now the single largest ARR01-C cluster seen.
- **NEW sub-shape of ARR01-C: fires on `sizeof(*ptr)` (dereference-then-sizeof, sizing the pointee struct) as if it were `sizeof(ptr)` on a decayed array/pointer parameter — a different mistake from the member-array shape, since no array or member is involved at all.** `os_memset(params, 0, sizeof(*params));` (`:7765`) — `sizeof(*params)` correctly yields the pointee struct size; there is no decay here to misapply the rule to.
- **ARR39-C "double scaling... with pointer" misfired on plain `size_t`/`sizeof()` integer subtraction with no pointer arithmetic at all.** `buf_len - sizeof(pref) + 1` (`:5146`) computes a remaining-length integer for a `wpa_snprintf_hex()` call; neither operand is a pointer, so there is nothing to "double-scale". Narrower/more extreme than the previously-confirmed byte-pointer-arithmetic ARR39-C FP class (this one isn't pointer arithmetic to begin with).
- **INT10-C "modulo used with potentially signed operands" reconfirmed wrong-signedness-detection (2 instances, same variable): `r` is declared `unsigned int`, so `r % 3` can never produce an implementation-defined negative result** (`:7533,7711`) — same root cause as the previously-confirmed INT13-C wrong-type-detection instance, now on INT10-C.
- **EXP33-C "used/dereferenced uninitialized" misfired on a variable initialized via a pointer-output function 1-4 lines earlier that the tool doesn't track as an initializer.** `if (os_get_random((u8 *) &r, sizeof(r)) < 0) return -1;` immediately followed by `freq = 2412 + (r % 3) * 25;` still flags `r` as uninitialized (`:7533,7711`) — extends the existing "write-only-output-param function" EXP33-C FP class from struct-out-params to a scalar via `os_get_random()`.
- **INT32-C signed-overflow misfire on the same `os_get_random()`-seeded, modulo-bounded arithmetic** — `2412 + (r % 3) * 25` and `2412 + ((r + i) % 3) * 25` are provably bounded to [2412, 2462] by the `% 3` term, nowhere near `INT_MAX` (`:7533,7711`) — same "rule doesn't see the modulo-bounded range" shape as the existing INT32-C/INT33-C precedents in this file's part1.
- **INT33-C div-by-zero misfire on a count derived from `ARRAY_SIZE()` of a fixed-size array literal — compile-time provably non-zero, an even stronger case than the previously-confirmed "earlier-function guard" INT33-C FP class.** `unsigned int num_freqs = ARRAY_SIZE(freqs);` on a fixed 8-element `const int freqs[] = {...}` immediately precedes `freqs[r % num_freqs]` (`:7589`).
- **MEM05-C "VLA" misfire on a fixed compile-time-arithmetic-sized local array, extends the existing macro-sum shape to a plain integer-literal expression.** `char ssid_hex[32 * 2 + 1];` (`:5432`) is not a VLA at all.
- **EXP43-C "same pointer for output/input" misfired on a call where the callee is not `restrict`-qualified and explicitly, intentionally handles the aliased-pointer case.** `wpas_p2p_disconnect_safely(calling_wpa_s, calling_wpa_s);` (`:7434`) calls a function whose very first line is `if (calling_wpa_s == wpa_s && ...)` — the aliasing is a designed-for case, not UB.
- **Reconfirms in this batch: DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP extended to more `struct p2p_config` callback fields and one more `eloop_timeout_handler` (12 instances: `:4894,4980,5518,5600,5621,5732,5741,5750,5820,6727` plus 2 already-known shapes); DCL13-C plain-internal-helper real-if-low-value TP (15 instances, `wpa_s`/`mode`/`ssid` params on static/exported helpers never bound to a callback typedef, several of them structurally unused entirely e.g. `:4449,4529`); ## Confirmed/reinforced patterns (from batch `41plus_b63`, 150 findings, `src/ap/ieee802_11.c#part2of3`, lines ~3100-6890: PASN auth, handle_auth/handle_assoc, OWE DH key exchange, ML link processing, send_assoc_resp, handle_action)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (7 instances): ARR30-C/ARR37-C cross-function buffer-size identifier conflation extends to a *pointer* target, not just size arrays.** `pos` (a local `u8*`/`const u8*` walking a real, bounds-checked buffer — `resp_ies`, an IE inside `mgmt`, or `&mgmt->u.action`) is repeatedly reported as "Buffer 'pos' with size 2 (allocated at line 4118)" — that line is `size_t len[2];`, an unrelated local inside a completely different function (`owe_process_assoc_req`). Same root cause as the previously-documented `groups`/`dst`/`freqs`/`params` cross-function conflations, now confirmed specifically for a pointer-into-array named `pos` recurring at `:3499,4412,6703` (3 ARR30-C sites) plus the associated ARR37-C "non-array pointer"/"struct member pointer" misfires at the same sites (`:3493,3494,3496,3499,3523,3524,3525,6700,6703`) — sqc loses the array-provenance of `pos` (assigned from `&buf[0]`/an IE pointer/`&mgmt->u.action`) through the local pointer variable and then, separately, misattributes an unrelated function's same-named local as its "allocation site".
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances): MEM30-C/MEM31-C double-free and use-after-free misfire across if/return branches that are all mutually exclusive AND happen to share one variable name across the whole function body — `owe_process_assoc_req`'s `secret` (a `struct wpabuf *` freed via `wpabuf_clear_free()` in 4 different early-return branches plus one final fall-through free).** Reads of `secret` via `wpabuf_head(secret)`/`wpabuf_len(secret)` immediately before the *real* final free are flagged as UAF against that same final free, and the 4 early-branch frees are cross-flagged as "double-free" against each other and against the final free, even though only one branch executes per call. Same root cause as the previously-confirmed `rfkill.c`/`eap_server_psk.c` mutually-exclusive-branch family, now reconfirmed at higher density (9 MEM30-C findings from one function) — worth flagging as a strong candidate for an sqc control-flow fix (track frees per-branch/per-CFG-path, not per-variable-name-in-function).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, same file, 3rd+ instance across corpus): MEM30-C "accessing freed pointer"/reassign-then-check misfire extended to a struct field target freed via `wpabuf_free()` then immediately reassigned in the same statement pair** (`wpabuf_free(sta->p2p_ie); sta->p2p_ie = ieee802_11_vendor_ie_concat(...); if (sta->p2p_ie) ...` and the identical shape for `sta->wps_ie`). The read a few lines later reads the *new* value, not the freed one — same shape as the previously-confirmed `tlsv1_client_read.c:477` (`&conn->server_rsa_key`) entry, now on a plain (non-address-of) struct-field pointer reassignment.
## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b66`, 150 findings, `src/rsn_supp/wpa.c#part2of3`, lines ~4260-6010: MIB/status accessors, `wpa_sm_init`/`wpa_sm_deinit`, PMKSA cache callbacks+wrappers, MLO RSNE/GTK/IGTK/BIGTK link-state setters, assoc IE/RSNXE default generators, WNM-Sleep GTK/IGTK/BIGTK install)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances): ARR00-C/ARR30-C flag an array subscript that appears only inside a `sizeof(...)` operand as an "unvalidated index" access — the subscript is never evaluated at runtime (non-VLA), extending the established EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-is-not-a-dereference FP family to the array-bounds rules.** `wpa_sm_clear_mlo_group_keys`'s `os_memset(&sm->mlo.links[link_id].gtk, 0, sizeof(sm->mlo.links[link_id].gtk));` (`wpa.c:4812-4823`) gets ARR00-C+ARR30-C on the *dest* expression's `link_id` subscript (a real, if internally-bounded, runtime access — see below) **and** a duplicate ARR00-C+ARR30-C pair on the same `link_id` subscript inside the `sizeof(...)` second argument, which is compile-time-only. 6 field pairs (gtk/gtk_wnm_sleep/igtk/igtk_wnm_sleep/bigtk/bigtk_wnm_sleep) all show the doubled pattern.
- **Batch-local (not yet 3x independently confirmed elsewhere, but internally consistent across 6 sites): ARR00-C/ARR30-C on a `static` helper's un-validated index parameter, where the *only* caller in the whole file passes a `for` loop counter already bounded to the target array's own size.** `wpa_sm_clear_mlo_group_keys(struct wpa_sm *sm, int link_id)` never bounds-checks `link_id` itself, but its sole call site (`wpa_sm_set_mlo_params`, `wpa.c:4841,4970`) is `for (i = 0; i < MAX_NUM_MLD_LINKS; i++) ... wpa_sm_clear_mlo_group_keys(sm, i);`, and `sm->mlo.links[]` is declared `struct wpa_sm_link links[MAX_NUM_MLD_LINKS]` (`wpa.h:195`) — provably in-bounds on every call in the program. Graded FP (low/med confidence, judgment call) consistent with the existing "rule doesn't see a caller-side/earlier-function guard" theme (INT33-C/ARR30-C unbounded-loop entries above), but this is the first instance of that theme applied to a *cross-function, whole-call-graph* bound rather than an in-function guard.
- **Reinforces the confirmed ARR01-C "sizeof applied to a real struct-member array/struct field, not a decayed pointer" FP class at high volume (27 instances in one file).** Every `sizeof(sm->X)` / `sizeof(sm->mlo.links[i].X)` in this batch (`last_kck`, `ptk`, `tptk`, `gtk`, `gtk_wnm_sleep`, `igtk`, `igtk_wnm_sleep`, `bigtk`, `bigtk_wnm_sleep`, `p2p_ip_addr`, `pmk`, `xxkey`, `pmk_r0`, `pmk_r1`, and the `mlo.links[i]`/`mlo.links[link_id]` variants of the 6 GTK/IGTK/BIGTK fields) is `sizeof` of an actual fixed-size array or struct field declared in `wpa_i.h`/`wpa.h`, not the decayed pointer type of the `sm` parameter itself.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances): MEM30-C "accessing freed pointer" on a `if (sm->mlo.links[i].X) wpa_dbg(...)` debug-log guard that runs immediately *after* `os_free(sm->mlo.links[i].X)` but *before* the field is nulled out — extends the existing "MEM30-C false UAF from comparing a freed pointer's value, not dereferencing it" FP class (`eap_server_tls_common.c:342`) to a struct-field target checked purely for a non-NULL debug-log condition, never dereferenced.** `wpa_sm_set_mlo_params`'s `ap_rsne`/`ap_rsnxe`/`ap_rsnoe`/`ap_rsno2e`/`ap_rsnxoe` link fields all follow the identical shape: `os_free(sm->mlo.links[i].X); if (!ie || len == 0) { if (sm->mlo.links[i].X) wpa_dbg(...); sm->mlo.links[i].X = NULL; ...}` (`wpa.c:4863-4869,4884-4890,4905-4911,4926-4932,4947-4953`) — the `if (sm->mlo.links[i].X)` only reads the stale pointer *value* for a log message, then immediately nulls it; no memory access through the freed pointer ever occurs.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (14 instances across the file, extends the existing "plain internal accessor/wrapper with no mutation through the pointer" DCL13-C TP class to a `struct wpa_sm *sm` top-level state-machine handle, not just secondary params):** genuine (low-severity) TPs where a getter/thin-wrapper function only reads through `sm` or forwards `sm->pmksa`/`sm->X` to a callee without ever assigning to any `sm->field` — `wpa_sm_get_ap_rsne`/`wpa_sm_get_ap_rsnxe` (`:5163,5180`), `wpa_set_test_rsnxe_data` (`:5434`), `wpa_sm_ext_key_id`/`wpa_sm_ext_key_id_active` (`:5287,5293`), `wpa_sm_parse_own_wpa_ie` (`:5749`), `wpa_sm_pmksa_cache_list`/`_head`/`_add_entry`/`_remove`/`_get`/`_exists`/`_flush`/`external_pmksa_cache_flush` (`:5765,5771,5778,5795,5803,5833,5894,5900`), `wpa_sm_has_ft_keys`/`_has_ptk_installed` (`:5864,5880`), `wpa_sm_get_p2p_ip_addr` (`:5973`), and `buf` (not `sm`) in `wpa_wnmsleep_install_key` (`:5907`, read-only key-data buffer). Contrast with 2 instances this batch where the rule's own "not modified" premise is simply false: `wpa_sm_set_own_addr`'s `sm` (`:4983`, writes `sm->own_addr` via `os_memcpy`) and `wpa_sm_update_replay_ctr`'s `sm` (`:5888`, writes `sm->rx_replay_counter`) — both graded FP because the finding's factual claim is wrong, not because of any dispatch-contract exemption.
- **Reconfirmed at volume:** API00-C internal-API-no-NULL-check FP (≈45 instances, every `wpa_sm_*` entry point in this file is only ever called with `wpa_s->wpa` post-`wpa_sm_init()` or another already-non-NULL internal pointer); MEM10-C ad-hoc-NULL-check stylistic pedantry (14 instances); API05-C paired-pointer/size-param idiom (4 instances: `:4267,5205,5765` `buf`+`buflen`/`len`); MSC01-C no-final-else guard-clause pedantry (2 instances: `:4662` unmatched `pmk_len` left unchanged by design, `:5505` `else if` with an implicit do-nothing case); MSC17-C `#ifdef`-intervening-next-case fallthrough misfire (2 instances: `:5091,5126`, both have a real unconditional `break;` immediately followed by a `#ifdef CONFIG_TESTING_OPTIONS`/`#ifdef CONFIG_DPP2`-gated next case); EXP30-C pure-accessor/macro-arg unsequenced-side-effects misfire (3 instances: `:4307` `RSN_SUITE_ARG(...)` macro args, `:5215` `wpa_cipher_txt`/`wpa_key_mgmt_txt` getters, `:5335` the exact documented `wpabuf_head()`/`wpabuf_len()` sibling-argument shape); EXP33-C output-param-memset-first misfire extended to `wpa_parse_wpa_ie_rsn(rsne, rsne_len, &rsn)` (`wpa_common.c:2020` unconditionally `os_memset(data, 0, sizeof(*data))`s before any parse/early-return, so `rsn.capabilities` is always initialized by the time it's read — `wpa.c:5310`) and the `sizeof(*sm)` idiom in `os_zalloc(sizeof(*sm))` right before the NULL-check (`:4410`); MEM05-C fixed macro-sized array misfire (`char pmkid_txt[PMKID_LEN * 2 + 1]`, `:4269`); DCL30-C heap-vs-stack misfire (`wpa_sm_init` returns `sm`, itself `os_zalloc`'d heap memory, not an automatic-storage local, `:4431`); EXP40-C misfire where neither side of the assignment involves a `const`-qualified type at all (`char *pos = buf;` where `buf` is plain `char *buf`, `:5208`); MSC41-C hard-coded-sensitive-info on a `wpa_hexdump_key` title-string literal (`"Install GTK (WNM SLEEP)"`, `:5939`).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b65`, 137 findings, 1 file: `src/rsn_supp/wpa.c#part1of3`, lines ~1-4260: EAPOL-Key send/receive core, msg 1-4 of 4-Way Handshake, GTK/IGTK/BIGTK install, MLO link KDEs, AES-SIV/AES-WRAP key-data (de)cryption)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): EXP34-C "passing NULL to a function that doesn't check for NULL" misfires on `wpa_hexdump`/`wpa_hexdump_key`, both of which DO check `buf == NULL` internally (`src/utils/wpa_debug.c:282` et seq., prints `"[NULL]"`) — extends the existing "%p-format NULL argument is safe" EXP34-C FP family to a whole logging-function class, not just printf `%p`.** `wpa_eapol_key_send`'s `key_mic` (`wpa.c:138`) is unconditionally hexdumped even on the branch where it was left NULL a few lines earlier — safe by the callee's own documented NULL handling.
- **Reinforces the existing "ARR30-C/ARR37-C cross-function buffer-size identifier conflation" entry (further up this file, `owe_process_assoc_req`'s `size_t len[2]`) with 2 more instances in a different function pair.** `wpa_supplicant_send_2_of_4`'s and `wpa_supp_aead_decrypt`'s `pos` (both real, correctly-sized buffers) are reported as "Buffer 'pos' with size 2 (allocated at line 7161)" — line 7161 is `owe_process_assoc_resp`'s unrelated `size_t len[2];`. `:598,3782`.
- **Reinforces the existing "DCL13-C 'not modified' factually wrong on a pointer written through" entry (aes-ccm.c/aes-gcm.c/gas_query.c/ctrl_iface.c precedents) with 3 more instances, all via write-through-alias rather than a direct field write.** `wpa_supplicant_verify_eapol_key_mic`'s `key` (`os_memset(key + 1, 0, mic_len)`, `:3529`), `wpa_supplicant_decrypt_key_data`'s `key` (`WPA_PUT_BE16(((u8*)(key+1))+mic_len, ...)`, `:3607`), and `wpa_supp_aead_decrypt`'s `buf` (written through the `hdr`/`key`/`pos` aliases derived from `buf`, `:3757`) are all genuinely mutated through pointer arithmetic on the flagged parameter itself.
- **Reinforces the existing "MEM12-C false leak after the resource was already freed earlier in the same function" entry (`l2_packet_freebsd.c` precedent) with 6 more instances, one function.** `wpa_supplicant_send_2_of_4`'s `rsn_ie_buf`/`buf2` are correctly freed on every one of 6 return paths (`:591,608,637,690,701,713`); MEM12-C reports "Leaked: rsn_ie_buf, buf2" at every one anyway, apparently not tracking the `os_free()` calls immediately preceding (or, for 3 of the 6, several statements preceding) each return.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM30-C "use-after-free: passing freed pointer" misfires by conflating a variable freed on a sibling, mutually-exclusive early-return branch with the same variable used later on the surviving path — extends the file's own free/access-mutually-exclusive-branch family (already documented for MEM31-C/ARR00-C) to MEM30-C on a reassigned (not literally freed-then-used) local.** `wpa_supplicant_send_2_of_4`'s `wpa_ie` is reassigned (`wpa_ie = rsn_ie_buf` / `wpa_ie = buf2`) on paths that never free those buffers before the flagged use; the *only* `os_free(rsn_ie_buf)` calls are on sibling error branches that return immediately. `:616` (flagged at a plain `wpa_hexdump` read) and `:668` (flagged at an `os_memcpy` read that itself precedes the real `os_free(rsn_ie_buf); os_free(buf2);` two lines later) — the second sub-shape is an ordering bug (free noticed but its position in program order relative to the use not checked), distinct from the branch-conflation sub-shape.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: ARR00-C "subtracting pointers from different arrays" fires on plain `size_t`-`size_t` scalar subtraction used as an array index, with no pointer operands anywhere in the expression** — same category error as the already-confirmed ARR36-C scalar-ternary misapplication, now on ARR00-C. `plain[plain_len - pad_len] = 0xdd;` (`plain_len`, `pad_len` both `size_t`) flagged as pointer subtraction between `'plain_len'`/`'wpa_ie_len'` and `'pad_len'`/`'8'`, none of which are pointers. `:693,2433`.
- **Reinforces "DCL30-C/ARR36-C/ARR00-C pos/end/start wire-buffer-builder-idiom" family with the inverse mistake: ARR00-C flags `pos - kde`/`kde_len = pos - kde` as "different arrays" when `pos` and `kde` are provably the same buffer (`kde` aliases `kde_buf`, `pos` walks forward from `kde`).** `:1130,1146`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP07-C "do not assume constant values" fires on a bit-extraction shift whose amount is directly tied to the same-expression `BIT(13)` literal already present** (`(key_info & (BIT(13)|BIT(14)|BIT(15))) >> 13`) — not an assumption about an opaque/external constant's value at all, the `13` is self-documenting from the adjacent `BIT(13)`. `:3733`. Only 1 instance so far.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b73`, 48 findings, 1 file: `src/ap/wpa_auth_ft.c#part3of3`, lines ~4480-4960: FT-over-DS (RRB) sequence-number request/response handlers, `wpa_ft_rrb_rx`/`wpa_ft_rrb_oui_rx` frame dispatch, PMK-R1 push)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (8 instances, one macro): EXP33-C "used/may be used uninitialized" misfires on an out-param set by a helper whose call is itself guarded by `if (helper(...) < 0 || badlen) goto out;` — reaching the use proves the helper succeeded and therefore set the out-param.** hostap's `RRB_GET_AUTH`/`RRB_GET_SRC` macro (`wpa_auth_ft.c:599-613`) expands to exactly this shape around `wpa_ft_rrb_get_tlv()`, which only writes `*tlv_data`/`*tlv_len` on success (`:142-176`); every macro-set `f_nonce`/`f_nonce_len`/`f_r0kh_id`/`f_r0kh_id_len`/`f_r1kh_id` use downstream of the macro is flagged anyway. sqc doesn't track that falling through a `goto`-on-failure guard implies the guarded call succeeded. Same root idea as the existing INT33-C/INT30-C/ARR30-C "rule doesn't see an earlier same-function guard" family, now extended to EXP33-C initialization-state tracking specifically. `:4549(x2),4570,4571,4574,4623,4624`.
- **NEW, batch-local: EXP33-C "may be used uninitialized" on a variable set unconditionally by an out-param helper, where the helper call and the use sit in two textually-separate `if` blocks that test the identical (invariant) condition.** `wpa_ft_rrb_lookup_r1kh(..., &r1kh, &r1kh_wildcard)` unconditionally sets `*r1kh_wildcard = NULL` as its first statement, called inside `if (!to_r1kh) { ... }` (`:4463-4479`); the flagged use is inside a *second*, separate `if (!to_r1kh) { ... }` block further down (`:4504-4518`). Since `to_r1kh` is never reassigned between the two blocks, the second always executes iff the first did — but sqc apparently doesn't correlate two syntactically distinct `if`s guarding the identical unmodified condition. 1 instance so far (`:4506`), watch for the same shape (split by an intervening unrelated `if (!to_r0kh)` block) elsewhere in RRB-style dual-KH dispatch code.
- **NEW, batch-local: FLP30-C "floating-point variable used as loop counter" fired on a `struct ft_remote_r1kh *` pointer — flat type misclassification, not a heuristic judgment call.** `for (r1kh = *wpa_auth->conf.r1kh_list; r1kh; r1kh = r1kh->next)` (`:4950`): `r1kh` is declared as a pointer, not any floating-point type. Same "rule-engine variable-type misclassification" family as the confirmed INT30-C pointer-mislabeled-as-unsigned-int and ARR01-C non-parameter-array bugs — only 1 instance so far, but the failure mode (wrong type entirely, not a wrong heuristic) makes it worth flagging early.
- **NEW, batch-local: MSC37-C "may reach end without returning a value" fired on a function where every path already has an explicit `return`.** `wpa_ft_rrb_rx_seq_resp` ends with `return 0;` on the normal path followed immediately by `out: return -1;` reached only via earlier `goto out;`; there is no path that falls off the end. Same goto/label CFG-blindness family as this file's MSC07-C "unreachable code after return" misfires (`:4521,4691`) — worth watching for a 3rd rule hit by the same root cause, matching the file's own already-documented mutually-exclusive-branch/goto family.
- **Reconfirmed at volume in this batch:** MSC41-C "hard-coded sensitive information" on `RRB_GET_AUTH`'s plain descriptive `txt` argument (`"seq request"`/`"seq"`/`"seq response"`) — 6 instances (`:4548,4551,4552,4622,4666`, one more at the `wpa_ft_rrb_rx_seq_resp` reset branch); MSC13-C "declared but never used"/"dead assignment" macro-blind to `dl_list_for_each`-loop or macro-internal reads (5 instances: `f_r1kh_id_len:4535`, `f_seq_len:4606`, `found:4626,4635`, `r0found:4937` — the latter three all read immediately after their `dl_list_for_each` loop via `if (!found)`/`r0 = r0found`); MSC07-C goto-label-after-return (2 instances: `:4521,4691`); DCL30-C "local variable assigned through pointer parameter"/"to global/static variable" (3 instances: `r1kh:4515`, `r1kh_wildcard:4517` — both point into the persistent `conf.r1kh_list`, not automatic storage; `sta_addr:4756` — flagged as global/static when it's an ordinary same-function local, a category error already reconfirmed 5+ times elsewhere in the corpus); ARR39-C misfire on byte-pointer single-scaled arithmetic (`data + sizeof(u16)[+alen]`, 2 instances: `:4844,4846`) and on plain non-pointer `size_t` subtraction (2 instances: `:4731,4847`); INT30-C mislabels pointer arithmetic as unsigned-integer wrap (`:4846`) and misses a domain bound from a `u16`-sourced value (`sizeof(u16)+alen` capped at ~65537, `:4839`) and an earlier same-function guard (`:4847`); API00-C internal-only-API no-NULL-check FP (5 instances: `wpa_auth`/`src_addr`/`dst_addr`/`addr` params, all from the single internal driver-glue call site); EXP30-C `MAC2STR` pure-accessor-arg misfire (4 instances); ARR01-C `sizeof(ptr->fixed_array_member)` (`sizeof(r1kh->key)`, 1 instance); ARR02-C local-array-sized-by-initializer misfire (`push[]`/`push_auth[]`, 2 instances); MSC01-C deliberate wire-opcode-dispatch guard-clause FP (switch on `oui_suffix`, 1 instance); DCL13-C genuine low-value TP on a plain internal helper param (`r1kh` in `wpa_ft_generate_pmk_r1` — no field of `r1kh` itself is written; the only mutation is through `r1kh->seq`'s pointee, which C's const rules don't propagate through, so `const` would compile fine).

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b70`, 62 findings, `src/p2p/p2p.c#part3of3`, lines ~6260-7419: PASN pairing/PMKSA helpers, PASN Authentication frame RX/TX dispatch, `p2p_handle_pasn_auth`/`p2p_pasn_auth_rx`, `p2p_parse_data_element`, `p2p_get_dira_info`)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED by reading `exp08_c.rs`: EXP08-C "pointer arithmetic on struct pointer with byte offset" is a rule-engine bug that fires on ANY `-`/`+` binary expression whose right operand text contains the substring `offsetof`, without checking that the left operand is actually a pointer.** `check_struct_pointer_arithmetic()` has `if right_text.contains("offsetof") || (looks_like_struct_pointer(left) && ...)` — the `offsetof`-substring branch short-circuits the left-operand pointer check entirely. Fired twice on `len - offsetof(struct ieee80211_mgmt, u.auth.variable)` (`:6722,6758`) where `len`/`ies_len` are plain `size_t` byte-length locals, not pointers — there is no pointer arithmetic here at all, just an integer length computation using `offsetof` to size a header. Expect this wherever `<size_t var> - offsetof(...)` appears (a common hostap idiom for "payload length after a variable-length header").
- **NEW, batch-local: MEM31-C false leak ignoring `wpabuf_concat()`'s documented "always frees both inputs" contract.** `wpabuf_concat(a, b)`'s own doc comment (`wpabuf.c:238`) states both buffers are freed regardless of return value. `p2p_pasn_service_hash()` returns `wpabuf_concat(buf, extra_ies)` (`p2p.c:6340`) — `buf`, allocated a few lines earlier, is freed inside the callee even though sqc sees no explicit `wpabuf_free(buf)`/return-of-buf in the caller. Same root cause (rule not modeling a callee's documented unconditional-free contract) as the already-confirmed `register()`/BIO-helper/`send_and_recv_glb` ownership-transfer MEM31-C FP family — `wpabuf_concat` is a new instance of that family, not a new class. `:6330,6340`.
- Reconfirms in this batch: ARR01-C `sizeof(ptr->fixed_array_member)` on `p2p->dev_sae_password`/`peer_sae_password`/`peer_dik_data`/`pasn_ptk` (9 instances: `:6267,6268,6271,7033,7040,7245,7247,7332`); MEM31-C mutually-exclusive-branch/goto-frees-at-label misfire (3 instances: `:6592,6674,6942`, all `extra_ies` freed unconditionally at the function's own `out:` label); MEM31-C ownership-transfer-to-a-longer-lived-struct-field extended to `pasn->pasn_groups` (`os_free()`'d and reassigned on every call to `p2p_handle_pasn_auth`, not a per-call-scoped local) — 6 instances (`:7215,7221,7227,7234,7248,7252`); EXP30-C pure-accessor-args (`wpabuf_head_u8`/`wpabuf_len`/`wpabuf_mhead_u8`, 6 instances: `:6477,6599,6912,6948,7145`, plus `:9` col); API00-C internal-only-API FP (7 instances, including a pure 3-param thin-forwarding wrapper `p2p_pasn_pmksa_set_pmk:7316`); DCL13-C plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP (4 instances: `dev:6852`, `p2p:7057,7316,7358`); MSC01-C no-final-else guard-clause pedantry on wire-opcode/state dispatch chains where the missing else is an intentional no-op (3 instances: `:6838,7157,7229`); ENV01-C wholesale misfire on a fixed crypto buffer with zero `getenv()` in the function (`:7095`); ERR02-C name-substring misfire on `wpa_snprintf_hex()` (2 instances: `:7402,7410`), extending the established `wpa_snprintf_hex`/`os_snprintf` FP class; EXP36-C alignment-1-to-4 cast graded genuine low-severity TP per established disposition, buffer alignment unproven in-function (`:7129`); INT10-C wrong-signedness-detection on `os_random() % 10` (`os_random()` returns `unsigned long`, `:6896`); INT14-C misattributes a bitwise op performed on one identifier (`capab >> flen*8`) to a different identifier (`flen`) that only ever does arithmetic (`:6356`); INT30-C "already validated upstream" — `data_len - 1` guarded by `data_len >= 1` in the same `if` condition (2 instances: `:6809,6829`); DCL30-C local-pointer-vs-local-storage misfire, `buf` in `p2p_pairing_generate_rsnxe` points to `wpabuf_alloc()` heap memory (`:6377`); EXP33-C write-only-output-param class extended to `wpa_pasn_parse_parameter_ie()` (`os_memset`'s the whole struct before any field write, called via `wpa_pasn_auth_rx`, `:7299`) and to `ieee802_11_parse_elems` (`:6766`); MSC13-C both correct dead-store TPs (`ie_len:6324` — NULL init never read before either early-return-unused or unconditional overwrite; `ret:7125,7259` — `= 0` init never read before either branch overwrites it; `pos:7353` — final `pos +=` in the function is never read afterward) and a real DCL13-C miss (`buf:7373` in `p2p_get_dira_info`, IS written via the `pos = buf` alias — extends the established `pos = buf` DCL13-C-alias-miss family, now the single largest recurring miss class in the corpus); API05-C `T *ptr, size_t len` idiom (`buf`/`buflen:7373`); EXP05-C cast-away-const graded genuine low-severity TP per established disposition, `(u8 *)addr` in `pasn_initiator_pmksa_cache_remove(pasn->pmksa, (u8 *)addr)` — doubly pointless since the callee's own parameter is already `const u8 *` (`:6656`).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b68`, 150 findings, 1 file: `src/p2p/p2p.c#part1of3`, lines 1-3663: core P2P context lifecycle, peer-device table, find/listen/connect/authorize, probe-req/action-frame RX dispatch, ASP service-advertisement list, PASN GO-negotiation completion)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (15 MEM30-C + 1 MEM31-C, one function each of two shapes): free-tracking conflates freeing a struct *member*/field with freeing the struct pointer itself, then cascades into false UAF/double-free for the rest of the function.** Two sub-shapes: (a) *intra-function* — `p2p_deinit(p2p)` calls `os_free(p2p->cfg->dev_name)` / `os_free(p2p->groups)` / etc. (`p2p.c:3256-3262`), and every one of these direct member-frees is treated as if `p2p` itself were freed; every subsequent `p2p->X` access or `foo(p2p)` call through the rest of the function is then flagged as UAF (`:3263,3265,3266,3267,3268`), and the real, single, correct `os_free(p2p)` at the very end (`:3270`) is flagged as a double-free. Same root cause recurs in `p2p_flush()`'s `p2ps_prov_free(p2p)` call (`:3287`, "double free detected" despite `p2ps_prov_free()` itself doing `os_free(p2p->p2ps_prov); p2p->p2ps_prov = NULL;` — not touching `p2p` at all). (b) *interprocedural* — `p2p_find()` calls `p2p_free_req_dev_types(p2p)` (`:1210`), whose body does `os_free(p2p->req_dev_types); p2p->req_dev_types = NULL;`; the tool attributes that inner member-free to `p2p` itself and flags the unrelated, immediately-following `os_memcpy(p2p->find_dev_id_buf, ...)`/`p2p->find_dev_id = ...` (`:1221,1222`) as UAF, even though `p2p` was never freed anywhere in `p2p_find()`. This is an interprocedural extension of the already-documented `16-40_b3` "MEM30-C conflates 'helper frees some sub-fields of `*ptr`' with '`*ptr` itself being freed'" entry — that entry was intra-function/direct-member-free only; this batch shows the same conflation propagating through a one-level function call, and shows it can cascade into a *false double-free at the one genuinely correct free site*. Expect this shape anywhere a deinit/cleanup function frees several of its own struct's pointer fields before finally freeing the struct itself, or calls a small helper that frees-and-nulls one field.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances, one function): ARR00-C/EXP33-C "loop uses uninitialized variable as bound"/"variable used uninitialized" fires on a `for (idx = 0; idx < bound; idx++)` loop counter that IS initialized in that very same init-clause — reconfirms the `16-40_b4`/`wpabuf.c:362` batch-local entry, now promoted with 3 more instances in a different file.** `p2p_get_next_prog_freq()`'s `for (cl = 0; cl < c->reg_classes; cl++)` (`:1000`) and nested `for (ch = 0; ch < cla->channels; ch++)` (`:1004`), plus the outer `p2p_add_group_clients()`'s `for (c = 0; c < info.num_clients; c++)` (`:508`, paired with an EXP33-C "info is used uninitialized" on the same line — `info` is actually populated by-reference via `p2p_group_info_parse(gi, gi_len, &info)` two lines earlier, the standard output-param class below).
- **NEW, batch-local: EXP33-C/EXP34-C "may be used uninitialized"/"potential null pointer dereference" fires on loop-scoped variables (`ch`, `cla`) whose initialization is provably correlated with a sentinel flag (`found`) set only along the same code path that initializes them, in an `else` branch gated on that flag.** `p2p_get_next_prog_freq()`: `cla`/`ch` are only ever read in the `else` branch of `if (!found) {...} else { ch++; if (ch == cla->channels) ...}` (`:1021`, EXP33-C x2 + EXP34-C on `cla`); reaching the `else` means `found` was set to `1` inside the same double-`for` loop that also set `cla`/`ch`, so both are guaranteed initialized whenever `found` is true. sqc doesn't track the correlation between a boolean sentinel and the loop-scoped variables set alongside it. Only 1 instance so far, but a clean, easily-recognizable shape (`found`-guarded `else` branch reading loop variables set in the same loop that sets `found`).
- **NEW, batch-local: MSC13-C "value assigned is never read" misses a read that occurs in a *later iteration* of the same `dl_list_for_each` loop.** `p2p_continue_find()`'s `found = 1;` (`:3499`) is read by `if (!found) continue;` on every subsequent iteration of the same loop — real, just not visible to a single-iteration dead-store check. Distinct from (but same family as) the already-confirmed `16-40_b7`/`41plus_b73` "MSC13-C macro/loop-blind" entries; extends that family from macro-internal reads to genuine cross-iteration loop-carried flags. Only 1 instance so far.
- **NEW, batch-local: MSC13-C "value assigned is never read" misses a read via the same expression's enclosing comparison, plus a later use of the same variable after the enclosing if/else-if chain.** `p2p_search()`'s `freq = 0` then `(freq = p2p_get_next_prog_freq(p2p)) > 0` (`:1064`) — the assigned value is read immediately by the `> 0` test and again afterward at the `p2p->cfg->p2p_scan(..., freq, ...)` call; there is no path on which the assignment happens and is genuinely never read. Only 1 instance so far.
- **NEW, batch-local: INT32-C signed-multiply-overflow graded TP (not FP) despite superficially resembling the confirmed "protocol-bounded small value" FP family, because the relevant setter enforces no upper bound.** `p2p_listen_in_find()`'s `tu = (r % ((p2p->max_disc_int - p2p->min_disc_int) + 1) + p2p->min_disc_int) * 100` (`:288`) pairs with a genuinely-FP INT33-C/INT10-C (the divisor is provably `>= 1` because `p2p_set_disc_int()` rejects `min_disc_int > max_disc_int` and negative values) — but that same setter places no cap on `max_disc_int`'s magnitude, so a large value set via the `P2P_SET disc_int` ctrl_iface command is not excluded, and the multiply can genuinely overflow. Worth double-checking any other "rule doesn't see an earlier same-function/cross-function guard" FP call before defaulting to FP — the guard has to actually bound the value in the direction the flagged rule cares about, not just rule out a different failure mode (div-by-zero vs. overflow) on the same expression.
- Reconfirms in this batch: API00-C internal-only-API FP (32 instances, the largest single-batch count so far, including an integer-overflow-flavored variant on `num_req_dev_types` at `:1196`); ARR01-C `sizeof(ptr->fixed_array_member)` (20 instances: `dev_sae_password`/`peer_sae_password`/`device_name`/`manufacturer`/`model_name`/`model_number`/`serial_number`/`pri_dev_type`) plus the `sizeof(*cfg)`-for-allocation-sizing sub-shape (`:3174,3178`); DCL13-C eloop-callback dispatch-contract FP (`timeout_ctx`, 4 instances), DCL13-C misses-a-mutation-via-direct-field-write (2 instances: `p2p->intended_addr:157`, `p2p->ssid_set`/`p2p->dev_sae_password:1865`), and DCL13-C genuine low-value TP on plain read-only struct-pointer params including ones that only write through a *nested* nested pointer field (`p2p->cfg->X`) rather than `p2p`'s own fields (12 instances: `:145,151,702,1161,2329,2857,3087,3095,3118,3393,3399,3451`); EXP33-C output-param-written-by-callee (`os_get_random(&r,...)`, `p2p_group_info_parse(&info)`, `wps_parse_msg(&attr)`, `ieee802_11_parse_elems(&elems)`, `p2p_dfs_channel_filter(&p2p_chanlist)`, `p2p_channels_intersect(&intersection)`) and sizeof(*ptr) idiom (`sizeof(*p2p)`, `:3174`); DCL30-C local-pointer-vs-local-storage confusion (8 instances, including two `p2p_service_add_asp`/`p2ps_gen_hash`-adjacent linked-list-node shapes at `:2867,2961` and the top-level `p2p_init()` heap-allocated-then-returned `p2p` itself at `:3230`); MEM10-C ad-hoc-NULL-check stylistic pedantry (4 instances); MSC01-C guard-clause/no-final-else pedantry (10 instances, including two "switch has no default" wire-dispatch variants and one where a trailing `return -1;` after the chain already handles the unmatched case, `:3020`); INT14-C struct-pointer/member conflation (`msg->capability[i]`, 1 instance); EXP34-C internal-invariant-non-null (2 instances beyond the `found`-correlation one above); ARR02-C local 0-terminated initializer-array misfire (5 instances, `op_classes_*[]`); API05-C paired-bounds/fixed-ETH_ALEN-length idiom (4 instances); EXP05-C cast-to-a-const-consumer FP (`(u8*)ie` into `ieee802_11_parse_elems`'s own `const u8*` parameter, 1 instance).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b72`, 96 findings, `src/ap/wpa_auth_ft.c#part2of3`, lines ~2155-4501: FT GTK/IGTK/BIGTK subelement builders, RIC request/response processing, `wpa_sm_write_assoc_resp_ies`, `wpa_ft_process_auth_req`/`wpa_ft_validate_reassoc`, FT-over-DS action frames, and the RRB (R0KH/R1KH) pull/push/seq message handlers)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances, 2 functions): ARR00-C "pointer arithmetic goes N elements past the end of array X[1]" misfires on a plain, non-array pointer parameter whose only prior use is a byte-index expression (`rpos[0]`/`rpos[1]`, `data[1]`) — the rule infers a bogus 1-element array bound from the indexing syntax itself, not from any real declaration.** `rpos`/`data` are declared as ordinary `const u8 *`/`u8 *` parameters into a much larger wire buffer (bounds already enforced by an earlier `len` check, e.g. `wpa_ft_action_rx`'s `if (len < 14) return -1;` at `:3716` covers all of `data+2`/`data+8`/`data+14`). `wpa_ft_process_ric:2505,2506`; `wpa_ft_action_rx:3723,3724,3725`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM12-C "leaked: nbuf" false positive when a `realloc()` result is immediately reassigned back into the already-tracked variable (`subelem = nbuf;`) and the *tracked* variable is freed later — extends the `ctrl_iface.c` "aliased into a different tracked name" MEM12 class (documented under `41plus_b9`) with the wrap-and-append shape (IGTK/BIGTK/OCV subelement growth).** `wpa_sm_write_assoc_resp_ies`'s `nbuf = os_realloc(subelem, ...); subelem = nbuf;` pattern (×3, IGTK/BIGTK/OCV growth) is followed by `os_free(subelem)` on every later error path — freeing the same memory sqc still calls "nbuf". 9 instances (`:2662,2678,2694,2703,2741,2837` combined report "Leaked: nbuf" at up to 3x per site).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MSC13-C "value assigned to 'X' is never read" and WIN04-C both misfire on a bare C preprocessor directive line (`#endif`) sitting inside an `if`/`else if` chain, one of sqc's several documented preprocessor-branch-blind CFG confusions.** `wpa_ft_set_key_mgmt`'s `#endif /* CONFIG_FILS */` line (`:3040`) is reported as both a dead assignment to a variable named `'if'` (not a real identifier — sqc parsed the enclosing `else if` token as an lvalue) and as a function-pointer-without-encryption WIN04-C hit. Same root cause as the already-documented DCL40-C/MSC17-C/MSC37-C preprocessor-branch-blind family, now hitting MSC13-C+WIN04-C together on the exact same line.
- **Macro-argument-token misattribution, EXP33-C, extends the PRE00-C/PRE12-C "identifier-only macro parameter, never evaluated" category-error family to a non-PRE rule.** The file's `RRB_GET(type, field, ...)`/`RRB_GET_OPTIONAL(type, field, ...)` macros token-paste `field` into `f_##field`/`f_##field_len` — the *bare* `field` name passed at the call site (`pairwise`, `expires_in`, `session_timeout`) is never itself read there, only pasted. sqc treats the bare macro-argument token as a read of the like-named local `int` variable (which really is declared, and really is uninitialized at that point, but isn't touched by this statement), reporting "used uninitialized" on the *macro invocation line* itself. 3 instances, one file (`wpa_ft_rrb_rx_r1:4208,4227,4256` for `pairwise`/`expires_in`/`session_timeout`).
- **MSC13-C "value never read"/"declared but never used" macro-blindness extends to output-parameter macros: an `f_##field_len` set only via `&f_##field_len` inside the `RRB_GET*` macro expansion (address-of, so a real compiler would never warn) but whose value the surrounding code genuinely never reads afterward is reported as "declared but never used" — technically wrong (it IS referenced, as a macro output-arg) but the deeper "value discarded" observation is accurate.** 6 instances across 2 functions (`wpa_ft_rrb_rx_r1:4125`×2 [`f_r1kh_id_len`,`f_s1kh_id_len`],`4128,4129,4131`; `wpa_ft_rrb_rx_seq:4422`).
- **MSC13-C "dead assignment" false positive on an error-code *sentinel* (`ret = -2;`/`ret = -1;`) staged immediately before a `RRB_GET*`/`RRB_GET_AUTH` macro call whose internal `goto out;` on failure is the only path that reads it — sqc doesn't see the macro's embedded goto consuming the value, so it calls the staging assignment dead even though overwriting it (on the success path) is deliberate, not accidental.** `wpa_ft_rrb_rx_r1:4207` (`ret = -2;` before `RRB_GET(FT_RRB_PAIRWISE...)`), `wpa_ft_rrb_rx_resp:4343` (`ret = -1;` at declaration, read via `return ret;` if the very next `RRB_GET_AUTH(FT_RRB_NONCE...)` fails).
- Reconfirms in this batch: the `pos`/`end` wire-buffer-builder ARR36-C/ARR00-C triple-misfire family (`:2419,2450,2737`); the `sizeof(*uninitialized_ptr)` non-evaluating-context EXP33-C class (`rdie:2419,2497`; `tspec:2443`; `frame:3759,3850`); the WPS/RRB-macro output-param EXP33-C class extended wholesale to `RRB_GET`/`RRB_GET_AUTH`/`RRB_GET_OPTIONAL` (18+ instances: `:3973,3981,3996,4037,4038,4041,4053,4069,4140,4143,4202,4209,4214,4247,4249,4252,4254,4258,4352,4432,4433`); the DCL22-C no-signal/setjmp-context class (`pos:3834`); the MSC01-C no-final-else guard-clause class (`:3680`); the MSC07-C goto-target-reached-by-earlier-goto class (`pmk_r1_derived::3273`); the DCL37-C block-scope-local-misclassified-as-file-scope class (`_ftie:2748,2756,2762`); the MEM33-C "flexible array struct" rule-engine-bug class on a plain fixed-array struct (`vlan_description->tagged[32]`, `:3108`) and the sibling ARR01-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-is-correct class (`:3110`); the MSC41-C hardcoded-secret misfire on a debug msgtype string literal (`"pull request":3995`, `"seq":4429,4430`); DCL13-C dispatch-contract-adjacent plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TPs (14 instances: `sm`/`wpa_auth`/`end`/`parse` params never mutated, none bound to a vtable/eloop-callback typedef — `:2155,2193,2202,2297,2358,2407,2408,2841,2855,2868,3016,3057,3700,3826`); Closest CERT rule: ARR38-C (or ARR00-C, "guarantee that library functions do not form invalid pointers"). `wpa_auth_ft.c:2419-2430`. `upstream_present: unknown` (no separate upstream tracking checkout available in this environment).

## Confirmed/reinforced patterns (from batch `41plus_b69`, 150 findings, `src/p2p/p2p.c#part2of3`, lines ~3733-6265: P2P scan/action-frame callbacks, presence req/resp, WFD IE setters, DIRA/pairing helpers)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances, one file): MEM30-C "reassign-then-check" extends the existing p2p_sd.c:450 precedent to a whole family of WFD setter functions.** `p2p_set_wfd_dev_info`/`_r2_dev_info`/`_assoc_bssid`/`_coupled_sink_info` all do `wpabuf_free(p2p->field); if (elem) { p2p->field = wpabuf_dup(elem); if (p2p->field == NULL) return -1; } else p2p->field = NULL;` — sqc flags the `if (p2p->field == NULL)` check as a use-after-free access of the just-freed pointer, missing the intervening unconditional reassignment. `p2p.c:5495,5509,5523,5538`.
- **DCL13-C "plain read-only accessor, never forwarded to non-const call" clarification reconfirmed at high volume (10 instances) alongside the dispatch-contract FP family in the same file** — `p2p_scan_ie_buf_len`, `p2p_get_listen_channel`, `p2p_in_progress`, `p2p_update_wfd_ie_groups` (static internal helper), `p2p_dbg`/`p2p_info`/`p2p_err`, `is_p2p_6ghz_capable`, `p2p_wfd_enabled` (#ifdef-stub shape), `is_p2p_allow_6ghz`, `p2p_validate_dira`'s `dev` param — none of these forward the flagged pointer to a call requiring non-const, so all are genuine (low-severity) TPs, don't blanket-FP just because the file also hosts eloop-callback/forwarding-to-non-const DCL13 FPs. `p2p.c:3826,5114,5390,5412,5565,5581,5597,5964,5970,6063`.
- **DCL13-C "premise is simply false" (function DOES modify the flagged param) reconfirmed 3x in one file, extends the gas_query.c:803/config.c-setter class to direct field writes and to a field-of-a-dereferenced-alias write.** `p2p_set_own_freq_preference` writes `p2p->own_freq_preference = freq` (`:5341`); `p2p_config_sae_password` writes via `os_memset(p2p->dev_sae_password, ...)` (`:6265`); `p2p_derive_nonce_tag` writes through `dev_ik = &p2p->pairing_info->dev_ik; dev_ik->dira_nonce_len = ...` — an aliased-pointer write one level removed from the param itself (`:6005`).
- **DCL13-C "forwarded to a plain (non-vtable) function requiring non-const" extends the eloop/vtable-dispatch forwarding class to ordinary internal helper calls.** `p2p_get_peer_found`'s `p2p` is forwarded to `p2p_get_device(struct p2p_data *p2p, const u8 *addr)`, which itself takes non-const `p2p` — making the caller's param const would fail to compile even though `p2p_get_device` never modifies it. `p2p.c:5341` region — same root cause independently reconfirmed via `p2p_get_dik_id`→`p2p_get_device`.
- **API00-C internal-API-no-NULL-check FP class extended to a config-sourced integer-overflow variant (not just NULL checks).** `p2p_set_pref_chan`'s `num_pref_chan * sizeof(struct p2p_channel)` multiplication (feeding `os_memdup`) is flagged for missing overflow validation, but `num_pref_chan` is sourced from local wpa_supplicant config (`wpa_s->conf->num_p2p_pref_chan`), not attacker/network-controlled data — same trust-boundary reasoning as the NULL-check API00 FP class, just applied to the overflow sub-check. `p2p.c:5150`.
- **NEW, batch-local (3 instances, exactly at the 3x threshold): ERR33-C "vsnprintf return value ignored" is a genuine (very low severity) TP in hostap's `p2p_dbg`/`p2p_info`/`p2p_err` debug-log wrappers — distinct from the confirmed `wpabuf.c:309` FP (checked two lines later) because here the return value is truly never consulted anywhere in the function.** `vsnprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), fmt, ap); buf[sizeof(buf)-1] = '\0';` — the manual null-termination makes any *overflow* impossible regardless of the return value, so the only real gap is losing truncation/encoding-error awareness in the debug log; low value but not factually wrong like the wpabuf.c case. `p2p.c:5574,5590,5606`. Watch for the same wrapper shape (`wpa_printf`-style debug helpers) elsewhere before deciding whether to generalize.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b94`, 91 findings, `src/common/ieee802_11_common.c#part2of2`, lines 2680-4030: Multi-AP IE, country/global operating-class tables, 6 GHz PSC/sec-channel helpers, BSS-transition candidate-list parsing, EXT-capab/RSNXE helpers, EDMG encode, op-class-to-bandwidth/width switches, Multi-Link Element defrag, Basic MLE EML-capa/link-id getters, NSS/channel-width capability parsing)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (13 instances, one switch-heavy function pair): MSC17-C fallthrough misfires on stacked/grouped `case` labels that share one body with zero code between the labels themselves.** `op_class_to_bandwidth()`/`op_class_to_ch_width()`'s `case 81: case 82: return 20;`-shaped groups (`:3327,3332,3337,3342,3345,3348,3363,3390,3395,3400,3405,3408,3411`) are the standard, universally-idiomatic "multiple case values share one body" C pattern — there is no statement between the stacked labels for control to "fall through" past, so the rule's fallthrough concern (a case body with real code that's missing a terminator) doesn't apply at all. Distinct from the existing `#ifdef`-intervening-case MSC17-C FP class (different root cause: here nothing intervenes, the labels are just adjacent).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): ARR37-C/DCL30-C "non-array pointer"/"local automatic storage" misfires on a pointer walking a file-scope `static const` table via `op++`/return.** `get_oper_class()`'s `op = &global_op_class[0]; ... op++; ... return op;` (`:2956,2961`) — `op` is genuinely initialized from `&`(file-scope array)`[0]`, so `op++` is ordinary array-pointer arithmetic (not a "non-array pointer"), and the returned `op` points into a `static const` table that outlives the call (not automatic storage) — same "local pointer *variable* vs. local *storage*" confusion as the existing `comeback_token.c`/DCL30-C entry, now paired with an ARR37-C misfire on the same root cause.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, category error): ARR36-C "pointer subtraction between different arrays" misfires on a plain scalar `u8`/`int` subtraction with no pointers involved at all.** `get_vht_operation_channel_width()`'s `abs(seg1 - seg0)` (`:3886`) and `get_6ghz_operation_channel_width()`'s `abs(seg1 - seg0)` (`:3926`) — `seg0`/`seg1` are plain `u8` locals copied out of struct fields, not pointers; the rule appears to trigger on any subtraction of two identifiers it has seen associated with buffer-like structs, without checking the actual operand type.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): FLP02-C "floating-point equality" misfires on plain integer bitwise-equality checks with zero floating-point types in scope.** `center_idx_to_bw_6ghz()`'s `(idx & 0x1f) == 0xf` and `(idx & 0x1f) == 0x1f` (`:3016,3019`) — `idx` is `u8`, no `float`/`double` anywhere in the function. Factually wrong rule trigger, not a judgment call.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP40-C "pointer to const assigned to non-const pointer without cast" misfires on a same-constness pointer initialization.** `add_multi_ap_ie(u8 *buf, ...)`'s `u8 *pos = buf;` (`:2772`) — both `pos` and `buf` are plain non-const `u8 *`; no `const` is involved on either side. The rule's own message duplicates the RHS as if reformatting a `*pos = buf` write that doesn't exist in source (it's a declaration-with-initializer).
- **NEW, batch-local: API09-C "returns signed type but accumulates size values" category error.** `ieee802_11_defrag_mle_subelem()` (`:3535`) returns `num_frag_subelems`, a fragment *count* (documented "Returns: Number of Fragment subelements parsed"), not the accumulated `subelem_len` size value (that's written through the separate `*defrag_len` out-param) — the rule conflates the function's two distinct size_t/ssize_t-typed locals. Only 1 instance so far.

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances): ERR33-C/MEM04-C/MEM06-C/EXP05-C/ERR00-C pile-on on a single already-checked, exactly-sized, non-sensitive `malloc()` — extends several existing single-rule FP classes into a combined 5-rule misfire on one call site.** `hostapd_cli_open_connection`'s `cfile = malloc(flen); if (cfile == NULL) return NULL;` (`:129`) is checked on the very next line (ERR33-C/ERR00-C wrong), `flen` is provably `>= 2` (MEM04-C wrong), `cfile` only ever holds a directory/socket path (MEM06-C "sensitive data" wrong), and the paired `snprintf(cfile, flen, "%s/%s", ctrl_iface_dir, ifname)` (`:132`) has no actual cast in source at all (EXP05-C wrong) while being sized to exactly fit its output (ERR33-C/STR03-C wrong again, truncation is impossible by construction) — 8 total misfires on 2 adjacent lines.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): MEM12-C "leaked: ctrl_conn" fires on return paths that occur *before* the function has touched `ctrl_conn` at all.** `hostapd_cli_open_connection`'s malloc-failure return (`:131`) and client_socket_dir-`access()`-failure return (`:138`) both precede the `ctrl_conn = wpa_ctrl_open2(...)` assignment (`:141`) — there is nothing to leak on either path. Distinct from the same function's final `return ctrl_conn;` (`:143`), which is the standard ownership-transfer-on-return MEM12-C FP (the static global *is* the return value).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP34-C "does not check for NULL" is wrong when NULL is an explicitly-supported sentinel value for the callee.** `wpa_ctrl_open2(cfile, client_socket_dir)` (`:141`) — `client_socket_dir` defaults to (and can remain) NULL, and `wpa_ctrl_open()` itself calls `wpa_ctrl_open2(ctrl_path, NULL)` (`common/wpa_ctrl.c:90`), proving NULL is a first-class supported argument, not an unguarded hazard.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (13 instances): ERR33-C/STR03-C unchecked `snprintf()` building an hostapd command string from free-form, user-typed CLI `argv` text into a fixed-but-not-exactly-sized buffer is a genuine (low-severity) TP — first explicit verdict for this recurring shape.** `hostapd_cli_cmd_sta/_new_sta/_sa_query/_wps_pin/_wps_ap_pin/_wps_config`'s `snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "CMD %s ...", argv[N], ...)` calls (`:340,342,371,437,453,456,459,608,611,614,658,661,664`) never check the return value or use `os_snprintf_error()`, and the buffer (64-256 bytes) is not mathematically proven to fit arbitrary user-typed argv content (unlike the `os_snprintf_error()`-guarded siblings elsewhere in the same file, or provably-bounded cases below) — low real-world severity (local/admin CLI, not network-facing) but a real gap per rule text. **Contrast (FP):** `hostapd_cli_open_connection:132` (`flen` computed to exactly match the snprintf's output length) and `hostapd_cli_cmd_all_sta`'s `"STA-NEXT %s"` into `cmd[64]` (`:790`, `addr` is itself bounded to `addr_len=32` via `os_strlcpy` inside `wpa_ctrl_command_sta`) — both provably cannot truncate. Use this exact/provably-bounded-vs-generically-sized distinction to adjudicate any further "unchecked snprintf into a fixed CLI-command buffer" finding in this file or `wpa_cli.c`.
- **NEW: DCL13-C "plain internal helper, read-only param" TP exception (established in b84 for `print_cmd_help`) extends to `hostapd_cli_action_process`.** Not itself registered as a callback (only called from the pinned-signature `hostapd_cli_action_cb`); `msg` is genuinely never modified and only forwarded to `cli_event(const char *)`. Genuine if low-value TP. `:308`.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b88`, 122 findings, `src/crypto/crypto_wolfssl.c#part2of2`, lines ~1786-3817: EC point/key wrappers, ECDH, CSR, RSA-OAEP wolfSSL backend)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances): EXP05-C "cast away const" is a genuine TP when the cast bridges into a lazy-init/normalization helper that mutates the object in place, distinct from the existing read-only-overlay FP class.** `crypto_ec_point_to_bin`'s `ecc_point *p = (ecc_point *) point;` (`:1864`) feeds `ecc_map(p, ...)`, which converts a projective point to affine coordinates **in place** — a real write through the cast-away-const `point` parameter. `crypto_ec_key_debug_print`'s `(struct crypto_ec_key *) key` casts (`:2772,2775`) bridge into `crypto_ec_key_get_subject_public_key`/`_get_ecprivate_key`, both of which can call `crypto_ec_key_gen_public_key()` (lazy public-key derivation, `wc_ecc_make_pub_ex`) when the key is private-only — again a real mutation of the nominally-const object. Distinguish from the read-only overlay FP (e.g. `:1857,2013,2045,2061,2068,2077,2722,3095,3108` this same batch) by checking whether the callee chain can trigger a lazy-normalization/lazy-keygen side effect, not just whether the immediate callee's parameter is non-const.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): EXP05-C "cast away const" fires on a parameter that was never const-qualified in the first place — a straightforward tool factual error, not a judgment call.** `crypto_ec_point_add`'s output parameter `c` (`struct crypto_ec_point *c`, no const) is flagged as "cast away const" at both `(ecc_point *) c` sites (`:1985,1992`) — there is no const to cast away. Always verify the flagged variable's actual declared type before trusting an EXP05-C message.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, extends the `p2p_invitation.c` precedent to 3x/Confirmed tier): ENV01-C "fixed-size buffer may be used with environment variable" fires with zero `getenv`/environment code anywhere in the file.** `crypto_ec_point_debug_print`'s `u8 x[ECC_MAXSIZE]`/`y[ECC_MAXSIZE]` (`:2824,2825`) and `crypto_ec_key_verify_signature_r_s`/`crypto_ec_key_get_private_key`'s fixed crypto buffers (`:2891,2972,2976,2978`) are plain stack scratch buffers for EC coordinate/signature bytes — no environment-variable interaction exists in this file at all. Promote to a real rule-logic bug (fires on any fixed-size local array regardless of context), not a heuristic misfire specific to one codebase shape.
- **NEW: DCL13-C "forwarding to a mutator" FP family extends to a lazy-RNG-init helper call, distinct from the vtable/eloop/config-table shapes already documented.** `crypto_csr_sign`'s `key` (`:2970`) is flagged as an unmodified/const-eligible pointer, but the function calls `crypto_ec_key_init_rng(key)`, which lazily writes `key->rng` the first time it's needed — DCL13 missed the mutation because it happens inside a forwarded call, not a direct field write. Contrast with `crypto_ec_key_verify_signature`'s `key` (`:2564`), which never calls the RNG-init helper and is genuinely read-only (TP for const).
- **DCL13-C missed a direct struct-field write through the parameter itself (not an alias) — reconfirms the `ctrl_iface.c:1938`/`p2p_invitation.c:129` "tool miss" family with a new sub-shape (writing into a nested union/struct field via `os_memcpy`).** `crypto_csr_set_name`'s `csr` (`:3335`) is flagged as const-eligible, but the function writes through it directly: `os_memcpy(dest, name, name_len); dest[name_len] = '\0';` where `dest` is a pointer into `csr->req.c.subject.*`.
- **DCL13-C missed a mutation performed via a cast-alias local pointer, not just a plain alias — a stricter variant of the existing "aliased local pointer" miss family.** `crypto_ec_point_invert`'s `p` (`:2019`) is flagged as const-eligible, but the function does `ecc_point *point = (ecc_point *) p; mp_sub(&e->prime, point->y, point->y);` — `point->y` is genuinely written through the cast alias of `p`.
- **MSC07-C goto-label-blindness family extends to `switch`/`case` labels, not just `goto` targets.** `crypto_csr_init_type`'s `case cert_type_none:` (`:3253`), sitting immediately after the preceding case's `break;`, is flagged as unreachable dead code — it's a valid switch-dispatch jump target reached whenever `csr->type == cert_type_none`, not something "fallen into."
- **EXP43-C non-restrict-parameter FP reconfirmed on a different bignum function.** `mp_addmod(y2, &e->a, &e->prime, y2)`/`mp_addmod(y2, &e->b, &e->prime, y2)` (`:2046,2048`) alias their output with the first input on purpose (accumulator idiom `y2 += a mod prime`); `mp_addmod`'s parameters are plain `mp_int*`, no `restrict` — same non-restrict-parameter FP shape as the existing `aes_128_eax_encrypt` precedent (`16-40_b1`), now confirmed on a 2nd, unrelated function.
- **NEW: MEM03-C "sensitive buffer not cleared before exit" is a category error when the buffer IS the function's own return value.** `crypto_ecdh_set_peerkey`'s `secret` (`:2239`) is the heap-allocated ECDH shared secret being handed back to the caller for its own lifetime management — clearing it before `return secret;` would destroy the value the function exists to produce. Distinguish from a genuine MEM03 case (a local scratch copy of sensitive material that outlives its need and is never zeroed before the function's *actual* exit).
- **MEM30-C/MEM31-C mutually-exclusive-early-return-branch FP reconfirmed 2x in `os_free`-based (not just `wpabuf_free`) cleanup code, extending the `wnm_ap.c`/`crypto_openssl.c` precedent.** `crypto_ec_key_get_public_key`'s `os_free(der)` (`:2959` success path vs `:2963` fail: label) and `crypto_ec_key_set_pub_point`'s `os_free(buf)` (`:3126` vs `:3130`) are each reached by mutually exclusive control flow (the fail: free only executes via an earlier `goto fail` that jumps *over* the success-path free).
- **MEM31-C false double-free extends to the `os_free(NULL)`-is-safe family via an explicit NULL-out, not just a NULL-safe wrapper.** `crypto_rsa_key_read`'s `key_pem` (`:3739`) is explicitly set to NULL right after its early free (`:3713-3714`) on the success path, making the later `os_free(key_pem)` in `fail:` a safe no-op — same root cause as the existing `wpabuf_clear_free()`-is-NULL-safe entry, now shown for the plain `os_free()` + explicit-NULL-out idiom.
- **API00-C "does not validate pointer parameter" factually contradicted by the function's own code — not just a judgment call about internal-only reachability.** `crypto_ec_key_sign` (`:2518`) is flagged for not validating `key`, but its first statement is `if (!key || !key->eckey || !data || len == 0) { ...; goto fail; }`. Always check the actual function body before trusting this rule's "does not validate" claim.
- Reconfirms the internal-only-API family (API00-C/EXP34-C: internal opaque handles like `struct crypto_ec *e`, `struct crypto_ecdh *ecdh` are always valid post-init and never externally nullable) at very high density — 16 API00-C + 6 of 7 EXP34-C findings this batch, all FP.
- Reconfirms the read-only-cast-away-const EXP34-C^H^H EXP05-C FP family (10+ instances: `:1857,2013,2045,2047,2061,2068,2077,2722,3095,3108`) and the pure-getter EXP30-C FP family (9/9 findings this batch, all `wpabuf_head/len/mhead/size`, `mp_unsigned_bin_size`, `wc_RsaEncryptSize`).
- **FN found: resource leak + stale-buffer-use on an error path inside an x509-fallback helper.** `read_rsa_key_from_x509()`'s `wc_AllocDer(key_der, der_key_sz, ...)` (`:3646`) succeeds, but if the immediately following `wc_GetPubKeyDerFromCert(&cert, (*key_der)->buffer, &(*key_der)->length)` (`:3652`) fails, control reaches `fail:` (`:3659`), which frees only `cert`/`cert_der` — never `*key_der`. The allocated `DerBuffer` leaks, and worse, the caller `crypto_rsa_key_read()` only checks `if (!key_der)` to detect failure, so it will proceed to RSA-decode the never-actually-filled buffer as if it were valid key material.
- **NEW FN, real off-by-one argument-count bug:** `hostapd_cli_cmd_wps_config`'s guard checks `if (argc < 1)` (`:634`) but the error message and downstream logic require **two** arguments (`ssid` + at least one more); when invoked with exactly `argc == 1`, execution falls through to the final `else` branch (`:663-665`) and reads `argv[1]`, which is out of bounds (`argv[argc]` is the NULL sentinel) — a NULL/OOB pointer passed as a `%s` vararg to `snprintf`. Not flagged by sqc (ARR30-C/EXP34-C didn't catch the argc/argv-index mismatch). Closest rule: EXP34-C (or ARR38-C for the OOB index). `hostapd_cli.c:634,664`. `upstream_present: unknown` (no separate upstream tracking checkout available in this environment).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b78`, 150 findings, `src/common/dpp.c#part2of3`, lines ~2767-4983: connector timestamp/expiry parsing, config-object/connection-status-result RX/build (AES-SIV wrap/unwrap), configurator/bootstrap-info keygen and CRUD, `dpp_peer_intro`)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (26 instances, one file): MSC41-C "hard-coded sensitive information" extends from security-substring-matched debug labels to *any* plain descriptive string passed to `dpp_auth_fail(auth, txt)`.** `dpp_auth_fail()` (`:42`) just does `wpa_msg(auth->msg_ctx, MSG_INFO, DPP_EVENT_FAIL "%s", txt)` — `txt` is a human-readable protocol-error description (`"JSON root is not an object"`, `"Unsupported wi-fi_tech value"`, `"Missing or invalid required Wrapped Data attribute"`, etc.), not secret material, and most of these strings don't even contain a security-sounding substring (PASSWORD/KEY/PIN/AUTH) — broader misfire than the previously-documented substring-pattern-match class. 26 call sites (`:3235,3247,3262,3276,3343,3395,3413,3429,3434,3442,3458,3483,3494,3514,3536,3552,3601,3624,3640,3645,3655,3760,3783,3799,3804,3814`).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: ARR30-C cross-function buffer-size/decl-site conflation, `addr[N]` variant.** 8 findings (`:3611,3614,3698,3700,3770,3773,3922,3924`) all cite "Buffer 'addr' with size 1 (allocated at line 3988)" — but line 3988 (`const u8 *addr[1];`) is a *different function's* (`dpp_configurator_gen_kid`) unrelated same-named local array. Every flagged call site is actually in a function declaring `const u8 *addr[2]` (`dpp_conf_result_rx`, `dpp_conn_status_result_rx`, `dpp_build_conf_result`, `dpp_build_conn_status_result`), where `addr[1] = ...` is a valid in-bounds write/read. Same root-cause family as the `hostapd_cli.c` `argv`-conflation entry (`41plus_b83`) — same-named locals across different functions get their size/decl-site cross-attributed.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances): ARR39-C "double scaling" misfires on plain integer arithmetic that only happens to include a `sizeof`-free byte-count macro (`AES_BLOCK_SIZE`).** `wrapped_data_len - AES_BLOCK_SIZE` (`:3401,3617,3776`) and `4 + clear_len + AES_BLOCK_SIZE` (`:3678,3900`) are ordinary `u16`/`size_t` arithmetic with **no pointer operand at all** — extends the existing "ARR39-C pure integer sum, no pointer" class to subtraction and to a named byte-count constant instead of a literal.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): STR34-C "sign extension" misfires on a `char **` out-param pointer assignment, not a char value at all.** `*channel_list = os_strdup(token->string);` (`:3754,3836`, `channel_list` declared `char **`) — the rule appears to pattern-match "assignment through `*ptr` where `ptr`'s base type is char-ish" without checking that the assigned value is itself a pointer (`char *`), not a narrow character needing a cast.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM12-C "leaked" resources are actually freed via straight-line fall-through into a shared cleanup label, not just via `goto`.** `dpp_configurator_add`'s success path never jumps anywhere — it falls straight through into the `fail:` label immediately below the last statement, which unconditionally runs `bin_clear_free(privkey, ...); bin_clear_free(pp_key, ...);` (`:4923`). This is the same goto/label-blindness root cause as the confirmed MSC07-C/MSC37-C class, now demonstrated on a resource-leak rule rather than a control-flow rule.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM30-C/MEM31-C free-then-reassign FP class (established `41plus_b74` for `os_free()`+`os_strdup()`) extends to `os_free()`+`get_param()`.** `dpp_configurator_add`'s `curve` (`:4881` freed inside `if (curve) {...}`, then unconditionally reassigned via a fresh `curve = get_param(cmd, " curve=")` at `:4884` before the shared `fail:`'s final `os_free(curve)` at `:4917`) — the two frees target two different allocations, not a double free.

the `sizeof(*uninitialized_ptr)` non-evaluating-context EXP33-C class (`conf:4021`, `bi:4520`); the DCL30-C heap-vs-stack misfire extended to `os_zalloc`-backed structs returned by value (`conf:4048`) and to `dl_list_for_each`-iterated persistent-list elements returned or written through an out-param (`bi:4448,4467,4585,4731,4739,4760`; `json:3879` via `wpabuf_alloc`; `own_root:4214` via `json_parse`); the ARR01-C `sizeof(ptr->fixed_array_member)`/`sizeof(*ptr)`-is-correct class (`conf->kid_hash:4009`, `*intro:4235,4369`); the API00-C internal-only-API no-NULL-check FP class (16+ instances: `hdr:3585,3736`; ## Batch 41plus_b90 (src/tls/libtommath.c#part2of2, 120 findings, bundled third-party bignum lib)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (26 instances): EXP43-C "same pointer for output/input" no-restrict FP class extends wholesale to libtommath's internal bignum helpers** (`mp_sqr`, `mp_mul`, `mp_mul_2`, `mp_add`, `mp_sub`, `mp_div`, `mp_div_2d`, `s_mp_add`, `s_mp_sub`, `mp_mod_2d`, `s_mp_mul_digs`, `s_mp_mul_high_digs`, `fast_s_mp_mul_high_digs`). Grepping the whole file confirms zero `restrict` uses anywhere (`libtommath.c`, whole file) — every one of these calls aliases in-place (`mp_sqr(&res,&res)` etc.) by design, which is the library's normal idiom.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances): DCL31-C "called without prior declaration" fires on `redux(...)`, a local function-pointer variable** (`int (*redux)(mp_int*,mp_int*,mp_int*);` / `...,mp_digit);`), not an undeclared function — same function-pointer-variable-misread shape as the existing DCL31-C entry (`:169`), new instance class.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (1 instance): MSC13-C "dead assignment" misfires on a function-pointer variable (`redux = fast_mp_montgomery_reduce;`) that IS read multiple times afterward via call syntax (`redux(&res, P, mp)`)** — the tool doesn't recognize `ptr(...)` invocation as a read of `ptr`. Same root cause family as the DCL31-C function-pointer-variable blindness above; watch for recurrence.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (8 instances): ARR00-C/EXP33-C misfire on a modular-exponentiation windowing table (`mp_int M[...]`) across two sibling functions (`mp_exptmod_slow`-style and the montgomery-fast variant).** Every flagged M[] read/init is preceded, in the same function, by an `mp_init`/`mp_copy`/`mp_mod`/`mp_mul` that populates exactly that index before use (or, for the cleanup-loop hits at the `LBL_M` label, matches exactly the range that was `mp_init`'d earlier) — a per-index initialization-tracking miss on a table built incrementally with computed indices (`M[1<<(winsize-1)]`, `M[x-1]`→`M[x]`), not a real defect.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): ARR00-C/EXP33-C misfire on `mp_digit W[MP_WARRAY]`/`mp_word W[MP_WARRAY]` filled via pointer-alias loops** (`register mp_word *_W = W; ... *_W++ = ...;` copy-then-zero-fill) immediately before the flagged read — same "pointer-alias write not tracked as initialization" root cause as the existing t0..t3 EXP33-C/MSC13-C entry (`:804-816`), new instance.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (10 instances, 5 line-pairs): DCL37-C "_W" splits exactly along the established scope-vs-reserved-word axis.** `register mp_word _W;`/`register mp_word *_W;` are block-scope locals, so the "File-scope identifier" framing is FP (block-scope-misclassified-as-file-scope class, `:2601-2604`/`:5342` precedent) — but "_W" is underscore+uppercase, reserved in ALL scopes per C 7.1.3, so the paired "Reserved identifier '_W' should not be used" finding on the same line is TP (matches the `_INT`/`_STR` precedent, `:5229`).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (1 instance): FIO50-C fires on `u = (mp_digit)(r >> DIGIT_BIT);`**, plain integer arithmetic with zero I/O/FILE* anywhere nearby — reconfirms the existing FIO50-C-plain-arithmetic rule bug (`:446-449`) in a new file.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (1 instance): MEM33-C "flexible array structure" fires on `*_W++ = *tmpx++;`**, a scalar mp_digit→mp_word pointer-dereference copy with no struct/FAM involved at all — extends the existing MEM33-C-misapplied-to-plain-deref class (`:496`,`:1277`) to a pointer-increment idiom.
- **NEW (1 instance, watch for recurrence): DCL30-C "local variable assigned through pointer parameter — address will be invalid when function returns" is a flat category error on `*tmpc++ = u;`** — this stores u's *value* through an already-heap-owned dest pointer (`c->dp`); no address of any local is returned, stored, or escapes anywhere. Not the usual "heap vs. stack" DCL30 misfire shape — a distinct, more basic false-positive.
- **Reconfirms/extends `5432`'s "genuinely correct per rule text" INT13-C/INT10-C TP class (not the wrong-type FP class) to more instances in this file:** `ix&1`/`a->dp[ix>>1]` (INT13-C, `ix` is truly `int`), `mp_count_bits(b) % DIGIT_BIT` and `size % MP_PREC` (INT10-C, both truly signed `int` operands) — literal rule matches, graded TP (low severity/idiomatic in a mature bignum lib, not a tool misfire).
- **NEW (4 instances, not yet 3x-generalized beyond bignum bit-width code): INT34-C shift-validation and INT35-C `sizeof(...)*CHAR_BIT`-precision fire on `winsize`/`DIGIT_BIT`/`CHAR_BIT`-derived shifts and comba-cutoff comparisons.** `winsize` is bounded to `[2,8]` by an explicit lookup-table `if`/`else if` chain in the same function (rule doesn't see the same-function algorithmic bound, extends the `:376-379` "earlier guard" INT34-C family); the `sizeof(mp_word)*CHAR_BIT` uses are a conservative compile-time fast-path cutoff heuristic, not a real precision-dependent computation — graded TP-low (literal rule match, per the INT13-C "genuinely correct" precedent) rather than FP, since unlike INT34-C there's no visible same-function bound making it definitively safe by construction.
