## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b87`, 150 findings, `src/crypto/crypto_wolfssl.c` part1of2)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances): MEM30-C/MEM31-C "double-free" misfire on the `wc_FreeXxx(ptr); os_free(ptr);` container-vs-internal-state idiom.** wolfSSL's `wc_FreeRng`/`wc_ecc_free`/`wc_FreeDhKey` free only the *internal* buffers/state embedded inside the struct; the immediately-following `os_free(ptr)` frees the *container* struct itself — two disjoint memory regions, not a double free of the same allocation. Seen in `wc_rng_deinit` (`:111-112`), `ecc_key_deinit` (`:149-150`), `crypto_dh_init`'s `done:` (`:1120-1121`), `crypto_dh_derive_secret`'s `done:` (`:1152-1153`). Watch for the same shape with any other `wc_Free*`/`wc_*_free` + `os_free` pairing in other wolfSSL wrapper files.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, extends the existing MSC17-C/DCL40-C preprocessor-branch-blindness family to MEM30-C/MEM31-C): double-free misfire across mutually-exclusive `#ifdef CONFIG_FIPS ... #else ... #endif` branches.** `wc_rng_deinit`'s `#else` `wc_rng_free(rng)` (`:114`) and `ecc_key_deinit`'s `#else` `wc_ecc_key_free(key)` (`:152`) are each flagged as re-freeing a pointer already "freed" by the `#ifdef` branch's frees — but the two branches can never both execute (compile-time exclusive). Compounds with the `wc_FreeXxx+os_free` container-free misfire above in the same two functions.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances): MEM30-C use-after-free misfire extends the existing "mutually-exclusive if/goto/return branches" free-tracking bug from single-branch shapes to `switch`-case granularity.** `crypto_cipher_init`'s inner `switch (key_len) { ... default: os_free(ctx); return NULL; }` (`:803`) free is on a branch that already returns; subsequent same-case-body accesses (`:806,808,810`) are falsely flagged as UAF/double-free of that same `ctx`. Worse, the outer `switch (alg)`'s sibling `CRYPTO_CIPHER_ALG_3DES` case (`:818,819`) — mutually exclusive with the `CRYPTO_CIPHER_ALG_AES` case where the "free" happened — is also flagged, i.e. the bug crosses unrelated outer-switch cases, not just sibling branches of one `if`/`goto`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances): MEM30-C "use-after-free: returning freed pointer" misfire on the `ret = ptr; ptr = NULL; ... done: if (ptr) free(ptr);` ownership-hand-off idiom.** Setting `ptr = NULL` right after `ret = ptr` is precisely what prevents the cleanup label's conditional `if (ptr) free(ptr)` from touching the value now owned by `ret`; sqc doesn't track that the aliased pointer was nulled out before the conditional free runs, and reports `ret`'s return as reading a freed pointer. Seen in `dh5_init` (`:974-988`), `dh5_init_fixed` (`:1024-1032`), `dh5_derive_shared` (`:1056-1060`), `crypto_hash_init` (`:1221-1225`).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances): ARR01-C "sizeof applied to pointer/array parameter which decayed" misapplied to file-scope global const arrays referenced directly, not through any parameter.** `RFC3526_PRIME_1536[]`/`RFC3526_GENERATOR_1536[]` are file-scope `static const` arrays; `sizeof(RFC3526_PRIME_1536)` at their use sites (`dh5_init:961-962`, `dh5_init_fixed:1010-1011,1017`) refers to the array itself with full array type in scope — nothing decayed, no parameter involved at all. Distinct from the existing "member array via `->` retains type" ARR01-C misfire — this is a plain global, not even inside a struct.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (10+ instances): EXP05-C "cast away const" fires on casts of parameters that were never const-qualified in the wrapper's own signature — extends the `41plus_b33` "never-const-to-begin-with" class specifically to output/mutated params of the `crypto_bignum_*`/mp_int wrapper family.** Every `crypto_bignum_{add,mod,exptmod,inverse,sub,addmod,mulmod,sqrmod,rshift}()`'s output parameter (`r`/`d`/`c`, always declared plain non-const `struct crypto_bignum *`) triggers this when cast to `(mp_int *)` for the corresponding `mp_*` call — there is no const to cast away. Paired in the same functions with a *second*, distinct EXP05-C FP class: the `const`-declared input params (`a`/`b`/`m`/`e`) genuinely are cast away from const, but every `mp_*` call site here only reads them (output goes to the separate non-const out-param), so those are the already-established read-only-cast-away-const class instead. The two classes co-occur on almost every line in this cluster (`:1430-1583`) — check which param (const-input vs non-const-output) before citing either.
- Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed: INT13-C "bitwise operator used on signed operand" misidentifies the *shift-count* operand as the operand-of-concern rather than the value being shifted — `pkey[i] = (tmp >> i) | ...` flags signed `i` (the non-negative 0-6 shift count) instead of `tmp` (the value actually being shifted, which is unsigned anyway and thus has no real signed-right-shift hazard) (`des_encrypt`, `:545,546`). 2 instances, one function.
- Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed: FIO50-C "output operation on file stream follows input" fires on a plain local byte variable named `tmp` with zero file I/O anywhere in the function (`des_encrypt`, `:546`) — looks like a cross-function/cross-scope identifier-name conflation bug, same shape as the documented EXP39-C cross-function union conflation, now hitting a stream-tracking rule instead. Only 1 site (2 duplicate findings) so far.
- FN found (1 instance, moderate confidence): `read_rsa_key_from_x509()` (`:3614-3666`) — when the second `wc_GetPubKeyDerFromCert()` call (after `wc_AllocDer`) fails, the `fail:` label frees only `cert`/`cert_der`, never resets or frees the just-allocated `*key_der`. The caller `crypto_rsa_key_read()` only detects extraction failure via `key_der == NULL` (`:3700`), so this specific failure is silently treated as success and an allocated-but-not-populated DER buffer is handed to `wc_Rsa{Public,Private}KeyDecode()` — likely caught by that decode call failing on garbage ASN.1, but the error-handling contract between the two functions is broken. Closest CERT rule: ERR00-C (inconsistent error-handling policy across the two functions).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b89`, 150 findings, `src/tls/libtommath.c#part1of2`, lines 86-2028: vendored LibTomMath 0.41 bignum arithmetic core)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (30+ instances, extends the no-restrict-qualifier EXP43-C FP class to an entire vendored bignum library): EXP43-C "same pointer for output/input" misfires wholesale across `mp_add`/`mp_sub`/`mp_div_2`/`mp_div_2d`/`mp_mul_2d`/`mp_mul_d`/`mp_sqr`.** None of libtommath's `mp_*` functions are `restrict`-qualified anywhere in this file (grep for `restrict` finds zero hits besides an unrelated comment); the library's in-place idiom (`mp_sub(&t, &t, &v)`, `mp_div_2(&u, &u)`, etc.) is a designed-for, internally-safe aliasing case throughout — the single densest EXP43-C misfire cluster seen in the corpus so far.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (10+ instances): INT14-C category error — macro constants and typedef names misattributed as "variables" with mixed bitwise/arithmetic use.** `CHAR_BIT`/`DIGIT_BIT` are `#define`d integer literals and `mp_digit`/`mp_word` are `typedef` names, not variables at all; sqc's INT14-C detector treats any identifier appearing near both a `&`/`<<`/`>>` and a `+`/`-`/`/` in the same statement as a flagged "variable," including type and macro names. Distinct from (and additive to) the already-established "stylistic pedantry mismatch" INT14-C class for genuine variables (`size`, `D`/`d`, `winsize`, `tmp`) doing the standard shift/mask bit-extraction idiom — that sub-class is also confirmed here (8+ instances) but graded separately since the identifier really is a variable, just not a real portability hazard.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances): INT34-C shift-amount-validation misfire wholesale on compile-time-bounded or algorithm-bounded shifts in bignum digit code.** Shifts by `CHAR_BIT*sizeof(mp_digit)-1` / `CHAR_BIT*sizeof(mp_word)-2*DIGIT_BIT` are fixed compile-time constants within the shifted type's own width; shifts by `D`/`d` (`= b % DIGIT_BIT`, guarded `!= 0`) are bounded to `[1, DIGIT_BIT-1]`; shifts by `winsize-1`/`winsize` are bounded to `[1,8]` by an explicit if/else-if chain a few lines earlier (`s_mp_exptmod`, lines 1882-1898). Extends the existing "shift bounded by an earlier guard" INT34-C FP class to constant-width and small-enum-range shapes.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): ARR36-C category error — flags plain dereferenced-VALUE comparisons or plain-int struct-field arithmetic as "pointer comparison/subtraction between different arrays."** `mp_cmp_mag`'s `*tmpa > *tmpb`/`*tmpa < *tmpb` (`:941,945`) compare dereferenced *values*, not the `tmpa`/`tmpb` pointers themselves; `mp_div`'s `n - t` (`:1750,1755,1762`) is plain `int` arithmetic on locals derived from `x.used - 1`/`y.used - 1` — `x.used`/`y.used` are `int` struct fields, not pointers, so there is no array-pointer subtraction anywhere in the flagged statement.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances): MEM33-C "flexible array structure" misapplied where the struct in question (`mp_int`: `int used,alloc,sign; mp_digit *dp;`) has no flexible array member at all** — `dp` is an ordinary pointer field, not `T dp[]`. 3 of the 4 flagged lines aren't even struct assignments (`*tmpb++ = *tmpa++;` / `*bottom++ = *top++;` / `*top-- = *bottom--;`, all plain digit-array copy-loop statements); the 4th (`mp_exch`'s `*a = *b;`) is a real whole-struct shallow-copy swap idiom, intentional and correct since `dp` is meant to be swapped by pointer-value, not deep-copied.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): DCL31-C misfires on calling a local function-pointer VARIABLE, extending the existing `eap_gpsk_common.c` precedent.** `s_mp_exptmod`'s `int (*redux)(mp_int*,mp_int*,mp_int*)` is assigned `mp_reduce`/`mp_reduce_2k_l` earlier in the same function (lines 1932/1937) and then invoked as `redux(...)` (`:1967,1979,2028`) — a function-pointer call, not an implicitly-declared bare function.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances): EXP20-C "==1, function may return >1" is a genuine exact-{0,1}-contract FP, extending the OpenSSL-precedent to a local macro contract.** `mp_iszero(a)`/`mp_isodd(a)`/`mp_iseven(a)` (lines 125-127) are `#define`d to the ternary `(... ? MP_YES : MP_NO)` with `MP_YES==1`/`MP_NO==0` — a provable two-value contract, so `mp_isodd(&A) == 1` etc. is exactly correct usage, not an unsafe boolean-like test.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances): ARR00-C/EXP33-C "uninitialized array/variable" misfires on an array-of-mp_int where each index is initialized by an earlier `for` loop, not tracked per-index by sqc.** `s_mp_exptmod`'s `mp_int M[TAB_SIZE]` has `M[1]` initialized via `mp_init(&M[1])` (line 1908) and `M[1<<(winsize-1) .. (1<<winsize)-1]` initialized via a `for` loop (lines 1912-1921) before any of the flagged reads/writes (`:1918,1962,1976`x2) — sqc's array-of-struct initialization tracking doesn't connect the loop-based per-index `mp_init` calls to later loop-based per-index reads. Also (1 instance) EXP33-C flags `&M[1]` passed to `mp_init()` itself (`:1908`) as "reading from M" — passing an address to an initializer is not a read at all.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): FIO50-C "output operation on file stream follows input" misfires on plain bit-shift statements, extending the existing "FIO50-C fires on non-I/O arithmetic" FP class to the `<</>>` operators specifically.** `mp_mul_2d`'s `*tmpc = ((*tmpc << d) | r) & MP_MASK;` (`:1423`) shifts a digit-array pointer's pointee; no FILE stream, `stdio`, or I/O of any kind is involved anywhere in the function — looks like the same visual-token-conflation root cause already seen for INT14-C misattributing `<<`/`>>`-heavy statements.

- **Reconfirms in this batch:** PRE02-C single-token-negative-literal FP class extended to `MP_LT/MP_MEM/MP_VAL` (`:86,94,95`) and to a function-call-shaped macro body (`s_mp_mul`, `:131` — already atomic, wrapping is a no-op, 2nd file confirming the `aes_i.h` TE0/TD0-table precedent); DCL13-C plain-internal-static-helper genuine-if-low-value TP class (8 instances: `:212`x2,`300`x2,`700,919`x2,`1541` — none of these `mp_cmp*`/`mp_count_bits` helpers are bound to any dispatch contract); MSC13-C `||`-chain-blindness FP class (5 instances: `:1632,1633,1634,1641,1646`) and a *new* sub-shape of MSC13-C dead-store misfire on a single `if/else-if/#ifdef` chain where sqc doesn't see the branches as mutually exclusive (`mp_mul:493,499,515`); MEM10-C ad-hoc-NULL-check stylistic class (`:1038`); INT10-C signed-modulo-operand misfire on provably-nonnegative operands, bounded by an earlier `if (b<=0) return` guard, `mp_count_bits()`'s non-negative return, or (weaker, no explicit local guard but every real call site passes a provably-nonnegative value) `mp_grow`'s `size` parameter (7 instances: `:1057,1264,1402,1587,1592,1732`, `1402` graded slightly lower confidence since `mp_mul_2d` itself has no local `b<0` guard, unlike its `mp_div_2d` sibling). Two low-confidence/still-real findings worth a second look in a future audit pass rather than dismissed outright: INT32-C's "signed subtraction may overflow" on an all-`mp_digit`-(unsigned)-typed expression is a clean category error (`:1773`), but INT33-C's "division without checking for zero" on `tmp /= (mp_word) y.dp[t]` (`:1778`) is graded FP only by trusting the classic Knuth Algorithm D normalization invariant (lines 1732-1743 ensure the divisor's top digit's MSB is set) — flag for re-verification if this division-by-zero shape recurs in a codebase without that specific normalization step.


## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b93`, 150 findings, `src/common/ieee802_11_common.c#part1of2`, lines 1-2687: vendor-IE/MLE/element parsing dispatch tables, HT/VHT/link-profile parsers, WMM/tx-queue config setters, country/op-class-to-frequency tables, `fc2str`/`reason2str`/`status2str` X-macro accessors, MBO/Multi-AP IE builders)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (9 EXP33-C + 7 EXP34-C instances, extends the standing `for_each_element`-macro FP class to its "used uninitialized"/"null deref" shape specifically, not just the PRE-family shape already documented).** `for_each_element`/`for_each_element_id`/`for_each_element_extid` initialize their `elem` loop variable in the macro's own `for(...)` init clause (`elem = (const struct element *) (_data);`) before the loop condition or body ever runs; sqc's macro-expansion blindness misses this init and flags every loop body's first `elem->...` access as a use of an uninitialized/possibly-NULL pointer. Seen at `:283,284` (`ieee802_11_fragments_length`), `:463,464` (`__ieee802_11_parse_elems`), `:1215` (`ieee802_11_ie_count`), `:1228,1229` (`ieee802_11_vendor_ie_concat`), `:2436,2441` (`mb_ies_info_by_ies`), `:2608,2609` (`get_ie`), `:2632,2633` (`get_ie_ext`), `:2646,2647` (`get_vendor_ie`) — one file, 8 different call sites.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (60 instances, one file): MSC17-C "case falls through" misfires wholesale on stacked/grouped case labels sharing one body, extending the existing `#ifdef`-intervening-case MSC17-C FP class to the plain no-`#ifdef` stacked-label shape.** Every one of the five `ieee80211_chan_to_freq_{us,eu,jp,cn,global}()` per-region operating-class tables is written as `case 12: case 32: case 33: if (chan < 1 || chan > 11) return -1; return 2407 + 5 * chan;` — multiple case labels stacked with no code between them, all falling into one shared if/return body that always returns. sqc flags every label but the last in each stack as "falls through" even though there is no code to fall through *into* (the next label immediately follows) and the shared body never falls out the bottom either. `:1797-2044` (60 flagged lines across 5 functions).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM33-C "flexible array struct assignment" misfires on a plain `size_t *` output-param assignment to a struct member's address — no struct copy, no flexible array, at all.** `ieee802_11_parse_mle()`'s `*total_len = &elems->basic_mle_len;` (and the four sibling `probe_req_mle_len`/`reconf_mle_len`/`tdls_mle_len`/`prior_access_mle_len` assignments, `:242,247,252,257,262`) is a scalar `size_t*` write, not an assignment of one `struct ieee802_11_elems` instance into another. Reinforces the already-confirmed `xor_aes_block`/MEM33-C "no struct present at all" rule-engine-bug class (`16-40_b18`/`aes-ccm.c`) with a new sub-shape: taking the address of a struct member and writing it through an unrelated output-pointer parameter, rather than a plain `u32*` XOR.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (unique to this batch, 9 co-fired findings across 3 macro definitions): `C2S`/`R2S`/`S2S`-style "expand to a bare `case x: return #x;`" X-macros cause sqc to misparse the macro's *first invocation* as a self-defining, self-calling function.** `fc2str()`/`reason2str()`/`status2str()` each `#define`+immediately invoke a macro like `#define C2S(x) case x: return #x;` followed on the very next lines by bare invocations `C2S(WLAN_FC_STYPE_ASSOC_REQ)` etc. (no trailing semicolon, by design — it expands to a full `case`+`return` statement). On the *first* invocation line only, sqc emits DCL31-C ("C2S missing explicit return type"), MEM05-C ("recursive function... excessive stack allocation"), MSC04-C ("C2S calls itself directly"), and MSC37-C ("C2S has no return statement") — all four are a single category error: `C2S`/`S2S` are never functions at all, they're macros, and the "recursive self-call" sqc perceives is just the macro's textual name reappearing at each invocation site, not a real call graph edge. `:2192` (C2S), `:2316` (S2S, DCL31-C only observed there). On the macro *definitions* themselves (`:2187,2243,2314`), the already-confirmed X-macro PRE-family disposition holds: PRE00-C/PRE01-C/PRE12-C ("evaluates/parenthesize/multiple-eval") are FP because `x`/`r`/`s` is only ever a case-label target or `#`-stringified (neither is runtime evaluation); PRE05-C is FP because the parameter is always a bare enum-suffix identifier, never itself a macro needing pre-expansion; PRE11-C ("definition ends with `;`") is a genuine TP — the macro body literally is `case x: return #x;`.
- **NEW FN, high-confidence (CWE-125-shaped, closest rule ARR30-C/API00-C): `get_max_nss_capability()` reads past the validated length of an attacker-supplied HE Capabilities element.** `:3761` reads `hecaps->optional[0..3]` (`bw==CHAN_WIDTH_160`) or `optional[4..7]` (`bw==CHAN_WIDTH_80P80`) from `elems->he_capabilities`, but that element is only length-validated at parse time (`:381`) against `HE_CAPABILITIES_ELEM_MIN_LEN==21`, which covers only the mandatory MAC/PHY-capab-info + basic (<=80MHz) MCS map — the optional 160MHz/80+80MHz MCS-map octets (0, 4, or 8 extra bytes) are never guaranteed present, and `elems->he_capabilities_len` is never consulted inside this function at all. `wpa_supplicant/events.c:3487-3497` and `:3553-3560` call `get_max_nss_capability(&resp_elems, ..., bw)` on the AP's own (attacker-controlled) association-response elements, where `bw` is derived via `get_sta_operation_chan_width(ap_cw, sta_cw)` from the AP's *Operation* element (a different, independently-attacker-controlled IE) and the STA's own capability — so a malicious AP can advertise a wide-bandwidth Operation element alongside a minimal 21-byte HE Capabilities element to force a 4-8 byte out-of-bounds read past the parsed IE buffer in wpa_supplicant. `upstream_present: unknown` (no separate upstream tracking checkout available in this environment).
- Reconfirms in this batch (not re-detailed above): ARR01-C `sizeof(*ptr)`/`sizeof(ptr->member)` correct-idiom misapplication (5 instances: `:738,863,2687`, plus the `elems`/`multi_ap` pointer-param shape); MSC01-C switch-has-no-default stylistic-pedantry on intentionally-narrow dispatch tables (2 instances: `:755,909`); MEM10-C ad-hoc-NULL-check stylistic FP (3 instances: `:1212,1783`); ERR07-C/ERR34-C atoi()-immediately-range-checked FP (16 instances across `hostapd_config_wmm_ac`/`hostapd_config_tx_queue`) vs. genuine TP for the one unguarded `atoi()` feeding `i*10+d` with zero downstream check (`hostapd_config_read_int10:1376`, plus its INT32-C sibling findings at `:1385` — INT30-C on the same line is FP, misapplied to a signed not unsigned operand); DCL30-C local-pointer-vs-heap-storage confusion (`buf:1252`, `wpabuf_alloc`-backed); MSC37-C goto/label-blindness extended to `done:`/`out:` labels immediately followed by a return (3 instances: `:453,1004,2552`); DCL37-C double-underscore-prefixed function name genuine TP (`__ieee802_11_parse_elems:453`, matches the `__AKM`/`__must_check` precedent); ARR02-C array-sized-by-its-own-initializer FP (5 instances: `:1759,1763,1770,1774,2485`); API00-C internal-only-API FP (4 instances: `:1187,1196,1256,2656,2680`x2); EXP43-C no-real-aliasing FP (`wpabuf_put_data` into a freshly-allocated distinct buffer, `:1249`); DCL13-C alias-blindness on array params mutated through a derived element pointer (`ac = &wmm_ac_params[num]; ac->aifs = ...`/`queue = &tx_queue[num]`, 2 instances: `:1296,1398`) vs. DCL13-C plain-read-only-helper genuine-if-low-value TP (2 instances: `:2157,2456`).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b86`, 135 findings, `wpa_supplicant/events.c#part2of2`, lines ~4260-7542: MLO link parsing/reconfig, association/disassociation/deauth event handlers, `wpa_supplicant_event`'s central dispatch switch, `wpa_supplicant_event_global`)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances, one file): MSC17-C "case falls through" misfires on an ordinary switch-case label that is directly preceded by a real, unconditional `break;`** — a *third* MSC17-C misfire shape (distinct from the already-confirmed `#ifdef`-intervening-case and stacked-grouped-label shapes). `case EVENT_MICHAEL_MIC_FAILURE:` (`:6621`), `case EVENT_PMKID_CANDIDATE:` (`:6687`), and `case EVENT_TX_STATUS:` (`:6735`) each sit immediately after the *previous* case's own unconditional `break;` with no intervening code at all — there is nothing to fall through. A 4th instance in the same switch, `case EVENT_CH_SWITCH_STARTED:` (`:6886`), is the already-documented plain stacked-label shape (immediately followed by `case EVENT_CH_SWITCH:` sharing one body). All 4 in `wpa_supplicant_event`'s ~700-line dispatch switch — worth checking whether sqc's fallthrough analysis degrades on very large switch statements generally.
- **NEW, batch-local: MSC13-C "dead assignment" misses a read of the same variable on the *next iteration* of an enclosing loop (loop-carried read), reporting the loop-body assignment as dead even though the very next iteration reads it before reassigning again.** `wpas_tid_link_map()`'s `pos += res;` (`:6352`, end of a `for_each_link` loop body) is read by `os_snprintf(pos, end - pos, ...)` at the top of the next iteration (`:6346`) before `pos` is written again — dead only on the loop's *final* iteration, not "on any execution path" as sqc claims. Distinct from the standard MSC13-C true-positive dead-store shape (unconditional overwrite within the same straight-line body); here the read exists but is one loop iteration away. Watch for recurrence in other accumulator-pointer (`pos +=`) loop shapes.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (12+ instances): MSC04-C "indirect recursion" on chains that pass through `wpa_supplicant_deauthenticate` — reconfirms and generalizes the `41plus_b60`-precedent "direct synchronous re-entry" TP disposition to essentially every `wpa_supplicant_event`-dispatched handler that (directly or transitively) calls `wpa_supplicant_deauthenticate()`.** `wpa_supplicant_deauthenticate()` (`wpa_supplicant.c:5095`) unconditionally calls `wpa_supplicant_event(wpa_s, EVENT_DEAUTH, &event)` synchronously whenever it resolves a non-NULL `addr` (the common connected-and-tearing-down-a-link case) — so *any* handler reachable from `wpa_supplicant_event`'s switch that calls `wpa_supplicant_deauthenticate` (directly, like `wpa_supplicant_event_michael_mic_failure`/`wpas_link_reconfig`, or transitively via `wpa_drv_get_mlo_info`/`wpas_wps_cancel`/`wpas_p2p_group_delete`/`sme_check_sa_query_timeout`) closes a real, syntactically-present call-graph cycle back into `wpa_supplicant_event`. Graded TP (medium confidence) per the established precedent rather than blanket-FP, even though the *specific* re-entry into the originating handler would actually require the EVENT_DEAUTH branch of the switch to itself reach back to that same handler at runtime (which the coarse call-graph, not being event-type-sensitive, doesn't verify) — the prior analyst's precedent judged the "direct synchronous call, not capped by async/eloop dispatch" distinction sufficient for a competent-reviewer-worth-flagging risk, and this batch's ~14 instances are structurally the same shape. 14 instances: `:4426,4537,4923,5066,5173,5412,5423,5434,5480,5535,5693,6077,6360,6430`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, extends the interprocedural member-free-vs-struct-free conflation family from `41plus_b68`'s `p2p_deinit`/`p2p_free_req_dev_types` precedent to a *loop* context): `free_hw_features(ifs)` frees only `ifs->hw.modes` (a struct member), but sqc treats the call as freeing `ifs` itself, cascading into 22 false MEM30-C UAF findings on every subsequent `ifs->` access for the rest of that `dl_list_for_each` loop iteration, plus a false double-free-shaped MSC01-C-adjacent misfire on the loop's own if/else-if.** `wpa_supplicant_update_channel_list()`, `:5667,5668,5670,5671,5674,5675,5676,5677,5678,5680,5681,5682`. Same root cause, now confirmed to also propagate across loop-iteration-local reads of a per-iteration loop variable, not just a single function's straight-line body.
- Reconfirms in this batch (not re-detailed above): ARR37-C scalar-`size_t`-mistaken-for-pointer FP (`sta_info_len:4401`); MSC07-C goto/switch-label-blindness (`out::4420`, ordinary case label after a break `EVENT_ASSOC:6560`, mutually-exclusive-if/`#ifdef`-boundary shape `:7083`); MSC13-C factually-wrong dead-assignment refuted by an immediately-following read (`match:4450`, `resched:7328`, `wpa_s:7515,7535`); EXP33-C macro-hidden-init misfire extended to `for_each_link()` (4 instances: `:4467,4502,6348`) alongside the standing write-only-output-param class for `ieee802_11_parse_elems` (`elems:6212,6499`) and the preprocessor-branch-blind class (`bss:4849`, `reject_bss:6189`); `:6318,6319`); ENV01-C/MEM05-C zero-getenv/fixed-macro-sized-array wholesale misfires (`:6082,6083`); API00-C internal-only-API pedantry (`:6512,7507`); INT14-C base-identifier-not-member misattribution (`data`'s `->` access wrongly blamed for `wpa_s->valid_links`'s bitwise op, `:6855`); ## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b85`, 150 findings, `wpa_supplicant/events.c#part1of2`, lines 31-4309: BSS/network selection matching, roaming decision (`wpa_supplicant_need_to_roam_within_ess`), `wpa_supplicant_connect`/`_event_associnfo`/`_event_assoc`-adjacent helpers, EHT Multi-Link Association parsing)

- **REFINEMENT to the `41plus_b84`-precedent "MSC04-C through `wpa_supplicant_deauthenticate` is blanket TP" entry: the closing edge must actually be reachable under the SAME `wpa_event_type` that `wpa_supplicant_deauthenticate()` passes, not just any call-graph edge out of `wpa_supplicant_event`'s switch.** `wpa_supplicant_deauthenticate()` (`wpa_supplicant.c:5154`) unconditionally calls `wpa_supplicant_event(wpa_s, EVENT_DEAUTH, &event)` — the enum argument is a hardcoded literal, never a variable. `wpa_supplicant_event`'s ~700-line switch dispatches each handler under exactly one `case`; `wpas_event_deauth()` is the (real, reachable) `case EVENT_DEAUTH:` handler, but `wpa_supplicant_event_assoc()`/`wpa_supplicant_event_scan_results()`/`wnm_btm_resp_tx_status()` (`case EVENT_ASSOC`/`EVENT_SCAN_RESULTS`/`EVENT_TX_STATUS` respectively) are not — so any chain that reaches `wpa_supplicant_event` via a `wpa_supplicant_deauthenticate()` call and then closes through one of *those* handlers is a **false cycle**: the call-graph edge exists textually (for a different, unrelated call site that does pass the matching event type) but is statically unreachable via the deauthenticate-triggered call. Confirmed 8 instances in this batch, all FP under this refinement: `events.c:1977` (→`EVENT_TX_STATUS`), `:2467,2890,2972` (→`EVENT_SCAN_RESULTS`), `:3097,3144,3220,3642` (→`EVENT_ASSOC`). Conversely, chains that stay event-type-consistent all the way (`wpa_supplicant_deauthenticate`→`wpa_supplicant_event`→`wpas_event_deauth`→`wpas_event_disconnect`→`wpa_supplicant_event_disassoc_finish`→`wpas_connection_failed`→`wpa_supplicant_fast_associate`→back to the origin) ARE real/reachable and should stay TP (medium confidence, bounded by the finite BSSID-ignore list) — confirmed 2 instances, `:2706,2945`. Net: before marking any `wpa_supplicant_deauthenticate`-involving MSC04-C chain TP, check what event type reaches the closing hop and whether it matches `EVENT_DEAUTH`; do not apply the blanket-TP disposition without that check.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (7 instances): ARR36-C "pointer comparison/subtraction between pointers from different arrays" misfires on plain `int`/`unsigned int` relational comparisons where the *variable names* happen to originate from struct-field reads, but the actual flagged expression is between two scalar locals, not pointers at all.** `cur_est > sel_est`/`sel_est > cur_est` (`events.c:2294,2302`, both `unsigned int` locals copied from `->est_throughput`), `diff = sel_level - cur_level` (`:2311`, plain `int` subtraction), and the ubiquitous `len > l` IE-truncation check (`len`/`l` are both `int`, derived from `p[1] + 2` and `->req_ies_len`/`->beacon_ies_len` respectively) recur at `:3240,3710,3872,3929`. The rule's own message text names the *source* struct-field expression (`current_bss->est_throughput`, `data->assoc_info.req_ies_len`) rather than the actual (scalar, non-pointer) operands being compared — a factually-wrong "pointer" framing, not just a benign-but-technically-true finding. Distinct from (and a new sub-shape of) the long-standing pos/end-bounds-pair ARR36-C FP family, since no pointer is involved on either side at all here.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances): MSC09-C "non-ASCII byte in string/character literal" misfires on `\x`-hex-escaped literals used as raw binary comparison buffers (OUI/vendor-type byte sequences fed to `os_memcmp`), not human-readable text.** `os_memcmp(&p[2], "\x00\x50\xF2\x01\x01\x00", 6)` / `"\x50\x6F\x9A\x12"` (`events.c:3246,3248,3717,3719,3936`) are deliberate byte-pattern literals (WPA/RSN OUI matching) — MSC09-C's actual concern (locale/national-charset text portability) categorically doesn't apply to a `\xNN`-escaped binary comparison buffer; there's no "text" here to be non-portable.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances): INT13-C/INT14-C-family "bitwise operator used on signed operand" misattributes the flagged identifier to a struct *pointer* variable when the actual `&`-operand is a dereferenced member field of a different (often correctly-signed-for-the-op) type.** `buf[1] = res->qual & 0xff;` etc. (`events.c:2533-2536`) name `res` (a `struct wpa_scan_res *`, not an int at all) as the "signed operand"; the real operand is `res->qual`/`res->noise`/`res->level`/`res->tsf`. Same base-identifier-vs-member-field confusion documented for INT14-C elsewhere in this corpus, now confirmed on INT13-C too.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): ENV01-C "fixed-size buffer may be used with environment variable" fires on ordinary stack array declarations (`u8 drv_ssid[SSID_MAX_LEN];`) that have no `getenv()`/environment-variable interaction anywhere in the function at all** — not just the already-documented "zero `getenv()` in the whole function" shape, but firing directly on the declaration line itself with no plausible textual trigger. `events.c:174,225`. Factually wrong, not just low-value.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): EXP33-C "may be used uninitialized"/"is used uninitialized" fires on the bare *declaration* line of a pointer that is unconditionally assigned a few lines later, before any read — no actual use-before-init exists anywhere.** `const u8 *rnr_ie, *ie_end;` / `const struct ieee80211_neighbor_ap_info *info;` (`events.c:2421,2422`) and `const u8 *end;` (`:4269`) are flagged at their declarations; each is written unconditionally before its first read later in the same block. Distinct from the standing `sizeof(*ptr)` and macro-hidden-init EXP33-C FP classes — this is the rule flagging a declaration statement itself as if it were a use.
- **NEW, batch-local (1 instance, watch for recurrence): EXP33-C "may be used uninitialized" is factually wrong when the variable has an explicit initializer at the very declaration line being flagged.** `struct wpa_bss *bss = NULL;` (`events.c:4001`) is flagged "may be used uninitialized (not assigned on all paths)" despite the `= NULL` initializer being right there in the cited line.
- **NEW, batch-local (1 instance, watch for recurrence): MSC41-C "hardcoded sensitive information" misfires on a ctrl_iface status/reason-code string tag, not an actual secret.** `wpas_auth_failed(wpa_s, "NO_PSK_AVAILABLE", NULL)` (`events.c:3302`) — the literal names a *condition*, not a password/key/token value. Extends the already-confirmed hardcoded-secret-misfire-on-a-status-string class (previously seen on debug msgtype/hexdump-title strings) to `wpas_auth_failed`'s reason-tag argument specifically.
- **NEW FN (real bug, not previously flagged): `wpas_ml_parse_assoc()`'s EHT Basic Multi-Link Common Info length is only lower-bound checked, allowing a `size_t` underflow driven entirely by attacker-controlled wire data.** `common_info->len` (parsed straight from an Association-Response IE) is checked only via `if (common_info->len < expected_common_info_len) goto out;` (`events.c:4218`) — there is no upper-bound check against the actual remaining `ml_len`. `ml_len -= sizeof(*ml) + common_info->len;` (`:4264`) can wrap to a huge value if a malicious/corrupted AP sets `common_info->len` larger than `ml_len - sizeof(*ml)`, and `pos = ((u8 *) common_info) + common_info->len` (`:4263`) already points past the parsed `wpabuf`'s bounds; the following `while (ml_len > 2 && ...)` loop then walks `pos` far out of the allocated buffer. Closest CERT mapping: INT30-C (unsigned wraparound) / ARR38-C (out-of-bounds indexing via an unvalidated wire-derived offset).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b104`, 66 findings, `wpa_supplicant/dpp_supplicant.c#part2of2`, lines ~4350-5849: DPP GAS config-response handling, configurator-sign, network introduction, PKEX add/remove, DPP chirp presence-announcement channel selection, DPP reconfig, CA-cert/CSR ctrl_iface setter, DPP3 push-button announcement)

- **NEW, batch-local (3 instances, one function): INT31-C "signed to unsigned conversion without bounds check" misfires when the cast value is used *only* for an equality comparison against another unsigned value, never as an index/size/allocation argument.** `wpas_dpp_conf_set`'s `peer` (`int`, from `atoi()`) is cast `(unsigned int) peer` and compared against `auth->peer_bi->id`/`auth->tmp_peer_bi->id` (`unsigned int`) at `:4986,4999,5001`. A negative `peer` simply wraps to a huge unsigned value that can never equal a real (small, sequentially-assigned) bootstrap id — the conversion has no unsafe consequence, just a guaranteed non-match. Watch for recurrence before promoting past batch-local (same idiom recurs in sibling functions `wpas_dpp_ca_set`, but there gated by an explicit `peer >= 0 &&` guard first, so not the same shape).
- **Extends the existing "atoi() guarded by its own inline `> 0` condition" FP family (`41plus_b11`, check-then-assign order) to the reverse assign-then-check order — CONFIRMED, 3 shapes/6 findings.** `iter = atoi(pos + 6); if (iter <= 0) return -1;` (`wpas_dpp_chirp:5340`, `wpas_dpp_reconfig:5410`) and `listen_freq = atoi(pos + 8); if (listen_freq <= 0) return -1;` (`wpas_dpp_chirp:5347`) all reject atoi's own 0-on-failure return (and any negative value) via an unconditional early `return -1` immediately after the assignment, before the parsed value is used for anything — functionally identical protection to the check-then-assign idiom, just with the statements in the opposite order.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b96`, 86 findings, `wpa_supplicant/dbus/dbus_new.c#part2of2`, lines 2700-5710: global/network/BSS/STA/interface/P2P-peer/P2P-group/persistent-group D-Bus method/property/signal tables, uscore_to_dbus, NAN/HS20 signal emitters)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (9 instances): MSC07-C "unreachable code after unconditional return" fires on every `return 0;`/`return N;` immediately followed by an `error:`/`err:` goto-target label in this file — same goto-label-blindness FP class documented elsewhere in the corpus (`41plus_b85`-adjacent entries), now reconfirmed at high density for one file's init/register functions.** Lines 2881,3008,3245,3396,4667,4719,5013,5243,5384.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (13 instances): ENV01-C "fixed-size buffer may be used with environment variable" is a wholesale misfire across this entire file — zero `getenv()` calls exist anywhere in `dbus_new.c`.** Fires on ordinary `char foo[WPAS_DBUS_OBJECT_PATH_MAX]` path-building buffers with no environment-variable interaction at all. Lines 2953,3025,3154,3196,3307,3348,4882,4964,5030,5102,5201,5320,5408.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): API05-C "array parameter uses size variable declared after the array parameter" misfires when the cited "size variable" is actually a compile-time `#define` macro constant (`ETH_ALEN` = 6, `src/utils/common.h:344`) used directly as the array-bound in `u8 bssid[ETH_ALEN]`, not a separate runtime size parameter that could plausibly be declared in the wrong order.** `wpas_dbus_unregister_bss:3151`, `wpas_dbus_register_bss:3192`. Contrast: the `bssid` parameter itself IS a genuine DCL13-C TP at both sites (never referenced in either function body at all, wholly unused — a real, if trivial, const opportunity). **3RD/4TH CONFIRMATION (batch `41plus_b230`, `src/wps/wps_common.c`):** same shape with a different macro, `WPS_DEV_TYPE_LEN` sizing `u8 dev_type[WPS_DEV_TYPE_LEN]` — `wps_dev_type_str2bin:462`, `wps_dev_type_bin2str:485`. Now generalizes beyond one file/macro: any `T arr[SOME_MACRO]` array-parameter triggers this bogus "declared after" claim regardless of which macro. Treat as a wholesale FP whenever the cited "size variable" resolves to a `#define`, not a sibling parameter.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): ARR01-C "sizeof applied to pointer/array parameter which has decayed to a pointer" fires on `sizeof(wpas_dbus_interface_properties[0])`/`sizeof(wpas_dbus_interface_properties)` where the named identifier is a file-scope `static const` array, not a function parameter at all** — no decay is possible since there is no parameter in play. `:4621,4632`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances): ERR33-C/STR03-C/EXP05-C triple-misfire on `snprintf(addr_str, sizeof(addr_str), MACSTR, MAC2STR(peer_addr))` into a `char addr_str[20]` buffer.** MACSTR (`"%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x"`) always produces exactly 17 chars + NUL = 18 bytes, provably fitting the 20-byte buffer — extends the established "exact/provably-bounded snprintf" ERR33-C/STR03-C FP class (`41plus_b104`-adjacent `hostapd_cli_open_connection` entry) to a fixed-format (not just fixed-length-input) case. ## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b100`, 71 findings, `hostapd/hlr_auc_gw.c#part2of2`, lines 774-1125)

- **Reconfirms the cross-function/cross-invocation static-read blind spot (`crypto_openssl.c` precedent, 4 instances) at higher volume (7 instances) and now also *same-function* self-invocation, not just sibling functions.** `cleanup()`'s `sqn_changes=0`/`gsm_db=NULL`/`milenage_db=NULL`/`serv_sock=-1`/`socket_path=NULL`/`sqlite_db=NULL` (`hlr_auc_gw.c:942,947,955,964,968,974`) and `main()`'s `socket_path=NULL` (`:1105`) are each flagged MSC13-C "never read", but `cleanup()` is registered via `atexit(cleanup)` *and* called explicitly earlier in the same run — the guard checks at the top of `cleanup()` (`if (serv_sock >= 0)`, `if (socket_path)`, `if (sqlite_db)`, `g = gsm_db`, `m = milenage_db`) genuinely re-read these statics on the second (atexit-triggered) invocation. sqc's dead-assignment dataflow doesn't track a static/global write surviving into a later call of the very same function.
- **NEW, batch-local (2 call sites, watch for recurrence): INT00-C/DCL11-C cross-function identifier-name type conflation — same root cause as the established `EXP39-C` cross-function local-variable-name conflation class, now hitting a format-string-type-check pair of rules.** `aka_auts`'s `char *imsi` parameter (`hlr_auc_gw.c:812`) is correctly a string; at its own `printf("...%s...", imsi, ...)` calls (`:833,834,844`) sqc claims argument 1 is `unsigned long long`, matching only `db_get_milenage()`'s unrelated local `unsigned long long imsi;` (`:210`) in a completely different function — sqc resolved the type by variable *name* across function scopes rather than by the actual in-scope declaration.
- Reconfirms in this batch: MSC06-C "clearing sensitive data just before scope exit" misapplied to fixed-test-value buffers that are read afterward in the same function, not cleared-then-discarded (5 instances: `:774,775,776,777,778`); EXP05-C phantom cast-away-const with no cast present at all (`ck:777`); STR03-C misfire when the snprintf return IS checked two lines later (`ret<0||ret>=end-pos`) (2 instances: `:787,792`); ERR02-C name-substring misfire on `wpa_snprintf_hex()` (6 instances: `:798,800,802,804,806`); STR34-C plain-char-literal-assignment misfire, no widening conversion (6 instances: `:799,801,803,805,825,830`); MSC13-C genuine dead-store TP for a final `pos +=`/`pos =` never read before return (2 instances: `:795,806`); EXP33-C correlated-conditional-assignment blind spot (`res_len:806`, set in every branch gated by the same `failed` flag that gates its only read); API05-C `T*,size_t` idiom (4 instances: `:812`×2,`867`×2); DCL37-C block-scope-local-misclassified-as-file-scope (`_auts:815`); PRE32-C phantom-directive misfire on plain concatenated-string-literal printf calls with zero preprocessor tokens (6 instances: `:833,853`×2,`990`×2); ARR30-C bounded-index misfire when an earlier same-function clamp (`if (res>=sizeof(buf)) res=sizeof(buf)-1;`) already guarantees the bound (`:912`); FIO47-C Integer-vs-Pointer misclassification on `char buf[N]`/`%s` pairs (3 instances: `:914,926,1111`); CON07-C no-pthread wholesale misfire, zero threading in the whole file (2 instances: `:936,1020`); EXP33-C zero-init-guarantee FP on `static const char *socket_path;` (`:966`); MSC17-C `#ifdef`-intervening fallthrough misfire, `case 'D':` has a real `break;`/`return -1;` inside the `#ifdef CONFIG_SQLITE`/`#else` (`:1037`); API00-C/CON07-C/STR31-C `main()`-argc/argv-guaranteed-valid FP bundle (`:1020`); ERR07-C/ERR34-C atoi() graded **TP** (not the usual immediately-range-checked FP) because 0 is itself a legal value in the checked range (`ind_len=atoi(optarg)`, checked only against `<0||>32`, so a garbage non-numeric string silently passes as `ind_len=0` — mirrors the established `ping_interval`/`link_id` "0-is-a-valid-value" TP split, `:1052`); MEM30-C stack-escape misapplied to `optarg` (points into the OS-provided `argv[]` strings, process-lifetime storage, not a local array of `main()`) (2 instances: `:1059,1062`); MEM12-C ownership/leak-on-early-return graded genuine TP (low severity) when `sqlite_db` is opened but the function returns before `atexit(cleanup)`/explicit `cleanup()` ever runs (`:1092`, `serv_sock` co-cited but not actually a live resource there — it's the value that failed to open) vs. graded **FP** at the function's final return once `cleanup()` has already run and closed both resources on every path reaching it (`:1125`); ERR33-C ignored-return on `atexit`/`signal` graded genuine (low-severity) TP, 3 instances (`:1096,1097,1098`); SIG00-C/SIG01-C `signal()`-vs-`sigaction()` graded genuine TP, real signal-based handler with no masking (4 instances: `:1097,1098`×2); ## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b103`, 150 findings, `wpa_supplicant/dpp_supplicant.c#part1of2`, lines 1-4331: DPP ctrl_iface command handlers, auth-init/rx-auth state machine, PKEX exchange, GAS config request/response, network-introduction PMKSA add, push-button PKEX)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances, 1 function each pair, extends the existing free-then-reassign FP family with a distinct root cause): MEM31-C/MEM12-C conflate two lexically-disjoint, same-named local variables in separate sibling `{ }` block scopes as if they were one variable.** `wpas_dpp_handle_config_obj` declares a fresh `char *hex;`/`char *b64;` inside three/two separate `if (...) { char *hex; ...; os_free(hex); }` blocks (c_sign_key at `:1745`, pp_key at `:1760`→freed `:1770`, net_access_key at `:1774`→freed `:1791`; b64 for certbag `:1797` and cacert `:1807`→freed `:1813`) — each `hex`/`b64` is a distinct variable with its own allocation and its own single free, but sqc's free-tracking appears to be scoped to the variable *name*, not its lexical binding, so it reports "already freed" (MEM31-C, `:1770,1791,1813`) and, separately, "leaked: hex, hex, hex" at the function's final `return` (MEM12-C, `:1830`, even though each was already freed in its own block). Distinct from the previously-documented reassign-in-the-same-scope MEM31 FP class (`tls_openssl_ocsp.c`) — here there is no reassignment at all, just three unrelated declarations that happen to share an identifier in non-overlapping scopes.
- **DCL13-C eloop-timeout-callback dispatch-contract FP class reconfirmed at very high density (14 instances) for the standard `void (*)(void *eloop_ctx, void *timeout_ctx)` signature** — every `wpas_dpp_*_timeout`/`wpas_dpp_build_csr`/`wpas_dpp_build_new_key` handler in this file matches the shared `eloop_register_timeout()` callback typedef; `:196,305,443,472,489,629,695,731,1169,1862,1887,2023,2208,2225,2530,3131,4225,4226`.
- **DCL13-C `struct dpp_global_config` callback-vtable dispatch-contract FP — new callback-table member, same root cause as the eloop/EAP-method-table family.** `wpas_dpp_remove_bi(void *ctx, struct dpp_bootstrap_info *bi)`'s `bi` matches `dpp_global_config.remove_bi`'s fixed signature (`dpp.h:825`, wired at `dpp_supplicant.c:4885`); can't be tightened without breaking every other assignment to that function-pointer field. `:2445`.
- **DCL13-C "plain top-level ctrl_iface handler, read-only `wpa_s` param" — genuine (low-severity) TP, NOT the dispatch-contract FP, because these are called directly by name from `ctrl_iface.c`'s command dispatch (a big if/else-if chain), not through a function-pointer table with a shared signature.** `wpas_dpp_nfc_uri`/`_nfc_handover_req`/`_nfc_handover_sel` (`:117,129,161`, each only reads `wpa_s->dpp`), `wpas_dpp_connected` (`:329`), `wpas_dpp_pb_active`/`_allow_ir` (`:2244,2932`), and plain-function params `intro`/`ssid` in `wpas_dpp_send_private_peer_intro_update` (`:3842,3843`) — contrast with the eloop/vtable entries above.
- **DCL13-C "not modified" factually wrong — `wpa_s` IS modified through a nested struct-array field write.** `wpas_dpp_remove_pb_hash(wpa_s)` zeroes `info->rx_time.sec`/`.usec` where `info = &wpa_s->dpp_pb[i]` — a real write reachable through the parameter, same "finding factually wrong" class as the `wpa_supplicant_update_mac_addr`/`wpa_sm_set_own_addr` precedents. `:2251`.
- **API00-C internal-only-API FP class extends to ctrl_iface DPP command entry points (`wpa_s`/`cmd` on `wpas_dpp_qr_code`/`_nfc_uri`/`_nfc_handover_req/_sel`/`_auth_init`/`_listen`) and to a driver-only remain-on-channel callback (`wpas_dpp_remain_on_channel_cb`'s `duration`, bounded by hardware capability, not attacker input) and to the RX action-frame entry point (`wpas_dpp_rx_action`'s `src`, always supplied non-NULL by the driver's frame-RX wrapper).** ~10 instances (`:78,117,129,161,834,1084,1132,4081`).
- **EXP20-C "may return values > 1, use != 0" misfires on functions whose own documented contract is exactly a tri-state `{-1, 0, 1}` return, where `== 1` is the correct way to distinguish success from both "no-op" (0) and "error" (-1).** `dpp_notify_new_qr_code()` (`dpp_auth.c:936-953`, returns -1/0/1 only) at `:88`; `wpas_dpp_allow_ir()` (same file, returns -1/0/1 only) at `:2977`.
- **EXP34-C "potential null pointer dereference in member access" flags the exact `if (!ssid || !ssid->X || ...)` guard clause itself as the unguarded access — the `!ssid` short-circuits before `ssid->X` is ever evaluated.** Same `||`-short-circuit-blindness root cause as the EXP30-C/EXP45-C nl80211-message-build-chain family, now on `EXP34-C`. 3 instances: `:2667,2808,3972`.
- **EXP34-C "no NULL check" — interprocedural caller-guarantees-non-null miss, new shape (caller, not callee, holds the guard).** `wpas_dpp_start_gas_server`'s `auth = wpa_s->dpp_auth;` is dereferenced with no local NULL check, but both of its call sites (`wpas_dpp_auth_success:2110`, `wpas_dpp_rx_reconfig_auth_resp:2739`) only ever call it after already establishing `wpa_s->dpp_auth`/`auth` non-NULL. `:1387`.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b101`, 150 findings, `src/drivers/driver_wext.c#part1of2`, lines 42-1706)

- **NEW, batch-local (4 instances, worth promoting on a 3rd file): MEM12-C "returns without releasing all resources" false-leak on an `os_realloc`-into-`tmp`-then-early-return shape repeated across sibling `if`/`else if` string-match branches, with two distinct false-positive causes bundled together.** `wext_get_scan_custom`'s `wpa_ie=`/`rsn_ie=` branches: (a) the `if (tmp == NULL) return;` guard (`:1301`) has nothing allocated to leak (`tmp` is NULL — `os_realloc` itself failed); (b) the `if (hexstr2bin(...) < 0) return;` guard (`:1304`) fires *after* `res->ie = tmp;` already ran, so ownership is already transferred to the long-lived `res->ie` field, not leaked. The sibling `tsf=` branch's two early returns (`:1314,1319`) get the *same* "Leaked: tmp, tmp" message despite that branch never touching `tmp` at all (it only ever writes a local `u8 bin[8]` stack array) — sqc's leak-tracker appears to key off "a `u8 *tmp` is in lexical scope at this return" rather than "was anything assigned to `tmp` on this control-flow path."
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, one file — same shape as the paired-bounds `pos`/`end` ARR36-C family but distinct root cause): ARR36-C "pointers from different arrays" + STR34-C "signed char converted without cast" jointly misfire on the WE-19 `struct iw_event` unaligned-copy idiom, where the "different array" is actually a byte offset *within the same struct object*.** `char *dpos = (char *) &iwe_buf.u.data.length; int dlen = dpos - (char *) &iwe_buf;` (`driver_wext.c:440-441,1444-1445`, once in the live-event handler and once in the scan-results parser): `dpos` and `&iwe_buf` both point into the *same* local `struct iw_event iwe_buf`, so `dpos - (char*)&iwe_buf` is a well-defined intra-object byte-offset computation, not cross-array pointer subtraction. STR34-C additionally misapplies its char-widening-cast check to this same subtraction expression — `dpos` here is a pointer (its *type*, `char *`), not a char *value* being widened, so there's no signedness/widening conversion to flag at all.
- **Reinforces (new sub-shape) the cross-function/cross-scope EXP39-C union-write conflation class (`6-15_b3`), now via a shared *variable name* across two entirely unrelated *types*.** `wpa_driver_wext_get_scan_results`'s local `struct wext_scan_data data;` (a plain struct, not a union at all) has a field literally named `res` (`struct wpa_scan_res res;`); sqc reports "accessing union `data` member `res` after writing `michael_mic_failure`" (`:1460`) by matching the identifier `data` against an unrelated `union wpa_event_data data;` local declared in a *different* function elsewhere in the file — the flagged variable in scope at line 1460 isn't a union at all, so the message is doubly wrong (wrong object AND wrong type category).
- **Reconfirms `struct wpa_driver_ops`/`netlink_config`/`rfkill_config`/`eloop_timeout_handler` dispatch-contract DCL13-C FP family at high density in a single driver-wrapper file (≈25 instances): `get_bssid`/`get_ssid`/`scan2` (`wpa_driver_ops`, `priv`/`params`), `newlink_cb`/`dellink_cb` (`netlink_config`, `ifi`/`buf`), `blocked_cb`/`unblocked_cb` (`rfkill_config`, `ctx`), `wpa_driver_wext_send_rfkill`/`_scan_timeout` (`eloop_timeout_handler`, `eloop_ctx`).** Distinguish from the ~20 genuine (low-severity) TPs in the same file: plain internal-only static helpers never wired into any of those four dispatch tables (`wpa_driver_wext_set_auth_param`/`_set_bssid`/`_set_ssid`/`_set_freq`/`_giwscan`/`_set_psk`/`_set_key_ext`/`_own_ifname`/`_own_ifindex`/`wext_19_iw_point`, and every `wext_get_scan_*` helper) — none of these are `struct wpa_driver_ops` fields despite sharing the family's `void *priv`/struct-pointer naming convention, so const-qualifying them is a real (if low-value) opportunity.
- **Reconfirms the mutually-exclusive-branch free/access conflation class (`16-40_b1`) on a `switch`'s `default:`-with-immediate-`return` arm — MEM30-C "use-after-free" (both the "passing freed pointer" and "accessing member of freed pointer" sub-messages) fires on code that runs strictly *after* the switch, on the path where `ext` was never freed.** `wpa_driver_wext_set_key_ext`'s `switch (alg) { ...; default: os_free(ext); return -1; }` followed by `if (seq && seq_len) { ...; os_memcpy(ext->rx_seq, seq, seq_len); }` (`:1686` vs `:1693`) — the `default` arm's free+return is mutually exclusive with reaching line 1693 at all.

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances): DCL11-C/FIO47-C "format string expects 0 arguments but 1 provided" on `fprintf(f, "field=" MACSTR "\n", MAC2STR(addr))` — MACSTR/MAC2STR macro-opacity undercount, distinct sub-shape from the already-documented MAC2STR-as-pure-accessor (EXP30-C) and MACSTR-exact-length (ERR33-C/STR03-C/EXP05-C, `41plus_b104`-adjacent) entries.** `MACSTR` (`src/utils/common.h:448`) expands to `"%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x:%02x"` (6 specifiers) and `MAC2STR(a)` (`:447`) expands to 6 comma-separated array-index args; sqc evidently doesn't expand either macro when counting format args vs. provided args, so it sees a literal `MACSTR` argument-count of 0 vs. one opaque `MAC2STR(...)` "argument", reporting a mismatch that doesn't exist post-expansion. `config_file.c:1507,1766,1788` (both rules, each line).
- Also in this batch: PRE32-C misfires on 33 ordinary multi-line `fprintf()` calls with zero actual preprocessor directives (matches the long-established categorical FP, including the MACSTR-concatenation variant at the same 3 lines above); API00-C internal-only-API FP on `wpa_config_write`'s `config` param (always `wpa_s->conf` from ~15 internal call sites); MSC37-C preprocessor-branch-blind "reach end without return" (`#ifndef/#else CONFIG_NO_CONFIG_WRITE`, both branches return); ERR33-C/ERR00-C fopen-checked-next-line FP (`:1855`); POS02-C codebase-wide no-privilege-separation FP (`:1910`); MEM12-C preprocessor-branch-blind extended to a variable that isn't even in scope in the flagged branch (`tmp_name` is declared only inside `#ifndef CONFIG_NO_CONFIG_WRITE`, but MEM12-C flags it leaked at the `#else` branch's `return -1;`, `:1923`) plus two ordinary already-freed-earlier-in-function MEM12-C FPs (`:1859,1921`); DCL13-C "plain helper, read-only param" TP exception extended to `wpa_config_write_identity`'s `dev_ik` (`:1809`).
- **New, low-confidence judgment calls (watch for recurrence): FIO03-C/FIO06-C graded genuine (low-severity) TP for `wpa_config_write`'s `fopen(name, "w")` temp-file rewrite** — matches the `hlr_auc_gw.c:512` data-file-rewrite precedent, arguably stronger here since the file is `wpa_supplicant.conf` itself (carries PSK/passphrase secrets, making the FIO06-C "no explicit permissions" concern more substantive than a generic data file). **ERR00-C/ERR33-C on the paired `fclose(f)` at `:1904` graded genuine TP** per the established write-stream-vs-read-stream distinction (`hostapd_config_read_*`'s ignored-fclose-on-read-stream is FP; this is a write stream, so a close-time flush failure is a real unreported data-loss risk). **WIN03-C/FIO10-C graded FP (low confidence)** since `config_file.c` has zero Windows-specific (`_WIN32`/`CONFIG_NATIVE_WINDOWS`) handling anywhere and `config_winreg.c` is the dedicated Windows-registry backend selected via `CONFIG_BACKEND=winreg` in `wpa_supplicant/Makefile:224-225` — but no direct evidence rules out `CONFIG_BACKEND=file` ever being used on a Windows/MinGW build, so this is not as ironclad as the already-fully-confirmed WIN03-C/FIO10-C "file never built for Windows" precedent (`hlr_auc_gw.c`).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b108`, 57 findings, `src/ap/hostapd.c#part2of2`, lines ~4034-5330: interface add/remove, beacon-data build, CSA/CCA channel-switch settings, MLD link helpers, per-BSS/per-iface accessors)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances): EXP20-C "implicit boolean test, may be unclear what constitutes success/failure" misapplied to `!os_strcmp(a, b)`/`os_strcmp(a, b)` equality tests.** `os_strcmp`/`strcmp`'s 0=equal contract is exact and universally known — unlike the already-documented `sscanf`-single-specifier and OpenSSL-`==1` "provably exact contract" FP classes, this is arguably an even more clear-cut case since `!strcmp(...)` is one of the most common idioms in all of C. `hostapd.c:4084,4104,5117`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: ARR01-C "sizeof applied to pointer/array parameter which has decayed to a pointer" fires on `sizeof(*ptr)` (dereference-then-size, the textbook *correct* way to avoid decay) and even on `sizeof(struct_field)` where the flagged "parameter" isn't sized at all — the struct member being sized (`hapd->cs_freq_params`) is a fixed-size embedded struct, not an array/pointer.** Two distinct sub-shapes, both factually wrong: `os_memset(beacon, 0, sizeof(*beacon))` (`:4328`) and `sizeof(hapd->cs_freq_params)` (`:4692`).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MSC17-C fallthrough-CFG-blindness extends to a `case` block whose own `if`/`else` both unconditionally `return`, with no trailing `break` at all (not the established `#ifdef`-hidden-break sub-shape).** `case 80: if (x) return A; else return B;` immediately followed by `case 160:` — every path through case 80 already exits the function, so there is no real fallthrough despite the missing `break`. `hostapd.c:4597`.
- **Reconfirms API00-C internal-only-API FP at very high density (13 instances) for hostapd.c's own internal AP/BSS/MLD management functions** (`hostapd_remove_iface`, `hostapd_build_beacon_data`, `hostapd_cleanup_cs_params`, `hostapd_chan_switch_config`, `hostapd_force_channel_switch`, `hostapd_switch_channel_fallback`, `hostapd_cleanup_cca_params`, `hostapd_fill_cca_settings`, `hostapd_get_iface`, `hostapd_periodic_iface`, `hostapd_mld_get_link_bss`, `hostapd_get_punct_bitmap`) — all called only with pointers derived from the process's own long-lived `hapd_interfaces`/`hostapd_iface`/`hostapd_data` object graph, never externally-nullable.
- **Reconfirms the "plain helper, read-only param" DCL13-C genuine-if-low-value-TP exception at very high density (17 instances)** across small `hostapd_data*`/`hostapd_iface*` accessors (`hostapd_csa_in_progress`, `hostapd_chan_width_from_freq_params`, `hostapd_chan_switch_config`'s 2nd param, `hostapd_get_iface`, `hostapd_is_ml_partner`'s two params, `hostapd_mld_is_first_bss`, `hostapd_mld_get_first_bss`, `hostapd_get_punct_bitmap`, `hostapd_get_mbssid_bss_by_idx`, `hostapd_acceptable_sta_addr_bss`) — none forward into a non-const callee or match a callback typedef, so const really is a free, correct (if low-severity) improvement.
- **Reconfirms the DCL13-C callback/vtable dispatch-contract FP class for 2 new shapes:** an `eloop_timeout_handler`-typedef callback (`hostapd_switch_color_timeout_handler`'s `user_ctx`, `hostapd_ocv_check_csa_sa_query`'s `timeout_ctx`) and a generic per-module iterator callback (`hostapd_acceptable_sta_addr_iface`'s `iface`/`_ctx`, matching `hostapd_for_each_interface`'s fixed `int (*cb)(struct hostapd_iface *, void *)` typedef, `hostapd.h:757-759`).
- **Reconfirms the DCL30-C "confused local pointer variable with local storage" FP class**: `hostapd_mld_get_link_bss` returns `bss`, a local variable that points into the long-lived `iface->bss[]` array, not stack storage. `:5103`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: INT10-C wrong-signedness-detection extends to `os_random() % N` used as a *color/index* selector (not just the previously-documented direct-modulo case)** — `os_random()` returns `unsigned long`, so no instance in this file's BSS-color-collision handler (`:4943,4956`) can produce a negative modulo result; a *sibling* loop-invariant-bounded FP (`(r + 1) % HE_OPERATION_BSS_COLOR_MAX`, `:4948`) reconfirms the separate "provably non-negative via loop invariant" INT10-C FP class on the same variable.
- **NEW, batch-local: INT14-C misattributes "used with both bitwise and arithmetic operations" to a struct *pointer* variable (`hapd`) when only one of its *member fields* (`color_collision_bitmap`) is ever used bitwise — the pointer itself never appears in a bitwise expression, only via `->` member access.** Contrast with a same-function, textually-correct instance on a plain scalar (`r`, used both as a shift amount and in `%`/`+` arithmetic) graded genuine (low-value) TP. `hostapd.c:4938` (FP) vs `:4945` (TP).
- **NEW, batch-local: ARR00-C "loop uses uninitialized variable as bound" fires on a `for (b = 0; b < N; b++)` loop's own init clause — `b` is initialized in the exact statement cited, not uninitialized.** `hostapd.c:4957`.
- **NEW, batch-local: EXP36-C alignment-cast finding misidentifies the source pointer's declared type** — claims a cast is "from char *" when the actual parameter is declared `void *` (an eloop callback's untyped ctx arg); void*-to-struct-pointer casts have no alignment hazard once the underlying object is itself correctly aligned. `hostapd.c:4930`.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b109`, 150 findings, `wpa_supplicant/config_file.c#part1of2`, lines 93-1487: block readers, `wpa_config_read`, and the entire `write_*`/`wpa_config_write_*` config-serializer family)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED, dominant this batch (≈30 instances): DCL13-C misfires on a `FILE *f` param that is ONLY ever forwarded to `fprintf()`/`fclose()` — const-qualifying it would not compile, since neither libc function accepts a `const FILE *`.** Distinct root cause from the eloop/vtable dispatch-contract DCL13-C family (no callback typedef involved here, just an ordinary libc call whose first param is plain `FILE *`). Every `write_str`/`write_int`/`write_bssid`/`write_psk`/`write_proto`/`write_key_mgmt`/`write_pairwise`/`write_group`/`write_group_mgmt`/`write_auth_alg`/`write_eap`/`write_wep_key`/`write_go_p2p_dev_addr`/`write_p2p_client_list`/`write_p2p2_client_list`/`write_psk_list`/`write_mka_cak`/`write_mka_ckn`/`wpa_config_write_cred`/`wpa_config_write_blob`/`write_global_bin` hits this. Contrast: the same functions' *other* struct-pointer params (`cred`, `blob`, `config` in `wpa_config_write_network`) ARE genuine (if low-value) TPs when only read and never forwarded to a non-const callee — same "plain read-only helper param" disposition as the rest of the corpus, just now disambiguated from the FILE*-forwarding sub-case.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (≈35 instances): PRE32-C "called with preprocessor directives in arguments" is a wholesale phantom-directive misfire on plain `fprintf(f, "literal", field)` calls sitting inside (but not containing) `#ifdef`/`#endif` blocks.** No directive exists inside any flagged call's argument list — the `#ifdef CONFIG_P2P`/`CONFIG_WPS`/etc. wrapping the *surrounding* code is being conflated with the call itself. Extends the already-confirmed phantom-directive class (hostapd_cli.c/wpa_cli.c precedent) to this file's entire `wpa_config_write_global`/`wpa_config_write_cred` serializer bodies.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: INT00-C "format specifier '%s' does not match variable type 'int'" is flatly fabricated on ~17 plain `fprintf(f, "\t%s=%s\n", field, value)`/`fprintf(f, "\tfoo=%s\n", value)` calls where every arg is `char *` and no `int`/`%d` appears anywhere in the statement.** No plausible source object for the claim exists at the cited line; likely the same cross-function identifier-name resolution bug already documented for hostapd/config_file.c (`41plus_b20`) — `field`/`value` are reused across many small `write_*` helpers in this file, and sqc may be resolving the wrong function-scope's type.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL11-C/FIO47-C "argument count/type mismatch" on `fprintf(f, "\tpsk_list=%s" MACSTR "-%s\n", ..., MAC2STR(psk->addr), hex)` — macro-expansion blindness, not a real mismatch.** `MACSTR` expands to 6 `%02x` specifiers and `MAC2STR(x)` to 6 corresponding byte args; once expanded the format/arg counts balance exactly (8 specifiers, 8 args). sqc's static counter doesn't expand `MACSTR`/`MAC2STR` before counting — extends the established MACSTR/MAC2STR pure-accessor-arg EXP30-C FP class to argument-count-checking rules (DCL11-C, FIO47-C) for the first time.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP43-C category error on macro-only invocations for this file's `INTe(t,m)`/`INT_DEFe(t,m,def)` writer macros** — `INTe(erp, erp)`, `INT_DEFe(fragment_size, fragment_size, ...)`, `INT_DEFe(sim_num, sim_num, ...)` pass bare field-name *identifiers* (token-pasted into `#t`/`ssid->eap.m`), never pointers — extends the `__AKM`-macro EXP43-C category-error precedent (`driver_nl80211.c`, `41plus_b13`) to a new macro family.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: PRE00-C/PRE05-C/PRE12-C misfire on this file's `STR(t)`/`INT(t)`/`INT_DEF(t,def)`/`INTe(t,m)`/`INT_DEFe(t,m,def)` stringify-and-write macros** — `t`/`m` are always bare field-name identifiers at every call site (never a macro needing pre-expansion, never a side-effecting expression evaluated twice); same reasoning as the `hostapd/config_file.c:4227` `PARSE_TEST_PROBABILITY` precedent (`41plus_b25`), now confirmed on the writer-side sibling macro family.
- **Reconfirms EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-dereference (8 instances: `ssid/cred/blob/identity` each via `os_zalloc(sizeof(*x))`), DCL30-C local-pointer-vs-heap-storage confusion (6 instances, same 4 objects plus `config`), STR34-C plain-char-literal-assignment (6 instances), the fgets/wpa_config_get_line-outer-while ARR30-C misattribution (3 instances), os_free(NULL)-is-safe EXP34-C (1), the "tail"/"head" walk-guarantees-non-NULL EXP34-C shape (3 instances, new sub-shape of the callee/caller-already-guards family), MSC01-C guard-clause pedantry (2), the no-pthread CON03-C/CON07-C/CON33-C/CON34-C family (6 instances, first confirmation of this class specifically for wpa_supplicant's own config-file code, not just driver/CLI files), fclose()-on-read-only-stream low-value ERR00-C/ERR33-C (2), MSC13-C static-cross-call-significance (1) alongside a genuine dead-store TP (`head=NULL`, never read again), MEM05-C fixed-macro/constant-sized-array-not-a-VLA (3 instances), ARR00-C for-loop-init-clause-initialization miss (1), EXP30-C pure-accessor-args (`wpabuf_head`/`wpabuf_len`, 1), MEM10-C ad-hoc-NULL-check stylistic (3), and DCL37-C block-scope-local-misclassified-as-file-scope (`_buf` x2).**
- **Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed: EXP34-C "passing potentially null pointer 'buf'" on `wps_dev_type_bin2str(dev_type, _buf, sizeof(_buf))`'s result, where `WPS_DEV_TYPE_BUFSIZE` (21) is defined to exactly fit the worst-case width of its `"%u-%08X-%u"` format (5+1+8+1+5+NUL=21) — `os_snprintf` inside the callee can never truncate/fail, so the documented NULL-on-failure path is unreachable here. New provably-bounded-callee sub-shape of the existing exact-fit-snprintf FP family.**
- **Batch-local: WIN03-C "fopen() without 'N' flag" judged genuine (low-severity) TP, not FP** — unlike the confirmed WIN03-C/FIO10-C platform-inapplicable class (files never built for Windows), `config_file.o` is unconditionally in `wpa_supplicant/Makefile`'s `OBJS` and the file is compiled under `CONFIG_NATIVE_WINDOWS` builds too; no per-file Windows-exclusion applies here.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b113`, 150 findings, `wpa_supplicant/wps_supplicant.c#part1of2`, lines 16-2433: WPS event/credential handling, eloop/wps_context/wps_registrar_config callbacks, WPS PIN/PBC/NFC/ER start/stop, DH-key NFC refresh)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances, one function, worth watching for a 3rd file before generalizing further): WIN04-C "function pointer stored without encryption" fires on plain enum-constant assignments (`cred.encr_type = WPS_ENCR_WEP/TKIP/AES;`) that contain no function pointer at all, inside an if/else-if chain with an embedded `#ifdef CONFIG_TESTING_OPTIONS ... #endif` branch.** The same lines/vicinity also produce two nonsense MSC13-C findings — "value assigned to `'if'`" and "variable `'return'` declared but never used" — where the C *keywords* `if`/`return` are misidentified as variable names. All three findings cluster tightly around the `#ifdef` insertion point inside the `if`/`else if` chain, strongly suggesting a tokenizer/parser desync triggered by the conditional-compilation directive rather than three independent rule misfires. `wps_supplicant.c:2189,2192,2194,2197`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM30-C/MEM31-C struct-field reassignment blindness — extends the documented `eap_server_tls_common.c` `data->tls_out` gap (`41plus_b44`-adjacent) to a 2nd file/shape with a full leak+UAF+double-free false cluster (6 findings, one call site).** `wps->dh_privkey`/`wps->dh_pubkey` are freed (old values) then immediately reassigned via `wpabuf_dup()` (`:2427,2428`); sqc's free-state tracking doesn't clear on the struct-field reassignment, so it flags: the fresh `wpabuf_dup()` results as "leaked" (MEM31-C, since it doesn't see the failure-path frees at `:2431,2433` as covering them), the immediately-following NULL check as "use-after-free" (MEM30-C, `:2429`x2, referring to the *stale* pre-reassignment identity), and the failure-path frees themselves as "double-free" (MEM30-C, `:2431,2433`, since it thinks they re-free the pre-reassignment allocation rather than the fresh one). One coherent root cause, 6 findings.
- **NEW, batch-local: EXP33-C "used uninitialized" misses that a variable is initialized in the *first* operand of a for-loop init clause's comma expression and read in the *second* operand** — `for (ssid = wpa_s->conf->ssid, next = ssid ? ssid->next : NULL; ssid; ...)` reads `ssid` in the 2nd comma operand right after it's assigned in the 1st; C's comma operator sequences left-to-right so this is well-defined, not uninitialized. `wps_supplicant.c:286`. 1 instance so far — watch for recurrence on other `for (x = ..., y = x ? ... : ...; ...)` idioms.
- **NEW, batch-local: EXP39-C fires on a mutually-exclusive `switch`/`case` dispatch where the cited "earlier write" is actually just an `&data->m2d`-style address-of in a sibling `case` branch, never an actual write to that union member.** Distinct from the already-documented cross-*function* union conflation and the same-function-legitimate-CIS-reliance TP — this is a same-function, same-switch, mutually-exclusive-*branch* conflation (the general "mutually-exclusive control-flow branches treated as sequential" root cause, now applied to union member tracking for the first time). `wps_supplicant.c:889,1006`.

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b122`, 36 findings, `src/drivers/nl80211_copy.h#part2of2`, lines ~7680-8456: vendored Linux kernel nl80211 uapi enums — peer-measurement/FTM, HE OBSS-PD, BSS-color, iftype-AKM, FILS discovery, unsolicited-broadcast-probe-response, SAR, MBSSID, WIPHY-radio, S1G, NAN-capabilities attribute enums)

- **PROMOTED to fully confirmed (was batch-local at `41plus_b12`, 2 instances in `nl_ctrl.h`-style `nlmsgerr` enum; now 36 more instances, same file family): INT09-C "enum has duplicate value 0" is a wholesale rule-logic bug on the kernel `enum { __FOO_INVALID, ..., /* keep last */ NUM_FOO or __FOO_LAST, FOO_MAX = NUM_FOO - 1 (or __FOO_LAST - 1) };` sentinel/keep-last idiom.** Every one of the 18 enums in this file's range independently repeats the same false-positive pair: (a) the leading `__FOO_..._INVALID` sentinel (implicit 0, always the *first* enumerator — nothing precedes it to duplicate), flagged as "duplicate value 0 (implicitly)"; and (b) the trailing `FOO_..._MAX = NUM_FOO - 1` or `= __FOO_..._LAST - 1` (a computed expression that evaluates to the enum's highest ordinal, never 0 for any enum with ≥2 real members), flagged as "duplicate value 0 (explicitly)". sqc's INT09-C constant-value resolver appears to not evaluate `X - 1` expressions at all (or defaults unresolved expressions to 0), and separately treats the very first enumerator as eligible to "duplicate" nothing. 100% FP rate (36/36) in this batch; zero true duplicates found by manual inspection of any enum in range. High-value to fix upstream — this shape recurs throughout every vendored kernel header in the tree (`nl80211_copy.h` is ~8459 lines of exactly this idiom) and will keep generating dozens of guaranteed-FP findings per file until the rule's constant-expression evaluation is fixed.
- **Reconfirmed at much higher volume by `41plus_b121` (the other half of the same file, `nl80211_copy.h#part1of2`, lines 2-7654): 108/108 INT09-C findings FP**, same `__FOO_INVALID`(0, implicit)/`FOO_MAX = __FOO_AFTER_LAST - 1`(mis-evaluated to 0, explicit) pair across ~50 enums; also confirmed a **cascading 3rd-victim shape**: `enum nl80211_auth_type` has `NL80211_AUTHTYPE_AUTOMATIC` (no explicit value, i.e. computed as prior-enumerator + 1) flagged as duplicating `NL80211_AUTHTYPE_SHARED_KEY`'s real value 1 — because sqc's mis-resolved `MAX = 0` poisons the running implicit-value counter for every subsequent unlabeled enumerator, not just the `MAX` constant itself. Same batch: 39/39 EXP07-C "assumes constant value" on `1 << N` bit-flag enumerators (kernel ABI ioctl/regulatory-flag bit-packing, e.g. `NL80211_RRF_*`) and 1/1 PRE02-C on a single-token negative-literal macro (`NL80211_SCAN_RSSI_THOLD_OFF -300`) are both FP, matching the already-confirmed EXP07-C-bitpacking and PRE02-C-single-token-literal classes respectively — not new, just extended to this file. Also 2/2 DCL37-C: the file's own `__LINUX_NL80211_H` header guard (FP — intentionally mirrors the real external Linux kernel uapi header this is vendored from, same reasoning as the `_LINUX_TYPES_H` exception) and one `__NL80211_WOWLAN_PKTPAT_INVALID` reserved-double-underscore enum sentinel (FP, distinct from the `__must_check`/`__AKM` TP precedents — this identifier is verbatim-copied kernel naming, not a name hostap invented for its own code, so there's no independent authorship decision to correct).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b116`, 48 findings, `src/radius/radius_server.c#part2of2`, lines 2009-2673: RADIUS client-list loader, server init/deinit, MIB stats, EAP-method dispatch callbacks, sqlite session-field callback, dynamic authorization/CoA request)
