- **NEW sub-shape, batch-local: EXP33-C "may be used uninitialized" on two locals (`abuf`/`mbuf`) initialized across a *pair of separately-written* `if (data->ipv6)` / `if (!data->ipv6)` statements (the second one outside the `#ifdef CONFIG_IPV6` block guarding the first) rather than a single `if`/`else`.** Together the two ifs are exhaustive and always initialize both buffers, but sqc doesn't correlate two textually-separate, preprocessor-split complementary conditions as one exhaustive case split. Extends the existing correlated-conditional-assignment EXP33-C blind spot (`wpa_common.c:2513`, `41plus_b*` batches) to a preprocessor-fragmented variant. 2 instances (`radius_server.c:2266`).
- **NEW sub-shape, batch-local: DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP extends beyond eloop/EAP-method tables to a 3rd-party library callback prototype — `sqlite3_exec()`'s fixed `int(*)(void*,int,char**,char**)` signature.** `get_db_session_fields`'s `argv`/`col` params (`:2474`) are read-only in the body but can't be const-qualified without breaking the sqlite3 API contract. Same root cause as the eloop/EAP dispatch-contract class, just a different vtable owner (library call, not internal struct).
- **NEW, batch-local: MEM12-C "returns without releasing all resources" false leak on a fully-successful return that hands ownership of the struct (and its live fields) to the caller** — `radius_server_init`'s `return data;` (`:2123`) is flagged as leaking `data->eap_req_id_text`/`auth_sock`/`acct_sock`, but these are exactly the fields the caller is meant to own via the returned pointer, not resources being discarded. Distinct from the already-documented "freed earlier in the same function" and "persistent-list-ownership-transfer" MEM12-C FP sub-shapes — this one is a plain successful-construction return.
- **NEW, batch-local: MEM12-C false leak where the resources actually were released, just via an interprocedural cleanup call (`radius_server_deinit(data)`) immediately before the flagged `return NULL;`, not a direct `free()`/`os_free()` in the same function.** `radius_server_init`'s `fail:` path (`:2124-2126`) calls `radius_server_deinit(data)`, which itself frees `eap_req_id_text`, closes both sockets, and frees `data`; sqc's leak-check doesn't look inside the callee to see the cleanup. Interprocedural-cleanup-blindness variant of the existing "already freed" MEM12-C FP class.
- **NEW, batch-local: MSC37-C "non-void function may reach end without returning a value" misfires when the function's *entire body* (not just one branch or condition) is wrapped in `#ifdef X ... #else return -1; #endif`, and the `#ifdef` branch itself has an explicit `return` on every path.** `radius_server_dac_request` (`:2515`) returns on every path in both the `CONFIG_SQLITE` and `#else` branches; extends the existing "MSC37-C confused by `#ifdef` inside an `if` condition" batch-local note (`dbus_common.c:341`, `41plus_b24`) to a whole-function-body `#ifdef`/`#else` shape.
- **Reconfirms ERR07-C/ERR34-C default-TP disposition for un-range-checked `atoi()`** — `get_db_session_fields`'s `hs20_t_c_filtering`/`waiting_coa_ack`/`coa_ack_received` fields (`:2492,2494,2496`) parse sqlite-column text via plain `atoi()` with no subsequent range/sanity check (contrast with the `sae_pk_gen.c:48` FP where the parsed value is immediately checked against a narrow fixed set) — genuine low-severity TPs per literal rule text, not automatically FP just because `atoi` is a common idiom.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b124`, 33 findings, `src/utils/common.c#part2of2`, lines 1112-1344: `cstr_token`/`str_token`, `utf8_unescape`/`utf8_escape`, `ssid_parse`, `get_param`, `forced_memzero`/`memset_func`)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances, one file): DCL30-C "returns/stores pointer to local variable with automatic storage duration" misapplied to a local pointer *variable* whose value aliases into the caller-supplied input buffer, not local automatic-storage memory at all.** `cstr_token(const char *str, ...)`'s `token`/`end` locals are `const char *` set to positions *within* the caller-owned `str` string (`token = str` then advanced; `end = token + 1` then advanced) — the pointed-to memory belongs to the caller and stays valid after `cstr_token`/`str_token` return, so both `*last = end;` (`:1112`) and `return token;` (`:1113`) are safe. `str_token`'s own `char *token = (char *) cstr_token(...); return token;` (`:1132`) inherits the same aliasing and is likewise safe. This is a 3rd sub-shape of the existing "DCL30-C confuses local *variable* with local *storage*" family (previously: heap-backed `wpabuf_alloc()`/`os_zalloc()` pointers, and a `static const` table pointer) — here the backing store is neither heap nor static, but the *caller's own buffer*, which is just as valid a target for a pointer that outlives the function.
- **STR34-C misfires on a `const char **`/`char **` out-param pointer assignment (not a char value) — reconfirms the `dpp_supplicant.c:3754,3836` class in a new shape.** `*last = end;` (`:1112`, `last` is `const char **`, `*last` is a pointer) — no char-widening conversion exists at all.
- **NEW, batch-local (2 instances): MEM33-C "direct assignment of flexible array structure instances" misfires on a plain `char`-pointer copy-loop statement (`*outp++ = *inp++;`) with zero structs, flexible array members, or aggregate assignment anywhere in the function.** `utf8_unescape:1172`, `utf8_escape:1212`. Appears to pattern-match on `*p++ = *q++;` shape alone without checking the pointee type is actually a struct with a flexible array tail.
- **EXP40-C "pointer to const assigned to non-const pointer without cast" fires on a line where an explicit cast is already present in the exact expression quoted by the finding itself** — `char *token = (char *) cstr_token(...)` (`:1127`) — self-contradictory misfire.
- Reconfirms in this batch: STR34-C plain char-to-char literal assignment (`*outp = '\0'`/`*outp++ = '\\'`, 9 instances: `:1130,1161,1172`x3`,1179,1208,1212`x3`,1219,1255`); API05-C ptr+size-param idiom FP (5 instances: `:1136,1137,1185,1186,1342`, the last on `void *ptr, size_t len`); CON43-C switch-on-dereferenced-pointer no-thread misfire, extending the `tls_openssl.c:5098` precedent to 2 more instances (`utf8_unescape:1158`, `utf8_escape:1203`) plus a non-switch static-const-fnptr sub-shape (`memset_func:1339`, `const volatile` qualifiers mean the pointer is set once at init and never mutated, so no concurrent-write hazard exists to synchronize against); CON03-C reconfirmed factually-wrong-on-its-face (claims "not volatile" on a variable whose declaration literally includes `volatile`, `:1339`); DCL30-C/ARR00-C heap-vs-automatic-storage confusion (`get_param`'s `val`, `os_malloc`-backed, `:1327`x2); API00-C internal-only-API FP (`ssid_parse`'s `buf`, all 3 call sites already null-check or offset from an already-matched non-NULL string, `:1241`); DCL31-C function-pointer-*variable*-call misfire (`memset_func(...)`, a `static ... (* const volatile memset_func)(...)` declared 5 lines above its call, not an implicitly-declared bare function, `:1344`).
- **NEW, batch-local: WIN04-C "function pointer stored without encryption; consider EncodePointer()" on a `const`-qualified, program-lifetime static function pointer initialized once from a fixed libc symbol (`memset`) purely to defeat dead-store-elimination in `forced_memzero`** (`:1339`) — graded FP (medium confidence): the pointer can never be reassigned through its own type (`const`), is not attacker-influenced, and EncodePointer-style defenses target genuinely mutable, exploit-relevant function-pointer storage, not a compiler-optimization-defeat idiom. Only 1 instance seen; watch for recurrence before treating as fully confirmed.
- FN read-through: none found. Full file (1347 lines) read; all allocations (`os_malloc`/`os_realloc_array` in `wpa_config_parse_string`, `freq_range_list_parse`, `int_array_concat`, `int_array_add_unique`, `freq_range_list_str`, `get_param`, `dup_binstr`) are NULL-checked with clean error-path frees, and no fd/socket/lock resources exist in this file. Marking `src/utils/common.c` clean for FN.

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances, one function): MEM30-C "use-after-free" fires on a struct field that was `os_free()`'d and then immediately *reassigned* to a fresh value one line later, before any of the flagged reads** (`wps->new_psk:1733,1737,1740,1741` in `wps_build_cred` — `os_free(wps->new_psk); wps->new_psk = base64_encode(...);` then several reads of the fresh buffer). This is a struct-member-field extension of the already-shipped "MEM30 reassign + fresh-binding fix" (task 232), which appears to have only cleared freed-state for local-variable reassignment, not `ptr->field` reassignment — worth flagging to the sqc team as a residual gap in that fix's scope.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: WIN04-C/MSC13-C jointly misfire on plain `else if (EXPR)` lines that sit immediately adjacent to an `#ifndef`/`#ifdef`/`#endif` directive, with zero function pointers anywhere in the statement** (6 instances: `:1668,1671`x2`,1693`x2`,1705`x2`,1787`x2 across `wps_build_cred`'s auth/encr-type selection and `use_provided:`'s `#ifdef CONFIG_WPS_TESTING` stub-credential block). WIN04-C's claim is flatly wrong (no fn-ptr on the line at all, extending the already-documented `dpp.c:2120`/`wps_supplicant.c:2189` "flatly wrong claim"/enum-assignment sub-shapes to plain boolean `else if` conditions), and MSC13-C in the same spots misparses the `if` token of `else if` as a dead-assignment lvalue — both are the same underlying `#ifdef`-adjacent parser desync already documented for `wpa_ft_set_key_mgmt`/`wps_supplicant.c`, now confirmed as a *pair* that co-fires on the identical trigger line every time (5 of 6 instances hit both rules on the same line).
- **NEW, batch-local: INT14-C conflates a struct-pointer variable with two of its *different* dereferenced fields** (`wps:1665` — `wps->auth_type` used bitwise, unrelated `wps->new_psk_len` used arithmetically elsewhere in the same function) — a variant of the already-documented struct-pointer/dereferenced-member INT14-C conflation, here spanning two unrelated fields rather than one field used both ways.
- **NEW, batch-local: MSC07-C "unreachable code after unconditional break" misidentifies a normal `case LABEL:` immediately following the prior case's `break;` as dead code** (`case WPS_M3::3071` in `wps_process_wsc_msg`'s dispatch switch) — a `switch` case label is always reachable via its own case value regardless of what precedes it; distinct from the already-documented "goto-target-label-after-return" MSC07-C sub-shape (this one needs no goto at all, just adjacent case labels).
- **Reconfirms CON43-C single-threaded-eloop FP class, extended to `switch` on a dereferenced local parse-result field** (`*attr.msg_type:3054`, zero pthread usage, `attr` is a stack-local struct freshly populated by `wps_parse_msg` in the same function, not shared/concurrently-modified state).
- **Reconfirms STR31-C misapplied-to-non-char-array class** (`const u8 *addr[1]:2693`, a 1-element pointer array, not a character buffer).
- FN read-through: no new FN confirmed in the assigned range (`:23-3352`). One candidate examined and **not** reported, consistent with the `41plus_b120` resolution for the sibling function `wps_registrar_update_multi_ap` (`:3668`): `wps_registrar_init`'s `os_memcpy(reg->multi_ap_backhaul_ssid, cfg->multi_ap_backhaul_ssid, cfg->multi_ap_backhaul_ssid_len)` (`:701-704`) has no local bound check against `SSID_MAX_LEN`, but `cfg.multi_ap_backhaul_ssid_len` is populated in `wps_hostapd.c:1272` from `hapd->conf->multi_ap_backhaul_ssid.ssid_len`, the same config field `config_file.c` already validates `<= SSID_MAX_LEN` at parse time — not attacker-controlled wire data, not exploitable via this path.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b123`, 150 findings, `src/utils/common.c#part1of2`, lines 19-1107)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances, one file): STR34-C "assigned/converted without cast to unsigned char" fires on expressions that are not a char-value conversion at all — pointer arguments, address-of results, and pointer-to-pointer assignments.** `os_strlen(value)`/`os_strlen(str)` (`common.c:681,1039`) pass a `char *` *pointer* as an argument — no char scalar is being widened; `optarg = &argv[optind++][optchr + 1]` (`:420`) takes an address, yielding a `char *`, not a char value; `token = *last;` in `cstr_token` (`:1099`) assigns one pointer variable's value to another (`*last` dereferences a `const char **` to get a `const char *`). None of these five involve a char being converted to a wider integer type at all — a parser/rule-detection bug distinct from the already-documented "plain char-to-char, no widening" and "cross-scope name conflation" STR34-C FP classes; this one fires on non-char-typed expressions entirely. Worth checking for recurrence anywhere a pointer expression sits syntactically close to a dereference or address-of operator.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances, two functions): MEM30-C/DCL30-C misapplied to the standard `n = os_realloc_array(*res, ...); ...; *res = n;` grow-an-out-parameter idiom.** `int_array_concat` (`:909,917`) and `int_array_add_unique` (`:979,989`) each have an early branch (`os_free(*res); *res = NULL; return;`) on allocation failure, followed — only on the *other*, mutually-exclusive path — by the realloc-then-store-back sequence. sqc's free-tracking doesn't separate the branches (same root cause as the long-established "mutually-exclusive if/goto/return branches" class), flagging the realloc call as "dereferencing freed pointer" (MEM30-C) and the store-back as "writing to freed memory via res" (MEM30-C) + "local variable assigned through pointer parameter" (DCL30-C) — the last one doubly wrong since `n` is a heap pointer *value*, not local storage, and writing a heap pointer through a `T **` out-parameter is the correct, standard way to grow a caller-owned buffer.
- **Reinforces the DCL30-C/ARR00-C "local pointer variable confused with local array/automatic storage" class (5 more instances, one file):** `dup_binstr:778`, `freq_range_list_str:878`, and `wpa_config_parse_string`'s three `return str;`/`return (char *) str;` sites (`:655,678`, plus the accompanying ARR00-C at `:778`) all return a local pointer *variable* that itself points to `os_malloc()`'d heap memory — not local array storage.
- **Reinforces the ARR00-C/MEM05-C "function-`static` local array misidentified as automatic/VLA" class (2 more instances):** `wpa_ssid_txt`'s `static char ssid_txt[SSID_MAX_LEN*4+1]` (`:624,628,632`) — static storage duration, fixed compile-time size, safe to return a pointer to.
- **Reinforces the ENV01-C/MEM05-C "fires on an ordinary fixed-size buffer with zero getenv/VLA nearby" class** on the same `ssid_txt` declaration (`:624`).
- **Reinforces the MEM12-C "flow-insensitive Leaked: X list, doesn't check whether X was actually allocated/already-freed/being-returned on this path" class (3 instances, one function):** `wpa_config_parse_string:687` (str is NULL — malloc just failed, nothing to leak), `:690` (str was `os_free()`'d the line before), `:694` (`return (char *) str` is ownership transfer to the caller, the function's entire purpose — not a leak).
- **Reinforces the "mutually-exclusive if/return branches confuse free-tracking" class (ARR00-C "accessed after free" sub-shape, 4 more instances):** `wpa_config_parse_string:692`, `freq_range_list_parse:805,810,812` — in each case the only `os_free()` of the cited pointer sits in a sibling branch that returns immediately, never reaching the flagged line.
- **NEW, batch-local (2 instances, not yet 3x confirmed): DCL13-C misses a mutation performed via the `*ptr++ = value;` postfix-increment-dereference-assignment idiom**, distinct from the already-documented `param->field++` mutation-miss shape. `hwaddr_compact_aton`'s and `hwaddr_aton2`'s `addr` params (`:114,139`) are both genuinely written via `*addr++ = (a << 4) | b;` inside the function body, but DCL13-C claims "not modified, should be const" anyway.
- **NEW, batch-local: a real (if currently unreached) off-by-one buffer underflow correctly caught by ARR00-C.** `wpa_snprintf_hex_sep` (`:312`) does `pos[-1] = '\0';` unconditionally after its `for` loop; if `len == 0` the loop never executes, so `pos` still equals `buf` and the write lands one byte *before* the buffer. No current caller passes `len == 0` (grep confirms), so it's latent rather than exploitable, but a competent reviewer should flag it — contrast with the sibling `_wpa_snprintf_hex` (`:334`), which avoids the bug entirely by using `end[-1]` (always in-bounds since `buf_size >= 1` is checked) instead of `pos[-1]`. Graded TP.
- **Reconfirms the ERR07-C/ERR34-C "unchecked atoi(), no downstream validation" judgment-call class as genuinely TP here (2 instances, contrast with the `6-15_b3` FP resolution where the value *was* range-checked)**: `freq_range_list_parse`'s `atoi(pos)`/`atoi(pos2)` (`:805,810`) feed frequency-range min/max directly with no validation at all — malformed config text silently becomes a frequency of `0` instead of erroring out.
- **Reconfirms the "static/global cross-call-significance" MSC13-C FP class** on `getopt`'s `static int optchr` (`:409,431`) — assigned now, read on the *next* call via `if (optchr == 1)`.
- **Reconfirms the CON32-C/CON43-C/CON07-C/CON03-C "no pthread usage in this codebase's single-threaded tools" FP class** on the `#ifdef CONFIG_ANSI_C_EXTRA` `getopt()` reimplementation's `optchr` (`:382,384`) and `printf_decode`'s nested `switch (*pos)` (`:535,538`).
- **NEW, batch-local: MSC37-C "non-void function may reach end without returning" misapplied to a function actually declared `void`** (`wpa_unicode2ascii_inplace:461`) — a factually wrong premise, not a CFG-reachability miss.
- **NEW, batch-local: DCL37-C correctly catches a genuine double-underscore reserved identifier** (`__hide_aliasing_typecast:636`) — contrast with the already-documented single-underscore/block-scope-only DCL37-C FP class (C 7.1.3 reserves double-underscore-prefixed identifiers at *any* scope, so this one is a real, if low-severity, violation).

## Confirmed patterns (from batch `41plus_b128`, 30 findings, `src/drivers/driver_ndis.c#part2of2`, lines ~2470-3193: legacy Windows NDIS/NDISUIO/WZC driver backend)

- **Reconfirms at high density in one function family:** the mutually-exclusive-if/early-`return`-branch double-free/double-close CFG-blindness class, now hitting MEM31-C (`wpa_driver_ndis_init`'s 3 sequential `os_free(drv)` calls each in its own early-return branch, `:2840,2848,2857`) and FIO24-C (`wpa_driver_ndis_get_interfaces`'s `CloseHandle(ndisuio)` at two early-return branches plus the final success-path close, `:3011,3065` citing `:3004`) simultaneously; the `sizeof(*ptr)`-non-evaluating-context EXP33-C class (`drv:2817` in `os_zalloc(sizeof(*drv))`, `b:2980`, `niface:3047`); the DCL30-C heap-vs-stack confusion class (`drv:2931`, returned from `wpa_driver_ndis_init` but allocated via `os_zalloc`); MSC01-C no-final-else guard-clause pedantry (2 instances: `:2829,2916`); MSC37-C `#ifdef`-branch-blind reach-end (`wpa_driver_ndis_adapter_init:2696`, `wpa_driver_ndis_adapter_open:2733`, both compiled arms return on every path); ENV01-C wholesale misfire (`:2738`, zero `getenv()` in the file); CON03-C no-pthread FP (`driver_ndis_ndisuio_handle:2687`); DCL37-C block-scope-local misclassified as file-scope (`_names:3067`, a local `PTSTR` inside `wpa_driver_ndis_get_interfaces`, not file-scope); and DCL13-C plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP (`drv:2785` in `wpa_driver_ndis_adapter_close`, read-only; `global_priv:2974` in `wpa_driver_ndis_get_interfaces`, entirely unused) vs. the non-Windows stub-branch sub-shape (`drv:2672`, `wpa_driver_ndis_set_wzc`'s `#else` arm is a real no-op with a genuinely-unused param — extends the header-stub TP entry to a `.c`-file mutually-exclusive `#ifdef`/`#else` function-body stub, not just header `static inline` declarations).
- **NEW sub-shape of the ARR30-C name-based (not binding-based) buffer-size-citation conflation class: cross-`#ifdef`-branch, not just cross-function.** `wpa_driver_ndis_adapter_open`'s `WCHAR ifname[256]` (used under `#ifdef CONFIG_USE_NDISUIO`, index safely bounded by an earlier `if (len >= MAX_NDIS_DEVICE_NAME_LEN) return -1;`) is cited by sqc as "Buffer 'ifname' with size 128 allocated at line 2772" — an entirely unrelated `char ifname[128]` local declared in the mutually-exclusive `#else` arm of the very same function. `:2754`. Batch-local (1 instance) — watch for recurrence to promote out of "not yet 3x confirmed."
- **NEW sub-shape of the mutually-exclusive-branch double-free family: cross-*function*, not just cross-branch-within-one-function.** `wpa_driver_ndis_deinit`'s single, unconditional `os_free(drv)` (`:2969`) is flagged as re-freeing a `drv` "already freed" — but this function contains no earlier `os_free(drv)` at all; the only candidate earlier free of a same-named/same-typed `drv` local lives in the unrelated, already-returned-from `wpa_driver_ndis_init` (`:2840/2848/2857`). Same name+type-based (not binding-based) conflation root cause as the ARR30-C entry above and the standing EXP39-C cross-function union-conflation entry, now demonstrated on MEM31-C across a full function boundary. Also recurs at `:3193` (`wpa_driver_ndis_get_interfaces`'s non-NDISUIO-branch `os_free(niface)` conflated with the mutually-exclusive NDISUIO-branch's own earlier `os_free(niface)` in the same function, `:~3056`) — 2 instances this batch, watch for a 3rd to confirm as a standing class.
- **ARR30-C bounded-clamp-guarantees-safety reconfirmed:** `name[len] = '\0'` (`:3035`) is safe because `len` was clamped to `sizeof(name) - 1` immediately beforehand (`if (len >= sizeof(name)) len = sizeof(name) - 1;`), matching the established "earlier same-function clamp already guarantees the bound" disposition. Likewise the generic STR31-C "off-by-one, `array[i]` after a `for (i=pos; i<len; i++)` loop" heuristic misfires at `:2733` (`ifname[i] = L'\0'`) because `len < MAX_NDIS_DEVICE_NAME_LEN` was already enforced by an early-return guard.
- **INT32-C "signed subtraction may overflow" factually wrong — both operands are `size_t`.** `i - pos` (`:2753`) has `i, pos` both declared `size_t`, and the loop invariant (`i` starts at `pos`, only increments) guarantees `i >= pos` throughout, so there is no signed-overflow (or even unsigned-underflow) hazard at all.
- **EXP43-C "overlapping os_memcpy" factually wrong — dest range starts strictly after src range ends.** `os_memcpy(pos + 2, names, pos - names)` (`:3114`): dest is `[pos+2, pos+2+(pos-names))`, src is `[names, pos)`; since `pos + 2 > pos` always, `dest_start > src_end`, so the ranges are disjoint by construction. FP, not the established "same-pointer" EXP43 shape — a new "provably-disjoint-by-arithmetic" sub-shape.
- **STR34-C "char assigned without cast to unsigned char" misfires on a plain `char`-to-`char` assignment, no widening at all.** `*pos++ = pos2[0]` (`:3111`): both `pos` and `pos2` are declared `char *`; there is no wider integer type in the assignment for sign-extension to affect.
- **FN, real (low-severity, legacy/dead-path) bugs found in the UNICODE-adapter-name workaround block (`wpa_driver_ndis_get_interfaces`, non-NDISUIO branch, `:3100-3115`):** (a) the `while (pos2 < names + len)` loop reads `pos2[1]`/`pos2[2]`/`pos2[3]` (`:3106-3107`) without checking those individual offsets against `names + len`, permitting a 1-3 byte heap over-read when `pos2` is within 3 bytes of the buffer end — closest rule ARR30-C. (b) `os_memcpy(pos + 2, names, pos - names)` (`:3114`) writes up to `2*(pos-names)+2` bytes starting at `names[0]`, which can approach `len + 2` bytes into a buffer allocated with exactly `len` bytes (`_names = os_zalloc(len)`), a potential 1-2 byte heap buffer overflow write — closest rule ARR30-C. Both are old Win9x/Packet.dll compatibility code, not reachable on any currently-supported build; `upstream_present: unknown` (no separate upstream tracking checkout available in this environment).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b127`, 150 findings, `src/drivers/driver_ndis.c#part1of2`, lines 37-2408)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (22 instances, one file): DCL38-C "flexible array member should use [] not [1]" + STR31-C "character array too small" both misfire on Windows NDIS ABI-mirror struct fallback typedefs.** `NDIS_WLAN_BSSID_EX.IEs[1]`, `NDIS_802_11_WEP/KEY.KeyMaterial[1]`, `NDIS_802_11_BSSID_LIST_EX.Bssid[1]`, `NDIS_802_11_CAPABILITY.AuthenticationEncryptionSupported[1]`, `NDIS_802_11_PMKID.BSSIDInfo[1]`, `NDIS_802_11_PMKID_CANDIDATE_LIST.CandidateList[1]`, `DOT11_SCAN_REQUEST_V2.ucBuffer[1]` (lines 170,175,188,200,243,257,280,318,332,345,387) are fallback typedefs (`#ifndef OID_802_11_BSSID` etc.) intentionally mirroring the real Microsoft NDIS/Platform-SDK struct layout used when the true headers aren't available; the pre-C99 `[1]` "struct hack" is the actual Windows ABI convention here, not a local coding mistake, and the fields hold raw IE/key/candidate binary data, never NUL-terminated string content, so STR31-C's string-buffer-too-small concern is a category error on top. Twin/extends the general "flexible array member misapplied to non-char/ABI-fixed struct" theme already noted for `driver.h:2713`/`ieee802_1x_kay.h`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances): EXP36-C "alignment 1->4 cast" is factually correct-vs-wrong depending on the cast's *target* type's real alignment, refining the standing "graded TP per established disposition" default.** Casts to `(const u8 *)` (driver_ndis.c:536,564) have a target type with genuine 1-byte alignment — there is no possible alignment hazard regardless of the source buffer, and the tool's own "alignment 4" claim for `u8*` is simply wrong; graded FP. Casts to a real multi-field NDIS struct pointer with `ULONG`/enum members — `(NDIS_802_11_AUTHENTICATION_REQUEST *)`/`(NDIS_802_11_PMKID_CANDIDATE_LIST *)`/`(NDIS_802_11_STATUS_INDICATION *)` (:1552,1586,1630) — do have a genuine 4-byte alignment requirement on the destination type with an unproven-in-function source alignment; graded TP low severity per the existing disposition. Adjudicate EXP36-C by checking the cast's destination type's actual `_Alignof`, not by pattern-matching on rule text alone.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, one function): MEM30-C/EXP33-C sizeof(*ptr)-not-a-deref misfire extends to cross-#ifdef/#else-branch free-state conflation.** `ndis_get_oid`'s two mutually-exclusive `#ifdef CONFIG_USE_NDISUIO`/`#else` arms each declare their own, unrelated local named `o`; the first arm's `o` is genuinely freed on its error paths, and sqc's free-tracking bleeds that "freed" state into the second arm's fresh, never-freed `o`, flagging its `sizeof(*o)` size computation as a use-after-free dereference. Same root cause family as the standing `EXP39-C` cross-function union-name conflation and `ARR30-C`/`MEM31-C` cross-function buffer-name conflation classes, now demonstrated across `#ifdef` branches within a single function rather than across functions. `driver_ndis.c:499,566` (mirrors `ndis_set_oid`'s identical shape).
- **Reconfirms the DCL15-C/DCL19-C "should be static"/"only used in this file" misfire when the callee is invoked from a sibling translation unit sqc's cross-file scan didn't include, now for 5 non-static event-notification entry points** (`wpa_driver_ndis_event_connect/_disconnect/_media_specific/_adapter_arrival/_adapter_removal`, lines 1520,1532,1619,1650,1680) — all five are called from `src/drivers/driver_ndis_.c` (verified via grep), a companion file deliberately kept separate "to avoid conflicts with some of the header files" per its own comment; they genuinely require external linkage. Companion API00-C "no NULL check on drv" findings on the same 5 functions are the standard internal-only-API FP (drv always comes from the same internal call chain, never externally nullable).
- **NEW, batch-local: CON34-C/MSC30-C/MSC32-C rand()-quality/seeding FP-by-context class (previously batch-local, 1 instance in `driver_wext.c:1893`) now recurs a 2nd time in a near-identical twin function — promote toward confirmed.** `wpa_driver_ndis_disconnect`'s `ssid[i] = rand() & 0xff;` (`:716`) is the exact same "junk bytes to force a driver state change on disconnect" shape as the already-documented `wpa_driver_wext_disconnect`.

- **FN (real, low-severity, latent bug): `sizeof(status)` used instead of `sizeof(*status)` where `status` is `NDIS_802_11_STATUS_INDICATION *`, feeding both a pointer-advance and a length-decrement (`:1631,1632`).** sqc's ARR39-C caught this (graded TP here) but its own "double scaling" rationale doesn't quite match the actual defect — the bug is a `sizeof(ptr)` vs `sizeof(*ptr)` confusion that happens to be harmless on the 32-bit Windows targets this file historically builds for (`sizeof(NDIS_802_11_STATUS_INDICATION)==4==sizeof(pointer)` on 32-bit) but would silently underflow `data_len` (a `size_t`) on a 64-bit build where `sizeof(pointer)==8 > sizeof(struct)==4`, bypassing the `data_len < sizeof(*status)` guard in the two callees. Both old Win9x/Packet.dll compat code, not reachable on any currently-supported build. `upstream_present: unknown` (no separate upstream tracking checkout available in this environment).

## Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed (from `41plus_b138`, 17 findings, `src/ap/beacon.c#part2of2`, lines ~2919-3380: MLD per-STA-profile generation + beacon-refresh entry points)

- **NEW, batch-local (2 instances): ARR30-C "variable index" misfires when the index variable's own type range exactly matches the buffer's declared size, making out-of-bounds physically impossible regardless of loop count.** `hostapd_add_sta_profile`'s `u8 idx = non_inherit_ele_ext_list_len++;` / `u8 idx = non_inherit_ele_list_len++;` index into `u8 non_inherit_ele_ext_list[256]` / `u8 non_inherit_ele_list[256]` (`beacon.c:3054,3057`) — since `idx` is `u8` (range 0-255) and the arrays are exactly 256 elements (valid indices 0-255), every possible value of `idx` is in-bounds by construction. (There's a latent *logic* bug if more than 256 unique elements occur — `non_inherit_ele_ext_list_len++` wraps and overwrites index 0 — but that's not a memory-safety violation, which is what ARR30-C's message claims.) DCL30-C "returns pointer to local automatic storage" confuses the local pointer *variable* (`sta_profile`) with its *storage*, which is heap-allocated via `os_zalloc()` a few lines earlier in the caller (`hostapd_gen_sta_profile:3180`); EXP33-C "used uninitialized" misfires on a stack struct (`own_params`/`link_params`) populated via `hostapd_get_probe_resp_tmpl(hapd, &params, ...)`, a real (non-macro) function taking the struct's address as an output param and `os_memset`-zeroing + filling it before any possible read, with the call's own failure check gating the read (`:3212,3240`) — extends the standing output-param EXP33-C FP family from memset/recvfrom/strtol shapes to this one; ## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b135`, 150 findings, `src/common/dpp_tcp.c#part1of2`, lines 147-2500)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances, one function): MEM31-C "leak before return" blind to `dpp_connection_remove(conn)` on the immediately preceding line freeing the struct field it claims leaked.** `dpp_controller_rx`'s `conn->msg` (`wpabuf_alloc`'d at `:1786`) is flagged as leaked at 4 different `return;` statements (`:1803,1808,1817,1824`); three of those returns are directly preceded by `dpp_connection_remove(conn);`, which calls `dpp_connection_free()` and does `wpabuf_free(conn->msg);` — a real free, just interprocedural and on a struct field, which sqc's per-function leak check doesn't follow. The 4th (`:1817`) is the "need more data, wait for next `recv()`" partial-buffer-retention path — `conn->msg` is intentionally kept alive for the next call, not abandoned.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): EXP33-C "variable used uninitialized" misfires on a `struct sockaddr_in addr;` local populated by `accept(sock, (struct sockaddr *) &addr, &addr_len)` just above the flagged read.** `dpp_controller_tcp_cb:1877`, `dpp_relay_tcp_cb:2439` both read `addr.sin_addr`/`addr.sin_port` immediately after `accept()` writes through `&addr`; sqc's uninitialized-variable tracking doesn't recognize a syscall writing through an address-of parameter as initializing the variable — extends the standing "write via a function taking the destination by pointer, not tracked as an init" family (previously `os_memcpy` destination, `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref) to libc syscalls.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (8 instances across 5 call sites): API00-C "does not validate pointer/optional-string parameter" factually wrong when the parameter is demonstrably ternary-guarded (`x ? f(x) : default`) or short-circuit-checked in the very same function.** `dpp_tcp_init`'s `name` (`:2009`, `conn->name = os_strdup(name ? name : "Test");`), `dpp_tcp_auth`'s `name`/`mud_url`/`extra_conf_req_name`/`extra_conf_req_value` (`:2094`, all four assigned via a `cond ? os_strdup(cond) : NULL`/`"Test"` ternary one line below the flagged function-entry line), `dpp_controller_pkex_add`'s `code`/`identifier` (`:2304`, same ternary shape), and `dpp_relay_controller_available`'s `dpp` (`:711`, body is literally `return dpp && dl_list_len(&dpp->controllers) > 0;`) are all checked at or immediately after the point sqc claims is unguarded. Distinguish from the standing "internal-only API, never actually NULL at call sites" API00-C FP class (which applies when there's genuinely no check anywhere) — this is a stronger, purely-textual misfire: the check is right there in the function body.
- **NEW, batch-local (not yet 3x confirmed): MEM30-C "use-after-free" misfires on a struct-field pointer that is `wpabuf_free()`'d then reassigned to a fresh value on the very next 1-2 lines, before the flagged access.** `conn->msg_out` (`dpp_relay_tx:545`) and `auth->csr` (`dpp_tcp_build_csr:1545`) are both freed and then immediately reassigned (`conn->msg_out = dpp_tcp_encaps(...)`, `auth->csr = dpp_build_csr(...)`); the flagged line is a NULL-check/use of the *new* value, not the freed one. Same root-cause family as the already-documented "MEM30 reassign + fresh-binding fix" (task 232) but for a struct *field* rather than a local variable — the existing fix apparently only covers locals.
- **FN, real (medium-confidence, latent — not currently exploitable): wrong length variable passed as `maxlen` to `printf_encode()`.** `dpp_controller_rx_gas_req` (`:1452-1455`) allocates `buf = os_malloc(e_len * 4 + 1)` (sized for `auth->e_name`'s length, `e_len`) but calls `printf_encode(buf, len * 4 + 1, (const u8 *) auth->e_name, e_len)` — passing the *outer function's* `len` parameter (the incoming GAS Configuration Request message length, unrelated to `e_name`) as the buffer-size bound instead of `e_len`. Currently harmless because `printf_encode`'s internal loop is bounded by the correctly-passed 4th argument (`e_len`), so the maximum possible write (`4*e_len+1`) exactly matches the real allocation regardless of what `maxlen` says — but if `len` and `e_len` were ever to invert their current relationship (message length could in principle be smaller than the enrollee-name string carried in the DPP negotiation), the `end` boundary computed from the wrong `maxlen` would be miscalibrated. Closest rule: STR31-C (buffer sizing) / ARR38-C. `upstream_present: unknown` (no separate upstream tracking checkout in this environment) — matches upstream hostap as of the pinned commit, not a regression introduced locally.
- Reconfirms established patterns at high density (not re-detailed above): CON32-C/POS49-C bit-field-without-mutex + CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()`/`inet_ntoa()` thread-safety, all firing in this single-threaded (`eloop`-driven, zero pthread) file (~50 instances total, the largest class this batch); MSC05-C direct `time_t - time_t` subtraction — genuine (low-severity) TP, not the scalar-offset-adjustment FP shape (2 instances: `:2157,2942`); ERR07-C/ERR34-C `atoi()` TP/FP split reconfirmed: unguarded lookup-key/numeric-field TP (10 instances: `:114,145,321,850,861,890,921,3276,3295,3607`) vs. explicit post-`atoi()` sentinel/range/exhaustive-switch guard FP (3 instances: `hostapd_dpp_listen`'s `if (freq <= 0) return -1;` `:978`; the `ver=`-parsing exhaustive `if(v==1)/else if(v==2)/else return -1;` `:3338`; `hostapd_dpp_pkex_remove`'s `if (id_val == 0) return -1;` `:3375`).
- **NEW FN (control-flow correctness, not currently exploitable): missing `else` merges two independent `if`/`else-if` chains into one, only benign because a variable is hardcoded.** `hostapd_dpp_pb_pkex_init`'s `} if (sae && psk && pass_hex) {` (`:2547`) should be `} else if (...)` — as written, after the `conf_id > 0` chain (`:2535-2546`) completes (even by falling through with no match), the second independent chain is *also* evaluated. Currently harmless only because `conf_id` is hardcoded `-1` and never set `> 0` (see the file's own TODO at `:2500-2503`); if that TODO is ever implemented, a `conf_id > 0` match would fall through into re-evaluating the second chain, potentially overwriting the already-built `cmd` or hitting the final `else`'s `str_clear_free(pass_hex); ...; return;` even though a valid config was already produced. Closest rule: MSC01-C (guard-clause completeness), though the defect is really "two if-chains merged without else," not "missing final else" per se. `upstream_present: unknown` (no separate upstream tracking checkout available in this environment).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b143`, 150 findings, `src/fst/fst_ctrl_iface.c#part1of2`, lines 1-860)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (very high density, ~20 findings across 6 call sites, one file): `foreach_fst_group(g)` / `foreach_fst_group_iface(g, f)` unexpanded macro-loop headers get misparsed as K&R-style nested function definitions, cascading MSC13-C/MSC37-C/EXP33-C false positives — extends the existing `dl_list_for_each`/`foreach_fst_group` macro-blindness theme (which was previously confirmed only for DCL30-C, `16-40_b19`) to three more rule IDs via a distinct parse-shape mechanism.** Every `struct fst_group *g;` (or `*f`/`unsigned num`) declaration whose only use is inside a `foreach_fst_group(g) { ... }` / `foreach_fst_group_iface(g, f) { ... }` block gets a spurious MSC13-C "declared but never used" at the *declaration* line (sqc doesn't connect the outer variable to the macro-argument occurrence), while the macro-call-plus-brace-block itself (`foreach_fst_group(g) {`) gets parsed as if it were an old-style/K&R function definition — producing a false MSC37-C "non-void function may reach end without returning" and a false EXP33-C "'g' used uninitialized" *on the macro-invocation line itself*. Seen in `get_fst_group_by_id` (`:21,23`x2), `fst_ctrl_iface_notify` (`:85,97`x2), `get_peer_mbies` (`:562,575`x2), `list_groups` (`:631,634`x2), and `fst_ctrl_iface_mb_info`'s doubly-nested `foreach_fst_group(g){foreach_fst_group_iface(g,f){...}}` (`:745,746,747,750,752` — hits all three of `g`/`f`/`num`). Worth an sqc engine-level fix: recognize `foreach_fst_group`/`foreach_fst_group_iface` (and similarly-shaped `IDENT(args) { block }` macro-loop headers generally) as loop constructs, not candidate function definitions.
- **Reconfirms/extends established patterns at volume:** API05-C `T*,size_t` idiom on every `(session_id/group_id, char *buf, size_t buflen)`-shaped ctrl_iface handler signature (30+ instances) and on `(const char*, bool*, char**)`/`(const char*, char*, size_t, char**)` param-reader helpers; DCL13-C output-buffer-write-via-callee-or-alias FP extended to `os_snprintf(buf+ret,...)`-style forwarding (`buf` in `list_ifaces`/`print_band`/`fst_ctrl_iface_mb_info`, `:629,661,743`) and to a `cur_dest = buf` alias write (`fst_read_next_text_param`, `:839`), plus the fixed-callback-typedef FP on `list_session_enum_cb`'s `g` param (matches `fst_session_enum_clb`, `:469`); ERR02-C `os_snprintf()` misidentified as `sprintf()` (9 instances: `:501,670,672,676,678,681,683,685,687`); EXP30-C pure-accessor-args (`fst_iface_get_wpa_obj_ctx`, `MAC2STR`, `wpabuf_head`/`wpabuf_len`, `fst_iface_get_name`, 8 instances); ERR33-C/ERR00-C/ERR01-C/ERR30-C `strtoul()` genuine (low-severity) TP bundle, extending the `ctrl_iface.c:8899` "zero/weak validation" precedent to 7 more call sites in one file (`session_get/remove/initiate/transfer/teardown`'s bare `strtoul(id,NULL,0)` with no check at all, and `session_set/respond`'s `strtoul(id,&p,0)` with only a trailing-`' '`-character check, never a numeric range/errno guard); EXP34-C null-deref-on-strtoul-endptr FP (2 instances: `:225,335`); EXP45-C already-parenthesized `!(q = os_strchr(...))` idiom FP (`:225`); MSC01-C no-default-but-exhaustive-enum-switch pedantry (`switch(event_type)` covers all 5 `enum fst_event_type` values, `:108`); MSC07-C goto-label-after-return (`problem:` reached via earlier `goto`, `:590`); MSC13-C dl_list/loop-carried-read blindness (`found=1` read at the very next `if(!found)`, `:534`); MSC21-C misapplied to a pointer/cursor-sentinel loop (`addr != NULL` with a function-call "step" — not an arithmetic counter that can skip a target, `:543`); MEM31-C ownership-transfer-to-persistent-list FP (`fst_session_create()` adds `s` to `global_sessions_list` via `dl_list_add_tail`, freed later via `fst_session_delete` — not a leak, 2 instances `:261,269`); ARR30-C bounded-NUL-terminated-scan FP (`while(*temp) ... temp++`, `:804`); ENV01-C wholesale zero-`getenv()` misfire (`:560`); DCL15-C/DCL19-C cross-file-linkage-via-own-header-declaration FP (`fst_ctrl_cli`, declared `extern` in `fst_ctrl_iface.h`, `:740`); API00-C internal-only-API FP (`params`/`buflen` always non-NULL/fixed-size at every internal call site, 5 instances: `:743,821,839`x2,`839` dup); WIN04-C platform-inapplicable misfire on a UNIX ctrl_iface command-dispatch table (`:770`); ARR02-C array-sized-by-own-initializer genuine-if-trivial TP (`band_names[]`/`commands[]`, `:650,770`).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances): STR00-C/STR37-C `isspace()` missing `(unsigned char)` cast graded genuine (low-severity) TP, per the established `wpas_dbus_getter_state`/`tolower()` precedent that "the cast really is absent" even when runtime input is locally-trusted.** Every `isspace(p[0])`/`isspace(*temp)`/`isspace(**endp)` call in this file passes a plain (signed) `char`/`const char*` dereference with no cast (`:570,799,805,831,846,854`). Same disposition for `strtol()`'s missing `errno=0` reset/check (`fst_read_next_int_param`, `:830`, 2 rules) — no downstream range check substitutes for ERANGE detection.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: STR34-C misapplied to a `char**`-dereference *pointer* assignment, not a `char` scalar at all.** `*endp = (char *) params;` (`fst_read_next_int_param`/`fst_read_next_text_param`, `:827,845`) assigns a `char*` pointer value through a `char **endp` — there is no `char`-typed value being widened/sign-extended here, the rule's own type premise is factually wrong. Paired `EXP05-C` "cast away const" on the same lines is a legitimate but harmless read-only overlay, required by `strtol()`-style `char **endptr` contracts (pointer only ever advanced/read afterward, never written through).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM33-C "direct assignment of flexible array structure instances" wholly misapplied to a plain scalar char copy.** `*cur_dest = **endp;` (`fst_read_next_text_param:855`) is an ordinary one-byte character copy in a manual string-copy loop — no struct, no flexible array member, anywhere near this line. Paired STR34-C findings on the same line (3 instances: `:855`x3,`860`) are the already-established plain-char-to-char-assignment-no-widening FP class (`*cur_dest = **endp`, `*cur_dest = 0`).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b137`, 150 findings, `src/ap/beacon.c#part1of2`, lines 17-2950: beacon/probe-response IE builders, MBSSID/FILS-discovery frame construction, `sta_track_*`, `ieee802_11_build_ap_params`)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (very high density, 7 instances): DCL13-C "not modified" premise is factually wrong (not just low-value) for the file's `eid`/`pos` IE-builder parameters — these functions' entire purpose is to write through the pointer.** `hostapd_eid_ds_params:90`, `hostapd_eid_erp_info:105`, `hostapd_eid_pwr_constraint:129` (`eid` aliased by local `pos`, written via `*pos++`), `hostapd_eid_country_add:197` (`pos`), `hostapd_eid_ecsa:502`, `hostapd_eid_supported_op_classes:552`, `hostapd_eid_mbssid_config:656` all do `*eid++ = ...`/`*pos++ = ...` at least once in the function body. Contrast with the same functions' `hapd` param (read-only, correctly a genuine if low-value TP) and with `end`/`start`/`prev` in `hostapd_eid_country_add` (also genuinely read-only, correctly TP) — the split has to be checked per-parameter, not per-function.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances, one file): DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable" fires on `return eid;`/`return pos;` where `eid` is literally the function's own parameter (not a local at all) returned unchanged on an early-exit branch, or `pos`/`info` is a pointer derived from/aliasing a parameter or a `dl_list`-owned node.** `hostapd_eid_pwr_constraint:137,141,149,160` (`return eid;`, the parameter itself), `:193` (`return pos;`, `pos = eid` alias), `hostapd_eid_country:270,312,318` (same shape), `sta_track_get:1280` (`info` walks a heap-owned `dl_list`). Same root family as the already-documented "local pointer variable vs. local storage" confusion, extended here to the degenerate case where the "local variable" is actually the parameter itself.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (13 instances, one file): ARR36-C "pointers from different arrays" fires on `epos - pos`/`tailend - tailpos` bounds-remaining computations where both operands are provably the same output buffer (`epos = pos + len` / `tailend = tail + tail_len`, set once at function entry) — AND cites a variable name (`cca_pos`) that doesn't appear anywhere on the flagged line at all, just because a `cca_pos` local exists elsewhere in the same function.** `hostapd_probe_resp_fill_elems:848,867,868,873,874,932,986,1017,1018,1019,1021,1022,1023` (cites `param:pos`/`cca_pos`) and `ieee802_11_build_ap_params:2357,2374,2375,2377,2378,2446,2490` (cites `tail`/`cca_pos`). Extends the established `pos`/`end`-paired-buffer ARR36-C FP class with a concrete cross-line name-misattribution mechanism (previously only documented once, `driver_ndis.c` `41plus_b127`) — now confirmed 3x+ in a single file, promoting it to a general rule: always check whether the cited variable names actually occur on the flagged line before trusting an ARR36-C/ARR00-C message.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: ARR36-C "pointer comparison" category error — fires on two plain scalar (`u8`) locals, neither a pointer, and cites variable names absent from the line.** `hostapd_gen_fils_discovery_nss:1990`: `if (rx_nss > max_nss)` compares two `u8` values; the message cites `mcs[3 * i]` and `tx_nss`, neither of which appears on this line (they're used two lines earlier/later in the same small loop). Worse than the same-buffer misattribution above — there is no pointer type involved at all.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): ARR00-C misidentifies a bare `const u8 *` struct-pointer *field* (not a fixed-size array) as a 1-element array, flagging in-bounds `field + 1` advances as one-past-the-end.** `struct ieee802_11_elems::interworking` is declared `const u8 *interworking;` (`ieee802_11_common.h:72`, a pointer into the wire buffer, sized separately by `interworking_len`); `elems.interworking + 1` (guarded by `interworking_len == 7 || == 9`, `beacon.c:1649,1651`) is flagged as going "1 elements past the end of array elems.interworking[0]". New sub-shape of the established decayed-pointer/array-decay confusion family (previously seen on ARR01-C `sizeof`), now on ARR00-C bounds tracking for a struct pointer field rather than a function parameter.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances): INT14-C "bitwise+arithmetic on the same variable" fires when the bitwise op is actually on a *derived difference/shift expression* built from the variable, not on the variable itself.** `(pos - eid) & 1` (`hostapd_eid_country:310`) flags both `eid:265` and `pos:275` even though neither ever appears in a raw bitwise expression — only their difference does. `0x3 << (i * 2)` (`hostapd_gen_fils_discovery_nss:1949`) flags `i:1947` the same way (arithmetic `i*2` feeds a shift on the constant `0x3`, not on `i`). `(nss - 1) << FD_CAP_NSS_SHIFT` (`:2003`) flags `nss:2004` identically. `sizeof(hapd->conf->ssid.short_ssid) - 1 | FLAGS` flags `hapd:2083` even though `hapd` only ever appears via `->` member access. Extends the existing base-identifier/derived-expression INT14-C conflation family (previously documented for dereferenced-pointee and struct-member sub-shapes) to the pointer-difference and shift-count sub-shapes.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: EXP34-C "potential null pointer dereference" on a value whose non-NULL-ness is guaranteed by a *different variable's* boolean flag set earlier under the identical guard, not by a direct check on the dereferenced pointer itself.** `hostapd_gen_fils_discovery`'s `ctl |= FD_FRAME_CTL_MD_PRESENT` is set (`:2108`) only inside `if (mobility_domain)`; the later access `&mobility_domain[2]` (`:2181`) is itself guarded by `if (ctl & FD_FRAME_CTL_MD_PRESENT)`, so it is unreachable unless `mobility_domain` was non-NULL. sqc doesn't correlate the flag bit back to the pointer that set it. New sub-shape of the existing correlated-conditional-assignment blind spot (previously documented for a shared `res<0` guard on a same-branch `title` assignment, `wpa_common.c` `41plus_b91`).
- **Reconfirms established patterns at volume (not re-detailed above):** PRE08-C `ieee802_11*.h` header-family low-value-TP convention (6 instances, `:17`x3,`18`x2,`25`); DCL13-C plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP on read-only `hapd`/`params`/`mode`/`own_fdata`/`end`/`start`/`prev` (16 instances); EXP40-C phantom cast-away-const where neither side is const (`local_pwr_constraint`/`pos`, 2 instances: `:189,191`); ARR39-C pure-integer-sum-no-pointer misfire on `len +=`/`buflen +=`/`tail_len +=` sizing accumulators (12 instances: `:681`x3,`686,767`x3,`777,779,1410,2267`x2); MSC01-C no-final-else/no-default guard-clause pedantry (9 instances: `:793,966,1582,1974,2021,2551,2608`, all provably-deliberate mutually-exclusive dispatch chains with a safe pre-initialized/zero default); EXP30-C pure-accessor-args (`wpabuf_head`/`wpabuf_len` sibling args, `MAC2STR`, `wpa_ssid_txt`, `hostapd_get_oper_chwidth`/`_centr_freq_seg0/1_idx`/`hostapd_get_punct_bitmap`, 12 instances); ARR01-C `sizeof(*ptr)`/`sizeof(ptr->fixed_scalar_or_array_member)`-correct-idiom misattributed as decayed-pointer sizeof (7 instances: `params->mld_info:1101`, `hapd->partner_links[...]:1141`, `hapd->conf->ssid.short_ssid:2083,2152`, `*params:2243,2856`); API00-C internal-only-API no-NULL-check FP (9 instances: `hostapd_wpa_ie:322`, `sta_track_*:1286`x2,`1320,1347`x2,`1880`, `ieee802_11_build_ap_params:2229`); os_free(NULL)-is-safe EXP34-C FP (3 instances: `:648,2312,2313`); MSC07-C goto-target-label-after-return blindness (2 instances: `fail:646`, `fail:1157`); EXP34-C "callee guarantees non-null" (`hostapd_mbssid_get_tx_bss()` never returns NULL — `hostapd.c:96-102` — 5 instances: `:625,749,837,1069`; plus a `while ((info = dl_list_first(...)))` self-guard, `:1258`); API05-C `T*,size_t` idiom (1 instance: `:1365`); EXP33-C output-param-memset-first misfire (`hostapd_allowed_address`'s `out`, `os_memset(out,0,sizeof(*out))` as its first statement, `:1479`); DCL37-C double-underscore reserved-identifier genuine TP (`__ieee802_11_set_beacon:2717`, matches the `__ieee802_11_parse_elems`/`__AKM` precedent); MSC13-C dead-assignment-misses-a-later-read-past-the-loop-boundary FP (8 instances, one function: `hostapd_add_sta_profile`'s `ie_found`/`non_inherit_ele_*`/`add_vendor_ies`/`is_identical_vendor_ies`/`num_link_elem_vendor_ies`, all read after the `for_each_element` loop or later in the same iteration, `:2919-2924,2950`).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM12-C "Function returns without releasing all resources" both correctly and incorrectly flags the *same* `head`/`tail` pair in the same function, depending on the specific return — a genuine flow-insensitive-vs-genuine-leak split, not a uniform FP class.** `ieee802_11_build_ap_params`'s early-failure returns at `:2314,2396` are FP (tail/tailpos already `os_free()`'d on the immediately preceding line of that same branch); the success-path return at `:2684` is FP (tail is transferred to `params->tail` at `:2591`, an ownership transfer, not a leak). But the three early `return -1;` returns inside the `CONFIG_SAE` offload block (`:2571,2577,2584`) are a **genuine TP** — `head`/`tail` (and `resp`) are allocated earlier in the function (`:2248,2309,2540`) but only assigned into `params->head`/`params->tail`/`params->proberesp` at `:2589-2593`, *after* this block; all three early returns leak all three buffers. Worth flagging generally: MEM12-C's per-return "Leaked: X, Y" list must be checked per-return, since the same function can legitimately mix real leaks with false ones on different branches.
- **FN (real, narrow, low-severity): memory leak of `link_params.resp` on the `hostapd_gen_sta_profile()` failure branch inside the per-STA-profile MLD loop.** `hostapd_gen_per_sta_profiles` (`beacon.c:3184-3282`, outside this batch's covered line range but read for FN purposes) calls `hostapd_get_probe_resp_tmpl(link_bss, &link_params, true)` (`:3233`, allocates `link_params.resp`), then if the subsequent `hostapd_gen_sta_profile()` call fails (`:3249-3257`, e.g. `sta_profile_len` is 0 or exceeds `EHT_ML_MAX_STA_PROF_LEN`, or the internal `os_zalloc` fails) the loop does `continue;` without ever calling `os_free(link_params.resp)` — the only such free (`:3277`) is reached only on the success path. Each affiliated-MLD-link iteration that hits this branch leaks one probe-response-template buffer (roughly the size of `hostapd_probe_resp_elems_len()`, easily >100 bytes). Not present in the batch's own findings (this line range is likely covered by the file's part2of2). `upstream_present: unknown` (no separate upstream tracking checkout available to confirm against this pinned clone).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b147`, 150 findings, `src/crypto/crypto_module_tests.c#part1of2`, lines 27-2491: crypto/AES/SIV/OMAC/MD5/SHA1/SHA256/SHA384/HPKE/MSCHAP module self-tests)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (rule-engine bug, 3 instances): ARR30-C "out-of-bounds access" cites the wrong function's same-named local variable as the allocation site.** This file declares `const u8 *addr[N]`/`size_t len[N]` locals independently in 5 different self-test functions (sizes 3, 3, 2, 2, 2 at lines 89, 227, 943, 1840, 1950). Findings inside the two size-3 functions (`test_siv`/`test_omac1_vector`, `:123,255,271`, all `addr[2] = ...`) are flagged as "size 2 (allocated at line 1950)" — line 1950 is a completely unrelated size-2 `addr` declared in `test_sha384`, a different function entirely. The actual in-scope array is size 3 and every access is in-bounds. sqc's array-size tracking appears to pick up the *last* same-named declaration seen anywhere in the file rather than the one in the current function's scope. Worth an engine-level fix: array-bound provenance must be scope-qualified, not name-only.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (rule-engine bug, 12 instances, one function): ARR01-C "sizeof applied to pointer/array parameter... decayed to a pointer" fires on file-scope `static const u8 foo[]` array identifiers that are not parameters at all.** `test_sha1`'s `sizeof(key0)`/`sizeof(data0)`/`sizeof(prf0)`/`key1`/`data1`/`prf1`/`key2`/`data2`/`prf2` (`:1357-1377`) all refer to `static const u8` arrays declared at file scope (`:1158-1215`); `test_sha1` itself takes no parameters (`void`). sqc misidentifies these as decayed function-parameter arrays. Distinct from (but adjacent to) the already-documented "sizeof(ptr->fixed_array_member)"/"sizeof(*ptr)" ARR01-C correct-idiom misfire family — this is a plain identifier-classification bug, not a member-access or dereference misparse.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances, one file): EXP36-C "alignment issue" casting `char *` to `const u8 *` is a category error — `u8` is `typedef uint8_t`/`unsigned char`, alignment 1, identical to `char`, not the claimed alignment 4.** `test_sha384`'s `(const u8 *) data` where `data` is `const char *` (`:1963,1973,1975`). No real alignment mismatch is possible between two 1-byte-aligned types; sqc's alignment table appears to have a wrong entry for `u8` (perhaps conflating it with `u32`/a 4-byte type).
- **Reconfirms established classes at very high density in a pure self-test/test-vector file:** ARR02-C implicit-bounds-on-initializer-sized-array (80 instances, the largest single class in this batch — every hardcoded RFC/NIST test-vector array in the file); MSC09-C non-ASCII-byte-in-`\x`-escaped-raw-hash-constant (14 instances, MD5/SHA test-vector expected-output byte strings, `:905-938`); MSC01-C no-final-else guard-clause pedantry (3 instances: `:852,868,884`, all `if(...)else if(os_memcmp(...)!=0){...}` result-check chains where "no error" is the correct implicit default); MEM05-C fixed-`sizeof()`-based/compile-time-constant array misidentified as a VLA (2 instances: `:88` `2*AES_BLOCK_SIZE+sizeof(plaintext_2)`, `:311` `data[sizeof(msg)]`); ARR39-C "scaled pointer arithmetic" misapplied to a plain array-declarator size expression with no pointer operand at all (`u8 out[2*AES_BLOCK_SIZE+sizeof(plaintext_2)]`, `:88`); EXP33-C "may be used uninitialized" on a local `addr[]` whose every used element is assigned earlier in the same straight-line block before use (3 instances: `:274,952,1850`); the reassign-then-free MEM30/MEM31-C double-free FP class extended to a plain local `tmp`/`res_pt` reused across 2-3 sequential malloc-or-alloc/use/free cycles in the same function, each free targeting a *different* live allocation (`tmp`: `:873,889` after fresh `os_malloc()` at `:861,877`; `res_pt`: `:2446` after fresh `hpke_base_open()` reassignment at `:2417-2418`) plus its sibling MEM12-C false-leak-on-an-alloc-failed-branch shape (`tmp` NULL on the `if(!tmp)return -1;` branch itself, `:863,879,892`) and false-leak-immediately-after-the-actual-free shape (`res_pt` freed on the line directly above the flagged return, `:2450`); MSC37-C preprocessor-branch-blind "reach end without returning" (4 instances: `:896,984,1945,2473` — 3 of the 4 are `#ifndef X ... #else ... #endif` shapes where both arms return; the 4th, `test_sha256`, has a single unconditional `return errors;` with no `#ifdef` involved at all — a CFG bug, not preprocessor-blindness, on a function with several brace-less `if/else` result-check chains and a nested nested-`#ifdef`-inside-`if(key)` block; all 4 findings are also line-misattributed to the *next* function's signature line rather than the actual function body); EXP30-C pure-accessor-args (`wpabuf_head`/`wpabuf_len` sibling arguments, 6 instances: `:2348,2356,2367,2405,2418,2428`); EXP34-C "passing NULL to a function that doesn't check" where the callee explicitly does (`wpa_hexdump_buf`'s `buf ? wpabuf_head(buf) : NULL` ternary in `wpa_debug.h:115-118`, `:2363`); EXP43-C "overlapping restrict-qualified regions" on a function (`crypto_ec_key_set_pub`) whose `x`/`y` params are plain `const u8 *`, not restrict-qualified at all (`:2395`) — same "no restrict anywhere" root cause as the general EXP43-C misfire family; CON07-C/CON32-C/CON33-C-style no-pthread "unsynchronized shared static access" misfire (`test_sha1`, zero threading anywhere in this file, `:1349`); DCL00-C/STR05-C genuine (if low-value) TPs on `username`/`password`/`iv_c` locals that truly are never modified after initialization (`:42,2477,2478`) — no FP counter-pattern found for these two rules in this file.
- **NEW, batch-local (not yet 3x confirmed elsewhere): MSC41-C "hard-coded sensitive information" and MEM03-C "sensitive buffer not cleared" both misfire on published RFC test-vector constants inside a one-shot module self-test, not live secret material.** `test_ms_funcs`'s `password = "clientPass"` (`:2478`) is the literal RFC 2759 MS-CHAP example password (a public, published constant, not a real credential) — MSC41-C's "don't embed secrets in source" concern doesn't apply to a publicly-known test fixture. The same buffer, plus `password_hash`/`master_secret` (`:2478,2487,1004`), are also flagged MEM03-C "not cleared before exit" — but these are RFC/EAP-FAST test vectors used exactly once by a startup self-test, never real user secrets, so there is nothing sensitive to scrub. Adjacent to (but distinct from) the already-documented "MEM03-C misfire on a random decoy buffer that isn't actually secret material" class (`stub_password`) — here the buffers *are* the algorithm's real working data, just sourced from a public test vector rather than live input.
