## Confirmed/reinforced patterns (from batch `41plus_b158`, 145 findings, 1 file: `src/radius/radius.c`, lines 52-1953, effectively the whole file: RADIUS message alloc/free/dump/finish/verify, MPPE-key encrypt/decrypt, VLAN/tunnel-password attribute parsing)

- **REINFORCED at high volume (7 instances): the cross-function array-size/decl-site conflation bug on ARR30-C (previously confirmed in `41plus_b147`'s crypto self-tests and `41plus_b151`'s ctrl_iface_unix.c) recurs identically in ordinary (non-test, non-ctrl_iface) production code.** `radius_msg_finish_srv`/`radius_msg_verify_das_req`/`radius_msg_verify` each declare their own local `const u8 *addr[4]` and write `addr[3] = secret;` — all in-bounds — but sqc cites "Buffer 'addr' with size 3 (allocated at line 1788)", where line 1788 is an unrelated `const u8 *addr[3]` declared inside `radius_msg_get_tunnel_password`, a different function entirely (`:514,636,667,1063`). The same bug recurs on `buf`/`pos` (3 more instances, `:1541,1847,1867`), where a completely different function's parameter/heap pointer is cited against the unrelated local `char buf[10]` declared at line 1684 inside `radius_msg_get_vlanid` — and in one case (`:1557`) the "buffer" being bounds-checked is actually a `size_t` loop index, not a pointer at all. Confirms this is a systemic, name-only (not scope-qualified) array-provenance bug in sqc's bounds engine, not confined to test/self-test files.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (10 instances, one file): EXP34-C "potential null pointer dereference" fires on `attr`/`tmp` immediately after `radius_get_attr_hdr(msg, i)`, a static helper that is pure pointer arithmetic (`wpabuf_mhead_u8(msg->buf) + msg->attr_pos[idx]`) and can never return NULL.** Seen at `:678,947,982,1084,1127,1591,1615,1638,1695,1941` — every one of this file's attribute-iteration loops. sqc appears to treat *any* pointer-typed local assigned from a function call as potentially-NULL by default, without checking whether the callee's return expression can actually produce NULL. Distinct from the established "callee guarantees non-null" EXP34-C FP class (which was about a documented/observed callee contract) — here the callee is trivially provably non-null from its one-line body.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances, one function, `decrypt_ms_key`/sibling `radius_msg_add_mppe_keys`): MEM12-C/ARR00-C free-tracking is flow-insensitive across independent branches of the same `if`, producing both false leaks and false use-after-frees on the same handful of lines.** `plain[0]` is read (`ARR00-C` "accessed after freed", `:1231`x2,`1237,1243`) on branches where `plain` was never freed at all yet on that path (the read always precedes that branch's own `os_free(plain)`), while separately `MEM12-C` "leaked ppos, plain" fires on returns immediately *after* the correct `os_free(plain)` in the same branch (`:1222,1234,1240,1245`) or on the alloc-failed branch where nothing was ever allocated (`:1201,1431`). Also flags `ppos` as a separately-leaked resource even though it is never anything but an alias pointer walking through `plain`'s own buffer, never a second allocation.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM31-C "double free" fires when a pointer is freed, then reassigned to a fresh allocation, then freed a second time — sqc's double-free tracking doesn't clear "freed" state on reassignment (contrast with the MEM30-C/task-232 fix, which does).** `key` in `radius_msg_get_ms_keys` (`os_free(key)` at :1329, reassigned via a fresh `radius_msg_get_vendor_attr()` call at :1332, freed again at :1344) and `buf` in `radius_msg_add_mppe_keys` (freed at :1423, reassigned via fresh `os_malloc()` at :1429, freed again at :1449) are both flagged as double-frees of the *same* allocation; both are actually two independent, correctly-freed allocations that happen to share a variable name.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances): EXP33-C "may be used uninitialized" fires on an `addr[]`/`elen[]` (or `len[]`) array element that is only ever *read* under the exact count guard that also gates whether it was *written* two lines earlier — e.g. `md5_vector(first ? 3 : 2, addr, elen, hash)` only touches `addr[2]` when `first` is true, which is exactly when `addr[2] = ...` was just assigned.** `decrypt_ms_key:1219`, `encrypt_ms_key:1286`, `radius_msg_get_tunnel_password:1841` (a variant where the same `addr[3]` is reused across two sequential calls with different counts, 2 then 3, in the same function). New sub-shape of the file's broader "correlated guard" EXP33-C blind spot, specific to a `count`-parameterized vector-hash-input array rather than a boolean-gated scalar.
- **NEW FN (2 instances, same bug in two sibling functions): missing length validation before a fixed-size `os_memcpy` from an attacker-controlled RADIUS attribute.** `radius_msg_verify_das_req:699` and `radius_msg_verify_msg_auth:996` both do `os_memcpy(orig, attr + 1, MD5_MAC_LEN)` (16 bytes) on a `Message-Authenticator` attribute located purely by `type` match, with no check that `attr->length >= sizeof(*attr) + MD5_MAC_LEN`. A RADIUS peer that sends a short Message-Authenticator attribute (RADIUS attribute length is an attacker-controlled 8-bit field) causes an out-of-bounds read past the actual attribute into adjacent message-buffer/heap memory. Not present in sqc's own findings for this file — a real miss in exactly the "RADIUS attribute parsing without length validation on attacker-controlled wire data" class the audit brief calls out as a priority FN area.
- **Reconfirms established classes at high density:** API00-C internal-only-API FP (24 instances, this file's largest single class — every accessor/getter/setter taking `msg`/`secret`/`data`/`attrs`/`id` as a param, plus several integer-overflow sub-variants on lengths that are always internally/config-derived, never attacker-controlled at that specific call boundary); DCL13-C plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP (13 instances: `:52,58,65,316,621,718,1025,1099,1303,1352,1507,1782,1932`); the `sizeof(*uninitialized_ptr)`-is-a-non-evaluating-context EXP33-C class (7 instances: `:106,856,872,887,1125,1313,1362,1396` — sizes assigned right before a `os_zalloc`/`os_calloc`/`os_memdup` call); ARR01-C `sizeof(ptr->fixed_array_member)`/`sizeof(*ptr)`-is-the-correct-idiom misattributed as decayed-pointer sizeof (7 instances: `:82,500,703,725,1002,1102`); DCL30-C local-pointer-*variable*-vs-heap-storage confusion (9 instances: `:119,453,903,968,1162,1245,1347,1377` — every one of this file's "returns pointer to local variable" findings is actually `os_zalloc`/`os_memdup`/`wpabuf_alloc`-backed heap memory); EXP30-C pure-accessor-args (`wpabuf_head`/`wpabuf_len` sibling args to `hmac_md5`/`md5_vector`, 6 instances: `:471,501,544,704,1004`, plus the side-effect-free logging-macro variant at `:415`); MEM10-C ad-hoc-NULL-check stylistic pedantry (5 instances: `:129,941,1031,1118,1895`); ARR39-C pure-integer-sum-no-pointer misfire (2 instances: `:1419,1445`, `hlen + elen - sizeof(vendor_id)` assigned to a plain integer struct field); MSC07-C goto-target-reached-by-earlier-goto blindness (`radius_msg_parse`'s `fail:` label, `:905`); DCL37-C block-scope-local-`_len` misclassified as file-scope (`:1257`, extending the established `_ftie` precedent to a new identifier); ARR02-C array-sized-by-its-own-compile-time-initializer (`radius_attrs[]:171`); MSC01-C no-final-else/no-default guard-clause pedantry on provably-intentional "ignore unrecognized value" dispatch (3 instances: `:760,1706,1742`); ARR00-C "reading from uninitialized array" on a bare `&tunnel[idx]` address-of expression that never actually reads the array's contents, on an array that was also `os_memset` to 0 beforehand anyway (3 instances: `:1702,1704,1751`); the pointer-mistaken-for-a-1-element-array ARR00-C shape, now on a heap pointer (`str`) whose real bound was already explicitly checked earlier in the same function (`:1883`).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b151`, 150 findings, 1 file:
`wpa_supplicant/ctrl_iface_unix.c`, entire file, lines 26-1388)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (9 instances, one file): POS02-C "privileged operation without subsequent privilege dropping" fires on every `chmod`/`bind` call in the UNIX-domain ctrl_iface setup, but wpa_supplicant/hostapd never drop privileges after startup — the process needs ongoing elevated capabilities (netlink, driver ioctls) for its entire lifetime, so there is no "drop privileges after this privileged op" step to be missing.** `wpas_ctrl_iface_open_sock`'s `chmod:557,594,660` / `bind:621,635`, and `wpas_global_ctrl_iface_open_sock`'s `bind:1231,1244,1258` / `chmod:1309,1316` are all just setting up a local control-socket's permissions/path, not the kind of "bind privileged port, then setuid down" pattern POS02-C targets. Treat as FP by default anywhere in hostap unless a specific function is shown to actually call `setuid`/`setgid` elsewhere in the same process lifecycle.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances, one file): DCL31-C "called without prior declaration" fires on `lchown()` despite `<unistd.h>` being `#include`d at the top of the file (`:14`) — sqc doesn't expand/parse system headers, so POSIX functions declared only there (not in project source) look undeclared.** `wpas_ctrl_iface_open_sock:586,654`, `wpas_global_ctrl_iface_open_sock:1302`. Expect this shape for any libc/POSIX function whose only declaration is in a system header sqc doesn't parse; distinct from the genuine DCL31-C class (a function truly missing any declaration, project-internal or system).
- **Reconfirms established classes at very high density:** CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()` no-pthread FP (36 instances, by far the largest class in this batch — every `wpa_printf(...,strerror(errno))` error-log call in the file); API05-C `T*,size_t`-idiom / bare-string-param blanket noise (10 instances: `:64,66,76`x2,`391,428,430,941,943`); STR34-C plain char-to-char `*p = '\0'`/`*p = '_'` idiom (6 instances: `:261,285,529,884` plus the 2 above); EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref right at an assignment (4 instances: `:395,711,1361`, extending the established class to `msg`/`priv`); DCL30-C local-pointer-*variable*-vs-heap-storage confusion on `buf`/`priv` (6 instances: `:291,720,764,774,1370,1379`); the goto-`fail:`-label mutually-exclusive-branch free-tracking-doesn't-separate-branches class, now confirmed on `fname`/`buf` double-free/UAF claims (`:665,699,701`x2) and extended to ARR00-C "accessed after freed" on a `buf[res]='\0'` reached only via the continuing (non-freeing) branch (`:158,1126`); MSC07-C goto-label blindness ("unreachable code after return" on the `fail:` label itself, `:692,1347`); MEM12-C false-leak when the resource (`priv->sock`) is intentionally retained/eloop-registered in a long-lived struct rather than leaked (`:690,1345`); MSC01-C no-final-else pedantry where the implicit default is already correct (`:199,730,1156`); the cross-function array-size/decl-site conflation bug on ARR30-C, now citing an unrelated `char buf[256]` from a *different* function (`wpa_supplicant_ctrl_iface_wait:1040`) as the allocation site for a completely different `os_malloc`'d `buf` in 2 other functions (`:158,1126`) — plus one *correctly*-attributed instance in the same rule on the real `buf[256]`/`recvfrom(...,sizeof(buf)-1,...)` bound, still FP because the access is providably in-bounds (`:1060`); DCL37-C block-scope-`_errno`/`_bssid`-style locals misclassified as file-scope (2 instances: `:209,983`); EXP34-C `strtol()`'s `endp` guaranteed non-NULL by contract even on parse failure (2 instances: `:575,1294`); the genuine dead-`NULL`/`0`-initial-assignment MSC13-C TP shape, now on `dir`/`gid_str`/`gid` locals unconditionally overwritten by both branches of an if/else before their first read (5 instances: `:247,508`x2,`854,1281` — distinguish from the FP "misses a later read" shape documented elsewhere); DCL13-C's established read-only-field-forward genuine-if-low-value TP disposition (6 instances: `:243,314,807,808` plus the eloop-callback-signature FP counter-example at `:359`); EXP05-C cast-away-const on a read-only sendmsg/iovec buffer (`ifname`/`buf`, `:965,975`).
- **NEW, batch-local (not yet 3x confirmed elsewhere): ERR33-C/ERR00-C/ERR30-C's `strtol()`-error-checking findings correctly split TP from the sibling EXP34-C FP on the very same call.** `wpas_ctrl_iface_open_sock:574` and `wpas_global_ctrl_iface_open_sock:1293` each do check for parse failure via `*gid_str=='\0' || *endp!='\0'` (defeating EXP34-C's "endp might be NULL" and partially defeating ERR34-C-style "no error check" claims), but never reset `errno=0` first nor check `ERANGE` afterward — so the *overflow* detection path genuinely is missing, a real (if low-severity, locally-trusted-config-value) violation of ERR33-C/ERR00-C/ERR30-C's literal text. Same call site, 3 co-located rules judged TP while EXP34-C on the same line is FP — another instance of the "single call site legitimately splits TP/FP across co-located rule hits" lesson already documented for sscanf in `ctrl_iface.c`.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b149`, 150 findings, `src/common/dpp_crypto.c#part1of2`, lines 25-2563: DPP curve tables, HKDF/HMAC key-derivation helpers (dpp_derive_k1/k2/pmk/pmkid/bk_ke), dpp_keygen, dpp_process_signed_connector/dpp_check_signed_connector, dpp_gen_r_auth/i_auth, PKEX Qi/Qr/z derivation, dpp_build_csr, dpp_pfs_init, dpp_reconfig_derive_ke_*, dpp_sign_connector, dpp_gen_reconfig_id)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (extends the sae.c "no aliasing exists on this line at all" EXP43-C sub-shape, `41plus_b141`, to a new function family): `dpp_hmac`/`dpp_hmac_vector`/`dpp_hkdf_expand` calls throughout dpp_crypto.c are flagged "same pointer for output/input" when the key/secret/data input and the mac/out output are always three (or two) entirely distinct buffers.** Every one of 16 instances checked (`dpp_hmac(salt, Mx, prk)`-shape at `:194,399,426,1152,1631`; `dpp_hkdf_expand(prk, info, k1/k2/pmk/ke/...)`-shape at `:405,433,489,1158,1759,1852,2113,2205,2438`; `dpp_hmac_vector(auth->bk/k, addr, tmp/auth_i)`-shape at `:2431,2466`) uses a distinct local array or distinct struct field for the input vs. the output parameter — no real aliasing, not even the legal no-`restrict` in-place case. Same root cause as the sae.c `hkdf_expand`/`hkdf_extract` misattribution, now the single densest cluster of this exact sub-shape seen in the corpus (16 instances in one file).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, extends the DCL13-C "genuine-const-would-break-compilation" sub-shape, `41plus_b127` `drv:1532`, from direct field writes to output-param-mediated writes): a struct pointer param is passed to a function whose signature writes through one of the struct's own fixed-array fields as a non-const output parameter — const-qualifying the struct pointer would make that field-decay non-compilable.** `dpp_derive_bk_ke`'s `auth` (`:444`): `dpp_hmac_vector(..., auth->bk)` and `dpp_hkdf_expand(..., auth->ke, ...)` both write through `auth->bk`/`auth->ke` (fixed `u8[]` struct members) via their non-const `mac`/`out` params. `dpp_bi_pubkey_hash`'s `bi` (`:548`): `sha256_vector(..., bi->pubkey_hash)`/`sha256_vector(..., bi->pubkey_hash_chirp)` likewise write through `bi`'s fixed-array fields. In both cases DCL13-C's "not modified" premise is factually wrong, not just low-value — `const struct X *` would make the field decay to `const u8 *`, incompatible with the callee's non-const output-param type.
- **Reconfirms MSC13-C dead-initial-NULL-assignment genuine-TP class at unusually high density for a single file (9 instances): a pointer local is initialized to NULL/its declaration default and then unconditionally overwritten by a real call before any goto/read reaches it.** `der:82` (dpp_debug_print_key), `pix/prx/bix:971` (dpp_gen_i_auth — contrast with `brx`, not flagged, which genuinely can be read via its init value if an earlier goto fires), `own_key:1687`, `pr:1789`, `signed1/signed2:1962`, `csign:2230`, `pp:2353`, `e_id:2354`. All verified: no goto/return/read exists between the NULL init and the unconditional reassignment.
- **Reconfirms in this batch (not re-detailed above):** API00-C internal-only-API FP class at very high density (≈35 instances, every `dpp_derive_*`/`dpp_pkex_derive_*`/`dpp_gen_*`/`dpp_check_signed_connector`/`dpp_validate_csr` helper, including the length-overflow sub-variant on EC-derived/protocol-bounded lengths); API05-C pointer+size_t idiom (10 instances); ENV01-C wholesale zero-`getenv()` misfire (24 instances — the single largest class this batch, confirmed zero `getenv()` calls anywhere in the file); MEM05-C fixed-macro-sized-array-misidentified-as-VLA (3 instances, `nonces[2*DPP_MAX_NONCE_LEN]`); STR31-C misapplied to non-char arrays (`const u8 *addr[1]`/`size_t len[1]`, 4 instances); ARR01-C `sizeof(*ptr)`/`sizeof(ptr->fixed_array_member)` correct-idiom misapplication (3 instances: `info:737`, `auth->Lx:1081,1123`); EXP30-C pure-accessor-args (`wpabuf_head`/`wpabuf_len` sibling args, 10 instances); MSC07-C goto-label-blindness on `fail:`/`out:` labels immediately after an unconditional return (6 instances); MSC37-C goto-label-blindness extended to the `out:`/`goto out`-from-`fail:` two-hop shape (2 instances: `:1459,1534`); EXP34-C `os_free(NULL)`-safe (1 instance) and `crypto_ec_key_deinit`/`crypto_ec_point_deinit`-NULL-safe-wrapper class extended to 3 more call sites (`:1864,2373,2563`); DCL30-C heap-vs-stack confusion (7 instances: 3 `return <heap ptr>` shape, 2 `*out_param = <heap ptr>` shape); ARR00-C same-buffer pos/end-renamed-pointer subtraction misfire (1 instance, `signed_start`/`signed_end` both within `connector`); INT32-C/INT30-C small-protocol-bounded-value misfire (3 instances); ARR30-C "malloc'd len+1, index at exactly len" bounds-safe-by-construction misfire (1 instance); EXP33-C count-guarded scatter-gather `addr[N]` partial-init misfire (2 instances: `:1493,1568`); STR34-C plain char-to-char assignment (3 instances); MSC41-C hexdump-title-not-a-secret (2 instances); DCL13-C plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP (6 instances: `auth`/`conf` params on functions that only read, never write, the struct) vs. the two genuine-const-would-break-compilation FPs above; DCL00-C/STR05-C genuine (trivial) TP on a never-reassigned string-literal local (`dot:1908`); MEM03-C misfire on a buffer that IS cleared via `bin_clear_free()` in the cleanup path (`password:2089`); MEM30-C/MEM31-C mutually-exclusive-success-vs-fail-path free misfire (`pub:2043`); EXP40-C phantom cast-away-const where neither side is const (`*pos=buf:211`); INT14-C genuinely-correct-per-rule-text stylistic TP on a real variable used with both bitwise and arithmetic ops (2 instances: `len:237`, `signature_len:804`).

## Confirmed/reinforced patterns (from batch `41plus_b160`, 143 findings, 1 file: `src/tls/tlsv1_server_write.c`, the TLSv1 server-side handshake-message-builder twin of the already-audited `tlsv1_client_read.c`/`tlsv1_client_ocsp.c` files)

- **Reconfirms at the highest density seen yet (≈100 combined instances, one file): the ARR37-C "non-array pointer" misfire on a `u8 *pos` that walks a real heap buffer** (every `tls_write_server_*` helper receives `pos = *msgpos`, itself derived from `msg = os_malloc(msglen)` in `tls_send_server_hello`/`tls_send_change_cipher_spec`, or from a local fixed array `payload[]`/`verify_data[]`/`alert[]`) — every `pos++`/`pos +=`/`pos[i]`/`pos -= 2` site across the file (lines 53-809, ~68 ARR37-C instances) and the paired **ARR30-C cross-function buffer-size/decl-site conflation** (23 instances, all citing "Buffer 'pos' with size 1 (allocated at line 802)" — line 802 is `u8 payload[1];`, an unrelated single-byte flag local in a completely different function, `tls_write_server_change_cipher_spec`) and the paired **ARR36-C "pointers from different arrays" on the `end`/`pos`(`msgpos`) parameter pair** (16 instances) — `end` and `*msgpos`/`pos` are always threaded from the same caller-owned buffer through the whole `tls_write_server_hello`→...→`tls_write_server_hello_done` call chain. All three sub-shapes are pre-existing, heavily-confirmed corpus classes (see `pos`/`end`-paired-buffer entries above, the addr-decl-site conflation entries, and the "ARR37-C pointer legitimately walks a real array" class) — cite those rather than re-deriving.
- **NEW density record for MEM12-C "false leak after the resource was already freed" (11 instances, one function, `tls_write_server_key_exchange`):** every error-path `return -1` after `dh_ys = os_malloc(dh_ys_len)` succeeds (`:456,506,520,534,590,617,629,662,683,691`) gets an identical flow-insensitive "Leaked: conn->dh_secret, dh_ys" — but `dh_ys` is explicitly `os_free()`'d immediately before each of the first four returns (`:455,505,519,533`) and is freed even earlier, right after its final productive use, at `:540`, for every return from `:587` onward; the one instance where `dh_ys` genuinely hasn't been allocated yet (`:448`, the `os_malloc` failure branch itself) cites it as leaked too. `conn->dh_secret` is a **persistent `conn`-owned field** (freed by `os_free(conn->dh_secret)` at the top of this same function on the *next* call, `:406`, and ultimately by the connection's own deinit) — not a function-local leak at all, same as the established param/struct-owned-field MEM12/MEM31 ownership-transfer FP class. All 11 instances FP.
- **Reconfirms the established "same-file-distance" DCL31-C FP sub-shape** (`41plus_b?`/`config_file.c`/`dpp.c` precedents): `tls_write_server_finished` is `static`-defined at `:831` and called correctly ~150/~200 lines later at `:976,1024` — flagged as "called without prior declaration" anyway. 2 instances, FP.
- **NEW, batch-local (not yet 3x confirmed): EXP34-C "potential null pointer dereference in member access" fires on a pointer whose non-nullness is guaranteed by the enclosing `while (cert)` loop's own condition**, extending the general "rule doesn't see loop invariants" family (INT30-C wrap, ARR30-C bounded-scan) to EXP34-C. `tls_server_cert_chain_der_len`'s and `tls_write_server_certificate`'s identical `cert = x509_certificate_get_subject(conn->cred->trusted_certs, &cert->issuer);` (`:35,247`), both inside `while (cert) { ... }`, take `&cert->issuer` — a member-address computation (no actual dereference/read) on a pointer already checked non-NULL by the loop guard one line above.
- **NEW, batch-local: EXP33-C "used uninitialized" fires on plain address-computation of an output-param destination, not a read.** `hash + 19` passed as the output buffer to `tlsv12_key_x_server_params_hash(...)` (`:575`) — `hash` is a 100-byte local array; the call *writes* into it starting at offset 19, and bytes 0-18 are `os_memcpy`'d separately (`:610-612`) before any read. ### FN read-through (`41plus_b160`)

No new missed bugs found. The file is a well-guarded, internally-consistent TLS server-write path: every buffer write is preceded by an explicit `end - pos` capacity check (`tls_write_server_certificate`, `_certificate_status`, `_key_exchange`, `_certificate_request` all bounds-check before writing variable-length fields), `tls_write_server_hello`/`_hello_done`/`_change_cipher_spec`/`_finished` write only fixed/record-bounded amounts into buffers sized generously by the caller (`msglen = 1000 + cert_chain_len + ocsp_resp_len`, or a fixed local array sized for the exact message), and every `os_malloc`/`os_readfile` failure path returns cleanly with the correct partial frees (`ocsp_resp` freed on every exit from `tls_send_server_hello`, `msg` freed on every failure exit). No unchecked length from wire/attacker input reaches an allocation size or memcpy length in this file — all lengths originate from local config (`cert->cert_len`, `dh_p_len`, `ocsp_resp_len` from a local file) or from `TLS_*_LEN` compile-time constants.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b155`, 146 findings, entire file: `src/crypto/crypto_linux.c`, the Linux AF_ALG kernel-crypto backend)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances, one file): MSC41-C "hard-coded sensitive information" misfires on Linux kernel-crypto-API transform/algorithm name string literals passed to `linux_af_alg_skcipher()`.** `"ecb(aes)"` (`:499,519`), `"ecb(arc4)"` (`:552`), `"ecb(des)"` (`:629`), `"cbc(aes)"` (`:688`), `"kw(aes)"` (`:797`) are all AF_ALG transform-name identifiers (the kernel's crypto-algorithm selector string, analogous to an OpenSSL cipher name), never secret/password/key/token material. Distinct from the already-documented `wpa_hexdump_key`-title-string MSC41-C misfire family — this is a new sub-shape (algorithm-identifier argument, not a debug-log title).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances, one file): MEM05-C "VLA with runtime-sized allocation" misapplied to `char buf[CMSG_SPACE(sizeof(u32))]`.** `CMSG_SPACE()` is a standard POSIX ancillary-data sizing macro that expands to compile-time arithmetic on `sizeof()` + alignment constants — never runtime-sized. `:451,542,612,932`. Extends the established MEM05-C fixed-size-macro-expression FP family to this specific system macro.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances, one file): STR31-C "character array too small to hold string data" misapplied to `sendmsg`/`recvmsg` ancillary-data (cmsg) byte buffers — `char buf[CMSG_SPACE(...)]`/`char buf[100]` — that are never used to hold a NUL-terminated string at all**, just raw `cmsghdr` control-message bytes populated via `CMSG_FIRSTHDR`/`CMSG_DATA`. `:452,613,680,789,933`. Extends the existing "STR31-C misapplied to non-char/non-string buffer" family.
- **Reconfirms (this file, one function `crypto_hash_init`/`crypto_cipher_init`, ~20 instances): the free/access-tracking mutually-exclusive-branch class extends to a `switch`'s `default:` case vs. the fall-through path after the switch.** Both functions `os_free(ctx); return NULL;` in `default:`, then unconditionally use `ctx->s`/`ctx->skcipher` a few lines later on the *only reachable* (non-default) continuation — sqc's free-tracking doesn't see that the `default:` branch's `return` makes it disjoint from every subsequent line. Produces a long cascade of MEM30-C UAF + MEM30/31-C double-free findings that are all FP for the same root cause (`:288,289,294,297,298,302,303,306,307,311` in `crypto_hash_init`; `:897,898,915,919,920,925` in `crypto_cipher_init`), plus the sibling DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable" misfire on the same `ctx`/`skcipher` (heap via `os_zalloc`, not automatic storage — established DCL30-C class) at the functions' final `return ctx;`/`return skcipher;` (`:311,441,925`).
- **Reconfirms established classes at very high density in this file:** CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()` no-pthread FP (25 instances, every error-log call in the file); EXP05-C cast-away-const on read-only `iovec.iov_base` (`(void*)in`/`(void*)clear`, 4 instances: `:458,633,939` — matches the `16-40_b22` `driver_nl80211_monitor.c:165` precedent exactly); DCL39-C "struct passed to trust-boundary function may leak padding bytes" on `sendmsg(&msg,...)` where `msg` is `os_memset`-zeroed immediately beforehand (7 instances: `:473,575,648,717,826,915,954` — matches the `16-40_b22` `driver_nl80211_monitor.c:188` precedent exactly); EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref right after an `os_zalloc(sizeof(*ptr))`/`msg_controllen` computation (7 instances: `ctx:245,871`, `skcipher:419`, `alg_iv:698,807,906`); FIO24-C branch-blind double-close misfire, now extended to a `goto fail:`-label-vs-earlier-independent-early-return shape (`:82` vs `:74`, `:119` vs both, `:306` vs `:297`); API00-C internal-only-API FP (`sha1_vector`, `omac1_aes_*`, `aes_unwrap`, `crypto_cipher_encrypt/decrypt`, 12 instances — all crypto-vector primitives called only with valid internally-owned buffers); API05-C `T*,size_t`/`addr[],len[]+num_elem` idiom (2 instances: `:57,415`); POS02-C codebase-wide no-privilege-separation FP (`bind()` on the AF_ALG socket, `:45` — same established class as `driver_nl80211_monitor.c:125`/`ctrl_iface_unix.c`); MSC07-C goto-label-blindness ("unreachable after return" on a `fail:`-reached line, `:442`); FIO50-C name-based misfire flagging a plain non-stream `u8 tmp` variable purely because of its identifier, with zero I/O nearby (`:625` — same established class as `sae_pk_gen.c:162`); INT13-C/INT14-C stylistic-pedantry on a DES parity-bit-computation loop shifting an always-non-negative `u8`-promoted-to-`int` by a bounded loop counter (`:624,625` — no real signed-shift UB, same established INT14-C class); The two sibling `read()`-failure branches immediately below (`:834-839`, `:840-846`) correctly call the deinit — this is an inconsistent/skipped cleanup on just the one `sendmsg`-failure path, closest CERT mapping MEM31-C ("free dynamically allocated memory when no longer needed") / FIO42-C-adjacent (fd leak).

- **Reconfirms at very high density in this file:** ENV01-C/MEM05-C wholesale zero-`getenv()`/fixed-macro-sized-array misfire (9+8 instances — no `getenv()` call anywhere in the file; every flagged array is `u8 buf[CONST_EXPR]`); ARR01-C `sizeof(ptr->fixed_array_member)` idiom (`auth->Mx/Nx/Lx/k1/k2:46,48,50,52,53`); ARR39-C "double scaling"/INT30-C "may wrap" misfired on pure `size_t` integer sizing arithmetic with no pointer operand at all (`attr_len`/`unwrapped_len` builders, 9+11 instances); the `pos[-1]`-after-`*pos++`-write ARR00-C/ARR30-C negative-subscript idiom (`:186,355,361,363`, both rules each time); MSC01-C no-final-else guard-clause pedantry (9 instances); the DCL31-C same-file-distance blind spot (`dpp_auth_build_resp:233`→called `:586,656`; `dpp_auth_build_req:59`→called `:1291`); `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref EXP33-C (`bi:1141`); DCL30-C local-pointer-variable-vs-heap-storage confusion (`msg:1126` via `wpabuf_alloc`, `auth:1298` via `dpp_alloc_auth`/`os_zalloc`); MSC07-C/MSC37-C goto-label-blindness (6 MSC07-C instances, all immediately precede a `fail:`/`not_compatible:` label; 1 MSC37-C on `dpp_auth_init` whose every path returns via `out:`); API00-C internal-only-API no-NULL-check (dispatch-path `msg_ctx`/`hdr`/`dpp`/`own_bi` params, always non-NULL from the validated receive path; `own_bi` NULL is explicitly anticipated/handled by `dpp_autogen_bootstrap_key`); API05-C pointer+own-size-param idiom (`hdr`+`attr_len:668`); MSC41-C "hard-coded sensitive info" on plain protocol failure-reason/hexdump-title string literals (30+ instances, e.g. `dpp_auth_fail(auth, "AES-SIV decryption failed")`, `dpp_debug_print_key("Peer (Initiator) Protocol Key", pi)` — none are secrets).
- **Reinforces the mutually-exclusive-branch double-free/leak misfire family at high density, one new sub-shape.** Three independent `unwrapped`/`unwrapped2` buffers (`dpp_auth_req_rx:929`, `dpp_auth_resp_rx:1717,1728,1729,1733,1736,1737,1739`, `dpp_auth_conf_rx:1973`) are each freed exactly once per actual control-flow path (either an early `return` right after freeing, or the shared `fail:` label — never both), but sqc's flow-insensitive tracking (a) claims MEM31-C double-free when a `goto fail`-reachable free follows an already-taken, disjoint `return`-after-free branch, and (b) claims MEM12-C "Leaked: unwrapped, unwrapped2" on `return` statements that sit textually right after the exact `bin_clear_free()` calls that free them. New wrinkle, 2nd file to show it (1st was `nai_realm_free(realm, count)` in an earlier batch, categorical_patterns.md ~line 6020): the `*_len` companion argument to `bin_clear_free(ptr, len)` (a `size_t`, not a pointer) is itself flagged as "already freed" (MEM30-C/MEM31C on `unwrapped_len`/`unwrapped2_len`, `:929,1736,1737,1973`) — now 2x-confirmed as a real (if minor) sqc argument-extraction bug riding on top of the branch-conflation misfire, not just a one-off.

### FN read-through (`41plus_b157`)

One latent-but-benign code-quality nit, not a reportable security FN: `dpp_auth_build_resp_ok` (`:483-491`) discards the `secret_len` out-param written by `dpp_ecdh(..., auth->Nx, &secret_len)` and instead reads/writes `auth->secret_len` (a stale value left over from the earlier M.x derivation) at `:488,489,491`. Currently harmless because M.x and N.x are derived on the same curve (ECDH x-coordinate length is a fixed per-curve constant), so the stale value is numerically identical to what `secret_len` would have held — but it is a dead output param and would silently misbehave if a future mixed-curve code path were ever introduced. No unchecked malloc, missing wire-length validation, or unfreed error-path resource was found elsewhere in the file — every `os_malloc`/`wpabuf_alloc` call is NULL-checked, every `wrapped_*_len - AES_BLOCK_SIZE` subtraction is preceded by an explicit `< AES_BLOCK_SIZE` guard, and every DPP attribute pulled from attacker-controlled wire data (`dpp_get_attr`) is length-validated before use.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b161`, 142 findings, 1 file: `src/drivers/driver_bsd.c`, lines 32-1752: BSD/net80211 ioctl driver backend)

- **NEW: EXP33-C "used uninitialized" misfire on a struct field WRITE

  a GET-style `ioctl()` that populates the struct's remaining fields —
  extends the existing ioctl-output-param family with a sharper root
  cause: the flagged statement is itself a write, not a read, and the

  `SIOCG80211BSSID` populates `bs.i_bssid` (`:1104`);

  `SIOCG80211NWID` fills `nwid` through the aliased pointer sqc doesn't

  established goto-target-label-blindness family to `switch`
  case-labels.** A `case` label immediately following another case's

  a different value, not unreachable code — same underlying "labels are

  variant, new syntactic shape. `driver_bsd.c:794` (`RTM_IEEE80211_REPLAY`

## Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed (from `41plus_b156`, `src/ap/ctrl_iface_ap.c`, 145 findings, 1 file)

- **ARR00-C "pointer arithmetic goes N elements past the end" misreads a
  runtime-length-prefixed `u8 *field` (element `[0]` holds a byte count,
  allocated as `os_malloc(1 + count)`) as a fixed-bound array of size 1
  (bound "0 to 0"), then flags `field + 1` as out-of-bounds — 2 instances,
  one file so far, watch for a 3rd elsewhere.** `sta->supp_op_classes`
  (`sta_info.h:254`, `u8 *supp_op_classes;`, allocated
  `os_malloc(1 + supp_op_classes_len)` in `ieee802_11_shared.c:972`) and
  `sta->ext_capability` (`sta_info.h:295`, allocated
  `os_malloc(1 + ext_capab_ie_len)` in `ieee802_11_shared.c:1211`) are
  both classic length-prefixed IE buffers (`buf[0]` = length,
  `buf[1..buf[0]]` = payload); the array-bound resolver appears to treat
  the plain `u8 *` struct-field declaration itself as the array,
  independent of its actual dynamic allocation size. `ctrl_iface_ap.c:364,444`.
- **DCL13-C misses writes-through-the-pointer on the dominant
  `char *buf, size_t buflen` ctrl_iface response-buffer idiom —
  reconfirms the `ieee802_11.c:7669`-class miss (`41plus_b64`) at high
  density in a different subsystem (STA/status dump helpers instead of
  IE builders).** Every `hostapd_write_ht_mcs_bitmask`/
  `hostapd_ctrl_iface_sta_mib`/`hostapd_ctrl_iface_acl_show_mac` `buf`
  param is written via `os_snprintf(buf + len, ...)`/`wpa_snprintf_hex(buf
  + len, ...)` throughout the function body, yet DCL13-C still suggests
  const. `ctrl_iface_ap.c:31,238,1860`. Contrast with the same file's
  genuinely-read-only `hapd`/`data`/`iface`/`mode`/`acl` DCL13-C findings,
  which remain real (if low-value) TPs.
- **ERR02-C "sprintf return value not checked" fires on `os_snprintf()`
  calls whose return *is* checked, one line later, via the codebase's
  own `os_snprintf_error()` helper — the rule's checked-return detector
  doesn't recognize that wrapper as a check.** 3 instances:
  `ctrl_iface_ap.c:363,385,399` (each immediately followed by
  `if (!os_snprintf_error(buflen - len, res)) len += res;`). Distinct
  from the already-documented `wpa_snprintf_hex`-name-substring ERR02-C
  misfire (which fires on a function that isn't `sprintf` at all) —
  this is a second, independent ERR02-C failure mode on genuine
  `os_snprintf()` calls.

## Batch-local, not yet 3x confirmed (2026-08-07, `41plus_b163`, p2p_pd.c)

- **Macro-argument-name / unrelated-local-variable name collision causes
  both EXP33-C "used uninitialized" and EXP43-C "same pointer for
  output/input" misfires on `do {...} while(0)` boolean-check macros
  whose parameter name happens to match a local variable elsewhere in
  the same function.** `p2ps_validate_pd_req`'s `P2PS_PD_REQ_CHECK(_val,
  _attr)` macro (`p2p_pd.c:560-566`) is invoked as
  `P2PS_PD_REQ_CHECK(group_id, group_id)` etc. (`:647-652`) where both
  macro arguments are the *same* locally-scoped `u8 group_id = 0;`-style
  variable (`:553-558`); the macro body only tests `(_val) &&
  !msg->_attr` — a plain boolean check against a message field, not a
  function call, and definitely not two aliased pointers — but sqc
  flags each invocation as EXP43-C "called with same pointer for output
  and input parameters" (6 instances, `:647-652`), apparently misparsing
  the macro call as a function call with pointer arguments. Separately,
  `p2p_validate_p2ps_pd_resp`'s sibling macro `P2PS_PD_RESP_CHECK(1,
  adv_id)` / `P2PS_PD_RESP_CHECK(1, session_id)` (`:1555,1559`) expands
  to `msg->adv_id` / `msg->session_id` (message struct fields) — but sqc
  reports EXP33-C "Variable 'adv_id'/'session_id' is used uninitialized"
  against the *unrelated* local `u32 adv_id`/`u32 session_id` declared a
  few lines above (`:1543-1544`) and assigned later at `:1563-1564`;
  the macro's `_attr` text apparently gets matched to the identically-
  named local rather than resolved as `msg->_attr`. Only 2 (EXP33) + 6
  (EXP43) instances in this one file so not yet at the 3x-recurrence bar
  for a fully confirmed cross-batch class, but the root cause (macro
  formal-parameter text colliding with an unrelated same-named local or
  member) is a plausible generalizable failure mode — watch for it
  wherever a `do {...} while(0)`-style validation macro's argument name
  textually matches a local variable in the caller.
- **Reconfirms `p2ps_prov_free(p2p)` "frees only `p2p->p2ps_prov`, not
  `p2p` itself" (already-confirmed `16-40_b3`/`41plus` class, see the
  `p2p.c:3287` entry above) at very high density in its own definition
  file.** `p2p_pd.c` calls `p2ps_prov_free(p2p)` seven times
  (`:1491,1858,1951,1961,1976,2001,2216`); every one is misread as
  freeing `p2p` itself, cascading into ~60 MEM30-C
  use-after-free/double-free findings on `p2p` through the rest of
  `p2p_handle_prov_disc_resp`/`p2p_send_prov_disc_req` (`:1965-2247`).
  Verified against the actual definition (`:2272-2276`:
  `os_free(p2p->p2ps_prov); p2p->p2ps_prov = NULL;` — never touches
  `p2p`).
- **NEW-shape MEM31-C false leak/double-free on a device-struct-owned
  `wpabuf` field reassigned via the `wpabuf_free(old); x =
  wpabuf_dup(new);` idiom (extends the general param-owned-struct-field
  MEM31 FP class to a specific recurring field name).** `dev->info.
  wfd_subelems` is freed and re-dup'd at `p2p_pd.c:932-933,1818-1819`
  (and identically elsewhere in `p2p.c`/`p2p_go_neg.c`); every
  subsequent `goto out`/early-return in the same function is flagged as
  a "potential leak" of that dup (20 instances:
  `:933,943,959,972,994,1051,1058,1157,1182,1189,1202,1212,1218,1319,
  1819,1827,1859,1977,2002,2018`), but the field is owned by the
  long-lived `p2p_device` struct (freed at device teardown,
  `p2p.c:980`, or on the next reassignment) — no local leak exists on
  any of these paths.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b162`, 140 findings, `src/eap_peer/eap.c`, full file)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL30-C/ARR00-C/MEM12-C "heap pointer misclassified as

  (`os_zalloc`, `:2255`), `eap_get_phase2_types`'s `buf` (`os_malloc`,
  `:2757`), `eap_get_eapRespData`'s `resp` (transferred from `sm->eapRespData`,
  `:3139`) — every one flagged DCL30-C, several also ARR00-C

### New FN this batch (not sqc-flagged)

- `eap_get_ext_password()` (`eap.c:2840-2847`) copies the plaintext

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b164`, 138 findings, one file: `src/utils/os_internal.c` — the CONFIG_OS=internal no-libc example backend implementing os_memcpy/os_memmove/os_memset/os_memcmp/os_strlen/os_strchr/os_strrchr/os_strcmp/os_strncmp/os_strlcpy/os_strdup/os_strstr/os_snprintf)

- **NEW, high-density (~30 instances): "thin os_* wrapper mirrors the underlying libc function's own contract" — API00-C/EXP34-C false positives across every os_mem*/os_str*/os_snprintf definition in this file.** `os_memcpy`/`os_memmove`/`os_memset`/`os_memcmp`/`os_strlen`/`os_strchr`/`os_strrchr`/`os_strcmp`/`os_strncmp`/`os_strlcpy`/`os_strstr`/`os_snprintf` are all deliberately transparent, unvalidated pass-throughs that intentionally replicate the exact behavior (including lack of NULL-checking) of the standard C library function they stand in for on libc-less targets — flagging them for "not validating pointer parameter"/"potential null pointer dereference" holds the *replacement* to a higher contract than the *original* function it's required to match bit-for-bit. Distinct from the existing "internal-only API, caller-guaranteed non-null" API00-C class (which is about call-site knowledge); this is about a function's job being to faithfully mirror a specific external contract. Also extends to MEM04-C (`os_malloc`/`os_realloc` zero-size checks — malloc(0)/realloc(ptr,0) are themselves implementation-defined, not a defect in the wrapper) and MEM06-C (misapplied to the *generic*, data-agnostic allocator definition itself rather than a specific sensitive-data call site).
- **NEW: ARR30-C "unbounded while loop" misfires on a bounded decrement-counter loop (`while (n--)` / `while (--left != 0)`), distinct from the existing NUL-terminated-string-loop-bounded class.** 5 instances (`os_memcpy:289`, `os_memset:313`, `os_strlcpy:446`) — the loop's own countdown condition *is* the bound; the analyzer doesn't recognize decrement-and-test as bounds-checking, only explicit `<`/`<=` comparisons.
- **NEW: DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable" fires on a bare `return <param>;` where the parameter is the function's own caller-supplied pointer (the memcpy/memset-style "return dest unchanged" API idiom), not any local at all — a parameter-mistaken-for-local sub-shape distinct from the existing heap-vs-stack-confusion class.** `os_memcpy:291` (`return dest;`), `os_memset:315` (`return s;`). The existing heap-vs-stack class (`os_rel2abs_path:248` `buf` from `os_malloc`, `os_strdup:348` `res` from `os_malloc`) is reconfirmed alongside it in the same batch.
- **NEW: MEM33-C "direct assignment of flexible array structure instances" fires on a plain single-`char` pointer-dereference assignment (`*d++ = *s++;`) inside a byte-copy loop — pure category error, no struct or flexible array member anywhere.** 3 instances (`os_memcpy:290`, `os_memmove:304`, `os_strlcpy:447`), each paired with 3 STR34-C misfires on the same line (both operands are `char`, so there is no widening/sign-extension at all — reinforces the existing plain-char-assignment STR34-C FP class at unusually high per-line density).
- **NEW: STR34-C fires on a narrowing `char = int` fill-value assignment (`*p++ = c;` in `os_memset`, where `c` is the standard `int c` fill parameter) with the rule's own message describing the opposite (widening/read) direction — a direction-mismatch sub-shape.** `os_internal.c:314`. Also: STR34-C fires on a **pointer** argument (`needle`) passed to `os_strlen()`, describing it as a char scalar undergoing integer conversion when it's neither dereferenced nor converted at all (`os_strstr:480`) — a distinct name/type-category-error sub-shape.
- **NEW: ARR36-C "pointer subtraction between different arrays" / INT00-C "unsigned subtraction without guard" both fire on `*p1 - *p2`-style comparator return statements that subtract dereferenced *values*, not pointers.** `os_memcmp:334`, `os_strcmp:416`, `os_strncmp:435` (ARR36-C); `os_memcmp:334` (INT00-C, additionally wrong because `unsigned char` operands promote to `int` before subtraction per C integer promotion, so there's no unsigned wraparound at all). Matches the already-known `os_strcmp`-style signed-difference idiom but at higher density.
- **CON33-C/CON34-C no-pthread FP class extended to `gmtime()`** (previously only seen on `strerror()`/`inet_ntoa()`) — `os_internal.c:91`.
- **NEW: MEM12-C "leaked" fires citing (a) the function's own live return value right after the return statement, or (b) a pointer freed on the immediately preceding line — not the usual "mutually-exclusive branch" MEM12 shape.** `os_rel2abs_path:189,248` (citing `ret`/`buf`, both either returned or already freed one line above); `os_readfile:237` (citing `buf` which is still NULL in the just-failed-malloc branch — nothing to leak); `os_readfile:243` (citing `buf`, freed the line immediately above at `:242`).
- **NEW: MEM30-C "double-free" misfires across a retry loop where the pointer is freed then reassigned to a fresh allocation on the next iteration before any further use — the free-tracking doesn't account for loop-carried reassignment.** `os_rel2abs_path:188` (`buf` freed inside the `getcwd()`-ERANGE retry branch, then reassigned via `os_malloc()` at the top of the next iteration; the final free after the loop only ever fires once, on the iteration that broke out successfully).
- **NEW: ERR05-C "calls exit(), should report to caller" misapplied to a forked child's post-`execv()`-failure cleanup — extends the existing "termination is the legitimate purpose" exception (previously only seen for a top-level `signal()` handler) to the fork/exec-failure idiom, where `exit()` in the child is the standard, required pattern (never returning to the parent's continuation logic across the fork boundary).** `os_exec:550`.
- **FIO14-C "fseek(SEEK_END) not for binary streams" has the C standard backwards — the ftell/fseek(SEEK_END) danger applies to *text* streams; the stream here is opened `"rb"` (binary), which is exactly the well-defined case.** `os_readfile:230`.
- **FIO32-C "fseek/ftell on device file" is a bare heuristic misfire with no supporting evidence — `os_readfile()`'s `name` is always an admin-config-supplied regular file path (certs, TNC config, PAC files), never a special/device file.** `os_readfile:230,231,232`.
- **FIO19-C "fseek/ftell to compute file size instead of fstat()" graded genuine (if low real-world impact) TP** — `os_readfile:230` is the textbook anti-pattern this rule targets, unlike the FIO32-C misfire on the same line.
- **New FN this batch:** `os_exec()`'s forked child calls `exit(0)` (success) after `execv()` itself fails (`:550`), instead of a nonzero status — a caller using `wait_completion`/`waitpid()` cannot detect the exec failure from the child's reported exit status. No sqc finding covers this; closest rule ERR00-C (improper error propagation).
- Also reconfirmed at volume (no new mechanism): DCL31-C system-header-not-parsed FP class extended to `daemon()`/`random()`/`setenv()` (all declared only in `<unistd.h>`/`<stdlib.h>`, transitively included, `:106,150,206`); API05-C ptr+size_t idiom (very high density, ~25 instances across every os_mem*/os_str* signature); MEM10-C stylistic ad-hoc-NULL-check FP (`:342`); FIO24-C double-close-across-mutually-exclusive-branches (`os_readfile:241,246` vs. the malloc-failure branch's close at `:236`); DCL37-C block-scope-local misclassified as file-scope (`_program`/`_arg:523`); EXP05-C cast-away-const-read-only-overlay mirroring `strchr`/`strrchr`/`strstr`'s own standard signatures (`:385,400,483`); ERR00-C/ERR33-C "fopen not checked" factually wrong (checked the very next line, `os_daemonize:112`); MSC37-C preprocessor-branch-blind reach-end (`os_unsetenv:210`, both `#if`/`#else` arms return); MSC13-C dead-initial-`=NULL` trivial TP (`os_rel2abs_path:156`) plus a genuine misfire on a parameter's only-use-as-a-call-argument being miscounted as an unread store (`os_free:281`, FP); MEM05-C fixed-size-not-a-real-VLA class extended from macro-sized arrays to a `const int`-literal-sized array (`os_exec:524`, `MAX_ARG=30`).
- **DCL13-C on `wpa_supplicant/driver_i.h`'s ~120 `static inline wpa_drv_*` driver-wrapper functions — CONFIRMED TP class, extends the `ap_drv_ops.h`/`wpa_i.h` "read-only forwarding wrapper" precedent.** Verified programmatically: every flagged function only ever dereferences `wpa_s->field` (never forwards the bare `wpa_s` pointer itself into a `wpa_s->driver->op(...)` call, and never assigns/mutates through `wpa_s->`). Contrast `wpa_drv_init` (`:16`, NOT flagged by sqc) which *does* pass bare `wpa_s` as the `void *ctx` arg to `driver->init`/`init2` — correctly excluded since that forward would break under a `const` qualifier. The paired API05-C findings on `buf`/`buf_len` (`wpa_drv_driver_cmd:624`, `wpa_drv_status:709`) are the standard ptr+size_t-companion FP class.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b172`, 124 findings, one file: `src/ap/ap_drv_ops.c`, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): MSC17-C "case falls through" misfires on a `case` whose body is a nested `switch` that returns on every one of its own branches, including an exhaustive `default:`.** `hostapd_is_action_frame_link_agnostic` (`:960,970`) has an outer `switch (category)` where `case WLAN_ACTION_WNM:`/`case WLAN_ACTION_ROBUST_AV_STREAMING:` each contain only a nested `switch (sub_category) { ...; default: return false; }` — every path through the nested switch returns, so control can never reach the next outer `case` label, but sqc's fallthrough check apparently only looks for a *direct* `break`/`return`/`goto` as the case's last top-level statement and doesn't recognize an exhaustively-returning nested switch as terminal. Distinct from the existing `#ifdef`-intervening-next-case MSC17-C misfire class (no preprocessor involved here at all).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MEM31-C "double free" misfires when a function has two `#ifdef`-gated (or otherwise mutually exclusive) blocks that each declare their own block-scoped local with the *same name*, each freed exactly once within its own scope.** `hostapd_build_ap_extra_ies` declares `struct wpabuf *a` inside the `#ifdef CONFIG_WPS` block (`:158`, freed `:160`) and again inside the separate `#ifdef CONFIG_WIFI_DISPLAY` block (`:177`, freed `:180`) — two distinct variables that happen to share a name; sqc's free-tracking conflates them and flags the second free as a double-free of the first's already-freed pointer. Same root cause as the already-documented `hex`-in-two-sibling-`if`-blocks MEM31-C misfire (`41plus_b40`, `:1206`) and the two-sequential-`dl_list_for_each_safe`-loops-reusing-a-loop-var MEM31-C misfire — now confirmed a 3rd time with `#ifdef` blocks as the scope separator instead of `if`/loop bodies.
- Reconfirms in this batch (not re-detailed above): PRE08-C `ieee802_11*.h`/`hw_features*.h` header-family low-value-TP convention (4 instances, `:12`x3,`13`); API00-C internal-only-API no-NULL-check FP (59 instances — the largest single-batch count so far, essentially every driver-ops wrapper's `hapd`/`addr`/`ifname`/`ie`/etc. param); DCL13-C `ap_drv_ops.c` read-only-forwarding-wrapper genuine-if-low-value TP (35 instances — this file *is* the `ap_drv_ops.h`/`driver_i.h` precedent's origin file); EXP34-C internal-invariant-non-null on `hapd`/`sta` (`hapd->driver == NULL` guard-line self-deref, 7 instances); EXP33-C write-through-alias-not-tracked (`buf` written via `pos` by an eid-builder callee before use, `:84`) extended to a new sub-shape: a block-scoped loop local (`h_hapd:793`) assigned unconditionally on every path that reaches its use, where sqc's CFG apparently doesn't connect the loop's own `continue`-filtering `if` to the "assigned before used" fact; DCL30-C heap-vs-local-storage confusion (`beacon`/`proberesp`/`assocresp`, all `wpabuf_resize`/`wpabuf_put`-built heap objects assigned to the out-params at return, `:216-218`); MSC07-C goto-target-label-after-return (`fail:222`); MSC01-C no-final-else guard-clause pedantry with a safe pre-initialized/`memset`-zeroed default (5 instances: `:359,400,1026,1180,1295`); API05-C ptr+size_t idiom (`seq`/`seq_len:838`, `csa_offs`/`csa_offs_len:873`); INT13-C genuine (low-severity) TP on a truly-`int` (signed) `set_flags` used in `&`/`|` (`:335,336`); MSC13-C genuine trivial TP — `acs_ch_list_all = 0` at declaration (`:1224`) is unconditionally overwritten by an `if`/`else` before any read.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b165`, 137 findings, one file: `src/crypto/tls_gnutls.c`, the GnuTLS TLS backend, 2026-08-07)

- **CONFIRMED: the `tls_openssl.c`/`tls_wolfssl.c` `tls.h`-contract categorical FP families (DCL13-C on public interface functions, API00-C factually-wrong-on-ternary-guarded `tls_connection_established`, API05-C companion-pointer+size idiom, MSC37-C preprocessor-branch-blind reach-end, MSC01-C no-final-else optional-config guard clauses, MSC07-C goto-label-misfire, DCL30-C heap-vs-local-storage confusion, EXP30-C pure-accessor-args, EXP39-C cross-function `union tls_event_data` conflation, ARR01-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-correct-idiom, STR31-C misapplied-to-non-char-array, DCL37-C block-scope-local misclassified as file-scope, CON03-C/CON32-C/POS49-C no-pthread) extend verbatim to a **third** TLS backend (GnuTLS), confirming they are driven by the shared `tls.h` multi-backend interface and generic sqc gaps, not backend-specific.** ~110 of this batch's 137 findings are one of these already-documented classes; see prior `41plus_b44`/`b45`/`b133` entries for full detail, not re-derived here.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (9 instances, one function): MEM30-C false use-after-free — free-then-reallocate-via-output-param not recognized as clearing freed-state.** `tls_global_set_params()`: `gnutls_certificate_free_credentials(global->xcred)` (`:760`) frees the credentials, then `gnutls_certificate_allocate_credentials(&global->xcred)` (`:764`) immediately writes a **fresh** handle into `global->xcred` via its output-param (address-of) call — but sqc doesn't track that the field now holds a new value, so every subsequent legitimate use of `global->xcred` for the rest of the function (`:764,773,779,792,798,806,812,826,851`) is misflagged as accessing freed memory. Distinct from the already-documented `SSL_CTX_set_cert_store`/`X509_STORE_new` ownership-*transfer* MEM31-C FP family (openssl) — this is a same-variable free-then-realloc, not an ownership handoff to a different object.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances across 2 functions, extends the "MEM30 reassign clears freed-state" fix area to struct *fields*): MEM30-C false use-after-free on `conn->pull_buf` — the existing pointer-reassignment/fresh-binding fix (task 232, plain local pointer variables) does not cover a `struct`-field write.** `tls_connection_handshake()` (`:1477,1479,1568`) and `tls_connection_decrypt()` (`:1622,1624`) both do `wpabuf_free(conn->pull_buf); conn->pull_buf = wpabuf_dup(in_data); if (conn->pull_buf == NULL) ...; conn->pull_buf_offset = wpabuf_head(conn->pull_buf);` — the field reassignment on the line right after the free is not tracked as clearing the "freed" state, so the immediately-following NULL-check and dereference are misflagged as UAF, and the false state persists to a later use in the same function (`:1568`). Worth checking whether the points_to/free-tracking module's fresh-binding logic can be extended from local variables to `obj->field = expr` assignments generally.
- **NEW, genuine bug (moderate confidence): resource leak on 2 error paths in `tls_connection_init()`.** `tls_gnutls_init_session()` successfully initializes `conn->session` (a real GnuTLS session handle); if the subsequent `gnutls_credentials_set()` fails (`:263`) or `gnutls_certificate_allocate_credentials()` fails (`:271`), the function does `os_free(conn); return NULL;` on both paths without ever calling `gnutls_deinit(conn->session)` — the already-initialized session is leaked. Not flagged by sqc. Closest rule: MEM31-C. `upstream_present: unknown`.
- **NEW, genuine bug (low confidence, OOM-only trigger): `%s`-format NULL argument, same class as the `eap_sim_db.c` (`41plus_b159`) finding.** `tls_connection_verify_peer()`'s cert-chain loop (`:1300-1305`): if `os_malloc(len + 1)` fails, `buf` stays NULL, but the very next statement unconditionally does `wpa_printf(MSG_DEBUG, "...: %s", ..., buf)` with the NULL `buf` — real UB on most non-glibc libcs. `upstream_present: unknown`.
- **NEW, genuine bug (low confidence, OOM-only trigger): invalid free of a caller-owned output parameter.** `server_ocsp_status_req()` (the GnuTLS OCSP status-request callback): on `gnutls_malloc(len)` failure (`:732-734`), the code does `os_free(resp)` — but `resp` is a `gnutls_datum_t *` output parameter supplied by the GnuTLS library (typically the address of a caller-side local), not memory this function allocated; freeing it is undefined behavior. Closest rule: MEM34-C. `upstream_present: unknown`.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b171`, 125 findings, 1 file: `src/drivers/ndis_events.c`, lines 1-803: WMI/COM-based NdisMIndicateStatus() event receiver — DCOM wrapper functions, `IWbemObjectSink` vtable callbacks, multi-round WMI adapter-description lookup)

- **NEW: CON03-C/CON07-C break from the standing "no-pthread ⇒ single-threaded ⇒ FP" default for this specific file — genuine (if low-severity) TP.** Unlike the rest of hostapd/wpa_supplicant's eloop-only core, this file explicitly calls `CoInitializeEx(0, COINIT_MULTITHREADED)` (`:722`), putting the process's COM apartment in true multi-threaded mode; incoming `IWbemObjectSink::Indicate` notifications are dispatched by COM's own RPC worker threads, not marshaled onto the caller's thread. `wmi_refcnt`/`wmi_first` (`:21,22`) are plain `static int`s read/written from both `ndis_events_init`/`_destructor` (caller thread) and, via `ndis_events_release`→`ndis_events_destructor`, potentially a WMI callback thread when the last COM reference drops — a real cross-thread race, graded TP (med for the `--wmi_refcnt` compound op at `:141`, low for the once-guarded `wmi_first` check at `:22,735`). Distinguish from every other file in this codebase where the no-pthread default still holds.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances): DCL15-C/DCL19-C "should be static" correctly fires (genuine TP) on the file's own DCOM BSTR-conversion wrapper functions** (`call_IWbemServices_ExecQuery:43`, `call_IWbemServices_ExecNotificationQueryAsync:63`, `call_IWbemLocator_ConnectServer:84`) — verified via `grep -rn` that none of the three appear anywhere outside `ndis_events.c`. Direct contrast with the `driver_ndis.c` (`41plus_b127`) precedent where DCL15/19 misfired on functions genuinely called from a companion translation unit (`driver_ndis_.c`) sqc's scan missed — here there is no such companion caller, so the same-looking finding is a real (if low-value) TP. Always grep for actual cross-file callers before defaulting to the sibling-TU FP.
- **Reconfirms the DCL31-C "unresolvable Windows SDK header" FP class at very high density (68 instances, the majority of this batch)** — every flagged callee (`IWbemServices_ExecQuery/_Release/_CancelAsyncCall`, `IWbemLocator_ConnectServer/_Release`, `IEnumWbemClassObject_Next/_Release`, `IWbemClassObject_Get/_Release`, `IWbemObjectSink_AddRef/_Release`, `IsEqualIID`, `VariantInit/_Clear`, `SafeArrayGetLBound/_UBound/_GetElement`, `CoInitializeEx/_Security`, `CoCreateInstance`, `CoUninitialize`) is a COM macro/API declared only in Windows SDK headers (`<wbemidl.h>`/`<objbase.h>`), never present in this repo.
- **Reconfirms the mutually-exclusive-branch double-free/release CFG-blindness class (10 instances) in a new concrete shape: sequential WMI query "rounds" reusing the same two variable names.** `ndis_events_get_adapter` makes 3 independent WMI query round-trips, each reusing the same `pEnumerator`/`pObj` locals; within and across rounds, each `Release()` is either on a fail-then-return branch or the mutually-exclusive continue branch, and `pEnumerator`/`pObj` are freshly reassigned via a `Next()`/`ExecQuery()` output param before the next round's own release — sqc's free-tracker doesn't see the fresh output-param write as clearing the prior round's "freed" state. `:580,584,590,611,625,644,666,672,678,691`. Extends the `driver_ndis.c` (`41plus_b128`) precedent from cross-*function* reuse to same-function, sequential-round reuse.
- **NEW, batch-local: EXP43-C "same pointer for input/output" extends from NULL,NULL *test-harness* calls to real production Windows API calls with multiple legitimately-NULL optional parameters.** `CreateEvent(NULL, TRUE, FALSE, NULL)` (`:128`) and `CoInitializeSecurity(NULL, -1, NULL, NULL, ..., NULL, ..., NULL)` (`:737`) each have 2-4 literal `NULL` arguments among several optional params; misread as aliased restrict-qualified pointers purely because more than one argument is the `NULL` literal.
- **NEW, batch-local: MSC13-C "dead assignment" misses a read that happens on a *later invocation* of the same function, via a `static`-storage-duration guard flag.** `wmi_first = 0;` (`:735`) looks dead within the current call, but is read by `if (wmi_first)` (`:731`) on the *next* call to `ndis_events_init` — the guard's entire purpose is "once and only once per process." Distinct from the established cross-loop-iteration MSC13-C blind spot (`41plus_b111`); this is cross-*invocation*, via file-scope static state.
- **NEW, genuine bug (moderate confidence): COM object refcount leak on one WMI query-failure path.** `ndis_events_get_adapter`'s `IWbemClassObject_Get(pObj, L"Index", ...)` failure branch (`:546-552`) releases `pSvc` and returns, but — unlike every other failure branch in the same function (`:590,611,625,644,666,672,678,691`, all of which correctly release the in-flight `pObj`/`pEnumerator`) — never calls `IWbemClassObject_Release(pObj)`. Closest rule MEM31-C. `upstream_present: unknown`.
- **NEW, genuine bug (moderate confidence): unchecked adapter-re-query return value can leave a NULL pointer live one statement before a dereference.** `ndis_events_indicate`'s `MSNdis_NotifyAdapterArrival` handler calls `ndis_events_get_adapter(events, events->ifname, NULL)` (`:345`) without checking the return value; `ndis_events_get_adapter` unconditionally NULLs `events->adapter_desc` at entry and can return failure while leaving it NULL (when both the WMI re-query and the `desc==NULL` fallback fail) — the very next statement, `wcscmp(events->adapter_desc, vt.bstrVal)` (`:348`), then dereferences it. Closest rule EXP34-C. `upstream_present: unknown`.
- **NEW, genuine bug (moderate confidence): unchecked SafeArray bound calls can drive an uninitialized-length malloc + out-of-bounds copy loop.** `ndis_events_media_specific` discards the `HRESULT` from `SafeArrayGetLBound`/`SafeArrayGetUBound` (`:262,263`); `lower`/`upper` are plain uninitialized `LONG` locals, so a failure of either call feeds garbage into `data_len = upper - lower + 1` (`:264`), `os_malloc(data_len)`, and the `k = lower..upper` / `SafeArrayGetElement`+`*pos++` copy loop (`:274-277`) — a potential uninitialized-value-driven heap buffer overflow from untrusted NDIS status-indication data. Closest rule ERR33-C (root cause: discarded return value). `upstream_present: unknown`.
- Reconfirms in this batch (not re-detailed above): PRE00-C/PRE12-C genuine (low-severity) TP on `BstrAlloc`/`BstrFree` (`:38,39`), each evaluating its macro parameter twice with no established FP shape for these two rules; API00-C internal-only-API FP on DCOM wrapper params that are only forwarded, never dereferenced, by the wrapper itself (`:43,63,84,439,702`); API05-C `T *ptr, size_t len` idiom FP (`:194`); DCL37-C block-scope-local misclassified as file-scope (`_type:197`); EXP33-C both the `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref sub-shape (`events:710`) and a pointer-address-taken-not-a-read sub-shape (`buf + sizeof(buf)`, `:200`, a new variant of the same "not actually reading the value" family); INT14-C idiomatic 2-byte length-prefix bit-split FP (`:206`); STR34-C misapplied in the *write* direction — narrowing-assignment-into-char misread as a widening-read-of-char (`:211,212,276,470`); INT32-C same-small-stack-buffer pointer-subtraction-cannot-overflow FP (`:217`); EXP36-C `(u8 *)`-is-genuinely-1-byte-aligned FP (`:278`); DCL13-C split three ways: `IWbemObjectSink` vtable dispatch-contract FP (`ppObjArray:304`, `this`/`pObjParam:388,389`) vs. plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP (`events:141,192`); ARR02-C fully-enumerated NULL-terminated initializer-array FP (`class_list:421`); MEM10-C ad-hoc-NULL-check pedantry FP (`:457`); ARR38-C exactly-sized-buffer FP (`events->adapter_desc`, allocated `(len+1)*sizeof(WCHAR)`, `_snwprintf` size arg `len+1`, `:478`); ENV01-C wholesale zero-`getenv()` misfire (`:490`); DCL30-C heap-vs-stack confusion (`events`, `os_zalloc`'d, `:802`).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b174`, 117 findings, `wpa_supplicant/wpa_priv.c`, entire file, lines 89-1216)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED distinguishing test for DCL39-C in this file: the split is exactly zeroed-vs-not-zeroed.** All four `sendmsg()`/`sendto()` struct arguments that are `os_memset(&x, 0, sizeof(x))`'d immediately before use (`msg` at `wpa_priv_l2_rx:471`, `wpa_priv_send_event:884`, `wpa_supplicant_rx_eapol:1163`) are FP per the established memset-zeroed DCL39-C class. `wpa_priv_cmd_get_capa`'s `capa` (`struct wpa_driver_capa`, `:443`) is the odd one out — populated only via the driver's `get_capa()` field assignments plus 3 explicit field overwrites, never `os_memset`-zeroed — so its compiler-inserted padding bytes are genuinely never touched before `sendto(&capa, sizeof(capa), ...)`. Graded TP (medium), matching the established `driver_bsd.c:1105` "8th-instance, never-zeroed sibling" precedent (`16-40_b12`-adjacent entry) rather than the wholesale-FP default for this rule.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, matches the sizeof-not-a-deref family but on a `struct` value, not a pointer): EXP33-C "used uninitialized" fires on `sizeof(addr.sun_path)` where `addr` is a plain (non-pointer) automatic `struct sockaddr_un`, computing a member array's compile-time size, not reading any of `addr`'s actual bytes.** `wpa_priv_interface_init:804`. Same root cause as the standing `sizeof(*ptr)`/`sizeof(ptr->member)` misfire family, now confirmed to extend to `sizeof(struct_var.member)` on a not-yet-initialized plain struct local (as opposed to a pointer).
- **NEW, batch-local, real (moderate-confidence) FN: privsep length-check integer overflow on a world-writable local socket.** `wpa_priv_cmd_authenticate`'s `if (sizeof(*auth) + auth->ie_len + auth->auth_data_len > len)` (`:260`) and `wpa_priv_cmd_associate`'s `if (sizeof(*assoc) + assoc->wpa_ie_len > len)` (`:313`) both sum a fixed `sizeof()` with one or two attacker/peer-controlled `size_t` fields read straight off the wire; the sum can wrap around `SIZE_MAX` and pass the check even though the field(s) are enormous, after which `params.ie_len`/`params.wpa_ie_len` etc. are set to the oversized value while the corresponding pointer still points into the tiny 2000-byte stack `buf`. Because `wpa_priv_interface_init` `chmod()`s the control socket `S_IRWXU|S_IRWXG|S_IRWXO` (`:852`, itself the confirmed-FP POS02-C finding), any local user can reach this path — not just wpa_supplicant. Closest rule INT30-C (root cause) feeding an ARR30-C-shaped OOB read downstream. Watch other `privsep_cmd_*`-consuming handlers in this file/`hostapd`'s privsep peers for the same `sizeof(*hdr) + hdr->variable_len_field > len` shape.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b168`, 132 findings, `wpa_supplicant/scan.c`)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances, one file): MEM30-C/MEM12-C self-referential free-call-argument misfire — the rule flags a `os_free()`/`os_realloc_array()` call's own target expression as "accessing/dereferencing a freed pointer," i.e. it treats the free/realloc call itself as a post-free access rather than the (first and only) free.** `wpa_supplicant_trigger_scan`'s `os_free((u8 *) params->extra_ies);` (`:307`); `wpa_scan_free_params`'s five independent, distinct-field frees `params->ssids[i].ssid`/`extra_ies`/`mac_addr`/`bssid` (`:3891,3892,3901,3903`) — each is the *first* free of that field, not a re-access; `wpas_sched_scan_plans_set`'s `n = os_realloc_array(scan_plans, num + 1, ...)` (`:4214`) flags the realloc's own input argument as "dereferencing freed pointer 'scan_plans'" even though this is the standard incremental-realloc-in-a-loop idiom (`scan_plans = n;` each iteration) with no actual reuse of a stale pointer. Distinguish from genuine MEM30/MEM31 UAF, which requires a *second*, separate access after the free returns.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (≈11 instances): INT13-C/INT14-C member-access-attributed-to-base-pointer conflation — the rule flags a pointer *variable* for "bitwise and arithmetic operations" (INT14-C) or "bitwise operator used on signed operand of type int" (INT13-C) when the actual bitwise/arithmetic operation is applied to a struct *member* or array-indexed value reached through that pointer, not the pointer itself, and often misclaims the pointer's type as `int`.** `wpa_add_scan_freqs_list`'s `mode` (`struct hostapd_hw_modes *`, `:880` — bitwise op is on `mode->channels[i].flag`, arithmetic is `mode->num_channels`, `mode` itself is never touched); `wpa_scan_get_max_rate`'s `i` (`:2061` — bitwise is on `ie[i+2]`, not `i`); `dump_scan_res`'s `r` (`:2552`, same shape on `r->flags`); `scan_snr`'s `res` (INT13-C+INT14-C, `:2639,2646` — bitwise is on `res->flags`, and `res` is a `struct wpa_scan_res *`, not `int` as INT13-C claims); `get_partner_est_tput`'s `ap_info` (`:3453`, bitwise/arithmetic on `ap_info->tbtt_info_hdr`/`->tbtt_info_len`) and `mld_params` (`:3472` — `mld_params + 1` is real pointer arithmetic but the `& EHT_ML_LINK_ID_MSK` is on `*(mld_params+1)`, the dereferenced byte, not the pointer); plus `wpas_wps_in_use`'s `wpa_s` (`:1877`, bitwise on `ssid->key_mgmt`/arithmetic unrelated). Same root-cause family as the already-documented `link_id`/INT13-C "wrong-type-claim on an actually-unsigned param" theme, but generalized here to whole-pointer misattribution.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances): ARR00-C/ARR36-C category error — the rule reports "pointer subtraction/comparison between different arrays" on plain scalar (`int`/`size_t`) variables that are never pointers at all, and in one case cites completely unrelated identifiers from a different line in the same message.** `wpa_scan_result_compar`'s `abs(snr_b - snr_a)` (`:2458,2465` — `snr_a`/`snr_b` are local `int`s assigned via `MIN(snr_b_full, GREAT_SNR)`-style value copies, never pointers; message blames "'snr_b' from 'snr_b_full'" as if one were a pointer derived from the other's array); `wpas_start_pno`'s `num_match_ssid > num_ssid` (`:3973` — both plain `size_t` locals) where the ARR36-C message instead cites `wpa_s->max_match_sets`/`wpa_s->max_sched_scan_ssids`, identifiers from a *different* line (`:3984`) entirely.
- **NEW, batch-local: MSC04-C flow-insensitive call-graph phantom recursion — a claimed indirect-recursion cycle traverses a call edge that is guarded by an argument value that is always false/zero at that specific call site, so the cycle is not actually reachable.** `wpa_supplicant_req_sched_scan` (`:1692`) is flagged as indirectly recursive via `wpa_supplicant_set_state -> wpa_supplicant_start_autoscan -> autoscan_init -> request_scan -> wpa_supplicant_req_sched_scan`, but `wpa_supplicant_start_autoscan` always calls `autoscan_init(wpa_s, 0)` (`wpa_supplicant.c:1018`), and `autoscan_init` has `if (!req_scan) return 0;` *before* ever reaching `request_scan()` (`autoscan.c:107-108`) — the edge `autoscan_init -> request_scan` only exists for the *other* call site (`autoscan_init(wpa_s, 1)` from `ctrl_iface.c`), which the whole-program call graph conflates with this one. Watch for this shape (argument-value-gated early return severing a call-graph edge that a flow-insensitive analysis still draws) recurring elsewhere.
- **NEW, batch-local: ARR37-C "pointer arithmetic on non-array pointer" misfires on the pervasive `(struct T *) + 1` trailing-variable-data idiom.** `wpa_scan_result_compar`'s `(const u8 *) (wa + 1)`/`(wb + 1)` (`:2409,2414`) compute the address one past a single `struct wpa_scan_res` to reach IE bytes that were allocated as extra space after the fixed struct (flexible-array-member emulation without C99 syntax) — identical to the already-idiomatic `(res + 1)` pattern used throughout this same file (`wpa_scan_get_ie`, `dump_scan_res`, etc., never separately flagged). Pointer-to-one-past-a-single-object is well-defined per C99 6.5.6p7 treating any object as a 1-element array; not a real bug.
- **Reconfirms/extends in this batch (not re-detailed above):** DCL13-C eloop-timeout-callback dispatch-contract FP extended to `wpa_supplicant_delayed_sched_scan_timeout`/`wpa_supplicant_sched_scan_timeout` (`:346,358`) and the `scan_res_handler` vtable FP extended to `scan_only_handler` (`:3758`); plain-internal-helper DCL13-C genuine-if-low-value TP at high density, including two *entirely unused* params (`wpas_fils_req_param_add_max_channel`'s `wpa_s:591`, `wpa_add_scan_ssid`'s `wpa_s:924`, `get_partner_est_tput`'s `wpa_s:3438`) alongside the usual read-only-param shape (`:402,576,859,2530,2594,3422,4148`); EXP33-C static-function-called-not-a-variable parser bug extended to `wpa_supplicant_extra_ies` (`:311,1860`); EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-dereference extended to an *uninitialized*-pointer-used-only-in-`sizeof` sub-case (`ap_info:3576` before its first real assignment, `params:3795` in `os_zalloc(sizeof(*params))`); ARR01-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-correct-idiom (`ap_info:3450,3463`, `src->sched_scan_plans:3847`); MSC13-C both the loop-boundary-read-miss FP (`bss:473`, `dl_list_for_each`) and genuine dead-initial-assignment TP (`wps:730`, `partner_est_throughput:3512`); MEM12-C flow-insensitive leak-list FP reconfirmed on a provably-NULL-on-this-path field (`params->freqs:509`, guarded by an outer `params->freqs == NULL` check earlier in the same function); DCL30-C heap-vs-local-storage confusion at very high density (7 instances: `ssids:430` from `os_calloc`, `extra_ie:720,2212` from `wpabuf_alloc`, `scan_res:3715,3724` from the driver call, `params:3875` from `os_zalloc`); EXP40-C phantom cast-away-const where neither side is const (`*start = ssid:1276`); INT30-C wrap-on-small-driver/config-bounded-value FP (`params.num_ssids + 1:1290`, `num + 1:1424,1520` — all bounded by `WPAS_MAX_SCAN_SSIDS`/`num_multichan_concurrent`, far below any wrap threshold); MSC01-C no-final-else guard-clause pedantry at very high density (9 instances); DCL37-C block-scope-local misclassified as file-scope (`_wa`/`_wb` x4, qsort comparator locals); EXP05-C cast-away-const-read-only-overlay extended to the qsort `(void *) a/b` comparator-argument idiom (`:2372,2373,2487,2488`) and refuted where no cast-away-const exists at all (`token:4222`, already-`const char *` passed to a `const char *`-taking `sscanf`); ARR02-C initializer-sized-const-array FP extended to 15 MCS/SNR rate tables in one file (`:2665-2940`); INT32-C `abs()`-may-overflow-at-INT_MIN pedantry on provably small-bounded operands (SNR dB values, `:2458,2465,2466`; IE-derived `u8` channel-segment numbers, `:3215,3218,3219` — neither domain can ever approach `INT_MIN`); API00-C internal-only-API FP reconfirmed at very high density (17 of 19 instances — never-externally-nullable `wpa_s`/`res`/`ies`/`scan_res`/`mask` params) plus a doc-nullable-by-design pass-through sub-shape (`wpa_supplicant_get_scan_results`'s `info`/`bssid:3656`, `wpa_supplicant_update_scan_results`'s `bssid:3741`, both documented "%NULL for all/if not available" and never dereferenced in the function itself); WIN04-C wholesale-impractical function-pointer-encryption FP on an ordinary local qsort comparator variable (`compar:3663`); MSC07-C goto-target-label-after-return reconfirmed (`failed:3877`, `fail:4298`);
