### FN read-through note (`41plus_b168`)

Full read of `wpa_supplicant/scan.c` (4330 lines) found no additional high-confidence missed bugs beyond the findings already adjudicated above. Checked specifically: the RNR/ML-element parsing in `get_partner_est_tput`/`mlo_scan_est_throughput` (attacker-controlled Beacon/Probe-Response wire data) — all reads are bounds-checked against `len`/`tbtt_info_len` before use; every `os_calloc`/`os_malloc`/`os_realloc` call site in this file checks its return value; no unfreed allocation found on any early-return path (`params.filter_ssids`/`params.freqs` are freed unconditionally on all exits from `wpa_supplicant_scan`, `wpa_supplicant_req_sched_scan`, `wpas_start_pno`).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b169`, 127 findings, one file: `src/ap/ieee802_11_eht.c`, EHT/802.11be capability-IE builders + Multi-Link (ML) association/reconfiguration parsing, 2811 lines)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (8 instances): MEM30-C/MEM31-C free-state bleeds across two sequential, independent `dl_list_for_each_safe` loops in the same function that reuse the same loop-variable name — direct cross-file reconfirmation of the `ieee802_1x_kay.c` (`41plus_b111`) precedent.** `ml_deinit_link_reconf_req` has two back-to-back `dl_list_for_each_safe(info, tmp, ...)` loops (over `req_list->add_req` then `req_list->del_req`), each freeing its own list's nodes; sqc flags every `os_free(info)`/`dl_list_del(&info->list)` in the *second* loop as UAF/double-free of the *first* loop's already-freed `info`, even though the macro's own initializer clause reassigns `info` to a fresh, live node at the start of each loop. `ieee802_11_eht.c:1521,1523(x3),1524(x2 — MEM30-C+MEM31-C)`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances): EXP34-C "potential null pointer dereference" on `req_list` fires wholesale across a whole file's internal ML-reconfiguration helpers, none of which are ever reachable with a NULL `req_list`.** Two sub-shapes: (a) correlated same-statement guard — `req_list = *req_list_ptr;` immediately after `if (!(*req_list_ptr)) return;`/`if (!(*req_list_ptr)) {...goto fail;}` (`ml_deinit_link_reconf_req:1515`, `hostapd_parse_link_reconf_req_reconf_mle:2404`); (b) internal-invariant-never-null parameter — `req_list` is a plain `struct link_reconf_req_list *` parameter on `hostapd_reject_all_reconf_req`/`hostapd_send_link_reconf_resp`/`hostapd_validate_link_reconf_req`, each only ever called (once, from one call site apiece) after a successful non-NULL allocation upstream in `hostapd_handle_link_reconf_req` (`:1800,1859,2465`).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances, one file): ARR37-C "compound assignment on non-array pointer" misfires on a plain `size_t sta_info_len`/`sta_prof_len` byte-counter — direct reconfirmation of the `16-40_b3`/`16-40_b13` `size_t left` precedent in a 3rd/4th file.** `sta_info_len += link_info->nstr_bitmap_len` (`:1444`) and `sta_info_len += ETH_ALEN/2/3/nstr_bitmap_size` (`:2162,2167,2172,2198`) all operate on `size_t sta_info_len;` (declared `:1356,2105`) — a length counter, never a pointer of any kind.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances, one file): EXP40-C "pointer to const assigned to non-const pointer without cast" is a phantom finding where NEITHER side is const-qualified at all** — extends the existing `eap_sim_db.c`/`ieee802_1x_kay.c` "neither side const" EXP40-C FP class with a new recurring shape: `T *local = pos;` where `pos` is itself a plain (non-const) `u8 *`/local variable, not a function's const-qualified parameter. `u8 *buf = pos;` (`hostapd_reject_all_reconf_req:1798`), `u8 *kde_pos = pos;` (`:1970`), `u8 *mle_pos = pos;` (`:2012`) — all three `pos` locals are plain `u8 *`, declared without `const` in `hostapd_reject_all_reconf_req`'s own parameter list or `hostapd_send_link_reconf_resp`'s local declarations.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances, one file): EXP33-C "may be used uninitialized" on a local declared just before an early per-iteration `continue;` that skips it, then unconditionally assigned (before any read) on every path that doesn't `continue` — sqc's CFG doesn't see that the `continue` always precedes any use.** `link_bss` (`hostapd_eid_eht_basic_ml_common:532`, `hostapd_eid_eht_basic_ml_len:694` — both `if (link_id == hapd->mld_link_id || !link->valid) continue;` immediately followed by unconditional `link_bss = hostapd_mld_get_link_bss(...)`), `other_hapd` (`hostapd_mld_validate_assoc_info:1154`), `sub_elem_end` (`hostapd_process_ml_assoc_req:1358`, guarded by two earlier `continue;` branches that never reach `sub_elem_end`'s only use).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, cross-function): ARR00-C/ARR36-C "pointers/subtraction from different arrays" cites a pointer's *declaration-time initializer* (`= NULL;`) as its provenance instead of its real assignment a few lines later, when both the real assignment and the "different array" comparison target are offsets into the same wire buffer.** `hostapd_parse_link_reconf_req_sta_profile`'s `const u8 *sta_info = NULL, *end;` (`:2108`) is reassigned `sta_info = per_sta_prof->variable;` (`:2200`, itself `elem->data`, itself `buf`) before `*sta_info > end - sta_info` (`:2201`) and `sta_prof_len > (size_t)(end - sta_info)` (`:2263`) — `end` (`buf + len`) and `sta_info` are the same underlying buffer; sqc's array-provenance tracker appears to latch onto the `= NULL` declaration rather than the real assignment.
- **Reconfirms/extends in this batch (not re-detailed above):** DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable" on the `eid`-parameter/`pos`-alias-of-`eid` IE-builder idiom at very high density (11 instances: `:129,133,179,194,257,455,665,1064,1081,2783,2810`, plus `pos` derived from `mgmt->u.auth.variable`, a caller-frame pointer, at `:1064,1081` in `auth_skip_fixed_fields`) — direct extension of the `ieee802_11_ht.c`/`ieee802_11_vht.c` precedent to hostap's newest (EHT/802.11be) IE-builder file; DCL13-C misses the write-through-`*pos++`-alias mutation of an `eid` parameter (`hostapd_eid_eht_operation:183`) — factually wrong "not modified" claim, same `ieee802_11.c` precedent; DCL13-C plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP at high density (`hapd`/`mld_info`/`info`/`assoc_sta` params, ~14 instances, several structurally *unused* entirely — `hostapd_eid_eht_ml_beacon_len`'s `hapd:881`, `check_valid_eht_mcs_nss`'s `hapd:273`, `hostapd_process_ml_assoc_req_addr`'s `hapd:1174`) vs. the `ap_for_each_sta` iterator-callback dispatch-contract FP (`hostapd_ml_check_sta_entry_by_link_addr_iter`'s `hapd`/`sta:2058,2059`, matching the fixed `int (*cb)(struct hostapd_data *, struct sta_info *, void *)` typedef, `sta_info.h:351` — new callback family beyond the established `eloop_timeout_handler` precedent); MSC17-C fallthrough misfire on cases that already end in an unconditional `return` (`:1063`, `WLAN_AUTH_OPEN`/`WLAN_AUTH_EPPKE`); MSC01-C no-final-else graded FP where a trailing unconditional statement after the if/else-if chain already handles the "neither" case (`auth_skip_fixed_fields`'s `return pos;` after the SAE commit/confirm branches, `:1076`); EXP34-C same-condition short-circuit-guard FP extended to `lsta` (`!lsta || ... lsta->mld_info...`, `:2237`); EXP30-C side-effect-free-macro-arg FP extended to `MAC2STR` in `wpa_printf` debug logging (2 instances: `:1342,2072`); EXP33-C output-param-not-tracked FP extended to `ieee802_11_elems elems` populated by `ieee802_11_parse_elems(pos, ..., &elems, N)` (2 instances: `:1126,2655`) and the `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-dereference sub-class (`elem:2114`); ARR36-C same-buffer-cast-overlay FP extended twice more — `pos`/`kde_pos`/`mle_pos` all aliasing the single `os_zalloc`'d `buf` in `hostapd_send_link_reconf_resp` (3 instances: `:1974,2023,2026`), and `mgmt` (`(const struct ieee80211_mgmt *) buf`) vs. `mgmt->u.action.u.link_reconf_req.variable` in `hostapd_handle_link_reconf_req` (`:2648`); ## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b176`, 115 findings, `src/wps/httpread.c`, entire file, 848 lines)

- **STR37-C/STR00-C `ctype.h` missing-`(unsigned char)`-cast findings graded genuine (if low-severity) TP throughout this file, reinforcing the `wpas_dbus_getter_state`/`isspace()` precedent — now on directly network-received HTTP header/chunk/trailer bytes, the strongest-yet input-trust case for this class.** `isgraph`/`isdigit`/`isxdigit`/`isalpha`/`isupper`/`tolower` calls on `hbp`/`rawuri`/`cbp` throughout `word_eq`, `httpread_hdr_option_analyze`, `httpread_hdr_analyze` (≈34 instances) all pass a plain (possibly-signed) `char` with no cast, on bytes read straight off the WPS UPnP/HTTP TCP socket before any charset validation beyond the loop's own `isgraph`/`isdigit` test.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances, one file): STR34-C misfires in the *narrowing* (store) direction, extending the existing `os_internal.c`/`fst_read_next_text_param` "direction-mismatch" class (categorical_patterns.md:6659,6698) to a hex-decode + NUL-terminate idiom.** `*uri++ = hex2byte(rawuri + 1);` (`:273`, storing `hex2byte()`'s `int` 0-255 result into a `char`) and `*uri++ = c;` (`:276`, storing an already-widened `int c` back into `char`) are narrowing assignments, not the widening/sign-extension-on-read the rule targets; `*uri = 0;` (`:280`) and `*hbp = 0;` (`:441`) assign the literal `0`, with zero possible sign-extension. `httpread.c:273,276,280,441`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, one file, batch-local — watch for a 3rd): INT18-C "arithmetic evaluated in smaller type before comparison/assignment to a larger type" fires when BOTH operands and the destination are the same (plain `int`) type — no type-widening/promotion boundary exists on the line at all.** `new_alloc_nbytes = h->body_alloc_nbytes + HTTPREAD_BODYBUF_DELTA;` (`:497`) and the `h->content_length + 1` comparison (`:505`) — `body_alloc_nbytes`/`content_length`/`HTTPREAD_BODYBUF_DELTA`/`new_alloc_nbytes` are all `int`; the rule's stated premise (a smaller-type-then-widened computation) is factually false, even though a *real* (already mitigated by an explicit post-hoc wraparound check two lines later, `:506`) int-overflow concern exists in the same vicinity.

### FN read-through note (`41plus_b176`)

Full read of `src/wps/httpread.c` (848 lines) found no additional missed bugs beyond what sqc already flagged (the `atol()`/`strtoul()` missing-error-checking findings above are the file's two genuine, if narrow, weak spots on attacker-controlled `Content-Length`/chunk-size wire fields). All `os_malloc`/`os_realloc` call sites check for `NULL` and `goto bad`; the only socket owned by this module (`h->sd`) is explicitly documented as caller-owned and never closed here; `httpread_destroy()` frees `body`/`uri` unconditionally and is idempotent-safe (`os_free(NULL)`); no early-return path skips a prior allocation's cleanup.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b181`, 107 findings, `src/utils/wpa_debug.c`, 2026-08-07)

MSC13-C fired on `x = NULL;`/`x = os_strdup(...)` assignments to these same globals (`:206,576,619,629`) claiming the value is "never read" — but the value is read by *later calls* via the standard `if (!x) return;`/`if (x) ...` guards threaded throughout this file — also FP. Any rule reasoning about a static global's liveness/ownership needs cross-call analysis, not single-function-body analysis.
- **CON03-C/CON07-C/CON33-C/CON34-C no-thread FP class reconfirmed at very high density (33 instances) on this file's debug-infrastructure globals** (`wpa_debug_level`, `wpa_debug_show_keys`, `wpa_debug_timestamp`, `wpa_debug_syslog`, `wpa_debug_tracing_file`, `out_file`, `last_path`, `wpa_msg_cb`, `wpa_msg_ifname_cb`, `hostapd_logger_cb`) plus `strerror(errno)` at `:592` — same single-threaded eloop model as all prior CON03/07/33/34 FP entries.

None of these paths are attacker-controlled in the hostap threat model (kernel pseudo-file, kernel-reported mountpoint, or admin config), which caps real severity, but per this audit's literal-rule-text convention (matching the ERR33/ERR00 unchecked-I/O default) the violations are real as written. Worth revisiting if a stricter "no realistic attack surface = FP" convention is adopted elsewhere.
- **FN read-through: none found.** Full read of `wpa_debug.c` (916 lines) found no missed error-path resource leaks or unvalidated-input parsing — this is pure debug/logging infrastructure (no wire-format or attacker-controlled buffer parsing), and every `os_malloc`/`os_strdup` call site already has a NULL check with a clean early return.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b184`, 105 findings, `src/eap_peer/eap_ttls.c`, entire file, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (18+ instances, one file): MEM30-C field-free-vs-struct-free confusion.** When a struct pointer's *field* is freed via a helper (`eap_ttls_free_key(data)` frees `data->key_data`, or `os_free(data->session_id)`), the analyzer treats every subsequent `data->member` access as a use-after-free of `data` itself — but `data` (the struct pointer) was never freed, only one of its fields was, and it remains perfectly valid to keep dereferencing `data` afterward. `eap_ttls.c:226,310-331,1763,1773`. Same root family as the already-confirmed `ieee802_1x_kay.c` MEM31-C false-double-free-across-free-then-NULL-reset-then-goto-fail entry, but this is the plain if/else-branch variant rather than a goto-fail variant.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b191`, 100 findings, `src/ap/wpa_auth_ie.c`)

- **NEW, batch-local: ARR30-C "unbounded while loop with pointer increment" misfires on a byte-emission loop driven by right-shifting a fixed-width integer to zero (`while (capab) { *pos++ = capab & 0xff; capab >>= 8; }`).** Since `capab` is `u32`, the loop can run at most 4 iterations, and the caller already validated `len >= 2 + flen` (`flen` being the exact byte count this loop will emit) before entering it — provably bounded by both the operand's fixed width and an earlier explicit length check. `wpa_write_rsnxe:556`, `wpa_write_rsnxe_override:592`. Only 2 instances/1 batch so far; watch for a 3rd file before treating as fully generalized (distinct from the already-confirmed "bounded by an in-body per-iteration guard" ARR30-C shape — here the bound comes from the *type width* of the loop-driving variable, not a counter compared against a max).
- Reconfirms/extends established classes at very high density in this file: WIN04-C wholesale-impractical "function pointer without encryption" misfire extended to a single dense 35-instance burst — every hit is a plain enum-constant (`selector =`/`sm->wpa_key_mgmt =`) or protocol-flag assignment inside an `if(0){}else if`/`else if` AKM-selection chain riddled with `#ifdef CONFIG_FILS`/`CONFIG_IEEE80211R_AP`/`CONFIG_SHA384`/`CONFIG_SAE`/`CONFIG_OWE`/`CONFIG_DPP` blocks — no function pointer of any kind appears on any flagged line, matching the established `dpp.c:2120`/`wps_supplicant.c:2189` "flatly wrong claim" + `#ifdef`-adjacent-parser-desync families; ARR39-C "double scaling" on `buf + sizeof(buf)` where `buf` is `u8 buf[1500]` (7 instances) — byte-pointer arithmetic has no scaling to double, extends the established byte-pointer ARR39-C FP class; INT30-C "may wrap" on the size-checked IE-append idiom's own guard condition (`sizeof(buf) - (pos - buf) < X`, 5 instances) — the check that proves safety is not itself an overflow site, matches the `wpas_populate_assoc_ies` precedent; INT32-C "signed subtraction may overflow" on `(pos - buf) - 2` within the same small (<=1500-byte) fixed stack buffer (4 instances) — extends the established small-stack-buffer pointer-subtraction-cannot-overflow class; MSC01-C no-final-else/no-default guard-clause pedantry (6 instances) — every instance has either an explicit default value already assigned before the chain, both branches returning (fallthrough is the intended success path), or (one instance, `:1021`) a final `else` that genuinely exists later in the same `#ifdef`-split chain, misattributed due to preprocessor-branch-blindness; API00-C internal-only-API no-NULL-check FP (10 instances, `buf`/`pos`/`data`/`sm`/overflow-on-`data_len`/`data2_len`, all internally-owned/bounded); DCL13-C split three ways — genuine-if-low-value plain-read-only-helper TP (10 instances: `conf`/`assoc_sm`/`sm`/`wpa_auth` on static/one-line accessor functions) vs. the `wpa_auth_for_each_auth` callback typedef `int(*)(struct wpa_authenticator*,void*)` dispatch-contract FP (`wpa_auth_okc_iter`/`wpa_auth_pmksa_iter`'s `a`, 2 instances, new callback-typedef vtable beyond the already-documented eloop-timeout/driver-ops/sqlite3_exec families) vs. the alias-mutation-missed FP (`buf` written only through a derived `hdr`/`pos` pointer, 2 instances: `wpa_write_wpa_ie:28`, `wpa_write_rsnxe:534`); MEM12-C flow-insensitive false-leak on struct-owned persistent buffers (`sm->wpa_ie`/`sm->rsnxe`, freed via `os_free` before each realloc and at teardown, 2 instances) — extends the ownership-persists-elsewhere family from module-static globals to per-state-machine struct fields; ## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b199`, 94 findings, `wpa_supplicant/notify.c`, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances, one file): API00-C "does not validate integer parameter for overflow before arithmetic" on `os_zalloc(2 * ssi_len + 1)` in the NAN discovery-result/replied/receive notify wrappers is FP — bounded external-length, not the OSU-XML unbounded-malloc shape flagged as a genuine TP in the task brief.** `wpas_notify_nan_discovery_result`/`_replied`/`_receive` (`:1102,1131,1157`) all size a hex-dump buffer from a NAN Service-Specific-Info `ssi_len` (`size_t`) originating from `nan_de`/USD frame parsing. Unlike the Hotspot 2.0 OSU case (an XML-declared length with no wire-format ceiling), `ssi_len` here is always derived from a TLV/attribute length field bounded to at most a few hundred/thousand bytes by the underlying 802.11 frame size — `2*ssi_len+1` cannot reach `SIZE_MAX/2` on any real platform. Distinguishes the "unbounded declared-length-to-malloc" TP pattern from "external-but-wire-bounded-length-to-malloc" FP; check the length field's actual encoding width/frame ceiling before applying the OSU precedent, don't pattern-match on "external length feeds malloc" alone.
- **Reconfirms at high volume in a single dbus-notification-wrapper file (58 API00-C, 2 EXP34-C instances): the internal-only-API FP class extends cleanly to `wpas_notify_*` event-notification wrappers.** Every `wpas_notify_*` function in this file has 0-2 internal call sites (grep-verified across `wpa_supplicant.c`, `p2p_supplicant*.c`, `interworking.c`, `wps_supplicant.c`, `dbus/dbus_new_handlers.c`, `nan_supplicant.c`, `pr_supplicant.c`, `hs20_supplicant.c`), each passing a fixed non-NULL argument (already-validated struct fields, `&global` singletons, or values dereferenced earlier in the same caller block) — never an externally-nullable API surface. Two EXP34-C member-access-on-possibly-NULL findings (`wpas_notify_network_selected`'s `ssid->id` `:267`, `wpas_notify_network_removed`'s `ssid->key_mgmt` `:427`) are the same class: all 12 call sites of `wpas_notify_network_removed` alone were grep-verified to pass a non-NULL `ssid`.
- **Reconfirms: MSC01-C no-final-else on a 2-arm if/else-if whose omitted default is a legitimate no-op — FP (2 instances, `:103,114`, nested transition-state checks in `wpas_notify_state_changed`).**
- **Reconfirms: EXP30-C unsequenced-args misfire on pure accessor pairs — FP (2 instances): `wpabuf_head(cert->cert)`/`wpabuf_len(cert->cert)` (`:893`) and the standing `MAC2STR(dev_addr)`/`MAC2STR(peer_addr)` pure-read pair (`:1237`).**
- **Reconfirms: DCL13-C plain-helper-never-modified — genuine (if low-value) TP, 8 instances (`global`x3, `ssid`x3, `cert`, plus 2 fully-unused-param instances in the `wpas_notify_pmk_cache_added` TODO stub `:1077,1078`), none matching the eloop/dispatch-table FP shape since every one of these functions is called directly by name, not through a function-pointer contract.**
- **FN read-through note (`41plus_b199`):** read the full 1245-line file. No `os_malloc`/`os_zalloc`/`os_strdup` calls lack a NULL check (`cert_hex`/`ssi_hex`, both checked and both freed via `os_free` on every path). No sockets/fds in this file. File marked clean for FN.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b203`, 91 findings, `src/common/ieee802_11_defs.h`, 2026-08-07)

- **CONFIRMED (44 instances, this file): the previously batch-local `STRUCT_PACKED` DCL40-C bug now graduates to fully confirmed.** Every `struct X { ... } STRUCT_PACKED;` definition in this header (`ieee80211_hdr`, `ieee80211_mgmt`, every EHT/MLE/RRM/action-frame struct, etc.) gets flagged as an "incompatible declaration of object 'STRUCT_PACKED'" against every *other* `STRUCT_PACKED`-suffixed struct in the file — sqc's parser is treating the trailing `STRUCT_PACKED` attribute-macro token as if it were a redeclared identifier/object being compared across unrelated struct types, rather than a per-declaration packed-attribute annotation. Matches and massively extends the `eap_psk_common.h` single-instance entry (line ~504 above); safe to treat this shape as categorical FP anywhere `STRUCT_PACKED` (or equivalent `__attribute__((packed))`-wrapper macros) is used as a trailing struct annotation.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (26 instances, one file): MEM33-C "inline struct definition with flexible array member embedded ... in anonymous union" misfires on the standard 802.11 tagged wire-frame union idiom.** `struct ieee80211_mgmt`'s `union u { struct { ...; u8 variable[]; } STRUCT_PACKED auth; ... } u;` (and the nested `action.u` sub-union of per-action-code variants) is the textbook "one wire-format struct per frame subtype, mutually exclusive, dispatched by an outer discriminant field" pattern mirrored verbatim in the Linux kernel's own `struct ieee80211_mgmt` — every alternative's FAM struct is the last member of its own immediately enclosing struct, and the enclosing union is itself the last member all the way up the nesting chain. Technically brushes against the strict C11 6.7.2.1p3 wording ("a union containing such a structure ... shall not be a member of a structure"), but this is a decades-old, GCC/Clang-supported, ecosystem-wide convention no real reviewer would ask hostap to redesign; grade FP, medium confidence given the standard-text nuance.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances, one file): MEM33-C "flexible array structure 'X' declared with global storage. Only dynamic storage duration is allowed" fires on plain `struct X { ...; u8 variable[]; } STRUCT_PACKED;` TYPE definitions — no object/variable is declared anywhere on these lines at all** (`eht_ml_basic_common_info`/`ieee80211_eht_per_sta_profile`/`eht_ml_probe_req_common_info`/`eht_ml_reconf_common_info`/`eht_ml_reconf_sta_info`/`ieee80211_eht_ml`, `:2882,2940,2956,2989,3017,3032`). Rule-engine bug: mistaking a struct-type declaration for an instantiated global-storage-duration object.
- **Reconfirms/extends the established STR31-C non-char-array misapplication class (10 instances, extends `driver.h:2713`'s single-instance precedent from "Batch-local" toward fully confirmed): fires on plain `u8 variable[0]`/`u8 change_seq[1]` byte fields that hold raw binary wire data, never string content** (`:1016,2116,2228,2239,2249,2267,2311,2333,2370,3270`).
- **NEW, batch-local: DCL38-C "should use [] not [1]" misfires on `ieee80211_hdr_s1g_beacon.change_seq[1]` (`:1016`) — a genuine fixed 1-octet 802.11 "Change Sequence" field per spec, not a struct-hack/FAM placeholder; the truly variable trailing fields (`next_tbtt`/`compressed_ssid`/`ano`) are explicitly documented as *not* struct members at all (conditionally present, read via manual offset math elsewhere), so widening `change_seq` to `[]` would be actively wrong.**
- **NEW, batch-local but rule-text-correct: PRE01-C genuine (medium-confidence) TP on `IEEE80211_FC(type, stype)`'s `host_to_le16((type << 2) | (stype << 4))` — `type`/`stype` are used as bare rvalue operands inside `<<` with no individual parens (`:1028`).** Distinguishes from the token-paste/case-label-only PRE01-C FP family: every current call site passes a plain enum constant so there's no live bug, but per the established "graded on the macro definition, not current call sites" precedent (`41plus_b_INT_RANGE` entry above) this is a real latent precedence hazard, not a category error. The companion PRE02-C on the same line (`:1028`) stays FP — the macro body is a single `host_to_le16(...)` call, already an atomic primary expression.
- **NEW: a genuinely broken, currently-unused macro caught incidentally by a PRE02-C finding.** `TX_BF_CAP_CALIBRATION_MASK` (`:1345`) reads `((u32) (BIT(6) | BIT(7))` — 5 open parens, 4 close, missing the final `)` that every sibling `TX_BF_CAP_*` macro has. `grep`-verified zero uses anywhere in the tree, so it's dead code with no live impact, but it's a real, fixable typo; graded TP even though sqc's own PRE02-C rationale text (precedence-parenthesization) doesn't literally match the defect (unbalanced parens, not missing outer wrapping).
- **FN read-through note (`41plus_b203`):** this file is pure data/type definitions (structs, enums, `#define`s) plus two trivial 3-line `static inline bool` helpers (`he_reg_is_indoor`/`he_reg_is_sp`, `:2628,2634`, verified correct). ## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b197`, 95 findings, `src/drivers/driver_nl80211_scan.c`, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, batch-local, extends the confirmed "free-then-goto-retry" branch-blind-free family (previously only seen for MEM31-C, single mutually-exclusive branch, `driver_nl80211.c:7128`) to a much larger MEM30-C use-after-free/double-free cluster driven by a goto-retry loop that REALLOCATES before the flagged lines run.** `nl80211_get_scan_results`'s `-EAGAIN` retry path does `wpa_scan_results_free(res); goto try_again;`, which jumps back to the `try_again:` label and immediately does `res = os_zalloc(sizeof(*res));` before any of the function's later code (the `ret==0` success return, the noise-update loop, or the final failure-path free) can execute. Traced every branch of the function by hand: `res` is freed at most once on any single path, and the flagged "use-after-free"/"double-free" lines are all on paths where `res` is provably fresh. Produced 7 FP findings in one function (6 MEM30-C + 1 MEM31-C, `:1055,1056,1060,1061×2,1064,1068×2`), plus 1 DCL30-C FP on the same `res` ("returns pointer to local variable" — it's `os_zalloc`'d heap memory, not automatic storage, `:1064`). Watch for this exact shape (free-on-a-retry-branch immediately followed by `goto` back to a label that reallocates the same variable) anywhere else a `try_again:`/retry-loop idiom is used — it's a strictly worse case than the single-mutually-exclusive-branch shape already documented, since it can taint a whole downstream block of lines, not just the one free-adjacent line.
- **NEW, batch-local: FLP03-C "floating-point division without error checking" misfires on plain `int` arithmetic — extends the existing INT30/INT33 "rule doesn't see real operand types" category-error family to FLP03-C specifically.** `r->level /= 100; /* mBm to dBm */` (`:871`) — `level` is `int` per `struct wpa_scan_res` (`driver.h:420`); there is no floating-point type anywhere in the expression. ## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b208`, 88 findings, `src/drivers/driver_privsep.c`, entire file, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances, one file): MEM12-C "leaked struct-field resources" misfires on error/success returns from a `*_set_param()`/setup function that never itself owns the struct — the struct's own `deinit()` companion function is the real cleanup point, and is verified (via call-chain trace) to always run.** `wpa_driver_privsep_set_param()`'s early `return -1;`s (`:717,734,750,761,777,782`) each leave one or more of `drv->own_socket_path`/`drv->own_cmd_path`/`drv->priv_socket`/`drv->cmd_socket` un-freed *in that function*, and MEM12-C flags them as leaked — but `drv` itself is a long-lived object whose lifecycle is closed out by `wpa_driver_privsep_deinit()`, and tracing the actual caller chain (`wpa_supplicant.c:7638` `wpa_drv_set_param()` fails → `wpa_supplicant_init_iface` returns -1 → `wpa_supplicant.c:8337` `wpa_supplicant_deinit_iface()` → `wpa_drv_deinit()` → the driver's own `.deinit` op) confirms `deinit()` is unconditionally called on every `set_param` failure path in the real program, and `deinit()` correctly frees/closes every one of those fields (checked non-NULL/`>=0` first). Also covers the matching success-path `return 0;` (`:785`) where retaining the fields is by design, not a leak. Distinguish from the ordinary flow-insensitive MEM12-C FP (which is usually about a field being NULL-checked/provably-unset on the flagged path) — this is specifically about *cross-function* ownership: don't grade a struct-field MEM12-C leak as TP without checking whether the struct has a deinit/free companion function and whether it's guaranteed to run. Two of the six instances (`:717,750,761,777`) also have a same-function component that's simply wrong (the field claimed leaked was already freed 1-2 lines above in the same branch) — check both angles.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): DCL13-C splits a third way beyond the standing eloop-callback/vtable-dispatch vs. plain-internal-helper dichotomy — a plain *static* helper that IS switch-dispatched (never via a function-pointer table) can still be a genuine (if low-value) TP when the pointer param is only ever read.** `wpa_driver_privsep_event_auth`'s `buf` (`:390`) and `wpa_driver_privsep_event_assoc`'s `buf` (`:418`) are called directly from a `switch` in `wpa_driver_privsep_receive` (not through any function-pointer field), and both only read through `buf` (cast-and-copy-from, or offset-and-copy-from) — never write. Verified the assigned-out union field (`assoc_info.req_ies`) is itself declared `const u8 *`, so `const`-ing `buf` wouldn't break compilation. Contrast the same file's `deauthenticate`/`get_mac_addr` (vtable slots, `driver.h:3457,3582`) and `wpa_driver_privsep_receive` itself (bound as the `eloop_sock_handler` typedef, `eloop.h:43`) — genuinely fixed-signature and FP.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances, one file): EXP39-C "accessing union member X after writing member Y" cross-function conflation extends to a family of near-identical `wpa_driver_privsep_event_*` handlers that each declare their own local `union wpa_event_data data`, `os_memset(&data,0,...)`, then write exactly one member.** `:402,437,454,476,504` (`auth`/`assoc_info`/`interface_status`/`michael_mic_failure`/`ft_ies`) — the cited "earlier write to `freq`" doesn't exist in any of these functions; `freq` belongs to a different union member (`assoc_info.freq` or similar) written only in unrelated call sites elsewhere in the codebase. Same root cause as the previously-documented `driver.h:7333,7342` instance, now confirmed as a recurring shape specific to this file's per-event dispatch handlers, not a one-off.
- **NEW, batch-local: DCL15-C/DCL19-C "should be static" is a genuine TP for a driver's own `wpa_driver_*_ops` table when that driver's `.c` file is a build-time *substitute* for `drivers.c`, not a sibling compiled alongside it.** `wpa_driver_privsep_ops` (`:826`) — unlike every other `wpa_driver_*_ops` (nl80211/wext/bsd/macsec_linux, all confirmed FP because `drivers.c` references them by name and they're built together) this file defines its *own* `wpa_drivers[]` at `:846`, and `wpa_supplicant/Makefile:1982` shows `driver_privsep.o` is added to `OBJS` in place of `drivers.o` when `CONFIG_PRIVSEP` is set (see the `else` branch pulling in `drivers.o`) — `grep` confirms zero references to `wpa_driver_privsep_ops` anywhere outside this file. The companion `wpa_drivers[]` symbol on the very next flagged line (`:846`) stays FP as usual (declared `extern` in `driver.h:7389`, consumed by driver-selection code). Before defaulting to the standing "extern-linkage-needed" FP disposition for any `*_ops`/`wpa_drivers`-shaped DCL15/19 finding, verify with `grep` whether the specific symbol name is referenced outside its defining file — don't assume every driver module follows the drivers.c-registry pattern.
- **New FN (real, low-severity): resource leak on a malformed-datagram error path, not the mutually-exclusive-branch shape.** `wpa_driver_privsep_receive`'s "too short event message" branch (`res < (int) sizeof(int)`, `:546-549`) returns without `os_free(buf)`, while its sibling `res < 0` branch two lines above correctly frees it — a fresh 2000-byte `os_malloc()` leaked per short/malformed datagram on the AF_UNIX event socket. Closest rule MEM31-C/MEM01-C.

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (8 instances, one file `src/crypto/random.c`, batch `41plus_b207`): INT14-C "used with both bitwise and arithmetic operations" misattributes a masked-arithmetic composite `(var ± N) & mask` to whichever bare variable name appears inside the parens, even though that variable is never itself the direct operand of the `&`.** In `random_mix_pool`/`random_extract`, `pool_pos` (`:92,117`), the loop counter `i` (`:117`), the rotation amount `y` (`:74`, always accessed as `y & 31` before any `-`), and the `#define` offset constants `POOL_TAP1..5` (`:94-98`, not variables at all) are all flagged — but in every case the `&` applies to the *result* of a `+`/`-` on that name, not to the bare name directly. Distinguish from the genuinely-correct sibling in the same function: `input_rotate` (`:90-91`) IS bare-bitwise-ANDed (`input_rotate & 31`) in one statement and bare-arithmetic-`+=`'d in another, with no intervening mask — a real (if stylistic-only) dual direct use, graded TP(low). Same root family as the existing "bitwise op on dereference vs arithmetic op on the pointer itself" and "container-vs-member" INT14-C misattribution classes, now extended to a masked-composite-expression shape; watch for `(x op N) & mask` patterns elsewhere (common in ring-buffer/hash-mixing code).

Confirms the tool retroactively treats a free as applying to the line(s) immediately preceding it, independent of language backend (plain C list-management code, not just OpenSSL wrappers).
- **NEW, genuine TP counter-example in the same file, same rule: a real use-after-free via pointer-arithmetic-in-a-comparison, distinct from the ordering-confusion FP above.** `eth_get()` (FreeBSD/Apple-only `#if` block): `os_free(buf)` at `:898`, followed two lines later by `if (p >= buf + len)` at `:900` — `buf` is read (in address arithmetic feeding a comparison) *after* its one-and-only free, no reassignment or NULL-check in between. ### FN this batch

`dpp_pkex_finish()` (`:1342-1371`) leaks the entire `pkex` object (crypto keys `x`/`y`, `code`, `identifier`, `z`, wpabufs) when `dpp_bootstrap_key_hash(bi)` fails (`:1362-1365`): that branch frees only `bi` (`dpp_bootstrap_info_free(bi)`) and returns NULL, but never calls `dpp_pkex_free(pkex)` — unlike the success path just below, which does (`:1368`). All 3 call sites (`dpp_hostapd.c:2359,2392`, `dpp_supplicant.c:3352`) only `return`/bail on `!bi` without freeing their `pkex`/`hapd->dpp_pkex`/`wpa_s->dpp_pkex` either, so the leak isn't caught by the caller. Closest rule MEM31-C/MEM01-C. Low real-world trigger rate (`dpp_bootstrap_key_hash` failure is a rare crypto-hash error, not attacker-controlled on the common path), medium confidence. `upstream_present: unknown` (no separate upstream tracking checkout available to confirm against pinned commit `dcee60436`).

Secondary, lower-confidence: `dpp_pkex_build_exchange_req()`'s `pkex->enc_key = wpabuf_alloc_copy(Mx, 2 * curve->prime_len)` (`:149`) is never NULL-checked (unlike every other allocation in this file, which either goes through `goto fail` on failure or is checked before use) — if it fails, `pkex->enc_key` silently stays NULL, deferred to whatever later code reads it (retransmission path, not in this file). Not an immediate deref, so graded low confidence.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b215`, 83 findings, `src/ap/ieee802_11_shared.c`, 2026-08-07)

No new categorical classes — this file is almost entirely a straight reconfirmation of existing classes at high density, useful as a clean second oracle for the `eid`/`pos` IE-builder family:

- **DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable" — 18/18 instances FP,** all `hostapd_eid_*` IE builders (`u8 * hostapd_eid_X(struct hostapd_data *hapd, u8 *eid, ...)` returning either the `eid` parameter itself on an early-return, or `pos` after `pos = eid;` and in-place advancement). Every single flagged line traces back to the `eid` parameter alias, never real local/automatic storage — the strongest, most uniform instance of this pattern seen yet in one file.
- **API00-C "does not validate pointer/integer parameter" — 30/31 instances FP** (internal-only-API class: `hapd`/`eid`/`sta`/`addr`/`trans_id`/`ext_capab_ie` all caller-guaranteed valid from a small internal call-site set), plus one integer-overflow variant (`ap_copy_sta_supp_op_classes`'s `supp_op_classes_len`, `:965`) also FP — the length is a u8-bounded (<=255) wire IE length, can't overflow `1+len` in the subsequent `os_malloc`.
- **DCL13-C "pointer param should be const" splits cleanly along the brief's predicted line: 13/16 instances graded genuine (low-value) TP** — every `hostapd_eid_*`/`get_tx_parameters`/`hostapd_wfa_gen_capab` function here is a plain internal helper (not a dispatch-callback/vtable), and `hapd`/`sta` really are read-only in each — **vs. 2 instances that are a factually-wrong "not modified" miss**, where `eid` IS mutated through its own `pos = eid;` alias (`hostapd_eid_adv_proto:600`, `hostapd_eid_rsnxe:1114`), extending the standing write-through-alias-miss class from `ieee802_11.c`/`ieee802_11_eht.c` to this file.
- **MSC37-C "may reach end without returning" — both instances FP,** the standing preprocessor-branch-blind class: `hostapd_eid_owe_trans_len`/`hostapd_eid_owe_trans` each have an explicit `return` on both sides of `#ifdef CONFIG_OWE ... #else ... #endif`.
- **EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-dereference extended to the `X = os_zalloc(sizeof(*X) + n)` allocation-sizing idiom** (`mgmt:114`, `resp:209`) — same non-evaluated-context misfire as the established `os_zalloc(sizeof(*X))` shape, just with an added length term.
- **MSC07-C "unreachable code after break" — new, simpler sub-shape:** the "unreachable" code sqc flags is literally the next `case N:` label (`:406`) — not code after the break at all, just the switch's own next branch. Extends the existing goto/switch-label-blindness family with the plainest possible instance (label immediately following a `break;`, no intervening statements).
- Also reconfirmed at instance-count-1 each (not detailed further): FLP03-C integer-division misclassified as floating point (`:45`); EXP30-C pure-accessor/macro-arg class (`MAC2STR:268`, `wpabuf_head/len:678`); ARR36-C same-buffer-cast-overlay (`mgmt` vs `mgmt->u.action...variable:286`) and the pos/end-paired-bounds-parameter idiom (`hostapd_wfa_capab:1303,1306,1312`); EXP05-C read-only cast-away-const overlay, used only for pointer arithmetic (`(u8*)mgmt:286`); MSC01-C no-default guard-clause pedantry, unmatched `idx` intentionally leaves `*pos` at its already-set `0x00` (`:370`); INT32-C `abs()`-overflow misfire on values providably bounded to a `u8` range (`vht_op_info_chan_center_freq_seg{0,1}_idx:1073`); ARR30-C "unbounded" while-loop misfire on a loop that terminates via `capab` shrinking to 0, iteration count pre-validated against buffer space (`:1190`); MSC13-C genuine dead-initial-assignment TP (`other_hapd = NULL:1228`, never read before being overwritten); EXP34-C internal-invariant-non-null FP extended to an MLD link-lookup helper's own `sta`/`hapd` params (`hostapd_ml_get_assoc_sta:1237`).
- FN read-through: no missed bugs found. All IE-builder writes are bounded by config-derived (not attacker-controlled) lengths; the one attacker-facing parser (`ieee802_11_sa_query_action`) validates frame length against the fixed sa_query header before any full-width dereference of `trans_id`, and `check_ext_capab`/`hostapd_wfa_capab` gate every indexed read on the paired length param. `files_clean_for_fn: ["src/ap/ieee802_11_shared.c"]`.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b222`, 79 findings, `src/eap_peer/tncc.c`, entire file, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, real FN found via full read-through: off-by-one bounds bug in `tncc_read_config`'s line-splitting loop (POSIX/`os_readfile` path), missed entirely by sqc.** `os_readfile()` mallocs exactly `config_len` bytes with no NUL terminator. The scan `while (*line_end != '\n' && *line_end != '\r' && line_end < end) line_end++;` (`:1086-1088`) checks the bounds condition *last* in the `&&` chain, so it dereferences `*line_end` one iteration too late — a 1-byte OOB read at `config[config_len]` when the final config line has no trailing newline/CR. The following `*line_end = '\0';` (`:1089`) then writes that same OOB byte. Closest rules ARR38-C (OOB read via wrong loop-guard order) / ARR30-C (OOB write). Low real-world severity (local TNC config file, `#ifdef EAP_TNC` optional feature), medium confidence. `upstream_present: unknown`.
- **Reconfirms/extends the mutually-exclusive-branch MEM31-C double-free FP family (already CONFIRMED, see `:664,2563`) to a *4-way* branch shape within one loop iteration.** `tncc_read_config_reg`'s `val` (Windows-only IMC registry parsing) has `os_free(val)` on 4 disjoint continue/break paths (`:945,961,967,977`) — RegQueryValueEx failure / too-many-IMCs / `os_zalloc` failure / normal success-after-`os_strdup`. sqc flags 3 of the 4 as re-freeing an already-freed `val`; each is reached on its own exclusive branch of the same iteration, never more than once.
- **Reconfirms the ARR36-C/ARR00-C "message cites variable names that don't match the flagged line's actual identifiers" tool bug (previously 3x-confirmed on ARR36-C alone, see top-of-file `eap_sim_common.c` entry) — extends the mismatch to ARR00-C too.** `tncc_process_if_tnccs`'s `xmlend - xml` pointer subtraction (`:853`, both from `os_strstr()` on the same `buf`) is reported as subtracting `'xmlend' from 'pos2' and 'xml' from 'pos'` — code at that line has no `pos`/`pos2` at all. Separately, `tncc_read_config`'s `ARR36-C` at `:1087` cites `'pos'`/`'config'` while the actual comparison on that line is `line_end < end`.
- **NEW: DCL30-C "local variable assigned through pointer parameter, address will be invalid on return" misfires on a plain char VALUE store, not an address store.** `tncc_get_recommendation`'s `*pos2 = saved;` (`:679`, `saved` is a `char`) is reported as if the *address* of `saved` were being written through `pos2` — it's an ordinary character copy, no pointer/address involved at all. ## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b217`, 83 findings, `src/eap_server/eap_server.c`, entire file, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED: DCL13-C "getter returns a mutable pointer into the very
  struct the flagged param would be made const" — a genuine FP distinct from
  the read-only-plain-helper TP class.** `eap_get_interface(struct eap_sm *sm)`
  (`:2052`) never writes `sm` itself and just `return &sm->eap_if;`, so DCL13-C
  suggests `const`. But every real caller (`eapol_auth_sm.c:853`,
  `radius_server.c:634`, `eap_example_server.c:234`) stores that returned
  pointer and repeatedly *writes through it*
  (`sm->eap_if->eapRestart = true;`, `state->eap_if->retransWhile--;` in
  `eapol_auth_sm.c`) to drive the state machine — the entire point of the
  accessor is to hand out a mutable window into `sm`. Making `sm` const would
  force the return type to `const struct eap_eapol_interface *`, breaking
  every one of those call sites. Contrast with the plain read-only getters in
  this same file (`eap_get_identity`/`eap_get_serial_num`/`eap_get_method`/
  `eap_get_imsi`/`eap_sm_method_pending`, all graded genuine low-value TP)
  which return by-value or `const`-qualified data and have no such
  write-through contract. Watch for this shape elsewhere: a getter is FP for
  DCL13-C specifically when its return value is later mutated by the caller,
  not merely when the function body itself looks unmodifying.
- **Reconfirms/extends across-file the exact `41plus_b166`-family "guard
  clause N statements earlier" ARR00-C/ARR30-C/INT30-C bound-blindness class,
  now on the EAP *server*-side twin of that peer-side ERP re-auth code.**
  `eap_server.c`'s `SM_STATE(EAP, INITIATE_RECEIVED)` is structurally
  identical to `eap.c`'s `eap_peer_finish` already documented above: `nai[
  parse.keyname_len] = '\0'` (`:862`) guarded by `if (keyname_len > 253)
  goto fail;` 6 lines earlier; `end[-33]`/`end[-17]` (ARR00-C, `:908,916,941,
  953`) and `end - hdr - hash_len`/`end - hash_len` (INT30-C, `:930,932`) all
  proven safe by the `max_len < 1 + hash_len) ... goto fail;` check ~10 lines
  earlier (which establishes `end - start >= 17` or `>= 33` depending on
  cryptosuite). All FP — same interprocedural/long-range blind spot, now
  confirmed present on both the peer and server EAP-ERP implementations.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED, genuine serious TP: INT30-C unsigned underflow on
  `len -= sizeof(*nak)` with NO preceding "len >= sizeof(*nak)" check
  (`SM_STATE(EAP, NAK)`, `:620`).** `len` is set from the attacker-controlled
  `nak->length` wire field, only clamped to *not exceed* `wpabuf_len()` —
  never clamped to be *at least* `sizeof(*nak)`. A short (or zero) Nak length
  underflows `len` to a huge `size_t`, which then flows unchecked into
  `wpa_hexdump(..., nak_list, len)` and a `for (j=0;j<len;j++) nak_list[j]`
  scan inside `eap_sm_process_nak()` — a real out-of-bounds read on
  attacker-supplied EAP-Response/Nak data. Distinguish this from the
  adjacent, textually-similar-looking `end[-N]`/`end-hdr-hash_len` findings in
  the SAME file (`:908-953`), which ARE all FP per the guard-clause-exists
  pattern above — this one has no such guard anywhere in the function.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: ARR00-C/ARR01-C correctly catch `sizeof()` applied
  directly to a decayed pointer PARAMETER (not `sizeof(*ptr)`/
  `sizeof(ptr->member)`), a genuine (if low-severity/debug-only) TP.**
  `eap_server_mschap_rx_callback`'s `wpa_snprintf_hex_sep(hex_challenge,
  sizeof(hex_challenge), challenge, sizeof(challenge), ':')` (`:2086`) computes
  `sizeof(challenge)` where `challenge` is `const u8 *challenge` — sizeof of a
  pointer (4 or 8), not the actual challenge length. On 64-bit builds this
  happens to coincide with the real 8-byte MS-CHAP challenge length by
  coincidence, but is wrong (dumps only 4 bytes) on 32-bit builds.
  `CONFIG_TESTING_OPTIONS`-only debug helper, so low real-world severity, but
  a genuine class-of-bug hit, not a false positive — contrast sharply with
  the `sizeof(sm->user->methods[0])` FP three lines of context away in the
  same file (`:1632,1660,1669`), which sizes a real struct member and is
  correctly-idiomatic.
- **Reconfirms/extends in this batch (not detailed above):** the EXP33-C
  `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-dereference class at very high density (7 instances:

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b228`, 75 findings, `src/common/wpa_helpers.c`, entire file, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW verification technique: sibling-function guard contrast confirms a genuine ARR30-C off-by-one, rather than defaulting to the usual ARR30-C-is-FP prior.** `wpa_ctrl_request()`'s primary return path (`wpa_ctrl.c:580`, `*reply_len = res; break;`) can set the output length equal to the caller's full input buffer capacity when a `SOCK_DGRAM` reply exactly fills (or exceeds and gets truncated to) the buffer — there is no reservation of 1 byte for a NUL. `get_wpa_cli_event2` (`wpa_helpers.c:136-138`) explicitly guards this exact hazard (`if (len == buf_size) len--;` before `buf[len]='\0'`), proving the hazard is real and known to the codebase's own authors — but `wpa_command` (`:52`, `buf[128]`) and `get_wpa_status` (`:181`, `buf[4096]`) skip that guard and null-terminate at `buf[len]` unconditionally, a genuine 1-byte OOB write when the response exactly fills the buffer. Graded TP (med confidence — reachable only when wpa_supplicant's reply is >= buffer size, plausible for `STATUS` with many networks). The identical unguarded shape recurs in `wpa_command_resp` (`:78`, `resp[len]='\0'`) but sqc did NOT flag it there — logged as an FN; same root cause missed at a 3rd call site (also reached transitively via `add_network`/`add_cred`). **Takeaway: before defaulting an ARR30-C `buf[len]='\0'` finding to the usual FP bucket, check whether a sibling function in the same file guards the identical shape — an inconsistently-applied guard is strong evidence of a real bug, not a heuristic.**

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b229`, 75 findings, `src/utils/common.h`, entire file, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (12 instances): DCL37-C on `__BYTE_ORDER`/`__LITTLE_ENDIAN`/`__BIG_ENDIAN` is FP — extends the `_LINUX_TYPES_H`-mirroring exception to userspace portability macros.** On BSD/macOS (`:23-25,41-43`) these are `#define __BYTE_ORDER _BYTE_ORDER` etc., literally aliasing to the platform's own `<sys/endian.h>`/`<machine/endian.h>` names so portable code can use glibc's naming convention; the rtems block (`:58-60`) does the same against `<rtems/endian.h>`. The final fallback (`:165,166,168`, guarded by `#ifndef __BYTE_ORDER` etc.) only fires when no header defined them at all, providing the exact same names glibc's own `<endian.h>` would — not an independently-invented reserved name, same reasoning as `_LINUX_NL80211_H`/`_LINUX_TYPES_H`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (1 instance, refines the `__must_check` TP precedent): DCL37-C on `__func__` (`:422`) is FP, distinct from the self-authored-convention TP class.** This is a fallback `#define __func__ "..."` for compilers predating C99, i.e. providing the exact standard-mandated predefined-identifier name so downstream `__func__` usage stays transparent — mirrors the C *language standard* itself, not an arbitrary convention hostap invented (contrast: `__must_check`/`__force`/`__bitwise`/`__maybe_unused`, same file `:477-505`, stay TP — those are self-chosen sparse/kernel-style annotation names with no standard or vendored-header obligation to use that exact spelling).
- **Reconfirms at very high density (23 instances, not re-detailed above): API05-C ptr+size_t idiom / API02-C false "missing size param" extended to signatures that verbatim-mirror an external standard's API — `snprintf`/`vsnprintf` (`:397,400`, C99/POSIX prototypes), `getopt` (`:404`, POSIX `char *const argv[]` — also drew the matching ARR02-C "implicit bounds" FP, same reasoning), and `str_token` (`:614`, mirrors `strtok_r`'s `str`+opaque `char **context` shape).** Plus the plain ptr+size_t idiom at usual volume across `hexstr2bin`/`wpa_snprintf_hex*`/`hwaddr_mask_txt`/`printf_encode`/`printf_decode`/`dup_binstr`/`bin_clear_free`/`utf8_escape`/`utf8_unescape` (15 instances: `:522,528,530,531,534,545,546,557,608,615,616,617,618,638`, plus the `wpa_config_parse_string` `len` out-param single-scalar-pointer misread as an array, `:550`).
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances): API02-C "missing size_t param" false positive extends the NUL-terminated-string idiom to a 0-*sentinel*-terminated `int` array convention.** `int_array_len`/`_concat`/`_sort_unique`/`_equal`/`_dup` (`:597,598,599,602,603`) and `str_clear_free` (`:607`, plain NUL-terminated string) all self-describe their bound via a terminator value rather than a separate size parameter (confirmed via `int_array_len`'s `for (i = 0; a && a[i]; i++)`, `common.c:882-888`) — same "self-terminating buffer needs no size param" reasoning as the established NUL-terminated-string class, just extended past `char*`.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): PRE00-C/PRE12-C "evaluates parameter multiple times" is FP when the parameter is only ever a `sizeof(...)` operand.** `#define ARRAY_SIZE(a) (sizeof(a) / sizeof((a)[0]))` (`:605`) references `a` twice in the *text*, but `sizeof`'s operand is never evaluated at runtime per the C standard — extends the already-documented `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-dereference EXP33-C reasoning to the macro-multiple-evaluation PRE-family.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (4 instances, 2 macros): PRE02-C/PRE10-C category error on for-loop-generator macros.** `for_each_link`/`for_each_link_default` (`:626,631`) each expand to a full `for (...) ... if (...)` control-flow statement, meant to be followed by a loop body exactly like a real `for` statement (`for_each_link(links, i) { ... }`) — PRE02-C's "parenthesize the whole replacement list" fix is invalid C (same category error as the `__AKM` if-statement precedent), and PRE10-C's "wrap in do-while" fix would break the macro's entire purpose (it must stay a bare control-flow construct, not a single opaque statement). By contrast, the paired PRE00-C/PRE12-C on the loop variable itself (`__i`/`_links`, same 2 lines) stays genuine (low-severity) TP — the variable really does appear multiple times in the expansion (init/cond/increment/if-guard), matching the established `MIN`/`MAX`/`bswap_16`/`bswap_32`/`MAC2STR` real-macro-hazard TP class (all 5 reconfirmed here too, `:426,430,447,466,469`).
- **NEW, batch-local: PRE01-C category error when the "unparenthesized parameter" is a type name, not a value operand.** `#define aliasing_hide_typecast(a,t) (t *) __hide_aliasing_typecast((a))` (`:650`) — `t` is substituted into a cast `(t *)`; it's a type-name argument, not an rvalue expression, so PRE01-C's "wrap in parens" fix doesn't apply (parenthesizing a type name inside a cast is invalid/meaningless). Distinct from the already-documented token-paste/case-label-only PRE01-C FP shapes (`C2S`/`R2S`/`S2S`, `x`/`r`/`s` — `41plus_b_C2S` entry) — this is a new "type parameter" sub-shape of the same "graded on how the parameter is actually used in the definition" principle. `a` in the same macro is a genuine value operand and was correctly not flagged.
- Reconfirms at volume (not re-detailed above): DCL37-C double-underscore reserved-identifier genuine TP, matching the `__must_check`-precedent self-authored-convention class — `__force`/`__bitwise` (sparse-checker attribute macros, 4 instances: `:477,479,481,483`) and `__must_check`/`__maybe_unused` (GCC-attribute-wrapper macros, 4 instances: `:495,497,503,505`; `__must_check:495` *is* the file/line this precedent was originally established on) — plus `__hide_aliasing_typecast` (`:649`, both the "starts with underscore" and "reserved identifier" DCL37-C findings on the same declaration), matching the cross-file precedent for this exact identifier.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b226`, 77 findings, `src/common/nan_de.c`, entire file, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED genuine TP: INT33-C mod-by-zero, wire-reachable, distinguishes from the file's own look-alike FP a few hundred lines away.** `nan_de.c` has two near-identical bloom-filter helpers built around `crc %= bf_len * 8;`. `nan_check_bloom_filter` (`:1313`, called from `nan_srf_match`) is **unguarded**: `nan_de_rx_sda`'s `NAN_SRV_CTRL_RESP_FILTER` branch (`:1417-1426`) reads an attacker-controlled 1-byte SRF length `flen` straight off the wire with no lower bound, and `nan_srf_match` immediately does `srf_ctrl = *srf++; srf_len--;` — if the received frame sets `flen == 1` (and sets the `NAN_SRF_CTRL_BF` bit in that single byte), `srf_len` becomes 0 and reaches `nan_check_bloom_filter` as `bf_len == 0`, hitting the unguarded modulo. Real, remotely-triggerable DoS from a malicious NAN SDF. By contrast `bloom_filter_add` (`:1815`, called from `nan_build_bloom_filter`) IS safe — its only call site (`nan_de_subscribe`) gates the call behind `if (params->srf_bf_len) { ... }`, so `bf_len` can never be 0 there. **Lesson: don't pattern-match "div/mod by a parameter without an in-function zero-check" to a blanket verdict — check each call site's guard independently even when two functions look like near-duplicates of the same algorithm.**
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances): DCL13-C "not modified" is a genuine miss when the mutation is a single `os_memcpy`/similar write through a struct field, easy to eyeball-miss.** `nan_de_update_nmi`'s `de` (`:900`, `os_memcpy(de->nmi, nmi, ETH_ALEN)`) and `nan_de_derive_service_id`'s `srv` (`:1573`, `os_memcpy(srv->service_id, hash, NAN_SERVICE_ID_LEN)` at the very end of the function, easy to miss because it's conditional on `if (ret == 0)`). Extends the established "misses a mutation through an aliased field pointer" sub-shape (previously via a local alias variable) to the simpler case of a direct one-line `os_memcpy` into a struct field with no intermediate alias at all.
- **NEW, batch-local: DCL13-C splits cleanly by density in this file — 15 plain-internal-object-handle params (`de`/`srv`) genuinely never modified (`:167,266,533,636,676,1018,1049,1273,1322,1601,1755,1779,2059`, graded TP-low, consistent with the standing plain-internal-helper convention) vs. exactly 1 eloop-timeout-handler dispatch-contract FP (`nan_de_timer`'s `timeout_ctx`, `:696`) vs. the 2 genuine misses above.**

- **NEW, batch-local (2 findings, 1 root cause): ARR00-C "use-after-free" + MEM31-C "double free" misfire when two sibling (non-else, not mutually exclusive by construction) `if` blocks in the same function each declare their own same-named local pointer, and the tracker conflates the two distinct variables/allocations as one.** `ieee802_11_rx_wnm_notif_req_wfa`'s HS20_WNM_DEAUTH_IMMINENT_NOTICE branch (`:1874-1905`) declares `char *url;`, mallocs, uses, and frees its own `url` (`:1879,1895,1902`); the sibling HS20_WNM_T_C_ACCEPTANCE branch (`:1907-1931`) declares an entirely separate `char *url;` in its own block scope (`:1912`), mallocs/uses/frees independently (`:1922,1928`). sqc flags the second block's `url[url_len]='\0'` (`:1926`) as accessing memory already freed by the *first* block's `os_free(url)` (`:1902`), and the second block's `os_free(url)` (`:1928`) as a double-free of that same first-block object — but these are two different `char *` objects with disjoint lifetimes that happen to share a variable name across sibling block scopes. - **NEW, batch-local (1 instance): ARR00-C "loop uses uninitialized variable as bound" misfires on a plain function *parameter* (`int num_hw_features`), which always carries a caller-supplied, fully-determinate value — not "indeterminate" in the sense the rule claims (unlike a genuinely-uninitialized automatic local).** `hw_get_channel_freq:75`. Distinct from the existing "initialized in its own for-loop init-clause" ARR00-C FP family — this is a parameter, no local declaration/init-clause is even involved.
- **NEW, batch-local (1 instance, graded TP not FP): MSC01-C "if/else-if chain has no final else" on `hostapd_set_freq_params`'s `center_segment0` auto-derivation chain (`hw_features_common.c:731-745`) is a genuine (if narrow) correctness gap, not pedantry.** If `channel > 177` (the chain's last arm), `center_segment0` silently stays at its incoming value (0, since the block is only entered when `!center_segment0`), and the immediately-following `data->center_freq1 = 5000 + center_segment0 * 5;` (unconditional, outside the chain) computes a bogus 5000 MHz center frequency instead of erroring out — unlike the file's other 3 MSC01-C instances (`:195,224,657`, all deliberate "leave the prior/zero value" fallbacks with no consumer misuse), this one's fallthrough value IS consumed downstream for a wrong result. Low-severity since standard 5 GHz 80 MHz VHT segments (36-177) are believed exhaustive in practice, but the code has no explicit range validation.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b262`, 114 findings, 2 files: `wpa_supplicant/dbus/dbus_new_handlers_wps.c` entire file, `wpa_supplicant/mesh_mpm.c` entire file, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED, dangerous class (5 instances, one file): MEM30-C "use-after-free"/"double-free" hallucinates a free on a pointer that is never freed anywhere in the function at all — likely misattributes `ap_free_sta(hapd, sta)`'s free (which frees its *second* argument, `sta`) to the function's *first* argument instead.** `mesh_mpm_action_rx`'s `hapd` (`:1356,1358` use-after-free, `:1370` double-free, `:1373,1375` use-after-free) — `hapd = wpa_s->ifmsh->bss[0]` is assigned once at function entry and never passed to any `os_free`/`ap_free_sta`/`wpabuf_free`-style call within this function; `plink_free_count(hapd)` (the actual call at those lines) only reads `hapd->max_plinks`/`hapd->num_plinks`, doesn't free anything. Grep-verified: no free of `hapd` exists in `mesh_mpm_action_rx`. This is a *critical*-severity false positive (name-based heuristic on `plink_free_count`'s "free" substring, or cross-function confusion with `ap_free_sta`'s real but differently-ordered free elsewhere in the file), not just a low-value nuisance — watch for `*_free_count`/`*_free_*`-named accessor functions (that don't actually free anything) triggering this elsewhere.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (7 instances, one file): ARR39-C "scaled integer assignment/arithmetic with pointer, results in double scaling" misfires on a plain `size_t` byte-count accumulator variable that is never a pointer at all — a cruder failure mode than the previously-confirmed pure-integer-sum-no-pointer misfire (`categorical_patterns.md` `41plus_b248`, `2*sizeof(*result)+sizeof(*cb)`).** `mesh_mpm_send_plink_action`'s `buf_len` (declared `size_t buf_len;`, `:249,254,256`×2,`271,385`×3,`419`) is a running byte-length total (`buf_len += 3 + HE_MAX_MAC_CAPAB_SIZE + ...`) later passed to `wpabuf_alloc(buf_len)` — never dereferenced, incremented via pointer arithmetic, or typed as a pointer anywhere in the function. Same root cause (rule triggers on any `+=`/`+` expression containing a `sizeof()` or size-macro term, regardless of the LHS/operand's actual type) as the b248 precedent, now confirmed at higher density and on a named accumulator rather than an inline expression.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances, one file): MEM05-C "variable-length array with runtime-sized allocation" misfires on fixed-size local arrays whose bound is a compile-time-constant *expression* (macro/`sizeof()` sum) — not merely a macro-constant VLA (already documented, `categorical_patterns.md`'s `41plus_b27`-adjacent "MEM05-C/ARR32-C VLA-on-macro-constant" entry, which was a genuine VLA syntax `char *argv[max_args]`), but arrays that aren't even syntactically variable-length at all.** `u8 supp_rates[2 + 2 + 32]` (`:217`), `u8 ht_capa_oper[2 + 26 + 2 + 22]` (`:368`), `u8 vht_capa_oper[2 + 12 + 2 + 5]` (`:376`), `u8 he_capa_oper[3 + HE_MAX_MAC_CAPAB_SIZE + ... + sizeof(struct ieee80211_he_6ghz_band_cap)]` (`:385`), `u8 eht_capa_oper[3 + 2 + EHT_PHY_CAPAB_LEN + ... + sizeof(struct ieee80211_eht_operation)]` (`:419`) — every operand (literal, `#define` macro, `sizeof(struct X)`) is resolvable at compile time; none is a variable. Rule appears to treat any array-size expression containing `+`/`sizeof()` as "runtime-sized" regardless of whether the operands are actually variables.
- **NEW: EXP00-C "use parentheses to clarify operator precedence" fires on an expression that is already parenthesized exactly as the suggestion recommends.** `info = (bss->num_plinks > 63 ? 63 : bss->num_plinks) << 1;` (`:314`) — the ternary is already wrapped in explicit parens before the `<<`; the finding's own suggested fix is a no-op restating the existing code.
- **NEW, batch-local (not yet 3x confirmed elsewhere): ARR30-C "unvalidated function parameter index" extends the exhaustive-enum-coverage FP concept (previously MSC01-C-only) to an array-index context — a fixed-range `enum` parameter used to index a same-sized designated-initializer array, with every actual call site passing a compile-time enum literal.** `wpa_mesh_set_plink_state`'s `state` (`enum mesh_plink_state`, values 1-7 per `src/common/defs.h:425-433`) indexing `mplstate[state]` (`:463`) — `mplstate[]` is designated-initialized `[0]`..`[PLINK_BLOCKED]` (8 slots, covering the full enum range), and grep-verified every call site in the codebase passes a fixed `PLINK_*` enum constant, never a raw/attacker-derived int. Watch for recurrence on other `enum`-parameter-indexes-matching-sized-table shapes.
- **Reconfirms/extends in this batch (not re-detailed above):** DCL15-C "should be static" FP extended cleanly to the sibling `dbus_new_handlers_wps.c` accessor family (`wpas_dbus_getter/setter_process_credentials/_config_methods/_wps_device_name/_wps_manufacturer/_wps_device_model_name/_wps_device_model_number/_wps_device_serial_number/_wps_device_device_type`, 16 instances) — same `DECLARE_ACCESSOR`/property-desc-table extern-linkage requirement as the `dbus_new_handlers.c` precedent (`41plus_b29`); DCL13-C `WPADBusPropertyAccessor` `user_data`/`error` dispatch-contract FP extended to the same accessor family (9 instances); API00-C internal-only-API FP extended to `iter`/`error` params of the same accessors (14 instances) and to `wpas_dbus_handler_wps_start`'s `message`/`wpa_s` (2 instances); DCL31-C libdbus-unresolved-header FP (`dbus_message_iter_init`/`_next`×2/`_new_method_return`/`dbus_set_error`, 5 instances); STR30-C rule-logic-bug on already-const `property`/`format` params (`wpa_dbus_mark_property_changed:395`, `dbus_set_error:759`, 2 instances); ## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b260`, 114 findings, `src/eap_peer/eap_tls.c` + `src/utils/edit_readline.c`, entire files, 2026-08-07)

- **Reconfirms at very high density (10 instances, one function): the "`free`-named-helper frees only a sub-field of `*ptr`, not `*ptr` itself" MEM30-C misattribution class (`41plus_b107`/`b119`/`sta_info.c` precedents), on a new callee shape.** `eap_tls_success()`'s `eap_tls_free_key(data)` (`eap_tls.c:184`) only frees/NULLs `data->key_data`, and `os_free(data->session_id)` (`:199`) only frees the `session_id` member — every later `data->...` access in the same function is flagged MEM30-C "use-after-free of `data`" (`:185,189,190,191,193,200,202,203,204,205`), even though `data` itself is never freed anywhere in the function.
- **Reconfirms the branch-blind MEM30-C/DCL30-C "free inside an if-block that unconditionally returns, vs. a `return priv` reached only on the other, non-freeing branch" mutually-exclusive-path class.** `eap_tls_init_for_reauth()`: `os_free(data); return NULL;` inside `if (eap_peer_tls_reauth_init(...))` (`:327-329`) is mutually exclusive with the `return priv;` two lines later (`:331`), which is only reached when the `if` was false (no free happened) — sqc's CFG conflates the two paths, flagging both DCL30-C and MEM30-C "returning freed pointer" at `:331`.
- **NEW, batch-local: MSC13-C "dead store, never read" misfires when the flagged variable's only subsequent use is as the sole argument to `free()`/`os_free()`.** `edit_readline.c`'s `h = remove_history(where_history());` (`:168`) is read at the `if (h)` guard and via `h->line`/`h->data` and finally passed to `free(h)` itself (`:169-172`) — genuinely read multiple times; sqc's dead-store tracker apparently doesn't count a bare `free(x)`/`os_free(x)` call as a read of `x`. Watch for recurrence on other `ptr = alloc_or_getter(); ...; free(ptr);` shapes where the only reads before the final `free()` might otherwise look "unused" to a naive tracker.
- **NEW, batch-local: EXP34-C "possible NULL pointer dereference" fires on a variable dereferenced only inside the body of the very `while ((x = getter()))` loop whose condition already proves it non-NULL.** `edit_deinit()`'s `while ((h = current_history()))` (`:163`) guards every `h->...` access inside the loop body (`:164`); flagged anyway (`:164`). Distinct from the standard `X == NULL || f(X)` short-circuit-guard EXP34-C FP family — this is a loop-condition-as-guard shape instead of an `if`/`||`.
- Reconfirms in this batch (not re-detailed above): EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref (`data:52,88` in `eap_tls.c`); DCL30-C heap-vs-automatic-storage confusion at high density (`data:78,104`, `resp:233,300`, `key:364,382`, `id:400`, all `os_zalloc`/`os_memdup`-backed, `eap_tls.c`); ARR02-C array-sized-by-own-initializer (`eap_tls13_context[]:157`); MSC01-C no-final-else guard-clause pedantry (`eap_tls.c:67`); EXP20-C misapplied to an exact-length RFC 9190 protocol check rather than a boolean test (`wpabuf_len(resp)==1:280`); EXP34-C `eap_get_config(sm)`-result-never-null pervasive class (`config:227`); DCL13-C EAP-method `struct eap_method` vtable dispatch-contract FP extended to `has_reauth_data`/`deinit_for_reauth`/`isKeyAvailable`/`getKey`/`get_emsk`/`getSessionId` (12 instances, `eap_tls.c:304,311,343,350,368,386`) vs. plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP on the non-vtable `eap_tls_failure`'s `sm`/`data` (`:131,132`); API05-C `T*,size_t*` companion-pair idiom (`eap_tls.c:335,350,368,386`); MEM31-C ownership-transfer-to-registration-API FP, `eap_peer_method_register()`'s docstring explicitly forbidding the caller from freeing (`eap:408,434`); API02-C misfire on a function-pointer *type* declaration mistaken for an array-needing-size function (`edit_cmd_cb:19`); no-pthread CON03-C/CON07-C FP at volume (`edit_completion_cb:21`, `pending_completions:24`, `len/pos/pending_completions:39,41,42`, `pos:79`); WIN04-C misfire on a POSIX-only file with zero Windows API usage (`:21`); DCL31-C function-pointer-variable-call misfire (established class) extended to `edit_completion_cb`/`edit_eof_cb`/`edit_cmd_cb`/`filter_cb` (4 instances: `:67,104,108,167`) plus the standing DCL31-C `<readline/readline.h>`/`<readline/history.h>` system-header class at very high volume (~24 instances); EXP33-C static-variable-implicitly-zero-initialized FP (`edit_cb_ctx:67,104,167`); STR00-C wrong-type-claim (`pos` is `static int`, not `char`: `:53,54`); STR34-C char-to-char plain assignment (`*pos='\0'`:84`) and a wrong-type-claim variant (`ps` is `const char *`, not a plain `char` being widened: `:131`); MEM10-C ad-hoc-NULL-check pedantry (`:103`); API00-C internal-only-API FP (`edit_init`'s `cmd_cb`/`eof_cb`/`completion_cb`, always fixed non-NULL at the 3 real call sites in `wpa_cli.c`/`hostapd_cli.c`/`wlantest_cli.c`: `:112`); STR30-C const-qualified-callee-param rule-logic-bug extended to `rl_set_prompt(const char *)` (`:150`); ARR30-C NUL-terminated-string-traversal FP (`trunc_nl`'s `pos:82`) and a mislocated instance citing the wrong line (`163`, the real bounded pointer walk is `p++` at `:166`).

### FN read-through note (`41plus_b260`)

Both files read in full; no missed bugs found. `eap_tls.c`: every `os_zalloc`/`os_memdup` is NULL-checked, `eap_tls_deinit`/`eap_tls_free_key` free every allocated field exactly once with no double-free or leak on any path, and the EAP-method registration/dealloc ownership contract is followed correctly. `edit_readline.c`: `pending_completions` array is freed before every reassignment and at deinit, `edit_deinit`'s history-filtering loop frees only entries actually removed via `remove_history()`, and there are no unclosed fds or unchecked lengths (this is local interactive-CLI input, not attacker-controlled wire data). Both files added to `files_clean_for_fn`.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b257`, 120 findings, `src/common/dpp_backup.c` + `wpa_supplicant/ibss_rsn.c`, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (13 instances): MEM31-C "not freed"/"memory leak" misfires wholesale on `struct wpabuf *` values whose *last* use is being passed into `asn1_encaps()` (or a chain ending there), because `asn1_encaps()` (`src/tls/asn1.c:637`) unconditionally calls `wpabuf_clear_free(buf)` on its input before returning a *new* wrapper buffer — the analyzer doesn't see ownership transfer/free-on-behalf-of-caller through this ASN.1-encapsulation helper.** `dpp_backup.c` instances: `buf:55`, `attr:98,108`, `key:179`, `pwri:318`, plus the same-shape "potential leak due to goto" sub-variant (`salt:290`, actually always freed at the `fail:` label regardless of which goto reaches it). Any DPP/ASN.1-builder function ending in `return asn1_encaps(x, ...);` or freeing `x` at a shared `fail:`/cleanup label should be checked against this before trusting a MEM31-C hit.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (5 instances): EXP43-C "same pointer for output and input" misfires on `dpp_hkdf_expand()`/`dpp_pbkdf2()` calls whose secret/output arguments are in fact distinct pointers — apparent root cause is the analyzer conflating two *same-named length variables* (e.g. both `secret_len` and `outlen` passed as `key_len`) with the pointers themselves being aliased.** `dpp_backup.c:281,287,1154` (`dpp_hkdf_expand(key_len, auth->bk, key_len, ..., key, key_len)`, `dpp_pbkdf2(hash_len, key, key_len, ..., kek, hash_len)`) — secret/password and output are always different local arrays or struct fields, never the same address.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (~20 instances, one file): ARR36-C "pointer comparison/subtraction between pointers from different arrays" + ARR00-C "pointer arithmetic past end of array" both fire wholesale in ASN.1 DER parsers where `hdr.payload`/`pos`/`next`/`end` are all derived from the *same* caller-supplied buffer via `asn1_get_next`/`asn1_get_sequence`/`asn1_get_alg_id` output params.** Direct extension of the already-confirmed `tncs_parse_imv` pattern (main list, `41plus_b245`) to `dpp_parse_recipient_infos`/`dpp_parse_encrypted_content_info`/`dpp_parse_enveloped_data`/`dpp_parse_one_asymmetric_key` (`dpp_backup.c:560-786` in dense clusters). Any ASN.1/TLV parser walking a single buffer via header-output-param helpers should get this same treatment by default.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: MSC37-C "may reach end without returning" misfires on the `out:`-label-immediately-followed-by-`return`/`fail:`-falls-through-via-`goto out;` idiom** — extends the already-documented `goto out:`-label-misdetected-as-fallthrough class (main list, `16-40_b17`-adjacent entries) to a case with *two* labels (`out:` then `fail:`) where `fail:`'s own code ends in `goto out;`. `dpp_build_enveloped_data`, `dpp_backup.c:450`.
- **Extends the vtable/dispatch-contract DCL13-C FP family (previously eloop timeouts + EAP method tables + sqlite3_exec callbacks) to two more fixed-signature struct-of-function-pointers types: `struct wpa_sm_ctx` (`src/rsn_supp/wpa.h`) and `struct wpa_auth_callbacks` (`src/ap/wpa_auth.h`).** Every `supp_*`/`auth_*` static callback implementation assigned into a `wpa_sm_ctx`/`wpa_auth_callbacks` struct literal in `ibss_rsn.c` (`supp_set_state/get_state/ether_send/alloc_eapol/get_beacon_ie/set_key/get_network_ctx/mlme_setprotection/cancel_auth_timeout/deauthenticate/reconnect`, `auth_logger/get_psk/send_eapol/set_key/for_each_sta`, `ibss_rsn_disconnect`) gets a DCL13-C "ctx not modified, should be const" FP purely because the vtable's function-pointer typedef pins `void *ctx` — 18 instances this batch (`:55,62,85,114,187,194,204,210,216,271,282,300,373,380`). Contrast with the same file's genuine plain-internal-helper TPs on non-vtable static functions (`ibss_rsn_get_peer/ibss_set_sta_authorized/ibss_rsn_auth_init_group/_init/_send_auth/_is_auth_started/_process_rx_eapol`, 9 instances, `:27,398,399,446,484,515,540,786`) and one genuine DCL13-C-miss-a-mutation FP (`ibss_rsn_set_psk`'s `ibss_rsn`, written via `os_memcpy(ibss_rsn->psk, psk, PMK_LEN)`, `:861`).

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b261`, 114 findings, `src/utils/eloop_win.c` + `src/wps/http_client.c`, entire files, 2026-08-07)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (3 instances, one file): STR30-C/STR34-C/ARR36-C "modifies/compares against string literal" is control-flow-blind when a local pointer variable is set to a string literal in one branch (`path = "/";`) and separately set to a heap/strchr-derived pointer in a sibling branch, then only ever dereferenced/compared inside the *other* branch.** `http_client.c`'s `http_client_url_parse`: `path = os_strchr(addr, '/')` when non-NULL takes the `else` branch, which does `*path = '\0'` (`:204`) and later (guarded by `if (*path=='\0')`) `*path = '/'` (`:227`) and compares `port > path` (`:205`) — none of these lines are reachable when `path` holds the string-literal `"/"` (that only happens in the sibling `if (path==NULL)` branch, which never re-enters the `else` code). The analyzer conflates the two branches' possible values for the same variable name instead of tracking which branch it's actually in. Extends the general "confused-value-across-branches" class beyond the previously-documented EXP34-C/DCL11-C correlated-conditional-assignment blind spot to STR30/STR34/ARR36 specifically on a string-literal-vs-pointer branch split.
