## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `41plus_b274`, 99 findings, `src/l2_packet/l2_packet_privsep.c` + `src/ap/ieee802_11_he.c`, both entire files, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (7 instances, one file): DCL30-C "returns pointer to local variable with automatic storage duration" fires on `return eid;` / `return pos;` where `pos` was assigned `pos = eid;` at declaration/top-of-function — but `eid` is the function's own `u8 *eid` PARAMETER (the caller-owned output buffer), not a local array or any object with automatic storage at all. The rule appears to conflate "a local pointer *variable*" with "an object with automatic storage duration"; here the pointer variable merely aliases a parameter. `src/ap/ieee802_11_he.c:102,153,165,275,306,317,353` (`hostapd_eid_he_capab`/`_he_operation`/`_he_mu_edca_parameter_set`/`_spatial_reuse`, every `u8 *eid_or_pos_builder(...)` in the file). Distinct from the previously-documented heap-vs-automatic-storage-confusion DCL30-C class (which is about `os_malloc`/`os_zalloc` returns) — this is a parameter-aliasing sub-shape. Also produces companion FPs: DCL13-C "eid not modified, should be const" misfires the same way (the local `pos = eid;` IS written through via `*pos++ = ...`, so constifying `eid` would break the aliasing assignment) at every one of these same call sites (`:91,157,279,310,357`), and EXP33-C "dereference of uninitialized pointer" on `sizeof(*edca)`/`sizeof(*cap)` (`:286,386`) where the pointer is declared but not yet assigned — `sizeof` never evaluates/dereferences its operand.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED (2 instances, one file): ARR37-C "pointer arithmetic on struct member is undefined behavior" misidentifies a plain LOCAL pointer *variable* (never declared inside any struct, never accessed via `->`) merely because it was *initialized* from a struct member's address.** `epos` (`ieee802_11_he.c:99,125`, a bare `u8 *epos;` local, initialized `epos = (u8 *) &cap->he_basic_supported_mcs_set;` then walked with `epos += mcs_nss_size`) and `sta_mcs_set` (`:419,450`, a bare `const u8 *sta_mcs_set;` local similarly initialized from `&(...)->he_basic_supported_mcs_set`, then subscripted `sta_mcs_set[i*4]`). Neither variable is itself a struct member; both are ordinary local pointers, so subsequent pointer arithmetic/subscripting on them is completely well-defined.
- **NEW, CONFIRMED: INT13-C "bitwise operator used on signed operand" misapplied to the shift-COUNT (right) operand of `>>` instead of the shifted (left) VALUE operand.** `check_valid_he_mcs`'s loop variable `j` (`ieee802_11_he.c:455,458`, `(ap_tx_mcs_set >> (j * 2))` / `(sta_rx_mcs_set >> (j * 2))`) is only ever the shift amount; the values actually being shifted (`ap_tx_mcs_set`, `sta_rx_mcs_set`) are already unsigned `u16`. A signed shift-count is unremarkable C as long as it's non-negative and in range (guaranteed here by the bounding `for` loop). Same root confusion produces the companion INT14-C "used with both bitwise and arithmetic operations" FP on the same `j` (`:455`) and on `ppe_thres_hdr` elsewhere in the file (`:32`, where the arithmetic is on the *result* of `ppe_thres_hdr & MASK`, not on `ppe_thres_hdr` itself) — and, separately, INT14-C fired directly on a `#define` macro CONSTANT (`HE_PPE_THRES_NSS_MASK`, `:43`) as if it were a variable at all.
- **Extends the DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP class (previously: eloop timeout/socket handlers, `struct eap_method`/`wpa_auth_callbacks` vtables, `sqlite3_exec()` callbacks, and the `tls_none.c` multi-backend-stub precedent from `41plus_b231`) to `src/l2_packet/l2_packet.h`'s public multi-backend interface.** `l2_packet_privsep.c` is one of 7+ parallel backend implementations (`l2_packet_linux.c`, `_freebsd.c`, `_pcap.c`, `_ndis.c`, `_none.c`, `_winpcap.c`) of the exact same header-declared signatures; `l2` (and `buf` in the `l2_packet_get_ip_addr` stub) is unmodified only because *this particular backend* is a thin privsep-IPC forwarder/stub, not because the interface itself has no legitimate use for a non-const param (the Linux/FreeBSD/pcap backends genuinely read/write through these). `l2_packet_privsep.c:55,94(x2 — eloop_sock_handler typedef),267,280`.
- **CONFIRMS the FN-brief's precondition-ordering class (EAP/RADIUS-style wire-length validated too late), now on 802.11 management-frame IE parsing rather than EAP/RADIUS: `copy_sta_he_capab()` (`ieee802_11_he.c:472-500`) calls `check_valid_he_mcs(hapd, he_capab, opmode)` — which reads `sta_mcs_set[i*4]` at a fixed offset with NO length parameter at all (`:450-452`) — BEFORE `ieee80211_invalid_he_cap_size(he_capab, he_capab_len)` validates that the peer-supplied buffer is actually that long.** `he_capab`/`he_capab_len` come straight from the STA's wire HE-Capabilities IE (`elems->he_capabilities[_len]`, `ieee802_11.c:5463-5555`), so a truncated/malformed IE (as short as the 17-byte mac+phy-capab minimum, omitting the MCS-set field entirely) drives an out-of-bounds read past the actual IE buffer. Reported as an FN (closest rule ARR30-C); sqc did not flag it.
- No other missed bugs found in either file beyond the one FN above; `l2_packet_privsep.c`'s alloc/free and fd open/close pairs on every error path are correctly balanced (matching the existing MEM12-C "false leak already freed earlier" FP class at `:171,222,231`), *except* for the one real, silent (non-memory-safety) data-corruption bug in `l2_packet_send()` reported as a second FN: `io[1].iov_base = &dst_addr;` (`:71`) takes the address of the local `const u8 *dst_addr` PARAMETER itself instead of `(u8 *) dst_addr` (the actual MAC-address bytes it points to, correctly done for `buf` two lines below at `:75`) — sends 6 bytes of the pointer's own stack representation to the `wpa_priv` privileged helper as the destination address in `CONFIG_PRIVSEP` builds.

- Reconfirms in this batch (not re-detailed above): API00-C internal-only-API FP at high density (crypto primitives `sha1_vector`/`crypto_dh_init`/`crypto_dh_derive_secret`/`crypto_mod_exp`/`des_key_setup`/`des_block_encrypt`/`des_block_decrypt`/`des3_encrypt`, 15 instances, all called only by fixed internal wrappers with protocol-fixed buffer/key sizes); the INT14-C "stylistic-pedantry mismatch with real CERT intent" class reconfirmed on classic bit-permutation/parity code (5 instances: `crypto_gnutls.c:58`, `des-internal.c:280,282,287,409`); CON07-C no-pthread misfire, doubly wrong since the named `SP1..SP8` are also `static const` (never mutated at all) (`:318`); ### FN read-through note (`41plus_b276`)

Read both full files. Every payload/length parse in `eap_eke_process_*`/`eap_pwd_process_*` bounds-checks before reading (`pos + N > end` / `payloadlen < N` guards precede every fixed-field read); every `os_zalloc`/`os_malloc`/`os_memdup`/`wpabuf_alloc` call is NULL-checked with a clean fallback; `data->msgs`/`data->outbuf`/`data->inbuf` are freed on every reachable path (immediately, at the next `wpabuf_free`/reassignment, or deferred to `eap_eke_reset()`/`eap_pwd_reset()`). One narrow, low-severity edge case noted but not filed as a separate FN: `eap_pwd_process`'s fragment-reassembly path allocates `data->inbuf` when the Length bit is set (`:920`) but only frees/consumes it later when `data->in_frag_pos` is nonzero; a peer that sets the L bit without the M bit on a single (non-fragmented) message would leave `data->inbuf` allocated and unused until the next call or `eap_pwd_reset()` — same deferred-cleanup-via-reset() class as the MEM31-C FPs above, not an unbounded leak. Both files marked clean for FN purposes beyond that.

Watch for the same shape (call site of a multi-line-signature forward-declared `static` function) elsewhere.

### FN read-through note (`41plus_b286`)

`dfs.c`: no allocations in the file at all (pure channel-selection/state-machine logic over driver-owned arrays); reviewed all branches, no leak/UB class bugs found — clean for FN purposes.

`eap_mschapv2.c`: every `os_malloc`/`os_zalloc`/`eap_msg_alloc`/`wpabuf_alloc`/`os_memdup` is NULL-checked with a clean-teardown path (including all `goto fail` branches in `eap_mschapv2_change_password`), and `eap_peer_mschapv2_register`'s allocation is consumed correctly by its registration API — otherwise clean. One real FN filed: `eap_mschapv2_failure_txt`'s `C=` field parser (`:440`) computes `hex_len = os_strchr(pos, ' ') - (char *) pos;` with no NULL check on the `os_strchr()` result. If an EAP-MSCHAPv2 Failure message's `C=<hex>` field is the last token with no trailing space (attacker/rogue-AP-controlled wire data, RFC 2759 failure-request text), `os_strchr` returns NULL and the subtraction is pointer arithmetic on a NULL pointer — undefined behavior (closest CERT rule: ARR36-C, "do not subtract or compare two pointers that do not refer to the same array"). Low real-world severity (the resulting garbage `hex_len` almost never equals `PASSWD_CHANGE_CHAL_LEN * 2`, so it just falls through to the "invalid failure challenge len" log branch), but it is a genuine UB path sqc did not flag. `upstream_present: "unknown"` — no separate tracking checkout of the pinned `dcee60436` clone was available to confirm/refute against a newer upstream fix.

### FN read-through note (`41plus_b285`)

`tlsv1_cred.c`: one real (low-severity) logic FN — `search_tag()`'s loop bound `for (i = 0; i < len - plen; i++)` (`:98`) is off-by-one; it should be `i <= len - plen` to also test the last legal offset. As written, a tag occupying exactly the final `plen` bytes of the searched range (or a `len == plen` exact match) is never found. Used by every PEM boundary search in this file (certificate/key/DH-params BEGIN/END tags); closest CERT rule MSC22-C ("Avoid off-by-one errors when indexing an array"). Practical impact is low since real PEM buffers normally have trailing bytes after the END marker. `upstream_present: "unknown"`. `wpa_ft.c` had no FNs on full read-through.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `16-40_b33`, 117 findings, `src/ap/vlan_init.c` + `src/common/ptksa_cache.c` + `src/drivers/driver_nl80211.h` + `src/fst/fst_iface.h` + `src/utils/ext_password_file.c` + `src/ap/ap_list.c` + `src/ap/ctrl_iface_ap.h`, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW: DCL13-C on a `#ifdef CONFIG_X ... #else` stub-pair — refines the existing "genuinely-unused-in-both-branches" rule to be per-function, not per-file.** `ptksa_cache.c`'s `#else /* CONFIG_PTKSA_CACHE */` block provides empty-body stand-ins for `ptksa_cache_deinit/get/list/add/flush`, all sharing the primary (`#ifdef`) implementations' exact signatures. Verdict must be decided per function by checking whether the *primary* implementation mutates that specific param (writes through it, reassigns a field, or passes it to a call like `free()`/`os_free()` that requires non-const) — if so, FP (the stub's own emptiness doesn't matter, constifying would break the primary); if the primary implementation is genuinely read-only for that param too, TP (low value). Concretely: `ptksa` FP on `deinit`/`add`/`flush` (primary mutates `n_ptksa`/frees/list-splices) but TP on `get`/`list` (primary only reads via `dl_list_for_each`); `buf` FP on `list` (primary writes through it via `os_snprintf`); `ctx` FP on `add` (stored into a non-const struct field for later callback use, not provably read-only).
- **Reconfirms at high density in this batch (not re-detailed above):** DCL30-C heap-vs-automatic-storage confusion (6 instances: `n`/`vlan_init.c:233`, `e`/`ptksa_cache.c:148`, `data`/`ext_password_file.c:51`, `s`/`ap_list.c:60`, `ap`/`ap_list.c:165` — all `os_zalloc`-backed); EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref (4 instances: `vlan:146`, `n:206`, `entry:299`, `data:41`); API00-C internal-only-API FP at very high density (9 instances: `hapd`x5 across `vlan_init.c`, `mgmt`/`elems`/`iface` in `ap_list.c`, `life_time_expiry_cb` in `ptksa_cache.c`); CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()` no-pthread FP (6 instances across `vlan_init.c`/`ext_password_file.c`); MSC01-C no-final-else deliberate-prior-value-preserved/no-op-needed family (3 instances: `vlan_init.c:160,205`, `ap_list.c:85` — the latter a genuinely-empty-list case, not a value-preservation case); API01-C buffer-before-pointer FP extended to `driver_nl80211.h`'s `i802_bss`/`wpa_driver_nl80211_data` (`ifname`/`brname`/`phyname`, all verified bounded via `os_strlcpy(...,sizeof(field))` in `driver_nl80211.c`, 3 instances); API05-C ptr+size_t idiom at very high density (23 instances: `driver_nl80211.h` x6, `ctrl_iface_ap.h` x14 (every `buf`+`buflen`/`len` ctrl-iface command handler), `ptksa_cache.c` x2); API02-C misfiring on callback function pointers (4 instances, `driver_nl80211.h`'s `delayed_handler`/`valid_handler`/`ack_handler_custom`/`handler`) and on plain scalar `int *num` out-params (3 instances, `ctrl_iface_ap.h`'s ACL add/del/clear) and on NUL-terminated command strings with no separate length at all (3 instances, `ctrl_iface_ap.h`'s `cmd` params); PRE08-C low-value-TP header-family convention reconfirmed (3 instances, `ap_list.c`'s `ieee802_11_defs.h`/`ieee802_11_common.h`/`ieee802_11.h`); PRE02-C on an already-atomic (single function-call) macro replacement list — same-name self-referential `nla_nest_start` wrapper macro guarded by `#ifndef NL_CAPABILITY_VERSION_3_5_0`, wrapping parens add nothing (`driver_nl80211.h:21`); DCL13-C plain read-only static-inline accessor genuine-if-low-value TP at very high density (18 instances: `fst_iface.h`'s entire accessor family on `struct fst_iface *i`, `driver_nl80211.h:410`'s `nl80211_attr_supported`, `ap_list.c`'s `iface`/`ap` static helpers) vs. one genuinely-wholly-unused-param TP (`ap_list_init`'s `iface`, body is just `return 0;`, `ap_list.c:299`); INT14-C container-vs-member misattribution (`ap_list.c:44`, bitwise `&0x7f` is on `ap->supported_rates[i]`, not on the loop index `i`); ERR33-C/ERR00-C fgets-return-checked-via-while-condition FP (`ext_password_file.c:102`, `while ((pos = fgets(...)))` is itself the check); EXP34-C internal-invariant/while-condition-already-guards FP (`ext_password_file.c:108`, `pos` proven non-NULL by the enclosing `while` loop); EXP05-C phantom cast-away-const where no cast exists at all (`ext_password_file.c:102`, `f` is a plain non-const `FILE*`); DCL15-C/DCL19-C FP where the flagged file-scope variable genuinely needs external linkage — verified via grep for a matching `extern` declaration + real out-of-file use (`ext_password_file.c:144`'s `ext_password_file`, `extern`-declared in `ext_password_i.h`, referenced in `ext_password.c`); MEM03-C "sensitive buffer not cleared" misapplied to an ownership-transfer-via-return-value (`ext_password_file.c:84`'s `password`, a `wpabuf` handed to the caller, not a local left uncleared); DCL13-C dispatch-contract FP extended to a new vtable family — `struct ext_password_backend`'s `.init`/`.deinit`/`.get` (`ext_password_file.c:81`'s `ctx`, matching the same `void *ctx` fixed-signature-contract shape as `eap_method`/`eloop`/`wpa_auth_callbacks`).
- **Two genuine (if low-severity) literal-rule-text TPs, both graded low confidence given minimal real-world impact:** WIN03-C `fopen(path, "r")` missing the `'N'` flag (`ext_password_file.c:90`) — file has no platform guard excluding Windows builds, so the handle-inheritance concern is real per rule text (see `win-rules-need-windows-oracle` prior: still no Windows oracle codebase to confirm against); FIO20-C `fgets()` with no truncation check on the 512-byte line buffer (`ext_password_file.c:102`) and ERR00-C `fclose()` return ignored (`ext_password_file.c:139`) — both real gaps on an admin-controlled local password file, low practical severity.
- **INT36-C int-to-pointer sentinel, graded TP (low) per literal-rule-text default:** `ptksa_cache_init`'s `#else` stub `return (struct ptksa_cache *) 1;` (`ptksa_cache.c:352`) converts a literal `1` to a pointer with no alignment guarantee — technically what the rule flags — but the value is used purely as a truthy sentinel and never dereferenced anywhere in the `CONFIG_PTKSA_CACHE`-disabled build, so it's harmless in practice. Same disposition class as the established ERR07-C/ERR34-C `atoi()` "graded TP per rule text, low real risk" precedent.

## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `16-40_b30`, 117 findings, `src/pae/ieee802_1x_cp.c` + `src/tls/tlsv1_record.c` + `wpa_supplicant/bgscan_simple.c` + `src/crypto/ms_funcs.c` + `src/utils/edit_simple.c` + `src/utils/wpa_debug.h`, all entire files, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances, one file): ARR39-C "scaled integer arithmetic with pointer... results in double scaling" misfires on plain `u8 *`/`char *` (element size 1) pointer + `size_t` bound-check arithmetic (`buf + buf_size`, `out_data + rl->iv_size`) with no `sizeof()` multiplication anywhere in sight.** Since the pointed-to element size is 1, ordinary pointer-scaling by the compiler is a no-op — there is no second scaling operation to double. `tlsv1_record.c:160,179,196,218,240,386`, all in `tlsv1_record_send`/`tlsv1_record_receive`. Watch for recurrence on any `u8 *`/`char *` bound-check idiom (`ptr + len > end`).
- **NEW, batch-local extension: ARR36-C/ARR00-C "pointers from different arrays"/"pointer subtraction" firing on plain scalar (`size_t`/`u8`) variables that merely share cosmetic naming with pointer-ish identifiers elsewhere in the function, with no pointer operation on that line at all.** `tlsv1_record.c:348` (`*out_len < in_len`, both plain size_t), `:399` (`padlen >= plen`, u8 vs size_t), `:407` (`plen - padlen - 1` loop bound, all scalars) — extends the established param-name-vs-same-buffer ARR36-C FP family to a sub-shape where neither operand is a pointer at the flagged line at all.
- **NEW, batch-local: DCL13-C misses mutation performed by a function called with the pointer parameter itself as an argument (not a local alias), when the callee is reached only through a macro.** `ieee802_1x_cp_step_run`'s `sm` (`ieee802_1x_cp.c:508`) is never written directly in the function body, but `SM_STEP_RUN(CP)` expands to `sm_CP_Step(sm)`, which mutates `sm->CP_state`/`sm->changed` via `SM_ENTER`. Making the param const would break the call. Distinguish from the aliased-local-pointer-mutation FP family — here it's the same top-level parameter, mutated one call-frame down through a macro-hidden dispatch.
- **NEW, batch-local: DCL13-C misses mutation of a struct member array performed via a helper call at the very end of a long function, when the struct pointer is otherwise read-only for the whole body.** `tlsv1_record_receive`'s `rl` (`tlsv1_record.c:278`) reads many `rl->*` fields but is only actually mutated via `inc_byte_array(rl->read_seq_num, TLS_SEQ_NUM_LEN)` on the last line — easy to miss in a ~200-line function.
- **NEW, batch-local: DCL15-C/DCL19-C "should be static"/"minimize scope" misfire on module-registration vtable objects (`struct X_ops` tables) that have genuine, intentional extern linkage declared in a header and referenced from a central registry file.** `bgscan_simple_ops` (`bgscan_simple.c:330`) is `extern`-declared in `bgscan.h:45` and referenced by `&bgscan_simple_ops` in `bgscan.c:19` (the module list) — cannot be made static or scope-reduced without breaking the registration pattern. Same shape as the already-confirmed `struct wpa_driver_ops`/`struct eap_method` dispatch-table precedents but for DCL15-C/DCL19-C specifically rather than DCL13-C. Watch for recurrence across every `*_ops`/`*_methods` registration table in hostap (`eap_method`, `wpa_driver_ops`, `bgscan_ops`, etc.).
- **NEW, batch-local: MSC13-C "dead assignment" misfires on a file-scope/static variable reset at the top of an eloop-invoked callback, when the assigned value is read on a *future* invocation of the same callback rather than later in the same call.** `edit_read_char`'s `cmdbuf_pos = 0` (`edit_simple.c:43`) looks dead within the single invocation, but is read on every subsequent character/backspace event since `cmdbuf_pos` is `static` and the function is re-entered per-byte from eloop. sqc's dead-assignment scan appears scoped to a single function invocation, missing static-variable persistence across re-entrant calls.
- **NEW, batch-local: STR31-C "character array too small to hold any string data" misapplied to a small fixed-size buffer that is never used as a NUL-terminated C string at all** — `unsigned char buf[1]` in `edit_read_char` (`edit_simple.c:29`) holds one raw byte from `read()`, accessed only via `buf[0]`, never NUL-terminated or passed to any string function.
- **NEW, batch-local: DCL31-C "function called without prior declaration" misfires on calls through a declared file-scope function-pointer *variable*** (not a parameter) — `edit_eof_cb(edit_cb_ctx)` / `edit_cmd_cb(edit_cb_ctx, cmdbuf)` (`edit_simple.c:36,44`) call through `static void (*edit_eof_cb)(void *ctx);` / `static void (*edit_cmd_cb)(void *ctx, char *cmd);`, both declared at file scope above. Extends the already-confirmed "function-pointer-parameter-call misfire" to file-scope function-pointer variables.
- **NEW, batch-local: FIO47-C printf format-type mismatch misfires on a `char[N]` array argument to `%s`, classifying the array-to-pointer-decayed argument as "Integer" instead of "Pointer".** `printf("\r> %s", cmdbuf)` where `cmdbuf` is `static char cmdbuf[CMD_BUF_LEN]` (`edit_simple.c:97`) — a completely ordinary, correct `%s` usage.
- **Reconfirms/extends in this batch (not re-detailed above):** DCL13-C macro-hidden-mutation FP extended from `WPA_PUT_BE16`/wire-header writes to `WPA_PUT_LE16(ucs2_buffer + j, ...)` writing an OUT buffer param (`ms_funcs.c:26`, `utf8_to_ucs2`'s `ucs2_buffer`); EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref on the `os_zalloc`/allocation line (`ieee802_1x_cp.c:454`, `bgscan_simple.c:168`); DCL30-C heap-vs-local-storage confusion (`ieee802_1x_cp.c:504` `sm`, `bgscan_simple.c:216` `data`); INT33-C div-by-zero-after-same-function-guard, both the early-return sub-shape (`bgscan_simple.c:54`, guarded by `if (!data->use_btm_query...) return false;`) and the earlier-clamp sub-shape (`bgscan_simple.c:194`, `short_interval` clamped `<=0 -> 30` a few lines above) and a same-block-enclosing-if sub-shape new here (`tlsv1_record.c:237`, division literally inside `if (rl->iv_size) {...}`); INT30-C wrap-around-on-a-value-bounded-by-a-callee's-own-clamp (`ms_funcs.c:119`, `len *= 2` where `len<=256` is guaranteed by `utf8_to_ucs2`'s own 512-byte buffer check); MSC37-C SM_STEP-macro-hides-void-return-type (`ieee802_1x_cp.c:355`) and MSC01-C SM_STEP-switch-no-final-else (`ieee802_1x_cp.c:374,391,424,437`) reconfirmed on a 4th state machine (CP); MSC01-C no-final-else-is-a-deliberate-default extended to plain (non-state-machine) event-handler if/else-if chains (`bgscan_simple.c:116,292,311`, background-scan interval bookkeeping — leaving state unchanged when no condition matches is correct); API00-C internal-only-API FP at high density (14 instances: `ms_funcs.c` MSCHAPv2 helpers' `peer_challenge`/`auth_challenge`/`username`/`master_key`/`password_len`, `edit_simple.c`'s `cmd_cb`/`eof_cb`/`ps`, `tlsv1_record.c`'s `buf_size` overflow-validation sub-shape); DCL13-C eloop dispatch-contract FP (timeout and sock-read handlers, 6 instances) and `struct bgscan_ops`/`struct X_ops` vtable dispatch-contract FP extended to `notify_scan`/`notify_beacon_loss` (`bgscan_simple.c:233,254`); DCL13-C plain-internal-helper genuine-if-low-value TP (`ieee802_1x_cp.c:96` `changed_cipher`'s `sm`, `edit_simple.c:66,67` `completion_cb`/`ctx`, `tlsv1_record.c:150` `rl` in `tlsv1_record_send`); DCL00-C genuine-if-trivial TP on a never-reassigned loop-local (`ms_funcs.c:32`); ## Confirmed/new patterns (from batch `6-15_b9`, 108 findings across 8 files: `src/tls/pkcs1.c`, `src/utils/browser-system.c`, `wpa_supplicant/pr_supplicant.h`, `wpa_supplicant/wpa_gui-qt4/eventhistory.h`, `src/ap/ap_config.h`, `src/common/dragonfly.c`, `src/crypto/crypto_internal.c`, `src/crypto/tls.h`, 2026-08-08)

- **NEW, CONFIRMED (6 instances, one file): API05-C "pointer parameter should use conformant array syntax" fires on an opaque `void *tls_ctx` context-handle parameter, not just raw arrays.** `tls.h`'s `tls_ctx` (the TLS backend's opaque context token from `tls_init()`, never treated as an array anywhere) triggers the same conformant-array-syntax complaint as the established ptr+size idiom, on `tls_connection_set_verify`/`_export_key`/`_get_eap_fast_key`/`tls_get_version`/`tls_get_cipher`/`tls_connection_client_hello_ext` (`:370,403,422,554,567,591`). Extends the existing "CONFIRMED categorical FP" API05-C family (ptr+size idiom, bare-NUL-string idiom) to a third sub-shape: opaque handle/context pointers with no array semantics at all.
- **NEW, batch-local (2 instances, watch for 3x elsewhere): API02-C "pointer parameter without size argument" misfires on a `const struct wpabuf *` parameter, a self-describing buffer type that already carries its own length via `wpabuf_len()`.** `tls_connection_handshake2`/`tls_connection_decrypt2`'s `in_data` (`tls.h:458,509`) — no raw `size_t` companion is needed or idiomatic for a `wpabuf`.
- **NEW, batch-local (1 instance): API01-C "string buffer before pointer" misapplied to an array of pointers, not a raw byte buffer.** `tls_cert_data.altsubject` is `const char *altsubject[TLS_MAX_ALT_SUBJECT]` (an array of string pointers), not a `char[]` that could be overflowed by an unbounded write into the adjacent `serial_num` pointer — the rule's overflow premise doesn't apply to this shape at all (`tls.h:58`).
- Reconfirms at high density (not re-detailed above): EXP43-C no-restrict in-place `crypto_bignum_{add,mulmod,mod,rshift}`/`crypto_rsa_exptmod` accumulator idiom (7 instances across `pkcs1.c`/`dragonfly.c`); EXP34-C `crypto_bignum_deinit()` NULL-safe-wrapper class (2 instances, `dragonfly.c:65,102`); DCL30-C heap-vs-automatic-storage confusion (`tmp`/`ctx`, 2 instances); API00-C internal-only-API FP (7 instances); ENV01-C wholesale zero-`getenv()` misfire (2 instances, `dragonfly.c:118,228`); INT14-C pointer-vs-dereferenced-element conflation (`prime_bin[prime_len-1]`, `dragonfly.c:240`); MSC17-C fallthrough misfire, both the `#ifdef`-intervening-next-case sub-shape and the new "case label directly preceded by a real unconditional break" sub-shape (5 instances, `crypto_internal.c`) and the stacked/grouped-case-labels sub-shape (1 instance, `crypto_internal.c:154`); MEM30-C/MEM31-C double-free/use-after-free misfire from mutually-exclusive branch confusion (3 instances, `crypto_internal.c:139,311`); DCL15-C "should be static" flatly wrong on `crypto_global_init`, a real external API (`crypto_internal.c:320`); DCL13-C `#ifdef FEATURE...#else` no-op-stub genuine-if-low-value TP (11 instances, `pr_supplicant.h`) vs. C++ Qt-header misparse FP family extended to `MSC04-C` self-recursion (`eventhistory.h:16`); API01-C "buffer before pointer" bounded-write FP reconfirmed including the exact `country[3]`-before-pointer shape (`ap_config.h:1083`, direct match to the `proximity_ranging.h` precedent); PRE02-C single-token negative-literal FP (`VLAN_ID_WILDCARD -1`, `ap_config.h:134`); PRE08-C 8.3-legacy shared-header-prefix FP (`ap_config.h:16`); DCL13-C genuine-if-low-value TP on plain read-only getters (`hostapd_get_oper_chwidth`/`_centr_freq_seg0_idx`/`_seg1_idx`, 3 instances, `ap_config.h`); ERR05-C "exit() dictates error handling" misapplied to a forked child's post-`execv()`-failure cleanup (established fork/exec exception, `browser-system.c:106`); CON33-C/CON34-C `strerror()` no-pthread FP (4 instances); MSC01-C no-final-else guard-clause pedantry (`browser-system.c:43`); DCL40-C 31-significant-character judgment call, genuinely exact at 31 chars (`tls_connection_set_success_data`/`_resumed`, `tls.h:652`); ARR37-C category error firing on a `size_t` scalar mistaken for a pointer (`pkcs1.c:190`); MSC41-C `wpa_hexdump_key` misfire extended to a runtime decrypted-signature buffer argument, not a title string (4 instances, `pkcs1.c:160-186`) — new sub-shape of the established hexdump-title family (misfires on the call itself/buffer argument, not just the label string).
- **Genuine TPs this batch:** ERR07-C/ERR34-C `atoi()` on an OSU HTTP-redirect-derived substring with zero error/range checking (`browser-system.c:44`); EXP05-C genuine cast-away-const for `execv()`'s `char *const argv[]` idiom (`browser-system.c:101`); MSC07-C genuinely unreachable `return -1;` after a noreturn `exit(0)` call in a forked child (`browser-system.c:107`, low severity).

- **NEW, batch-local (2 instances, watch for recurrence): DCL13-C "not modified, should be const" misses that the pointer is forwarded wholesale (unchanged) into a callee that mutates the pointee, rather than mutated in the current function's own body.** `ieee802_11_auth.c`'s `hostapd_acl_cache_free(acl_cache)` forwards `acl_cache` into `hostapd_acl_cache_free_entry()` (non-const, calls `os_free()`) every loop iteration (`:66`); `offchannel.c`'s `offchannel_deinit(wpa_s)` forwards `wpa_s` unchanged into `offchannel_clear_pending_action_tx()`, which sets `wpa_s->pending_action_tx = NULL` (`:457`). Distinct from the existing "misses a mutation through an aliased local pointer" DCL13-C FP family (that one is about writing through a locally-derived alias of a struct field); this shape is about forwarding the *same, unaliased* pointer to a mutating callee.
- **NEW, batch-local (1 instance): DCL13-C "not modified" is also invalid when the param is returned by the function itself and the return type is non-const.** `offchannel.c`'s `wpas_get_tx_interface(wpa_s, src)` returns `wpa_s` directly on multiple paths; the function's return type is `struct wpa_supplicant *` (non-const), so constifying the `wpa_s` parameter would break the return statement without also changing the return type — the suggestion as literally given doesn't compile (`:22`).
- **NEW, batch-local (1 instance, real DCL13-C miss, not a stylistic quibble): a direct field write through the very param flagged.** `wps_attr_process.c`'s `wps_process_cred_mac_addr`'s `cred` param is flagged as unmodified, but the function's very next statement is `os_memcpy(cred->mac_addr, mac_addr, ETH_ALEN);` — a genuine write through `cred`, missed entirely (`:195`).

EXP34-C internal-invariant-never-null extended to a helper (`wpas_get_tx_interface`) whose every return path is provably non-NULL by inspection, not just a single guarded struct field (`offchannel.c:100,331`) and to `radius_msg_get_hdr()`'s return (`msg->hdr` unconditionally set in both `radius_msg_new()`/`radius_msg_parse()`, `ieee802_11_auth.c:499`); DCL30-C heap-vs-local-storage confusion (`offchannel.c`'s `iface:63`, a local pointer walking a heap-backed linked list, not stack storage; `upnp_xml.c`'s `value:220`/`buf:251`, both `os_zalloc`/`wpabuf_alloc_ext_data`-backed); ARR01-C `sizeof(*ptr)`/`sizeof(ptr->fixed_member)`-correct-idiom at volume (`wps_attr_process.c:113,186,271`, `ieee802_11_auth.c:256,275`, `ndisc_snoop.c:49`); EXP33-C `sizeof(*ptr)`-not-a-deref on a still-unassigned pointer (`ieee802_11_auth.c:528,727`, `ndisc_snoop.c:45`);
